author: theogonia777
text:
This has been asked many times before.  One of the problems with that sort of thing is that people will actually make more unnecessary posts in an attempt to get something upvoted.  Really it doesn't matter though.  It also opens the door to some clown going around and downvoting every post they see, regardless of whether or not it's a good post.  And I feel like the way some of the subforums on here tend to be, you would end up with every thread full of 20 downvotes per post.
Also if your post is good and people agree with it, they'll say that it's good or vice versa, which is probably cooler in terms of feedback because you actually know who likes your posts and why rather than that 20 anonymous people liked it, potentially none of which are active posters.
Though honestly one thing that I would like to see changed for the Like/Dislike system in the columns would be showing the individual number of likes and dislikes.  With the current system, a comment might have a total of +5 we'll say.  That only tells you that 5 more people upvoted than downvoted.  That could mean that 5 people upvoted and none downvoted or that 768 people upvoted and 763 people downvoted.  I think that that would be a lot more helpful.

author: hyvyys
text:
Most bad tab reports I get are silly comments that I can only respond to with clicking "Ignore report".
For instance:
This song is not accurate as it has 0 tabs and its not a chord only song or a single guitar
(Clearly coming from a user who doesn't distinguish between chord sheets, tabulateres and guitar pro tabs).
Clicking "Ignore report" doesn't seem to do anything. I did receive a new notification after that though, which was identical to the initial bad tab report notification (did I just notify myself someone reported my tab?)
I would instead would like to be able to reply to the report with a message (e.g. WTH do you mean my man?).
The only occasions where I actually get to improve on my tabs are 4-star ratings which are not accompanied by any message, but still make me go and look back at the tab at which point I typically immediately see what could be improved since they are often tabs I submitted years ago. So I don't see why the text field prompt shouldn't be also included for the 4-star ratings (as optional).
On a side note, users with 20 or less reputation should be required to select from a predefined list of reasons in order to cast a 1-star rating, because nothing they type manually will usually make any sense.

text:
Quote by Chrisiphone
I find it great to have an off-topic forum
Yes, i approve of off topic forums. I think it's a bit silly that UG's off topic forum is the most active forum on the entire site - and i'm certain that there's some members who only join to post in the pit, either knowing nothing about guitar playing or gear thus having nothing worthwhile to contribute to the other sections, or they don't even play guitar at all.
It's a difficult one, but i think that even though this site would be a lot less active without the pit, it would serve it's purpose a lot better, being an online resource for guitarists, because i think having the pit does attract people who actually aren't interested in learning about guitar techniques or gear or anything like that. And these people sometimes stumble into the proper forums though they have nothing worthwhile to contribute- i think the pit is responsible for a lot of the absolute drivel that gets posted in other forums that completely de-rails a lot of serious threads - it's the 'pit monkeys' accidentally making their way into the proper forums.
That being said, if you did remove the pit and all these people left, UG would just end up like mylespaul.com or something like that - very very snobby and elitist, and full of stuck up mid-life-crisis divorcees with more money than sense, who would gladly ridicule anyone with a guitar that didn't cost 4 digits.
So it really is a matter of whether members are willing to put up with a bit of ignorance combined with pre-teen arrogance, at the expense of outright snobbery

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Bear in mind that UG and Guitar Pro have commercial ties. Basically, UG is allowed to host Guitar Pro tabs because the users are required to purchase the Guitar Pro software if they want to access those tabs. An online dumbed-down flash version of the Guitar Pro software would not only require massive amounts of time and work from the programming team (which they can't afford at the moment), eat up loads and loads of bandwidth (which isn't desirable either), but it would also defeat the purpose of the commercial agreement between UG and GP.
So I don't see this happening, at all actually.

author: jamescnewman
text:
One of the things that I end up spending time on when learning a new song using the official/pro/power tabs is finding out which bits are the same and which are different.  "Just play it" is often the answer, but sometimes, you have to read through and analyse an entire track to find out that all of the verses are the same except the second, which has a different fill etc and then try to memorise which thing goes where.  Remembering back to the days of guitar magazines etc, this wasn't the case - each section was tabbed and then you had the song structure to put it together like lego.  Classical sheet music is easier to follow because it also has structure such as repeats, codas etc rather than writing everything out N times.
While this isn't easy to entirely fix overnight, there are plenty of enhancements that will help, would benefit a lot of users and could initially be options.  I have included some ideas below - 1 and 2 should be relatively easy as they don't fundamentally change the way things work or involve algorithmic complexity, just how things are rendered to the screen.  3 and 4 are more complex, however they cover the thought process that we are all probably going through manually at the moment.
1. Fixed Number of Bars per Line
The majority of rock songs follow patterns in four bar groups, however when tabs are rendered, bars/line is fairly haphazard and depends upon screen size, zoom, full screen on/off and bar complexity.  The result is that it is a time-consuming process to spot patterns etc that would otherwise be easy to spot by eye  i.e. "Have I already learnt this?... Yes - I can see that it's the same as the four bars before".  It would be great to be able to lock it at a specified number of bars per line, with each bar taking an even amount of space.  Optionally, you could bend this rule if there are 16 bars of rests for the bass during an intro etc, but you'd want to snap back into N/line when there's something to do.  You could allow tab authors to set this, default to 4, or leave it entirely as an option for the user (both global preferences and per-tab).
2. New Section on New Line
Start each section on a new line - this will provide clarity when new sections start and fix any bar to line alignment issues caused by irregular sections like a bridge with an odd length.
3. Bar Repeats
This is more algorithmically involved, but you could automatically detect repeated sections and use repeat signs ( ":" ) different endings and even codas depending upon your appetite complexity.  I think identical repeated sections would be relatively easy to detect with some parameters to stop it doing anything daft (e.g. repeat 1 bar 13 times would be better 3 * 4 bars repeated + 1 not even if they are all the same).  There is impact on the mapping between the user's click location in the score and playback location, but there are ways around that without too much complexity, such as clicking goes to the closest repeat to the current location.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeat_sign
4. Song Structure Repeats
There is already a song structure at the bottom of the page and in the score, however if sections are identical, you have to go back and read or play it, trying to compare with something that's several pages higher up.  It would be very helpful to give the user some idea of which sections are repeated e.g. is every verse the same or are they a little different.  This could get very complicated if you're trying to change the way the musical structure is rendered, however given that you already know where each section starts, you could simply colour the background of sections of bars that are the same as the last section of the same type (e.g. verse) in green.  If you're skimming the second verse and it's all green, you would therefore know there's nothing new to learn.  If the last bar in the section is not green, there's a new riff.

author: jamescnewman
text:
mandelstamdavid
Many thanks for taking a look and for responding so quickly.
This should be relevant to all users of any level because as with classical sheet music, the intention is to convey the music to the reader in the most clear and concise way possible.  If the score does not do this, time is inevitably spent trying to spot patterns etc rather than playing music.  Numbers 1 and 2 occur in almost every tab unless you are very lucky with screen size and bar similarity, however I have included an example below.  I assume that 3 and 4 speak for themselves, however let me know if not.  While playing with the zoom helps with line alignment, the user shouldn't have to do this and it doesn't work consistently for whole songs or new sections.
Links
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/its_so_easy_official_2598213
https://imgur.com/a/xk1FLhw
Example 1 - 100% Zoom
The score has arranged itself at three bars per line, which doesn't fit well with the music, hence patterns are more difficult to spot by eye
Sections begin in unpredictable parts of each line
Due to differing bar complexity, bars have uneven spacing, making the page look messy
When the interlude starts, there is just one note/bar and it's suddenly five bars per line, removing any coincidental line alignment from before
Example 2 - 90% Zoom
Some of the problems from 100% are still present (uneven bars, interlude spacing), however:
With four bars per line, patterns in the music are now very obvious (Point 1 in original post)
The verse and chorus sections have accidentally started at the beginning of a line due to 8 bars/section = exactly 2 lines, making them very clear (Point 2 in original post), although the interlude throws this pattern off
Example 1 [100%]: No alignment between music and lines
Example 2 [90%]: A lot better, but still not perfect

My feedback is this: the way you run your company is due for some serious criticism.

pro tabs hide other community versions from the side bar. Why? Why are you like this? Did an executive ask for that? Add links to community tabs back to the pro-tabs. You are a company whose public facing product is a website, why are you not designing it for the user?

A 50 dollar giveaway is pathetic, but you don't even check for the users location. Do not send me emails about "giveaways" where my country is not a valid participant. Also, stop giving away money. Give the money to your UI/UX developers if they're still alive in the basement you locked them in.
The sidebar to the left is too big. I do not need access to these things so let me resize how much the left panel takes up so I can make space for the chords AND my notes without having to scroll sideways. Your public facing product is a website. Design it better.
This window is too small too. Let us resize the damn box. I wrote half a 2000s forum post and I already have to scroll just to see what I wrote earlier. Are you serious? This product is finished. It needs maintenance, it needs fixing according to user feedback and it needs legal support. author: Wolfsbora
text:
After putting in quite a few years as staff on a custom PC (computers) forum where one of the big attractions is posting your rig in your own thread so that members can discuss it and provide feedback, I'm having serious difficulty understanding why a forum that has "guitar" in the name and is 95% based on guitars and equipment does not allow its members to start threads to discuss their guitars.
Is it a concern that a particular forum will be flooded with threads showing off and discussing their guitars (I literally cannot understand how this is a bad thing on a guitar forum)? If this is the issue, why not have a sub-forum dedicated to showing off gear? Also, I understand there is a thread for showing off guitars but it is limited to prevent people from chatting about each other's guitars. So what is the point?
I enjoy this forum, there is a lot of helpful information, great members, etc. However, it seems crazy to me that it's against the rules to open a thread to show and discuss your guitar.
Thanks for hearing me out!

https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=203917

text:

One's guitar can be simply their tool for making music, all the way to being one's pride and joy. This should be a place that allows discussion of such things. Maybe the guitar's owner can learn some new tricks or mods that could improve their guitar.

author: Wolfsbora
text:
dspellman
I respect that. I would just like to be able to post a thread that features my guitar for these reasons:
1. So I can always refer people to it if they're curious; this includes multiple photos
2. This same thread can be used to look for suggestions for parts for the same guitar without having to lay out a story every time; for example, I want new locking tuners on one of my guitars, instead if opening a new thread for each mod I'd like advice on, it's right there & easy for me to keep track of all suggestions
3. We're all here to talk about our gear, whether it be to help others, share interests or discussing opposing views. I'd like to be able to talk about my guitar, get rolling ideas on it, have people comment on it, etc
4. You're allowed to do build threads (which are awesome, btw). What if I change things on my guitar quite often? It's the same principle. I'd be able to update my thread stating I'm changing things and get feedback from people already familiar with the guitar and they'd be able to see the progression and often WHY I made the changes
5. On a business standpoint, it draws memberships, guests and advertisers and can drive search engine traffic. The internet is a place to showcase anything you want to so why is a guitar forum not allowing it's members to showcase their guitars?
Simple suggestion:
Create a sub-forum to allow for exactly the idea of showcasing. Either bring on another volunteer to moderate it or worst case scenario incorporate it into existing staff responsibilities (though, I am anti this solution).
By doing exactly this, people will either want to keep checking out the new guitars of members or people like
dspellman
can avoid it because it's not their thing.
For crying out loud I'll even moderate it. Just believe me, traffic will increase. Traffic leads to memberships and advertising.

author: jamescnewman
text:
I had a ton of issues with the editor used in these forums recently and imagine many other users also experience difficulties, which deters people from editing errors in posts or using formatting to provide clarity.  Consider replacing the current editor with a Markdown version (see
https://www.markdownguide.org/basic-syntax/
) as follows:
Markdown is widely used across the internet and user apps, hence non-technical people are becoming increasingly familiar with its syntax even if they don't know what it is called (Slack, WhatsApp etc)
If people don't want to use formatting and just write text, it doesn't get in the way
Optionally, if you want to help non-technical users, you can still have buttons for bold etc, but they would edit the markdown e.g. selecting text and hitting bold adds or removes surrounding double-asterisks, hitting the image button asks for URL and then adds the appropriate markdown
A preview button (like Jira) could be used to check the end-result
No hidden artefacts such as inconsistent line endings or hidden formatting problems to surprise the user while editing or after they submit
This would dramatically simplify your implementation as you wouldn't need to maintain a proprietary editor - there are a lot of open source libraries for markdown.  To illustrate the point that you should replace the current editor, here are the bugs I've seen so far with the current editor while making
one
post, all of which would go away with a clean markdown implementation:
When you start typing, it sometimes places the first character in the middle of the word e.g. "Guitar" would turn into "uiGtar"
When you edit a post, all of the bullets get taken out of their original position and placed at the end with double-spacing
When you edit a post, line spacing can be significantly altered and inconsistent line ending characters result in unexpected behaviour, such as the bullet button indenting unwanted lines or lines that are rendered in the editor disappearing when the update is saved
I have seen broken image icons pop in and out of existence while deleting text before or after them
When large images are inserted, adding a new line to text higher up can make the editor jump to a point far lower down the page, forcing the user to manually scroll up to see what they are writing
Pasting a url and then typing results in the words that follow becoming part of the URL
As an example, when I realised that I made a typo, editing involved copying the bullets that were thrown to the end, pasting them into a local editor to fix the hidden formatting, going back over the non-bulleted text in the forum editor to delete and re-add line endings (to avoid them being indented later), pasting the right bullets back into the right place, hitting the bullet button to make them back into bullets etc.  All just to fix one word!

author: naranjaa
text:
Hi
I've been having a few issues with chord transposition:
* altered chords get corrupted by transposition:
Am7b5  -1 => Gm75  instead of G#m7b5 (or Abm7b5)
Am7b5  +1 => Am75 instead of A#m7b5 (or Bbm7b5)
The alteration disappears as if it were applied to the root.
* others are not recognized and cannot be transposed : Fm7M, Fm7b13
ok, the first one can be written Fmmaj7, but considering Fm7 and F7M, wouldn't it be natural to have Fm7M ?
* the bass note is no more a chord note after transposition:
B7/A  +1 => C7/A# instead of C7/Bb  (a seventh of a C is always a B)
This one is probably more tricky, as it requires a knowledge of the chord notes.
An idea would be to maintain the distance between root and bass, both in number of semitones and number of letters.
Here is a test tab that shows more examples:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/user/tab/view?h=AaQP-YZreTYR-ANDy82wW4bS

author: NSpen1
text:
naranjaa
Am7b5 should be written Am7-5 for it to transpose.
Fm7M, no that's horrible as is F7M, they should be banned.  If everyone just used Fmaj7, Fm7 and Fmmaj7 there would be no confusion.
Fm7b13 is trickier, in theory that looks more like Dbmaj9/F so you can try that.
You're going to get everything with sharps at the moment when transposing, hopefully the proposed amendment to the transpose function will fix that.  So, you'd go +1 further to C#7/B, then back down and it should be C7/Bb.
Edit: yeah, using - and + instead of b and # should fix a lot of those.

They could find someone to reamp their guitars, program and sequence drums, record bass, and mix/master the track. Leading to a better, professional quality product without having to invest in a studio of your own.

author: theogonia777
text:
Advertising/promoting can be acceptable provided that it is done in the appropriate subforum for that particular thing (recordings, classifieds, promote your band, etc).  And I've seen enough of it where it is certainly there.
The big thing you have to understand is that it is not worthwhile to create a new subforum for something for which there doesn't seem to be a demand.  For example, there was a large drum thread for years in the Pit with thousands and thousands of posts before the drum forum was created.  And you know what?  It's a ghost town.  In Bands & Artists, various subfora are frequently being consolidated because there is just not adequate traffic.  It's just not worth having a subforum for something that will get one thread a month. This is why there is new keyboard forum, folk instrument forum, etc despite those having greater demand over the years than what you are asking for.

author: sjones
text:
I'd like to make a suggestion that the Promote Your Band forum have a thread that would be used for bands who are actively looking to book shows to hook up with each other.
I've been thinking of ideas for such a thread for a while and how it could be put set up. Also, I've thought of some rules and guidelines for such a thread, which I'd be glad to share if the Mods would like to consider giving their blessings to such a thread.
One of the biggest factors in why I suggest this thread is because not every band in PYB is looking to book. This way, bands who are looking to book gigs, looking for new bands/and venues, and looking to expand their base will have an easier way to get in contact with each other.
I'd be more than willing to help in overseeing this threads' creation and the day-to-day goings-on in it, this way it's no hassle to the Mods (of course, anything that breaks the forum rules or thread rules will be reported immediately).
In addition to this thread, and for another reason to allow it's creation, I'd like to do a monthly (or more frequent) article to highlight some of the shows that our UG member's bands have put on. This will be great promotion for them.
I kept this OP somewhat brief, but if the powers-that-be would like to discuss the allowance of such a thread in PYB (or whatever subforum they see fitting), I have more in depth ideas for the thread.
Thanks
sjones

author: sjones
text:
Quote by ZeGuitarist
I'm interested to see how this idea could develop. It sounds promising.
Thanks.
What I'm thinking is first, I'd obviously post some sort rules part. It would be separated into "Rules" (punishable, ban-warranting) and General Guidelines (More or Less a Tips section). I'd obviously link and restate to follow all forum-wide and subforum rules, and then add some specifically for the thread. I'll discuss these more in depth later, for now, I'd like to stay to the structuring of the thread.
Next, I will have a section of bands who are looking to book. This will include thier Genre, Location, Set Length, and any thing else we can think think of that will be beneficial. Along with this, any venues that they have strong contacts with, they could post those as well. For example, here's what I'd put for my band:
Quote by Example
Dissecting the Flood
MeloDeath/Metalcore/Progressive - Southeast Ohio & Nearby WVa. - 30 minute set
Venues and Other Contacts
Rader's Music Venue
-
J&S Media
I could probably do a better job of formatting that text as well (ideas, anyone
?), but that's the basic idea I had for the band "list". I was thinking I'd break the list down into regions (at least in the U.S.) and countries. This way it'd be easier to browse thru. I'm also thinking I should do something special, maybe a denotation or symbol/coloration change of some sort for bands who are willing to travel over a certain amount of time (Maybe an hour? 90 minutes?) to play.
I'd also like to keep a list of shows that the thread has set up in the OP (or a reserved 2nd post). Bands or Forum users new to the site and thread could use this to see what's happening around them, and use it to their advantage to jump on shows.
I'd like bands to either post or PM me pics/videos/recordings/or press about their shows so I could use it in an article for UG as well.
I'm also thinking I could add in a Reference list of Good/Bad users. This though, I am up in the air about.
I'm open to hearing any more suggestions on sections to add in to the OP (or OP's) of the thread. Those are all the ideas I have off the top of my head for the "structuring" of the thread, so I'll now digress back into the rules/guidelines section.
First, the thread specific rules. This will be preceeded by some sort of reminder to observe all forum and sub-forum rules in addition to these
1. Gigs are set up at your own risk. Ultimate-Guitar or anyone associated with this website or this thread ARE NOT RESPONSIBLE for anything bad that should occur because of gigs you set up in this thread. This includes, but is not restricted to such things as: Theft of Gear or Money of any kind, Any sort of vehicular problems, any sort crimes any forum user or band member may commit, violence of any sort, ect.
If you are a subject to anything negative such as listed above or actions/events otherwise not listed, please report any offenders to those in charge of this thread and forum, and also to the appropriate autorities.
2. Anyone who commits "gig fraud" -- Intentionally setting up a gig to either "troll" another band into wasting their time and money to drive to a gig that has not been set up, OR, setting up a show to intentionally screw another band/forum member out of money will face appropriate consequences (AKA- BANSTICK).
3. Anyone who intentionally breaks any sort of guarantee (money or otherwise) and it can be proven beyond reasonable doubt that it was an intentional action, will face the appropriate consequences.
4. Keep this thread on topic. A bit of off-topic chat will be fine as long as it's within reason of the purpose of this thread, however, let's keep it within it's limits. In-Post warnings (not UG official warnings) will be given out if things get too out of hand. Any further nonsense will result in UG-Official Warnings and Bans.
5. Post or PM your band(s), venues, and any other links in an appropriate manner. If vital information is missing your band may not get posted accurately or at all. If any links contain inappropriate material, you will be subject to punishment.
Those are some rules I thought of off the top of my head. Of course, they're open to amendments and also I'd like to hear any more suggestions for rules.
Now to the "Guidelines/Tips" section. These are not punishable offenses for the most part, but tips to help the process of booking gigs to go smoothly.
When booking gigs, use these guidelines as help to make sure everything goes smoothly.
- Discuss and agree on money. Guarantees? Cut of the Door? Can merch be sold and does the venue ask for some sort of cut of sales?
(EDIT: THIS IS THE ONLY PUNISHABLE OFFENSE IN THIS SECTION: ONLY A VENUE MAY ASK FOR A CUT OF MERCH SALES. ANYONE WHO IS CAUGHT ASKING FOR MERCH SALES THAT IS NOT A REPRESENTITIVE OF A VENUE WILL BE PUNISHED)
- Discuss any PA and Gear Related Issues. In-House PA? Bands provide PA? Any gear sharing need to take place?
- Discuss and agree on Time of show/Set length/and any other issues related to the showbill itself. This also includes order of bands who will be playing.
- Discuss any venue-related issues. Age restrictions? Soundchecks/Backlining? Is there a time where you must be packed and out of the venue? Is there a rental fee? Soundman and how good are they?
- GIVE GOOD, ACCURATE DIRECTIONS AND/OR USE GOOGLE MAPS!
- In general, discuss and agree on ANYTHING that's important to the success your specific gig.
I'll also include sections about "How to Appropriately submit your band's information" with the example I used earlier in this post, and also sections pertaining to how to submit videos/recordings/other media for use in the related Article I'll be writing.
Well, that was long. I think I've covered everything I have in my mind for the thread. I'd really like mroe input and discussion about things before it goes "live" on the forum (if permission is granted, that is.) I really think it's a great idea and could be great for the bands and UG. Plus, it might get more people into the PYB forum, which would be great.
I'd also like to discuss with the appropriate Mods, providing this thread gets the go ahead, some way to arrange some sort of Mod privilages that would help me with the oversight of this thread. I'm not certain but I believe this would require me to be a Mod of the PYB SubForum, which wouldn't hurt as I'm generally browing PYB on an almost daily basis anyway, and could help with not only the upkeep of this thread but also the general upkeep of PYB (Deleting Spam, Keeping the Double Posts of bands to a minimum, and generally enforcing the other SubForum rules which at times I've seen go for days without being noticed.). Of course, I know it's taboo to ask for these privilages, but they are not for some "power-hunger" reason and I ask mainly to lend a hand with the upkeep of this thread and to take any potential burden off of the other Mods. It would be very helpful in the fact that I could "Check-Off" the posts that include band submissions without taking up forum space with more posts. If you'd consider it, I'd be more than willing to have a discussion about it.

author: Crazy Drummer69
text:
Hey everybody!
I was ecstatic to see that drum tabs are now officially supported by UG. Although I understand that UG is, and always will be, predominately dominated by guitar-related topics, I think that it's time that the drums receive their own forum in the Instruments category.
The new forum would further show UGs support towards expanding into the greatest online musician-oriented informative site on the internet. There are many topics to be discussed, and no proper place to discuss them in. I'd even be willing to moderate the forum to help get it going (if you want references and relevant experience I am prepared to discuss it in private).
Let's face it, the only good site to find drum tabs on was MXTabs.com, which is back up again but I think its BS that I can't even see some of the tabs that I've transcribed because the label hasn't given permission for my country (Canada) to view their music. That is why UG will always thrive. Great content, a strong community, fair moderators, and no copyright fiascos to deal with. I'm proud to be a member.
"If you build it, they will come," drum tabs are supported and people are submitting them, its only a matter of time before the population increases just like the guitar population has. UG should embrace, and encourage it, rather than try to suppress it.
P.S.
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1062965
was written on 02-07-2009,
before drum tabs were supported
, that is why I am advancing this suggestion.
P.P.S. Others who have suggested the same thing were told to submit their tabs to 911tabs.com, run by the same people as UG, but failed to realize that 911tabs is simply a search engine, not a storage site like UG, turning creative minds away from this amazing resource.
P.P.P.S. Drums are new to UG, there's lots of uncharted territory and much work to do, I want to repay my debt to UG by contributing where I can and I'm sure theres hundreds/thousands just waiting for the same opportunity.

author: garykob
text:
I think you should remove the ability for users to rate a tab if they are only using TabPro instead of the actual GuitarPro program.  My tabs are painstakingly created and mixed using the GuitarPro program, not TabPro, and although I don’t mind UltimateGuitar using my tabs for TabPro, there are lots of imperfections with that conversion.  TabPro does not faithfully reproduce whammy bar, volume swells, and other effects. The equalization and instrument sounds are not the same, etc.  Check out how bad this 5-star tab came out with TabPro:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/r/rolling_stones/brown_sugar_ver4_guitar_pro.htm
In this case the awful "bass" track you are hearing is really my saxophone track (in a different key), and then they put my bass line as their "drums". And my drum track is completely gone.  Someone listening to the TabPro version could understandably rate this tab a 1-star, which would be wrong.

author: garykob
text:
Here is another example.  User fleming215 just gave me a 3 star rating on my otherwise 5 star tab of Mama Told Me Not To Come:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/t/three_dog_night/mama_told_me_not_to_come_guitar_pro.htm
I am pretty sure the 3 star rating was because he listened it to it using the TabPro program which is completely wrong, sounds horrible--I would give it a 1 star.  This tab was painstakingly created for GuitarPro6, not for TabPro.  In the TabPro version my bass was mistakenly assigned to drums.  My drums were mistakenly assigned to Electric Guitar #3, my Lead Guitar was mistakenly assigned to Bass, and my Drum track is completely missing.  Does someone manually translate each tab from GP6 to TabPro, or is it somehow done automatically?  Whatever your process, it appears to be extremely unreliable, and you definitely should not be letting people rate us based on TabPro.

author: brettsanace
text:
The existence of this thread is exactly why the L4 requirements should be secret. L4 is granted to people who have demonstrated that they have the necessary skills and can be trusted not to abuse the privileges and powers that come with it (Veto voting, submitting tabs without going through the TPA queue), not to those people who are simply seeking to enhance their status and reputation by ticking off a list of qualification criteria i.e. glory mongers. This thread and many of the comments would seem to put you
TylerStacytabs
and
calebstrovas1
into the second category.
Quote by TylerStacytabs
NSpen1  why should you be level 5  you only ever vote on corrections and not actual tabs,
Well firstly, that is an incorrect comment as NSpen1 does comment and vote on new tabs, and it is also a naive comment as checking corrections requires more musical knowledge and skill than checking new tabs which largely involves checking formatting and inserting stock comments about, adding section headings, putting chords above all lyric lines etc.
Putting a list of criteria e.g. X number of tabs would just encourage people to submit crap tabs, whilst they may not be approved it still wastes peoples' time in the queue, and as I alluded to previously the tabs may be approved because tab approval is largely based on correct formatting not accuracy, which down the track will also waste peoples' time in correcting or deleting the tabs. Similarly, requirements about the number of ratings would encourage people to get their friends to vote, and requirements about queue participation would encourage people who don't know what they are doing to comment/vote in the queue or to copy other peoples comments/votes. None of these outcomes would demonstrate that someone deserves to be L4.
With regards, to harsh comments from moderators, I think you will find that initially the comments are friendly and helpful and that they tend to get harsher the more they have to repeat the same comments over and over again to the same people. Also the fact that the comments are harsh doesn't mean they are wrong.

author: thequadrat
text:
TylerStacytabs
calebstrovas1
All right. Some explainers here.
1. Users
.
Let's start from separating active users into two camps - tab authors and mods/voters in TPA.
Authors are extremely different, from newbies to crazy jazz theory freaks and 'classy-look-style' tab lovers, that's why we have a huge sets of how authors would like to present their tab to the public. When you start submitting tabs to UG you firstly notice some basic rules in the guides or in the comments of your tab of how it should look to be approved. You are getting used to it when surfing through UG tabs on the site and with every new submit because you start to figure out that lots of tabs look the same in terms of interface and it's easy to navigate with one style. Mods, UG staff and experienced users will leave you a comment in TPA to lead into the right road to make a good looking tab.
The same big difference we have in TPA comments when authors starting to vote. Sometimes they are wrong and do not follow voting rules and judge subjectively.
Last 6 months the average amount of new tabs daily is around 500. It's impossible to listen to all of them by mods and some UG mods that are working in TPA every day and as guys said above - we check only formatting for the unique tabs (no any other version on the site) and sometimes musical part when you need to check and compare tab with the existing version. Also, there are many cases when authors messing with artist and song names, meta information, tab formatting,  ticking wrong checkboxes, etc., so here we are to fix all of that and point out mistakes.
Corrections is the place where we can dive into the music and check what's right or wrong in the tab.
So, we are trying to raise the culture of making good looking tab but for the musical parts we have our great community to make a collective decision. Think of it like Wikipedia for musicians
. You can also be on the justice side and make correction while you learning the tab and found something wrong. And you can be sure that this correction will be reviewed.
Moderators. These guys are the most experienced and know a lot of UG mechanics so they can make a proper decision in controversial situations and find a good solution for almost any problem. Especially it helps in working with duplicates, abusers, copy-pasters and other submissions which will not make the catalog better.
So, on both hands, we are trying to make tabs look better and left authors music vision of the song untouched so it could be judged publically, not by the 'weird UG staff/mods'.
2. Levels.
As I said above, with every new tab you are getting more familiar with submission and approval rules, tab formatting and the whole process overall.
The first three levels indicate your passion to make tabs. The more - the better. So when you got L3 we think that you are good enough to make no mistakes when you sending tabs.
L4-5 are more advanced and the main advantages of them are auto-approve and veto-right. It means way more responsibility, attention to the process and adequate judging skills. Also, there are cases when we cut the level from some authors because some extra power driving people crazy sometimes. The same with moderators. We are all humans anyway
Also, being L4-5 means that your actions are watched by UG monitoring systems, it is double-checking for us to be sure we have the right authors with the right levels.
So, if you are making good tabs you can be sure that it will be approved. If you met mod's comment - it means they try to help you to make a better tab or point out the reason why your vote is not right. If you are happy just with making tabs - that's cool, you are free to send as much as you want. I think that a nice example is
Neckwringer
- #6 author of all-time with 5k+ tabs (damn, how is it possible?
and being happy with his L3.
Trying to get L4 by commenting and voting in TPA just to build activity points is not a way how to get it and it's bad practice. Helping in TPA is some sort of mentoring - sharing your experience with newbies as a master who already done this road. UG and mods work hard to make you a better and more accurate tabber and it is your way to pay back - spread the knowledge. Objectively and rules-oriented. No need to spam about empty lines between songparts in every tab, it's not a strict rule.
By the way, levels on UG are quite old and we have some ideas about it but when it will be the time.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
These are forums, not board meetings.  If you try to legislate every last aspect of behaviour with rules, you'll suck the life right out of them.
Sure there are occasions where a thread gets jacked because of puns.  And on some of those occasions the puns are funny and creative.  And sometimes the conversation goes off on a tangent to a completely different area than was defined by the OP.  This is not necessarily a bad thing.
Make the environment so stiff and rigid that it becomes impossible to have occasional nuisances, and you'll also make it infertile for serendipitous fun and creativity.  That's a high price to pay.
Forums aren't perfect.  Never have been.  Never will be.  Such is life.
Instead of more rules, I suggest target advertising to shape the personal habits of the people posting so they are in a better frame of mind, before they post.  For instance, UG might run ads to encourage dietary changes to promote better attitudes.  Perhaps products like this:

Community Updates is a Widget, aka: Module.  There is a thread just for those.  But no big deal, really.
I dunno if it's really worth adding notifications for picture comments to the Community Updates widget.  There are tons of things that could generate notifications.  Better to add those things that don't already generate notifications through other means, yeah?
You can get email notifications on several items if you check the appropriate boxes in the
Account Settings
page in your My Profile.  I think this is a pretty good way to keep track of those areas of your profile you seldom visit yourself.  Try getting your notifications that way.  I think you'll like it.
The number of data entries in each user's Community Updates stack is limited.  So when new things happen, the older events drop off the list.  Add too many other items and you'll miss notifications if they drop off the list before you check it.
At present, Community Updates is geared around activities on your friends' profiles and posts in Groups you belong to.  It's probably better to keep it focused in that direction, and add notifications for other events in the community, rather than what happens on your own profile.

author: TheVolta
text:
Hello UG Community and Programmers.
I noticed that this thread got a little off-topic, but is clearly where my post belongs.
I am a long-time user of the site and have seen many improvements over the years, however, there are a few *very important* implementations that have been overlooked and could easily be addressed:
1) Display Chords default fingering - the Display Chords function is great, however, from my experience, I am constantly adjusting the default chord formation and required to scroll through the many variations to find my preferred chord fingering. I find it strange that the most common fingerings are not usually 2nd or 3rd (for things like C and D), but have the user search through 4 or 5 to find them (obvious secondary barre chord fingerings). In short, it would be nice to have the site remember what chord variation the user selected. You could have this work the same way you have the Transpose function save the data, or, better yet, include a setting in the user profile where they may indicate their chord fingering preferences. This would save many people like myself a lot of time, eliminating the need to scroll through variations on each tab to find our preference.
2) Display Chords Auto-scroll - The function that displays chords above the tabulature should allow the user to decide whether the chord diagrams auto-scroll, much like the Auto-scroll controller. Ideally, the diagrams would be selectable and moveable, must like the Auto-scroll controller.
3) Global/individual chord variation - When holding your cursor over individual chords and selection a certain variation, the user should have the option of changing the fingering for the entire song (changing the Display Chord diagram and all chords accordingly), or altering just that single chord. I find myself changing chords and moving my mouse away accidentally, just to find myself having to re-select my choice variation.
4) Preset tuning chords - Currently, the user who submitted the tab specifies the tuning. Alternate tuning displays chord diagrams relative to that tuning specified. It would be nice if the interface allowed the user to select which tuning they would like the chords displayed for (e.g. Though a tab was submitted in Drop D, I would like the be able to select the chord diagrams for Standard Tuning, instead of having all of them relate to Drop D)
In short, the chord diagrams could be utilized to their full potential if programmed to behave more flexibly. They should allow presets by the user (eventually, allowing the user to select their own priority fingering in their profile settings, or otherwise), remember individual chord alterations (of less concern, but effective), but **MUST** float the chord diagrams above the tab, and move with the screen auto-scroll.
Again, I love the site, and don't mean to sound critical, but the site would make a huge stride towards perfect if these changes were implemented. I would appreciate some feedback from other members or staff if possible.
Thanks for everything!

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Suggestion 1:
Bulletins from groups.
1 -  The Admin of a profile group will have the ability to select whether Admin, Mod, or Member can send bulletins to all members of the group.
2  -  Bulletins would be created in a section of the group forum, similar to the way threads are created.
3  -  When completed, a copy of the bulletin would be available to members in an area similar to their private messages.
Alternate scheme:
Group threads and group comments would have the ability to initiate "flags" set on members' Profile Maintenance Home.  Members would be notified when any thread had been added to, in the groups they select to receive these notices from.  The flag would indicate which group the new activity occurred in.
This kind of function is important for members who belong to many groups.  It's very inconvenient to check every group for new activity.  I believe many groups grow stale prematurely because there is such a long delay between on member posting in a group and other members seeing the posting.
Suggestion 2:
UG Forum Pop-Ups.
Members would be able to select which Profile functions will initiate a Forum pop-up to alert them of group activity.  Activities such as new Profile PMs, new Profile comments, new post on Profile group thread, new blog subscription, new photo comments, etc, would each be selectable to enable initiating a forum pop-up.
The forum pop-up doesn't need to show which Profile activity triggered it, only that there was new profile activity.
As it is now, Profile messages and comments are often unnoticed for long periods of time.  Adding this feature would greatly enhance the use of the Profile pages.
Cheers,
SYK

UG Forum Pop-Ups.
Members would be able to select which Profile functions will initiate a Forum pop-up to alert them of group activity.  Activities such as new Profile PMs, new Profile comments, new post on Profile group thread, new blog subscription, new photo comments, etc, would each be selectable to enable initiating a forum pop-up.
The forum pop-up doesn't need to show which Profile activity triggered it, only that there was new profile activity.
As it is now, Profile messages and comments are often unnoticed for long periods of time.  Adding this feature would greatly enhance the use of the Profile pages.
Cheers,

author: pAmpH
text:
I personally think that 'Private' user profiles shouldn't be allowed, or better yet, remove the option to have one.
Sure it's cool and mysterious to have a private profile so that nobody can see what's on there and all that, but I think the novelty has worn off a little...
My reasons/thoughts to back this up are as follows:
* What do you people have to hide? Seriously, it's a Guitar website, not some kind of stalker information database. If the reason why you have a private profile is because you don't want people to know your age/birthday/location etc, don't put it in there and only tell people who you want to know.
* This isn't (Sorry for the pathetic example) MySpace. MySpace (as well as many other websites similar to it) have private profiles as well, and this annoys me (Personally) to a certain extent. Why bother making a profile if nobody can view it unless they be your friend? What if they don't want to?
* By the time I typed all this out I got distracted and forgot what else I was going to say, so I guess that will have to do...
But anyway, it's just a thought and I'm not having a go at anyone about it (Sorry if it sounded like I was).
Cheers.

Hey guys,
don't know if it's been posted before, but.. I was browsing the profiles today, and i managed to get an idea on how to make the whole browsing more ergonomical...
Basically, i found that it would be really cool if the MP3 player was separate from the whole site, and acting as a whole and playing the files you click on...

sounds good to me....what do you think?

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Dmitry, if you're listening ...
1  -
Thank you
for adding the
Report!
lines to the Profile functions especially to the pictures.  There have been very few people abusing the profiles, but I had seen a few that were WAY over the line.  I don't have to bother the Mods about stuff like this any more.
2  -
Thank you
for putting this whole thing together.  At first I though it would just be BS like myspace, but I love it now!
3  -
Thank you
for all your work straightening out the bugs.  A project like this is never without complications.  Some people got a little whiny about the problems that cropped up during bug fixes.  I don't think they appreciate how big the code must be and the level of interaction from one subroutine to another.  I was impressed at how quickly you eliminated some of the problems that occurred.
4  -
Thank you
for popping onto my page, just to say hi.  I don't know if you are doing that to random people, or if you picked my page for some special reason.  Either way, it made me giggle that someone as important as you, took the time to say hi to someone you don't know.
5  -
We know
bug fixes are the most important issue for now.  These requests are for whenever you have time.  One of those "it would be nice if ..." sort of things.
Getting the time on the Profile Pages, like it is on the Forums.
Ability to delete favorite tabs on our favorite pages.
Add a "quote" button to the comments window.
Pop-up window for notification of Private Messages on the new system, while browsing the Forums.
Button to subscribe to ALL of your friends' Blogs at one time.
Bulletins function added.  Within
groups
, you could create a bulletin and send it out to
all members of the group
.  On your Profile Page you could send it to all your friends.  Blogs on the Profile Page make bulletins there less important, but for Groups, bulletins would be ACE.
-OR-
Create a blog function for Groups, and allow group members to subscribe to the group blog?
Ability to see who else is viewing the group, while you're in there.
Edit or Delete comment that you make on someone else's page.
I think I've brought all the issues forward to this point in the thread.
Again. Dmitry ... thank you.

author: Carmel
text:
Ok, I wasn't sure if to post it in here or in a separate thread, but lets have a go here first, since it is more to do with the profiles.
Links to the forums on the profiles:
Like we have links to groups on our profiles, I think it would be nice if we could link to our favourite forums, by that I mean of course inside UG.
There are two ways to go about it, as I see it:
One - let us have on the side of our profiles (like the groups) a list of "favourite forums" (that you can tick on your account options) and this will also give insight to what the user is interested in and where they like to hang out on UG.
Two - have an automated post count that automatically presents in which forums the user is most active in (could be done by posts per month, in order to see the currently active users OR total posts, which then may include old users that may no longer be active but have contributed to that forum a lot) - however, this may not be possible to do, I wouldn't know.
This way you can also search for users that are highly active in certain forums and ask them questions and advice - if it's possible to add to the search options.
Sure, you can search for users' posts by forum and see how many they have in each, but I think this would be a nicer way to tie the profiles and the forums together more tightly.
Opinions?

author: smb
text: That's a great idea...I like the monthly thing. It would certainly tell you a lot about a user.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by carmel_l
Links to the forums on the profiles:
Like we have links to groups on our profiles, I think it would be nice if we could link to our favourite forums, by that I mean of course inside UG.
you can put links to your favourite forums in your "about" section now.
one advantage to your proposal is that it would be in a predictable place on all users' profiles.
another advantage: more people would do this.
Quote by carmel_l
One - let us have on the side of our profiles (like the groups) a list of "favourite forums" (that you can tick on your account options) and this will also give insight to what the user is interested in and where they like to hang out on UG.
this would be fairly easy to implement.
Quote by carmel_l
Two - have an automated post count that automatically presents in which forums the user is most active in (could be done by posts per month, in order to see the currently active users OR total posts, which then may include old users that may no longer be active but have contributed to that forum a lot) - however, this may not be possible to do, I wouldn't know.
possible, yes.  but certainly more difficult.
it would require taking stats from the forums on a regular basis.
this might cause a problem with managing resources,
by causing increased load on the forum server(s)
we already have a stripped down version of the search function
because the full version caused forum slow-downs.
care would need to be taken in the way stats were obtained
to prevent too much load at one time.
Quote by carmel_l
This way you can also search for users that are highly active in certain forums and ask them questions and advice - if it's possible to add to the search options.
this would be better served by an additional function.
(a) separate page(s) of most frequent users of each forum.
the names could be ranked according to usage.
next to each username would be the number of posts he/she has in that forum.
perhaps two entries.
one for the number of posts during the last three months
the second entry would be total posts in that users history
it still says nothing about the
quality
of posts, but does give a clue to activity.
Quote by carmel_l
Sure, you can search for users' posts by forum and see how many they have in each, but I think this would be a nicer way to tie the profiles and the forums together more tightly.
better integration of the forums and profiles is always a desired goal.
i suspect at some point the vB forum structure will have to go,
being replaced by something written by UG's own programmers.
this would leave the door wide open for new features.
but it would also be a massive project.
until then, incremental improvements like the ones you've suggested
will be difficult, but possible.

author: jjnijholt
text:
It is almost universally the case that later tabs are better than earlier tabs - not in the least becasue UG has done a great job at quality control for new submissions.
Unfortunately, older tabs will, simply as a function of time, have more ratings and so appear more legitimate.
As a moderately active tabber this is very frustrating, because new ratings are *not* easy to come by, especially if you're tabbing unpopular stuff. It would be motivational to level the playing field a bit by, for instance, discounting all ratings that are five years and older. This makes the older tabs appear less legitimate and gets more clicks to newer tabs. How do you feel about this?

author: thequadrat
text:
jjnijholt
we have a 'correction' function that lets users update and improve older tabs. All contributors are displayed on the tab page so everybody's impact is valuable and mentioned. Popular new tabs will get ratings, views and favorites quite fast but with unpopular stuff it's just a question of time.
We do not reduce any reactions and views, it has only a cumulative function. Newer tabs have the same value as the older tabs if we speak about good tabs

author: soldierkahn
text:
Hi folks, I just had an idea while i was jamming out and wanted to make it a suggestion here. I apologize if its been covered already, its my first post.
I absolutely LOVE the Official tabs you all make for us and that service is wonderful. But how about those people who have a band or a song that they are just in love with completely but since the band isnt well-known or popular, they stand no chance of getting an official tab for the song.
So I thought, what about a paid-service where if a Pro user loves a song enough and wants to learn it bad enough (or at least get the official tab made for the backing track), the user can pay a fee for the song to be included in that week's tab workload you all have? Im not sure how the fine details would work but i know I for one have at least 5 songs that I would be more than willing to pay to have an official tab made.
i wouldnt think it would impact the Pro users because the current standing practice of upvoting for the most popular tabs would stay in place, but there could also be a "que" of paid tabs that will be completed that week as well.
again, im sorry if this has already been suggested.

mandelstamdavid

author: N-D
text:
soldierkahn
Just talked about your solution with our team - it's a great idea, but it was already discussed before - one official/Pro tab costs $30~50 for us, so that's the reason why we make tabs only for popular songs. So we think ask our users to pay $50 for one song they want is too much
Anyway thank you again for your solution - and try your luck with our tab requests!
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/forumdisplay.php?f=120

author: soldierkahn
text:
N-D
no problem, i can see where you gentlemen and ladies are coming from from a business standpoint, and I would totally agree that the cost might offput potential customers if it were advertised that way.
If I could present a fair compromise?  ( i dont want it to seem like im trying to argue)
While I agree that the cost may seem a bit high for the majority of members (this works to my advantage) to want to pay for an individual Official Tab, I know that I cannot be the only member who has a song they're dying to figure out how to play (or to just have an instrumental backing track of the song to play to), but without it being popular itll stand no chance of getting voted on.
What could be done instead is, instead of advertising the cost of personally requesting an Official Tab, wait until AFTER a person becomes a Pro User (meaning theyve already subscribed to the site), and then simply offer the service (by sending new members a notification/message to the user's inbox right after the account is created) as being available if the user feels comfortable paying the $50 for the song.
If you are correct that most members would not want to pay that cost, then adding this feature wouldnt impact the UG staff's productivity level because there wouldnt be many of the requests. I can't speak for others, but I feel completely comfortable with that price per Official Tab. I think for the amount of effort it takes to create one, I think youre asking price is more than fair. I have disposable income and a fiery passion for jamming to music. I have a job that doesnt allow me to be in a band, so being able to play to these Official Tabs are the closest i can get to being back on stage. It also helps me out because it gives me chord progressions to loop playback on and practice my scales. Its way more pricey if i wanted to try and make my own backing tracks, so that $50 is a bargain.
Again, I hope that Im not coming off as argumentative, but I wouldn't hesitate dropping $200 a month on having very SPECIFIC Official Tabs to play to. Not everyone is going to be willing to pay that, but I can't be the only one who feels this way. Either way, Im still a happy customerwith the always growing bank of official tabs, but being able to have this service available if so desired would be a definitely cool feature.

author: Roc8995
text:
To be fair, those are links to the direct answers to most of your questions. Dismissive as they were, those two responses were accurate and relevant.
Hopefully those links cleared up some of the reasons why your suggestion doesn't reflect the reality of the situation. Rights to play a song and rights to publishing chords/music/tab are completely separate entities, negotiated separately. Your premise from the start was flawed. It's not impossible that some service could merge the user experience of those two entities in the future*, but that is a different approach and not at all the same thing as assuming that they're the same copyright. Spotify therefore has no publishing rights that UG can use for tabs. They could leverage them in the future, I suppose, but I don't see why they'd share with us at that point.
* This might look like (for example) an app that plays a song from Spotify while simultaneously showing the tab for that song on the screen. It would still require licensing for the play rights and the tab rights, so it's not at all what you're suggesting, but it illustrates one way that an app could use both types in the same service. The issue remains that having the rights to play a song does not also give you the right to publish the music for it.

text:
Quote by dandhjohn
Having the ability to
update the reviews for typos and corrections
would be a nice feature.  We can do that to Tabs, why not reviews?
Totally unnecessary, imo.
Tabs need to be corrected / updated.  A tab that is mostly correct is acceptable.  And if the author discovers errors and wants to make it more correct, that is possible (after the proposed corrections are reviewed by the Tab Team.
Reviews are quite different.  You're expected to KNOW what you're reviewing and do a proper job of it right from the gate.  Else wait until you do know, before submitting.
Typos in a review?  Shouldn't happen.  You should take appropriate care in proofreading your work before submission.  And (hopefully) a review with typos will be rejected.
Get it right the first time.

author: chacho.bruh
text:
So lately I've been trying to get back into the submission queue, because we all want more songs with better tabs, but I've noticed sometimes that tabs which really don't meet standards are being accepted onto the site, which helps nobody. All  we end up with is duplicates, or tabs for songs which are just plain wrong, or which are hard to read.
I don't want to name drop, but if you look at the recently approved listing in the queue, you'll see a single name on 90% of the tabs that were approved today. Often the votes are within a minute of each other, and some just should not be on the site. This leads me to believe that the person isn't really checking the tabs, playing them, making sure they match the song, and that they aren't really concerned with the quality of what's being submitted.
It's immensely frustrating when I'm in the queue, looking at a tab that doesn't really have the quality at the time to go onto the site, only to click reject, refresh the page, and discover that someone approved it with 5 points before I had time to reject it and suggest the corrections needed to make it a good tab.
I don't know if this is being done as a UG point scoring exercise, or because the person figures the more tabs on the site the better, but the end result is having lots of duplicate songs, songs which are incorrect, or tabs which are near incomprehensible on the site.
I don't even have a practicable solution, apart from maybe removing the ability of mods and such to instantly accept tabs, because very rarely does it happen when 2 or more people have to vote. I just needed to get this off my chest because it's easily one of the most frustrating things about UG for me.

author: GreatGecko
text:
mandelstamdavid
Hi, thanks for replying to my post. I frequently use this site for tabs and I love it cause it has a very large catalogue of songs.
After some research, it seems you can in fact copy and paste a tab straight into Word, but you have to change the font to Courier New. I wish that was more clearly labeled somewhere. I bet lots of people have this same problem as Word is one of the most used text editors in the world. Also, I'm not a computer programmer, but maybe there is some way when you copy/paste into Word, the font can autochange to Courier New, as that seems to fix formatting issues and other people wouldn't have the same issue in the future.
Also, I wish there was an easy click sliding mechanic that allowed you to easily move around different parts of the tab to your own liking so it would fill the white space on screen (kind of like the wrapping function in an Excel cell). Ideally, you could click and drag to rearrange where whole lines and parts of the tab would go or simply autosnap lines further down bringing them up to better fit your screen size with less empty space. Currently, reformatting the tab in a text editor is a pain because you have to copy paste each line on a six line guitar tab over and over one at a time and keep resizing how much fits on one line. Also, adding notes, especially chords is annoying on a text editor. This might require a huge site upgrade, but being able to insert chords (selected from a list or entered on a piano-like area you could click on, like in many music editors) in tab form using drag/drop methods would be amazing and a huge advance for this site. Although, I imagine it might be incredibly painful to have to reformat the existing thousands of tabs. Maybe you could add that option, but keep the old tabs and people will naturally start migrating over to the improved system. I haven't actually written any tabs on this site, so I am not fully sure how it works, but there are some that obviously should be reformatted to save space. For instance on One by Metallica (the highest rated/most popular version), there are lots of lines with only one small small stanza with plenty of space for more notes, but the author I guess decided to put a new line for each tiny like 6-8 note section. On the solo, for each line, there are a few notes that got cut off and moved to the next line when they obviously belong to the previous line. I'm sure there are lots of other examples. It took me like 2 hours in a text editor just to fix these simple things, but I wish there was an easier way. Thanks very much!

author: Amuro Jay
text:
Quote by P1ayingW1thF1re
How can you review an album less than a week after it leaks? Give it some time mang, perhaps your opinion will change
I'm not saying that just because I don't like this band, either; there is always a "honeymoon" period with these things, and once it's over a more definitive stance on the work will emerge. Yeah!
Quote by MustangMan311
Reviewing an album and then having a follow-up maybe a year later is always something I've wanted to see in a review site.
I think these quotes are pretty self-explanatory.
There's a lot of users who review albums with initial excitement and give them high scores, but a few months down the line, their opinion changes completely. I've had this happen with a lot of the early reviews I've written.
So as MustangMan311 has stated, having a follow-up review seems like a good idea. It would really give an insight to the replay value of an album over time.
I think what could be done is that a new review feature could be added where reviewers can go back to their reviews any time a year after the original publish date and under a new section labeled "afterthoughts" (or something similar) they could give an updated opinion of the album. They can discuss how their opinion has changed, if they continued to listen to it throughout the year(s), or they could even pick apart their own review.
Thoughts?

author: Amuro Jay
text:
Some people obsess over an album for more than a month or two before coming to terms with how they really feel about it. It really depends on the person.
But, you guys are right, a year is way too long. Perhaps follow-ups can be published as soon as a month or two after, but that doesn't mean everyone's gonna do it right away. Some people will wait longer, some people won't.

author: JustLikeMe
text:
First of all, every single one review shouldn't be perfect. Only best reviewers are trying to write the most helpful and fair reviews. And I can understand that, it's good. For that we have reviews' rating system (helpful or not), so the most helpful one will be on the top anyway.
And second, you shouldn't hide your first impressions of new album, don't be shy of your first emotions. Even if you'll change your attitude later, that doesn't matter. If you feel good with it right now- that's great, isn't it? Let the new listener feel great too by listening to the new music. That's what we're listening the music for, the emotions.
Also the review should be posted close to the album' release date, so everyone would get to know about it's release and will be able to discuss it in the comments.

text:
Oh just to clarify, I wasn't talking about the UG writers, I know that they put a lot of thought into their reviews. I meant more for the regular users.
And of course, it would be an optional feature. It could come in handy for gear reviews. You learn a lot more about a guitar over time than in the first week you own it.

author: NSpen1
text:
At the moment we only get a notification if someone comments on our own profile.
We need to get notifications if anyone replies to a comment we have made on someone else's profile.  If we have commented on someone else's profile and it's something that we would hope to get a reply to, we're not going to know if there is a reply unless we keep checking their profile.
And I frequently get people asking me questions on my profile because of my tab mod status and at the moment I don't feel like I can reply directly to them because they will quite likely not know I have replied and will never see it.  So I can reply on their profile, but I would much prefer to reply directly both so that question and answer are together, and so that I don't have a lot of comments on my profile that it may look like I haven't bothered to answer.
Honestly, this is something basic and obvious that should have been done from the beginning (and may well have been working like that before the 'new' profiles).

Ive been waiting for a while to see if this issue would get resolved by itself but i guess noone may have brought it up. When I am trying to find UG Official tabs for bands that are in the tuning Im in, I often get misled/misdirected.
An example of this:
Adidas by Korn
Tuning: A D G C F A D (A standard)
Say I have my 7 string out and im tuned a whole step, and I want to find songs I can learn from the list of Official tabs in the same tuning im in. I know that Korn uses this tuning, but I have no way of selecting just this tuning when trying to filter through tabs. Some will show up if i filter by "D tuning", but when you open the tab up youll see that its actually in A standard so its misleading to label it that. The closest that I could do is to filter by "A tuning" but just like with the D tuning previously, this is only going to show tabs tuned to A E A D F# B which is not the tuning that Im in so again, misleading.
I could use the "B standard" (BEADGBE) tuning as an examlpe too, because the only way i can filter by tabbs in that tuning is by using "B tuning" but again, thats B E A D F# B, not BEADGBE.
I know some may think that Im complaining about something insignificant, but its fairly significant to me. Depending on which tuning I want to play in for the day, Id love to be able to hop on here and explore other artists/songs that are in my exact tuning that I may not have heard of yet. I just wish that all tabs included the Key that its in so that I can filter by song key as well.

Okay, this is probably going to come off as me being an idiot and ranted, but at least I have reason for a ranting idiot.
I recently decided to work on submitting bass tabs for Metallica's first three albums (Cliff's days). I wanted to upload full song tabs for them and have them be correct, so I got the master bass track from each song I tabbed except for one (Whiplash, but the only thing missing are Cliff's little quirks in the song). Listening to Cliff's original bassline and tabbing them by ear (which I have been learning to play things for four years by ear), I was satisfied that I had the notes down properly and cleared up all the confusion about the bass track in the songs (assuming they were accepted). Orion and Master of Puppets were astonishingly different to even the best tabs on the stie (some of which are pretty good). However, the tabs were rejected, and I'm fairly sure the reason is that there were "enough tabs already" for the songs. In that regard, I would be understanding IF tabs like this (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/tabs/m/metallica/for_whom_the_bell_tolls_ver3_btab.htm
) and this (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/tabs/m/metallica/master_of_puppets_btab.htm

Going into that, I already said I used the master bass track to listen to and tab the song out, playing the notes on my bass to try and get the correct ones tabbed out. author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Let me start out with a disclaimer:  I'm not a major tab contributor, so I don't know everything about the process.  I've never had a tab rejected, so I don't have first-hand experience on that end.  But I do know few things about how the process is supposed to work and how it can break down.  I'll share with you, what i do know.
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
These go into the TPA (tabs pending approval)
UGers who successfully have uploaded enough tabs, have access to this area.
They vote and comment on the submitted tabs.
The Tab Moderators and Tab Master use these votes/comments to decide which tabs will be accepted.
An approved tab simply gets added to the archive.
A denied tab is not added to the archive.
An e-mail is generated that goes to the user who submitted the denied tab
This e-mail contains the reasons for denial from the comments submitted by users in the TPA
Where the system breaks down:
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
Not all tabs in the TPA get voted on / commented.
A tab without votes / comments must still be processed.
Decisions must be made quickly, because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
Tab Moderators / Tab Master often don't have time to write out the reason for denial because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
If a Tab is submitted where there are multiple versions already in existence, it is generally passed over, because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
While this might seem unfair, the fact is: most of these submissions for tabs with multiple versions are just copy/paste from other sites or some kid writing a poorly crafted tab.
Even if the tab has votes/comments, the information for denial can only be relayed to the author IF he has "receive e-mail from administrators" selected in his profile.
The Tab system on UG isn't perfect, but it does function.  Considering the heavy load on the system, it works well.  If you want to make a difference, once you have access to the TPA, become active in voting/commenting on the tab submissions.  This will greatly help with the heavy load.
Regarding pruning of extraneous tabs:
This does happen, but it's a touchy business.
Once accepted, a tab is part of UG's ranking system.
Removing a tab would change a user's ranking.
This is not something to take lightly.
It's a bit ungrateful to accept a tab, then to later say:
"Oh, we've change our minds.  No longer good enough."
Do you see the problem?
There is a certain
balance
that must be reached, between improvement in the archive and respect for previous submissions.
Regarding the specific circumstances you mentioned:
Virtually no one is likely to even look at a new version of MoP or any other extremely common song when it hits the TPA.  UG gets flooded with poor versions of those.
Please post in this thread:
WTF? Where is my tab?!?!
If your versions are indeed superior, they will get the attention they deserve from emad and/or the other Tab Mods and the Tab Master.
Does it seem like this should not have been necessary and part of the normal sequence of events?
Maybe, in a perfect world.
But with an overloaded system, one does the best one can.
Thanks in advance, for your cooperation.

author: chrislikesemail
text:
Hi Guys,
Probably already been suggested but why doesnt UG have a built in metronome for each song that can be set to the song tempo and be played on the APP?
Have i missed a way to activate a song tempo based metronome on the app for my own edited tabs, or Are you guys working on it?
I note the following workarounds aren't suitable:
- Obviosuly pro tabs have the metronome built into the song, but that's useless when making your own custom edits/ versions of tabs to play on stage and you need to quickly play a metronome to tempo of the song.
- Using the strumming pattern: Yes you can set that with a tempo and a count, but it only plays the audio on browser, iOS and Android Apps display the strumming pattern but the play icon is not visible - so you can't play strumming pattern through app to hear the tempo.
- Metronome: on iOS has a 'Preset' option where you can set a metronome tempo, then 'Add Preset' and name it to a song. But that Preset only appears on iOS (not android APP), and you have to click through to metronone and select preset to hear the tempo. too many steps when on stage.
Simplest solutioin would be to either make the strumming pattern playable on the APPs, or put a tempo button top of tabs.
Cheers,
Chris

I suggested Midi for two reasons:

Suggestions for the TPA because it really needs some work.
"Default Reasoning" for denying tabs. Most of the tabs we deny are "enough versions", "stolen tab", etc. Make it something like a checklist of common reasons, but have an "Other (specify)" option too.

"Priority approval" for trusted tabbers. text:
^ What jimmy_neutron and Deliriumbassist said is true. If we want to increase the overall quality of the reviews section, we shouldn't limit the amount of people who can submit reviews, but limit the amount of reviews that pass approval, i.e. raise the quality standards required for a review to be featured. In other words, any user should be allowed to submit reviews, but not any submitted review should be accepted.
However, I still think that limiting submissions to registered users only isn't a bad idea. An unregistered user who wants to submit an article or review can easily register in 5 minutes. The writer will consequently be credited for his/her review or article, since if he/she hadn't registered, the author will be listed as "Unregistered".
