author: ZeGuitarist
text:
^ I don't think that would work. A tab shows how a song is played on the guitar - it can be either accurate, or wrong. It will be rated accordingly, and accepted or denied accordingly.
Reviews and articles, however, are often subjective. You can't rate the "correctness" of a review, since the opinion of the reviewer may be different from someone else's. So, if we had a system like the TPA for reviews and articles as well, it would be abused massively. People would give low ratings to reviews they don't agree with, even though it may be a perfectly well written one.
At the moment, reviews and articles are checked and approved by the Russian office, and I don't believe this will change. However, some time ago, Colohue and I proposed to the UG team our plans to reform the UG Contributions forum, making it more active in reviewing previously approved submissions, effectively forming a second "barrier" for submissions, thus enhancing their quality.
Those plans have been in the freezer for some time now, but I think they can be revived if there's enough interest.
ZEDIT: Made the first move in trying to get the plans out of the muck. Hopefully we can achieve something this time.

We can slow the songs down and isolate voices, print scores, etc... 100% Kudos to the site and it's creators.  Let's appreciate what they have done for us, and understand their desire yet inability as a business model to offer MIDI files. author: allen.lee1017
text: gotta say, ive noticed over the past 10 years that taking personal time to learn music is just not something younger people do anymore, and its not something i see older people keeping up with and i hate being that guy but maybe a big part of the issue is not having accessible, ACCURATE tabs that people can easily get to AND DOWNLOAD. everyone has a computer these days but i don't see kids rushing to download tabs of their favorite pop or hip-hop tracks and start figuring out how their favorite music works like my friends and i did when we found things like gp5, tuxguitar, guitartabarchives, and early UG. why? well the only viable option today for hardly any form of written music learning is UG tabs for free, chord progressions (so interesting and fun), and Official UG tabs that can't be downloaded and can largely only be accessed through paying money. simply put, if you can't take the music you like, put it in the program you use, and be able to manipulate and understand at your own pace, then you won't have any good incentive to keep trying to learn music in general. on top of that, music is so far beyond being guitar centric that assuming everyone just wants the easy chord progression version of a track or plain text tabs is foolish, like yall do realize that a growing amount of musicians today are doing everything music related in a purely electronic form, right? Tabs in midi/gp form are ESSENTIAL, and access to them in a form where you can change and mess with them is equally as important so that learners can understand why things work how they do both in regards to the actual songs in question and the programs used as well. monetization models like the one UG uses essentially gatekeep the ability to learn, which in turn lowers its own user base and kills passion overall. over the past 2 years i stopped learning other peoples music to focus on writng my own but in all reality i know part of the reason i stopped learning other music is the fact that its such a goddamn inaccessible thing to do, and a large reason for that is UG being greedy. and really i think thats the final point. theres no reason not to give us the tools that weve been asking for other than UG being worried about their bank account instead of actually being good at providing the service the whole site is built around. rant over.

author: Till From Kenig
text:
cmoaln11
UG has deals with most of the major music publishers (Sony, Alfred, Kobalt, etc) and these publishers usually represent thousands of smaller publishers which means they have literally millions of songs in their catalogs. So it's not necessary to sign a deal with each songwriter individually. If I'm not mistaken Beatles are licensed through Sony Music and Tool is licensed through Hal-Leonard. Some of the small indie publishers are licensed through Harry Fox Agency. All that happened quite a while ago. UG almost got closed down with mxtabs and the others, and yes getting those deals was extremely complicated back in the time. Here is the only press-release I was able to find
https://digitalmediawire.com/2010/04/07/hfa-adds-web-ringtone-licensing-licenses-ultimate-guitar/
. Tabs existed in a gray area back in 2006, nowadays you can't work without a license. Again, look it up how mxtabs, olga, and others were closed more than 10 years ago.
And you're right that having downloads in the ad-supported service is a hard sell. But UG is using a freemium model, free service attracts users who convert to subscribers. And UG pays a significant share of subscription revenues as royalties. So it's not just 0.001$ from the ad shown on the website (
https://smallbusiness.chron.com/typical-cpm-74763.html)
, copyright holders also get a share of subscription revenues. Also, I don't think it makes sense to compare UG with streaming services, tab books don't make that much revenue as cd sales, besides distributing tabs requires a different set of legal rights.

author: UG Support
text:
Bigg_Bill7
thank you for raising this question in the forum. We'd like to clarify how to accurately notate the chord, typically written as
“Cmadd#11”
.
Here’s the correct and widely accepted format:
The added notes are clearly separated by parentheses, helping avoid confusion with other chord types.
According to standard chord notation practices, “add” designates an extra tone added to a basic triad, and “♯11” specifies that the eleventh is raised.
Importantly, an “add” chord does
not
imply inclusion of 7ths, 9ths, or other extensions beyond what’s specified—only what’s explicitly stated.
[h]Example[/h]
Cm(add ♯11)
= C – E♭ – G with an added F♯
This keeps the chord concise and musically precise.
We hope this clears things up! If you'd like suggestions for alternative but acceptable notations or fingerings, feel free to ask—happy to help.

author: NSpen1
text:
UG Support
Sorry, but you shouldn't be answering questions about chord names to be used on the site.
This doesn't help at all, Cm(add ♯11) is totally not something we would ever use.
For recognition on the site - parentheses in chord names are best avoided unless there's no other way to write the chord.  We do not use ♯ (or ♭) symbols.  There should never be a space in a chord name like you have after add.
The poster was only asking for a name for the chord that would be recognised on the site, I don't think he needs a theory lesson.
I've already stated that there unfortunately isn't a name for Cmadd#11 which will be recognised, keeping it as a Cm type chord.  If you think you know differently please feel free to give the name.

author: tlopez113
text:
Dear ultimate guitar team,
First off, I do not mean to insult or demonize, but rather offer my perspective. In the time since picking up guitar about four years ago, I have been using your website on my phone and desktop nearly exclusively. In my opinion, this is due to ultimate guitar becoming the decisive winner in tab reader functionality, aestetics, and most importantly, variety of content. Though maybe it has become too decisive of a winner, becoming an unavoidable super-giant of tabs, advertisements, and in app purchases along the way. On the other hand, I understand the need for a steady paycheck, as publishing sheet music from a private domain for the public must come with a hefty price (and even heftier paperwork! ) And while your feedback may sound like an enraged mob with poor reading skills, they clearly feel deceived into buying an incomplete app (pay-to-use features) with ads to boot. To make matters worse, these 'premiums' are easily found for free elsewhere. While convenience of in-app features is certainly on the table, downloading a separate app for free isn't much of a leap, especially since I already payed for ultimate guitar once. Finally, there's no rule against showing advertisements in a paid app, but it is distasteful. And it's a shame that the experience of the largest and best tab site is ruined consequently, especially for beginners.

author: UG Support
text:
tlopez113
Thanks for your feedback.
Tabs&Chords app does have Basic and Full versions.
Purchasing the Basic version of Tabs&Chords app gives you access to
1,000,000 tabs and chords&lyrics; auto scroll, transpose and offline access to favorites.
Full version unlocks access to:
1. 200,000 Pro/interactive tabs
2. Tab Tools (fit to screen, air printing, emailing tabs)
3. Guitar Tools (tuners, metronome, chord library)
4. Lessons
Please note that with the Basic version you have access to more than 1 mln tabs and offline access to favorites.
If you don't want to pay for the in-apps you do have a choice with the variety of free apps, however our very high quality tools are convinently packed in one app along with all the tabs + we provide support, while free aps' developers mainly don't give a shit
Cheers!

author: fanapathy
text:
I agree that people who have made tabs themselves are generally more qualified to rate tabs.
The issue with this is, not many people have submitted tabs. We're looking at a really low % of users having 5 tabs+. These users are also less likely to use/view tabs, because they already know how to transcribe songs themselves.
In my experience, about 0.2% of people rate tabs at all (1 in 500 views). That's already a super low ratio. If in addition only tabbers were allowed to rate, it would drop immensely. Tabs just wouldn't get rated.

author: Joshua Garcia
text:
Well, you're half way right. I do strongly believe that any user that gives a rating below 3 stars should at least be forced to give an explanation. That way, if it is some bogus reason, a tab mod can look into it and get it removed.
But as for the 5 contribution requirement part, I'm not sure how well that would work out. Obviously there's a fair share of users who will rate badly just because they didn't like it, but most of the time, users who can't tab for themselves will rate fairly based on how well they learned the song through your tab. It wouldn't be right to take that away from them. There would definitely be a decrease of tabs being rated as well. Then, knowing which tab is more reliable will become even harder for everyone.

Hi and welcome!
I'm not sure if I understand you correctly and you did not add any links to the videos and the UG chord sheet, so it's difficult to tell. But the transpose function is the correct place to adjust the chords to use a capo.
Example:
- The song you want to play is in Eb and that means "a lot of barre chords". You want to get rid of them.
- You transpose the chord sheet --3 to C
- You put the capo on the 3rd fret.
- Now playing the song in C, it will "sound" in Eb because the capo 3rd fret means every chord you play will sound three semi--tones higher.
- So you transpose and then use the capo to keep the pitch.
Dos that make sense?

author: Maitinin
text:
Hi there UG Team and Users
Let me start saying that I think the mission of this site is to spread as much correct knowledge of music as possible - and as simple and clearly as it’s possible!
Now, as an example, I was wondering why there are 38 versions of Enter Sandman; that includes 10 guitar text tabs and 9 guitar pro version!
- Who needs all these tabs? If I was to look for this song, I'd find it absolutely confusing with so many tabs to choose from. Of course I could just pick a tab rated 5 stars, but the general overview is still completely messed up. Who needs version 3-6 when they are only rated 3 stars? They'll just be standing there on the list gathering dust forever! (No personal offense to the ones that did version 3-6!
)
Wouldn't it make everything more dynamic if, let's say, tabs rated 1, 2 or 3 stars could be suggested discarded? Just as well as you can participate in approving tabs, you could also participate in discarding tabs. – How about a page similar to the approval page, where users could vote for or against a suggestion for discarding a tab? That'd be pertinent users, obviously, like users that are subscribed for Metallica-tabs, in this case, or users that have submitted Metallica-tabs for other songs.
I know this system could easily be abused and exacerbate the competition that many submitters unfortunately feel, and that's why it needs to be thought thoroughly through! (Hah, try to repeat those three words ten times
)
My vision is definitely not that each song has to have only 3 version of it, but I just want to avoid 9 similar and superfluous versions that do nothing but confusing everyone.
I think this would also have a great positive effect of creating more communication between the users that are interested in how a song is played. I think that is often missing on this site. Communication and committed discussion is the most educative thing in the world!
I know this idea generally sounds a bit controversial, so I'd really like some response to it!
Sincerely
Jon Sebastian Frederiksen, aka Maitinin

- having few versions that makes the picture very sharp, but at the same time threatens this website's future existence.
Right now this site is way over to the site of having too many versions, and I think it should balance more little towards the middle.

author: motoclangers
text:
Quote by Ian Paul Gint
Hello everybody!
It's been some time since we made actual improvements to the site and now we finally feel like we're up to it again. We've gathered a whole lot of requests, complaints and suggestions from our users (many thanks to everyone who wrote us!), thought them over and picked the most popular ones. Most of these new, projected feats are basically common sense improvements, like search options, however some of them do come from our specific user's requests (customizing tab view).
Following features are now being considered to the site:
1. Alphabetical listing of songs under the page numbers on the artist's page
Most requested feature, helps you find the right song without browsing through all the pages A to Z. Since some artists may have up to several thousand tabs, searching for a particular song tablature is at times difficult, so we decided to make it a little easier for everyone.
E.g., if you are looking for “Harvester of Sorrow” by Metallica on the artist's page
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/tabs/metallica_tabs.htm
, you'll just have to put the cursor on the page number and the pop-up box will indicate the first letter of the first and the last tab on that page (pg 8, G-I).
2. Browsing tabs by genres and difficulty
Another popular feat, designed to give our users an opportunity for prompt 	search. You will be able to jump to the list of “hard rock” or “thrash metal” tabs right from the main page, same for the difficulty level. These criteria should be applied by our users, so please don't be surprised after not finding Metallica in “surf rock”, even if it seems indisputable to you.
3. Songs search box on the artist's page
Again, designed for easier and faster search of the exact tab. If you know the exact song you are looking for, you'll just have to type its name in the search box and pick the song the drop-down list (similar to the main page).
4. Customize tab viewing options (font, size, color, bgrd)
Well, standard fonts and colors may be boring. With this option, you'll be able to customize view parameters to make the tab look exactly the way you want it to.
5. Search in favorites
Many users have hundreds of tabs in their Favorites and browsing through them sometimes is like a pain in the a**. Most probably it would be another search box, however, if you have another better idea, share it with us.
That's how the list looks like for the moment, it's not final, the feats above are yet to be tested and improved. It may take up to several months to introduce and make them work properly for you.
Now the ball is on your side. Please, leave your opinion/comment on these new feats below. Let's make ultimate-guitar.com better together!
Hi There,
I like the idea of being able to search artist tabs A-Z, it would make a lot of sense,and would enable quicker search.
Mark W

author: Lemoninfluence
text:
Quote by DroneBlues27
i posted this in the comments section of the article, but saw a moderator say it would be more likely seen here so here it is!:
Ok UG i haven't posted for a while, but I felt the need to do so for this article. I think that most of UG's overhead should be dedicated to the tabbing portion of the site. Although there are so many other qualities to this site that I love (articles, news, forums, etc.), I feel that UG's forte (pun very intended) should most definitely be tabs.
I think UG should consider the reality of the internet and the content out there that in some respects, but not all, supersedes UG's content. If you google guitar tabs, UG is the first site to pop up right on top. If you google music news or another category, for instance, UG is (sadly) not the first site. In fact, you'd have to go through probably dozens of pages to find UG. The average user will most likely click something on the first page. This is where UG can thrive. If UG can strive for perfect guitar tabs, as well as expand (as they have been with the features of UG plus) then almost undoubtedly UG can achieve a sort of guitar tab monopoly online. Let's face it though, with the economy of the world (namely the US where I'm from) in turmoil, people aren't even willing to pay $0.99 for their favorite song let alone several dollars for some of the features that UG has.
Although this strategy might be a little bold and have short term costs, I think the long term investment potential is far greater. In this age, "free is for me" is a popular slogan. If UG made more of it's features free, I think they would see an exponential increase in downloads as well as website traffic. Wherever there is dense web traffic, there is an even denser check that an advertiser is willing to write to market on a site. And although for users ads may be a pain in the ass, those who desire the service enough are willing to look past that and deal with that small inconvenience. I have a feeling, although i could be dead wrong, that UG doesn't make the majority of it's money from people paying for the ad-free version of the site. I think UG is concentrating too much on short term profits rather than long term investment. It's only a matter of time until people will find another site/service that is free and the people (sheep-le) will flock to that, which inevitably will damage UG's well-being.
Moral of my story: make stuff free, maybe not forever. just give it a shot UG and see what happens. Maybe give incentives to your employees for ways to cut corners/ improve the site. But maybe you won't even have to cut corners! if you look at how far down the comments go on some of news articles and discussions, it's unbelievable how much space is empty that could be used for ads. And the beautiful part about it for the user, is most of the time a user is able to download some sort of ad blocker to block the ads anyway.
PLEASE UG GIVE YOUR LOYAL USERS FREEEEEDDDOMMMMM AND YOU WILL EARN FREEDOM IN THE PROCESS!
UG is free. Always has been. Or at least the main features are.
The only things that are paid features are extra, luxury features such as the iphone/android app and UG plus. And they were introduced because people kept posting about how they'd willingly pay to have an ad free version of the site etc.
Advertising has always been UG's main source of revenue. And although people complain about the ads, they very rarely report any in the bad ads forum. What they do is they usually take your advice and search for some plugin that blocks the ads. Which actually harms UG as they get less revenue.
All in all, I don't know what you're trying to suggest other than 'give me free stuff'... which is already the case.

author: TheVolta
text:
Hello UG Community and Programmers.
I noticed that this thread got a little off-topic, but is clearly where my post belongs.
I am a long-time user of the site and have seen many improvements over the years, however, there are a few *very important* implementations that have been overlooked and could easily be addressed:
1) Display Chords default fingering - the Display Chords function is great, however, from my experience, I am constantly adjusting the default chord formation and required to scroll through the many variations to find my preferred chord fingering.  I find it strange that the most common fingerings are not usually 2nd or 3rd (for things like C and D), but have the user search through 4 or 5 to find them (obvious secondary barre chord fingerings).  In short, it would be nice to have the site remember what chord variation the user selected.  You could have this work the same way you have the Transpose function save the data, or, better yet, include a setting in the user profile where they may indicate their chord fingering preferences.  This would save many people like myself a lot of time, eliminating the need to scroll through variations on each tab to find our preference.
2) Display Chords Auto-scroll - The function that displays chords above the tabulature should allow the user to decide whether the chord diagrams auto-scroll, much like the Auto-scroll controller.  Ideally, the diagrams would be selectable and moveable, must like the Auto-scroll controller.
3) Global/individual chord variation - When holding your cursor over individual chords and selection a certain variation, the user should have the option of changing the fingering for the entire song (changing the Display Chord diagram and all chords accordingly), or altering just that single chord.  I find myself changing chords and moving my mouse away accidentally, just to find myself having to re-select my choice variation.
4) Preset tuning chords - Currently, the user who submitted the tab specifies the tuning.  Alternate tuning displays chord diagrams relative to that tuning specified.  It would be nice if the interface allowed the user to select which tuning they would like the chords displayed for (e.g. Though a tab was submitted in Drop D, I would like the be able to select the chord diagrams for Standard Tuning, instead of having all of them relate to Drop D)
In short, the chord diagrams could be utilized to their full potential if programmed to behave more flexibly.  They should allow presets by the user (eventually, allowing the user to select their own priority fingering in their profile settings, or otherwise), remember individual chord alterations (of less concern, but effective), but **MUST** float the chord diagrams above the tab, and move with the screen auto-scroll.
Again, I love the site, and don't mean to sound critical, but the site would make a huge stride towards perfect if these changes were implemented.  I would appreciate some feedback from other members or staff if possible.
Thanks for everything!

author: Ian Paul Gint
text:
Hello everybody!
It's been some time since we made actual improvements to the site and now we finally feel like we're up to it again. We've gathered a whole lot of requests, complaints and suggestions from our users (many thanks to everyone who wrote us!), thought them over and picked the most popular ones. Most of these new, projected feats are basically common sense improvements, like search options, however some of them do come from our specific user's requests (customizing tab view).
Following features are now being considered to the site:
1. Alphabetical listing of songs under the page numbers on the artist's page
Most requested feature, helps you find the right song without browsing through all the pages A to Z. Since some artists may have up to several thousand tabs, searching for a particular song tablature is at times difficult, so we decided to make it a little easier for everyone.
E.g., if you are looking for “Harvester of Sorrow” by Metallica on the artist's page
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/tabs/metallica_tabs.htm
, you'll just have to put the cursor on the page number and the pop-up box will indicate the first letter of the first and the last tab on that page (pg 8, G-I).
2. Browsing tabs by genres and difficulty
Another popular feat, designed to give our users an opportunity for prompt 	search. You will be able to jump to the list of “hard rock” or “thrash metal” tabs right from the main page, same for the difficulty level. These criteria should be applied by our users, so please don't be surprised after not finding Metallica in “surf rock”, even if it seems indisputable to you.
3. Songs search box on the artist's page
Again, designed for easier and faster search of the exact tab. If you know the exact song you are looking for, you'll just have to type its name in the search box and pick the song the drop-down list (similar to the main page).
4. Customize tab viewing options (font, size, color, bgrd)
Well, standard fonts and colors may be boring. With this option, you'll be able to customize view parameters to make the tab look exactly the way you want it to.
5. Search in favorites
Many users have hundreds of tabs in their Favorites and browsing through them sometimes is like a pain in the a**. Most probably it would be another search box, however, if you have another better idea, share it with us.
That's how the list looks like for the moment, it's not final, the feats above are yet to be tested and improved. It may take up to several months to introduce and make them work properly for you.
Now the ball is on your side. Please, leave your opinion/comment on these new feats below. Let's make ultimate-guitar.com better together!

author: paddyirishman
text:
I agree with the comments in the news article about cleaning up the tab library.  The fact that there are 7 mediocre versions of a tab prevents any new and possibly better tabs from getting accepted most of the time.  I know this isn't a policy but many people scanning the Approval Queue don't seem to go to much trouble comparing versions before deciding to approve/reject if they see numerous existing tabs listed.
We should be able to update/edit our own tabs directly from the tab's page rather than going through this unnecessarily long click-fest to get to the little blue U.  The same "Update Tab" link which appears on the tab when it resides in the approval queue should persist when the tab is accepted.  Likewise, managing our own tabs from within our profile page should be much more direct.  Everything about it seems messy and disorganised.
If a tab author comments on his/her own tab they shouldn't get an email notification reporting that someone posted a new comment on their tab.  A small problem but it's kinda irritating and unnecessary.
Define exactly what the "Difficulty" option is for.  Currently it seems to have two meanings.  The first is regarding how difficult the song is to play, the second is about how "complete" the tab is.  If the song is complete but extremely simple the first meaning is to be disregarded.  This makes absolutely no sense, is completely arbitrary/pointless and only serves to confuse rather than inform users searching for tabs suitable for them.  I suggest making "Difficulty" refer only to how hard the tab is to play and to introduce a new option called "Completeness" or something similar.
Add a more extensive and varied list of tunings to the tuning drop-down menu in the tab submission form.
An "Updated" icon next to a tab (or some other notifier signifying that changes have been made) would be really handy.  If a tab is updated/corrected there's currently no obvious way to know.
Give credit to the original tabbers whose work appears in the Tab Pro library, maybe even linking directly to the original Guitar Pro tab from within the Tab Pro page.  Besides being the courteous and fair thing to do it also serves a practical function - if a Tab Pro user wants to discuss the tab or suggest corrections to the author they currently aren't able to do so.  If I were paying for this service I'd expect to have more, not less, interaction with the tab authors.

author: DroneBlues27
text:
i posted this in the comments section of the article, but saw a moderator say it would be more likely seen here so here it is!:
Ok UG i haven't posted for a while, but I felt the need to do so for this article. I think that most of UG's overhead should be dedicated to the tabbing portion of the site. Although there are so many other qualities to this site that I love (articles, news, forums, etc.), I feel that UG's forte (pun very intended) should most definitely be tabs.
I think UG should consider the reality of the internet and the content out there that in some respects, but not all, supersedes UG's content. If you google guitar tabs, UG is the first site to pop up right on top. If you google music news or another category, for instance, UG is (sadly) not the first site. In fact, you'd have to go through probably dozens of pages to find UG. The average user will most likely click something on the first page. This is where UG can thrive. If UG can strive for perfect guitar tabs, as well as expand (as they have been with the features of UG plus) then almost undoubtedly UG can achieve a sort of guitar tab monopoly online. Let's face it though, with the economy of the world (namely the US where I'm from) in turmoil, people aren't even willing to pay $0.99 for their favorite song let alone several dollars for some of the features that UG has.
Although this strategy might be a little bold and have short term costs, I think the long term investment potential is far greater. In this age, "free is for me" is a popular slogan. If UG made more of it's features free, I think they would see an exponential increase in downloads as well as website traffic. Wherever there is dense web traffic, there is an even denser check that an advertiser is willing to write to market on a site. And although for users ads may be a pain in the ass, those who desire the service enough are willing to look past that and deal with that small inconvenience. I have a feeling, although i could be dead wrong, that UG doesn't make the majority of it's money from people paying for the ad-free version of the site. I think UG is concentrating too much on short term profits rather than long term investment. It's only a matter of time until people will find another site/service that is free and the people (sheep-le) will flock to that, which inevitably will damage UG's well-being.
Moral of my story: make stuff free, maybe not forever. just give it a shot UG and see what happens. Maybe give incentives to your employees for ways to cut corners/ improve the site. But maybe you won't even have to cut corners! if you look at how far down the comments go on some of news articles and discussions, it's unbelievable how much space is empty that could be used for ads. And the beautiful part about it for the user, is most of the time a user is able to download some sort of ad blocker to block the ads anyway.
PLEASE UG GIVE YOUR LOYAL USERS FREEEEEDDDOMMMMM AND YOU WILL EARN FREEDOM IN THE PROCESS!

author: RaddishRobb
text:
Hello UG Community,
I believe there should be an option to display # chords as the equivalent "flat" chords.
Example:
The key of Eb has 3 flats:      Eb,  F,    G,    Ab, Bb, C,   D
The key of D# has 9 sharps;  D#, E#, F##, G#, A#, B#, C##.
If I'm reading tabs for a song in C, and transposing to Eb,  I get a jumble of D#, F, G, G#, A#, C, D
This result I find very difficult to read and interpret relative to the key center.
Do you agree? Why or Why not?
Is there a reason why UG automatically chooses #'s and neglects b's?  (no pun intended)

author: naranjaa
text:
Hi everyone,
I'll be glad to see a "flat" feature integrated to the site and the app.
To me transposition is one the most important functionalities, I use it all the time to accompany singers.
Making it "right" in all cases is certainly complex, when you have chords out of the key, or with modulations or key changes within the song.
And a "theoretically right" transposition would lead to printing in some cases for instance Cb7 rather than B7, which is probably not what everyone wants.
Until something gets decided and implemented by UG, I made a browser extension for "all sharps to flats":
Firefox:
https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/ug-chords-to-flats/
Chrome:
https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/ug-chords-to-flats/denhegbijdfbckdmjjmjbcfdhjogadlh
When viewing a chord tab, click the "bUG" button at the right of the address bar, then the "b" (flat) button that appears, to rewrite the tab using flat chords.
I've been forking the sources provided by
NeoMvsEu
above in this thread, so thank you for starting something on this subject!
The sources are here:
https://github.com/naaraanjaa/UGChordstoFlats

Hi guys!
We have an idea to solve this "sharp/flats" problem and it based on the transpose option:
- when you transpose chords up all the chords are transposed as sharp chords;
- when you transpose chords down all the chords are transposed as flat chords;
- there will be a Reset option to return to the original author's visualization.
For example, if you want to change sharp chords to flat chords in default key you should transpose up for a semitone once and then down for a semitone once. This system gives you an opportunity to change accidentals in every key.
What do you think?

author: sakiwioz
text:
As a MIDI sequencer/user of a few decades and many years of creating sound fonts, I turned to Guitar Pro for a more authentic guitar sound albeit the rest still sounds better with even the old GM soundbank. GP7 comes out and allows selecting the track to be either RSE or MIDI. Great except the latency adjustment goes the wrong way for me.
That aside, I still find it easier to use various controllers in MIDI, guitar expression is easily handled with the old pitch wheel and more control over everything really. Don't even let me go near key pressure and after touch responses.
So the question is, why do I create Guitar Pro files for UG when the player basically supports and uses MIDI? Why don't I just upload the MIDI. There are hundreds of free MIDI programs which now also have all those wonderful plugins and members would probably find them easier and more beneficial.
Yes it's a guitar site, but how many people would like to play along to an arrangement where THEY play the guitar. It's the whole reason I provide multi track GP's, so users can mute whatever track they want. Yes, the UG player does the same but it sounds shit to say the least and the official's even with backing track enabled sounds like you're in a tunnel.
A visual representation of bends, hammers etc can be obtained from the UG player which I'm sure can interpret controller events.
On another point ... HOW can you represent bars in chord sheets or is timing and chord placement not that important when playing?
The same for TABS, no indication on note lengths, tempo and its claimed this site is for learning ... what?
Thanks for reading my rant and I'll continue to contribute.

So the question is, why do I create Guitar Pro files for UG when the player basically supports and uses MIDI? Why don't I just upload the MIDI. There are hundreds of free MIDI programs which now also have all those wonderful plugins and members would probably find them easier and more beneficial.

author: sakiwioz
text:
Koenigtiamat
In regard to chord sheet s(chords) , I use songsheet generator (chordpro to put the chords in brackets) as I can place comments and more importantly, indicate where the bars are. I find it useful for songs by Dire Straits etc as when a string of chords are written in a row (into's and instrumentals), there is no way of knowing how many bars it's over and where the chord changes are unless you know the song well  which is catch 22 as you're trying to learn the song.
Actual TABS (not the generic term used in UG for all submissions) are mostly written in riff style. Tabbing originally was written more in rhythmic style but got "butchered" in time and now we have a whole bunch of dashes that mean nothing.

author: sakiwioz
text:
Koenigtiamat
My font banks can range from 1 - 381 instruments (30k to 1Gb), however large I want to make them. I have actually grouped mine into instrument types and favourites. Granted, like most, I have gleaned off the internet and modified but in a number of instances I have created from scratch (good 'ol Vienna). I use the standard (I think Roland) GM soundbank if I'm going to share or for pads and synths.
I would definitely co-operate in font creation/improvement albeit I'd need to reacquaint myself again.
I use another program as well, but not much, I think it is SF Arranger (under correction on that).
I wish GP could translate controllers better, even something basic like volume and filtered selection.

author: NSpen1
text:
sakiwioz
You can indicate timing both in chord sheets and tabs, it just depends how much the individual author can be bothered tbh.
Here's an example of a chord sheet that I just formatted the instrumental parts on :
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/metallica/whiskey_in_the_jar_chords_1148352
or
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/dont_cry_chords_337150
(chords are of varying lengths, from a whole bar down to just an eighth note)
For tabs, you get a wide range, from the worst which are written with no rhythmic information at all, numbers just in a line all spaced the same, to exports from guitar pro and power tab files, which to my mind have too much information and look cluttered.  When I write tabs I always try to arrange them in bars and spaced to show the timing as well as possible given the limitations of the format.

author: sakiwioz
text:
NSpen1
Hi, thanks for the examples. I have been trying to do using a "|" (pipe) character to denote bars. It is how I do it with SongSheet Generator. I have tried to do the same and did a quick check before this response, but still have the same issue :-
3.3.B. Extra symbols
:
Please remove extra symbols from chord lines, e.g. |
I don't create tabs (riffs) as I am useless at lead (can't play by ear - purely notional sheet reader), but rely on submissions to use in GP's which is quicker most times even with my limited ability.
I see what the issue is ... If there is no chord played in the bars on a line i.e. the same chord is used over a number of bars, it's spits the dummy!

author: NSpen1
text:
sakiwioz
Well, you can ignore Automagic in some situations, it doesn't have that much intelligence
Yes, the 'pipe' character, | , is exactly what I'm using.  You're not supposed to use those in chord lines which are above lyrics because the alignment of the chords with the lyrics gives you the timing and arguably it looks a bit messy.  So that's why you get "Please remove ..." coming up, but it's fine to use for instrumental parts.
If you have a chord repeating for a number of bars, instead of putting the chord each time, you can use the % symbol.

author: thetobster500
text:
I've been playing guitar by chords for about 5 years now and have tried a few times to learn keys better, but it's hard to do that if you can always just follow chords by their names. I'd really like an option to show chords as roman numerals or Nashville numbers, that would help to push me to learn keys and progressions better and get a feeling for the harmonies for certain progressions rather than just knowing the chord names. It would also make transposing much easier and be way better for playing in open tunings, as for example in open D i think of the chords by their placement on the neck rather than the name. It's harder to think in terms of progression in standard though, which is why i think it could help people learn as well. I know there was a different thread asking for this, but that one is a year old and closed, so i'd like to revisit the idea.
It should just be an option to turn on or off, i think since you offer a lot of non standard tunings and chord variations the argument of it being too complicated for beginners doesn't really hold any water.

author: jamesmickanen
text:
Has UG ever given review authors a "save as draft" feature? I think this would be a benefit to users, especially if the current outline of questions for each section is used as a template (features, sound, durability, etc). Personally, I usually copy and paste the questions from each section on to a word document as then address all the applicable questions as I write a rough draft of my review. When I am done I go to UG and copy and paste my responses into each section. I don't think I have ever sat down and wrote an entire review in one sitting while on the "submit a review" page. Some of my opinions form faster than others. Other times I need the gear I am reviewing in my hands to describe its characteristics.
Maybe I am just lazy, but I think adding a draft option to reviews would free up some of the hassle of copy and pasting from a word document to the website. I'm broke, ok. I admit it. I do not always have Wi-fi available. And there have been times where I have had a review saved on google docs and up to date on one device but unable to access and continue to edit my draft on another device. I imagine a simple template with the review questions/guidelines for each section. A "save" and "edit" button for creating drafts. As well as a submit button for what else but submit.  That should streamline the process. My process at least.

author: 4TonyG4
text:
I've read the article in the support section, and I'm aware that this is a work in progress. I'm posting here to bump the thread and make sure it's still a priority.
I think it would be best to put it under the account settings part. There is also a separate profile name. There's technically a separate forum name too I think. While I'm most interested in being able change my name, this split personalty profile also presents a problem. Not only is it possible to misidentify someone if they used separate names or nicknames for different ones, but people can exploit it to be intentionally misleading, or potentially even impersonate someone. Therefore I'm also interested in the way this feature is implemented, hoping that it will improve site usability and security.
I think the best option is to just have 2 names. Besides the username, you could have a display name, which the user would set either on the settings or profile page.
This would allow for 3 useful implementations. 1) It would allow people to stylize their names. Many username systems have character type or other limits, which would prevent some artists from properly displaying their names. Lots of modern artist are getting 'creative' with their names. I'm going to use a fictional artist for the examples. There's this new up-and-coming industrial and EDM artist who wants to upload the guitar tabs to his songs. His name is LiveCat, but he's stylized it Ly\/3cA+. There's lot of symbols in that which a lot of systems might not accept in the username entry form. A display name would allow them to stylize the profile without messing with security and encryption. This could work for some other odd naming conventions as well.
2. It would allow people competing for the same name to show the same profile name, even if they don't get the username, Lets say Ly\/3cA+ (LC for short) goes to sign up, and his stylized name doesn't work. He puts in the regular Arabic symbols, only to find out that Lyv3Cat has already been taken. So he sets his username to LiveCat, but then is able to set is display name to be Ly\/3cA+, and post under the name he wants. I imagine this will likely be the most common use case. Generic names followed by random characters like TheRaven69y420 could still show up as just The Raven, if they wanted.
3. The last one is similar in nature, though more focused to professional musicians (the previous two applied to everyone). Many of us have LLCs set up for our solo or band page, often separate ones for each project. A lot of these companies are the same name as the band, but many aren't. So while LC wouldn't want it to say Lyv3Cat LLC on his profile, it would be even worse if his company were something like Industrial Beats Unlimited LLC. Usually, in direct business dealings, the entity will sign up with the full LLC name (especially if the account is set up by a manager), and the modifying the appearance to the profile to suit the specific brand. A display name would make this easy to do.
The forum should automatically use the username if it's not hidden or the display name if it is. The username would be the same as now (except with the ability to change it, probably on a cooldown).
I'm aware that I can make a new account and then get this one transferred over there, but I still want it linked to this email address. I am aware that I can change the email, but that's a lot of shuffling that I don't feel is worth the effort. Plus, I still want my kinda OG UG join date. So I'm going to just bide my time for now, until I can change it, and occasionally poke you in that direction.
Though I've been a member for over 20 years, I've really only ever looked up tabs. This year, I'm 100% refocusing on music. Not only will I be playing the tabs more, so more frequently providing feedback, but I will also be tabbing other songs, as well as my own, once they're published. I also really like the new content options, and will be leaning into those heavily. I plan to check out UG Sing as soon as I finish this post. Naturally, posting more content on the site, I'm going to want to make sure my username better reflects my brand, and doesn't doxx me at all. I'm very much looking forward to the implementation of this feature.

author: NSpen1
text:
thequadrat
It's really not true.  Instruments are tuned according to intervals, guitar standard tuning is in perfect fourths with the exception of the one major third, violins in perfect 5ths, etc.
And B-Gb-B-E-Ab-Db is horrible to look at, for the same reasons a piece of music with those letters together is.  Those pitches named as they are do not go together, there are no flat keys with B and E.  It's as if you were to write a tab in the key of B major and use Gb instead of F# or Abm instead of G#m, it's just absurd.
I actually can't believe we are having this conversation again.  I'll try to dig up the previous one so hopefully we don't have to keep going round in circles.
Oh, and this
Quote by thequadrat
It also easier to read it as DGCFAD with flats.
No, DGCFAD with flats is Db Gb Cb Fb Ab Db, exactly what I put, not D♭-G♭-B-E-A♭-D♭.  The relationships between the notes stay the same, exactly as they do when transposing keys, if you do it right.  Either all the accidentals change or all the letters change, not a mixture of the two.
And no need to put Cb or Fb or use a bodged together tuning when C# F# B E G# C# makes perfect sense.

author: JazzDeath

Hey, I don't know if this is the proper place for this but I imagine it is.
Many of the regular visitors and contributors in the T&C forum have expressed their desire for the sub-forum to be better moderated as to prevent;
- People offering C4C without actually returning the favor
(for those who do not frequent this forum, it entails giving a critique back for getting a critique on your piece)
- Excessive flaming and trolling in other people's threads
(Useless posts, flaming the writer or his genre without any true reason, completely off topic discussions with no relevance to the actual topic)

(which brings new pieces out of the front page and hinders other people's chances of exposure)
- Submission of pieces which are unfinished without clearly stating it in the post

- Copying other people's works and taking credit for it

I'd gladly take up the responsibility of being moderator of these forums, and a few others have also stated their interest in doing so; I believe I've shown myself to be very objective amongst other people who frequently access the forum and I use it often enough to be aware of what's going on. author: huevos
text:
I concur with JD.
If one of the 3 of us gets nominated for modship, the T&C (sub) forums would be a much more efficient place for sharing music.
While I do take a more elitist view on the issue (raising the needs of the serious contributors above those of the casual mass), it is because I want an incentive based program where those that work hard on their pieces will reap the rewards of being a more productive member of the boards (circular logic is circular).
To accomplish this, I would allow leniency of the rules for contributors that are trustworthy, in terms of how quickly and constructively they criticize the works of others.
Once it's established that certain users fall under this criteria, I would hope that others would aspire to becoming more productive as well.
Of course, this is a far too Utopian view on the matter. Plus, it's probably not enough incentive to just be "a good person" for the sake of being good.
Ultimately, I would like a forum with users that streamline how they present their works, but with a broad diversity from one another when it comes to the actual work they are presenting.

author: fanapathy
text:
Hi,
This is written with GuitarPro tabs in mind, as I do not know how the procedures are with ASCII based tabs.
Currently, updating an already approved tab requires another approval.
Apparently sometimes these updates do not go through - I'm guessing they either get rejected by accident or somehow lost in the system. Additionally, these approvals may take a long time although they are usually updated within a couple of days.
This results in extended waiting time, more users will get an incorrect version, besides it probably costs resources that could otherwise go towards quality control of new tabs.
If a tabber discovers significant mistakes in his/her tab, he wants it corrected/updated right away to both prevent users from viewing a flawed tab and to avoid getting a bad rating based on that.
I can understand there are probably good reasons for this policy, such as if someone turns their tab into an advertisement or provides bad links within their tab - or if they change the tab to another song to promote their band, etc.
Ensuring Tab Pro compatibility might be another reason.
There's already a "Report bad tab" feature that users can click if a tab is inappropriate.
I have heard about a "Trusted tabber" status one can gain on UG, however that it requires some 50+ tabs plus a good average rating. I'm not sure which privileges it grants or if it's even relevant to tab submissions - regardless very few contributors will gain such a thing.
Therefore, I suggest implementing instant updates of tabs. If requirements are needed, they may be based on date of registration, average rating or total number of approved tabs.

author: killergege
text:
Hi !
I have a suggestion for a little improvement of the "submit your tab" screen.
I had a problem with a tab I submitted.
I worked on a song with a tab downloaded from UG. While working I noticed that there are some mistakes (measures too copy-pasted, riff played too many times...). Though that tab was nicely rated.
So I decided to correct the tab and upload it.
As there were already several tabs for that song, my contribution has been rejected. But after explaining what has been improved and why mine was better than the existing one, I managed to have the tab approved.
So here is my point :
I think there should be a new field in the "Submit your tab" screen that allows the user to explain what is different from the other existing tab, why its contribution should be approved.
Why ?
- I guess that often the tab submitted are based on the existing tabs, but with some improvements, so it would help the approbators to know what has changed.
- I like to follow the approval queue and check the tab of the bands I like. But it is often hard and take some time to compare the submitted tab to the existing just to try to find the differences. Most approvers will see that a lot of other version exist, without checking if the new one is better (and my experience shows that even nice ratings doesn't mean it's not improvable).
- It may force the user to think "what does my version add to the existing ones".
- There may be less people complaining that their tab has been rejected because they had a chance to explain their intent and the rejection can be justified by the approbator based on that information
I didn't find that suggestion in this forum, I hope it is not redundant.
Thanks for reading.

author: AllJudasPriest
text:
Quote by killergege
I may be a little radical but I repeat :
what I expect from UG is to provide correct tabs.
Well that might be your biggest mistake right there. Unless the song is your own or you were in the recording process to personally witness the recording, you are unable to submit an
accurate
or
correct
transcription.
All transcriptions are 100% subjective, which means no transcription can ever be accurate. Even if the notes sound completely correct to your ears, that does not mean the transcription is accurate. Because music is idiosyncratic, it is impossible to know if how you play it is the way it is played.
You might consider this splitting hairs and in one way you would be correct. However, due to the fact that every single transcription, including those found in professional songbooks, are centered around interpretation, then it is not just impossible but a tad bit arrogant to say your transcription is
accurate
or
correct
.
Besides, since you value UG so much in terms of getting transcriptions up, then stop wasting time in doing this and actually transcribe songs that have no transcriptions to them.
Who cares if X song with 17 versions is accurate enough?
Why not just submit X song with 0 versions so the database can grow accordingly.

author: Martin Scott
text:
What's the point in there being a language filter? "fück" (without the umlaut) becomes "****", "cünt" (without the umlaut) becomes "****", etc. We still know that "****" is a swear-word, and most of the time, can work out exactly what swear word it was, or at the least narrow it down to two or three. Lately I've just been asterisking one letter when I wanted to swear. But I post on a few forums, and none of them have a language filter, and are
much
better off for it. I don't believe that removing the language filter would be giving everyone a "license to swear" or anything like that. Other language filter-less forums I post on don't have any higher frequency of swearing than these forums do. I think if we're mature about this, we can admit to ourselves and to everyone else that the language filter accomplishes
nothing
but making the forums look stupid when people swear. It can also be frustrating when talking about certain bands, films, books, etc, which have swear words in the title.
I don't expect anything to actually be done about this (I don't think I've ever seen a moderator on UG the entire time I've been a member), but I would like to suggest removing the language filter. It's utter nonsense, and people still swear, and other people still 'read' the swear words, and see them as swear words. If I post "That guitar is rough as ****", 99% of people read the "****" as "fück", with the remaining 1% reading it as "shít" (yeah, I plucked these statistics out of thin air). Even my 8 year old nephew would correctly identify it as "fück", and he
never
swears (his mother does a lot, haha). I must ask- If my 8 year old nephew can immediately see straight through the censorship on UG and correctly identify the original word, then surely the censorship itself is completely irrelevant, pointless, and nullified? The average age here is pretty damn high compared to the other forums I post at which have no language filters, so I think it's time to stop treating us all like babies.
Who ****ing agrees with me?

author: mullet_318
text:
wk010203041
Not sure if you ever got this figured out, but for an X its just a muted string.  I would just lift my finger a bit so it 'thuds' but doesnt ring out (and is not fretted).  If its over two strings then just rest your finger(s) over those two strings.  If its X X X in a row then you just play it 3 times.
Alternately you can essentially palm mute (moving your palm from behind the bridge to rest over the strings, thus muting them from ringing out when you hit the string) but again not fret anything for a thud sound.  This is not to be confused with actual palm muting (typically noted by a PM................. over a barre or what have you, which is the same muting style as option2 but on a fretted note, so that it sounds like a dead 7 for instance rather than a dead open or 0).
So for something like G to an A
-  -  -
-  -  -
-  -  -
5 X  7
5 X  7
3 X  5
you would be playing the fretted notes/chord, and just lift your fret hand up so nothing is fretted but still covering those strings to get a muted sound.  A lot of songs especially easier power chord songs will use this for a transition so your not really lifting off the strings when you move but continue to play through the switch to another chord/position.
Hope that makes sense.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Hi Benji!
Quote by Benjibum
Maybe a review panel???
Are UG big enough yet to have "sample" guitars sent in to test and review, like guitar magazines?
You should totally write to all the guitar companies and ask =]
This isn't a bad idea, but I doubt the logistics could be worked out to make it happen.
1  -  You'd need reviewers with CREDENTIALS and name recognition to make this attractive enough for companies to want to send in samples.
2  -  You'd need to get these guitars around to the different members of the panel.  I doubt they'd all live in the same city.
3  -  You'd need an incentive for these major players to bother writing about the guitars.  Do they get to keep a few of the guitars?  Do they get paid?
UG probably has enough exposure and viewers, but without name players participating, I doubt this will have legs.
Quote by Benjibum
Im not sure if anything CAN be done about it, just thought i'd bring it up
Something CAN be done, even in the absence of a review panel.  But each reader has to do that for himself.  It's called
filtering
.  Does the review sound like it was written by a 14 year old fanboy?  Of course that Squire Affinity Strat or Epi LB Special II sounds like a world-champion.  For that matter any review that is 100% positive should be taken with some scrutiny.
No guitar is perfect.  But if you read the review and can determine where this guitar's strengths and weakness lie, you can get an idea whether it's worth considering for your particular needs.  And reviews can NEVER take the place of auditioning a guitar in person.  Even if it's of excellent build quality, it might not fit your personal tastes.
Quote by 601210
Reviews are always, always prone to bias no matter where you go.
Bingo!

After reading the first sentence on this page, would a reasonable person accept that this is an example of a song that officially has two different titles? author: maxpowweer
text: I have personally, submitted about 27 guitar and bass tabs in the past couple of years using UG, but there's one thing that annoys me. It when people use the tab, and don't leave any kind of feed back! I'm not a glory seeker, but I simple want to know if the tab was any good! I have had hundreds of people looking at my tabs, and yet I'll get one, maybe two people raring it. It's especially annoying when people give it 3/5 for example,  what was wrong? Is it asking a lot for people to leave a comment about where I went wrong or how it could be improved? If they were able to rate it, they must have been logged on and able to leave a comment. Does anyone else feel the same? Like I say, I'm not seeking praise, and glory, but an indication of the accuracy of it.

You have to realize rating/leaving feedback requires registering with UG. And hardly anyone likes to go through the trouble of registering
just

As for badly rated tabs, I believe they are looking into a method where users must leave a comment before rating a tab below 3 or 2 stars.

author: waldinator
text:
It seems like the general agreement for writing chords, is just write them one after another. Ignoring the fact if it's played 1 beat, 2 beats or 1 bar etc.
That means, that you can never just play the chords correctly, if you didn't hear the song before. So a friend says: "hey, can you play the song ... on guitar?" - "Sure, I don't know the song, but I can just google the chords and play it
BUT we have to listen to the original Song before, because it's never written correctly in UG, so I have to guess the length of the chords and remember that instantly" :/
So pleeeeease, let's make an agreement how we write them. Sure, most Chords are 1 Bar or half Bar. So you could write (Riptide
Am G C C when you just repeat the C for another half Bar. But it's getting complicated when you have a lot of them.
So my suggestion: just use ~ for playing it again: Am G C ~
or using ( ) to play it half long as usual eg: (Am G) C
So you can write in the beginning if the chords are played full bar -> (Am G) C  or half bar  Am G C ~
The brakets makes sence for example for this chord progression:
Am Em F (C G) you can write in the beginning: "Chord-Length Full Bar" and even the speed "120 Bpm" and everybody can play it instantly. could be so easy
So we need an addition to the "Chords formatting rules" otherwise you get the errors to your contributed tab:
3.3.B. Extra symbols
:
Please remove extra symbols from chord lines, e.g. ( ) ~
then it's also possible to finally put lyrics in a good structure. e.g. one line in 1, 2 or 4 bars. Sometimes a chord is changing before the lyric line finished, so I like to mark the place with a "v" where the chord would be. So you could write this riptide line also like this (only as example, it makes more sence in other songs):
Am       G                        C         ~                  v
I love you when you're singing that song, and I got a lump in my throat,
Am        G                       C        ~
   'cause you're gonna sing the words wrong
much better than this (ver 5), right? :O
Em          D                     G
I love you when you're singing that song and
                    Em
I got a lump in my throat cause
    D                   G
You're gonna sing the words wrong

Don't need for this special, if it's to complicated.

But PLEEEASE add the length for the chords! thx

author: andrewtc4
text:
Right now, UG's web interface uses a slider to control playback tempo from 10% to 150%. This is really hard to use, not only because it's generally hard to get to a precise value, but because sometimes, in my experience at least, the mouse control sticks, causing the slider control to be grabbed inadvertently until the mouse is clicked again. This causes unwanted tempo changes if I accidentally bump my mouse while the playback is going.
To counter this, I suggest making the tempo control a spinbox.  The min and max values can stay the same, but a spinbox would make getting precise tempo a snap.

author: Colohue
text:
It would be a useful addition if, as an example, one week we had a collection of bands from the metal forum, the next pop, punk and ska and so on. However, speaking from personal experience, I predict that what will actually happen will be this.
There will be a ton of articles on relatively unknown to completely unknown metal bands. While this is a good thing, some poor person will say 'they sound sort of like Metallica crossed with Iron Maiden' in the comments. Five minutes later one hundred users will post a comment similar to this: '(profanity profanity profanity) you (profanity). Nobody's better than (Metallica/Iron Maiden).' This is not altogether a bad thing. In fact, I readily support the idea because it will give me more people that I may punish..
For a while there will be no new articles while other areas consider what they might write about. Then, a couple of weeks later, somebody who frequents the 'Nu Metal' section will write an article on unknown Nu Metal bands that they think a Nu Metal fan might listen to. Fifteen minutes later, I, or one of my colleagues, will wander into this article only to discover a thousand and one posts saying: 'listen to some real metal, (homosexual slandour).' Again, I readily support this too for the same reason as above.
Now, I find it quite likely that we'll have a lot more from the metal selection than anywhere else due to the fact that a lot more people frequent the metal forum. This isn't a problem. We will however, have little to nothing from certain unpopular areas.
Then we have the issue with the writers and, more importantly, the wannabe writers. First, people will be undecided as to who should submit the work, as several people are likely to have worked on it. Secondly, people are likely to dispute which bands should be featured. This leads to one of two things:
1, Multiple articles on several bands, many of which contain differing opinions on one band in question.
2, A million articles on each seperate band, also containing rebuttal articles from other users of a continually decreasing quality.
Honestly, I think this is a marvellous idea. My opinion is thus:
Plan it
. Make a group for this project, give it a name, select a few writers and a few lead writers, then get planning. You'll need people on board that regularly post in all B&A areas, as well as people to submit the articles. Also, at the end of each article, you should give gratitudes to all the people who worked on each piece. Those who work the hardest should have the rights to the next submission.
All in all, I'd love to see this happen. I think that you might be asking a bit much if you expect it to be on the front page every time, but a running feature is far more likely, especially if they have a uniform title, a regular schedule, and are submitted by several different people.
One last piece of advice. To ensure any help is given and to maintain a persistently capable quality, please be sure to use the UG Contribution forum. This way the regulars there can add their thoughts, opinions, and help you keep each piece at a style worthy of the front page.
Thank you for your time,
Tom Colohue

author: webbtje
text:
I'll address the helpful wall of text in stages
I hadn't really thought of the fact that some of the subforums are a lot less popular than others. Nu-metal is quite full of tumbleweed these days, and there probably aren't any regular contributors in there, and for that matter 'unknown' and 'nu-metal' are pretty oxymoronic. But that's kind of my point - even if it's a small nu-metal article, with 5 posters each, it'll be a change from Korn, and it'll open the boundaries a bit.
Then we have the issue with the writers and, more importantly, the wannabe writers. First, people will be undecided as to who should submit the work, as several people are likely to have worked on it.
True. I suggest that for each forum that's willing to take part (hopefully as many as possible), there should be a general consensus on who wants to take what bands. First come first served might sound harsh, but it would stop bickering over bands and artists. It's quite clear that not everything could be printed, else 42 people would do an article on Ne Obliviscaris within 5 minutes (no offense y'all).
Make a group for this project, give it a name, select a few writers and a few lead writers, then get planning.
My idea is to have it self-contained within each forum. We now have a thread for this in t'metal forum, I suggest the others that want to take part do the same, post their paragraph for the article coming up so everyone can OK them and suggest any improvements, info which has been left out, etc etc.

Quote by Colohue

The list goes on and on. The point is, in truth, pointless. As Nick said above, Riffs and Recordings is your friend. You'll get everything you need there. Also, 34 out of 1,200,000 really isn't that many.
I disagree with this point, electronica is a VERY broad term covering just about as many genres and artists as, say, rock, if not more genres. The production techniques are completely different from the genres you mentioned, which are all based on conventional instruments and therefore have (more or less) the same production techniques, save maybe the types of amps & other gear. If people were arguing for, say, an IDM forum, or a hard trance forum, or dubstep, or whatever, I'd be inclined to agree with you, but electronica covers so many different types of music that is, at this point, not covered by any of the forums.
Also, the electronic album thread is maybe 2 days old, 34 different users (and about 40 submissions so far) is quite a lot given the time the thread's been up. A lot more have expressed interest in creating songs for the album, all they need is time. It's unfair to consider that number to represent the population of UG that's passionate about electronic music and want to discuss it.

author: WugtheBug
text:
As far as I can tell by briefly looking at Tomplay, it appears they basically just play actual recorded song audio in the background while scrolling through sheet music.
Honestly I would say from a music teachers perspective, this should be worse since the music doesn't actually line up quite right with what is being played, whereas midi-based interactive sheet music, like on UG, don't sound quite as good but don't have that problem that Tomplay has. You could emulate Tomplay for free on UG just by listening to the actual song while playing along to the sheet music.

author: pat1984v
text:
I'd like to propose a new feature for Ultimate Guitar that allows users to adjust tabs based on their guitar's tuning.
Why This Feature?
Many guitarists play in various tunings. While it's ideal to use a song's original tuning, it's not always practical. This feature would allow users to easily play a piece in a different tuning without recalculating the tab, which can be a mental challenge sometimes.
Examples:
A power chord in E standard tuning (EADGBE) could be easily adapted for Drop D (DADGBE).
Any song in in a lower tuning (i.e. Drop C) could be played in a higher tuning (Drop D).
More specific scenario, the "Lead Guitar" part of "Heavy Is The Crown" (originally in AEADGB) is playable in standard tuning.
And so forth...
This feature could be integrated into the tab viewer, allowing users to:
Select their current guitar tuning.
Select the desired tuning for the tab.
The tab would then automatically update in real-time to reflect the new fret numbers and string positions.

author: pmalavi
text:
I’ve noticed that the transpose feature simply replaces the original chord with a new transposed chord without taking into account the number of characters used to represent either chord. This can lead to alignment problems as flats and sharps automatically pop up or get removed. For example, in Ed Sheeran’s Shape of You (
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/e/ed_sheeran/shape_of_you_crd.htm),
the first line in the original (no capo) is:
....C#m.................F#m
The club isn't the best place to find a lover
However, when transposed down -4 (capo 4th fret) for easier chords, the second chord (Dm) becomes misaligned:
....Am.................Dm
The club isn't the best place to find a lover
This is because the original C#m has 3 characters but when transposed, that becomes 2 characters (Am) and the remainder of the line shifts to the left.
REQUEST: Can the transpose algorithm be modified to detect the number of characters in an original chord then add or takeaway spaces around the new transposed chord so the same number of characters is maintained? This would help maintain chord alignment throughout a song. In the above example, the C#m would be replaced with “Am ” (note the single space after the Am). Three characters then replace three characters to give the correct alignment:
....Am..................Dm
The club isn't the best place to find a lover
It may not sound like a big deal but accurate chord alignment over lyrics really improves the playability of a song. The above is a simple example but I’ve seen several instances where the transpose feature can dramatically alter alignment and hurt the playability of a tab.

author: paddyirishman
text:
I've considered tabbing my ASCII tabs in such a way that they will spread across printed pages evenly, without staves of tab being split in two, to make the tabs more "functional" for users when they're working from the printed version.  It then occurred to me that it'd make more sense and would be infinitely less time consuming for tab sites themselves to do this.  If the site could detect when blocks of text or dashes are grouped in tight paragraphs and make sure they aren't split across the pages (by simply shifting them down until they're beyond the end of the page) this would solve the problem.  Obviously it'd also be good to have this as an option rather than a policy and should only apply to the printer-friendly view, with a preview page showing the printer-friendly version with visible page breaks for the user to inspect.  The possibility of manual adjustment at this stage would make the feature even better.
Cheers!

What UG is doing is providing a means of display for it's members.

author: Steve Plod
text:
Hey guys! I've noticed in the electric guitar forums, people often start threads asking about what guitar they should buy. In many cases, they aren't clear on what they want, and there can be headaches and a lot of time wasted in trying to find what the person wants/needs in a guitar.
I think we should have a standard "FAQ", so that when someone asks the question, "what guitar should I buy", he or she copies the following FAQ and answers the questions.
This would save a lot of time, and the guitar pros on the forum will get used to seeing this standardized method quickly and be able to answer questions accurately and helpfully.
So the following is an example of what I think is a good layout:
START COPY
==========
1) What is your budget? If possible, in your own currency AND U.S. Dollars.
2) What style of music will you play on the guitar?
3) Are there any brands that catch your fancy, or that you really don't like?
4) What body style of guitar do you like?
5) Do you have access to a guitar store, so that you can easily try multiple guitars?
6) When do you plan on buying a guitar?
7) Do you plan on buying your guitar:
a. From a store
b. From the internet (eg. Musician's Friend)
c. Used (includes Ebay)
d. Other (please state)
6) Please state any additional features you need. It's also helpful if you can indicate how experienced you are with guitars. If you're a n00b and don't know how to answer some questions, just say so!
==========
END COPY
So what do you think?

author: Peter Arens
text:
Hi all,
there seems to be much confusion about the right direction of the arrows in the strumming pattern.
Basically the arrow up shows the movement from lower to higher notes when you stroke down from E to e'
and the arrow up shows the movement from the higher to the lower notes when you stroke up from e' to E.
What matters is what you hear, and not, what you see!
I think, that the right direction of the arrows should be more explained in the "Tablature Guide"
and on the page "Submit new tab" page.
On the latter you see "Strumming Pattern" and "use".
Here you could explain the arrows (up and down) more detailed:
for strokes, you could say downstrokes and upstrokes.
Kind regards

author: NSpen1
text:
Peter Arens
No, you have that the wrong way round.  A down arrow is from lower to higher notes when you stroke down from E to e, an up arrow is from higher to lower notes when you stroke up from e to E.  It's the physical direction that you strum.
It is in the Tab Guide, 1.9 Strumming Patterns
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/help/rubric
Hopefully that's clear enough?

author: Peter Arens
text:
Yes, i've seen this just on the page "Tablature Guide". But in the usual way of musical notation this is wrong!
For example, if you notate a D-chord in GP6 and select Note/Brush downstroke you get an arrow up from D, A, D, to F#.

author: NSpen1
text: Yeah, I know what you mean, it has to be that way because of how tablature is arranged.  But we did discuss this before the strumming pattern interface was released to the wider public, and that exact point was brought up.  It was felt that to do it according to the physical direction was the best way, and what most people would be expecting, although there is of course going to be some ambiguity whichever way you do it.

author: The_Casinator
text:
I think they recorded into a stereo amp using an old fuzz pedal, it's intentionally lo-fi and, quite frankly, sucks to try and recreate that in a live setting.
I would save up for a better amp first of all, yours might ironically reach the lo-fi sounds but it's not in the way you'd like to reach it.
How I would do it is get a cheap tube amp (or anything else decent) and get one of these puppies:
https://thefuzzshack.com/welcome-to-the-fuzz-shack/4589526571
They're not too expensive and they're less subtle than a drunk uncle at Christmas dinner, but they do what you look for very well. Satanic Fuzz Ritual or Funeral Party would be the ones to check out first.
Alternatively dime any distortion pedal you can find and remove all bass and mids.
