text:
Hi I work extensively with metadata and also play the guitar from time to time. Looking around at the various tab bank services, it amazes me that there isn't a common metadata format.
Has there been any thought of Ultimate Guitar creating a community standard metadata format? The company is of large enough and holds enough power to do this, and it would benefit many other communities. If not, I think that it would be worth considering from the standpoints of
Bettering the Community: A common format would enable easier searching, saving, and long term preservation of the documents.
Community Integration: This is a perfect opportunity for someone to create a standard that others follow, making themselves a key player in community standards
Any thoughts?

author: N-D
text:
redcarduck
Hi! Thanks a lot for your suggestions! Maybe you could already hear about it - we're working on our huge metadata project called UG DB (Ultimate Guitar DataBase) - there are a lot of work her, and most of it is still hidden from the community - but soon we'll make it available to all our users. And of course integration with the community will be the key factor in it as well.
So for now you can read the common information about UG DB here:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/ug_news/ultimate_guitar_database_project_ug_becomes_a_music_encyclopedia.html
And of course we'll announce all the upcoming changes as well!
So please stay tuned - and all other feedback and comments will be appreciated!

author: redcarduck
text:
That looks like a really awesome project and I'm happy that it's in the works! Is this a pretty much in-house effort at this point or has there been discussion with a broader group in terms of what the overall goal/features are?
Fun Possibilities:
Versioning tabs. Imagine someone finds a tab and wants to build off/expand on it. If you use GIT in the backend this can be a simple fork operation and you'll get a nice version list for free. Late stage integration of GIT can be a huge pain, and I strongly recommend considering it.
Open Source the specs! You already have a GitHub organization and it would be a great place for people to start issues/feature requests and to contribute as well.
Have an API. It would be fantastic for the ability to search the vast database with an API. This is an obvious place to make money too. Like most API services, just charge for more than x queries a day. I imagine there are plenty of apps that would love to be able to integrate your database.

author: redcarduck
text:
Actually just to update. I ran across the Music Ontology. I'm not sure if you're familiar with RDF, but the Music Ontology describes a common vocabulary that can be used to represent information about music (tracks, live shows, etc). I would strongly suggest using an existing standard; if Google incorporates it into its crawler (you would inject the json-ld representation of the object into the web page) you would probably get some really nice results.
https://musicontology.com/docs/getting-started.html

Yes, "official" UG staff transcribe songs all the time. Find someone who has done some of the artists you like and see if they're willing to take it on.

Hi folks,
I'm David, head of UG Guitar Team. Sorry that we didn’t tell you about the changes well enough and thus caused the misunderstanding. Let me make things more clear for you.
Official tabs are a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
Every official tab includes:
Chords with lyrics
, perfect for beginner guitarists
Interactive tab
with playback for more advanced players
Backing track
that is synchronized with the tab
Tonebridge preset
to get the original sound of the song
When you request an official tab you basically get everything you might get when requesting any other type of tab, and even more with backing track and Tonebridge.
Also, there is a pretty sad statistics. Generally, up to 85% of tab requests remain unfulfilled. This means that if you leave a regular request, you have about 15% chance of getting a tab (less with guitar pro tabs). Our ultimate goal is to make the chance of getting an official tab close to 100%, so you will always get a tab when you request it.
You can read more in our announcement:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/announcement.php?f=120&announcementid=208

Cheers!

author: aaron_wacker
text:
I really love the tab requests feature and the opportunity to do a chord sheet for someone that is trying to play the song.  I'd say the one thing about it that isn't fun is when you spend an hour doing one for someone and then it goes into the queue, doesn't get approved, then gets downvoted because on its way there someone else creates a different version.  Maybe if once it were submitted you leave it open for other submissions for a few days for any other submissions.
If the submission has a few chord differences, has all the parts, and is original, let it in and let the community decide about it as its accepted.  That way you don't loose the investment of time people spend trying to help.  It is too easy to downvote in my opinion.  I've had a few rejections and have to say, they make me kind of bitter that I wasted effort on them, and they make me less likely to sit down, listen and play through the song, map out the chords and submit.  Anything you can do to fix that process would be appreciated.
When I look at older songs too I want to try a few different versions since sometimes you find one that would be rejected now but got through in the past, and it just sounds the best, or was complete where another one was not.

author: aaron_wacker
text:
It is a bit hard for me to let go of a song I did chords for.  I did one song that while in the approval queue a verbatim copy of the song came into the same queue before mine got approved.  It astounds me a bit since usually I have a few minute differences (e.g. a sharp minor where others hear a different note).  Well when it was in queue it got downvoted multiple times and then rejected as a duplicate (of the exact copy of the one I put in).  Now while its feasible someone came up with the exact same lyrics and notes as mine at each step, its also feasible I could be struck by lightning.
There needs to be a better way to check versions and timestamps and when two things go into a queue it is compared against what is there.  In this case I feel kind of cheated, granted we are all just placing chords on songs we didn't write so I should just let it go right?  The thing is - it kind of wrecks the fun part about submitting these where others haven't and I'd like you to be aware of it.  I'll continue doing the ones in queue that have multiple requests but for repeat contributers for requests you should make the process better.
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/queue/decision/view/?id=2323895

author: DropDeee

Dunno, sounds like a bit of a long shot.   When submissions can be approved by the most novice of UG members within minutes of being submitted, it's almost down to luck whether you get approved first.
I personally start at the earliest of submissions when reviewing tabs as I know there's usually the least amount of chance that someone has already suggested fixes, then work my way towards the oldest ones.   In saying that though, I rarely approve tabs, mostly I just suggest fixes ('please remove unused techniques from the legend' kind of thing).
When fulfilling requested tabs, one thing I tend to always do is reply to the request and state that I'm 'currently working on this tab and should have it submitted by tonight/tomorrow' so anyone who also considers fulfilling the tab is aware that someone else is already working on it.   I have noticed other people do this also but when it's been a week since they last said 'I should have it done by tomorrow' then I feel the request is still fair game.

author: mendace
text:
Hi guys!
We have added a couple of new rules to the tab requests forum:
An author must clearly claim the request from which time they will have 7 days to fulfill the request.
After the 7 days have elapsed the first author to fulfill the request will receive the bonus points.
Whilst an author may request the lyrics, doing so does not constitute claiming the request.
The requesting or receiving of lyrics has no bearing on the 7 day limit for claimed requests.
These rules will be enforced from this point forward. You can find the full list of rules in this announcement:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/announcement.php?f=120&announcementid=233

author: mendace
text:
Thank you all for your feedback, it is valuable to hear what you think about this
It's true that someone could save up 21 requests and then fulfill them all at the same time. However, we looked at some older requests (both open requests and fulfilled ones) and found that there isn't much hoarding happening. Some authors do save up requests, yes, but not to that extent. I don't think it's inherently a bad thing to save up requests either. We want to give tab authors the freedom to fulfill tab requests when it suits them best. Some authors might not be able to make tabs during the weekdays because they are working or taking care of their kids or whatever it could be; we don't want to limit these authors to only being able to fulfill a couple of requests on the weekend if they are willing to do more.
About asking for lyrics - We have had a couple of cases where it wasn't clear whether a request had been claimed or not. If a tab author asks the requestor (or other users) to provide the lyrics then they are obviously interested in fulfilling the request, but if the author isn't able to make a tab without receiving help from others then there's a risk that the request will be abandoned after a while if the requestor doesn't answer. For this reason we thought it would be best to leave the request open and let other authors claim it if they are willing to transcribe the lyrics themselves. It's perfectly fine to ask for lyrics but authors cannot claim a request unless they have everything they need to start working on a tab.
7 days might be a lot for chord charts but it's not a lot for guitar pro tabs for example. We want to keep the rules as simple as possible and not introduce different rules for different tab types. We'll try these rules for now and see how it goes. If we find that 7 days is too long then we can always adjust the time limit later. And remember that it is still possible to ask other authors if it's okay to take over their request if they have claimed one you'd really like to do. If they haven't started working on it yet then they might be willing to let you take over

Hi guys,I just want to bump this year old post in this thread:
Quote by Sabi.R
1. To have kind of filtering system for contributors to choose the genre, type of the tabs (chord, tab, guitar pro, ...), etc.
Every tabber has their own taste of music but it's very hard to find such from the requests. Hi!
I've got a couple of questions in regard to the preferred author option for requests. I haven't used that option so far, mainly because I always thought that it would be cheeky to ask someone directly. But meanwhile, I'm at least a bit aware of the IQ point system, although I don't understand all the aspects of it, yet. I've read the Tab requests FAQ, as well as this whole thread, but I still have questions :-) So here they are:
1) If I choose a preferred author, will he get more IQ points for fulfilling the request than he would get if he wasn't a chosen author and just discovered the request in the request list?
2) If I choose a preferred author, will the request still be listed in the request list for everybody, or will the request only be sent to that chosen author?
3) If I choose a preferred author, will that request still be offered to other authors within in the bonanza system (which I also don't completely understand so far, but anyway ...)
4) Do tabbers tend to like getting chosen author or do they tend to find it cheeky?
5) Can tabbers choose not be be suggested as preferred authors, so that I can be sure that those who are suggested really want to be asked?
6) How do tabbers get informed when they are chosen? Per inbox message, per notification / email, or will that request go directly into their personal bonanza queue?

author: mendace
text:
MazeDaBaze
1) They might, the request will be their bonanza as soon as the timer for their current bonanza runs out
2) It will still show in the request list (please note that other users can't see who you chose, only the preferred author will know)
3) Yes, there are a lot more tab authors than requests so several different users can have the same request as their bonanza
4) Some like it, some don't, it depends on the person
5) No, not at the moment
6) Via email and notifications on the site

author: h0spid
text:
We want to make it more interesting and fun to fulfill tab requests and have a couple of ideas how to do that.
Today we introduce Bonanza feature: we select one request specially for you and if you will fulfill it in 3 days you'll get additional 20 IQ. Here how it looks like:
FAQ:
Who gets and can fulfill Bonanza tab request?
Every tab author gets their personal Bonanza tab request every 3 days (or after fulfilling their current Bonanza request). You can check your current Bonanza request on the home page in the "tab requests" section or main
Tab Request page
How are tabs for Bonanza requests selected?
All Bonanza requests are personalized. They are based on your preferred tab types and requests you've fulfilled previously.
When does the countdown for Bonanza request start?
The countdown starts as soon as you see the request on the UG main page or main
Tab Request page
Can the same Bonanza request appear for different authors?
Yup, because there are about 500 requests and thousands of tab authors. But every author who fulfills Bonanza request will get extra UG IQ points.
How many extra UG IQ points I will get for a fulfilled Bonanza request?
You will get 20 UG IQ for each Bonanza request and there is no limit on how many Bonanza requests you can fulfill.
When will I get a new Bonanza request?
You'll get new Bonanza request when the timer expires or when you fulfill your current Bonanza request. Check out the home page or main
Tab Request page
to get a new request.
What if my Bonanza tab was rejected?
Nothing bad happens
You can correct your tab and submit it again, but in this case, you're not going to get extra IQ for it.
What if my submitted tab will not be reviewed during Bonanza request countdown?
We consider the time when the tab was submitted, so if the tab is approved you will get your UG IQ points.

This brings up a good point - are you asking for stats on ALL requests or just official requests or UG 'independent' authors such as myself?
You're probably talking about "official" requests but I will tackle the UG 'free' independent author requests as well. If it's an obscure song that you request 'officially' you're right, it will probably never be transcribed as not enough votes will ever get cast for it. The same goes for requesting via the 'freebie' independent author route - though you will have a MUCH better chance of having an independent author do it than an official one as it comes down to musical tastes (some of us like bizarre stuff and will do it for the challenge or self satisfaction). [**note: you should request both official AND GP when you request one as I have seen requests for official tabs that I would have gladly done - knowing full well that the official team will never do it - but I cannot do "official" tabs as I am not part of the "UG official team". Thus that song will never be transcribed]
The problem with the "official" requests is that it is a money making scheme based on voting - this is how you keep getting transcriptions of songs that have been transcribed in guitar magazines DOZENS of time before. I'm not knocking UG for making money. God bless them for it. It gives the guitar(and bass) playing community a place to come together as the guitar playing industry as a whole shrinks.
The tabbing gap should be bridged in my opinion which is why UG should start a program for us independent authors to share in the money part of it. If there were a financial incentive for the more prolific independent transcribers, people may be able to get their obscure wishes fulfilled. If you're willing to PAY for a transcription, I am sure there are many highly qualified transcriptionists here that would love to do it as a freelancer. HOWEVER, this goes back to the music industry in general - it went bust because music went digital which made it easy to steal and we all know how no one wants to pay for their music. These tab sites are great, but for many, only as long as it's free.

I'm not sure but I will do freelance - if I like the song.  I have done several in the past. However, this is just a hobby for me so I don't need some corporate policy on doing anything and everything someone comes up with.
Another note on your comment - I don't know how well freelancers would do in submitting 'offical tabs' for money. I, for one, would not be able to do the "official" tabs because those guys are monsters and add the vocal melody in which, to me, is like one long continuous melodic guitar solo throughout the whole song. That's too much work for me. There's a reason UG call theirs "official". These guys are PROs, for the most part.
Another thing that would make that NOT work is that they do tons of tabs so when people pay for a subscriptions that averages out the income over lots of tabs done by lots of (officially employed) people. How would you figure out how to pay one 'outside' guy for contributing one song - taking money out of the corporate bank? Then there's the question of how much is it worth? A song by "Dream Theater" would be more difficult to do than one by "The Kinks"by  multiple orders of magnitude. The pay would have to be commensurate.
I think the "for pay service" model would have to be a separate model altogether - a one on one contract. Of course, all of this is just wasted time thinking and talking about it as it will never happen. I doubt there are many people who would pay for it anyway. Perhaps someone should open a thread advertising their services and see what happens. As mentioned in my  earlier comment - people are used to getting :"stuff" for free.

author: RenGold
text:
fabiofsumi
Well, there are 2 different MOST WANTED TABS queues. One queue of MWT is generated automatically for songs, where other types than chords exists. Like a song has a version type GUITAR PRO and TAB, but no type CHORD. In that case it automatically goes into this queue. The problem is that these songs are quite old (bands like THE CURE, THE WHO, KISS etc.). You can find this listed on the home page or listed pressing the MOST WANTED button (underneath buttons MY CONTRIBUTION, PENDING APPROVAL, TAB CONTEST, MY DRAFTS and above MY STATS. I know that another version of MWT's (MOST WANTED TABS) exists somewhere, but I was active for a while in the one mentioned above.
The second link you added is the TAB REQUESTS queue on the FORUM. Anyone can ask for a tab and anyone can answer here and create these requested tabs. Very seldom it happens that a song exists in both queues, but please don't complain here every time you see a tab mentioned in one queue, but not in the other. This saves you sending us about 2000 complaints (and saves us receiving 2000 complaints from you).

author: mendace
text:
You can't "rig" the system but you can predict which request will be your next bonanza.
1. There is a section with recommended tab requests on the home page, one of those requests will more than likely be your next bonanza. If you claim the requests that are in that list and just wait for them to turn into bonanzas then you can get +36 IQ for the majority of the requests you fulfill. Use the "Not interested" function to clear requests that have been claimed to minimize the risk of getting the same bonanza as someone else. It's not a foolproof system by any means and sometimes you will get a bonanza request that is not on the list but it's a good place to start.
2. If a requester selects you as the preferred author then their request will eventually turn into your bonanza. Don't go around asking people to select you as the preferred author though, then there's no point in having a request system.
And please refrain from name-calling and personal attacks or I will start removing posts from this thread.

author: michum
text:
h0spid
I was trying to fulfill some bonanza requests for the last weeks now. And sorry but I have to say, the system doesn't work good at all.
It feels like every second request I get is wrong or broken. Wrong song names, wrong artist names, wrong tab type.
So instead of doing the tab, you as a writer first search for possible mistakes, even mistakes you would never think of.
Also you have to get good knowledge of the specific type of search system we use at UG.
The search system can't find a song, or expects it to be different songs if a simple letter is missing, like an -s at the ending. Or things written apart or together as one word (like King Snake vs. Kingsnake) - couldn't this be done much better?
Then you reach out for a tab moderator to fix the broken request. And then as soon as it's repaired, the bonanza is gone. I'm not talking about the 3 days being passed, it's just gone no matter how much time you had left.
Another possibility is, you did the job, submit the tab in time but don't get paid - um, don't get your points. (We're all not getting paid anyway, this is all just supposed to be fun...) So you run after tab moderators again, and have to ask for your missing points. Which feels like begging for something, and is time consuming and awkward if it happens all over and over. While in reality you did your part of the deal exactly as agreed upon, the UG system just fails you.
Obviously the requests are not moderated. So, anyone can write any name there, generating unfulfillable requests. Why isn't there any kind of control in the first place, e.g. to check for valid song and artist names? In comparision: any time I (try to) submit a tab it is checked, and only certain ways of spelling are allowed. Why can't the requests be checked?
Some things are kind of generally not good taken care of. Just as an example: Beatles songs; there are so many versions of the same song out there, anthology versions, dozens of different takes, demos. Still, UG allows only the proper song title without added "anthology version" or "take 10" in it.
Which the requesting person doesn't know - and if "corrected" to the right name, it's impossible for the search engine to distinguish, because there ARE multiple versions of that song already on the site, just not the one wanted.
So even if spelled right this songs are unfulfillable requests.
all in all:
I understand the purpose of setting up the bonanza challenge was to encourage writers to do more tabs, or to fulfill requests in a given time. I just wanted to say, the way it is now, it works the opposite direction. It is frustrating and discouraging. Up to the point that I as a writer feel put down, like tricked and fooled.
Not always of course, sometimes it works. But the failure is much too often.
Thanks

author: Danjo's Guitar
text:
So recently I've become completely obsessed with gear, not only in a GAS way, but any time I see other musicians performing I'm almost more interested in what gear their using than I am in the musicians themselves. When I am unable to tell what all they have in their set-up, and they do something cool or interesting, this leads me to the question "How are they doing that?!"
Currently my best bet (if its a famous artist) is to hop onto wikipedia and see if their gear is listed, and then use that list to make a guess at what could be making that certain sound. This is not a very effective method, because most of the time I have no idea what combinations of things they could be using to get a certain effect, and a lot of articles don't even mention the gear that people use.
I think I can say for certain that I'm not the only one who asks this question, and I think its also safe to assume that there is someone out on the internet, probably even on UG, who can answer this question for me, no matter what song or artist I'm talking about. The problem then becomes the place to do it. I suppose I could make a new forum thread every time I wanted to know, but then my question might not always get answered, and it would not necessarily be in a good place for other users to access this same information.
My proposal then is to set up an area of the site where a recording/video of a song can be accompanied with notes on what gear is being used to achieve what sounds. Time stamps corresponding to the recording/video would be helpful as well to denote specific things. This would obviously be based upon user contributions, but multiple versions of the same song (like we see in tabs) would be wholly unnecessary.

wjvanpatten
Hi guys!
We have been thinking about the sharp/flats feature for several days and now we want to ask your feedback about our idea:
- when you transpose chords up all the chords are transposed as sharp chords
- when you transpose chords down all the chords are transposed as flat chords
- there will be a Reset option to return to the original author's visualization
For example, if you want to change sharp chords to flat chords in default key you should transpose up for a semitone once and then down for a semitone once. This system gives you an opportunity to change accidentals in every key.

author: Wing00
text: It's not personal at all. No one is made to play certain songs or certain ways. Everyone will take a long time to be able to play "The Finish Line" without mistakes or without developing flawed technique, but most can play Ode to Joy within a month. It's all relative. You ever think that maybe the person is asking because they expect experienced people to give them some advice, not to be brought down or ridiculed because they're asking something.

author: benonbass1
text:
Of course it's a personal thing, due to everyone's differing skill levels. It's all relative.
Two guys could have been playing for exactly the same amount of time, but one might learn a song in a week, another might pick it up in 2 days.
I did think that, and I mentioned it in my post. Asking for advice is perfectly expectable and a great idea when it's available.
But asking how long it will take them is not going to help them achieve their goal, just tell them how long someone thinks they might take, that is unlikely to be helpful anyway.
It's very hard for anyone else to be able to judge your skill, even with examples. They may be great at one aspect at playing but terrible at another. Thus rendering the question pretty much unanswerable, without giving potentially misleading answers, and how much better off does that get you?

author: daniel.rutter.7
text:
I uploaded a chord sheet for a song a few weeks back that had the chords in the right place, had no errors that I could see and was uploaded in a format that was clear (at least it was to me). I had two separate moderators mark it as rejected for being "incomplete". I would just like to point out, when a song is a 4 chord song and nothing changes throughout, I shouldn't need to submit the entire lyrics for the song with the chord changes in the right place. Any semi competent guitarist could work it out after the verse and chorus are properly marked.
Meanwhile these admins are picking on my apparently incomplete tab, while I see other submissions that don't even have lyrics, or have blatantly incorrect chords... and these are approved.
I feel if moderators are going to be anal about chord sheets being properly formatted and completed... then they need to be anal about everything that is submitted.
It would be good to hear from a site admin about this. I'd like to know why moderators are allowed to be so picky yet so lax... are they not following the exact same rule set given to them?

author: KennyM79
text:
I'm not an admin, but I'm picky as hell about formatting. Chord sheets require all the lyrics to be listed, their corresponding chords to be present, every single time. I didn't see your submission, so I can't really comment on it.
Formatting is very important. If the tab/chord sheet isn't formatted correctly, it's not going to be very helpful.
I see people in the approval queue just go through and approve every single tab in there, even if it's wrong, poorly formatted, etc. I don't think some people even bother to take the time to look at what they're approving. These people should not be allowed to have a say because they abuse the system.
At the same time, there is an ABUNDANCE of stupidity that gets submitted. It's mind-boggling to me when I see tabs that look to be just a bunch of numbers clumped together, and the author somehow thinks that's in any way helpful to readers. It's frustrating, and then some of them get defensive and argumentative when they receive any type of constructive criticism about how they can make their tab better.
For some reason, UG won't do anything with the garbage tabs they've allowed on their site. I don't know why, and it would only stand to improve the quality of the site.
I like that everything needs to go through the approval process, but I don't like that they don't have a policy that allows them to go back and delete poorly-formatted, mis-labeled, and inaccurate tabs. Even if many users have voted it 1-star.

author: evfidripiy
text:
Urthman
, that's a great idea. But Guitar Pro ASCII-convertation is not perfect and it doesn't completely fit
UG Tab Formatting rules

You can convert your tab to text, correct it according to our guide, submit it and community will check, suggest an improvements if necessary and approve your tab with pleasure

author: jimmy_neutron
text:
Thread search tools are features brought in on a later version of vBulletin. The version we are running on UG is quite old, but it has been heavily optimized by the Russians for faster loading, better integration with the profiles and the rest of the site, yada yada. So to update the forum software would mean that all that work would be lost.
You have two alternative options. Use your browser's search function: Hit ctrl + f(windows), (cmd + a)Mac, and type in the terms you are looking for. This will search everything in the current browser window.
UG's search function: Type in your search terms, and select show results as posts, rather than as threads.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by Greenfinger182
Very much like the "View All Forum Posts by _______" feature, I think it would be cool to be able to see people's responses to news, articles, and reviews on the site.
This is useful in the forums.  Less so on articles.
In the forums, the users and discussion is what's being featured.  If you wanna follow a user around to different topics to see their opinion on various subjects and interact with them, that's fine.  But when it comes to the main site, the situation is quite different.  There, the article itself is the feature, not the back and forth discussion between commenters.  There is already too much of that.  And too much arguing.  Enabling people to track each others comments would encourage more of what should not be there in the first place.
If you want open discussions, use the forums.  Comments on articles were meant to be just that.  An opportunity for you to voice your opinion to the person who wrote the article.  UG can't prevent comments from becoming discussions between commenters, but I don't think they'll want to encourage it.
If you want to track your own comments, bookmark the articles you comment on.

author: mgiannamore921
text:
In it's current form, the Lessons section feels like an afterthought.  It's hidden away in the wiki section, and then in a secondary menu on the left side of the page, and it doesn't get better from there. Here are a few suggestions:
1.) A Link in the Main Navigation Menu
Should be common sense. If you want to drive more visitors to this section, include a link to the page in your main navigation.  The more awareness people have of this section, the larger the learning community is, the more content there will be.
2.) Sort by Views / Popularity
Currently, the only way to find good lessons is to look through each page (sorted permanently by date submitted) and find which post has a lot of upvotes.  There should be a way to view the most popular lessons of the Week / Month / All-time so you don't have dig through a bunch of pages to find something.
3.) Better Rating System
Upvote and downvote is too basic of a system.  The 1 to 5 star system utilized on the rest of the site allows for a more nuanced review.
4.) Pro Lessons
A section for pro members with lessons from Studio Musicians or maybe even the occasional guest Rockstar would be neat too. For example, Josh Homme of Queens of the Stone Age has a very unique approach to guitar playing, it would cool to hear him (or another professional) explain what kind of scales/progressions he uses to write his music.

Think of notes as letters, chords as words and songs as stories. You could write a story about wizards using the same set of letters and many of the same words as harry potter, but if you based your story ON harry potter and just used synonyms in certain places you'd definitely be in breach of copyright.

Think of notes as letters, chords as words and songs as stories. You could write a story about wizards using the same set of letters and many of the same words as harry potter, but if you based your story ON harry potter and just used synonyms in certain places you'd definitely be in breach of copyright.
I understand your point. But, to use the Harry Potter analogy, writing down the chord progression would be the equivalent of writing and reproducing a blurb or summary of the book. A story about wizards etc, could describe a number of books, just like a chord progression could described a number of songs. I guess you could argue the copyright infringement might be in rewriting the book from the summary, or in covering/performing the song from the chords, but not in the writing down of the chords.
The other major difference is that if chords are words, you are talking about a dictionary which is much smaller with many derivatives of certain words. Back to the visual arts again, it is like owning the rights to using a certain shade of red, blue and green in combination with each other. in general, chords cannot be copyrighted.

tabs can count as an adaptation of a work and thus can be counted as copyright infringement in many jurisdictions.
UG will have consulted a lawyer before taking these actions and any lawyer worth their salt will have told them that they're likely to be held liable for copyright infringement if they don't comply.

author: NSpen1
text:
This relates to the new Bad Rating for a Good tab? thread (formerly Good tab, BAD rating!!)
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1832452
The reasoning behind removing bad ratings has apparently changed.  This mainly relates to 3 star ratings, I trust that there will be no problem removing any obvious nonsense 1 and 2 star ratings.  Previously the reasoning was that a 3 star rating on a "good tab" would not be removed if the tab already had lots of ratings because one 3 star rating would not affect the average, but it would be removed from a tab with few ratings because it would make a difference to the overall rating.  This seemed to make sense to me.  Now the reasoning is the opposite, that a 3 star rating will not be removed from a tab "which has not been rated at least 10 times", and we have to wait for more ratings before we can get an unjustified one removed.
I'd like to point out what we should all know by now, that just because a tab has lots of high ratings that does not mean it's accurate.  It's quite easy for a tab for a popular song (especially chords) to get lots of high ratings just because the song is popular, and many people can't tell when something is correct or not.  The new tab rating system
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/ug_news/ug_has_a_new_tab_rating_system_now_heres_how_it_works.html
was supposed to help with that - "if a tab is very popular and has dozens of votes, one more bad vote against it won't affect the tabs rating."  Also see point 4, Bigger chance for new tabs - that's something that's still a problem, especially if there's a tab that might have been on the site for 15 years and has a large number of ratings largely because of that, it's very hard to get users to look at a new tab which may be much better.  If you won't remove average ratings from good new tabs that makes it even harder for them to get noticed.
(Sidenote - the description "worth learning" for a 3 star rating is, and always has been, nonsense, as I and other people have previously pointed out.  Can't we just call it what it is, "average"?, i.e. there should be quite a bit wrong with the tab to justify giving that rating.)
I'd like to suggest that the criteria for removing 3 star ratings should basically go back to what it was before.  But I also don't have a problem with them being removed from tabs with lots of high ratings, if there seems to be no good reason for a 3 star rating.  I'd like to think that
emad
, who has the task of removing the ratings, would be fairly quickly able to see if a tab is high quality and doesn't deserve an average rating.  He has indicated that he would be open to input from other users about ratings, so if tab mods / higher level authors can help out there I don't see that there should be a problem.  Or anyone actually, no one needs to prove their credentials, if they can objectively say why / how a tab is accurate or not then their input would be helpful.
Thanks for reading!

author: NSpen1
text:
mandelstamdavid
Well, this is kinda hypothetical because it's not as if I or anyone else have been checking other authors' tabs to see if a 3-star rating is fair or not.  What happens at the moment :
If we happen to get a 3-star rating we'll generally try to contact the user to ask why they gave that rating.  Usually we get no reply, probably in at least 95% of cases - that's why there has been a suggestion made to make it mandatory to give a reason for a 3-star rating as well as 1 and 2 stars.
So then we'll post on the Bad Rating for a Good tab? thread and, well, basically do what it says in the first post there
"In order to remove rating off your tab you should ensure me that your tab doesn't deserve such rating. Post as much information as needed about why someone shouldn't have given your tab that bad rating!"
Of course as authors we don't think we make 3-star quality tabs - an average tab which would have substantial errors - but you don't have to take our word for it, if the reasoning we give isn't convincing then that's where emad or other unbiased authors could check the tab for accuracy.  So yes, notes and chords obviously, I wouldn't be too bothered about lyrics since not all types of tab submission have them and I wouldn't regard wrong lyrics as a reason to drop two whole stars from the maximum rating (unless they were hilariously badly wrong, I suppose).
The criteria for removing 3-star ratings at the moment comes from your end, as set out in the first post in that thread, but you've asked me what I think so I'd say it should be that a 3-star rating should be removed if no reasonable case can be made that the tab has significant inaccuracies (rather than oh, it got so many 5-star ratings already therefore it must be right).

author: NSpen1
text:
No, ratings are not just subjective and opinions, of course some are for the reasons already given, people rating because they like a song or not, or they can't tell whether something's right, or it's too hard for them to play, or they wanted the lead parts in a chord chart or whatever.  But it's quite possible to give objective ratings also - if you say it's not
DON CZARSKI
you're basically saying anyone can tab whatever they want for a song and it's just opinion as to whether it's correct, that no one can objectively say whether a chord or note is correct.
You could look at any of the 1 or 2 star ratings I've given tabs and see exactly the reasons why.  I could objectively give a 4 star rating to a tab because it's largely correct but has some errors and I could point out exactly what those errors are.  Objectivity in ratings does exist.
Agree with
motoclangers
that a rating system is required, there are obviously large differences in quality between some tabs, and there's no benefit to doing away with the rating system other than saving the hurt feelings of some people who receive low ratings.
There's no more objectivity involved in people adding tabs to favourites than there is in ratings, people give it a good or bad rating because they think it's good or bad, they add it to favourites because they think it's good, or don't add it if they think it's bad.  Quite possibly less, since I can imagine people adding a tab to favourites before they've played it, so they have it 'bookmarked' to come back to later.

author: Colohue
text:
Quote by Diversion2007
can someone explain the pulse one to me?-
The Pulse is a graph that shows your input to the community day by day compared to the growth of the community en masse. Having a higher personal bar than that of the community means that you're putting more in than you're getting out, which is a good thing.
Personally I've already worked out how to trick it, but I won't be sharing that information.
Forum posts are not the only thing that affect the pulse. In fact, posts in the Pit barely register. The real use is via the profiles. Checking out groups, commenting on pictures and listening to mp3s are some of the things that you can do. Other ways of increasing your personal pulse are through viewing lots of different user profiles and getting a high amount of views yourself. Uploading tabs, columns, lessons and news gives a definite boost because you're giving something directly to the community in that way.
The Pulse seems to max at 120, certainly I've never gotten it higher, but maintaining that will be tricky. It's a personal thing, but I can see people getting very very addicted to it.

Quick answer, full of speculation:
When first conceived, the concept was called Modules.

It's my suspicion that in UG 8.0 all (or most) elements will be modularized.  The mandatory modules (news, reviews, etc) are not widgets. I think its crucial since a lot of people are still stuck on GP5.2 and not even 6, id imagine the market for 7 is even smaller, so if we could either upload all different GP versions or the site internally converted a single version of a tab into all other versions and the user could select which one to download, that would be great.

I actually proposed this years ago, dont know why its not implemented yet.

author: SpeedSterHR
text:
UG Support
I think a lot of users would be interested in GP7.  The GP tabs are really the best part of this great site and Arobas Music surveyed their users for what features to add--and then they actually implemented many of the suggestions.  I'm surprised there wasn't a UG Staff review about GP7 right when it came out (turns out it was in Beta way back during Winter NAMM.  I understand if they're not sponsoring content here, but I think UG stands a lot to gain from their users being aware of GP7.  I can't believe I'm just hearing about GP7 accidentally now.
Also, when you do implement it, I'd humbly suggest that you don't accept "locked" tabs.  Some ego-centric tabbers might get off on submitting locked tabs, but that goes against the whole spirit of this site.  Some of the best tabs on UG started as a very flawed 1-guitar GP3 file and now, a decade plus later have evolved to where all the flaws are fixed, along with having the rest of the band added in, yet there are still "fingerprints" left from the original version if you know what to look for.  It would be a real shame if we lost that collaborative spirit here--it's one of the things that makes UG so awesome.
Keep up the great work.

author: MazeDaBaze

Hi!
I'd just like to remark, that it took me months to find out how to handle blogs on UG in general, and that was caused only by a small irritation of the wordings: Usually, a "Blog" is a whole thing, and each posting is a "Blog Posting".
So what usually is a "Blog posting", is named a "Blog" on UG. And what usually is a "Blog", is named "Blogs" on UG.
So as a new user you simply don't understand "Why should I put up another blog for my profile?" and "How can I put up another posting of my existing Blog?", and then "Can that be, that each Blog has only one posting, and that you shall make a whole new Blog for each posting?"
And it's the same from the reader's perspective: New users think: "Did the blog owner really stop this blog already after the first posting?" - and so on.
So may you want to change the labels accordingly.
This applies for all Blogs on UG: Profile Blogs as well as Group Blogs (and maybe there are some other Blogs to which it also applies, but which I don't have in mind atm).
You might find this not relevant, but there are several of such smaller issues on the website, which alltogether cause quite a lot of confusion for the users, and I think that it also causes that not only a few users simply give up trying to understand and using the site, just because of such aspects of site navigation. So I hope that I can help with these kind of hints.

author: Roc8995

Look through the tab requests subforum, and notice how many of those requests are completed. Most requests go unfulfilled, and if nobody is interested or able to tab the thing you've asked for, yours is probably going to end up one of them. Tabbers are volunteers and users just like you, and they have no obligation to listen to you specifically or fulfill every single tab request.
I'm going to close this thread since this this isn't a suggestion for UG. It's unfortunate that your tabs aren't being made, but that's not a site issue. Lots of people ask for tabs that never get made, it's just the nature of a system where anyone can make a request. It takes a lot more time and effort to create a tab than it does to ask for it. We can't solicit complaints from everyone who's ever had a tab request go unfulfilled.

author: Cavalcade
text:
I'm not seeing anything missing in the stuff I usually play, and I checked Testament and Metallica and most of their stuff seems to be there. 95%, you said? Well, sucks to be you.
Now, let me drop some hot, steaming copyright law on y'all suckas. When a record is released, the rights to it are usually shared between the band and their label, as per a contract.
Those rights include distributing tabs, and any kind of transcription!
Tabs are copyrightable intellectual property, after all, like audio recordings. To keep running
at all
without being ass-deep in lawyers, Ultimate Guitar pays licensing fees to a group that takes care of all the royalty issues for them. The labels have UG by the balls as it is. That's just how it is.
Now, if a label wants a tab taken off UG, there's not much UG can do. Labels
own
the rights. UG pays to
borrow
them. The labels are well within their rights to go "can't let you do that, UG!" (or "I'm sorry, UG, I can't let you do that" if you prefer), and tell them to pull a tab. As you can see from the
very generous
number of tabs that are still
here
, they only do this for a handful of bands. Most of the time, so they can release a tab book or something, and charge guitarists (that can't just play by ear) for the tabs that gracious people on the internet with a lot of free time give them for free.
Yeah, it sucks. Yeah, it always comes back to "labels are evil". So? What you gonna do?
This message does not, in any way, reflect the Ultimate Guitar team's stance on anything, this is just me. I did my homework on this, though.

author: AcousticMetal99
text:
Cavalcade, your argument really doesn't hold.
This is not a case of copyright infringement, unless the uploader went and looked in a published, certified book or other document and copied that in directly. The fact of the matter is, these tabs are what people ~think~ the music is - yes, on many songs they may be correct. However, the ability to figure out music is not an offence, and besides that they may have inaccuracies. So now we come to sharing what they think the music is - there's still nothing wrong with that, in the same way as you can quote sections of a book or article in anything else, provided you reference it, and IT IS NOT FOR COMMERCIAL USE. That is the important bit - I doubt many of the people on UG are professionals who use tabs by others to make a living. Do you also wish to complain about any Battle of the Bands competition or tribute acts? Surely they are far more likely to be in breach of copyright?
Another example is the way that you can buy a CD or digital download, and play it when friends come round - are you going to say that it's illegal for them to hear it because they didn't purchase it? Well what if those friends are musically talented and happen to transcribe the music by ear themselves so they can play it, because they like it? Is that then an offence?
I should also point out that sites like UG, by allowing many people to learn some version of a song, most likely increases the number of people listening to those bands, because they learn and play those songs to people they (may or may not) know, who could then decide to listen to the band.
Anyway, rant over. I personally haven't noticed any tabs being removed?

The fact of the matter is, these tabs are what people ~think~ the music is - yes, on many songs they may be correct. However, the ability to figure out music is not an offence, and besides that they may have inaccuracies.
Intent intent intent. When someone uploads a GP tab, they are actively trying to reproduce and distribute the music. Not the actual audio itself, maybe, but the music, which is also copyrighted.
Remember, copyright doesn't just cover a recording; it covers the notes and words themselves, and getting a few notes wrong here and there doesn't change jack shit.
Quote by AcousticMetal99
IT IS NOT FOR COMMERCIAL USE. That is the important bit
What, no. Whether or not it's for commercial use has nothing to do with it, for starters. Your examples of BotB/tribute bands? Guess what?
They pay royalties.
Them, or the places they perform at. If they don't, what they're doing is legally questionable, at least. And second, Ultimate Guitar
is commercial use.
They make money off ad revenue, and services such as Tab Pro, by using tabs.
Attribution is important, sure. But you shouldn't expect a medal for tagging your tab with the right song/artist. That's the bare minimum. That's
expected
of you. In the same way that uploading a whole album to YouTube and saying " OWNS THIS MUSIC, NOT ME, NO COPYRIGHT INTENDED" doesn't make it legal, crediting the band doesn't mean their label has to give you distribution rights.
Guitarists seem to have a naively optimistic view of copyright law. I've written and uploaded several full-band Guitar Pro tabs, close to 100% accurate, but only after accepting that in order to help other people learn them, I have to give the labels and copyright holders involved the right to pull the plug on all of it, in the unlikely case that they want to. (Or the band, but it's usually the label. Bands are thrilled to have people tab their music out for them.) It's a small price to pay for helping people teach themselves to become better musicians, which, in turn, is how I learned.

author: SkyValley
text:
Quote by TJ1991
This post is one of the biggest steaming piles of uninformed crap I've ever read. You clearly don't know the first thing about hearing impairment. Why should someone with hearing problems not be into music? If it's good enough for Beethoven, etc. Discrimination, well done.
You clearly know nothing about the thyroid gland, either.
Are you SERIOUS?  Are people ACTUALLY claiming hearing impairment as an excuse for tone deafness???
Let me tell you a story, when I started music school they played two notes for me and asked "which note is higher?"  I couldn't tell!  I was completely tone deaf and all the notes seemed the same to me.  However, after 4 years of serious study and tons of practice I now have near-perfect pitch.  I can hum the high E string without hearing it.  I can pick out Bb, C, and a few other notes just on blind hearing tests.  If someone plays a scale, arpeggio, or mode to me without me looking I can tell what it is.
It's because I PRACTICED and I never made up bullshit excuses on being "hearing impaired" or "tone deaf."  There's no such THING as tone-deaf, anymore than a person who doesn't speak French is "French-deaf!"  You just never took the time to learn the language!
Notes are just frequencies, you don't need to hear them very loud for your brain to process the musical information.  Even if you are almost deaf, as long as you can hear the note at all your brain can process the information.  You would literally need to be brain damaged or have some sort of mental deficiency to be incapable of learning to differentiate notes.  Poor hearing is no excuse.
I'm sure that some people have a much harder time learning to hear into music than others (I know I did) but anyone can do it if you really, really care about being a good musician.  Beethoven could compose late in his career after his hearing went because he studied music so much that he could arrange it all in his head and know what it would sound like.  That's a skill that we should ALL be developing!
Your accusation of "discrimination" is totally unfounded.  I am living proof that someone with no musical background or natural talent can develop the skills necessary to transcribe music by ear.  How am I discriminating against people by wanting them to do things the right way?

I consider myself a successful musician.
I have no eardrum in my right ear, and a lot of scar tissue covering the one in my left ear. People said that I shouldn't swim because if I dived, the pressure buildup would be painful. I went ahead and learnt how to swim anyway. I get a lot of enjoyment out of swimming, same as I get a lot of enjoyment out of music. So you tell me, with my poor hearing, why shouldn't I be a musician?
I'll accept your apology when/if you make one.

author: fanapathy
text:
Quote by SkyValley
Tabs are a bullshit way to learn music anyway.  (and tons of other arrogant bs)
Not only an offense to said those more challenged with hearing (you are not them, even if
you
could with
your
mind and body - doesn't mean that you could if you were
them
)
You're also shitting all over transcribers and people who make tabs.
I don't care how good you claim your ears are, you're not gonna be able to hear everything in some muddy high-gain low tuned riff or some super fast double lead solo, which doesn't stand out in the mix, just by listening to it. The transcriber could have spent several hours slowing down, isolating and equalizing - to make sure every note, bend, slide, HOPO, vibrato, etc is spot on.
Now you could do this yourself, but many don't have the resources, equipment, knowledge or skill to do it - and if you first put in all that time and effort, you might as well make a tab and share it.
There's nothing wrong with using tabs as an aid, though there does come a day where you start to notice that the tab with 100 5-star ratings wasn't as accurate as you first thought.

I'm often seeing old threads from years ago being resurrected. Sometimes it is appropriate, but more often the OP has long gone and the advice or opinion offered in the reply is adding nothing. And I do see these posts being manually closed by mods.

https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=492698#24

author: tkvoice
text:
The standard used to accept/reject submitted songs for "chords" is not useful for people who play & sing at the same time.
Most songs we play have a repeated sequence of chord patterns and the lyrics that are sung underneath these patterns are delivered at various rates. When people just place a bunch of lyrics down and place chords above them it does not help the singing musician figure out the vocal delivery with respect to the groove of the song.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/t/the_cars/just_what_i_needed_ver2_crd.htm
--------------Example 1-----------------------
Artist: The Cars
Song: Just What I Needed

[Verse]

Scratchy E
E                  B
I don’t mind you coming here
C#m             G#
Wasting all my time
E                               B
‘Cause when you’re standing oh so     near
C#m                     G#
I kind of lose my mind, yeah
E                        B
It’s not the perfume that you wear
C#m                    G#
It’s not the ribbons in your hair
E                  B
I don’t mind you coming here
G#                     A
And wasting all my time
----------------------------------------------------------------
The lyrics and chords are correct above but  could be formatted better to  show the repeated pattern like this:
--------------Example 2-----------------------
E                  B         C#m             G#
I don’t mind you coming here Wasting all my time

E                               B          C#m                     G#
‘Cause when you’re standing oh so     near I kind of lose my mind, yeah

E                        B         C#m                    G#
It’s not the perfume that you wear It’s not the ribbons in your hair

E                  B         G#                     A
I don’t mind you coming here And wasting all my time
----------------------------------------------------------------
Notice the first two three lines of lyrics share the same chord pattern. This was not too obvious in the previous formatting.
Why not take this formatting further and lay the lyrics out underneath a consistent chord spacing like this:
--------------Example 3------------------------
E                             B             C#m                      G#
            I don’t mind you coming here         and wasting all my time

E                             B             C#m                      G#
  Cause when you’re standing oh so near           I kind of lose my mind

E                             B             C#m                      G#
        It’s not the perfume that you wear     It’s not the ribbons in your hair

E                             B             G#                       A
            I don’t mind you coming here         And wasting all my time
----------------------------------------------------------------
Formatted like this it is easy for the singing musician to visually see the phrasing (delivery of singing) compared to the rhythm of the music.
Why not take this formatting a little further and condense the repeated chords in order to clean up the clutter and help with getting the song to fit on 1 or 2 pages correctly (so you don't have to flip pages when using a binder)
--------------Example 4 -----------------------
E                             B             C#m                      G#
            I don’t mind you coming here         and wasting all my time
  Cause when you’re standing oh so near           I kind of lose my mind
        It’s not the perfume that you wear     It’s not the ribbons in your hair

E                             B             G#                       A
            I don’t mind you coming here         And wasting all my time
----------------------------------------------------------------
I would love to see all of the songs on Ultimate Guitar formatted in this method.
I have submitted many songs using this format only to have them rejected because "I don't have chords above all lyrics" along with suggestions like  "show me the strumming pattern" (etc.) Personally I don't want to see Strumming Patterns or repeated Chords above a bunch of unsyncopatted lyrics ( this adds zero value) I realize that others may see value in that but I have 100s of songs formatted using my method and have had nothing but compliments from every musician I have shared them with.
I say the standards should be changed to include this type of formatting maybe could be flagged as a new type too.
In past years this type of formatting was allows and you can tell by the voting that people love it.
Other things can be added too to help musicians ... Here is one of my un-othodox songs (submitted years ago before the formatting nazi's took over) that gets great reviews:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/p/pink_floyd/dogs_ver3_crd.htm

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
Your side of this discussion is also completely based on personal preference, that is, opinion, and in this case, a very deeply-entrenched one.
UG created its own style guide to work with its own tools, including auto-scrolling. Having compact lyrics like in a hymnal, with all lyrics of a specific musical section stacked by order or appearance, prevents this function from working properly. Furthermore, the majority of modern songs aren't identical from section to section, and doing this
E                            B             C#m                     G#
  I don’t mind you           coming here      wasting all my       time
E                            B             C#m                     G#
 'Cause when you’re standing oh so near,      I kind of lose my    mind, yeah
E                            B             C#m                     G#
  It’s not the perfume       that you wear,   it’s not the ribbons in your hair
E                            B             G#                      A
  I don’t mind you           coming here      and wasting all my      time
or variants is still relatively hard to read. If you want to have a hymnal, make sheet music, not a chord chart. That gives you the detail you want without having to complain about how a site's publication format differs from your personal taste.
Finally, cut the condescension and backhanded remarks. It's adding exactly 0 to discussion.
For the record, I usually only keep lyrics and the key when I need to sing and play simultaneously. I internalize the songs as much as possible beforehand. In this case,
readability is key
, and that is most easily done with left-justified text or sheet music.

You need to submit it as a correction, not 'Publish to UG' as a new version.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
I just wanted to say that I find it extremely comical and ironical that this thread, which is about spam, has now degraded to a spam thread
My on-topic opinion: first of all, UG allows users to be banned 3 times before they get banend forever, and each ban is preceded by a warning. Users get enough chances, IMO, if they still can't stop breaking the rules after all that, they deserve their perma.
Secondly, there's the matter of "what if a user unknowingly and/or unintentionally contributed to spam or something similar, and earned himself that extra warning, granting him a perma he didn't deserve?" To assess this problem, I think the FotB itself is a good enough means to judge every individual ban. Mods can see on any user's record what the reason for every warning/ban the user ever received was... so if a user thinks their permanent ban was unjust, or that they behaved themselves well for long enough/contributed to UG enough to deserve a lighter punishment, the mods can look into the matter relatively easily. Most permabanned users simply deserve their perma, though.
IMO, this is all up to the mods' judgement. Their word is final; it's even in the rules.

I know that there used to be a way to load up a random tab within certain parameters at this link:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/advanced_search.html
(Before I go on, I know there are two other now locked posts about this topic, but neither of them really say anything about why random tab search was awesome. And because they are both locked, I can't post in those)

That section is fine and dandy, but the problem there is that it is full of songs that I already know of and just haven't learned yet, or otherwise popular songs with millions of tab views. It actually was much more similar to the explore page than the recommended section. Just if the explore page had one extra button that selected a random tab among all the ones that fit your applied filters. I could discover new artists, songs, genres even sometimes. It's way better than sifting though 1000 pages of tabs/chords and trying to pick among the dispersed songs I don't know. Instead it was like it forced me to learn some particular song, skipping all the down time. It was awesome, it worked perfectly, and I would love to be able to use it again.
If it's a matter of adding a "random" button on the explore page, I'd find out how to do it and do it for free if you let me haha
If it's a matter of that old link's page being on the old UI and not wanting to put in the time to update it, I certainly don't mind if was open to use with the old look because it worked great and the functionality of it is all I really cared about anyway.

author: epimentel232
text:
Good day,
I posted this on the "UG Authors' Community" forum, and figured that it would also be worth posting it here >
I recently had a discussion with someone over why chord sheets, UG song postings that are chords above lyrics, may not be effective, especially towards beginners. They aren't like Guitar Pro tabs which have valuable information such as time signature, BPM, measure bars, and etc; this leads people to have to listen to the song while viewing tabs in other to truly grasp the timing/speed of the song, when to play each chord, and the dynamics of each chord. While I think listening and analyzing music is inevitably one of the best ways to learn, I think it's possible that UG could use at least a few improvements to the chord sheet format. The website already has a functionality to show and play various chords; it'd be useful to also provide some way to play each of the chords in sequence. This could be implemented through the tab editor which would allow authors to emulate how the song would actually be played. Visually, on the website, it may simply play the chords in sequence like I mentioned with the chords, BPM, and time signature appropriately configured and monitored by tab authors. It may coexist with the auto-scroll feature as well, playing the chords (maybe even simply highlighting them as they go by) and scrolling down the page as needed.
Perhaps there could also be some sort of visualization for piano since, as an example, it wouldn't make sense to play C major all the way down at C1, lest it sound muddy, or as high as C6 where it'll sound too bright without depth. Or, at least some indication of the octave in which the chords should be placed.
Introducing this slightly more interactive web page for chord sheets will be much clearer than cluttering up the sheet with text-based logistics; many people probably don't even read the description for example, and simply want to delve into the chords. I think some of these small changes will give users a smoother experience when it comes to learning tabs; it'd be a good step forward for the website.
This isn't an attempt to replace Guitar Pro with chord sheets either, but it'd be beneficial to at least play the chords in sequence, and with correct timing to users (which would of course be implemented and monitored by tab authors as I mentioned).

author: Doheuvel
text:
epimentel232
As an author of over 4 700 of these chord sheets my experience  is that these current chord sheets are effective to the majority of the users.
Most users here are hobby guitar players, often self-taught and this simple notation sets them on their way to learn their favourite songs.  What I do I always mention the BPM's in the tabs I make - I also, wherever applicable, repeat chords indeed above the lyrics, but I also repeat them on the beat even if the same chord is played twice or more.
The way I work out tabs is by playing along to the (official) YouTube or Spotify song - in real time - and I imagine the guitar players using the tab to do exactly the same.  It's simple and effective. Always provide a link to the song tabbed as well.  Complicationg this simple way of subscribing a song would in my opinion scare away the beginning guitar players.  In my experience any complication - will negatively impact the use of these chord sheets.
From what I've seen during all of these years is that:
1)  a lot of people do not use/look at the notes you write at the top of the chord sheet (as a help to playing a song),
2)  they often do not look at the chord finger setting you give thus commenting that the song does not sound right,
3)  some don't even look at where the capo is supposed to be - and
4)  as a fourth point the use of the transpose / play along etc. buttons is not very known.
All this to say that in my opinion - leave it as it is - don't (over) complicate.  It's effective to a lot of UG Users today.
If  you play along to the link provided, you read  the lyrics & see the corresponding chords. This way you also hear the beats/speed the song is played at.
Just my 2 cents.
Sorry I did not see your post in the  "UG Authors' Community" forum.

author: epimentel232
text:
Doheuvel
I definitely see where you're coming from; in my post I mentioned that one of the best ways to work on a song is to have the chord sheet on the side while playing along with the link provided, and so I agree with your points. In all the chord sheets I've written so far I made sure to provide a link to the offcial video I exactly took the chords from, and I heavily suggest users to listen to the song while playing.
My suggestion was simply to add a sort of player which would play the chords in time as they go by. Some songs are a bit more involved than others at certain points, whether it be rhythmically or chordal; the hobbyist, even while listening to the song, may have a hard to playing said parts. In my opinion I feel like an audio player wouldn't complicate things at all as it would merely be playing the chords aloud to you. It'd just be a tool users could use to hopefully get a better sense of the song.
A player on the website which goes through the song doesn't have to interfere with the already simple notation of UG. It'd just be a button you could press (like the autoscroll feature), which would then go through the song as detailed in my post.
I appreciate your input.

author: NotAtWork
text:
Please add the ability to download all playlists (with tab references—not the actual tabs) that can serve as a backup in much the same way as the current download personal tabs provides. I create a playlist for each major gig (~250 playlists to date) and retain it as a history of what songs were performed. This is handy from the tab's add-to-playlist perspective as it shows if I'm performing a song too often or too little.
I've always been nervous about not being able to download my playlists at the same time that I make a downloaded backup of my personal tabs.  The recent add personal tab to playlist bug that deleted the personal tab rather than adding it emphasized this concern, as the unfortunate deletion of my personal tab (backup up, at least) also removed it from all my playlists, with no record of which playlists it had been in.
Ideally, the ability to create/restore a playlist from the downloaded backup would be wonderful, but for now I would settle for downloading a zip file containing the playlist song list (in custom order) as a text file for each playlist.

author: redsg1
text:
Hey, I've been using this site for many years and few things really get on my nerves and I wanted to throw it out here..I'm sure people talked about some of them before but still nothing changed so I'll just say what I think and whatever the Mods decide is fine.
1. something has to be done with the songs that have 30 versions! even 5 is too much! I'll explain- when I want to play a song, I need to open all versions and try all of them until I find the best one. this is such a pain in the ass! in some cases 1-2 of the tabs have a 5 star rating by a big amount of voters and the rest get 2-4 stars, so that makes things better BUT
2. after some amount of time, it would be great if those tabs that have a very low 3-1 rating be just deleted!!!! why are they still there?? there are 10 tabs better! the list of tabs becomes so long that for every song I need to go to the next page! I think after a YEAR of a tab being rated low it should be just removed.
3. the rating system is just BAD! users that submitted a tab for the same song are allowed to vote on each others versions which is bullshit cause it's never a good rating! other thing is that the users can change their rating. so if they want the tab to have 3 stars, and it has 5 stars they don't rate- 3, they rate- 1 to get the avg to where they want! this is just not cool cuz the tab has no chances of ever getting to have 5 stars again after that 1 asshole rated.
another thing is the rating itself. God knows what made people rate the way they rated. so if someone rates 3 or 4 the owner of the tab doesn't know what's wrong with the tab and can't make it better (which causes 10 more versions to be submitted by every asshole that thinks he found 1 chord that is better!). I suggest that it should be required to leave a comment that explains low rating, just like in the section of tabs to be approved. no need to supply the correction but just the place in the tab that wasn't good.
one more thing- when there are few versions of the same song and it's hard to remember which 1 is better the user can rate his fav tab 5 and the rest 3 just to make it visible to him next time he'll want to play that song- nothing prevents this from happening.
4. and back to multiple versions of the same song. I agree that it's good to have few versions but only when they are very different. usually the first tab isn't perfect so someone posts a 2nd ver which isn't perfect and then more versions come, why they get worst each time I'll never know (maybe because of what I said in point 3). besides the fact that this implies to the first tabber that his job wasn't good enough and makes him never want to tab again for this site I think there's a better way to go about this.
I suggest that for every correction submitted the user will receive some points for it, like ranking for adding tabs and such. so if there's 1 version that isn't perfect, instead of submitting 10 more shitty vers that never get deleted from the site, users that have corrections leave them on the first tab, get points for it as a motivation and then the tab owner can improve his tab. in the end we'll get 1 GOOD version! isn't it great?
5. another reason for many versions is the tabs in queue section! so, a new album comes out, someone decides to tab it first so the fans can enjoy playing it. and after a lot of work and time, they are done. first versions are waiting to get approved. as we know this might take weeks! in good case 1-2 days. so while we are waiting, someone else gets the idea to tab the same songs. the problem is that this someone never submitted a tab before & he can't see the tabs in queue page and know that someone before him did it already! so he tabs the same thing..and as if that's not bad enough both of the tabs usually get approved unless someone notices the similarity and votes to reject 1 of the tabs, hopefully they don't reject the first tabs, but that doesn't matter, both tabbers wasted their time to tab the songs.
I suggest that those users that can't approve/reject tabs yet, be allowed to see the list of tabs waiting for approval to avoid what I just explained.
I know that if nothing changes the site is still gonna be the best, but even the tiniest improvement would be very appreciated!!!
thank you for reading.

author: Wuai Bel Ree
text:
Okay, imagine this:
You go into advanced search. You put a band you like in this band field, and then set the tuning filter to 'standard tuning'. You click search. Dozens of tabs come up, and you start browsing through them. After awhile you notice something - half of the tabs you're looking at are tabbed in Drop D. "But I set the tuning filter to standard tuning only!" you think to yourself. You let out a big sigh, and spend the next 10 minutes going through tabs to find which ones are actually in standard tuning and which ones were incorrectly labeled during the submission process.
Pain in the butt, right?
So how about a system that lets users mark tabs as a different tuning then what they're currently labeled as? You know, maybe a button on the tab that brings up a drop down menu or something with all the different tunings on it, and then users select the correct tuning. To keep trolls from purposely mislabeling tab tunings, the system could rely on a majority vote. Like whatever tuning is selected more than any other by users, that's the tuning that the advanced search will use for the tuning filter. Then the days of finding bar chords instead of power chords when searching in standard tuning will be no more.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by Thornography
Yeah, the mods mod their own forum because they know things about their own forum and they're good with guitar/bass/amps/song writing etc, but
the Pit has no real standard of knowledge, so anyone can mod it
(not alone, obviously) as long as they know how to tell spam apart from a real thread.
You might want to cover up.  Your ignorance is showing.
The Pit would absolutely be
the hardest
of all forums to moderate properly and effectively.
This stems from the fact that it's "off-topic", meaning conversations on an extremely diverse subjects occur.  There is far more required than the ability to "know how to tell spam apart from a real thread".  Among the knowledge required is the ability to know what belongs in the Pit and what doesn't.  Tons of
non-spam
threads get closed because they belong in other forums, and the TS simply put them in Pit for greater exposure.  Others are closed because the OP is divisive and used to polarize and incite hostility among UGers.  Others still are closed because they spawn an attitude of hate or intolerance toward groups, genres, or individuals.
For effective moderation, any forum needs a
small
group of like-minded individuals in charge who have a similar set of standards.  This improves the uniformity in enforcement of the rules.  Expanding the group dilutes the uniformity.
Most of all, Pit Mods need to have a well developed sense of humour.  Knowing when to temper rule enforcement with a sense of fun and frivolity is skill not many have.  Balance is important, otherwise the Pit can go to extremes.  Too loose and it becomes reckless, hostile, and cluttered with tripe.  Too tight and it becomes stifled and boring.
Our world is not perfect, nor is the Pit.
But they both reach a sense of balance.
The Mods we have now are doing a fine job, imho.
The only need for new Mods there is by attrition.
