Quote by stratman_mjc
You make it sound a lot harder than it should be imo... Anyone who understands the rules and has a vague knowledge of the structure of the forums should be able to figure out what belongs in the pit, let alone a mod.
i make it sound easier than actually it is.  don't just focus on knowing the rules and which forum things belong in.  those are things that differentiate good users from the rest.  a moderator is judge, jury, and executioner.  this requires a high level of discretion and balance.
knowing when to close a thread, even when it doesn't appear to be breaking any specific rule is a skill not many have.  knowing when to leave one open, although it might be over the line, one that even fewer have a handle on.  the ability to discern when warnings/bannings are appropriate is an even more difficult call.
the peculiar brand of humor and wisdom amidst near chaos, is one huge magnet UG has, attracting users.  often users go on to explore other areas of UG and contribute greatly, though some remain in the Pit for their entire time here.  upsetting the balance in the Pit would cause it to lose much of its charm.
there are things that happen behind the scenes in UG that you and i will never know about and therefore won't be able to base a value judgment on.  what seems logical on the surface, isn't always the true nature of the beast.
Quote by stratman_mjc
The idea itself is good, in that any mod can come into the pit and close a rule-breaking thread, but I understand this may be difficult to implement.
pretty much that.  looks good on the surface.  but underneath, it adds more problems.
one of the built-in beauties of having mods away for a while is that it requires users to exercise their own discretion.  some simply report the problems and have the good sense to ignore the spam threads after that.  others feel compelled to respond, keeping the garbage at the top of the index.  they identify themselves as part of the problem.  it all balances out in the end.

author: seemeel
text:
I was browsing through the reviews section looking at modern opinions on some classic records, and it struck as being rather silly that all music is classified as 'Compact Discs'.
I suggest that this be changed to '
Records
'.  This term traditionally applied to vinyl records, but when alternatives such as cassette tapes and CDs were developed, the term came to mean the
music
, rather than the physical medium that you bought.  And now with so much online music buying and pirating, the term is broader than ever.
So I think that to review a compact disc is silly - shall we look at how shiny it is?  How circular?  No, we listen to it, and review the music that we hear, and (for the sake of the argument) this is the same as you get on a vinyl version.  So to pigeon-hole all music as being compact discs is short sighted, ignorant and lazy.
I personally own more vinyls than CDs, and while CDs (up until a few years ago) made up the vast majority of music sales, it's just not true any more.  You can still buy this year's records on vinyl, as you can on CD and on the itunes.
This is also silly, given the number of reviews of Beatles, Led Zep, Rolling Stones, Pink Floyd, The Who, and many many others, all of whom were releasing records long before CDs and digital music were even thought of.  To to say that Beatles falls under the Compact Disc banner is unbelievable.  I have 17 Beatles vinyls (yes, there are some duplicates) and no CDs.  By your logic, this means I have no Beatles albums, because they're not on Compact Disc.
In summary - You might think that I'm making rather a large fuss about a title for music reviews, but it's worth it because everything I have said is true.  Compact Disc is a storage medium, same as vinyl or cassette tape or HDD, so to classify all music as being on compact disc is absolutely ridiculous.  Call the section Records.
Sort it out UG.

author: seemeel
text:
Quote by Colohue
but in reality it still means that vinyl record.
I disagree.  Even today, bands talk about their new record, don't they?  And unless they're Mick and Keef they're probably not going to do a vinyl pressing.
When vinyl was the
only
format for storing music, the term record (still generic) was only ever applied to vinyl, so the two became somewhat synonymous.  However, today we have multiple formats and I think the term 'record' applies equally to music stamped in vinyl as it does to 1s and 0s burnt onto a piece pf plastic.  The term that is only ever applied to vinyl (though it's equally as valid for any other format) is
LP
(long playing - 42 minutes!).
However, I concede that the term
album
is just as appropriate, for the majority of recordings.  But what about an EP, for instance, or a demo record?  These are not albums (in the traditional sense), so maybe that is another thing to consider.
And talking about the fact that when this website was set up, CDs were in their heyday - so what?  That's no excuse for failing to make progress.  What if the website had been set up yesterday, when digital music sales account for more income to the labels than CD sales?  Just because it was the prevailing format of that time doesn't make it universal.  I hope you see my point.

author: rebelmidget
text:
I feel like there should be different forums or sub-forums for Poetry, Lyrics, and Fiction.
The reason for this being, many who post in the S&L forum are first time and developing songwriters who aren't necessarily getting the types of feedback they expect and need to grow.
I often see lyrics critiqued as if they were a poem. Internet English professors lay into some posts for their simplicity or forced rhymes as if they were critiquing legitimate poetry instead of simple lyrics. This can be discouraging and detrimental to the progress of young kids who go from writing what they feel to writing to impress a sweater-vest clad Indie college student with a Macbook who thinks he knows everything about everything.
By allowing UG'ers to post their creations as either Poetry, Lyrics, or Fiction you would allow for more focused and productive discussion of all three forms of writing.
Just a thought.
Let me know if I'm totally off base here.

~b

author: rebelmidget
text:
Quote by nightraven
there's not that much difference between poetry and lyrics. and are you upset because someone's piece got a proper critique? this is the most absurd thread ever. how can you grow as a writer if you're being praised for writing ****.
besides, dividing the forum like you said would confirm the already massive split between the regulars and the 'newbies'.
You're totally missing the point
and there is a big difference between poetry and lyrics.
There is a split and it should be acknowledged. It's not necessarily a split between regulars and noobs, but more between people who are into poetry and all of it's artistic merit and people who are just writing songs.
I said nothing about praising ****. I give good critiques with constructive criticism to new writers. Sometimes I have a hard time not lmao-ing some of their lines. But I don't treat their songs as if they were a Franz Wright poem.

author: rebelmidget
text:
The point I'm making is that a song and a poem should each be approached with their own mindset. They are two distinct forms of writing and I think it would be beneficial for a line to be drawn between the two via separate forums.
The forum title is deceptive in a way because it is called Songwriting and Lyrics, but many of the posts are free verse poetry, streams of consciousness, or any number of pieces that aren't lyrics, and I don't think I've ever seen a thread discussing songwriting itself.
All I'm suggesting is a more organized forum and a differentiation between two art forms.
As I said I could be totally off base. I have no idea what the logistics of doing it would be because I don't know the first thing about maintaining  a website.

Additional subforums are extremely hard to justify.  zappp is very resistant to add any unless very strong justifications can be made.  Just getting S&L Techniques added required a ton of great deal of thought in the decision making process.  But if songwriters aren't getting the types of feedback they need, S&L should be looking for what the causes and possible solutions are.
Quote by rebelmidget
I often see lyrics critiqued as if they were a poem. Internet English professors lay into some posts for their simplicity or forced rhymes as if they were critiquing legitimate poetry instead of simple lyrics. This can be discouraging and detrimental to the progress of young kids who go from writing what they feel to writing to impress a sweater-vest clad Indie college student with a Macbook who thinks he knows everything about everything.
This indeed can be a problem, both ways.  Songsters critiquing poetry and prose as if it were a song.  Writers approaching songs with only poetry objectives in mind.
All writing
does
share some common elements, and poets have great skills when it comes to assisting in the songwriting process.  But vastly different objectives take priority in songs as compared to poems.  It takes an awareness of these differences for those critiquing to be effective.
Quote by rebelmidget
By allowing UG'ers to post their creations as either Poetry, Lyrics, or Fiction you would allow for more focused and productive discussion of all three forms of writing.
Even were it easy to add additional forum divisions between Poetry, Lyrics, and Fiction, it would probably be unwise to do so.  By having all within one forum, it forces those involved in the critique process to be exposed to other disciplines.
In my humble opinion, a more effective solution to the problems you've voiced would be to have those critiquing approach the writings with the proper frame of reference.
Simply stating (in the preface to a piece) the type of work (song, poem, prose, fiction) gives those who would critique it a valuable piece of info to start with.  In addition, the preface can include the style of feedback the author wishes to have for that particular piece.
To segregate the songwriters from the poets does a great disservice to both.
I suggest taking this discussion to the S&L Feedback thread.  Not with the intent to segregate, but rather to explore ways to get the writers more and better feedback of a type they prefer.
To be blunt:  Additional subforums are not in the cards.  But improvement of what the existing forums have to offer is always a desired objective.
Best of luck

author: NSpen1
text:
As it stands this is really counter-intuitive and unhelpful.
Cb
Abm
Gb
Ebm
Db
etc.
It's very silly to have to look halfway down the list or right at the bottom to find a common key.
When the list of keys was added, someone said it was based on something to do with solfège, but that doesn't mean it makes any sense.
The obvious way is to make the list with the most common keys first / by order of least sharps and flats.
C
Am
G
Em
F
Dm
D
Bm
Bb
Gm
A
F#m
Eb
Cm
You can work the rest out.
Or you could adjust it slightly based on how frequently certain keys are used on guitar, so e.g. E major would be higher.
Then again, if you wanted to make it easy for people to find the key they're looking for
C D E F G A B  followed by the same with sharps, then flats. Then the same with minor or actually C Cm D Dm, etc could be better.
or start from A if you really want to dumb it down
That would still be better than the current order.

author: N04Hz_Ark
text:
Hello Ultimate Guitar Team,
As some of your team are probably aware, there was an exploit in your system that allowed downloading 'Official' and even removed/blocked tabs from your site. Congratulations on fixing it.
I am creating this thread in hopes of getting a better understanding of the law behind why some tabs are not able to be shared to this website, even if they are
user-submitted
,
user-created
and
user-interpretated
.
I find it extremely ridiculous that artists and labels demand your website to comply with them in terms of removing their songs that have been tabbed out by your users. It's quite honestly heart-breaking – and your site might even start to receive more of these 'copyright claims' so to speak – to see hundreds of tabs – that are important culturally, and even for improving ones musicianship – being removed from being learnt.
For example, Rage Against The Machine's "
Killing In the Name
" is "about revolution against racism and authority abuse of power […] and has been noted for its distinctive guitar riffs".
You cannot learn this song on Ultimate Guitar.
What will happen to Ultimate Guitar when more artists and labels demand your website remove tabs, that your own users created?
Ultimate Guitar has one of the most important websites in my lifetime. I have learnt so many songs and riffs from
user-created tabs
.I have even taken several hours
creating my own
. I get upset when people edit them taking my credits off, I would only get even more upset when they get completely taken down from the artist themselves.
So, what is their reasoning? Do they want to sell their own songbooks? Sure. Artists like August Burns Red want to sell you their songbook. They deserve that right, and I'm not arguing against that. What I'm arguing for is when artists like August Burns Red decide to not allow user-created tabs to be shared to this website, but they only half-ass their own songbooks. I am yet to see
any
songbook that has a higher quality level-of-detail compared to what users have submitted to this website. For reference, you have the ability to purchase PDF and Guitar Pro files from their stores. But guess what? Most of them are guitar only and don't even feature all the correct instrumentation; too lazy to do drum notation.
But what about artists that don't do songbooks? As far as I'm aware, Rage Against the Machine don't have any form of 'official songbook' where I can learn their songs on guitar. Is there no 'legal' way for fans and musicians to learn these songs? All I can say is: I'm glad I started playing guitar over a decade ago, where I was able to view how to play "
Killing in the Name
".
Ultimate Guitar needs to do better. Your users are with you, but when everything gets removed, will we care, or will we find some other website?

author: pat1984v
text:
I'd like to recommend a new feature for Ultimate Guitar: the ability to display lyrics alongside any instrument's tab or notation, not just the vocal part.
Why This Feature?
Currently, lyrics are tied to the vocal part. However, musicians playing other instruments often need to see the lyrics for various reasons:
Timing: Drummers, bassists, and guitarists frequently use lyrics as cues for song structure, transitions, and phrasing, ensuring their parts align perfectly with the vocals.
Singing Along: Many instrumentalists enjoy singing along while playing. Having the lyrics visible with their own instrument's tab makes this much easier, eliminating the need to constantly switch focus or memorize the lyrics separately.
Thank you for consideration

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1742262
Researching sharps and flats is more helpful, considering that search only allows searches for 3+ characters.
The guitar was not made to be a flat instrument, though. In standard tuning, it lends itself most easily to sharp keys Em, E, G, D, and A. Transposition has always lent itself to sharps automatically, and if you log out and try the transposition tool, you'll see that it's so.

Does anyone else think it would be a good idea to have a total post count by/near our names in the forums?

author: Hydra150
text:
We do have post counts - click on a person's username to see their profile, where it'll give their post count.
I'm not bothered about whether this is also displayed next to the avatar, I suppose it could give some users something to be proud of, but we have to remember that the number of posts doesn't always correlate with the quality of posts - giving the post count prominence could give talkative idiots a sense of authority. It wasn't too long ago that every other post in The Pit was mocking someone's join date, this could be another distraction to worthwhile discussion.
It's also worth noting that the current post counter doesn't include posts in the off-topic forum. I wouldn't be opposed to changing that, or having another number in brackets next to it including The Pit, but I understand why it's the way it is.

author: Spamwise
text:
So I was thinking it might be cool to add in a couple new options for tabs. Specifically, "genre" and "difficulty". I realize that these are both very broad and relative terms, but for the "genre" search option it'd just be really broad. for example, instead of having "thrash metal" and "nu metal", there'd be "metal", and instead of "jazz fusion" or "smooth jazz" there'd be "jazz". I think this would be a good option for people who have little experience in a specific genre, but would still like to learn songs from that genre. Classifying difficulty would be a little harder, as there are no real standards for difficulty. Another thing that would be nice is an "advanced search", where you could enter the artist and song name. So if what you're searching is a common song name you wouldn't have to go through tons of pages to find the song you want.
just some ideas.

author: rcheetah
text:
UG doesn’t accept translated versions of songs. I got this.
But apart from the fact, that this rule is – thankfully – not enforced consequently, I don’t get the reason behind this.
UG is a tool to find and play chords and other notations. For doing so, it even has features like autoscroll and transposition. But translated versions of songs are rejected. Why is that? It’s very hard to play a song for example in german, with english lyrics. You can’t see where to change chords, you can’t sing along, and in general it gives you a headache. So the solution would be, to copy it into your Word, change the lyrics and rewrite the chords just to play it. But isn’t writing and viewing chords, what UG is there for?
So why are translated versions not welcome? I see why it’s not a “version“, this way things would get very cluttered. But adding it with the translated title seems totally fine with me.
I UG doesn’t want that, why don’t you add a feature to change languages similar to versions (a drop down to switch languages). So it would stay connected with the original song, but still has the translated version.
I think this would be way better, than just rejecting every translation, just because of … well … yeah … thats the point: why?
Ps: To be clear, I’m not talking about translated lyrics that are there to understand what the original lyrics mean. I’m talking about versions of a song in a different language. So versions that are singable in this language.

author: rcheetah
text:
mechanicact1
I think you completely missed my point.
Yes, they will have the same chords. And yes, atm UG considers it a duplicate. But that doesn’t mean they aren’t useful or should have no right to exist on this platform.
That’s my point and my suggestion: to make translated versions a valid contribution to the site. And hence I am in the
Site Suggestion
forum.
And yes, I know I could save them as a personal tab. Actually, everyone could save every song as a personal tab. So why is it, that there are public versions of Nothing Else Matters on UG at all? Why doesn’t every user write them for him-/herself, and saves it as a personal tab? Because sharing the tabs is the point of UG. One person does the work for one song, and everyone else will profit from his work. A community.
That is why there are for example german versions of “Boldly I approach” on UG, although this would be considered a duplicate at the moment. Because there are hundreds of people who will use this version to play the song. Don’t believe me? Ver 1 has over 100 Ratings! And only a fraction of the people using it will be actually rating it. So hundreds if not thousands of people prefer this version over the original english version. It isn’t clutter that nobody would use. I explained the reason for that in my first post. It’s hard to play from a sheet of a different language.
So to conclude:
It is useful, it is reasonable, it does follow the spirit and the purpose of UG, and everyone will profit.
So why is it prohibited, and not embraced?
And I don’t want to be the guy that just moans, and doesn’t come up with something constructive. Thats why I made a suggestion on how to implement it without losing the connection to the original song. That was the only reason that I could make up in my mind, why UG may doesn’t want translated versions.

author: netwiznick
text:
Having done a search, this seems to be a long standing issue - I'm on Windows, don't know if it's the same on other platforms, but it would appear to be so.
I have mapped midi foot pedals to the up and down buttons on my keyboard. However, this has the effect of scrolling through the notes on official tabs, rather than moving the page up and down. Since the left and right arrows already do this, there's no need to hijack the up and down for the same effect. Using the down or right arrows on the keyboard will scroll the page down when you get to the end of what's being displayed, but the same doesn't happen in reverse. If you scroll back up the cursor/position in the song is above what's being displayed, and you have to keep scrolling until the display suddenly jumps and you have to find your position again.
SO
- make the up and down arrows scroll the page as normal, not scroll through the notation
- keep the cursor position in the notation in view all the time
For anyone else reading this with the same issue I'm going to try mapping the midi to mouse scrolls.
Edit: I've got the mouse scrolls working - arrow up and down would still be better though, as then I can program it to continue until I release the switch. As it is I have to repeatedly press the switch to scroll.

author: brettsanace
text:
I'm sure this will be dismissed out of hand but I'll put it forward anyway.
I know that the strums in patterns can be displayed in different colours because when you listen to them they highlight red, and, I'm not sure when, but I have also seen then highlight blue. It would be helpful if, when entering a pattern, that the submitter could indicate a chord change eg "Shift+C" or "Enter" or whatever you want, which would change the colour of the following strums until the next chord change when they would revert back to the original colour ie Red, Blue, Red, Blue etc. I'm not suggesting a different colour for each chord, simply alternating colours to reflect when the chord changes occur.
I know, as most people who read these forums tend to be more advanced players, you are probably all thinking this is unnecessary as it is obvious when the chord changes occur but I believe it would be helpful for beginner players. For example, I have seen many strumming patterns that are 4 bars long, which means the strumming is different for each bar and sometimes the chord changes occur at the beginning of each bar, sometimes they happen mid bar, and sometimes they happen at the end of the bar and are tied over to the next bar.
This could be implemented in two ways:
When creating the pattern and when displaying the pattern on the site the strums actually display in the alternating colours. This would be easier when creating the pattern. It doesn't matter if the colours are black and red, or red and blue, or whatever you prefer. Of course this would stuff up the "listen/play" function which highlights the currently black strums in red in time with the audio (except the highlighting and audio aren't actually synchronised at the moment (see
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1811122#6
)). However, this feature could still be kept by using a different colour or simply bolding the strums in time with the audio.
When creating the pattern and viewing it on the site the strums still appear as black but the alternating colours appear during the "listen/play" feature ie when highlighting the strums in time with the audio.
I prefer the first option.
I realise that whilst a strumming pattern may be consistent throughout the song/verses/choruses, the chord changes may not always be consistent, (though generally they are), and in these cases it would not be necessary to use this feature when creating the pattern ie never enter "Shift+C" in which case the pattern would simply continue to display as all black strums (as would all of the existing strumming patterns until such time as they are edited/corrected).

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
brettsanace
Hi.
Thanks you for the detailed suggection
You're right, it can be helpful for beginners but there are two pitfalls.
At first, we want the strumming's interface to be pretty simple. Your idea extends functionality of the patterns but at the same time it makes the interface harder to understand and use (new buttons, new symbols, new shortcuts, new rules).
At second, now we're using only one chord in the playback of a pattern regardless to the song key and chords. So if we use
coloured strums to highlight chord changes, we'll have to use actual chords in the playback.
I think, a logical extension of your idea is to show strumming patterns in a tab pro interface where you can also see chord shapes, etc. It's not bad, but it contradicts our original idea

author: brettsanace
text:
mandelstamdavid
It really only requires one more command. You already use Shift+Arrow and Ctrl+Arrow, you could maybe use Alt+Arrow to indicate the chord/colour change (not sure what to do if the chord change occurs on an emphasised or muted strum). Maybe simply a toggle colour switch somewhere rather than a command - that way you just enter the pattern as normal but each time you want to switch colours you just click the colour toggle before entering the strum (it only requires 2 colours so a toggle would be fine).
I don't think it would be necessary to use a different chord sound for the strums. It is just meant to be a visual timing aid. If people want to hear the actual chord sounds they can listen to Youtube or mouse over the chord chart in the tab. I also realise that generally this feature would not be required but there are some strumming patterns where it would be really useful, and as such
I really don't think it would take much to implement this. As I said you are already using different coloured strums so it just requires a mechanism for the person entering the pattern to indicate when the colours should change. I also would not see the need to retrofit all strumming patterns with the coloured strums but over time I would think the ones that needed it might get corrected and of course the feature would be available for new patterns added.

author: mandelstamdavid

brettsanace
At first glance it requires one command, a couple of icons and an explanation of these commands and icons. Howbeit, I'll save your idea to our backlog and let's wait a similar feedback from other users

author: The Madcap
text:
I made this comic in a thread in the Pit (
Click here to see
) and it's basically about how it's annoying how the forum, when you click last page, always takes you to the very bottom of the page once it's done loading to the last post. And these were some of the responses to the comic:
Quote by StewieSwan
I hate that shit, too.  Especially if I'm about to click a link or something and the page decides to take that very moment to jump to the post.  RAAAAGE
Quote by LordBishek
And me. I just noticed the stupid "last page" and "last post" buttons have the same functionality, seems really pointless. If you make a thread in SS, I'm sure it'll be considered. Let me know and I'll put in my support.
Quote by OneHappyCamper
You are not alone there, Madcap.
Quote by Gibson_SG_uzr55
Madcap, I concur
. Whendid that start? It didn't used to do that.
1. Like LordBishek said, we have two links very close to each other serving the same function.
2. I don't think users mind having to scroll down to see the last post. If they do, they can still have the option by clicking last post.
3. This is an active forum, and often times if you leave the forum for 2 minutes, a thread can have 10 or even 20 posts that you haven't read yet, so the feature takes you passed that, and you have to scroll up in order to see the other posts, which often times in conversational.
4. It's very annoying, especially in threads where lots of pictures are posted.
5. "Last Page" and "Last Post" are clearly two different things, so it makes no sense that they serve the same function.
That's my argument. It's a small annoyance that tons of users (especially in active forums like The Pit) can feel and agree with I'm sure, and I see no reason why it's more beneficial to have them both take you to the last post.
In short, I'm not saying to
completely
eliminate the feature. I'm simply saying that clicking "Last Page" should
only
take you to the last page, and nothing more. While "Last Post" (which is a link all the way to the right of the thread, under date and time) will actually take you to the last post.
Thank you, fine young gentlemen.

One of the reasons all the for the changes in the home page was to increase the traffic there and improve users' awareness of activities all across UG.  A separate page dilutes that a bit.  Less reason to go to the home page.  Adding more entries and a scroll feature to the UG Community module might be possible.  But adding a filter would be tricky.
The Widgets are a little different than the rest of the modules on the home page.  The are only seen by members who are logged in.  There is a stack of data, probably in the user's account settings, that holds the preferences for the individual user regarding which Widgets are being used and the specific kind of information those widget provide.  You can edit many of the widgets for according to what you want them to do.
But anyone who isn't logged in won't have unique account settings.  Making options available would be annoying for people who aren't members of the site.  With nowhere to store the settings, it would revert to whatever default, every time they refresh the page.

author: NSpen1
text: Yeah, you can't submit two versions with the same title, it won't let you do that.  But what some people have done in the past is submitted them by adding "live", "acoustic" or "ver2" to the title.  Then once they're in the queue or in the case of higher level authors, on the site (as they bypass the queue), the title can be changed by a Tab Mod.  This seems to work ok as long as there are enough differences between two versions of a song to justify a second tab.

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
JuHeMo
Hi. You can upload different tabs for live and acoustic versions and also for recordings but don't forget to write version descriptions. Tabs must be really different, not the same with a different meta information. What about different tunings and capo... what is the main goal of these new versions?  We already have a transpose option and you can also write advices to people in the tab

author: JuHeMo
text:
mandelstamdavid
My experience is that I can't upload different versions, even with different meta (Live, Acoustic) markings. Others have confirmed this.
In most cases, using the transpose feature is acceptable. However, I don't think it is particularly obvious to beginners that transposing DOWN by X steps, and playing with capo UP by X frets, keeps the same chord pitch.
For me, it is important to present a good chord voicing/fingering. This can be particularly valuable for atypical chords. In alternate tunings or capo positions, the resulting chord names sometimes just don't align as a simple transposition.  An author could make notes about alternate tunings and capo positions, but in the end, a separate tab/chord may be cleanest. The impression I get is that less is more when publishing tabs. Stick to the format. Limit the fluff.
Also, transposing is not supported for tablature - only chords.
If it doesn't make sense to change, then so be it.  Just a "Site Suggestion", after all.  Or, is it a bug?  Depends how the programmers and admins intended it to work.
Thanks for considering.

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
JuHeMo
Thanks for the detailed answer
We don't allow authors to publish transposed versions because we want our catalog to be orderly and useful. If we stop rejecting these tabs, our catalog will become hard to use very quickly. Also,  it requires a lot of changes in the site structure (including UG IQ system) that we dind't plan.
I think, the best way is to create a one tab that include all of transposed versions, chord shapes, notes and advices. Our rules don't forbid it

But writing books is no easy task.  And most authors would want to have their own names as the "brand identity". author: wowdude03
text:
Hi i have some issues with the voting system and wish to know if other users feel the same.
So, the reason i joined this community is to learn songs. If i dont know a song, and i think i need help with it, then a Tab community seems a good place.
From one side this idea of having a group that share their interpretations on songs is awesome because many songs dont have official transcriptions available, or because these "official" ones are not that good. So with many people working together this problem can be overcome. So far so good.
I have an issue with the tab rate/voting system (or with how people deal with it) that is:
its a classic "5 star" system.  The interesting point is that 4 stars is "Accurate" and 5 stars is "Excelent".
First thing i asked myself was : "- how can a transcription be more than accurate?"" but oh well, lets see the tabs. Then i chose my favorite band and checked its available tabs here. Well what i found was really discouraging.
Most of the "5 star" tabs i checked contained many errors, wrong and missing notes, techniques etc.  So the next thing i thought was "- how can a wrong tab be avaluated excellent when it is not even accurate....
My point is, the way the system works (or the way people use it) makes us learn wrong stuff believing we are getting something "more than accurate".
You guys will probably not change the voting system, so the solution i can come up with is:  You guys should encourage people to vote more, to rate more the tabs. BUT the important thing is they should be encouraged to try to be accurate when evaluating one. People shouldnt vote 5 stars because "the song is cool". Or even if it is a good tab, with all instruments and all, if they find ANY importand mistakes, they should be encouraged to vote 3 stars since "worth learning" is much more realistic to any tab that is not 4"accurate".
The reality for most tabs with 5 stars i checked is, it had errors (an "A" note where it should be a "G" etc) so if we are being real here, it should get 3 stars.
Seriously, its very sad that people learn songs wrong, believing they are getting it right.
People HAVE to be more consientious in their voting, so people KNOW that the tab needs improving and someone can do something. If the tab is "sold as perfect", most people wont try to question it.
Another suggestion other than try to estimulate people to be more critic when voting, is that the comment section below the tab should be changeable. People should be able to Delete or Edit their comments  below the tabs.  This way we could get better feedback. Also the newer comments should be displayed first and the older for last. Because the tabs are suposed to be updated, right? Makes more sense that when someone is downloading a tab he/she can check the last/more updated comments, and not the 6 year old ones (the newer ones are hidden and we have to click ans scroll down to read, its not good).
I am just being brief here, and i know this is a "BIG" discussion that involves the very core of how we use this site, but i wanted to mention this since i could not find these concerns anywhere.
regards,
Eddie82

author: davidst.vz
text:
In case anyone wants to know, I finally figured this out. You can't change any settings on the website they're all taken from the Guitar Pro file.
The web player ignores a lot of GP file settings, but it does use track volumes.  So just set volumes for the website in the file, and use your effects chain to adjust the volume for good guitar pro playback.
For instrument selection, it uses MIDI program.  Switch from RSE to MIDI mode, choose a MIDI program (i.e. instrument) then switch back to RSE.  The UG website will use the MIDI instrument selected even though you're using RSE in Guitar Pro. UG just ignores all the RSE settings.

author: ferdinandvandam
text:
I've been a paid member of Ultimate Guitar Tabs for several years now. As a piano player who mostly plays chords, the app has been a great help. I really appreciate the features like linking to YouTube and Spotify, the ability to transpose songs, and the option to simplify chords—those have truly made a difference in how I learn and play.
That said, I've recently decided to cancel my subscription. The reason? It's honestly a bit frustrating that every time I open the app, I’m met with a full-screen ad promoting in-app purchases or courses. I understand the need for promotion, but these pop-ups have become increasingly intrusive and difficult to dismiss. It feels like I'm being sold to within an app I already paid for—and that just got too annoying over time.
I still think UG Tabs is a fantastic tool, and I hope the team takes this kind of feedback to heart. Maybe I'll return someday if the user experience becomes more focused again on making music, not selling extras.

author: UG Support
text:
ferdinandvandam
first off all, thank you so much for being a part of the UG community for all these years—and for such a thoughtful, honest message. It really means a lot that you took the time to share both what you’ve enjoyed and what’s been frustrating.
We’re genuinely sorry to hear you’ve decided to cancel your subscription. It’s always tough to see a longtime member leave, especially one who’s found real value in features like chord simplification, transposing, and YouTube/Spotify integration. That’s exactly the kind of experience we want to provide—helpful, musical, and inspiring.
Your feedback about the pop-ups is totally fair. We’ve been hearing similar concerns from other users, and I want you to know that we’re not brushing it off. We’re actively collecting all this input and sharing it directly with our Dev team. Finding the right balance between promoting new tools and respecting the experience of paid users is something we
are
working on.
We absolutely hope to welcome you back one day—and if you do decide to give UG another shot, we’ll do our best to make sure it feels like the music-focused space it should be.
Wishing you all the best in your piano journey

I play guitar and bass.  I've found that using interval numbers instead of chord names is much easier to learn.  For example, a song that is in G might use a G-Em-C-D progression.  However, if I want this song in a different key, I need to have a different chord chart with all different chords.  By using numbers, I can have the same chart for all keys!  This progression is 1, 6m, 4, 5, no matter what key is being used.
Several worship song sites are offering numbers as an option now, such as CCLI SongSelect, Worship Together, and Essential Worship.
If UG would implement this feature, it would easily become my one-stop shop for getting chords to songs for both guitar and bass.  It could simply be a transpose option, such as other sites do.  Any chance of getting this moved to the front burner?

author: Deliriumbassist
text: I can't speak for my fellow bass mods, but I feel it isn't necessary. I very much hold a belief that anyone can learn from anybody. The bass forum is a relatively established community at the moment (albeit it is an open one), which means new users may find it difficult to find their place as it were. A karma system would simply make that harder for new users. In the bass forum, if something is answered wrongly, or incompletely, there will often be a decent rebuttal or addition from someone. It isn't like bad advice is rampant throughout the forum. Forums are about discussion and learning, and I feel a karma system may actually take away from that. The joy of having everyone equal is that it teaches a lot about perspective and application which is important in music.

author: thanksgiving
text:
First off I know the Pit is not a doctor.
The idea of this thread wouldn't be to diagnose people. The reason to post in this thread is either:
A) You have seen a doctor and you have been diagnosed with "insert word here" and people who have been through the same situation can give morale support or maybe little things that help them along the way.
or
B) You are going to see a doctor and you have an appointment, but you are looking for ideas of what you might have, just to put your mind at ease or to let you search up some information about it before you see a Doctor, just to get a little pre-information.
I know you might get some people coming in who won't want to see a Doctor, but I think that this thread and the users in it would give the person more of an incentive to see a doctor, than if they just kept their worries to themself.
It's up to you guys and maybe you might be able to suggest some changes or add some more to this idea.
Just a thought.

There are two main ways that the chord tabs are used: Auto-scroll on the screen, and printed out on paper. Here's the thing.  Something like Wikipedia has a huge number of highly educated contributors and editors.  And their database is immense.  It doesn't make much sense to attempt to duplicate that on UG.  And in terms of UG specific stuff, it becomes a chore to manage for what is likely to be relatively little usable input.
Then there's the overhead in additional server space and a new structure for the new database.  These things cost.  Real dollar investment, paying for programmers time, server/cpu resources.  There are tons of areas where existing UG structure could use improvement.  Some of that is happening right now, but delays are inevitable.  Adding a massive project would dilute the improvement efforts as well as members using what's already here.
Regarding "Pit" issues.  Wiki databases work best with factual/historical information.  The Pit is more about opinion, subjective matters, and personal tastes.  Most of what goes on in the Pit would be poor choices for a database.  Disagreement and bickering about differing opinions/philosophy is fine in a forum environment.  But when it comes to generating a database, that's a whole nuther thang.  And who makes the final determination on which edit stays?  A complicated system of hierarchy would have to arise or there would be chaos.
Just seems like opening a big ole can of worms.

However, in an violinist's orchestral part it would likely be B#. Why?  For the same reason I stated earlier.  Sometime it's not always about being right?  Classical world and pop world use mostly the same music theory, but not always.
In the key of C the vi6 for classical arrangers the notes are a,c,e and f. (we do only use notes in that key unless altered)  In the pop world an Am6 is a,c,e and f sharp.  Different.

They would never write in C# in the strictly pop world. Db, yes, but not C#. They'd use a capo or transpose to avoid C# if possible. author: brettsanace
text:
UG Support
mendace
Just to re-iterate earlier comments, this thread should be closed or definitely unstuck/unpinned.
The intention of this sticky thread was simply to make people aware of the link to the "Ideas Center" (I know this as it was originally my suggestion to create this sticky thread). Now users come to this thread and when they realise the Ideas Center no longer exist they simply post their suggestions as comments on this thread. This has resulted in this thread becoming a sub/pseudo Site Suggestions forum within the Site Suggestions forum.
If this thread were closed people would post their suggestions as threads in the Site Suggestion forum as was the original intention, rather than as comments within this thread.
The advantages of this are that
UG Support
only need to check the main forum for new threads (suggestions) rather than also having to sort through new comments in this thread looking for those that are new suggestions. Also, due to the coloured icons beside each thread in the main Site Suggestion forum it is easier to see when new comments have been added to each thread. Also for users if the suggestions are posted as threads in the Site Suggestion forum (as they should be) rather than as comments in this thread it is easier for people to search to see if the suggestion has already been made and simply add their comment to the relevant thread.
Now for one final suggestion before this thread is hopefully closed. In the Site Suggestion forum (and probably other forums) when you mouse over the blue pin next to a sticky post it says "Sticky forum" but should say "Sticky thread".

Corrections
Overall, a good correction may have more value than a new submission in that it improves the catalog and at the same time removes a "Bad Tab"

author: ryansbus8
text:
Three suggestions.
Download Official tabs.  You can go into the site and download all the UG Pro tabs, but you cannot download the official tabs. It would be nice if you could download official tabs to have them offline on a computer and just have them in general. It seems weird to me that the Official tabs are pro tabs made by UG Staff but you can't download them like Pro tabs.
Full song length shots. I think it would be a cool idea to be able to pull up the song you are trying to play in shots, and have the shots take the song length +5 seconds on each end for you to get ready and end the song so you can play through an entire song in one shot. The short length that you have now makes it kind of disappointing and not as fun as being able to play through the entire song.
Make it so Bass tabs can be changed to intro. Please change it so that Bass tabs can be changed to just intro and not the whole song. There are many people who put work into their Bass tabs but then their tabs get a bunch of comments and rejections just because they wanted to make an intro piece for the Bass, but since you can only make full song tabs for Bass, they are forced to tab out the whole song. This just seems a bit weird to me considering that regular guitar tabs can be changed to intro only, and sometimes Bass only plays in the intro too.
Edit (New suggestion): Add in the option to make outro tabs, for both tab and bass, probably not chords.
Edit (New suggestion 2): Change it so that when you are mentioning another person, their name for the mention does not go straight to the bottom of the comment, but instead goes to where you're typing. It is super annoying when you are making a comment and are in the middle of the page, but want to mention somebody because then their mention name goes to the bottom of the comment box and you have to reorder the entire comment just to put it where you want it. This to me is one of the dumbest features of UG commenting and it would be so much better if the mention went where your typing cursor is instead of assuming you want to mention them at the very bottom of the comment.
Edit (New suggestion 3): Make it so certain special characters can be allowed into song titles. There are lots of songs that have certain symbols and special characters, take a song by The Fray. The song on UG has to be called Over My Head Cable Car, but the song is actually Over My Head (Cable Car) because the Cable Car piece is an alternate title, but since you can't put in parentheses, you can't name the song correctly, which seems dumb to me since we always say songs need to be named correctly.
Edit (New suggestion 4): Allow .png and .jpeg attachments in forum threads, and attach regular photos into the text body instead of just link URLs. It's dumb that you can't attach regular photos in normal ways, you can only attach online photos through URL links, and that's just dumb.

text:
In a recent interview, the Pink Floyd guitarist all but killed the hopes and dreams of a full-on reunion.
Hopes were high after the band reunited for one gig at Live 8 in '05, but, alas, it doesn't look promising, reports Shoutmouth.com.

"Everything went so well [with my last album], I can’t see why I would want to be going back to that old thing. It’s very retrogressive. I want to look forward, and looking back isn’t my joy.

author: Phil Starr
text:
After submitting my first few tabs/chords I am concerned that we may be missing out on quite a lot of new tabs because, frankly, the whole process is offputting.
I've had tabs rejected because of using the wrong font, putting the wrong word in the title (live version) and for not guessing that I was inputting ascii code. At least I think that is why they were rejected because there was no feedback.
Eventually I found 'wtf where is my tab' 'wtf why my tabs have been rejected' 'UG will accept your tabs' and a beginners guide to making tabs and chords but it took me hours to find all this. I would much rather have been playing with my guitar than the computer and that is the point, musicians aren't always computer geeks. We need it easy.
I've three suggestions:
Put the tabbers guides in a more prominent position on the site, like at the front. make the guide pop up automatically when you post a tab for anybody with a low rating/first time tabbers or for everyone but with a button to switch it off.
send an automatic message for rejected tabs to give the tabber the chance to put things right.
Improve the data entry system with more foolproof templates for tab/chords etc. perhaps making it compatible with rtf files or Word documents. (Sorry I do realise how difficult that would be)
UG is a great site and is rapidly becoming the default site for guitarists but it depends on the generosity of the tabbers. Keep up the good work but make it easier for us to grow.

author: cflat
text:
I think most new tabbers get rejected for trying to tab a song that already has more than 5 versions, and it's a popular song. Smoke on the Water by deep purple is probably not the best song to practice your tabbing skills. Find something unique that has very few versions.
Don't copy other peoples tabs, it becomes obvious after awhile.
Get the name of the song right, get the name of the band right. Otherwise it'll just make the searching harder for the viewer. And also, some people do this just to get there version of Smook on the waater by deep purple passed the watchful eyes.
Always do a few searches for the song before you tab it, don't waste your effort on it if there's plenty of them there already. And if you didn't find it on your first search, make sure your spelling is right or includes all the words. (yes I'm repeating myself and I had to edit this paragraph, twice)
Make sure you double check it a few times before submitting, play the tab as if someone else would. I do this multiple times and still submit stuff with errors.
When you submit, click on the preview button. If it doesn't look right, then something is wrong. Fix it, or ask for help in the forums.
There's really only a few simple guidelines to try and follow and you'll be happier you did.
PS. I've had my tabs rejected too for trying to improve on tabs that didn't need much improvement.

author: Schism1985
text:
I'm not going to lie, this issue affects me as well as many other UGers, but I think it really needs to be brought up.
I'll illustrate my point with a subjective example, however I'm sure this is far from a unique case:
Within my first 3 months of using UG I was (admittedly) a complete dumb ass, I was a total "pit monkey" who posted inflammatory comments, contributed nothing useful to the site, made multis etc. etc.
Well after those first 3 months, Carmel banned me (with good reason), because of all of the above reasons (multiple accounts, over lapping warnings from other offenses and so on) this first ban became a single 3-4 month long ban.
The thing is, the ban actually "worked" for me. Once I started using UG again, I almost completely abandoned posting in the Pit and started contributing to other forums, particularly Gear Building and Customizing. Since I've returned I've had 2 lengthy reviews posted on the main page of the site, a comprehensive "Pick Up Buying Guide" thread-- which literally took me hours to compile-- stickied, and have established myself as a helpful and (usually) friendly regular in the GB&C forum.
Here's where the problem is:
Occasionally I commit infringements (the majority of which are accidental) which result in warnings. Because of my prior offenses (which now occurred over 2 years ago), each warning is 60 days long. In short this means that if I make 2 minor infringements within a 60 period I'll be permanently banned from UG even though I haven't been in FOTB for more than 2 years.
Am I the only one who sees something wrong with that? I know I’m not alone here, users like SomeoneYouKnew who make overwhelmingly useful contributions to the site are being permanently banned… regardless of how helpful they are. And yet meanwhile pit monkeys who gain followings are able to repeal old bans through “User Elimination” threads even if they don’t intelligently contribute to the site at all.
I propose a sort of “appeals process” for UGers. This process could apply solely to users who have not been banned for a period of more than “X” years, yet whose past bans could potentially result in them being perma’d for relatively minor infractions.
I’m interested to hear what you all think about this, I really think that it could be done in a way which is both efficient and well executed.

author: the.chortler
text:
I do not participate at Ultimate Guitar any more for a few reasons, mostly personal.  However, I still get the emails telling me that someone has made a "correction" to my tabs.  Sometimes it does not make a big difference, sometimes it is just plain wrong and would ruin it.  I spent a lot of time with the tabs I uploaded, keeping them simple, making sure they were formatted correctly, testing out multiple chords for each one.  As a result every one of my tabs has a rating approaching a 5.   I am tired of coming back and trying out their version and either rejecting it or being disappointed with minor changes.
Here is my suggestion.  Stop allowing anyone to correct a tab if it has good ratings and feedback.  I understand you want to keep duplicates down to a minimum to prevent clutter, but there was a time when the community could rate the tabs and over time the good ones would rise to the top.  Now, the good ones are in danger of being destroyed by being "improved."
I have written out tabs for well over 300 songs that are not currently on Ultimate Guitar.  This is one of the reasons I will not bother to upload them, there is too high of a chance of them being ruined.
I am not angry, just disappointed.

author: pazil
text:
the.chortler
Hi! Thank you for your opinion. Can you please show the tabs which have become worse after the corrections?

author: the.chortler
text:
pazil
, to the best of my knowledge, there are none.  I have returned to the site and rejected the ones that were bad.  I do not have any way that I know of to go back to see which ones those were.  As for the tabs that I did not reject, I do not know if they were eventually approved or not.  Aside from going through my tabs one by one to see if any have a co-author I am not sure how I would ever know that.  Here is the tab that is currently under review:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=542171
They added a verse I am not familiar with.  I do not mind this so much, but in that verse the spacing is messed up and the chords do not appear in the correct places.  They also made very minor chord changes in two places.  They changed a D to a D/F# and a G to a G/B.  Neither one of these ruins the song at all, though I would argue that it is unnecessary.  Unfortunately, when they made that change, the spacing also became messed up at the end of that line.  The contributor mentions that they took the chords from Hymnody.  This is a site similar to Ultimate Guitar, but focused solely on hymns and most of their tabs are not as good.
I do not want to be a jerk and reject every minor change like this, nor do I want to feel like I need to babysit my contributions to make sure no one is messing them up.  Other than preventing corrections to highly rated tabs, I don't have any ideas for how we can work to both improve existing tabs and also keep from making any worse.

author: MH400
text:
Yes, I read the sticky.  I know it says don't ask, but I want to know
why
you're so adamant we can't have one.
Lets look at it this way.
What does the stereotypical band consist of?
Vocals / lyrics
Guitar
Bass
Drums.
We have a lyrics forum, guitar forum and bass forum.  Yet not a drum forum?  You can't say that 'Drums aren't a guitar', because neither are lyrics.  To say this would be double standards.
You can't turn around and say its Ultimate GUITAR dot com, because its Ultimate-guitar.com / off topic / bands and artists / songwriting / band leading / gear ads / news / reviews etc.
The truth is, this isn't just a guitar website anymore.  Its a website based on guitar, with extras added for different interests.  Drums are an interest closely related to guitar (just like Songwriting and band leading), and its blindingly obvious that many of our users play drums.
Plus the fact that UG hosts drum tabs.  Why have tabs but not a forum?  To me, that seems pointless and rather silly.  If the tabs are hosted to attract more users and generate traffic, then surely a drum forum would do the same?
Also, bandwidth obviously isn't an issue.  We have space for a silly 'Llama forum', yet not a useful forum that would be full of help and resources?  Come on, guys.  Seriously?
List of recent Pit Drum threads.
Surely thats proof that it would be active?
The fact of the matter is that:
Users want a drum forum.
It would be active.
It would benefit users.
Bandwidth wouldn't be an issue.
Its closely related to guitar.
This isn't just a guitar website anymore.
There really isn't a valid reason for saying no.
Also, if people keep asking to the extent that you feel the need to include it in the 'Don't suggest these' sticky, then surely it shows its what the users want?
What I want to know is why you keep refusing it.  I've never seen a proper, well thought out answer in a Drum forum request thread.  I've only ever seen it mindlessly get shut down.
I expect the same to happen here, due to it being the mentality of these forums.
I await a reply.

Users think that the (big) EDIT button is the way to edit a tab which is on the site and submit a correction but it isn't.  The (small) Edit button is for moderators to edit a tab and the Suggest correction button is for users to submit a correction with.  The EDIT button is for saving a tab on the site as a personal tab and then making what changes you want to it.
Having two edit buttons is obviously crazy to begin with.
This is a big problem and has been discussed at length over a period of about 2 years but UG still haven't fixed it.
They have claimed that these are special cases, 1 or 2 confused users, or it happens once a week.  This is obviously completely untrue, as
Benster28
said, he and I could both post a dozen cases a day of intended corrections being submitted as new tabs due to the EDIT button.  I think that's a conservative estimate actually.
We got as far as an acknowledgement of the problem and an intention to start a project to rename a button in the coming weeks, but that was then "put off for a while".  And presumably moved to the legendary/mythical backlog.
Meanwhile the confusion continues ... this should be fixed as soon as possible.
If anyone needs any more proof that this isn't a minor problem, or just the odd case, I'm putting all the posts related to the issue from the Site Suggestions thread (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1865844
) below.  Then that can be used for general smaller suggestions as originally intended, and anything about the EDIT button posted here.
There are of course many more posts about it prior to that in other threads on the forum.
We have people apologising for submitting new tabs when they didn't mean to and it's really not their fault, and the very first post from the thread says "Sort out your site, mate".

Regarding the on-going "EDIT" button debate, here's an idea for your consideration:
- Remove the small "Edit" button that allows Level 4 users to edit a published tab
- Remove the "SUGGEST CORRECTION" button at the bottom of every tab
Instead, have a single "EDIT" button located where the current button is. Just as you've done with chords, usernames and contributors, a floating pop-up window could appear with a set of choices when a user hovers over the "EDIT" button. The choices could be labeled as:
1. Submit correction for review
2. Submit brand new version for review
3. Modify and save as personal tab
4. Edit existing tab
A few notes:
- Option 1 would take users to a "Submit Correction to TPA" page (replaces the previous "SUGGEST CORRECTION" button)
- Option 2 would take users to a "Submit New Tab to TPA" page (replaces the previous "PUBLISH TO UG" button in the Save As Personal Tab page)
- Option 3 would take users to the "Save as personal tab" page (no change except the "PUBLISH TO UG" button must be removed)
- Option 4 would allow direct edits and only appear in the pop-up list for Level 4 users (replaces the previous small "Edit" button)
Benefits of this approach:
1. A single Edit button that covers all forms of editing
2. Precise descriptors telling users exactly what their editing is doing within the system
3. A clean user interface that avoids multiple buttons or long button names

author: RmB303
text:
Already posted in the new members Q&A Forum, but a kind soul suggested I might be better off posting here instead, so . . .
Firstly - Hi to all the mods, and please hear my plea.
I was a right handed guitarist for over ten years who had to give up years ago due to a severe accident involving my left hand.
I've now decided to have a go at learning to play left handed, and am finding this site to be a fantastic source of info. - Flattery always pays ;-)
Is there any chance that I (and all the other 'genuine' lefties on this site) could have a forum dedicated towards those of us who play the guitar 'the wrong way round'?
There's some great info here, but all chord shapes and scale/arpeggio patterns require amending before use.
I've already started translating some of the excellent articles on this site so that they are usable by lefties, and would gladly post what I've got so far - along with a link to the original post; and a credit to the original author of course :-)
Could this possibly be done? (I'm sure a certain 'Jimi' and 'Kurt' from Seattle would have approved, as would Mr Iommi, among many others).
The best place could probably be under the 'Instruments' category.
Any other lefties could then start to post what info they have converted, and it could become a great resource for all of us.

author: icronic
text:
I don't really see the purpose of doing that.
99% of the material you'll run across is going to be expressly written for the purpose of right handed players, and even then the only thing that doesn't translate are chord fingerings if they're transcribed horizontally instead of vertically. In this case all you really have to do is mentally flip the image, and remember that the left side is the low E and the right is the high E, instead of vise versa.
Not to mention it could get left handed players in a lot of trouble if they're handed a chart written for a right handed person, and they haven't bothered to learn how to properly read it.
Again, it really shouldn't be too difficult for any lefty to flip things over in their head and as far as I'm concerned, there is no reason at all to rewrite all these chords and things for a left handed person as all it will really do is act as a crutch.
Sure it's confusing at first, but honestly I don't think it took me any more than two weeks to be able to easily read chords and charts and all that.

The first part tells it search only ultimate-guitar.com.  Putting the chord progression in quotes does 2 things.  1, it requires matches on all.  2, it sorts the results so that it shows the hits that were in that specific order (am, dm, g, c, f) show at the top.

In half-step down tuning you play an E shape, you call it an E, the chord diagram is an E, it only _sounds_ a half step lower. Guitar Pro works like that.

author: NSpen1
text:
Adding the stuff from the other thread :
It's because of a fundamental flaw in the system UG uses, and one of the things about the site that most badly needs fixing. You're absolutely right, the chord is played as a G shape and that's the way that anyone sensible is going to be thinking of it. You play a G and because of the half-step tuning it sounds as F#, but you don't want to have to mentally transpose every chord by a half step. The official tabs are slightly different as they're written with the pitches that actually sound whereas the vast majority of tabs written by users in half-step down tuning are written according to the chord shapes you play, which is how it should be done. But because of the system all the chord diagrams are messed up, so if you put G it'll tell you you have to play a G# barre chord.
Sweet Child O' Mine for instance is played as if it was in D, the tuning means it sounds as Db
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/sweet_child_o_mine_official_1910965
This is how it should be written
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/sweet_child_o_mine_chords_176076
More Than Words, you think of it being in G, sounds as F# due to the tuning.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/extreme/more_than_words_official_1982595
This is how it should be written
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/extreme/more_than_words_chords_14087
btw Highway To Hell is not supposed to be in half-step down tuning, it's just that the tuning on that album is all over the place, 30 cents down here, 65 cents down there. It's supposed to be played in A in standard. (And I don't know who on earth thought that was a good strumming pattern to use.)
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/acdc/highway_to_hell_official_1916729
How it should be
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/acdc/highway_to_hell_chords_139966
It's A, D/F#, G, not Ab, Db/F, Gb
Users have resorted to writing tabs for half-step down tuning with the tuning set as standard to avoid the wrong chord shapes, and then writing a note on the tab to say it should be half step down. Previously you were able to at least put the tuning to "not selected" so that it wouldn't wrongly say "standard" but that possibility has been removed. It was also useful for when you had a song in a non-standard tuning that wasn't among UG's list of tunings.
I've posted about it many times, and I still hope that they'll eventually fix it.
Last thread on it
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1814902
And I don't believe any research is needed, I must have given enough examples by now, and I have more if needed of course

I would also really appreciate seeing this fixed.
I think even most of the professional artists that I play are using these tunings as "negative capos" - because you'll see them sometimes choose a different one of these tunings to play the same song depending on they key they want to sing in at the time... I would be shocked if they're thinking, "Ah, now that I'm tuned down, I have to play this standard chord progression as Gb Db Ebm7 Cbadd9."
And for me at least, I also think D tuning is often easier to play with standard tuning shapes. Don't you think novice guitarists would almost surely be less intimidated and confused with D being presented as xx0232 rather than xx1343 (half step down) or 022100 (D tuning)?
I'd also really appreciate being able to have "Drop C#" use Drop D tuning chords. Again, I think it's way easier to think D is 000232 rather than 111343.
If more research needs to be done, I think having someone at UG play through the top tabs in these tunings using the suggested chord shapes would be a lot of evidence that either the tab authors love to use very difficult chords and incorrect keys or that the suggested shapes aren't what the authors intended...

author: maguri
text:
Quote by mandelstamdavid
Ah, it's my mistake. I meant Eb, of course
I'm not confident that all the users understand it like you. Anyway, well, we need to research it. And I agree that for a non-profeccional guitar player it's a hell to transpose all the chords
Not "all" users will understand it like you - right, there might be people who think differently, but I guess they are a tiny, tiny minority.
Everybody will agree that playing an E-shape on a guitar tuned down one semi-tone will sound Eb or D#. But when talking among themselves about how to play the chords,  guitarists will refer to an E-shaped chord as E (making a mental note that the chord will, of course, sound like the tuning of the guitar). I worked and played in recording studios and on stages in Germany, Great Britain and Japan with local and international guitar players and played with professional, semi-professional and hobby guitarists: Professionals and hobby players alike called an E-shape "E", even if it did not sound in E because the guitar was tuned down.  This is how guitarists think and the representation on a site called Ultimate "Guitar" should reflect that, I guess.
Example::
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/the_beatles/for_no_one_chords_17250
Guitar is tuned half-step down. You play C and it sounds in B. Tuning Half-Step-Down is selected in meta data and all the chord shapes that are shown when hovering over the highlighted chord symbols are incorrect. That's non-guitaristic.

author: MaggaraMarine
text:
The outro solo (that you linked here) is in Am, not in Dm and it's actually played over the chord progression of the chorus. The solo in the middle of the song is in Dm and in that case the solo just ends on an A note that sounds good over both keys (it's a very "safe" note in both keys - in the key of Dm it's the 5th and in the key of Am it's the tonic).
It's really all about targeting a chord tone. If you listen to the album version, he plays an ascending scale run that is targeting the A. But actually, any note in the Am chord would work - you could also target C or E. This actually applies to following chord changes in general - you want to target chord tones. This means playing something that leads to the chord tone that you are targeting and you would play the "target tone" exactly when the chord changes.
Here's a lesson on targeting chord tones. Yes, I know he talks about jazz and plays the bass, but the same thing can be applied to rock lead guitar too. Though, in rock music I would say that there's nothing wrong with targeting the root, and actually targeting the 7th of a chord may sound a bit too "jazzy" since most chords in rock music are triads, not 7th chords. So instead of starting with 3rd, 5th and 7th, start with the root, 3rd and 5th.

author: nycounterpoint
text:
It isn't just about the chord charts, though those are helpful.
Sometimes playing the original chord on a ukulele just doesn't produce the right timbre or feeling, even if all the notes are theoretically the same. Fancier chords aren't always completely doable since a ukulele has fewer strings, and even if you can cover all the necessary notes with your four strings, the voicing can be different, like you have an open sounding chord when you need a closed one (yes, you could theoretically use a different fingering, but alternate ukulele fingerings can be extremely impractical); sometimes using a substitution just makes the song fit the instrument better.
Unless it's a straightforward 4-chord song that only uses major and minor and V7 chords, I very often have to make at least one substitution somewhere to achieve the sound I want from my instrument.

But the thing is that's what's happening now. There's no transposition necessary. A C-chord (not shape, which is why the system needs to show a different chord for an identical uke/guitar tab) can be played on the uke and the guitar, piano, whatever, equally and sound the "same". Identical tabs are being copied and approved for uke just so the system will show a uke chord to a uke player. Now if someone improves one of those identical tabs the other remains unedited. Even if they posted the same suggestion one might be approved by one person and and the other rejected by another.
I have put hard work into tabs that are specifically for uke and don't want the current system with a uke category abolished. But there is no need for basic chord tabs to be duplicated. The system should just show uke chords for uke players. It wouldn't even be a "switcher". It would simply show the uke chord diagram for a C 0003 instead of the guitar diagram for C x32010. No one would spend their time making a simple chord/lyric tab for ukulele as it stands now with the current system because it would be rejected as being a duplicate of a guitar tab. -----------------------------------
Basic guitar to uke tutorial for all those confused
: Lets say you have a song in the key of C, and it starts with a C chord. If you want to sound like a uke using your guitar you put a capo on 5 AND transpose down -5 and start with a G-shape, 320003. Those two cancel out and you still can play along and sing to the original in C. You can play the 4 high strings, xx0003, to make it sound more like a uke (a tenor uke specifically, but that's only different than a regular uke by an octave in one string). NOW on the uke you do play that G shape, 0003, and do you know what that is called on a uke? A C-chord. No transposition.

text:
Two issues:
1) When I use the "transpose" function on chord charts, UG tends to only show chords with sharps rather than their flat equivalents that are sometimes more appropriate.
On the UG desktop web interface, there's an option "use flats" which essentially solves this problem for chords since the original chart should have the note degrees correct, but this feature doesn't exist on the android app sadly. It would be great to have this setting on mobile!
2) Secondly, the translation of official tabs to standard notation feature exists on android and iOS but not on the desktop web interface, and it also seems to map all accidentals to sharps resulting in things like G#s in the key of Fm (see Dream On official tab Lead Guitar 2 for example).
It would be really great in this case if there were a cleverer algorithm to map to in-key notes first, and then maybe a simple preference to prefer flats or sharps for out-of-key notes. (or an even clevererer algorithm that I can't think of on the spot
)

author: Baby Joel
text:
Alright, so I searched 'tuning' and looked at the most recent threads, and didn't really find what I wanted.
So basically, when you request a song to be tabbed, you have to enter in what tuning you want the song to be in.
This becomes a problem if you request something that is played by a 7 string, 8 string, is in some bizarre tuning that no one ever ever uses, or if you dont' know what tuning the song is. If you don't know what tuning it's in, how can you be expected to state what tuning it's in?
Basically, I think we need to have an input method where you can state how many strings, and the tuning of each string. Also, I think there should be an option called something like 'Whatever tuning the song is in'. Because frankly, there are too many times when I can't tell whether a song is in Eb or E standard.
If something like this is already implemented, I apologise. As far as I could tell, this hasn't been implemented yet.

author: fanapathy
text:
Hey,
I am assuming at the time that any tab is worth X amounts of points, whether it be chords format, tab format or GP/equivalent format.
If this is the case, it needs to be changed. If it's not the case, this thread should be ignored.
Chords is the most basic form of transcription. Tab is a more detailed approach, while GP typically tries to imitate the entire composition.
From what I've seen, the top contributors on UG by far are the chord submitters. Some of them mash out on average multiple "tabs" per day.
The work of a chord tab is typically googling the lyrics and transcribing the general chords of a song. For a decent transcriber, this can be done in less than half an hour. Tabbing would take a few hours and tabbing more instruments accurately easily takes 10+ hours depending on the complexity of the song.
My point here is that the effort in various forms of submissions vary significantly and therefore should have different value in the ranking system of UG.
I noticed over new years that UG had some public tribute toward top contributors and that the "winner" for the year was some guy who spams out a massive amount of these chord format tabs and had submitted over 600 in a year or something like that (maybe more).
This is an impossible achievement for people who make more detailed tabs and therefore I suggest a more balanced points system on UG.
A side effect of this may be encouraging more GP submissions and a larger catalog of tabs for Tab Pro.
