author: Fox-x-x
text:
Hello guys!
Your ratings didn't disappear. Several tabs just don't have enough votes to be displayed. When a tab gets 3 votes the rating becomes visible.
We've recently launched the new rating system which is more objective and mathematically sophisticated.
You can find the formulas and their verbal interpretations in these posts:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/ug_news/ug_has_a_new_tab_rating_system_now_heres_how_it_works.html
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/article/blog/view?id=8
Overall, here's the effect the new system should have:
1) Tab authors' level won't be affected. Although the level of tab authors depends on the average rating of their tabs, the new system won't affect it. If your level is III, you won't be demoted, no matter how the average rating of your tabs changes within the new system.
2) No fraud. No more 1-star trolling or 5-star rigging. If a tab is not very popular, its rating also depends on the average rating of all UG tabs (which is 4.5), and any bad votes won't decrease the rating too much. And if a tab is very popular and hasdozens of votes, one more bad vote against it won't affect the tabs rating.
3) More objective rating. Since most tabs on UG have a rating of about 4.5, we use this number as a starting point of the tabs' rating. Any vote will increase or decrease the rating, but it takes more than a couple of votes to represent the real users' opinion on the quality of the tab. We think that it takes at least 5 votes to achieve the minimum amount of objectiveness.
4) Bigger chance for new tabs. The best tabs are not always tabs that get many votes. Sometimes a new tab appears on the website and it's much better that any other tab of the same song. Unfortunately, it's hard for it to get to the top. We believe that the new system will help new great tabs become popular.
And one more thing
Soon we will launch the new system aimed at stimulating more rates from users!
Rock on!

author: killergege
text:
Hi,
Following a conversation on the
WTF? Where is my tab?!?!
topic, here are some ideas about the tab submission & validation.
This is a topic that has already been discussed few years ago but I think it would be a good idea to bring it up again.
Prevent any rejection without a reason
, even for a higher level moderator ! I don't understand why there is a need for the
WTF? Where is my tab?!?!
topic : you can explain what you changed when you submit a tab and any "normal" user have to put a reason when they reject a tab. The forum is full of people asking why their tab has been rejected. At least giving a reason might explain some rejections ! Are some moderators rejecting tabs too quickly ? I guess forcing them to also put a reason could reduce the number of messages here.
Add a mandatory dropdown list with common reasons
, in order to indicate the reason in one click - but still leaving the text field to add details, but make it optional.
This dropdown list will simplify a justified rejection and improve consistency.
There should be a common policy amonst the Tab Moderators
, in order to handle the submission the same way, whatever the moderator is. You often encounter tabs rejected by a tab moderator but accepted when submitted unchanged on the "WTF? Where is my tab?!?!" topic.
Make the submission explaination mandatory if another tab already exist.
As I said, users can explain what changed in the tab they submit in order to help validation, but it is not really obvious (it's just a link lost in a lot of text) so few people use it. And add the field in the main "submission" screen ! The user should have a good reason to submit a new version of a tab.
Some people might say that if this field is mandatory, a lot of people might put random text in the field. That's okay. Just add an appropriate rejection reason for that. It would simplify the validator's work in this case as he doesn't need to open the tab before rejecting it
.
The tabber has spent some time (and maybe hours) to create the tab, I guess he can spend 5 minutes explaining why his tab is better than existing ones.
See
this post
, it is the original feature request for this idea.
Prevent the submission of a tab is the user is not registered.
This is a good solution when you are launching a site, but now this is doing more harm than good as nobody will be able to apply any correction and it will push users to submit a new version for only slight corrections.

author: henricdav
text:
Firstly, thanks for a great service!
However, it constantly bothers me that transposed chords don't show up in their "natural" key.
An example: If I transpose a song two steps down which was originally in C, the song should now be in Bb and not in A# as the website now suggests. This is of course not always the case, but the algorithm should as a first choice choose chords from the circle of fifths in the first place instead of always the #-variant as it is now.
Hence, A# becomes Bb, C# becomes Db but F# is fine as it is
There might be a better way which is more correct though, please suggest!
There could as a substitute or complement for this maybe be a setting in which the user could choose between showing the chords as flat or sharp (if someone would want to play a song in A# for some reason.)

author: Captaincranky
text:
henricdav
NSpen1
Our transposition software fails to take into account two basic principles of western diatonic music.
1: When forming a key scale, if you stop before a natural note in the chromatic scale, the note is a flat. When you go past a natural note forming a scale, the note becomes a sharp.
2: Just as importantly, you must have a note named after each note in the musical alphabet, A, B, C, D, E, F, & G.
If we examine the example given, the key of F would contain these notes: F G, A, A#, C, D, E, & F (8va). So, it's fair to conclude the software ALWAYS ASSUMES, it's going past a chromatic natural when changing key. Hence the reason it never shows flats.
So, if the software is licensed, I'm not sure what can be done about, other than complain to the publishers.
If the software is proprietary to UG, I think our developers are savvy enough to program a corrected matrix variable into it. This is obviously dependent on cost, time, and a willingness on the part of the site to rectify the issue.
(Keep in mind, I'm not a software engineer, and "matrix variable", is the best descriptor I could come up with as a layman).

author: NoeNie
text:
It has been
pointed out before
that the Transpose feature in the app is slow, presumably because it involves a server roundtrip. For me, each roudtrip takes 1 second, so transposing from C to Gb takes ~10 seconds (because I can't precisely hit the button again right when it loaded the next step). For slower internet connections, this would take even longer.
Here's my proposal that solves another issue at the same time and is hopefully quite easy to implement.
Please design the transpose controls like this
:
-1 C Db D Eb E F Gb G Ab A Bb B +1
(That's if "Use flats" is enabled in the quick settings, otherwise use C# and so on.)
Then highlight the key that the song is currently in (some tabs have this as metadata, especially the pro ones, otherwise use the first chord in the tab as a crude heuristic -- this doesn't have to be music-theoretically correct, it just needs to be usable). When the user presses another button, transpose directly to that song.
The Transpose function already takes a whole row on the mobile UI. I hope all the above chords would fit, but two rows would work as well.
This has the following usability advantages:
Only 1 server roundtrip. You can keep your server-side transposing implementation and nobody will care anymore.
Users don't have to count how many steps they want/need to do (e.g. if I see the first chord on the sheet is A, but people around me are playing E, I need to count to -5 in my head first, which takes time). With the proposed feature, I'd just click on E.
Users don't have to keep track of how many times they pressed the +1/-1 button already. Especially with the slowness, but also generally when chatting to people at the same time, it happens regularly to me that I press a few times, get distracted, have to scroll down to see what the chord is now, have to scroll back up and continue the transposing.
Users can communicate the key they use more clearly, at least if everyone is using the UG app. No more "I'm playing it in Bb." -- "By that, do you mean the first chord of the verse, the first chord of the chorus, or the base chord of the overall harmony?". Now it's simply "I pressed Bb in UG." and that will turn out the same for everyone.
There is already a somewhat similar transpose slider in the quick settings, but it's buried two clicks away (some users might not even know it exists for this reason, so they're left with the worse UX of the main transpose buttons) and it doesn't use chord names (so users still have to do the math in their head that I described above).

author: musicforte
text:
There is a nice feature that I have found from other music apps that I think would be a huge improvement to Ultimate Guitar.
Say you have a song and you see these chords:
D# - - - Bb - - - Ab - - - D#
The Problem
This not might be friendly to read for some musicians.  It's a I-V-IV-I progression in the key of Eb (not D#.)
But forget the technical mumbo jumbo.  Let's just say, someone has an easier time reading in flats...
Here's The Solution
With some other apps I have used, relative keys are switched, depending if you are clicking transpose up or transpose down.
But the other apps, are not user contributions either, so the key does not contain awkward relative chords.
If Ultimate Guitar can was able to understand key signatures, is it possible this could be fixed?
Examples
Transposing up from the original chords (above) would output:
E - - - B - - - A - - - E
Transposing up again would ouput:
F - - - C - - - Bb - - - F (notice the Bb.  This is correct for the key of F Not A#.)
But what if I prefer a key signature with sharps?  Fine I could transpose down once from the original key. The output would be:
D - - - A - - - G - - - D
And then transpose up again.  The output would be:
D# - - - A# - - - G# - - - D#
And vice versa.  If I prefer flats, I would transpose up again to the key of F, and then down to the key of EB.
Eb - - - Bb - - - Ab - - - Eb
Make sense?
=========================
Do correct key signatures or the ability to switch between relative keys (D# vs Eb) matter to you?
If so, reply or something...

author: coman91
text:
One quick suggestion for improving the rating system. Make it so that only contributing members can rate tabs. Not only should you be a UG member to rate other people's material, but you should also be a contributor yourself. Why? Because if you're a decent contributor you know the hard work that can go into tabbing, and you'll better be able to rate someone else's efforts and will be more willing to give feedback in the form of comments or pm's.
The way the system is set up now leaves contributors vulnerable to lazy raters or people who are spiteful and may give you a really poor rating just to mess with you.
Prime example:
I wrote a tab for "Funk #49" by Black Keys that was damned near perfect and some guy gave me 1/5 stars. The guy literally just made the profile that day. He had, like, 3 profile views (if that) and he wasn't a contributor. When I left him a polite message asking for feedback on how to improve the tab, I got no response.
Part of me thinks that the rating system isn't that important. That no one really cares about it. Then I stop and realize just how big of an impact the rating system has on how I view tabs. When I do a tab search, I don't usually bother with anything rated below 4 stars unless the higher rated stuff isn't really that good.
If this doesn't sound feasible, at least make it mandatory for raters to leave a comment of 20-40 characters or something. At least give the contributors some written feedback instead of a poor rating and no feedback to improve the tab with.

I heard from people that the tonebridge app and features is dead and that it's not getting attention or love from the UG team. After downloading it and messing around with it, I can see that. Im on Android and the last time it was updated was on April 14 2018!
Alot of features that was talked about in articles on launch was workshop (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/ug_news/free_tool_to_create_your_own_tonebridge_presets.html)
where you have multiple amps and presets to mess around with and could even submit some to be reviewed and accepted by the UG team and officially put in the app.
That was a lie. It's not even in the app at all! No mention of it anywhere! Don't advertise things if it's not going to be in the app!
Secondly, the tonebridhe request forms is dead as no requests are being filled
Lastly, there would be pedals in the app for songs like KoRn Predictable Where the pedal is made for the whole song, yet it's not a official one / doesn't even sound like the tone in the actual song! It just uses the default rock preset. When I go request a official preset of the song, I can't cause it has "already been made". A default rock sound is not official, it's just a default preset!
All in all, I love the idea and usability of the tonebridge app for android, I really do! But there's so much missing! All you need to do is add the workshop feature, fix latency a little (from what I heard), update app every now and then, add a tunner, and lastly, show support for the app and the request forms! Now again, im on android so I don't know if IOS has these features or not. Before you say it's because Android has limitations, it's 2022! Shut it. Plus Android has more features and compatibility than Apple will ever have!
That's my rant. Don't take this as hate, I just don't want to see this amazing app die! Im new to guitar and this makes learning so much fun! But please add the workshop to Android!
Love You UG!

author: netwiznick
text:
UG Support
As has been pointed out above there is a logout function in 'settings'. It's clear (unsurprisingly) from the comments also that it's not where people expect to find it, and so think it doesn't exist. It's not going to be a technical issue to put it somewhere more intuitive unless the site is coded using black magic.
My perception is that the site is designed by techies rather than by UX professionals basing design on best practice and user research. That's why logout is in the 'wrong' place.
It's also why
- the current speed indicator in tabs is almost invisible, and the speed control is only a slider with + and - buttons
- we can't find out what's in an app update, even though the app itself invites feedback on updates (my post on which has received no reply)
- the link to any instruction on how to use the system is buried in footer in an un-intuitive link
- you can't upload local image files to a post - it has to be a url
- you can't upload a docx file to a post, just doc
Whether it applies here or not I don't know, but in my experience it also tends to be the case with engineer-designed sites that there is an attitude that anything that doesn't fit with their worldview is an edge case or not important. I note that Muse group was advertising for a UX researcher for UG so there appears to be some sort of UX structure there - I wonder if they are given enough support. If they want to talk to me I'd be happy to do so.

text:
I've noticed a slowly increasing amount of
relevant
threads being made in the Pit.  By this I mean questions or posts relating to guitar/bands etc that should, strictly speaking, be put in other sections of the forums.
No one seems to mind, since I'm guessing the majority of traffic for the site is passing through the pit.
To combat this, my sugesstion is having something similar to the forum section on the front page, highlighting new threads/posts made in other parts of the forum, but put alongside the list of pit threads.  This would allow the Pit monkeys even easier access to these forum should they want to make a post.
Obviously if people want to post in the other sections, they go to them.  And in an ideal world all members would visit every section of the forums, but that's not the way it happens.  The reality is that if people want lots of responses quickly they'd post in the pit no matter the subject.
It's not a major problem, but it might make things a bit easier.  I also know this would be hard to implement, but then it's only a suggestion.  What do you guys think?

author: Pencom
text:
N-D
Again, thanks N-D for your response. I've said this before but it still bears repeating, UG is the "only" web site of this kind, that I'm aware of, that actually solicits opinions from people not employed by the company. It is their own web site and UG is absolutely under no obligation to do this. I believe the thinking is that two heads are generally better then one. The net result is just as we see it; the best guitar web site in the world, by far. No other web site comes close, in my opinion. The site is, as has been mentioned, very dynamic. Dynamic oriented towards a better user experience rather then on revenue enhancements.
I don't know where else to discuss this, so I'll bring it up here, on this forum (I'm not on the other one anymore
).
On each tab page there is "STRUMMING Edit" and "Suggest Correction". Several years ago I brought up this subject and it didn't go anywhere. I'd like to return to it, if I may. I'm asking UG and also the other folks on this forum to give me their opinion (s) on "when may a tab be considered done?" For me, tabs submitted to UG are not necessarily "dynamic". The proposition was put forth years ago that there were just so many bad, incomplete and duplicate tabs on UG that something had to be done. Other sites just leave them alone. UG takes actionable steps to actually improve tabs so that everyone benefits. That is why, if you really, really want the absolute best tab of any given song, UG is the "only" site you need go to. My point is: "when does UG consider a tab 'corrected'?" Or does UG consider all tabs to be "dynamic", i.e, never actually corrected? Tabs are always in a state of flux?
I use my own tab here to illustrate my point, because I believe every tab author here can site their own: Can't Help Falling In Love. I believe this tab is "done". NSpen1 kindly provided the strumming pattern. I believe that is also "done". By UG posting on this tab (as in so many other tabs I would also consider "done") "Strumming Edit" and "Suggest Correction", UG is saying that the tab is "not" done. UG is suggesting that someone fix it. And, like anything else, when you solicit someone's opinion you will surely get an earful, done or not. The TMs as good as they are cannot, in the long run, prevent people from changing tabs. Should (God forbid) NSpen1 leave UG then I can 100% guarantee that someone (s) will try to change his strumming pattern.  I have heard the argument that it only improves the tab (s). Up to a point, this is correct. Up to a point. "After" that point has been reached what you generally get are "opinions". "I used to play this way", "I heard a live concert that played it this way", "I never use a capo", "this chord sounds better IMHO" etc. The list is endless.
Does UG want a "finished" product or does UG want continued tab controversy? In my case, the song in question is and has always been open to having many more versions. By allowing a correct tab to be changed to someone else's idea of correct is self defeating, in my opinion.
Here is what I propose and would solicit opinions (keep it nice
). At some point...UG considers a tab (s) "done", complete and no longer subject to outsiders changing it. That does not mean "suggestions" cannot be made. I'm going out on a limb here but I believe everyone reading this has tabs of their own which they consider "done". The question is how this would be accomplished? Maybe UG has a panel that reviews tabs and concludes a tab is done or tab is still open to corrections. I also believe that sometimes the word "correction" is used instead of "interpretation".
In summary, I would suggest that because UG has tens of thousands of tabs that really do need work (some of mine among them), tabs that are for all extent and purposes complete, and accurate to be closed..."done". I'm already hearing...'NOOOOOOOOOOOO!!". When I say "done" that does not mean it can never be changed. It means that the tab author does the changing based on suggestions they may hear. The point being that if something is not put into place quality, complete, accurate etc. tabs will always be subjected to unnecessary and unwarranted changes.

author: brettsanace
text:
Pencom
In theory I agree with you in that an author should be able to lock their tab and any suggested corrections would come via comments rather than the TPA queue and the the author could chose to follow the comment or not. However, practically it is not that easy, as the system needs to cater for all tab types. You are thinking in terms of Chord tabs where it is fairly easy to raise suggested changes in  comments, but as
LMBozovich
has hinted at if you are suggesting a change to a tab/pro tab it is not that easy to suggest a change to a drum fill or guitar solo in a comment.
The system could be changed so that if the author selected the "lock" function that only the author could approve changes submitted to the TPA queue, but then what would happen if the author moved on with their life, or even died, and stopped using UG each day, the suggested corrections would sit their forever unless some rule was introduced such as "If not approved after a month they are deleted from the queue". To do the correction the person would then have to create an alternative tab which would go against the current policy of not approving similar tabs (which I'm sure you agree with) where they are simply transposed or change a major chord to a 7th chord etc. There would be other rules required such as "Unregistered users could not lock their tab".
I'm not trying to dismiss your suggestion because as I said I agree with it in theory, I'm just trying to highlight that from UG's perspective these things are not necessarily straight forward and that when trying to satisfy everyone sometimes compromises need to be made. NB: I don't work for UG - but hey, if there are any jobs going guys I'm open to it

author: Pencom
text:

Hi. Thank you for your quick response. I know, over the years. people comment that Pencom does not like people "messing" with his tabs. I believe it is more accurate to say that Pencom does not like "incompetent" people messing with his tabs. Is that really different from anyone else? There is a world of difference between the two previous statements. The way things are now set up, the "only firewall" between competent and incompetent people wanting to change tabs are the TMs.
To the point of my posting, I believe you are very competent to do what you have been doing. I very much applaud what you are doing. However, "after" you have finished doing what you say you are doing....."are you done"? In other words....is the pie baked and ready to eat.....or....are you going to allow someone else to add say, whip cream to it? The question, again, is will UG set up something to determine what tabs are "done" and what tabs still need work? IF X number of tabs are deemed to be correct in terms of formatting, lyrics, author, title etc. and....more controversial, correct chords, then can those tabs be taken off the "Suggest Correction" list? If UG puts X number of tabs to bed, so to speak, then it frees up the TMs to spend more time on tabs that really do need work.

author: Pencom

Thank you. I will be blunt, it is my belief that a significant portion of the worlds population is made up of ignorant people. Some might even call them idiots. Some people call me an idiot.

author: Pencom
text:
NSpen1
Thank you. Regardless of how this discussion goes I could not be happier. Much of this newfound joy can be attributed to people like you (NSpen1). Why? In the not so distant past a certain dark atmosphere hung over the forums, primarily the result of a certain personality. That personality is, as far as I can see, gone or at least neutralized. We don't have to always agree with each other to have meaningful dialogue. If something good comes out of that dialogue, so much the better. I won't revisit those dark times again, but don't think for a minute that your presence has gone unappreciated.
Yes, I believe this check box issue should be explored because IF it does nothing then it should be either, activated,  removed or its function better explained.
About the locking of tabs; I have been using a bit of semantics. Again there is a big difference between "suggestions for tab correction" and waking up one morning to find someone has actually "corrected" a tab. I have never, ever remotely suggested that free speech be curtailed. Never. Trying to disprove a negative is almost impossible. I cannot easily disprove that any tab, no matter how good it might be, can't be in some way be improved. All of us here reading this probably have tabs that come in different complexity levels. Some of our tabs are dirt simple. Most rock and folk songs are pretty straightforward. Some, however, are more complex and some are very, very complex. Speaking for myself, I can say with a certain level of certainty some of my tabs are 100% correct, in the context of the target audience I'm trying to reach. Others are more complex and I'm not 100% certain. Some tabs I'm just not happy with and look forward to suggestions. I, like most people, am never, ever always right. On the other hand, I'm not always wrong. And that is my beef.
Right now the system says that....let's say UG has 1 million tabs just to throw out a number, all 1 million tabs are not correct. If one says that all 1 million tabs are open to correction then, by default, all 1 million tabs on UG are considered "incorrect". That means that all of your tabs, all of my tabs and all the tabs of everyone here are deemed, by UG to be incorrect. Frankly, I have very little incentive to post new tabs if they are judged to be incorrect from the get go. By continuing with this system there is no ultimate reward for doing the right thing. Instead, UG should set a "criteria" for all tabs and "when" those tabs fulfill that criteria the "Suggest Corrections" stays .....but it goes to "verbal statements", i.e., "I suggest Dm instead of D over the following words..." The "Suggest Corrections" does not allow someone to start hacking away at the tab. That someone, by the way, has probably never been vetted.  I find myself in arguments with people I don't know, I don't know what their musical skills are. I don't know if they have an agenda. Common sense would dictate that, regardless of the endeavor, nobody should be allowed meaningful input into anything unless they have demonstrated that they know what they are doing or talking about. That does not stop people from expressing their opinions. It only stops people from going beyond opinion expressions to putting their opinions into action.  I'm not comfortable with the notion that all opinions should be judged equally.  Prove to me that your opinion should be considered by showing me your resume.  Right now, anyone...anyone can change a tab.  That's insane.
And what exactly is correct? Someone please tell me. There has been no criteria set for this term. How can UG ask for correct tabs when nobody knows what that means. I was playing a song from Acoustic Guitar that had the following chords in it: Em6 F#dim7 Em6 F#dim7. It was, as far as I could tell, correct. It is not how I would have tabbed the song. That is why there are numerous variations of song tabs allowed. Allow people to play that version but don't expect those chords to be inserted into another version because then you are selectively excluding your target audience.
Why the never ending correction cycle? UG is a business. It is a good business model to develop systems that encourage people to return to the same web site over and over again. Advertisers pay more money for increased viewers, i.e., more eyeballs on the ads. The system encourages everyone to "put in their two cents". So, the system "asks" every viewer to suggest corrections to tabs. And when that tab has been "so called" corrected then it asks someone else to correct that correction and it never ends because the theory is "there is no such thing as a 100% correct tab". Well, I believe that there are correct tabs. Some of those correct tabs are yours and people who are viewing this. The ancient Greek gods used to punish Sisyphus by making him push a rock up a slope and just before it reached the top the rock rolled back down the hill. This went on for eternity.
I have heard and appreciate the argument that the tab author can go back in and change anything back to the way it was. I have a suggestion; why not move away from the all tabs are inherently incorrect to some tabs are, for the target audience that they were written for, correct and deemed correct by UG. Lets stop pretending that "some" of our tabs are not correct. We know they are.

author: brettsanace
text:
Pencom
I agree with most of what you have said, except for the bit about the system allowing users to "start hacking away at the tab". The system allows users to suggest corrections via the TPA Queue. The exception to this is TMs (and I'm not sure about Level V authors - which could be an issue), and the TMs have probably demonstrated their musical nous to obtain that position. Whilst a great many of the corrections approved in the TPA are approved by the TMs not all are. A correction could be approved by five Level 1 authors all casting their 1 point vote (who have not demonstrated their musical nous). I myself have made some ridiculous comments on corrections in the TPA queue (usually strumming patterns), however I know my limitations so tend to Comment when I am not sure, and only Vote when I am positive, and 95% of the time it is for rejection. However, I have seen some blatantly obvious incorrect "corrections" get approved (though admittedly most were subsequently reverted).
My point is that the problem might be the approval process. It may be better to just allow all and sundry to comment on corrections as opposed to voting on them, and leave the actual voting/approval to TMs. This may increase the workload for TMs, but they also wouldn't have to waste time fixing incorrect "corrections". Maybe approval could continue to be allowed for Level 5 authors to alleviate the workload. Of course this would not be popular with all the Level, 1, 2, 3 & 4 authors who would say what is the point of having different levels if all we can do is comment.
Or maybe the process could be left as is for "New Tabs" ie everyone can vote, but changed for "Corrections" where only TMs , Level 5 and the Tab's Author can vote (but every level could comment).

author: Pencom
text:
brettsanace
Thank you...and again, having people like you on the forum is a breath of fresh air. Informed, intelligent and well presented opinions.
I'm not as well versed on the TMs and the approval process (I was once a TM) as I should be. That's my fault. The only thing that I'm aware of is seeing two screens side by side; one side my tab and other side is what someone has gone to the trouble to rewrite. IF I don't reject it or some TM does not reject it, it is my understanding that the new version writes over my old tab. If I'm wrong about that then I apologize in advance. For me, for it to be assumed that should nobody reject the corrections "I'm" the one who is incorrect highly offends me. Highly. Have I gotten that correct? If nobody, for whatever reason, acts on a correction then that correction over rides the original submission? So, someone, such as you or any of the other people on this forum, who have done many, many, many tabs is now "not" given the benefit of the doubt over a completely unknown person? What I would "like" but probably will never get is: IF a correction suggestion is made and it is not acted upon within a certain period of time the suggested correction is canceled (rejected is somewhat pejorative). That does not preclude someone else (not the same person) from also offering corrections. Is that too extreme a stance for me to take, and to ask others here to take?  The people who protect my tabs and your tabs are here today, but they will (figuratively speaking) be gone tomorrow. Then what?
My main point is really about the tab corrections lock. UG goes to great pains (very well done, I might add) to explain how they want tabs to be presented etc. for submission. Another reason UG is far and away better then any other tab site. Yet....what is missing, in my opinion, is there appears to be no guidelines about what they consider to be a "correct" tab. I mean, is the tab ok, sort of good, really good, better then most etc.....or...is the tab complete, and correct and put to bed?  There should be a beginning and an end.  I see so many tabs out there that I consider perfect.  But with the "allow me to fix your tab button"  UG is just asking for people to submit "musical opinions" about the tab....not real musical improvements. You know from the song.."If everybody's right then no body is wrong".  I'm not clear on what UG's goals are. Are the goals to get the most tabs and the most correct tabs? Or, is the goal to keep an ongoing, everyone can participate type of thing? You know, a Facebook type of thing.
I think, if we put our heads together, we can come up with some system that starts to recognize when certain tabs are "correct" and "done". Surely....

author: Pencom
text:
Tikken
Hello. I would like to submit something for UG to consider. This has to do with the "2.2 Rejecting a correction section". I would like to "discuss" the  possible inclusion of another bullet point, after:
"
Inaccurate correction.
Correction that is wrong musically or suggests a wrong formatting."
Ok, I know I'm going to get some flak for suggesting this, but here goes. I'm suggesting the addition of another category: "Musical Opinion". This is something I've brought up before a few years ago but I'm still thinking about it. It is somewhat difficult to define. I strongly believe that there is a "middle" area between "wrong" and "right" regarding a tab. I would like to call this area "musical opinion" for lack of a better term. There are a number of times when I'm confronted with a "correction" that I'm both reluctant to accept "or" to reject. I can't say that the person making the suggestion is wrong, yet the suggestion does not fit with my idea of how I would like my tab to be shown. I suspect most of us have confronted the same situation, we neither agree nor do we disagree with the suggestion. I suspect that there are a number of folks who feel something is either black or it is white. I believe there are also a lot of grey areas when it comes to music. I would like to term these grey areas "musical opinions". I'm asking UG to think about this and get back to us with their opinion on this subject, and how it should be handled, if at all. Just a suggestion here: "Correction that is wrong musically, musical opinion* or suggests a wrong formatting".
*Musical Opinion is defined as: "UG would need to fill this in" ...or, perhaps open it up for discussion with some tab authors.

Yeah, I'm afraid I'm much more on the side of it's either black or white.  It may not always be easy to tell or hear, but yes, objectively either one note is played or another one, this chord or that chord.  I can't see any sort of 'musical opinion' addition working. I don't think that's quite the same thing, you can objectively say the band is either playing in drop Ab/G# or drop A.  If someone comes along and offers a correction for that song based on listening to it live, and says it should be in drop A, then you would reject it because it's wrong, that's not a matter of opinion.
If someone tabs a 7-string song on a 6-string then you could consider it 'wrong' from the point of view of it being transcribed for the wrong instrument or perhaps having notes an octave higher than they were originally played, or 'right' because the notes tabbed are correct.  But I would simply consider that an arrangement for 6-string guitar of something that was originally played on 7-string, not some nebulous 'musical opinion'.

author: Pencom
text:
Tikken
Hi..I want to thank everyone here for their input on this subject. Again, in my view, the important thing here is that opinions are expressed and discussed. Not every suggestion to UG is necessarily workable but it's interesting to throw out some new ideas.
You mention that you prefer to have every lick etc. put on the tabs that you play. I certainly can't argue with that approach. One of the reasons UG has a number of versions for each song is it allows for just that sort of thing. It is my belief that most of the "users" who come to UG are probably not the worlds greatest guitar players. I've mentioned before that I live in a town comprised of professional musicians. I doubt that the tabs on UG would have any interest for them. However, these folks are in the minority, relative to the huge number of world wide guitar players. My tabs are essentially basic chords that allow the user to put in their own licks. It's just my style and not a suggestion for anyone else to emulate.  It may be my style of writing tabs that encourages folks to want to "add" things to them. Can't say for sure.
Regarding, "musical opinions", oddly enough I came up with this idea from some TMs who had responded to some corrections by using the term "opinion". I can't recall off the top of my head who these TMs were or the songs, but that is where I got the idea. In other words, they were rejecting the corrections because of what they termed opinions. (perhaps 'musical opinions' could be replaced with 'musical interpretations') This whole thing got started because one of my tabs "Atlantis" was removed because it was said that chords needed to be placed over the spoken lyrics. I posted the song for everyone to hear. Atlantis is much like a number of other songs that have spoken lyrics with background music. A number of Elvis Presley, Motown etc. songs also use the same technique. The reason why one cannot effectively place chords over the spoken lyrics is that Donovan is speaking in one "cadence" and the music is performed in a "different" cadence. That is why, "in my opinion", the tabs that have chords above the spoken lyrics are wrong. (this brings up the question....what is the status of my two tabs that have been removed? Is UG going to restore them? I know you were working on this, but I'm not clear on what the outcome is) When a tab like this is removed UG is taking away the opportunity for users to play the tab the way I believe it should be played. Again, I'm not suggesting that the way I tab it is the way other people "must" play it. It is not at all clear to me what is being gained by limiting the choices of the users. "If in doubt, don't take it out".

I would like to take the time to thank Brett for starting the New Website Feedback thread. Clearly it has generated a lot of needed discussion. Having said all of that, I would love to see Brett, or anyone else here, start up a new thread. Call it say..."all things UG" or "thoughts on the UG website" etc. Whatever it is called it would allow a high level of discussion about anything having to do with UG. First I love having this platform to go to. It makes learning new songs quickly so much easier that what I had tried before. I have some suggestions for the Playlists and Personal tabs.

author: Pencom
text:
Hi...this is directed at the UG staff. I've brought this up before but it apparently got no reaction so I'm bringing it up again.
Titles of song parts, i.e., Verse, Intro, Chorus Capo etc. should be separated by a line space. When there is no separation it looks too crowded and bunched up. This distracts the eyes of the user. UG already provides a line space in their normal web site format as you can see below. This may seem like a small thing but unless it is corrected countless people will keep trying to "edit" tabs with what they perceive to be the proper format. It would take UG less then 5 minutes to add a line space to their example and be done with it. Please do this.
B. Song parts  recommended
Song parts (intro, chorus, verse, solo, etc.) need to be marked. If song is not parted into "chorus," "verse" - you don't need to indicate them. The part name is put into square brackets: [Intro].
[Verse 1]
Am             C                       Dm
Same bed, but it feels just a little bit bigger
[Verse 1]
Am             C                       Dm
Same bed, but it feels just a little bit bigger

author: mandelstamdavid

controversial issue. Many people don't like an additional line because it makes a print version longer and also a tab becomes harder to autoscroll.

author: Pencom
text:
mandelstamdavid
Thank you...I understand what you are saying, however take a look at my posting "without" spacing; shown below:  Do you like it?  I don't, and it's for a reason.  First, it looks awful.  Second, it makes reading the posting more difficult.  The "first" order of business, in my opinion, for UG regarding tabs,  is "ease" of use.  Many guitar players are at a stage where they must "both" look at the screen and then look at their hands on the guitar.  This is why you really don't want to "jam" up the screen.  This is also why the "chords" have a different color then the lyrics, so the eyes can differentiate. What UG does about this formatting issue will effect all tabs for years to come.  I really think UG should get the formatting correct at the beginning

author: brettsanace
text: I find this really frustrating as it is quite simple. There are three distinct functions. "Edit" which applies to the tab's author, Tab Moderators (and maybe Level IV and V authors, I don't know as I am only Level III) which means that you can change the tab directly.  "Suggest Corrections" which is used by every one else and must go through the queue. "Personal" which has nothing to do with the original tab but creates a new tab which the user can edit at their will. The current "EDIT" link at the top of the page relates to the third function and thus has nothing to do with "editing"  the existing tab. So the first two functions involve editing the original tab whilst the third one doesn't which is why it should not be called "EDIT"  but should instead be called "Personal".

If the author doesn't provide the link then the "Listen" option shouldn't appear. If not populated the option shouldn't appear.

Hi...I thought I'd put my two cents into this conversation, for what it's worth. Clearly, having two words EDIT and Edit on the same page performing completely different operations is non intuitive. On multiple occasions I've clicked on the EDIT button by mistake. Whatever fix you ultimately come up with should be one that uses different words or wording for each operation.
This allows me to segue into something I've brought up before ("Pencom, we are sick of hearing about this..."). Please keep an open mind to having a "clean screen" option. You can put the option on the "more" (...) section, if you like. Over the years UG has made it's tab pages very "feature rich". This is a very good thing. The more features you have the more options the user has. This is not a complaint on my part. UG should be applauded for this, and I do. Where I'm coming from is....many people, myself included, "only" want to play the tab, and play the tab with the "least" amount of visual distractions. The user can "toggle" between the main screen and the "clean" screen.  No body that I'm aware of would like a cluttered screen when reading a digital book on their iPad, so why read a cluttered tab screen? author: Pencom
text:
mandelstamdavid
Thank you. I've said it before and I'll say it again, UG is the only web site, of any kind, that I'm aware of that actually solicits user opinions. I wish more web sites would copy UG in that regard.
As someone who has spent most of his adult life selling and promoting goods, services and ideas I'm approaching the UG web site from a somewhat different angle. After seeing all the wonderful things that make up the UG web site I sit back and speculate about potentially missed opportunities. You keep mentioning that "users" have not asked or requested certain features therefore UG shows no interest in new "suggested" features. While this approach is very democratic it is not forward thinking or dynamic. For example; no one that I'm aware of "asked" Apple to develop the iPhone. Steve Jobs did and look where Apple is today.
Regarding submitting tabs to UG. UG should and needs to "ask" people to do it. Yes, you have a button at the top. I know what it is and everyone else here knows what it is but we are not the people who UG  needs to convince to submit tabs. UG should have a "box" near the top of the home page saying something like (just my words..) "UG Wants You To Submit Tabs" etc, etc. and..."It's easy and here is how you do it". UG should be "selling" a concept here. Right now UG is "offering" but not "selling". I'm convinced that a lot of people who visit the UG web site leave without giving much thought to "contributing". Why? UG does not ask them to. This is coming from the sales person in me.
Regarding the "clean screens". Again, this is part of the idea that UG should not be a follower strictly based on what people may or may not say. UG needs to "lead". People you ask may not "know" what they want. It is up to UG, in my judgment, to offer new features (within reason of course) that current users have not thought of. I find it hard to believe that anyone would say to UG that they can't stand an uncluttered tab screen. Please give it some thought.

As this was raised on this thread and because I have my doubts as to whether it will ever get out of the Mods Forum, I thought I would elaborate in the hope that a UG IT person might read this (
h0spid
)
This is my recommended solution but obviously there may better ways to implement.
Another flag/check box should be added to each user's profile settings called "Don't allow strumming patterns on my tabs" (or something similar). The default value for this field should be unchecked. It is up to authors who don't want strumming patterns on their tabs to go to their profile settings and click the check box. If the check box is ticked then the author is added to a database table say, "No strumming patterns", and when a UG user selects a chord tab this table is searched and if the author appears in the table the line "There is no strumming pattern for this song yet. Create and get +5 IQ" should not appear on the author's chord tab when it is presented to the user.
It is not necessary to promote this feature. If an author complains about strumming patterns being added to their tabs it is easy enough for a Tab Moderator to refer them to the option in their profile settings. Currently there are only about a half dozen authors who have expressed their wish not to have strumming patterns on their tabs (
NSpen1
can give you their names). As there are so few they could be contacted directly and told to check the check box after it has been implemented or the check box for these authors could be auto-checked as part of the implementation.
By implementing this it will stop UG users from creating and submitting strumming patterns only to be told they have wasted their time. It will also mean that Tab Moderators/Reviewers don't need to try and remember which authors don't want strumming patterns, and can just judge each pattern on its merits. If, an author who doesn't want strumming patterns on their chord tabs fails to check the check box in their profile settings, then it will be their responsibility to delete the pattern from their tab. This should only be required one time, as once they complain they will be informed by a Tab Moderator about the option in their profile settings. If they fail to act on this advice to click one box, then it is tough luck, they will either have to continue to delete the strumming patterns or leave them on their tabs.
I don't believe there is much effort required to implement this automated process in place of the current manual process.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
NSpen1
Concert tuning is much more understandable across all instrument players. Just because guitar is the quintessential transposing instrument (up and down, capos and tunings) doesn't mean the notes themselves change. Perhaps the way to play the desired concert note is different depending on capo and tuning, but the transposition function already helps with that.
You're putting way too much emphasis on the original transcriptions with your approach as well. Not everyone wants to play in the original key or method, and enforcing capo and shapes based on E is going to make finding a suitable set of notes harder for people with less experience. I consistently transpose things to different keys once I'm used enough to a song, and placing metadata-based constraints (besides the string names) in order to dictate both shape and sound is too much. It's not that hard to use the transposition function once you get the hang of it or ask enough questions, and it'll make the site more marketable than just bedroom guitarists.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
I could repeat the same things to you, but that doesn't really get the communication anywhere. This isn't a competition about who's most right or wrong; otherwise, we have lost the point of even contributing to the site. Consider this before replying without really knowing for sure what the other party is discussing or where they're coming from.
What you pointed out about the past tense is not necessarily a bug in itself. There is a chance that, if the restart date (beginning of the week) is closer than the end date (end of the week), past tense may be used. They restarted at 12:00 AM PST, midnight where the UG US office is. This is why I wrote "
If
you want past tense" (emphasis added). Without further information, there is no point in assuming that one's knowledge of the situation is complete.
As someone who has been around non-native speakers their entire life, studied how language comes together, and taught ESL overseas, I would like to think that my view of the situation is a bit clearer and more nuanced as opposed to a predominantly monolingual viewpoint, which ignores the deep structures in language. Far too often, words are taken for granted without thinking about their interactions within a sentence.
Answering the question "when will the list update?" will yield the natural English response "It updates/will update/is going to update in [an hour/X time/three minutes]". Once English learners know what preposition to use to mean what they want, this is not a problem at all. The adverbial phrase is the only thing that's added. "[An hour/X time/three minutes] to update" is ambiguous, contains unspoken (implied) words, is a fragment that is not easily remade into a sentence, and has an embedded clause.

Here's something that doesn't work correctly in the old site, but would be really nice if it did in the new one.  Chord charts with non-standard tuning, mostly a half-step down. author: NeoMvsEu
text:
NSpen1
Do you mind telling me how you'd see capos or transposed chords working relative to tuning, relative to standard shapes or the actual tuning? Actual professional transcriptions show both concert chords and chords relative to capo, although if it's a downtuned variant of standard, chords are often (not always) written relative to standard.
What would C# mean exactly in half-step down? If the notes are relative to concert tuning, it's easy to communicate "D shape, tune down 1/2 step". However, communicating the same to other people who aren't playing the instrument fails completely.
I've been in a group that's played Bastille's "Pompeii" led by a guitarist who gave everybody the guitarist's version of the chords, and it didn't work for that exact reason: the difference in communication. The guitarist was playing one set of chords, and everyone else was not on the same page. We had to stop rehearsal, print out new chord charts, and only then did it work out.
This isn't a large grey area conversation, or a solution that's easy or even practical to make at times. Maybe it's frustrating to have to read "Eb" (or "D#") in order to see 022100 on a half-step down chart (by transposing to that chord), but this is a lot more complicated than presented. This isn't about guitarists or uke players solely; this is about communicating to the entire ensemble effectively.

Its one of those double-edge swords (full of metaphors, I am).  I have read comments by prolific tab authors who eschew being rated by non-contributors, if at all.
I have read some unecessarily vitriolic reviews, pointless comments and incorrect "corrections" from others - contributors and otherwise - that do not, in my opinion, add anything to this wonderful resource we have available to us.  I have also seen some very constructive criticism and suggestions made by people who obviously appreciate UG and its community.
The subjectivity of the ratings process is going to appeal to some, and irritate others.  I personally look at tabs for songs that I want to learn, and where there are many, I look for the one with the highest rating, that has been rated the most, to begin with.  I have found errors in these ones.  If it doesn't suit me or my ear, I look for another with high ratings.  I will often look at tabs with low- or no rating at all, to see if they fit my style better.  I admit that I do start with the highly rated tabs.
I will never give a "bad" rating, or make unnecessary criticism, because I have not contributed a tab, and it seems pointless to negatively criticise the efforts of a volunteer.
If I like the tab, am able to play it reasonably well, and it fits what my knowledge of the original song is, then I will give it a 5, maybe a 4 if something isn't quite right.  I never give 3 or less.
I have sometimes not given ratings to tabs that already have many.  My contribution wouldn't make a difference.
It's a little pointless, because the tabs stay there forever, even if they are badly written, have low or no ratings compared with umpteen others for the same song.  It does help when trying to find a tab that suits me.

author: brettsanace
text:
OK this is probably not the proper thread for this conversation but since it has started I want to add my 2 cents worth.
Everyone seems to agree that people tend to look at the tabs with the highest ratings first, which makes the rating system an important feature of UG, which is why rating tabs should be encouraged, and if, as some people have suggested, that ratings have reduced since the release of the new version of UG then this is an issue that needs to be addressed (though it is hard to tell if this true due to lack of statistics from before and after).
The problem with the rating system is that it serves two different purposes. Firstly there are the "advanced" players who are looking for the tab to be exactly as the artist recorded it. These people may say "It only gets 4 stars because the G chord should actually be a Gsus4", I believe this group is in the minority. Then there are the "Beginner/Intermediate" group that are looking for a tab that their skill levels allow them to play. These people will say "This version gets  5 stars because I can play a G chord unlike that weird Gsus4 in the other version". I believe this group is probably the majority of UG users.
However, it probably doesn't matter that there are these differing objectives of the rating system.  If we end up with a couple of highly rated tabs for each song, where one is the "perfect" tab and one is the "easy" tab then everyone will be happy. Either way, users should still be encouraged to rate tabs, and if the ratings have actually dropped then that is an issue that does belong on this thread.

author: Pencom
text:
pf2407
Hi, let me state right up front here that I don't have a dog in this fight.
In other words, if a notation is effective then we should all consider using it. The problem, as I see it, is that unlike sheet music and tablature, there are not a lot of specific rules for writing chords (tabs). I started doing this tab\chord writing thing years ago....making stuff up because of the lack of defined rules. To it's credit, UG has narrowed a lot of variables down so that we all have a more consistent interface. This issue we are now speaking about is one of the "few" areas that have not been adequately addressed.
First of all, as far as I'm aware, 100% of people looking at chorded tabs "already" are familiar with the song. A professional musician can play a song using "well written" sheet music without ever having heard the song. Since UG "primarily" caters to non professional musicians the chorded tabs need to be more or less self explanatory. The user already knows the song and just looks for the proper chords, located over the proper "syllables".  Just locating chords over the proper words are not, in themselves, good enough. Using "tablature" notation does not really work well. For example: \ means slide down...but / means slide up and, of course, resembles a slash chord. To illustrate the point here is a fairly well know tune; Sweet Home Alabama. The opening notes are well known. Dum Dum Dum\Dum Dum Dum Dum\Dum Dum Dum Dum.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/lynyrd_skynyrd/sweet_home_alabama_chords_1053582
If you look at the comments you will see that nobody has ever asked me what the "\" means. They hear it in the song so they already know. The case has been put forth that instead of a "\" we should use a dash "-".  I'm completely ok with that. But when, and "until" UG defines the standard I'm going to continue to use the backslash because it works, for me. Now, I also believe that the case could \ should be made that lacking notation guidance,  each tab author might want to "explain" what any controversial notation means.

text:

"Personal" or "Save as Personal" names are not very clear to users, while "Edit" is simple and clear. That's why we decided to use "Edit".
Ok here are a few ideas for you to consider.
In the top right corner we add a fourth link called "PERSONAL" along with the existing three of "EDIT", "ADD TO PLAYLIST" and "FAVORITE". PERSONAL should use the same portrait (head & shoulders) silhouette icon that you use elsewhere eg in My Tabs.

Well when you scroll through a tab the icons for the existing three links are pinned so that they are always viewable and if you mouse over the icon the description appears eg "FAVORITE". This same concept could be employed at the top of the page and just show the four icons without the descriptions which would only appear when the cursor was on the icon. "PERSONAL" should work the same as "EDIT" works now, that is it is used to create a personal tab, though I would get rid of the intermediate "Creating Personal Tab" pop-up screen as it is not needed.
"EDIT" should now be used to actually edit the tab unlike the current situation. Now here is the clever bit!!! If the tab author clicks the "EDIT" link it should take them to the Edit page that the current "Edit" link takes them to, and if any other user clicks the "EDIT" link it should take them to the Correction page the same as if they clicked the "SUGGEST CORRECTION" button below the tab. author: brettsanace
text:
New Messages System
(I posted this comment on the article but don't know if anyone from UG reads them especially as most of the comments are joke comments, so I thought I would post it here.)
You are replacing what was essentially an email system with a messaging system - they are not the same thing. I'm not a fan of the new system.  In the old system each message had a subject which made it easy to find a particular thread if you wanted to send another message related to that particular subject. Also only the subjects were displayed (like an email inbox) not the full texts which again made this process more efficient. Now you are required to scroll through an entire chat history to try and find a particular "message" or reply from the past and as there is no subject and each message displays full text you have to scan and hope that you notice what you are looking for. Even if you find it you can't reply to that particular message/comment, as all you can do is add to the end of your one long continuous chat. You also can't reply to specific quotes from the earlier message, like you could in the old system. I guess you could copy some text and paste it into your comment and then add your reply but if the original was from a month ago with many comments in between it won't really make sense without being in the context of a thread/subject. I am happy to have a messaging feature added to UG but you can't use it to replace the old system as they have a different focus and functionality. The new system is conversation based and the old system was subject/thread based. That is why smartphones have separate apps for email and messages, because they are different!

author: sixthcrusifix
text:
Could we have some type of voting system for the chord suggestions at least? I see someone requested the most common Cadd9 to be added back in 2017 but that hasn't been done and that person was banned (hopefully not for making that request). To me it's a bit absurd when I see very common chord voicing that are nowhere to be found in the suggestions or not the default one. At the very least it'd be nice if the community could vote on what shows up when you hover over a chord.
Cadd9 is especially egregious. I think 99% of the time I see Cadd9 it's part of a walk down/up or it is just used to add color to the C chord or go along with the lyrics. And virtually 100% of the time this is done by simply lifting up one's finger from the D string to give you x30010. Yet the default suggestion for Cadd9 is X32030. Hey don't get me wrong, they both sound fine, but I have never seen anyone play that chord in my life.
From a music theory perspective the second chord would seem more "correct" since adding the 9th would be adding the higher D. That being said, it just isn't how that chord is used. There are a ton of songs that use the X30010 voicing, it's extremely popular and very common and yet we have no logical way to include it in a chord sheet because
it isn't even listed anywhere on the alternate voicings pop-up of the Cadd9 chord
, in order to get it you have to use one of the insane alternate names that no one would ever think of: Em7#5/C or G6sus4/C.
This is far from the only case as well. The D/F# chord is another great example. This chord is used all over the place and it's simply a D chord with your thumb on the low E string to create an F#. If you want UG to display this chord you, again, have to use a weird alternate name.

author: NSpen1
text:
sixthcrusifix
This is a very strange post.  Cadd9 as x32030 or x32033 is exceedingly common.  Haven't you seen the millions of tabs that people write using only G, Em(7), Cadd9 and D through the whole song? (chords almost all with 33 on the top two strings).
x30010 is Cadd2, I think you'll find it's the very first voicing for that name.
D/F# could be better though - the 3rd shape given is 2xx232 using fingers 1, 2 and 3 (why xx?), that could be changed to what you say, except I'm not sure if voicings using the thumb are catered for.  The 7th shape is one I often use 20023x.

author: sixthcrusifix

Cadd2 works nicely for UG but I've never heard anyone call it that by name. I know X32033 is "the" Cadd9 but I guess I just haven't used it in very many songs vs. Cadd2, which everyone is always calling Cadd9. But yeah D/F# makes no real sense on UG and that happens with a lot of slash chords; B/C is really weird (It's like a big box).

author: sixthcrusifix
text:
NSpen1
When I hover over B/C I get X31402 which is almost as bad as a D-shape bar chord in terms of finger acrobatics (Oddly enough the fret positions line up with the fingers it suggests using). I certainly do avoid most pop music from the past 10-15 years, I mostly try to cover Aimee Mann.
I don't mind writing specific instructions but it's ridiculously convenient when the chord hints work with you. I'm not familiar with a lot of chords so I use Jamplay.com's chord finder to figure out what chords I'm playing a lot and that's where I got x30010 as Cadd9 because that's what it shows, including several alternatives which have funky names (but actually do work in UG). Cadd2 doesn't even show up so I hadn't even heard about it (I mean I guess from a theory perspective I should have been able to guess).
I don't doubt the default Cadd9 is the most common one I just lamented that Cadd2 wasn't included since it's the same notes and generally interchangeable for rhythm guitar.

author: Dexex
text:
I want to request the administrators of the chart/tab review process to do two things:
(1 Enforce or amend the evaluation rubric posted here (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/help/rubric).
(2 Close the loophole which allows moderators to reject a chart or tab for "lack of formatting" without declaring specific errors which can be corrected. By not requiring specifics, moderators are empowered to reject any chart/tab for any reason, or for no reason at all, simply by claiming "Lack of formatting."
Backstory RE: The Rubric
I submitted a chord chart for "Get Me Out Of Here," a song that has very active chord progressions. There was no other chart for the song anywhere on the net that showed those chord progressions. The formatting I used to try to make a playable chart failed. The chart was rejected for "Lack of formatting."
I accept (now) that my formatting failed, but I appealed, in part, because of instructions to moderators in the rubric. Under "How to use this document for tab writing?" the rubric states:
"Our moderators will use this document as a guide. If two or more criteria will be in 'Bad' grade, your submission will be rejected."
Notice it says, "two or more criteria," not two or more moderators in agreement. The criteria are:
- Improvement over existing body
- Accuracy of tabs
- Completeness
- Fills
- Notation (legend)
- Timing
- Formatting
It does not say, "if two or more moderators give a single criteria a 'bad' grade, a submission will be rejected." Yet that is what happened. Upon appeal, two more moderators rejected my chart for "Lack of formatting." But no second criteria was cited as a reason for rejection. By the rules spelled out in the rubric, the chart should have been accepted.
So I ask that all of the rubric be enforced, or that it be amended to reflect what actually happens. If it is obsolete, replace it and delete the obsolete version from the web.
RE: Lack of formatting:
I had another chart rejected for "Lack of formatting." I could find no errors, so I appealed. The rationale offered on appeal was that I had misspelled the name of the song — not on the chart itself — but in the form used to submit the chart for review. The song was "Desperate Guy." In a hurry, I had dropped the "s," calling the song "Deperate Guy." That was an error for sure, but it was a simple typo. The chart itself had no format errors.
When I learned what my "Lack of formatting" error was, I resubmitted the chart. To date, it has earned 10 five-star ratings. A more helpful response from the moderator would have pointed out the specific reason(s) for the rejection, and encouraged correction and re-submittal. That didn't happen. We could have avoided a lot of frustration if moderators were simply required to be specific when claiming "lack of formatting" errors.
More evidence of a problem:
After my failure with the "Get Me Out Of Here" chart, I tabbed it. The tab was accepted, but the following from the "Votes & comments" section underscores the problem.
Ryan Crane voted to reject with 1 point
Lack of formatting.
ayreon77
ryan you have to give some explanation why you [are]
rejecting all these tabs, this one is pretty good.
ayreon77 voted to approve with 5 points
Clearly, even other moderators are confused by "Lack of formatting" being used as a justification for rejecting a submission. I invite you to review the tab to see for yourself if it warranted a rejection for "Lack of formatting." If not, then "Lack of formatting" is being used indiscriminately.
I believe that allowing nonconstructive criticism to continue will ultimately discourage people from submitting charts and tabs, thereby making UG a poorer resource for us all.
Respectfully submitted,
Dexex

author: Colohue
text:
Tell you what you want to do then.
Since there are many many lessons and very few moderators, who do have to cover all the other areas as well, there are a few ways contributors can help them out.
For example, instead of having them traipse through numerous different lessons and columns, some with strange titles and even stranger content we can post our contributions in the
UG Contribution
area. Here they can look through the lessons posted by people who have made them not only more accessable but more available to comments and scrutiny. This also means that other users and moderators without the ability to work with lessons or columns can comment and assist.
There is also a thread there designed to aid in column and lesson creation, this can be found
here
. Using this we can make sure that our contribution stands out and is accurate enough to be uploaded.
Most of the moderators are Russian, and so this is not their natural language. This is a Russian run website after all and all in all they do a good job, especially considering how many websites in the US and other English speaking countries were shut down because of their tab databases. As contributors it's up to us to be good writers. Also one thing which I have been guilty of is submitting a lesson as if it is a forum post, when instead of using bold tabs with '[' signs I should be using '<' signs. It's then up to the moderator to put that right. It can take a while and needs a very methodical touch.
If you are annoyed by the language used I can completely understand, but it's up to the user submitting it, so best to comment on their work about it. Otherwise perhaps you could post some revision ideas for them or for the moderators who have the ability to change things. Personally when I make a new lesson I put it onto UG Contribution then PM PiCSeL, who looks it through and does the best he can to make sure it's good enough to be worth uploading.
Asking for more lessons is not going to help. Posting clear, concise and helpful lessons in a practised, methodical way will. I hope you do so, because I do agree, we do need more accurate and helpful lessons. Just see what's missing and go for it.

If you are tooling around the net, and find an article that you think would be good to post on UG, you are allowed to do so. BUT- you absolutely MUST give the author credit. Even on the internet, copying and pasting someones work, and calling it your own is plagiarism.
Taking someone else's article without their permission and crediting their name is still illegal... it's still copyrighted content and more or less blantant theft. No different than posting a Metallica MP3 and saying it's by Metallica... Since UG has advertisements and such, they are basically using other people's work for profit. On the other hand, that's exactly what Youtube does, and they aren't going anywhere.

You don't need to have done something to have a valid opinion.)
3. "**** you." You know. That's always the best argument.
Since the people who submit the worst articles don't care at all, often don't even have the capacity to understand how terrible their work is, and use extremely childish arguments to defend their horrible work, it basically becomes the moderators' responsibility to clean up or reject such work. If they are Russian and they don't read or write English well, that's understandable, but maybe they should get some more fluent English speakers to work with the submitted content.

author: Spaztikko
text:
I had an idea about a different way to deal with adbots that could be more effective, at least on the frontline.
Firstly, give every single (or a large, and I mean substantial amount thereof) user the power to send a new user to an area similar to the FotB, eg "quarantine". Quarantine is a place where, if a new account (ie up to a fortnight old) does something suspicious eg posts ads, or does something borderline that people aren't too sure about, goes.
The user in question is then checked through via a current mod, or whoever that is in the roles currently in place. If it is confirmed to be an advertisement/spam/pornbot, the account is banned. If unjust, the user is set free and can continue as a normal poster.
Current users who abuse the system get the privilege taken away from them, of course.
I think that a system in place like this will enable more adbots to be taken out faster than beforehand, while still ensuring that innocent users do not get caught up.
I was thinking of this when I remembered a moderator somewhere tell us they spent more then half their time online killing adbots rather than actually contributing stuff, and as such I felt this could potentially alleviate the presence that the adbots have on both the mod's time and the user's screens.

Also, I dont propose we get rid of the report system either, but since that either is for older users and generally flames/spam/etc, or very new users with ads/pr0n/spam/etc, the current report system could still do it's job and new bots could be killed by the general public, saving time and less report feeds.

author: Roc8995
text:
Unfortunately this sort of system would create a ton of headaches - perhaps I can convince you.
I should note that these are my opinions and impressions and don't represent UG's official stance.
First, we have a
ton
of new users. 3300 people registered yesterday. That's nuts. A large proportion of new users have a specific question that they want answered, right away, and they want to post quickly to get help. A big reason why we haven't implemented waiting periods, quarantines, etc. is that turning those users away, or making them jump through hoops to get help, is going to prevent them from returning, which is what we really want. Even more than new members, we want people coming back to UG and becoming part of the community.
Second, giving users the power to 'banish' or 'quarantine' is a bit nerve-wracking. While I'm sure the vast majority of users would take it seriously and use it properly, the only way to verify whether they are or not is to monitor the results. Even if it took a certain number of users to create the quarantine, I have a bad feeling the Pit or groups of users who communicate outside of UG would occasionally abuse it. This would take more mod power than we currently use to police. We use the report system because by not giving users the ability to actually take action, we remove the motivation to misuse the system. Nothing happens if you send a fake report; if you disingenuously quarantined another user, you've ruined someone else's experience, and then a mod has to go back and fix it, in which case more effort has been expended than it would take to just delete a few spam posts.
To make it shorter - we'd rather give real people a pleasant experience, and avoid false punishments, than have a few bots have an ad up for 10 minutes.

author: Spaztikko
text:
Thats cool, I can see where you're coming from.
Of course this idea of sending people to a quarantine place is scary, and you're bang on with pretty much all the negatives here.
The way I thought about this though is that, quite simply, you only give responsible users the privilege to use the power. That way you have people you can rely on to handle responsibly, and if the power is misused there are always warnings and bans able to be given too, as well as the permanent loss of the power. As you said, a ton of users register here. When up to user discretion, if the poster gives a question they need answered it can be done, and if it is a general bot they can go away.

author: Krieger91
text:
I was thinking about this the other day.
Lots and lots of people comment on those articles, the only problem is, after a while, there is literally no point.
I haven't written in one for ages, because, for some reason, by the time it appears on my news feed, there are so many comments, that anything I write will be ignored.
Many people would like to have their opinion heard (read) and they resort to answering the top comments to hog the first space. Which is fricking annoying.
Would this work (Or something along these lines; consider it a starting point)?
Every 20 or 50 comments (you choose), all the comments get wrapped and hidden in tags, that can be revealed (think of something along the lines of the spoiler tags in the forum section).
Within these tags, comments can still be upvoted (avoids people double voting. There should be a rule in which you must reveal the tags, ctrl-f your comment and close) and answered, if there's a discussion that can be had.
50 comments afterwards, it happens again. Different tags, maybe. Or it kind of defeats the point.
That way, after a certain amount of comments, there is more hope that your comment will be read, as it will almost always appear as top comment. Once you've checked in the tags.
The amount of times I've got to a WQ article, thought of an answer, that maybe someone hasn't thought of, but there's hardly any point in writing because I know that it won't be read. Then maybe I mention it on the Friday article, and someone is like "hey yeah, that's a good one. How come it didn't get voted?"
It would also avoid people hogging all the space by pretentiously answering the top comments.
