author: travislausch
text:
I've noted in the comments on the review of Scale The Summit's new album that the "lyrics" section of reviews can pose some issues with instrumental albums.
So I have a couple of ideas that might alleviate this problem:
1) Completely remove the "lyrics" section altogether. Definitely the most rash action, but honestly, there are probably a lot of people like myself who simply don't care about lyrics in a song or album, and I always have no idea what to write in that section, even when I'm reviewing an album with lyrics. And considering the rise of popularity with instrumental bands like STS and Animals As Leaders and post-rock bands like God Is An Astronaut and Mogwai, and so many jazz instrumental albums, it makes less and less sense to give lyrics their own section in reviews. And "singer skills" is something that appears under both the "lyrics" and "sound" section of the reviews anyways.
2) Okay, some people really do care about lyrics, so maybe removing that section isn't going to please a lot of people. But perhaps add a "N/A" score to the drop down and have your programmers figure out how to make that have zero impact on the total score of the album. That way, if there are no lyrics, you don't have to rank them at all, you can just go "N/A" and that's it!
3) A hybrid of the above solutions. Make the entire "lyrics" section optional. You can just choose not to have that section in your reviews or leave it in. If it's an instrumental record's review, there won't even BE a "lyrics" section, just "sound" and "overall impression". Have it so you can opt out by clicking a check box or something like that.
Just some ideas to make the process of writing reviews more streamlined for the end-user.

author: MikeyRoberto
text:
This has been very frustrating for me this past week. I'm trying to upload GuitarPro tabs for songs by the band Invalids which I've copied directly from the guitarist of the band's own Tabit files (with permission, of course) and no Invalids song follows a verse/chorus format, they're a math rock band, and five of the songs I tried to post are all under a minute long, so the fact that 4.8 is being thrown at me for every single one just leads me to believe none of these people are even listening to the tab because if they did they would realize that there isn't a verse or a chorus. I even labeled different parts with letters and updated the tab and got back a message saying "no changes made," so then I have to explain that yes I did in fact make a change; it's to the point that I have the message saved in notepad so I can just copy and paste it. Even when I upload a tab that I've already gone through and labeled each section with letters I still get the 4.8 recommendation. Pete asked me to upload all of the Invalids tabs that I've got, but I didn't realize how tiresome the process of getting a tab approved would be.
I understand there's a 3 day waiting period to allow the tabber to fix mistakes before approving, but under section 1.3 of the Approval Guide it states that “You can immediately approve a tab if it has no musical or formatting mistakes.” Given that I'm uploading tabs that were copied directly from the band themselves, and they've been checked over multiple times by myself and other musicians to ensure their accuracy I don't get why a person who voted to approve one of my tabs was told, "wait 3 days before voting on this." There is no reason to wait when there's nothing I could possibly to do make the tab any better.
indusapoth
Incidentally, your tabs have been helping me out for years, particularly your Haken and Tricot tabs, so it feels good to be sort of vindicated by seeing you're also annoyed by this. You're pretty much right on the money with "potentially discouraging to new users who have indeed taken the time to label their sections."

author: jasonw.whitson
text:
First let me say that I love your website and enjoy your official tabs very much!  I am a music educator with 20+ years of experience in both high school and college.  I play guitar and bass, but recently a lot more time on bass as I play for school musical productions and churches.  I have paid for the official tabs for quite a while and happily.  I tend to be less of a tab reader, using it only as a reference for position on the neck and primarily read notation as that is what I am far more familiar with.
While I love the features of official tabs I would really like to change one thing.  The ability to read notation in official parts without the odd enharmonic spellings.
For example:  On your non official chord charts the key will be listed as Eb, but the chords will use sharp names, like D#.  This is confusing on a couple of levels - 1. When you are in Eb your mind thinks the key (Eb, Ab, Bb, Cm Fm Gm Ddim) and then seeing D#, G# A# creates unnecessary confusion.  2. The sharp chords are really more theoretical, as they are really not something we see in major diatonic based music, unless we have a lot of secondary dominants or accidentals in certain minor keys.
Now, you fix this problem in your features by turning on flats in the non-official chord charts.
I would love that feature in the official tab notation sections on the individual parts.
For example: Led Zeppelin's "Hey, Hey, What Can I Do". It's in the key of Db. However the tab alters all of the notes to be the sharp enharmonic equivalent except for Bb and Eb - The tonic Db is always notated as C#, Ab is G# and so on.  It is confusing for someone like me that is used to reading notation where I know I am in a certain key and where I am on the neck for those notes...seeing the accidentals makes me have to think about what's happening and creates instances where scale patterns or skips appear to be different intervals on first glance.  I also think it is potentially confusing for musicians who want to give reading notation a chance.
You can transpose keys in the official tab, so in the above example it's actually easier to read in the key of D (transposing that in my head to Db is far easier than reading the Db version.)
Could you possibly add an [allow flats] option in your official tabs?
Again, I truly enjoy using your site to practice or just enjoy playing some of my favorite music!  Thank you!

author: ninelima
text:
I propose a search function to find incomplete chord sheets and suggests them for completion.
Perhaps placed somewhere under TAB REQUESTS or Suggested for you.
It should be fairly simple to identify incomplete chord sheets programmatically. Since a complete chord sheet would typically have about  50% chord lines and 50% lyric lines, looking at this ratio should be able to identify potential incomplete tabs.
A successful completion of a previously tagged incomplete, should have a higher IQ reward that a simple correction. Perhaps close to a new chord sheet.

author: ninelima
text:
mandelstamdavid
Aah! the language! English is not my first language.
No, this would not be applicable to songs with only one verse and/or chorus.
Assume:
tab = chord sheet
I was thinking like this:
There are many tabs that have only chords for the first verse and chorus and then followed by the remaining verses (without chords). These tabs would be really good candidates for "correction" because they are already there and there is an example (the first verse/chorus).
Tabs like these, is a very good place for novice tabbers  to start. That is what I did, but it was difficult for me to find suitable tabs (like these)
So ... How would we determine if a tab is complete or incomplete?
I suggest that we count the number of total lines of the tab. Call that t. Then count the total lines that have chords on them, call that c. then x = c / t;
I posit that for a complete tab x should be less than, but close to 0.5. Maybe 0.3  to 0.4, but you will need to do some tests on your metadata to determine a good suitable metric for x.
I hope this makes sense to you ... I recommend a 2 drink minimum :-)

author: martin788
text:
Hello,
One thing I use in my personal tabs is notation for duration of chords. Chord tabs with chord names but without duration can be tricky to interpret correctly without any idea of duration. Is there an accepted way to give some indications of duration in chord tabs?
For the record, this is how I do it in my personal tabs. At the beginning of the tab I write 4/8 or some similar measure information, that is also the default duration of a chord. When the chord lasts for two measures or more measures, I write the number of measures after it like so:
Em 2
If on the other hand the chord lasts half a measure, i.e. the measure is shared between two chords, I wrote the two chords between brackets like so:
(Em Am)
That's it. I find this extremely helpful. Recently I published a tab using this notation, and it was rejected because of it, so I had to suppress the duration information. As a consequence, today I just made a new tab for my own use, and I made it personal and didn't publish it because it uses the duration information, and I was too lazy to make two versions, one complete for me and one stripped of duration information for everyone. It's a bit unfortunate as other people may like the tab. And it's unfortunate for me as well as other people may have improved on the tab, which might benefit me as well.
Any suggestion? Thank you.
PS: I hesitated between "Tab talk" and this group as the correct destination for the message...

author: martin788
text:
I actually like % better than my numbers and will use that, thanks!
I also agree that bar signs and proportional space can be a solution, especially in instrumental parts.
I'm still not entirely convinced for lyrics. A typical case is that most chords have the same duration, but on a few spots they are half the duration. Using bar signs everywhere clutters the tab. Suddenly using bar signs doesn't work well. And even if the chords are precisely placed on the lyrics, the player can't know for sure that they are (they frequently are not!) and the timing can be quite challenging to figure out for beginners who don't have a sense of what is typical and so cannot guess. I agree on the other hand that brackets are misleading to the uninitiated.
So here's another idea. Use an hyphen to "bind" two chords of half duration (reminiscent of the beaming of eight notes compared to unbeamed quarter notes). To take the One chord tab linked by NSpen1, instead of (present):
|Em      |G      |A      |C   B7  |
you'd get:
Em        G       A       C - B7
So: no need to use bars everywhere; and a minimal sign is used that will be gracefully ignored by the uninitiated. The sign's meaning can even be guessed by the uninitiated since the hyphen is normally used to fuse two items into one.
This could be extended, when the duration is a quarter of the normal one (which is rare in my experience), by using an equal sign ("double hyphen", reminiscent of the double beaming of sixteenth notes). So instead of (present):
|Em      |G      |A      |C   B7  |Em B Em D/F# |
you'd get:
Em        G       A       C - B7  Em=B=Em=D/F#
This also solves the ambiguity when a 4-beat bar contains 3 chords. And there's even a triple bar symbol available (see it here if it displays correctly: ≡ ) that could bind chords half that duration. My two cents, in case the suggestion is found useful.
PS: will my tabs be accepted now if I use hyphens in this way?

author: MaggaraMarine
text:
I just don't see the reason for inventing your own signs. Bar lines work just fine for the purpose of chord tabs. People who use chord tabs will already be familiar with how the song goes. Nobody "sight reads" chord tabs - they use chord sheets for a simple way of memorizing song structure, lyrics and chords. If you want more details, you want something more specific than just chord tabs. The thing is, the more symbols you have to use, the more complicated it gets.
My question would be, what about songs where the chord changes on the off-beat, for example if the song is based on a common rhythm like dotted quarter + 8th tied to a half note (so the chord change happens on the "and" of 2)? You would need yet another symbol for that. But that's why chord tabs aren't made to notate exact details in the song. That's what sheet music is for. To use chord tabs, you need to listen to the song first.
If I write my own chord sheets, I always use barlines, and if there are some rhythms that I need to remember, I write them using traditional rhythmic notation (but UG doesn't allow that at the moment, and I think it's fine - as I said, I don't think chord tabs need to be that specific).

author: martin788
text:
The reason why I invented brackets, which I now turned into hyphens, is to indicate where suddenly in a song two chords are half the ordinary duration. I have found that without this indication I will often mess up.
I don't sight read in the sense of discovering the song for the first time in the chord tab and expecting it to contain everything, but I do play as I read, that's what the Autoscroll function is for as far as I understand, and signalling when chords are half their duration (or when they last for several bars which I will in future indicate with %) is part of the basic info I need in the tab to not mess up when playing the song.
Note that I have many tabs (200+) and that I sing while I play the guitar. That means I need, in real time, to read the lyrics (often not in my mother tongue), sing them, read the chords and play the guitar. So the exceptional changes in chord durations are like little traps, especially when I have not sung that particular song for a few months, in which I will often fall if there is no clear indication.
Bar lines might work but it's annoying to use them throughout. Question: would a tab be accepted with this:
Em      G      A      |C   B7|
instead of this (present):
|Em     |G     |A      |C   B7|
? I cannot bring myself to the latter as it's too annoying and redundant. Right now (in my personal tabs) I indicate the bar duration in the heading (e.g. 4/8), then it's assumed that the chords last this duration, and then I just add convenient notation when the duration is several bars (was number, will be %) or only fractions of bars (was brackets, will be hyphens). That seems the obvious way to go as far as I'm concerned. But I might use bar signs as shown above if accepted, for the sake of sharing the tabs.
Regarding your last question, if we consider the case where in a 4-beat bar one chord lasts for the first 3 beats and the second chord is on the last beat, then that's:
C - C=Am
per my previous message.

author: Phil Starr
text:
It's good to see a sensible debate about this. Ive tried a couple of times to start one going with little success.
The main reason good tabs get rejected is because of poor formatting and technical problems due to the way the site is set up. For instance I submitted the chords for a song three times before they were accepted. They were being rejected because of tagging them as 'live version' and when I changed it to 'live' it went up. Rejection often has nothing to do with musical accuracy which means we lose good songs. Some times we must be losing good tabbers
The solution would be to give better instructions to rejected tabbers and to make the techniques for tabbing more transparent. Perhaps a 'new to UG' section or a standard email or message to rejected tabbers?
To be fair the staff can't possibly do quality control, hundreds of tabs go up each week and the only way of checking would be to try to play them. They cleared 4000 tabs in the first couple of weeks in january.
If you haven't had three tabs accepted you won't know about the pre approval list. All submitted tabs are put up for us to look at and recommend or not. A good system but underused.
The other thing that would help would be if more people rated. My half dozen tabs have attracted one rating in 4000 hits so 5 of them are still unrated. If say, 1 in a hundred rated then the 40 ratings would give people a rough idea if they were any good. My articles have all been rated.
I absolutely agree with the idea that we should be reluctant to throw out somone's hard work and looking at a number of tabs helps you understand the song but for beginners a bad tab can waste a lot of time and be very discouraging .

author: astodds
text:
Hey. My name is Andrew, and I've been using UG for around 3 years now. As i've been submitting tabs, I've noticed that sometimes your have a tab that is better than most of the other ones that have been posted for the same song, but you have posted yours a month later or so. As a result, the other person has much more views, ratings and comments on their tab, even though it may not be the best one anymore.
With that, there are a number of things that could be done to fix this. I have thought up a few ideas for this, but the main one is this:
Have a "Certificate of Excellence" for the best tabs of a certain song. This could be represented next to the star rating with a different symbol, e.g. a blue star and the number of blue stars. How would this work? Well there are a few answers to that. First, while your tab is being reviewed, a moderator could add a blue star if they think your piece stands out and is exceptional. Also, this could be available to only certain members (e.g. people with a ranking over 40,000, people, people with a score over 25, or people with over 5 contributions) There would be no "Down vote" to this feature, just positive ratings.
Hopefully this can be made possible in one of the next updates.
-astodds

author: Roc8995
text:
Admins have consistently declined requests for more people to review tabs, citing a need to keep the number fairly small to keep quality high. Asking for reviewers to officially endorse tabs is far too much extra work, plus then the second we do that, we'll have people complaining that their tab was better, or was pushed aside because a "preferred user" had a tab, even if it wasn't better, is just a nightmare.
I think it's reasonable to expect better tabs to rise to the tab naturally. Eventually the better, newer ones should rise above the old ones. A small tweak to the value of votes - newer ones mattering a tad more than old ones, for example - might help. I don't think we need to add manual labor to the process.

author: astodds
text:
It's no more manual labor than pressing a button. Also, it could be helpful to see what experienced guitarists think about the piece, and showing that statistic with the amount of stars. It would ultimately be better for the guitar community.
Furthermore, countless times i've seen tabs in the top 100 section that are nowhere near as good as the tabs that are in the later versions. It could really help to make the good tabs stand out.

author: Roc8995
text:
It's far more effort than pressing a button, obviously, even if we disagree about the semantics of how "manual" it is. You're asking editors to be closely familiar with every song they see, and play or read through the tab thoroughly enough to make a judgment not only about how close it is, but how much closer it might be than another tab that exists already for the song. That's a lot to ask from a handful of volunteers, and it also invites a lot of questions about abuse or preferential treatment from the people who now have the power to effectively overrule the user base on tab quality.
That's a lot of work when you multiply it by the volume that our approval people are expected to work through. I don't think it's viable with our current model. I think it makes way more sense to refine a model that relies on crowdsourcing the input of users who actually care about the tab after it's been published.

author: astodds

author: Roc8995
text:
I'm not riled up. I am trying to explain why your suggestion does not exist on UG in the way you say it should. If your idea is simply "highlight good tabs," then I'm all for it. This is what my version of constructive criticism looks like, I'm sorry if it seemed rude to you.

Furthermore, there needs to be better quality control. The fact that plagiarism of this level got past the people in charge of the news on this site probably means there needs to be real changes implemented regarding how that part of the website operates. This is a serious ethical issue that Niass cannot take full blame for; an issue that leaves the website open to cease-and-desist letters, take-down notices, etc. This kind of plagiarism is the result of serious editorial issues at Ultimate-Guitar - where there seems to be little oversight regarding the publications (as is often commented on in the comments sections of articles where people complain about the poor proofing of articles).
Here is a useful link about plagiarism and journalistic ethics. Whoever is in charge of news on this website should probably review relevant literature and have a discussion with the editorial board and/or contributors to the section.
https://www.spj.org/ethics-papers-plagiarism.asp

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
UG Support
May I ask why tabs are not held to the same standard when there is possible material gain involved with implementation of the IQ system? The UG standard is one thing, and lyric rights are another; how is usage of the same musical information between two submissions not plagiarism, though?

author: Emptywordsbass
text:
NeoMvsEu
I think the issues of compensation for user-generated digital labor are a very complex ethical issues. However, I do believe the two critical distinctions between the situations (news submissions and tab submissions) have to do with representation and scale. As staff of UG, their news contributions should be held to a higher standard because they represent the website in some official capacity (whether compensated or not - I am unsure of how that functions on this website). Second, news articles are presumably submitted and published at a much lower rate than tabs, making their regulation quite feasible (whereas regulating tab for plagiarism would be relatively difficult).
Furthermore, as far as copyright is concerned,one does not have the right to a transcription of a musical work unless they own the right to the work they are transcribing or perform some kind of derivative transformation/rearrangement that fundamentally alters the work (and still, the copyright owner must approve to the publication of the derivative work). Anyone can transcribe music in whatever form they want for personal use (just as people may sample songs for personal use) but the moment the person wishes to distribute/publish the work, the rights of the copyright owner come into play. UG's licensing agreements therefor allow for the website to be protected, and people whose tabs are copied online are not being infringed as they never have rights beyond being able to publish the transcription. That's why multiple publishing companies can all publish basically the same transcriptions of the same songs without being sued by one another - its because they never own the song, just the right to publish it.
Edit - Upon second thought, I guess someone could own the specific transcription of a text if they had a licensing agreement with a copyright owner of a song to own the transcription, but barring that, the transcriber would not own the rights to their transcription.

That is correct. C9 is a DOMINANT 9th chord, not an added tone chord. In this case, you'd get 1-3-5-b7-9.

text:
The count-in feature is really useful in conjunction with the metronome for practicing tabs, and I'm glad it exists. However, I do have a couple of suggestions to improve it
There is currently a gap between when the count-in ends and when the playback actually starts; this is rather confusing, and it would be great if you could remove it so that audio flows smoothly from count-in to playback.
The count-in is broken for songs in which the time signature changes. Take, for example, the official tab for Avenged Sevenfold's "Beast and the Harlot". The song begins with an intro in 9/8 that transitions to 6/8, and then to 4/4 for the main portion of the song; the outro is the same as the intro, meaning it goes from 4/4 in the final chorus to 9/8 to 6/8. If, for instance, I want to practice the chorus, in 4/4, I still get a count-in in 9/8, which is really confusing because those time signatures have very different feels. It would be much more helpful if the count-in were in the proper time signature.
Keep up the great work everyone, and stay safe!

author: kilbie
text:
For discussing playing instruments at the moment there is the Bass Guitar, Electric Guitar, Acoustic & Classical Guitar, Guitar & Bass Basics, and Advanced Techniques.
The bass, electric and acoustic forums are all mostly used for discussion of the actual instrument. Like which one to buy, how someone broke their guitar/bass, and identifying a guitar/bass. These forums occasionally also get threads about which song to learn.
The Guitar & Bass basics is a forum for beginners asking questions about what song to learn, what the best way to practice is, and how to string their guitar. Most of the threads in the Advanced techniques forum are about guitar techniques.
There is no forum at the moment for general discussion about guitar and bass. These threads usually go in the electric guitar, bass, acoustic forum, or the pit. If the thread ends up in the bass or guitar forums the people in the other forum will miss out. The thread goes in the pit, it will not be taken seriously.
The forum that is for guitar and bass could have all the guitar shop stories, threads about things to remember for performances, how a guitar/bass was damaged, which guitar/bass to bring to college, and everything else that is not about specific models of guitars and bass and guitar parts (no 'which guitar' or 'what guitar is this' threads'). Also the forum would not be for guitar technique or for beginners asking beginner questions, there are already forums for that.
The point of this forum would be for the threads that don't really fit in with the other threads in the guitar and bass forums. Because almost all the threads in those forums are about which guitar to buy, why a certain brand of guitar is awesome, and how to fix a broken guitar.
Does anyone else think a forum for guitar and bass would be a good idea.

I frequently post in threads and end up moving them to my bookmarks toolbar so that I can revisit them at some point in the future to see whether anyone has replied to my post, because I'm narcissistic that way. author: Pan-Tallica
text:
So there has been some obvious frustration with the content posted on this site of late. Before I express any criticism, I should say that I believe the team has done a good job with the addition of "Monday fresh"-type articles and the re-vamping of the columns section. These are both very promising, and I believe will serve the site well in the long-run. Unfortunately, they might be a moot point if the users are not satisfied with the articles being posted. I don't want to see people leaving out of frustration.
I am curious to know how the news content is found. It seems to be the case that a few major music news sites (like NME) are searched for recent news, and anything deemed "good enough" is posted on UG with credit going to the site from which the article was obtained. Am I right about this process?
If so, can articles be taken from ANY site, so long as credit is given? Or is there some sort of agreement which must be made with another site in order to use their content?
If it is the case that content can be taken from anywhere, perhaps it is time to start looking in... other places. The fact of the matter is that many users don't want to read about mainstream gossip regarding Nickelback, Courtney Love, or Axl Rose (although that is the easiest news to find). Unfortunately, it seems to be the case that when 1 legitimate article is posted along with 2 "gossipy" articles, all three articles get painted with the same brush. In other words, people are not going to respond well to the news unless they care
consistently
. It is a shame to see people frustrated about the news because the lessons and interviews are fantastic.
I am curious about this process because I want to help in some way. There has to be some means of fixing this issue - all we need is to start a bit of a discussion.

author: Colohue
text:
The news section is largely user generated. That's why it's always late and largely taken from other websites. It's also why some articles are credited and some are not.
The quality control is nonexistent unless you wear the UG Team brand. This isn't a news website. UG doesn't care about unique journalism, interesting debates and breaking news on the front page. UG cares about the tabs and keeping people around for the tabs.
The updates that have been done have been designed to appeal to the masses. Like and dislike is a perfect example of this. However, it's all that they can do. Music news websites work on a 24/7 basis, writing articles as and when they come in. UG is an office in Kaliningrad. They all want to go home at night, the same as everybody else.
All they can do is hire bloggers and aim to appeal to the ignorant masses in the attempt to ensure that they die as slowly as possible. Hopefully they're looking at new advertising markets. Android have been looking to generate mutual interest, as an example, and I'm busy generating contacts, but not for UG. My last attempt at a new market was the animation, but that didn't exactly go far. They're just not interested anymore.
The economy is limiting. UG has to stick to the tab niche in order to survive. The news is only there as an addition, not as a source of entertainment. There's already too much crammed onto the main page, and each individual section is sparse and impossible to navigate. It's tough, but there's really nothing that can be done. The news has been going downhill since even before I was a CC, and one of the reasons I stopped was that I could hardly delete comments insulting UG when I completely agreed.

author: sixxtoes
text:
Hey everyone, I just need to vent some frustration with the process around a tab I recently submitted.
So I hear a song and immediately come here to grab the chords and play along. I find the song under the wrong artist name (They listed the writer of the song rather than the band that actually played the song) and begin to play along.  Immediately I notice some chords are missing, some are in the wrong spots, and later on there's an incorrect lyric (actually 2).
I get to work. I message the artist and clarify the lyrics, put the proper chords in the proper spots, add in some of the bass notes, and list this song under the correct artist. I go to bed happy with my tab submission.
I wake up to my tab rejected because a version already exists. I immediately point out the many differences between my version and the other version and the admin decides to put my tab up as a correction instead.  This correction gets passed and the tab is now at least accurate, yay!
My beef is simple. The tab that's listed is 100% my work.  I got the correct lyrics, I figured out the correct chords and placed them in the correct spots.  The original author put the bare minimum effort, but currently my creation sits with their name on it.  Literally nothing of the original authors work is left except a 2 line sentence introducing the song, but they are still called the 'author'. My name is listed as the bottom of 3 contributors despite the fact that I did literally all the work.
Rant over.
Should authorship of a tab change if more than 50% of the original tab changes? Or should the first person to submit it (regardless of accuracy) be forever the author of that tab?  Am I just sour grapes?

author: NSpen1
text:
sixxtoes
It would have been helpful if you had given the link, or even said what the artist and song was.
Anyway, the correction is here
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=464555
The two tabs look very similar to me, I don't think you have a case at all.
I mean, "I got the correct lyrics".  There's literally one word different (and some o's added on the oohs).  Chord placement is always a correction, not a reason for a new tab.  So the only change of any real significance is the addition of some A chords.
And if you find a tab on the site under the wrong artist, you should not submit your own similar tab under the correct artist, instead you should post in the
Contribution Title/Metadata Change thread -
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1701390
to tell us to move it.

of one of them, update the chords, and it keeps telling me to publish the tab... so I think okay, I'll finally start contributing back and polish this up, so I hit the button to do it. Then it's rejected because it looks like a duplicate with minor corrections. BRUH, YOU GUYS ASKED ME TO SUBMIT IT through the UX. And now every time I login, I see this stupid rejection thing and there's no way to delete it. I get it, UG is full of a bunch of passive aggressive people who can barely play guitar and tell the difference between a G chord and a G/B, that's fine, but just let me play in peace and make personal tabs without badgering me to submit it so you can reject it.

author: NSpen1
text:
davidknise
No, what I said is just the truth.  If someone is posting about a submission they have a query about they should absolutely say what it is and give the link instead of being vague, that should be obvious.  And in the case above, there is not enough difference for a new tab version.
Quote by davidknise
Do you guys want the website and tabs to improve or not?
Yes, by submitting corrections where appropriate, not by submitting new tabs under a different artist name to the existing one.  And it was approved as a correction.
Otherwise, quoting works sometimes, sometimes not, it would be nice if they could fix that.
And I agree that it's often not helpful when the system keeps prompting you to submit a personal tab.  However, that doesn't mean you have to submit it, there is a notice saying to check existing versions and that we don't accept duplicates, and you also should be able to turn off the prompts.
You don't have to add a strumming pattern, that's optional.  Your tab is in fact an even more obvious correction of an existing one, not a new version, than the one first posted about here.

author: davidknise
text:
NSpen1
mine's a UX issue with the site. I made a
Personal Edit
and I clicked the link requesting me to publish from the editing page. Every time I save a personal tab, it asks me to publish, it's annoying. If y'all are trying to run a
business
that
charges
you should take
legitimate feedback
, especially about UI/UX issues.
I'm a software engineer and respect what it takes to make software, so I'm always happy to pay, but I'm not paying for overlords who don't care about correctness to waste my time constantly prompting me to publish my stuff.
> The two tabs look very similar to me, I don't think you have a case at all.
Similar can be a HUGE difference. If I put G D Em C in a song... that's not the same as G 320033, D/F 2x0232, Em7 022033, Cadd9 x3033. You're stating that correcting the position of a chord over lyrics is "too similar." That along with phrases like "even more obvious" and "sorry, but" mean "I don't know this song, no I'm not going to listen, and we don't care if the tabs are actually correct at all. If it's close that's good enough." That's what most of the tabs on this site get you... close. None of the three versions of Got What I Got by Jason Aldean are right, yet the highest voted one with 184 and 5 star rating is the furthest away from correct. Could I tab it out for others... yes. But knowing that you're only accepting "already close enough" means I'm not going to put any effort into sharing. A huge disservice to the community.

author: NSpen1
text:
davidknise
Okay, I did the same thing with this very tab, saved as a personal tab, changed a few chords.  Clicked save, then I get the notice
Checking the "Don't show this message again" box should solve that problem.  I'm not going to click SEND A PUBLIC COPY because if I do it may go straight on the site, but if you do that you should still have another stage where you can compare your tab against existing versions and decide whether to submit or not.
Now you may feel that there are improvements that can be made to that process; that's definitely something you can post about in Site Suggestions.
Edit: Well, checking the "Don't show this message again" box doesn't work for me, I still keep getting that again and again, every time I save.  I agree that is annoying.  So that appears to be a bug, and it might be better to just get rid of it altogether.
Well, those are very cliched variations to the most cliched progression ever ... I wouldn't regard that as a huge difference or a reason for a new tab, it's rather a correction, variations on the basic chords.
Your tab has Em instead of Em7, and G/B instead of Bm.  I put it as a correction
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=471413
It's very very similar.  It couldn't possibly be a new version.  We shouldn't have multiple versions for the same song with one or two chords only changed (or the chords shifted in position by a few characters).
It's not the case that we don't care whether tabs are correct, but making corrections to existing similar tabs is the way that should be done.

author: brobrocean69
text:
When searching for songs in my own library during live gigs, they only show up if you type it exactly as the title or artist is written.  For example, if you wan't "Mary Jane's Last Dance" and "Last Dance" is searched, it won't appear.  Or for artists like "The Eagles," it is listed as "Eagles."  It would be helpful if there was an option to search one word of the title or artist to show the song in the search bar when taking requests.  Thank you!
In addition, I'd love to use the app during gigs (which I have a subscription for), but it won't allow multiple tabs to be open at once so multiple songs can be ready immediately.  For this reason, I'm forced to use a browser.  For a working musician, there can't be time between songs to allow for the wifi or data connection to load the next song.  Many of the features aren't available through a browser on an ipad, which is fine, but that just means the app needs to be configured to allow multiple tabs to be open.  Thanks again!

author: jimmy_neutron
text:
Notifications if someone has posted in your thread simply wouldn't work. If your thread become anyway busy, you will become completely overcome by notifications, when it is so easy to tell if your thread has been posted in, by simply loading the forums and seeing is it marked with a new posts icon.
As for notifications for responding to your comment, i assume you mean quoted? This has been suggested before, and the consensus, if i recall correctly, was that it would be a massive resource hof, it would require the forum software to be hacked by the Russians(only done when absolutely necessary), and generally more trouble than it is worth.
Instead, if you want to see if you have been quoted, go into the search
function
, not the bar. Search your username, and set the results as view posts. That way is even better imo, as it shows if anyone has mentioned you somewhere, and not just quoted.

author: masonburkhalt1
text:
My objection to the vulgarity has nothing to do with morality and everything to do with business sense.  I honestly didn't know that their slogan was "Play it Fucking Loud," but now that I do, I think the slogan is equally ridiculous.
NeoMvsEu
UGMKZ
Yes UG is a secular site and I understand that the "rock and roll" persona is kind of their thing. Most other companies in most other industries are also secular and also try to identify with their niche of users though and can still do that without potentially offending people.  That said, the problem I have with it is that they (and you apparently) are assuming that every person going to this site are rockers who DGAF.  The problem is that UG is by far the most recognizable tab source on the Internet, and the fact that UG chooses to have that overall persona just doesn't make good business sense and is pretty ignorant from a business perspective.  It's not going to stop me from using the site or anything, I just have to agree with OP that it's insensitive in general to ALL possible consumers of the site who may feel differently, which can hurt their business and overall is just a bad idea.  I learned how to play guitar when I was like...10.  I personally feel like (even though I curse and am not personally offended by it) that I also wouldn't want my young child to be exposed to vulgarity at such a young age and if I found out this was on the site they were using to learn how to play I'd be pissed.  Also, what about all of the parents who put parental controls on their kids computers who in turn are just unable to know about or access the best guitar tab site on the web because there are cuss words on the site.  It's slightly unfair to the kid that because he's not a "ride or die" rocker, he just doesn't even know about UG...  I guess my point is, in literally any circumstance where a business or person does not think past perspectives that are not aligned with their own, unnecessary conflict and turmoil is bound to follow.  As a business it's totally ridiculous that UG didn't think about this.  It's not even about catering to people with a moralistic or religious viewpoint, it's about trying not to isolate ANY potential or prospective consumers.  #endrant

It's clear their really trying to profit from this site in various ways, so it's only common sense that if you own a business and you are really trying to make it profitable you don't want to turn people away unnecessarily.  That's all I'm saying.  It's ignorant in general to have a business but not consider that this kind of blatant crassness is just in poor taste and is likely hurting their profit margins.  I understand not everything is about money and all, but as a business that wants to stay in business, this kind of thing is just so basic and so common sense that it's ridiculous that they opted for the decision to be vulgar in their slogan and emails.  If they didn't think about that then they need a better group of business minds running things, and if they did think of it and opted to go for it anyway that's even worse, and they still should consider a better group of business minded marketing professionals to run things so that they can maximize their success potential.

author: MikeyRoberto
text:
I'm trying to be mostly even-minded about this, but it's just been such a frustrating experience trying to get these tabs uploaded. I'm doing a favour for the band Invalids by posting GuitarPro versions of their songs, Pete (the guitarist of the band) has tabbed everything in Tabit, but since not a lot of people use that program he asked me to upload the songs that I've input in to GP. Invalids' music is really complex, and doesn't usually follow basic verse/chorus compositions so I opt to label separate sections with Letter Markings which are under the same menu as the Intro/Verse/Chorus/Bridge etc. Markings. When you buy tab books from SheetHappens this is also how GuitarPro files have different sections labeled, and since most of the GuitarPro tabs that I use are from SheetHappens this is just what feels best for me when it comes to labeling each part of a song. Now, where the annoyance comes in is despite all of the effort I put in to making my tabs presentable, and making sure the format is neat, and there are no glaring errors, without fail basically every single one of my tabs has received the comment:
"
4.8. Missing GP song parts.
Please mark all parts of the song (Intro, Chorus, Verse, Solo, etc). In addition to Shift + Insert; In GP7 you can also use the Menu->Section->Edit; In GP6 you can use Menu-Section->Insert/Remove."
I have even pre-emptively left a comment on my own pending tab saying, "I have labeled separate sections with letters. This song does not follow a verse/chorus format, thus section 4.8 of the Ultimate Guitar Tablature Guide is non-applicable. Everything is copied directly from the band’s official Tabit tabs with permission, and has been checked over multiple times to ensure it’s accuracy" and a user replied to that comment, quoting 4.8. This same user I have replied to a number of times, explaining to them that I have in fact labeled every section with Letter Markings, and they continue to leave the 4.8 comment on my tabs. I believe it may be because the old Tab Pro player that displays on the pending approval page for whatever reason does not display Letter Markings while it does display Intro/Verse/Chorus markings. The New Player does display Letter Markings, but I imagine not everybody would be using the New Player. That being said, I'm not writing GuitarPro tabs to be viewed in the Tab Pro Player, I am writing GuitarPro tabs to be downloaded and viewed in GuitarPro. I'm getting the impression that many people who are voting and commenting on GuitarPro tabs in the Approval Queue are not actually downloading the tabs and opening them in the program themselves and are rather just looking at it in the Player, which displays a stripped down version of the work authors have actually done. If you are going to be voting on the approval of a GuitarPro tab it is only logical that you should actually download the tab. You owe that courtesy to the tab author.
Also, section 4.8 isn't even required, in the Tablature Guide this is just a recommendation. As an example, many of my tabs contain muted tracks so I can show different fingerings/capo placements, and section 4.5 recommends not to set tracks to mute, yet nobody has ever quoted that to me in the comments. Or section 4.3 with Chord Representation, I've never included any chord names in my tabs. Even section 4.10, adding info like song title, band name, album etc, which is something that I actually did accidentally forget to do for all of my tabs that have been approved has never been quoted to me. So what the heck, why is section 4.8 everybody's go-to section to quote? It is incredibly frustrating.

author: baxissimo
text:
My premise here is that it's impossible for a tab site to offer the "perfect" tab for every single user.  Because when it comes to tabs, "perfect" is in the eye of the beholder.
For me I may know the solo so well that I don't need the tab for it in my writeup -- it's just clutter to me.  Or maybe I just need a few notes to remind me.  Or maybe I want lines of text wrapped differently for my small screen phone.  Or maybe I want a reminder to play some part quieter or louder.
Or maybe I have my own original songs that I'd like to have the tab for accessible through the same nice interface offered by the the UG app and website (with autoscroll and chord highlighting, etc.)
So I don't think it's really possible to have a finite set of tabs that will fully satisfy everyone.
For that reason I think it would be great if a user could create their own private tabs.
As far as I know NO ONE has something like this currently. UG could be the first!  I think this would be a fantastic feature, particularly for songwriters, but really for anyone who is particular about their tabs.

One of the biggest features that would help beginners and open up the Ultimate Guitar app and site to more people would be to allow the user to pick a default instrument and tuning as part of his profile either on the website or within the mobile app- Then when that user clicks on a chord within a song, like G7 for example, the app will show the G7 fingering for the instrument the person has as his 'active' instrument.
It's tough learning the Ukulele when I have to keep switching back and forth between either a chord fingering printout or another Uke chord app to see the ukulele fingering for a given chord when the UG app only shows the guitar fingering... unless I use the UKE version of a song if it's been uploaded. It would also cut down on the number of duplicate tab listings to sift through.
I've been using Ultimate Guitar for years now. I love it. I just don't play enough to learn all the variations of every chord.
Thank you.

The worst example was where someone took a friends AK47 model and put it on Turbosquid (where you upload your models, and others can buy them for a certain price) claiming it was his.

So it could be worse

author: curtisanderson721
text:
The rhythm is made up of 3 things:
1. Time signature (how many beats are in a bar)
2. The divisions/ subdivisions of those beats ( quarter notes, eighth notes, sixteenth notes, etc.)
3. Tempo
The strumming pattern is nothing more than whether or not the strings are hit, missed, or muted on a series of down and up beats. Without the rhythm, the strumming pattern is not only useless, but also counter productive. If you know the rhythm you can alter the strumming pattern or create your own to make the song uniquely fit your style.

author: brettsanace
text:
DiddyD
mandelstamdavid
maguri
I am not disagreeing with any of you, as I respect everyone's right not to allow strumming patterns which is why I created this thread, but I would like to clarify a couple of things. When
NSpen1
says that most of the patterns are not useful he is talking about submitted patterns, not added patterns. As with all corrections, strumming patterns go through a review process before they are approved and added to the tab. Actually many of them go through a double review because if they are approved by someone else I will often check them again and NSpen1 always does (so maybe that is a triple review process). It is probably about 90% of submitted strumming patterns that are rejected with only 10% being approved (often after being corrected). If you come across crap strumming patterns on tabs it is usually because the author has added them themselves without going through the TPA Queue. I don't think anyone is saying that an approved strumming pattern is the only way that a song can be played, similar to having chord tabs and tab tabs they may be played differently.
I also think that having strumming patterns on the site is beneficial for beginners. When you think about how many songs have the same chord progressions often the only thing that distinguishes one song from the other is the rhythm, tempo, riffs. From spending a lot of time reviewing submitted strumming patterns it seems that most beginners think that every song in the world can be played with D_DU_UDU, so I think when they see and can listen to a more accurate pattern, using say sixteenths or triplets, it not only makes them happy because their playing will sound more like the recorded song, but it also educates them as to how to work with rhythm/strumming which I think should be a goal of this site.
Anyway, just to summarise:
- Happy for people not to allow strumming patterns.
- Nearly all approved strumming patterns will be correct.
- I think strumming patterns are a beneficial feature.

author: NSpen1
text:
I believe some of the definitions/string names used by UG for different tunings are not the best, largely because of the insistence on only using sharps, e.g. half step down tuning, C standard.
I think some may have been fixed for Guitar Pro files (and Official files?) as I've seen some flats appearing there, but it would be good to get this changed across the whole site.
You can find some background here, that may give you (more than) enough arguments for and against.
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1723970
I propose that these tunings be changed :
Half-step down tuning to Eb, Ab, Db, Gb, Bb, Eb  instead of  D# G# C# F# A# D#
Drop D + a half-step down to Db, Ab, Db, Gb, Bb, Eb  instead of  C# G# C# F# A# D#
C standard to C F Bb Eb G C instead of  C F A# D# G C
Drop Bb (drop D + two steps down) to Bb F Bb Eb G C  instead of  A# F A# D# G C
C standard and drop Bb are also theoretically incorrect as they are at the moment, the guitar is tuned in intervals of perfect fourths, not augmented thirds (e.g. F to Bb, not F to A#), and a major third, not a diminished fourth (Eb to G, not D# to G).

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by koola
It would make it a lot less expensive to run UG if it ran on phpBB or mybb or some other open source forum software.
So why stick with vBulletin?
For now, we have a version of vB that has been tweaked extensively to do what's necessary for UG's specific needs.
I suspect the future might bring a change to a different forum platform.
Perhaps even one built by the programmers in UG Office.
But there is much to be done.
With a suite of specialized applications like UG, extensive testing would be necessary before the new applications could be opened to the public.  Once opened to the public, tons of bugs and problems would still need to be address.  Having 1000+ users accessing different areas of the site at the same time requires sophisticated methods of managing system resources.
The next version of software for the main page section of UG an keeping all current areas of UG running smoothly are the top priorities, atm.

If you earn a reputation for being knowledgeable and helpful on a particular subject then you'll find you're regularly asked for advice on that topic anyway. For example, I get a lot of PMs about Ibanez basses and Ashdown bass amps in particular. This isn't because I'm on some list of who to listen to, but because the content of what I say makes it clear I know what I'm talking about and I've helped plenty of people choose gear they're very happy with.
There doesn't need to be a specific chat channel for gear advice or a list of users you can contact on instant messengers because the forum is the best place to get gear advice. You get the opinions of multiple users, and there's pretty much always someone who owns or has at least used the item in question.
I would also argue that the most knowledgeable UGers are older, and usually have other things to do than answer MSN friend requests or respond to emails when someone else could deal with the question sooner. I think it'd be detrimental to the quality of advice if questions were rerouted from the public forum.

For afterwards, if, for example, you're doing a theory lesson, you'd have to give it a day or two to leave the front page before taking it off to edit, unless it can be altered in real time, which isn't likely without access to the coding.

I think it would make the comments sections on articles tidier and easier to use if the threads were collapsible (preferably by default, requiring an "open thread" button to view all the replies).
When scrolling through comments on articles, it seems a bit absurd to have to scroll through masses of replies to one comment before reaching the next comment. And then there are replies to replies and replies to those replies and so on.

Having the option to view replies would be much better, as opposed to them all just being there.
Cheers

Hey UG,
I want to start by saying how awesome your site it. The tabs you provide and continue to provide have expanded my musical knowledge exponentially. I have been using this platform for about two years (as a pro member). During this time I have been thoroughly pleased with the sites usability and aesthetic.
There is one thing however, that would make this site a million times better: an additional column displaying the key of a song. This might seem non essential, however the key to a song is a crucial component in building ones knowledge of music theory. Often, I will learn songs based on their key to understand the little tricks/progressions an artist uses. I am aware you can filter for keys when searching in the tabs section of the website. However it would be great if I could click on an artists name & be able to view the keys of each of the songs in their catalogue.

James

author: Unmercenary
text:
When using the auto transpose feature, there should be a small script that increments/decrements the tab numbers by one. Obviously there are some edge cases, like decrementing an open string, but these can be individually addressed as much as possible. Even if the result is at times unusual notation (like -1), the feature would still be useful when e.g. quickly reviewing a piece in a different key for band rehearsal. In addition a '-' can easily be read by a musician as a '+' on a different string.
To keep it simple just writing a script to increment/decrement the numbers seems a very feasible extension to current functionality. Some thought needs to be given to how to identify tab blocks as opposed to chord blocks, as not to adjust any chord notation and time signatures. Because these are often a part of text with a high density of '---' characters it is certainly doable. As a coder myself, I cannot imagine it would take long to implement correctly.
I am aware that certain pieces are very different to play in certain keys, and under no illusion that this will change that. However there are a good number of cases where it is feasible, and such a tool might even help musicians determine whether a certain key is feasible in the first place (e.g. for a particular riff).

author: DarkDragon786
text:
I think it would be useful to be able to navigate the pages of a tabs from the top of a page. That's probably not too clear, so I'll give an example.
If you go browse the tabs on the site by artist and go to the Green Day tabs, you'll see that there are 14 pages of tabs. To change between pages you have to scroll down to the bottom of the page to navigate the pages. If the same page navigation bar was also put near the top of the list of tabs, it would make browsing for a specific song more convenient.
When looking for a specific tab you sort of have to guess what page it will be on. If you find yourself on the wrong page, it would be more convenient to be able to change the page without scrolling to the bottom.
This is a very minor issue, but it's a convenience thing, and I can't imagine it being much of a change in terms of effort involved in modifying the site. Anyway, I hope the site administrators read this post and consider implementing my suggestion.

author: EndTheRapture51
text:
My screen is dark.
UG Black has been forced upon us and many of us find it hard to read. Everyone can have their personal preference but light dark text on dark background is very hard for many of us to read. In fact there have been studies showing it is harder to read this way.
However, most studies have shown that dark characters on a light background are superior to light characters on a dark background (when the refresh rate is fairly high). For example, Bauer and Cavonius (1980) found that participants were 26% more accurate in reading text when they read it with dark characters on a light background.
Reference: Bauer, D., & Cavonius, C., R. (1980). Improving the legibility of visual display units through contrast reversal. In E. Grandjean, E. Vigliani (Eds.), Ergonomic Aspects of Visual Display Terminals (pp. 137-142). London: Taylor & Francis
Please can we have the option for UG Classic back. After 9 years of using the forums that way, it's a shame we've been forced into using black all of a sudden. Taking away a choice for us makes no sense.

author: EndTheRapture51
text:
People with astigmatism (aproximately 50% of the population) find it harder to read white text on black than black text on white. Part of this has to do with light levels: with a bright display (white background) the iris closes a bit more, decreasing the effect of the “deformed” lens; with a dark display (black background) the iris opens to receive more light and the deformation of the lens creates a much fuzzier focus at the eye.
Jason Harrison – Post Doctoral Fellow, Imager Lab Manager – Sensory Perception and Interaction Research Group, University of British Columbia
As a user with astigmatism I'd hope you cater for our needs and make the website easy to use and accessible for all.

author: Nemesis44UK
text:
I've been away from this website for a while, having basically given up the guitar, but I'm back and some things about the redesign has caught my eye.
Firstly - There doesn't appear to be any way of publishing an article any more, which is a shame.
Secondly - All the gear reviews seem to have gone, which reduces the usefulness of the site somewhat. I used to like checking out real reviews of gear that people owned and it was often long term tests where faults would only occur later.
Thirdly and most importantly - In the articles, I see the same old names from decades ago. There truly can't be much to say that hasn't already been said about Dave Gilmour, Randy Rhoads, Dave Mustaine or Sebastian Bach (he doesn't even play guitar!)
I genuinely believe that UG needs to seek out some new blood and give them a boost into public awareness, people like: Mike Stringer from Spiritbox, Josh Middleton from Sylosis, Sophie Lloyd, Cici von Strangelove or Billy Strings.
It would be nice to cover UP AND COMING artists rather than those (admittedly) rock legends who really have run out of things to say.

author: Beserker
text:
I suggest that we create one additional sub-forum in this area. It would go like this: The 'Progressive' appellation would be removed from the '80s rock, shred & progressive' forum (it's not right to have the likes of Allan Holdsworth rubbing shoulders with GNR), and be merged with the similarly relocated 'jazz' of 'blues & jazz'. The logic there is that jazz, being quite a bit less popular here than blues, gets completely sidelined in that forum, and additionally, jazz is a massive, widespread genre that is often as far removed from it's progenitor blues as you could possibly get. It's two sets of people that don't really mix.
So I think that one more forum, perhaps titled something like 'jazz, prog & fusion' would sit nicely and redirect the like-minded fans of those genres away from the overpowering presence of blues elitists and shred snobs
...giving them a nice cosy place of thier own while producing minimal clutter. You know it makes sense.

author: LessThanLuke
text: Then that shows how worthless and flimsy the ToS is, doesn't it? Substantial changes to a contract, which I still contend this would be, would be grounds for legal action. If content is provided on the onus that it be distributed for free, and the provider begins selling that content without first gaining the permission of the content creator, they have broken the law, at least in the UK. Writing a song for a charity album, which the label then decides to charge money for afterward, is illegal, for example. This follows the same rule, and the ambiguous wording of a Terms of Service agreement does not change that fact.

Hello. I wrote the following as a comment to a giveaway article a sent it as a PM to Niass, but it seems to have gone unnoticed, so I'm trying here.
Hey, I have a suggestion. Because you allow to enter yourself into the giveaways using any email without actually being registered on UG, I believe many, if not most, of the entries are actually from "fake" emails. 2388287
2456867
These are 68,580 apart. I assume the whole lot could be well over 100,000. Are these all really from unique active users of UG? I know you also advertise these on your Facebook page and perhaps there are giveaway applicators that come from there and aren't registered on ultimate-guitar.com, but I of course don't know how many.
I think you should implement a system where only a registered ultimate-guitar.com user can apply for the giveaways, combined with a required minimum activity level on the forums. If you don't want to leave out your Facebook followers who aren't registered to UG, perhaps you can make a way where you can apply from FB itself; a person can still own a bunch of fake FB profiles, but hoarding dozens of these is more of a task than just creating a bunch of emails and that's it.
Just my 2 cents. I'm simply afraid opportunists might be trying to cheat their ways into winning on the back of users who actually use the website.

author: daxarms
text: I was asked to make this suggestion here, would it be possible to just set threads to automatically lock after x days without activity including viewing? If a person wants a thread unlocked they can request it with the reason they want to, and a mod can either grant the request or tell the user to start a new thread. For instance a thread on modding and repair or guitar technique might warrant unlocking if the user has new information but a thread of "what's your favorite song to play" might not because those threads show up all the time. The recommended threads could also be split into "for reading" so if they're locked but of a similar topic they're still available to read, and "for discussion" for open threads of similar topics.

author: SteveyLat
text:
Hi there;  I’ve noticed a large number of tabs (not just user-submitted tabs, but
official
tabs) that are sometimes painfully difficult to read due to improper beaming of notes.
If you do not know what beaming is, a beam is the thick horizontal line that connects eighth notes and quarter notes to each other. The way the notes are beamed can tell the reader of the music where the beat lands and where phrases begin and end. Improperly beamed music can be hard to read due to difficulty interpreting syncopation and where the beat lands. For more info on beaming, see the following links (assuming you have knowledge of basic music theory):
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(music)
https://www.ars-nova.com/Theory%20Q&A/Q57.html
https://www.mymusictheory.com/learn-music-theory/for-students/grade-1/grade-1-course/129-7-beaming-notes
Now, many UG tabs suffer from improper beaming. For example, the following image is the guitar part from the UG official tab of Iron Maiden’s “Fear of the Dark”:
While the notes themselves are rhythmically correct to the listener, there are several instances of bad beaming making the tab hard to read. In measures 10, 12, and 14 there is a tied sixteenth note that should just be an eighth note. The dotted eighth note in all measures is between beats 2 and 3, obscuring the timing of the melody; the note should be split up into a tied sixteenth note and eighth note such that the reader can clearly read where beat 3 lands during the duration of the note. I would also like to point out that the dots of dotted notes are very small and hard to recognize in UG tabs (they often look comparable to dust specs on my monitor). Lastly, the two eighth notes on the B-string (going from fret 8 to 6) are beamed together, so they look like the beat starts with the 8th fret note; really, the 6th fret lands on beat 4, therefore these two notes should not be beamed together.
The same riff, but properly notated, would look like this:
I think we can all agree that this is much smoother and easier to read.
Another notable example is the vocal part from the UG official tab of Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven”:
First of all, what are all those rests doing there before the vocals even come in? All those measures could just be whole note rests. When the vocals do come in, there are many similar issues to “Fear of the Dark”. A cleaned-up version would look like the following (aside from the lyrics that got compressed together):
Once again, much easier to read. All rhythms are simpler and clearer.
Here are several more examples of incorrect beaming, all from official tabs:
The main riff of “Back In Black” by AC/DC
Intro to “Wish You Were Here” by Pink Floyd
Interlude sections in “Sweet Home Alabama” by Lynyrd Skynyrd
I hope all of that makes sense. Any professionally written piece of real sheet music has the beaming notated properly. Given how accurate official UG tabs are otherwise, this is probably the largest issue that keeps these tabs from being the highest quality possible. If anyone has any questions or wants more examples, I’d be happy to answer.
Thanks,
Steve

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
SteveyLat
Thanks for your report.
All Official Tabs are created in Guitar Pro. This program beams noted automatically based on internal algorithms. We can change the beaming manually, but we don't do it because of it would slow down the process of creating tabs. Next step is our online player because it could change the beaming from the GP.
We released a beta-version of a new online player today. You can read more about this here:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1922256
Next step is fixing bugs and improving it based on a feedback. Please check the update and share your thoughts about beaming in the thread
What about the rest notes in the “Stairway to Heaven” tab - it's our fault, will be fixed soon.

author: DarthTyrannus83
text:
The new tab submission page/approval queue is really nice, includes pretty much everything i asked for.
But theres still one thing that really bugs me and can potentially confuse people. When submitting a guitar pro tab, the tuning selection, though having been expanded, is still insufficient. Especially when submitting 7/8-string songs.
What i suggest is, make it like in guitar pro itself, where you choose the number of strings, and then manually adjust the note of every string. That way you can correctly represent any custom tuning without any confusion or limitation. Then have the system automatically recognize the tuning if it is in the database, and if not, just leave it as is.
For example, ive recently submitted an 8-string drop E tab, and since there was no such option, i left it as standard tuning (note that drop E on 8 string translates to standard E tuning on 6 string guitar), but that potentially might lead to people incorrectly thinking its a 6 string song, only to open the tab and find its actually 8.
And also please add an info box for guitar pro tabs on the tab page, kinda like theres always some info written by the author in text tabs.

Details on the tab? Would have helped to have seen it myself.
Normally when I choose "lack of formatting" from the selection, it's because of one or more of a few things that go against UG's tab guidelines (click "Tabs guide" from the submission page's left column):
- Tab staves that show only a few of the strings rather than all of them.
- Bar lines that aren't properly lined up
- Tab numbers (usually in chords) that aren't lined up
- Tab numbers being too close together or difficult to read in some other way
- Tab width exceeding that of the guidelines (you actually can't approve a tab like that, the system doesn't allow it)
So if it had anything like that, it's to be expected. If not, try it again, reply here, and if I see it and decide it doesn't have any of those issues (and no accuracy/copy-paste credit issues or anything like that), I'd be more than happy to give it an approve vote.

The problem I find is the tab owner getting "cocky" and rejecting every correction that comes his way, even when the corrections improve the tab
But in that case, I guess you can leave the tab to have 1 stars then?
What I want is there to be less versions of tabs of a song, but be more accurate.
I don't want one version of the song to have the chords, another version to have the solo, another version to have the tricky licks in the verse, or whatever. I want one that has all, and everybody collaborates on that one.
How about this as an idea:
Incorporate Tab Pro/Guitar Pro as an in-website app for tab collaboration.
Then every song in the UG archives can have a "special" collaborative Tab Pro tab in it. In this one, EVERY user can access the Tab Pro tab, and just add stuff in in an online mode. After they are done (they could save their progress and everything), they can send the changes to the tab owner. The tab owner can supervise these changes, accept them, and merge them together. You then end up with a single Tab Pro tab, where everybody can correct and improve over time.
You won't have a separate (ASCII) tab for the guitar, for the bass, for the solo, etc. You'll have a single Tab Pro one with everything in it, in the most accurate way possible.
This way, all the possible info about the tab is centralized, and if it has good votes you know it's good.
Even better, you don't need those "genius" tabbers to make them. Right now, I see lots of 5 star Guitar/Tab Pro tabs that are very very accurate and good, but are made only by a single user. I assume there are very few of this type of user, and they spend a lot of time with every tab of theirs. However, with this system, that type of user will spend less time on the tabs (because others will collaborate with him), therefore can put out more great tabs. Also, people less skilled in making tabs will have their work perfected by the community, making the quality of their tabs as good as the one from the "geniuses".
In the end, the net result is that you end up with more and more GREAT tabs. You also make people collaborate and work together which is always nice.
Yes, perhaps just include it to UG+ users, since they'd need access to Tab Pro, at least to a Tab Pro Editor (dunno if that exists yet, if not it might have to be implemented or have a deal with the company that does it, dunno how it works in UG haha).
Also, maybe in this case, you could include Tab Pro free for any UG user? Or any user in general? At least just the "Playback" mode (not Editor mode).
I've seen lots of sites who have similar playback apps that can be accessed by any user and guest. If not this system will kind of fail, since nobody basically will be able to access these tabs.
And of course, every user and guest should be able to easily export said tab to ASCII, or Guitar Pro, etc. But all from a SINGLE TAB.
When this system is put into place, you can then keep improving it over and over. Include a ranking system (maybe just use the UG collaboration points, or maybe another one) for people that collaborate. E.g the more corrections you make and stuff you include in the tab (that is accepted), the more points you get. If you added 3 bars to the tab, you get 3 points; if you added 30 bars to the tab, you get 30 points; stuff like that.
Maybe you can use this new point system to discuss what I was stating before: What if the tab owner sucks and ruins a good collaboration because he gets cocky or asshole-ish or just plain ****s up the tab? Well, maybe you can make it so that users with high amount of points (maybe 1000 for example), are able to take control of specific tabs, accept their corrections, merges, etc, like if they were "Tab moderators". By "moderating" these tabs successfully, they'd get more points in return too, etc.
There could also be "mini-forums" for discussions about the tab. There could be a display of the version history of the tab, with every single previous version of it. These versions can be downloaded by anyone, because it doesn't hurt (if for example someone didn't really like a specific correction, well, he can download a previous version). The tab owner or "Tab moderators" should also be able to go back to a previous version if the current one gets too ****ed up somehow.
I mean, yes, this seems like a LOT of work; but well, baby steps no?

author: DarthTyrannus83
text:
One major problem i see with UG concerns the guitar pro tabs. Specifically, it would be nice to be able to upload both GP5 and GP6 versions of tabs, or have UG automatically convert gp6 to 5 and offer
both
versions in the tab page, with a respective warning that a converted version might have some mistakes due to unsupported software features.
Its great to see the tab update system has finally moved on from being vote-based, cause theres usually a need for a lot of minor fixes after uploading a tab, and having to go through the voting anew used to be a pain, so great job with removing that.
Please include a link to the main song page when viewing a particular tab, not only just other versions of the same type of tab, eg: when viewing a guitar pro tab page, it would only link to other
guitar pro
versions, not all versions in general, which is really annoying when trying to quickly compare them, the only other way around being having to search for the song again or go to the band page and scroll to find the song.
Also, get more tunings in the list when uploading a pro tab and an option for 7/8 string guitars. Pro tabs also need to have tab description/info on the tab page for quick reference, i know theres an info window supported inside the tab, but its inconvenient and not everyone bothers to check it.
Im kinda wary about collaborative editing, since im one of those guys whos really elaborate with his tabs, i only tab in gp with mostly all instruments, i watch lots of live gigs/covers and spend hours a day in Transcribe slowing down/EQ-ing the song to get everything as accurate as possible, then again i still find minor mistakes after i upload the tab, but i correct and update it as soon as possible, so at the end im pretty sure my tabs are 95-99% correct, depending on the difficulty/audibility of the song. With that said it would be a bummer seing my tabs being tampered with, and im pretty sure im not talking only for me here.
I do agree a lot of the songs need major tab revision, i just dont think collaborative editing is the way to go. Maybe implement a time-based due date system, in which a correction request is sent to the tab author and if he fails to respond within, say, a month, only then the community gains the right to make edits?
So, here are my suggestions in a nutshell:
1) Autoconversion of gp6 to gp5 and availability of both versions when uploading a gp6 version for accessibility reasons.
2) Add a link to the main song page with
ALL
tab versions when viewing a particular tab.
3) More tunings (including 7/8 string) in the list for Pro tab uploads and the addition of info section for Pro tabs.
4) Date-based response system for collaboration correction requests.
Thanks

author: Teh D Bot
text:
Quote by fanapathy
Also how the **** do I level up? I'm at level 3 which I reached at 10 tabs and I have like 40+. I should be at like level 12 imo. Do I evolve when I reach a certain level?
There are 4 'levels' which are for the tab approval queue
Level 1 = 1 approved tab; points towards accepting/rejecting tabs = 1
Level 2 = 5 approved tabs; points towards accepting/rejecting tabs = 2
Level 3 = 10 approved tabs; points towards accepting/rejecting tabs = 3
Level 4 = 10 approved tabs of high quality; points towards accepting/rejecting tabs = 5
5 points are required to approve or reject tabs
Level 4 is the old "Trusted Tabber"
and then there are Tab Moderators
And I agree that additional tunings are in fact overdue, including lower tunings and tunings for guitars with an increased amount of strings. Maybe a step towards this would be to compile a list of tunings which need to be added.
