author: coman91
text:
Quote by wbce
Hey ya'll, Im new to this kinda thing. But I posted two tabs that are still pending, and was wonderin' these tabs then may not get published for the public to see?
Not really the place to be posting about this, but I'll clue you in anyways because I've been there before.
Patience is a virtue, man. It can take a few days, especially if your tab isn't by a more popular artist. Basically, the mods approve what they like or what is popular first and foremost. It also depends on the season (I've noticed more tabbing occurs in the summer. More tabs awaiting approval = longer waiting time). The rate at which tabs are approved is typically 100-400 (higher in the summertime) a day, and they only work on weekdays.
Example, my tabs for the new releases from the upcoming Black Keys album were approved the day after posting because theyre sought after (Fever already has like 3000 views after being approved a few weeks ago). Tabs I've posted by less popular artists (Junior Kimbrough, Mississippi Fred Mcdowell) have sometimes taken up to 2-3 weeks to get approved.
Rule of thumb: If there are a lot of tabs behind you on the list (tabs posted before yours) you're going to have to wait a while.

author: GaryBillington
text:
Multiple versions of a tab are fine, so long as there aren't multiple versions of an identical tab.
So long as the different versions cover alternative positions of the same thing, they can be useful for viewing and working out how you're most comfortable playing a part.
Even if there are slight mistakes, like SGstriker said they are useful guidelines.  Personally I never follow a tab 100% anyway - I look at a few of the available tabs to get an idea what I need to play, then use that as a starting point to actually work a song out by ear.  I never actually learn from a tab note for note.

If you have some comments or suggestions for our tabs  please feel free to tell us about it.
Yes and no.
I find a lot of tabs are wrong(even if it's just a note or two, it matters), and it almost seems like tabs with multiple versions are just copies of one tab(regardless of if it's wrong) with maybe a change or two instead of something new or different.
really evident when a song has 3+ tabs all with the same mistakes.
that being said I find most tabs to be really helpful, especially when I'm having a problem learning a riff on my own. And even more so with songs that have multiple tab versions as they probably all do something different and it's nice to figure out which way you find most comfortable so easily
I think though if I were to improve the tabs in any way, I'd make it so there couldn't be multiple versions of the exact same tab. if there's going to be a version 2 or 3, It should be done significantly different or fix the mistakes in a different one(at which point the wrong tab should be removed), or offer a different way to play the song all together.
EDIT: I also think you should be able to flag a tab as 'incorrect' or something and be able to submit a correction to it which would get reviewed and then either implemented to the original tab or rejected.
Would cut down on a lot of the alternate tabs that are just corrections or better versions of another
EDIT2: and maybe even have a log of corrections that have been made on a tab that people can see if they want to so the original posters work is never undermined. It will still be there in its original glory, but the main tab people will see will be the one with corrections

author: NemX162
text:
I would like to see more rigorously enforced standards on tab format at flow.  It should be a rule to put at least one '-' between numbers, especially for two digit numbers.  There should never be a need to clarify, "These are 11's not 1's..."  Layout of sections in tabs should be standardized.  If a song has discrete parts, it should be labeled as sections: chorus, verse, fill ... It would even be cool to see links in tabs that let you quickly jump to that part of the song, perhaps a floating link on the title bar.  This way, if you are playing along and need to get back to the chorus quickly, you can click "chorus" to make it jump there.
Overall, I think if there were more standards to the form of the tabs, it would enable future additions of features.  If the page designer knows what kind of content to expect in the tab box, they can easily write robust and helpful functionality around it.  It would also make it less of a pain to read.  No more tabs that are a large, unlabeled page of repeating parts with numbers squeezed together on one line.

text:

Yes and no.
I find a lot of tabs are wrong(even if it's just a note or two, it matters), and it almost seems like tabs with multiple versions are just copies of one tab(regardless of if it's wrong) with maybe a change or two instead of something new or different.
really evident when a song has 3+ tabs all with the same mistakes.
that being said I find most tabs to be really helpful, especially when I'm having a problem learning a riff on my own. And even more so with songs that have multiple tab versions as they probably all do something different and it's nice to figure out which way you find most comfortable so easily
I think though if I were to improve the tabs in any way, I'd make it so there couldn't be multiple versions of the exact same tab. if there's going to be a version 2 or 3, It should be done significantly different or fix the mistakes in a different one(at which point the wrong tab should be removed), or offer a different way to play the song all together.
EDIT: I also think you should be able to flag a tab as 'incorrect' or something and be able to submit a correction to it which would get reviewed and then either implemented to the original tab or rejected.
Would cut down on a lot of the alternate tabs that are just corrections or better versions of another
EDIT2: and maybe even have a log of corrections that have been made on a tab that people can see if they want to so the original posters work is never undermined. It will still be there in its original glory, but the main tab people will see will be the one with corrections
This sums up my feelings pretty well.

If you mean only the highest-rated version would show up in results, and you would have to click on that tab just to see the other versions, then definitely not. More than once I've found tabs where the highest rated version is vastly inferior to more modestly rated versions. author: Colohue
text:
I think people should stop ignoring the copyright issue here. Tabs are extremely subjective in manners of fingerings, chord inversions and positional play. They can be worked out by ear without encroaching any sort of copyright and the layout tends to display that.
Sheet music is not. Sheet music is easy to scan, copy or re-make and, since there's no way of telling, if your music is correct, it still could easily look as though it is copyrighted material.
In my opinion this is far too risky and not worth the hassle.

author: Koenigtiamat
text:
Hi from Official Tabs team! We want to deliver Official tabs faster for you, that's why we want to collect some feedback about a feature that could be implemented.
This is how sequence of the Official tab creation looks:
1) Our tabbers create the tab
2) We create Tonebridge preset for this song
3) The team of guitarists and sound engineers create the Backing track.
4) Tab became approved and visible for all.
On average, it takes about
2 days
to create the Backing track for already completed tab, and only after that the tab appears on the website. However, there are many OT users who are not using Backing track or Tonebridge features, they are interested in the tab itself.
So, we can possibly approve and make available Official Tabs
2 days faster
but the Backing track feature and Tonebridge preset will on these tabs will be locked for a couple days until our team finishes working on them.
It will help the users who only interested in the Official tab to get access to tab two days faster than now.
Thus, official tabs for new singles and albums will be delivered to community as quickly as possible, often even on the day of release.
Share your thought in the comments and please complete the poll!

author: kidrick
text:
The format UG forces makes the autoscroll function very frusterating. Take this song for example
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/awolnation/sail-chords-1097835
The Intro is 14 seconds long and takes 6 line = 2.3 seconds per line. The first verse is 28 seconds and is 14 lines = seconds per line.2 seconds per line. The Chorus is 14 seconds and 14 lines = 1second per line. Verse2 = 1.85 seconds per line.
This makes the autoscroll pretty useless. It's pretty illogical to have a time based scroll function and not have the song match up to be time based. The autoscroll via microphone is not a viable solution.
Two solutions:
1 - allow people to write one chord per bar even if the chord repeats and don't force the extra spaces for Intro, verse etc. Instead, ask people to consider continuity of the pacing of the lyrics and chords.
2 - A more robust solution is a scroll speed marker that's embedded in the tab but not visible. So i put markers at each song section and tell the app the scroll speed or how long I want it to take to get to the next section. If the verse takes 52 seconds to sing, then I could put 52 beside the verse 1 label and it will take 52 seconds to scroll to the next label at the chorus. Or use a beat or bar count that can update with a tempo setting. An elegant way to once and for all set the scroll speed once per song that works even when changing font sizes or screen sizes.

author: samuwel
text:
In my opinion, the sub forums of gear ads actually make the ads more difficult to use.
It would make more sense in my view to have the forums sorted by main countries (USA/Canada; UK; Europe; Australia; Rest of world, perhaps) . I'm pretty certain this has been suggested before, but can't see why it hasn't been implemented?
The great majority of frequent traders on the forums (myself included) do not browse just within one of the current sub-forums and tend to look for good deals within their own country.
I'm aware this system sort of exists in the UK/US/AUS ad threads but it's messy and doesn't really work.
I'm keen to hear other peoples views on this also...

text:
I agree. I live in the UK and its takes forever to look through the ad's, even with the new system.
Around 7 out of 10 times I have to find out whether the ad is from the UK or US by identifying either $ or £ in the posts.
The best way for both sellers and buyers I would say, is have the forums as before, only with the mandatory [UK]/[US] etc. and then, have the option to filter out the UK's and the US's (using the search function).
I don't know what you could do about those who will ship internationally, however, very little sellers even do that, unless its a small item.
My other suggestion, which I myself and probably most others who are after specific items would like most. Would be to split the categories even further, and strictly stick to them.
For example:
Gear Ads
Sub-forums:
Guitar | Head | Cab | Combo | Rack | Pedals | Accessories | Studio
[perhaps more sub categories for things such as 6/7/Trem/Hardtail Guitars, and SS/Tube/Modelling Heads]
(and then have the location in-title as mandatory)
This leaves a much smaller amount of pages to go through, enough to look through most likely all the pages, but still allows the international sellers to advertise worldwide.
Sorry to bore you, but you'll attract ALOT more sellers/buyers through this!!

author: AeroRocker
text:
If we want our smiley arsenal to expand, we really need to remove some of the useless ones that clutter the list. It would make much more sense to add a small inconvenience to users who want these (by searching for them/linking them) instead of keeping them around. In my opinion, these are the latter:
The gun/fighting emoticons
I only ever see these clogging up signatures. they are only used as decorations to show "how badass" a user is, and never really contributes to a topic.
Bounce
Sorry...but what is this supposed to be used for? It also drifts from the style.
Fart
Way too long to be useful, and rarely shows up.
Redbite
I've seen it used, but it seems more annoying than useful
Others as well...maybe I'm being too harsh, but they seem like clutter to me.

author: adompostma
text:
Hello,
First of all, thanks for all the work that you've done on the official tabs and the iPad app. I truly appreciate it! Worth the price of admission and a lot better than having to write up my own tabs with corrections, even if I have your excellent site to thank for providing the baseline.
Now on to the requests - apologies if this ends up being a duplication and I admittedly have no concept of the amount of coding that would be required to implement a change like this, but it would be fantastic if the
official
tabs could be modified in five ways (at least that I can see at the current moment) and clearly the utility of each of these varies:
1. Allow for a modified fingering - i.e. if it's presented as requiring playing the fifth fret on the A string, have an option to change it to show up as open fret on the D string. This can be particularly helpful for some bass lines I've seen. While I know what notes I can play, when I'm using the tab for playing live, I can't think that fast to change up what I'm playing as I read the tab.
2. Provide for alternate tunings - I could be the only one in the world who would want this, but the ability to change the tuning that the midi is playing in would be super helpful since we typically play with guitars tuned down a whole step and that would allow me to change the tabs back and forth for different tunings. I know this can likely be achieved with the transpose button, but what can I say...
3. Put the tuning notes more prominent/obvious/in your face on the tabs - perhaps have the string notations on the beginning of every line - not a huge deal, but it happens where I don't notice the drop D tuning or that it's tuned half a step down. Sure, I could be more diligent in reading over the tab before I start, but it certainly makes it a more useable tool for playing live, especially if your singer wants to throw out a relatively unpracticed song.
4. Allow for the option to condense repeated sections of a tab - i.e. if the software/algorithm/whatever recognizes that the same riff/motif is played four times, it shows the option to collapse and show it as a repeat or to show each bar - would help with following along while practicing ("playing" the track is workable, but I would find it preferable to be able to compress the amount of information)
5. To echo what another user said, it would be helpful if there was an option to show lyrics on tabs (switchable might be best as some songs don't need it while you can easily get lost in others without it)
Again, thanks so much and even if you weren't to change any of these things, I'm still sticking around!

author: Koenigtiamat
text:
adompostma
Hi! Firstly, thank you for your well-structured feedback. I Will try to reply to each point
1)  Yes, I think it could be very helpful, especially because official tabs can't be downloaded. But it will be very hard to implement this feature on the app,  so it's not in the our to-do list.
2)  Again. it could be helpful, but it's even more hard to develop. For instance, some notes could be lost (same as in Guitar Pro), that could confuse users. I will think about this feature, but not before the next quarter.
3) Honestly, you are the first one who ask us for this feature. We need to get more feedback on this
4) We decided not to use that kind of symbols the official tabs first appeared. The reason is simple: we have a lot of newcomers who have just started playing guitar and don't know the musical notation, so such symbols can confuse them.
5) We are going to implement this feature right after we release new player on Web-version of our site =)

author: Sabhaois
text:
Here is my suggestion to the software engineers for this site.
This may be a hard one or maybe not I am not a programmer. Many tabs do not take into account what fingers can actually do. How difficult would it be to create a snap to string function.
The way I see this working is that for a certain passage of music when the notes are right but the fingering is impossible.
A user could take the notes one by one and drag them to a different string and the back end would automatically change the fret number to the corresponding number for that note on the new string.
in the following example I took a bass line that is nearly impossible to finger at 144 beats a minute made a few minor changes and the line makes sense.
|-------2---------2---------2----------2-----|--------2-------2---------1-------------|
|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------4----|
|--0---------0--------0-----------0----------|---0--------0----------------------------|
|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------4--------2---------|
Mama Im Coming Home Official by Ozzy Osbourne Bass tab measures 88 and 89
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
|-------7---------7---------7----------7------|--------7-------7---------6---------4---|
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
|---5--------5--------5-----------5-----------|---5--------5-----------4--------2------|
|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
Same line modified to make the fingering functional
And a fifth string added for five string players  who constantly need to change the fingering on a bass line.
There would have to be a way for a person to save and possibly share there fingerings with other users of the site.

author: NSpen1
text:
jeff.ferren
Probably because you shouldn't be changing it on every song.  Some keys should have sharps, some should have flats.
One thing which could be useful to do though is to make the "Use Flats" option a true toggle switch.  I have had a few requests from people to be able to do it the other way, like "Use Sharps".  Because if you're transposing a tab which is written with flats to begin with and you transpose into a key which should use sharps, then you're stuck with the incorrect flats and can't change them
You'd have to make the left position "Use Sharps" and the right position "Use Flats" and make sure it only worked when the tab was transposed from its original key, not so that every tab got changed to sharps to begin with.  And if you transpose one way and then come back to the original key, the tab needs to go back to its original state, not have the toggle switch still applied to it in any way.

author: outisen
text:
Hey Guys,
First, thanks for all the work you've done in creating and maintaining this community. I think it's very great.
There is one thing that bugs me, and that's the forum organization. It really needs to be broken down further. Take the "Electric Guitar" section for example. The influx of new threads in there is absolutely tremendous and a new thread could be potentially buried on the second page in a matter of minutes on some days (correct me if I'm wrong). That section consists of people asking for gear suggestions, playing tips, general gear questions, miscellaneous stuff, song specific threads, etc. etc. Any one of those topics I just mentioned could be a section in and of itself. I think it'd be better if clicking on a lot of current forum sections should result in being taken to a "folder" with more subsections such as the ones just mentioned.
This would remove the clutter and make rules for new threads slightly less restrictive and also make thread locking and moderation much easier. There are a lot of threads wasting memory that should have been locked or deleted but ended up being on page 21. The fewer threads there are in memory, the better the search function works!
My 2 cents
edit**
I forgot to mention, further subdivision would eliminate the need for "the Ultimate [blank] Thread"s such as the Guitar Setup Q&A thread. That thread is useful to somebody asking the question, but most people won't read every page of that thread. There should just be a separate section for those kinds of questions.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by outisen
Hey Guys,
First, thanks for all the work you've done in creating and maintaining this community. I think it's very great.
Nice opening!  You didn't start out whining and complaining.  You made a
compliment
, and expressed
gratitude
for what has already been done.
I can't speak for others, but I would imagine the UG staff would be willing at that point to
read and consider
anything you have to say,
more seriously
.
Quote by outisen
There is one thing that bugs me, and that's the forum organization. It really needs to be broken down further. Take the "Electric Guitar" section for example. The influx of new threads in there is absolutely tremendous and a new thread could be potentially buried on the second page in a matter of minutes on some days (correct me if I'm wrong). That section consists of people asking for gear suggestions, playing tips, general gear questions, miscellaneous stuff, song specific threads, etc. etc. Any one of those topics I just mentioned could be a section in and of itself. I think it'd be better if clicking on a lot of current forum sections should result in being taken to a "folder" with more subsections such as the ones just mentioned.
There are several problems with subdividing forums:
1  -  It's difficult to choose the proper divisions that will provide enough activity to make the subforum worth visiting AND be clear enough that users will know where to put things.
2  -  By subdividing, you often cause some people to NEVER visit.  If it's centered around something that they (in general) have little interest in, they will ignore that subforum.  If a thread is titled well, and has a carefully made OP, they
might
reply to it, if they see it in the main forum.
3  -  There is already a big enough problem with users putting their threads in The Pit
intentionally
misplacing them.  They do this because "I know this belongs in [
insert forum name here
] but nobody goes there."
Quote by outisen
This would remove the clutter and make rules for new threads slightly less restrictive and also make thread locking and moderation much easier. There are a lot of threads wasting memory that should have been locked or deleted but ended up being on page 21. The fewer threads there are in memory, the better the search function works!
My 2 cents
More like five cents worth.  You put a lot of thought into this.  That hasn't gone unnoticed.
Don't be afraid to report bad threads.  And if they're in the wrong forum, just politely mention that you will report the thread and ask a Mod to move it to the correct forum, if the thread was written well, but simply misplaced by a newbie.
Quote by outisen
edit**
I forgot to mention, further subdivision would eliminate the need for "the Ultimate [blank] Thread"s such as the Guitar Setup Q&A thread. That thread is useful to somebody asking the question, but most people won't read every page of that thread. There should just be a separate section for those kinds of questions.
No one is expected to read EVERY page of a stickied or 'Ultimate' thread.
You read the FIRST page:
The basic 'tutorial' section is there.  It might help you understand what you need to know, without the need for making a thread or post.  It will also help you understand the terminology being used.  That way, you will be speaking the same language as the people who can help you.
You read the LAST page or two:
Questions just like the one you have, may have been asked recently.  Why ask the same question a few days later?
NO ONE will complain
if you ask the same question as one that is buried in the middle of one of these threads.  Many people
do
read the entire thread.  They don't like to start their own threads or post their own questions.  Good for them.  They get the info they need without making a post.
Stickied / Ultimate / ONLY threads are extremely valuable resources.
They need to be
used,
not be made unnecessary.
Quote by jof1029
the problem is less that we dont have enough moderators, and that we have
too many stupid users
. not too many users, too many
stupid
members. people who cant read the forum descriptions, dont use the search, dont read the stickies, and generally just have no clue. if people just read the stickies and posted in the correct forum, we wouldnt have this problem. but then, i wouldnt be here if they did.
Imagine if there was an IQ requirement of 70 or above? (less than 70 = feeble-minded)
We'd lose 5% of our members, but 90% of the problems would go away.
Quote by jof1029
so, if something is in the wrong forum,
report it asking for a mod to move it. i get at least one report a day like that
. there are so many threads (many of which i dont have any interest in) so i dont have a chance to read them all (nor does any other mod). people complain that there need to be more mods, but they dont think that they could make our jobs easier by reporting threads in the wrong place and not bumping spam threads.
I'm glad you enjoy those kind of reports.
When I make them, I consider them love letters, just for you.
Seriously, guys.  Start looking to
help the mods
by working within the structure that is already here.  It doesn't take all that much effort on our part.  And it can make a huge difference in the way the forums operate.
Reporting doesn't have to mean you're asking for punishment.
It might just mean something has been done wrong and needs to be fixed.

author: blue_strat
text: Prog is rarely seen as a genre by itself - it's usually a description of a particular kind of rock or metal.  Pink Floyd are seen as progressive rock, for instance, but as they were active in the '60s and '70s, they're sometimes lumped in with Classic Rock. text:

Probably not.  At least not as a general rule.  There's a rule about spamming, so if they fit in that category they could result in a warning.  But it isn't as clearly defined as posting something like "rub icy hot on it" or a pear pic.  If the same thread has been done recently, telling someone they should have checked, and posted in the existing thread rather than starting a new one is a valid reply.  Doing that in a humorous manner (or an
attempt
at humor) isn't all that heinous.
Quote by Dinkydaisy
It's irritating, and if someone cares that much about a thread being repeated, they should just report the new one for being a duplicated of a recently made thread.
Yes, that is a better way to handle it, in most cases.  Some of us do just that.  Others have a fear of reporting.
I guess the question could be turned around a bit.  If we make search bar jokes a warning/ban, shouldn't we also make repeating threads a warning/ban?

text:
Hi!
I think there should be some changes made to how the “Pending Approval” queue works, especially with authors who have multiple tabs, or constantly deliver high quality tabs.
(As of now, there’s 906 in the Pending Approval queue)
Firstly, I just want to give a thank you to everyone who helps out in the approval process. I don’t go through the queue very often (really only when I submit a tab, I will kinda go through some because there are so many in the queue).
Secondly (the main point)
, for authors who submit high quality tabs — like myself and many others — they should be separated, or have the ability to be filtered out of the main queue. People who are submitting their first tab (as their tabs may be of low quality or are missing some rules that belong in tabs such as labelling sections, adding lyrics, whatever), or constantly have low rated tabs should go in the all section.

Top Authors will over a period of time be promoted through levels, IE Levels 1 to 3 are generally for those submitting few tabs or beginners as the level increases with the amount of submissions,so does the voting rights from 1 to 3 votes in TPA.
Those authors that reach level 4 and 5,the submissions they make automatically go straight onto site,and the have the power of 5 voting points within TPA,this will approve or reject a tab outright.
Generally the authors with tabs of high quality will be promoted to level 4,those with high quality tabs and high quality activity in TPA will go to level 5.
Level 4 and 5 authors are chosen by UG if they are proven trustworthy and knowledgeable .This system then separates  beginner authors and those who produce quality tabs.
This link may help explain further
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/help/approvalQueueFAQ
Hope this helps :-)

Everything that exists in the current official tab is done with higher quality. The bass part in the official tab is off, but not by nearly as much as yours is. There are a lot of double stops missing throughout the length of your submission, and it's better represented in the existing version.

You need not write an essay to back-up your claims; a succint list of a couple of the key differences would do
e.g.:
- Added a piano track
- Separated Drums/Tambourine
- Fixed Rhythm for bass line
- Removed additional double stops.
Your options at this stage seem to be:
1) Add your tab, hope it gets a better user rating than the existing one
- - If the old tab is bad this should happen over time, people will try it; think "this is a bit off" and look at your alternative version
2) Correct the mistakes in the existing one as you see them
- - If there are only a couple of changes you'd make, submit them as an edit, with a list like the above.
- - If the changes are pretty substantial a tab-mod will likely ask you to submit as a new tab, so you're back to option 1
There is already a system for this; asking mods in an unrelated forum to bypass it makes no sense. At best, you're desperate to get your tab approved, at worst it's an ego trip.

I know people have mentioned that sort of thing before, and part of the problem with that is that it can very well become a "my thread was closed for X reason but somebody else's thread wasn't" type of thing.  This is very tricky because there are numerous other factors.
For example, if Johnny_the_spammy13er made a thread on a serious topic, it could be taken as him just wanting to start trouble by giving his uneducated opinion, whereas if lolmnt or Madcap started the same topic, it would be more likely to turn into a serious discussion.
In such situations, a generic response might simply not be adequate, and then we come to the aforementioned problem of the amount of effort needed for a more in-depth explanation.

author: Roc8995
text:
Exactly. If the reason for closing a thread is so common and obvious that it can be described by one of a few options on a dropdown list, anyone who has bothered to read the rules will understand. People who haven't bothered to read the rules aren't really our priority.
Plus, as you say, it opens up a lot of room for issues of interpretation; we get users complaining all the time when they get banned for "spamming" because what they were really doing was "overposting." Their argument is that since we punished them for  the wrong thing we have to let them go, which is dumb but then we have to waste our time trying to explain that to someone who's just mad they're being punished. So we probably don't want to go down the road of a rigid list of thread closure reasons.
We do try to explain why a thread was closed, especially if it's not strictly against the rules. There is a list of moderators for each subforum at the bottom of the page, and we're always willing to explain why a thread was closed if you send a PM. Sometimes what we think may be obvious might not be obvious to everyone.

author: jessegreathouse
text:
I have a somewhat elaborate streaming setup that allows my streaming audience to watch me learn how to play songs on UG.
I'll try to make this short and to the point, but to cut off certain people who will not answer the question but rather try to tell me to do it another way, the reason I'm doing it this way is because I have two different use cases that I blend together for streaming. One is a production studio Macbook Pro, and the other is a different Macbook pro that runs the streaming software. These systems have separate concerns for a reason and I don't want to get into why I don't just do the whole thing on a single computer, but suffice it to say  because it takes a tremendous amount of resources to do both things on the same computer, and when a macbook pro uses that much resources the fans kick into high gear and take a big dump on the whole audio party. So that's why there's two.
So the problem I have is that I want to pipe the UG sound into Pro Tools, so I can hear it in my monitor, but not in the live feed. I just want to hear the metronome without my audience hearing it, because it sounds bad. Just like a performer plays to a click on stage, I want to be able to play to a click from the guitar tab I'm learning. I don't want the metronome to be coming out of the default sound device of my macbook, I want it to be loaded into a track in my DAW and mixed in like any other track.
I already have the software patching tools I need to send the output of my browser to Pro Tools as an input device. It works for Youtube, and other media embedded into HTML 5 elements. Please see these software tools I'm referring to if you have any questions:
[VB-Audio Cable](
https://vb-audio.com/Cable/)
creates virtual input and output devices.
[Audio Pick](
https://rain-fighters.github.io/AudioPick/)
routes the sound from a browser tab to a virtual audio input.
Unfortunately it seems like it doesn't work on UG like it does on media elements from other sites. No matter what I've tried, I can't seem to route the metronome from UG, into anything but the default output device, which is no bueno for me.
I'm going to stop there and just ask if anyone knows a solution for routing the sound from UG into my headphone monitors through my daw.
Thanks.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by Telecaster7
so, is there actually a way ot get around the problem of spammers? (and i'm more asking SYK, coz he's too smart for his own good
)
Look at the objective.  You want to make life difficult for a user based on WHAT he posts (or is planning to post).  This is no easy task to automate, unless you are willing to make life more difficult for other users.
Since the most heinous porn/gore/spam is often caused by multis, i have some thoughts on automating IP checks for new accounts.  During the email confirmation process, a user's account that matched a banned user's IP wouldn't be immediately activated.  Mod intervention would be necessary.  This wouldn't stop all, but it could go a long way, and wouldn't adversely affect the majority of users.
Automation is like dumping chemicals on your lawn to control weeds.
You need to be selective in what you're killing.
Getting the most effective weed control without damaging the lawn itself is not easy.
Mods are like weeding by hand.  It takes more work, but you can target only the weeds.

Having a staff that's too large is almost worse than having one that's too small.  Unless the staff is huge, there will always be some gaps in coverage when a forum doesn't have a Mod online for a short period of time.  And a huge staff brings different problems.  UG Team is just that: a team.  Not individuals, but a group who adopt a common policy.  Communication between members and consistency of enforcement are important targets for an effective team.  Too many members tends to dilute that.  Also, too many members leaves less for each member to do.  This could lead to complacency.
Imho right-sizing the staff, is a decision best left to the staff themselves.

author: andrewtc4
text:
Is there currently, or has there ever been, talk among the UG team about adding support for MuseScore file uploads in addition to the currently-allowed formats?  Being a general notation program, the guitar output is inferior in some ways, but the team behind MuseScore is actively working on this aspect of the program, as made clear by
https://github.com/musescore/MuseScore/projects/44.
Adding this support would likely be a lot of work, but the payoff would be great, especially for those songs that use more than just guitars, vocals, and drums, of which there are plenty.  MuseScore is also totally free—this lack of cost could incentivize users to help out with making corrections to songs.

author: ascend
text:
When uploading mp3s to ones profile, the following text and checkbox is presented:
Use the form below to upload your mp3 files. You can't upload copyrighted music, or files of other people without their permission.
Make sure you are not violating anyone's copyrights.
[] I confirm that the music I am uploading is
not copyrighted music
.
What is copyrighted music?
Music from signed artists
(Everything you hear on the radio!)
Music that was copied off official CDs or bought digitally
(You are not allowed to distribute MP3s even if it's from your own digital collection)
If you still try to upload a copyrighted mp3 file, you will be banned permanently.
It seems fairly evident that this is intended to prevent members from uploading mp3s of
others'
copyrighted works -- that is to say, members may upload their own original works, or works that are in the public domain; but they may not upload works that are currently copyrighted to someone else.
The difficulty I'm having with it is that ones own original works are, generally (in the US and most western countries), also automatically copyright to oneself, unless one explicitly releases them into the public domain (or produced them under contract for someone else, etc).  But for a member to upload their own original, copyrighted, compositions, they must tick a box confirming that it is
not copyrighted music
.
This creates an ambiguity: when you tick the "I confirm that the music I am uploading is not copyrighted music." box, you could be asserting:
that the music you are uploading is neither
Music from signed artists
, nor
Music that was copied off official CDs or bought digitally
, but may still be copyright to yourself (i.e. interpreting the text below "What is copyrighted music?" as a strict all-inclusive definition of "copyrighted music" for the purpose of the checkbox above); or
that the music you are uploading is your own original work, hereby released into the public domain (i.e. interpreting the text below "What is copyrighted music?" as merely a couple of examples of music likely to be copyrighted, but neither a definitive nor exhaustive list)
I've had a look through the privacy policy and terms of use and it seems to me that it is not UG's intent that members' original compositions must be released into the public domain in order to be posted on the site.
This leads me to believe that it is the first interpretation that is intended rather than the second one.  However, I'm still not comfortable with that ambiguity there.  Could the text on the upload page possibly be updated to make the intention (whatever it is) more explicit?

author: ascend
text:
Quote by Colohue
You do not own something unless you are capable of proving it.
Right.  And if you want to upload something that no-one save yourself has ever heard before (e.g. for critique), then until you upload it there's no need to prove ownership, because no-one else has so much as heard it.
Look at this from the other angle.  A hypothetical scenario:
You write an original composition and record a draft version.  This is currently your own copyrighted work.  You do all the reasonable things you would usually do in order to prove the song is your own.  You upload it to your profile to request mixing advice.
Some charming soul takes your draft song from your profile, adds some polish and releases it as their own original composition.  You sue their arse (quite rightly).
The first thing their defence lawyer is going to say in court is: "When you uploaded that to UG, you
confirmed that it was not copyrighted music
.  If it's not copyrighted, the copyright cannot be infringed."  All your effort to maintain proof of your ownership is wasted, because the case is now going to hinge on how the court interprets that "not copyrighted music" bit and whether or not the work is now in the public domain.
I'll grant that this isn't something most people will ever have to worry about (even having definitive proof of ownership doesn't mean you can actually afford to take someone to court to protect it -- sad state of the world).
My point here is to highlight that this issue exists, and that it could be avoided by simply rephrasing a couple of paragraphs of text on the upload page.

author: divid3d
text:
it's usually pretty damn obvious to anyone who has read and understands the rules why a thread has been reported, and usually people want to inform everyone as quickly as possible that the thread has been reported so they don't waste time giving a reason. i suppose it would be nice if people gave the threadstarter a reason but i don't think it's something that we will enforce.
we regularly state a reason when we close a thread, and if we don't, people are always welcome to PM a mod of that particular forum for more information. all you need to do is send a link to the thread (don't just say "why was my thread closed?" - we don't want to have to look up all of your threads and figure out which one you're talking about) and ask for more info on why it was closed. if that mod wasn't the one who closed it, they can direct you to the one who did close it.
also - threads aren't always closed for 'breaking the rules'. it may just be an overdone topic, a topic which is sensitive/usually leads to arguments, something a little too silly/pointless to continue, something that is more suited to a blog post rather than a forum thread (ranting/venting/etc)... there are lots of reasons, and we know the forums well enough to know what sort of topics will be successful and which will just result in spam/flaming/etc. if you break the rules you will
usually
get a warning for it, not just a thread closure.

UG is now mostly just a site to get guitar tabs, but it was once a dedicated social media site centered around guitarists. You couldn't have custom backgrounds, but you could upload your own MP3 files for either music or a demonstration of your skillz, and allow others to rate them, send messages, add friends, have groups, upload images of yourself and your guitar gear, and plus there were forums where people could discuss things too such as this one. If you liked someone's music, you could favorite it, and there was even the 5 or so top songs of the week that ended up on there. I was and still am friends with many of the bigger names on that site from back in those days, in fact, although we haven't spoken in a while. We'd often just chat about music and nonsense, and it was great getting to know the musicians behind the cool music that got uploaded. Some of those people had a falling out with the site about 10 years ago, and it seems like they actually killed the site in doing so. Then a few years later, all MP3 files were deleted and the ability to upload your own music was taken away. Furthermore, they completely wrecked the format of the profiles on UG somewhat recently. The most you can do there now is put a comment on someone's page and that's it. You can at least upload 1 minute of a 300 MB video to your profile now, though, but that's seriously just not the same. The forums are still going, but the people in the forums are often toxic and I try to avoid them. Hell, UG even used to have its own instant chat for friends to talk to one another on, but they nixed that years ago. The closest you might get to a site dedicated to music like that now is something like Reverbnation or Soundcloud, but it's just not the same. Those aren't social media sites like UG used to be.
So for suggestions, I'd recommend bringing back the features that this site had in 2009 and 2010.
If nothing else, bring back the old basic format for the profiles or a modern version of it, that way you could have groups, write blogs, embed YouTube videos, have band pages, add friends, and the like.
Furthermore, having the ability to upload your own MP3 files again would be sweet. It's 2020 now and auto-detecting licensed music should be easy enough. Those who upload that ought to be banned for a week or a month from uploading any other MP3 files, then permanently if they keep doing it. A 3 strikes rule should suffice.
Bring back the top page for top images and MP3 files that way some cool musicians get their stuff heard, even if they are just jamming out when drunk or some 15 year olds first picking up a guitar and recording something.
If you won't let people upload their MP3 files again because memory issues or fear of being sued, then there are alternatives. Perhaps have something similar to MP3s, but instead of this site hosting them, allow people to just link them from Reverbnation, Soundcloud, or even YouTube, which will then allow for the top page to exist again.
I've stopped using this site years ago because there's just nothing on it anymore. No music, hardly anyone in the profiles talk to one another and I'm not even certain if you can PM people these days with it, the only features it has are looking up tabs, reading articles, and messing around in forums. What does this site have to offer that something like Reddit or 911 tabs doesn't? These days, nothing. It used to offer a lot, but not anymore.

To show our appreciation for all of your hard work, we are giving away free bonus access to Tab Pro (part of our UG Plus online service) using the following scheme:
If you have submitted up to 5 tabs in the named formats, you will be awarded 1 month of free access to Tab Pro
If you have submitted between 6 and 10 tabs in the named formats, you will be awarded 3 months of free access to Tab Pro
If you have submitted more than 10 tabs in the named formats, you will be awarded 6 months of free access to Tab Pro
But that's not all. From now on, we will also be giving away bonus access to Tab Pro to all regular contributors. The way it works is as follows: if you contribute at least one Guitar Pro/Power Tab tab in three month, your Tab Pro access will be extended for one more month. The free Tab Pro access will be given to you every three month.
Those of you who already have a Tab Pro subscription don't need to worry about missing out either; the bonus access will be added to your current subscription.
Best regards,
Ultimate Guitar Team

author: paddyirishman
text:
The Tab Pro service should be seen as a separate thing from the Tab Pro library.  The library is the problem.
The library is pushed forward like it's a database of professional-grade tabs, when it's just a list of the highest rated Guitar Pro tabs from the main website, a fact which was not made clear to either the original tabbers or the paying customers until long after the service went live and the
community
made it known.  This is dishonest; people paying for access to the library (separate from the Tab Pro service itself) are being conned into thinking they're paying for quality tablature which, as a secondary consideration, happens to be playable from within Tab Pro.  If they were only paying for the Tab Pro service everyone would live happily ever after because no one would feel like they'd just been sodomised by the invisible man.
If the Tab Pro software allowed you to load in tabs from the free part of the website
at will
- as opposed to being restricted to the library of tabs defined by UG - everything would be fine.  If the library is done away with, and therefore left out of the advertising, there would be no problem.  There'd be no grievances about crediting the original tabbers, no grievances about the tabbers feeling completely detached from their own work, no grievances about making money from your users in a direct and underhanded way.  It would essentially just become a web-based Guitar Pro, which is what we all had in mind when we had been asking for in-browser tab playback capabilities for all these years.
To those who justify the problems with this service by saying UG needs cash to pay for the development of the Tab Pro software: I'm pretty sure that argument is more circular than physics permits.  It also doesn't really take into account the things the tab contributors are worried about.  Namely, credit (which I understand is forthcoming) and the inclusion of our tabs - which we share for free - in the Tab Pro library
[see above for why that's bad]
.

author: Ian Paul Gint
text:
Fellow users!
Let me express my personal opinion. I was not the one who created paid services and apps and I'm not the one who uses them, so I do understand what you mean, every word is true.
Here's a thought - since day one, UG has never ever done anything to restrict access to its users' tabs, always been free, always will - that's what UG stands for: largest tab sharing community in the universe, free and open-minded. All these years we've been maintaining the site and forum in order to give our users (each and every one of them) the best they can possibly get. For most of the people it's just like that - enter the site, find the tab, download it and play - and it's cool with us. We wouldn't want you to know about all the legal, technical and web battles we've had (and still have) to fight through in order to get what you see - that'd probably be just bitching
. It was always about users and not about us.
Then, more and more people beginning to say "I'd like to have tabs on my mobile device" or "I'd like to have tabs playable". Again, we gotta respond to that and give our users what they really want and ask for.
As you may know, developing a mobile app or service is not an easy thing - takes up helluva work and invetsment. Is it fair to charge for the app or service (not for the tabs themselves) that allows you to view/play the songs? - decide for yourself.
Meanwhile, thanks to everyone for caring. It's good that you've brought this matter upfront and that we can discuss it freely and without prejudices.
With all due respect,
Ian Paul Gint of UG Team

Hi there UG-staff
My profile is called Maitinin and, according to your high scores, I have the 16th most active profile here and have been dedicated to your site for several years now, so please take this serious.

Hope you'll take this case into consideration!
Sincerely with the greatest respect and dedication to your website!
Jon Sebastian Frederiksen aka Maitinin

author: brettsanace
text:
Problem
When submitting a tab if you include N.C. (No Chord) in the chord line above the lyrics any other chords in the chord line will not highlight.
Authors could correct this if they knew the format of the HTML tags to manually put around the non-displaying chords when creating the tab but generally they don't. So the only way to fix the tab is to wait until after the tab is approved and then edit the tab, as the edit function includes "Set [ch]", and  "Remove [ch]" buttons and a "Manually highlight chords" toggle switch, which can be used to make the chords display.
Having to correct errors after the tab is approved is not the ideal situation, as it would be preferable if the author could submit a correct tab to start with. To resolve this the following suggestions are proposed.
Preferred Solution
N.C. should be included in the table of chords in the database so that it automatically highlights, and when the cursor is hovered over it in a tab there should be a pop-up which says "No Chord". (Thanks to
k9f100
for this suggestion)
Now if this doesn't fit with the format of the database tables e.g. having text rather than a chord chart, or if the chord recognition and chord charts is not UG IP but is licensed third party software then the following is recommended.
Alternate Solution
When authors are creating/submitting chord tabs that they are provided with the "Set [ch]", and  "Remove [ch]" buttons and the "Manually highlight chords" toggle switch. The authors already have these editing functions after their tab is approved and I can't see why they can't have them whilst they are creating their tabs.

To add a tiny footnote to your point, Brett: when creating a tab, Automagic detects an error/incorrect format in every line where N.C. is included (even if the line also contains several chords in the correct places) and gives the message "Missing Chords: Chords should be placed above every line of text where they should be played or use N.C. if there are no music played on this line."
This can be confusing especially for a new contributor because there's nothing for him/her to correct, and they have already put N.C. in those lines.

author: Frankie!
text:
Some suggested changes to the site:
1.  Provide the capability to insert chord diagrams into the lyrics.  I'm not that good of a guitarist so it's easiest to have the chords on top of the lyrics.  Maybe cut and paste the chords?
2.  Display page selection option at top of the tabs list.  Oftentimes I know right off the bat that that I need the next page of tabs.  Having to scroll down to the bottom of the tabs to go to the next page is a pain.
3.  Configure the chords page of a song to allow fan folding.  I use a music stand during practice.  To enable me to spread out multiple sheets of a song so I don't have to turn pages while playing, I staple the pages to allow fan folding.  Say you have a song that requires three pages.  I place page number one right side up, page two upside down, and page three right side up.  I staple page one and two together on the right side.  I staple page two and three together on the left side.  This arrangement lets me open up the pages in such a way that all pages are arranged normally.  Here's the problem:  When opening the music up, the stapled edges create a yanged up edge so I fold the edges in such a way to straighten things out.  I suggest that the music pages have two lines on the edge to be stapled; one to use as a guide for stapeling, the other as a guide for folding.  This would enable a much neater edge.
4. Provide templates for chords, fretboards, and the ability to edit these templates to create a chord diagram.

text:
I was wondering why the tab version list visible in the left sidebar is collapsed to just four versions when there are more than five versions. This is an issue mostly because this way,
if I'm viewing Version 5 (or 6) or higher, I'm not able to immediately see that
. I have to click somewhere just to check what page I'm on. And... I don't really see any other content below the version list that would be pushed down by it if it was longer. So maybe we could get rid of the collapsible with no harm?
Other than that, since there
is no
content below this list in the sidebar, why not add some? One thing that comes to mind, and that would make the tab page look immensely more interactive, would be to include a more complete list of the contributions related to the song. Why not show the list of tabs on a page with chords? Why not give links to acoustic and live versions, and on an acoustic chords page, a list of links to the 'regular' chords versions?
I understand that too much stuff might be overwhelming and confusing, especially in the beginning. Maybe you can hide those stuff under a collapsible if you must have one (or a few) in that place
Trying to make a mockup for you I realized that there are lots of different types of content, so maybe including all of them like Ukulele, Bass, Official, Power, Guitar Pro, Pro in one place is overkill... but worth considering? (What is even the difference between pro and guitar pro (and power?)?). But something along these lines, a clean list of contributions of the same type for the current song, and then a list of collapsible lists of other types of contributions for the song:
MORE VERSIONS
Ver 1 ★★☆☆☆ 5
Ver 2 ★★★★☆ 5
Ver 3 ★★★☆☆ 5
Ver 4 ★★★★★ 5
Ver 5 ★★★☆☆ 5
Ver 6 ★★★★☆ 5
Ver 7 ★★☆☆☆ 5
ACOUSTIC CHORDS ▼
LIVE CHORDS ▼
TABS ▼
Not all songs have all kinds of contributions, so maybe there is a reasonable way to include all of them as crosslinks. On a sidenote, the title of the tab page looks like this:
Call Me When Youre Sober chords by
Evanescence
The song title and contribution type are only distinguished by capitalization. This is technically not an issue, but it is kind of clumsy. I was not blessed with an instant brilliant idea of how to fix this, but I believe there exists one. I remember it was already discussed here on the forum that the titles can't have apostrophes in them. But in my small mind it is still kind of beyond my mental ability to understand why an additional data field cannot be introduced that would contain the full correct title for display purposes: such field could be initially empty in all existing tabs, and could be slowly continued to be filled in, little by little. The old field would be still used, without the need to modify existing code, in all those creepy places like URLs and I God knows where else
(Unless adding a field to a DB table is such a big deal – it basically is dropping the table and creating it anew in some DBs? I guess it's more than a few minutes' job with the size of your data).
PS. Sorry for pestering you here on the forum lately. I hope you don't mind too much?

author: brettsanace
text:
I'm not sure if this already exists but I assume it doesn't.
LIV & LV authors can submit tabs directly by-passing the TPA queue, however if they attempt to submit a tab when there is already one for the same song and tab type (ie chord, tab, pro ... ) in the TPA queue it should not be allowed to go through to the site until the other one has cleared the queue. There are two reasons why this should be applied:
1) We all know the importance of getting Version 1 of a tab, and it isn't really fair if someone has had a tab sitting in the queue for two days and then a LIV or V author submits one and snatches the Version 1 position.
2) It is possible (and I'm not suggesting any LIV or V authors would do or have done this, but it is better to be safe than sorry) that a tab in the queue could be copied and posted (maybe with some slight modifications) by a LIV or V author before the other one clears the queue.
I know this isn't a big deal but being an ex-auditor and IT Business Analyst I just like to see controls built into the system, I just can't help it (I think it might be a form of OCD).

IF there are currently no versions of a type of tab (chord, tab, pro etc) on the site

Song Name

Tab Type

author: jlawrence0723
text:
Ways to tackle duplicate tab problem:
**allow moderators to designate a "recommended" tab among the duplicates with a star. This could automatically be placed on the most popular or highest rated tab, and could be changed to a different tab based on which one the moderators prefer
** build a list of acceptable reasons to have a duplicate, so moderators can refer to these when considering.
** re-order tabs: instead of having all the versions listed in the order they were first published, list them in order of popularity ( Version 1: most popular, version 2, second most popular, etc)
** make any tab less than 4 stars unavailable for viewing on the site.
** Invent classification system for tabs that indicates its condition-- (i.e. incomplete, functional, and complete ) You could automate the system to recognize tabs that are of any of these status, prevent any "complete" tabs from being suggested for editing, and indicate to editors which tabs would be rife for editing (basic).
** allow editors to edit a tab's status from published to draft. We could do this for 2 or 3 star tabs or ones that are being destroyed in the comments or otherwise.
** require all authors to state where they heard the song published and encourage them to post a link.
** allow editors to mark tabs as a duplicate, and for users to see this designation
**build a set of standards for high quality tabs, and allow moderators to designate these high-quality tabs. Then, make a UG trademarked symbol for high quality and make these chord charts only available to pro members. Lastly, make these version 1 on the entire website. Once a tab is designated High Quality, all other versions not designated High Quality will be considered duplicates and will all be unpublished and made into drafts.

author: mendace
text:
I have to disagree with this suggestion. All the requesters are doing is choosing a preferred author, not the only author they will accept a tab from (if that's the case they should ask you personally via PM to make a tab for them, not submit a request).
The preferred author suggestions are usually pretty bad as the system just picks some random authors and not necessarily the most active tabbers for that particular tab type and style. This means that unless the tab requester manually types in the name of their preferred author (which they usually won't do, they'll just pick someone at random), you'll get tab requests with preferred authors that won't fulfill the requests. New users won't know who the active tabbers are so they don't know who to ask to create a tab for them. The more experienced requesters know that they can just mention someone in the forum thread and they'll make a tab for them.
Displaying the name of the preferred author might work for chord requests as there are a lot of tabbers who are interested in submitting this type of tab so someone will fulfill the request at some point. I don't think it would work at all for other tab types as there are so few tabbers who create GP/bass/guitar tabs from requests. If someone does happen to come across a request they would like to work on but it says someone else's name on there, I think they would be discouraged from tabbing out that song.
If I saw a request in the queue and I wanted to work on it but it said "Preferred author: Username" I would quickly close the forum thread and never look at it again because why bother? But the preferred author might not even be active on the site anymore. Experienced tabbers will see someone else's name on the request and they'll either a) close the request, b) ignore what it says and submit a tab anyways, or c) ask the preferred author if they want to make a tab or if it's okay for them to go ahead and submit one. It usually takes people a little while to respond so by the time the preferred author gives you a thumbs up or down (if they answer at all), you will have moved on to a different request and then no one will submit a tab for that request because it has been pushed so far back in the list of requests that people won't find it.
If someone truly wants a specific author to create a tab for them then they can either write that person's name in the request description or, like I said, request songs via PM. Requests are open to everyone, just because the requester would like a certain author to help them out that doesn't mean that other users can't submit a tab for that request. The main purpose of the tab request system is to let people request songs that are missing and tabbers can get inspiration and some extra points for tabbing sought-after songs.

author: cam765
text:
Here are some issues/points for improvement I have noticed in the new player so far (Chrome Windows 10):
Switching tracks while the song is playing in the new player cause a short delay/hiccup were as the old player does not
The number pad still does not work for selecting tracks (this worked on the old old player that was removed a year ago or so)
On the fly tabbing forward and backward (arrow keys while song is playing) seems to work better in the new player than the old player, however, there is an inconsistency with the long repeated rests. When using the up or down arrow to move in the song into one of those repeated rests, the track will jump to the very beginning of the song. This is frustrating as you lose your place in the song. Using the left and right arrows does not have this issue but the jump size is smaller and not as useful.
Notes that are tied in (not played but continue to ring) is misleading. They are actually shown where as in the old player they are hidden. This makes it look like a note should be played when it shouldn't be. This is an actual deal breaker as it causes confusion when learning a song.
New player improvements:
The font and layout I think make it easier to read (I think) and more notes fit on the screen at one time.
The long rests help to condense tracks with few notes and they don't loop over themselves which would make it hard to know when they end.
Suggested improvements:
A dark mode (like the app) would be nice
Viewing multiple tracks at once
If the track switching delay is removed, tie-in notes are hidden and the tabbing through extended rests is fixed then I would call the new player an improvement over the old one. I still prefer the old old player as it did not have these issues and the number pad could be used to change tracks.
Is there a plan to remove the old player?

text:
Quote by fender-lespaul
If it's possible could this be implemented as when i look through it you see the same tabs over and over.
1  -  Tabs requests can be sorted by song name or artist name.  Scan the list in the appropriate fashion.  If a song has already been requested, you'll find it.
2  -  It won't make any difference if there is a search function, if people don't actually use it before making requests.
3  -  There might be a few who will use the search that wouldn't bother to scan the sorted list.  It could do a little bit of good.
4  -  Biggest problem with search is misspelled name.  If the person making the request misspells the name in the search, they WON'T find the existing request.  There have been TONS of misspelled duplicate requests.
5  -  A new and improved search engine for the rest of the site is currently being worked on.  It will have the ability to discern some of the misspelled words and make spelling suggestions.  When finished, it might be applicable to tab requests.
6  -  Stay tuned.

author: pmalavi
text:
I recently experienced a situation where:
1. I submitted a tab to the approval queue.
2. Five days later, another tabber submitted their tab of the same song to the queue .
3. The other tabber's tab was voted on, accepted, and published.
4. My tab was rejected for being too similar to the published tab even though I was first into the queue.
Both of our tabs are indeed very similar however:
- When the other tabber started tabbing, they could not know the same tab existed in the queue (my tab was unpublished).
- My tab can't be accused of being too similar to a tab that did not exist at the time I started tabbing!
I understand there can be a delay going through the Approval Queue backlog and that similar tabs can build up in the queue. However, I believe
Approvers should approve or reject tabs in the order they were received in the queue
. This would avoid situations like the one I experienced.
Are there guidelines for how to deal with similar tabs in the queue? Could we request that Approvers follow a first-in, first-published process? Any thoughts appreciated.
For what it's worth, my tab was Space Between by Sia (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/submit/approval?id=1810233).
I don't particularly care that it's published since there's a good tab out there now. I'd just like to avoid this situation in the future for myself and other users.
Thanks,
Pat

EVERY POST that gets an EF would have to be reviewed by the Mods.

And there is a DANGER here.
Normal forum dynamics are:
-  people post their opinions.
-  others post to agree or disagree ... or to offer their own opinion.
-  people reading those opinions have the responsibility of deciding for themselves whether the opinion suits them.
Enter the EF system:
Without moderation, this is just a way for users to sign-on to agreement.
You get to know
who
decided to take the time to endorse this, by seeing the username.
With moderation, you FORCE the UG staff to decide whether this opinion exemplary.
This is, in essence, giving an
official
endorsement.
I'm not willing to believe zappp wants the UG Mod Staff to have to
speak for UG
in regards to any and every opinion that might be expressed.
It's tough enough to draw the line between acceptable forum
behaviour
and not.  But that's all a forum mod should be asked to do, in regards to the posts.  Making judgments on the various opinions is just not realistic.

author: kyrreca
text:
I'm not sure if this is the right place to post this, if not I hope a mod can move it to the appropriate forum.
Just to make it clear: I love the tab section on UG. It's a great resource for any guitarist. It's really awesome how many people contribute and make good tabs.
However, there are users who for some reason (either they're just plain stupid, or they want to increase their ranking on UG), do their best to clutter up the site. Everyone knows that there are about 300 tabs for songs like Sweet Child O' Mine, and there are no more tabs needed. But it's understandable that people who are new to tabbing want to help out, and they might not realize that their version of the Smoke on the Water riff is not needed. These tabs get rejected anyway.
On the other hand, there are people who take existing tabs, change the header and post it as their own. This is completely useless, and it contributes nothing to the site. Of course, they take the top rated tabs, and if the people voting to reject/approve don't check the existing versions, tabs like this are likely to be approved.
There is also at least one user who continuously posts chord sheets for well known songs, like House of the Rising Sun or Knocking on Heavens Door, and posts five identical versios, contributed to different artists, like U2, The Beatles and Eric Clapton.  This is also completely worthless, and again it does nothing but clutter up the tab section, which is cluttered enough as it is.
I suggest that UG makes  "report"-button in the tab approval section, for tabs like this. These users wish not to contribute to the community, they just want to boost their user rating or their egos. I'm not saying it should be instantly bannable, but I think three strikes = temp ban would be reasonable.
I don't know if anyone agrees with this, but these tab spammers annoy the hell out of me. As I said, I really like the tab database, and it's sad that some people are trying to make it worse instead of better.
That's all. If you agree with me, please say so, and if you disagree please say so too.

author: phrilser
text:
It's been great to see Ultimate Guitar making steps to grow and change to keep pace with what users are looking for. That said, I think working within the existing branding is a major hindrance to that effort.
Looking at the current top ten tabs on the site right now, every single one is, rather, a chord sheet. In fact, there are only three actual guitar tabs in the daily top 100, with the first clocking in at #47, and one of the three being "Stairway to Heaven". And if I were to compare the artists I frequently see in the daily top tabs list on the homepage to those that are regularly featured in the news section, the overlap would be so low, week-to-week, it might as well be a statistical anomaly. I've never, to my memory, seen a story about Lady Gaga or Ed Sheeran or the Goo Goo Dolls featured on the site, but those are all artists in the top ten viewed tabs today. Sheeran has two in the all-time top ten, including the #1 spot, which nearly doubles "Stairway"'s hit count. Posting stories about the artists people using the site actually listen to and are interested in would drive pageviews, which would drive adviews, which would be good for the site's bottom line, wouldn't it?
Despite its user base being largely more concerned with chord sheets (over 1.1 million compared to ~350 thousand guitar tabs; and nearly 50% more ukulele chord sheets than bass tabs), the focus of the overall branding of the site - the "vibes", if you will - is still very much geared toward hard rock/heavy metal enthusiasts, with a lot of the non-tab material looking at guitarists in those genres and their gear. And absolutely no shade being thrown here: I love those genres, and would hate to see them driven off the site. That's the scene the site was made for, and it should always remain an important part of what Ultimate Guitar does. But, I don't get the impression that it's what the vast majority of people coming here are looking for. I believe Ultimate Guitar needs to embrace its position as the go-to amateur guitar music resource on the internet, and I believe part of that is greatly expanding content that appeals to all kinds of guitarists. It'd be good for the site and good for its users.
Thank you for attending my TED Talk.

author: UG Support
text:
phrilser
hi!
Thank you so much for your message — this is incredibly thoughtful, well-articulated feedback, and we truly appreciate you taking the time to share it with us.
You're absolutely right that Ultimate Guitar has been evolving, and it’s heartening to hear that you’ve noticed and appreciate those efforts. At the same time, we completely understand your points about how the branding, content focus, and representation of user interests could be more in sync with the actual behavior and preferences of our broader community.
The data you’ve shared — about the dominance of chord sheets, the disparity in tab types, and the artists users are engaging with most — is extremely valuable. We agree that there’s a huge opportunity to better reflect the diversity of our audience, both in terms of musical taste and in the content we feature outside of tabs. Your suggestion to bring more attention to popular, high-interest artists like Ed Sheeran, Lady Gaga, or Goo Goo Dolls in our news/editorial content is especially relevant. It's a strong point, and you're absolutely right that aligning editorial content more closely with what our users are actively engaging with could benefit both the user experience and the platform's sustainability.
Your perspective on the site's branding and overall "vibe" is also something we take seriously. UG has deep roots in rock and metal culture, and we’ll always hold space for that legacy — but you're spot-on that the user base has grown and diversified significantly. If we want to continue being the go-to music resource for guitarists of all levels and styles, we need to reflect the full range of players and preferences in our community.
Please rest assured that we’re going to share this feedback with our Team
, including those responsible for content strategy, branding, and platform development. Input like yours is not only heard — it's essential to helping us grow in the right direction.
Thanks again for your insight and for being such a thoughtful member of the UG community. We're grateful for users like you who care enough to help us improve.
Warm regards,
Aydar
Ultimate Guitar Support Team

author: UG Support
text:
phrilser
is there anything else we can add to the feedback from you?

author: phrilser
text:
UG Support
Hm, not sure, really. I think you guys are on the right track with the changes being made to the experience. More and better social integration might be good — more expansive and customisable profiles, with those and the forums being more a part of regular site usage. Looking at some publicly available metrics, it seems that most users only look at a few pages and don't spend very long on the site. It might help if there were more incentives to sticking around and making an account. Not things for sale like songbooks and lessons, but the ability to just hang out and share the experience of playing and learning  and enjoying music.
But, I'm no expert. I assume y'all have the numbers to look at, and the skills to interpret them into website functionality. I'm just making observations.

author: UG Support
text:
phrilser
yYou're absolutely right that more meaningful social integration and ways for users to stick around and connect could make a big difference. We’ve been actively exploring ways to bring the community aspect more to the forefront — whether that’s through more customizable profiles, easier ways to share progress, or better visibility and engagement in the forums.
And yes, while we do have data and tools to analyze user behavior, hearing real observations like yours gives us important context numbers alone can’t provide. We’ll definitely pass your feedback along to the team — it’s clear you care about the community and the experience, and that means a lot to us.
Thanks again for taking the time to share this — and please feel free to keep the ideas coming!

I've noticed often when coming back to tabs I saved as favorites but where the label, artist, DCMA, or whoever, has requested be taken down of course are removed. I am then left to look at other websites to find tabs again.  Sometimes I'll use archive.org to see if they have an old snapshot of the UG page where the tab in question was. Usually I will make a copy of the other site page and come back to UG and save it as a Personal tab. I like everything under one roof and UG really is the best I've seen.
My suggestion would be if UG receives a take down request from a label or artist, if a UG user already had it saved as a favorite put programming into place that would convert those favorites to personal tabs for the UG user. Should a UG user later delete that personal tab they can't get it back since the tab has been taken down per request. And of course no UG users can view them either per the take down request.
I think this gets UG around any legal lability as you are taking down the down from any new UG users to get to it. I don't believe take down requests, even from the DCMA, can apply retroactively to those who have already viewed previously.  That is most likely how archive.org is able to retain a snap of the web page if they crawled it previously.
I hope this makes sense the way I am explaining. And if this can't be done in this manner, can you possibly implement a faster way to change favorite to personal? The Edit > Make Personal edits > Save, is a great feature but I'm sure many like me have 100's or maybe even 1000's of favorites. It takes a lot of time moving through them all.
thanks,
LT
