author: MattStephen
text:
So,  for instance, a B7 chord has a lot of ways to be played.  when you hover over the chord you get all the variations, right?
so, please, can we add something to tag chords by variation (when necessary/wanted) like, 'B7v2', (i don't think 'v's are in use? )  the v2 would be variation 2, so if you print the song it prints chord variation number two, and also on hover you get the variation 2.  you should still be able to see all the other available variations/finger positions to sound the chord just like before, but it should automatically hover the intended chord shape when told to do so by the user when creating the doc.
you should be able to print, B7v1 B7v2 B7v3 B7v4 etc all back to back, and show the differences of shapes within the song construction.
PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE
reasoning
1)if you want a song to sound correct, you need the correct fingering/shape for the chord!  it is utter chaos deciphering notes, and scrolling the chord hover variations menu, every time you want to learn the proper sounding technique.  tired of seeing 'play the power chords' and then a bunch of 244322 and such. just F#v1 (if thats actually the right version im going by memory here, pretty sure the hover starts with the power chord anyway. if not, say it was variation 4 we would write F#v4)
2)im working on some new era musicals theories and teachings, and I really just want to specify which chord variations print when I print a new progression idea.
love,
Matt

author: MattStephen
text:
i just realized how awesome this would be for the chord search, search B7v and you get all the variations of a B7 to show, instead of only one variation, a limitation of the current chord search.  if you want to know the variations of a B7, you have to open a song with  a B7 and hover to find them.
love,
Matt

author: thewildkindness
text:
UG Support
Personally, I have several tabs that use tunings not covered by the drop-down, and I don't even have that many contributions! Open-chord tunings often have several variants that are not covered by the options on the drop-down menu. Normally I'm content to just pick 'not selected' for the tuning, since I make it obvious within the tab what the tuning is.
However, this leaves it open for other users to select the tuning for you during the approval process, and once a tuning has been selected it appears that you cannot return to 'not selected.' For me at least, this has resulted in a case where another contributor selected an incorrect tuning from the drop-down which I now cannot fix.
It's not a huge deal, but this could be avoided either by providing an 'other' field in the drop-down, or simply by allowing 'not selected' as an option even after another tuning has been selected.

author: uhh_me?
text:
Is creating a completely new forum necessary? Not arguing against it, just trying to understand the logic behind it. It sounds like, based on both the discussion that we mods had ages ago and the other thread, the idea at the heart of revamping B&A is to bring people together to stimulate conversation. Wouldn't a new forum wind up pulling people out of the conversation?
I mean, look at nu-metal. That had a sub-forum all to itself. It was used a lot for a while and then died down even when B&A was going strong. As a result, it was merged into metal. I'm not saying that electronic music is a fad like nu-metal just that discussion faded away after a period.
As it has been in the past, most electronic music conversation has centered around the Techno & Dance thread in Other and that big thread in The Pit. No one has ever said that those were the only threads that could be used. It was just decided by you guys that those would be the places to discuss.
The Other forum could have become the de facto Electronic fourm. Why didn't it? Why couldn't it be now or under the possible upcoming revised version of B&A? Couldn't a simple retitling of Other serve the same purpose? Something like "Electronic, Hip-Hop, and Other" with a appropriate description to go with it.

author: uhh_me?
text: There was also a lot of positive energy behind starting a drum forum which is, at this point, getting pretty low numbers. Again, not standing against this idea, just trying to see how we can ensure that people get what they want in a sustainable way. I'd hate for people to get invested in making sure a new sub-forum gets off the ground just for it to fall apart because of disuse six months down the line.

author: opmjeff
text:
Use case:
Many bands rehearse from a shared master playlist and select a subset of songs during each practice session.
Current behavior:
When Ultimate Guitar is used in a web browser, users can infer which songs were played by reviewing browser history. In the mobile app, there is no equivalent mechanism to view or recall previously opened songs.
Problem:
The app lacks a session-level or historical view of recently accessed songs, making it difficult for band members to remember which material was covered in a specific rehearsal.
Proposed feature:
Add a song access history (optionally session-grouped by date/time) within the Ultimate Guitar app.
Value:
Enables musicians to review rehearsal content between practices
Helps individuals prioritize difficult songs for focused, at-home practice
Improves rehearsal continuity without requiring external tracking tools
Encourages deeper, repeat app engagement
Scope (minimal viable):
Automatically log recently opened songs with timestamps
Viewable list filtered by date or rehearsal session
No social or sharing features required for initial release

author: GaryBillington
text:
Quote by Lemoninfluence
UG has been getting revenue from the get go (it wouldn't have lasted otherwise) and now that they're choosing to provide extra services on top of the existing ones, contributors should be paid?
if that's the logic, should we not also be charged to access the tab archive?
Yes, UG has always been getting revenue right from the start, but (as far as I recall) that revenue was always through advertisement.
I think the point being made here is that UG is now charging users for access via certain platforms to the content they have provided, therefore the users which have contributed should be granted access free of charge  (obviously I'm only referring to significant contributors, not just anyone who submits a single tab).
I kind of agree with that philosophy, but I could imagine putting the processes in place to administer it correctly would be a lot of work, therefore it would cost a lot of money and force the site to increase it's charges to non-contributing users.
It's also worth noting that a little while ago, something along these lines did happen relating to the approval of submitted tabs.  I don't know how successful it was, but users who reviewed & approved tabs on the waiting list were offered temporary free access to UG+.

author: theogonia777
text:
I have been an active member of this forum for the last 4 years or so and have enjoyed my time here immensely.  I think a big contributing factor is the quality control of threads, users, topics, and discussions in the forums.
Moderators are generally good at knowing which threads to close and which should be allowed to continue and know how to identify when discussions get out of hand to the point of descending beyond potential for productive conversations.
However, one major exception to this sticks out:  the Musician Talk subforum.
My main grievance with that particularly subforum is the prevalence of a "holier than though" dad rock elitist attitude that many of the regulars possess, a sentiment that the moderators seem to echo.  It's as if they legitimately believe that music died circa 1975 and that any pursuits not made with the aim of reviving rock 'n' roll music to it's so called "glory days" is completely worthless.
Whenever an opposing view or thought is presented, somebody will always post something along the lines of "that's not how Jimi would have done it" (without knowing how, in fact, Jimi would have done it were he still alive today) followed usually by somebody else chiming in with "kids these days" or "music will never be the way it used to be".
Basically anyone asking for new ideas or a modern perspective on music is met with disapproval and rejection.  When a brave soul occasionally strays in from another subforum and dares to question the sanctity of the Gospel According to Clapton, they are met with insults, logical fallacies, and close-minded ignorance on the part of the legion of past-clingers.
The worst part is the moderation.  Anytime that Team Dad Rock starts to trail, a moderator will step in and shut down the thread in order to prevent the spread of post-1980s perspectives, thus preventing the possibility of a brighter, more openminded Musician Talk forum where the older folk realize that music is not only still alive, but in fact stronger than ever.
Instead we are left with a totalitarian dystopia that rejects the voice of the changing times and the new schools of thought ushered in my the current generation.
This needs to be rectified as soon as possible.  My suggestion is the immediate liquidation of the current moderation personnel in favor of a new moderating crew that will keep the forum up to the high standards of this forum:  willT08, Baby Joel, and myself.
Thank you for your time.

author: sanjurox4
text:
Hello All,
I would like to suggest implementing a "Request Strum Pattern" (BPM included) functionality.
@UG - Similarly to the pro user's available "request official tab" rating system, create an additional pro user request-type functionality with interesting chord tablatures, where the company hires an additional musician to sit down part-time and do 15-20 songs/per shift.
Afterwards, the created "official bpm & strum pattern" will then be exported to all tab versions of the song in a compact box, as a type of suggestion/tooltip for the user.
Also, the aforementioned idea could be implemented as a "Request Acoustic" functionality.
Priority - could be even a few years before a similar functionality becomes an absolute necessity, but the cost-effectiveness and accessibleness of implementation makes it worthwhile for sooner development. The Official Tabs contain the same information, but are way slower to make and have lots of additional information, which is unnecessary for bedroom musicians. The Acoustic Version could be a sort of "first stage" verification and the usual Official Tab "second stage", which becomes available after a Chord tablature has been upgraded to an Acoustic Version
For further information on how to proceed with the implementation of such a functionality, please contact me via e-mail.
P.S. Long-time user of the tabs, but first time using the forum. Couldn't find similar requests, please delete the thread if it has already been posted/discussed.  Also, would have sent a private message, if there was a contacts e-mail address available on the main page.
Regards

author: sanjurox4
text:
Hello
mandelstamdavid
,
Thanks!
Request Acoustic could be a lowkey official version of a tablature - just the "chords" section from an official tab.
E.g. the user is a bedroom musician, who wants to play Africa by Toto, so they head over and find the official tab and go to the chords section, because they don't really need the 5 synth tabs, the shaker, the maracas, the agogo tab, etc.
The benefits are, that this official acoustic/chord version of the tab can then be further upgraded to a full fledged official tab after enough requests from the community.  Additionally, the team can save a lot of time spent of tabbing out all instruments to a song, which will not necesserilly be used by the majority of the community which only benefits from the Chords section. Also, tabbing out only chords along with strum pattern would be far more time-efficient than all instruments to a song.
Also, "Official Chords" might actually be a more suitable name.
Regards,

author: Colohue
text:
Good idea, but here are a few issues:
1. The users who wrote those lessons/columns put a lot of time and effort into them. They are available for people to use on UG, but it's also advertising their own talents in doing so. If there's a big book to be made, some of these people are worth of royalties.
2. For free? Consider the work it would take.
3. Though my work and ZeGuitarist's work generally comes as a package, whereas I could also probably talk to Nolan Whyte and blood_and_gold as well, that's still only a few people with the common purpose of doing this. Each individual is entitled to their own work, so it's important that they have their say.
4. The order of the pieces, the organisation, the arrangement, etc. Who would decide it and what use is best available?
5. What about users like Josh Urban who are no longer with us? His lessons are some of the best, but we can't just take his work and use it without his permission.
6. Why not just come to UG and read them?
Other than that, good idea. I like it and, to be honest, if I could print my stuff off in book form I most certainly would.

author: aprilthelear
text:
Please. I beg.
There are a couple of songs that have great riff lines or just interesting chord fingerpicking that makes a song *chefs kiss*. Trouble is I want to look at the 'Pro' tabs to see how to play it, and see the lyrics so I know where I'm at in the song and what the lyrics are.
Other problem is sometimes I'm looking at the numbers on the tabs and seeing them all occuring together and going 'heck what chord is that'. Most guitar song books that I've picked up are in this sort of a format
Em
|----------0
|--------0--
|------0----
|---2-------
|--2--------
|-0---------
I   am
So you can see the base chord (which the chords sheet already has), and the lyric (which is already a pro tab), as well as the notes to show you how it's played. This also allows me to pick through some parts and then switch to playing the chords where I'm not quite at the stage where I can do fancy finger work and sing at the same time.
I only recently got pro and there are some user submitted tabs that have this better presented for some of the songs. NGL after having just got Pro I'm wondering if it's a mistake and I should just go back to the user submit life. Otherwise I'm tempted to print out the tabs and then hand write in the chords and lyrics based on the other 'tracks' in the player but that just seems like a lot of work for something that I'd normally expect to find there.
Please forgive if this ability is already there somewhere. I messed around with settings and could not get it to appear, but it would be super helpful for us singer players, and probably handy to others as they try to learn songs.

text:
Instead of someone creating a contest thread then everyone asking what's the deadline, how is it judged, who am I facing, etc. -- have a template that answers all of this.
For example, instead of creating a thread for a Metal Contest and answering everyone's questions about the contest -- there would be a template that already has all the answers you need.
You would go to create a contest.  Then there would be the options
1.)  Original or Cover
2.)  Genre
3.)  Instruments
4.)  Contestants
5.)  Judges
6.)  Judging criteria
7.)  Deadline

Badbishop's contest record

Win                   Chessnut212     17-8 (Votes)    Funk Slap riffs            12/19/07

author: mkonnorw
text:
I find it annoying that the requests for official tabs generated automatically by UG Robot don't specify the version of the song requested. For example, on most requests for anime openings/endings, it doesn't clarify whether the request is for the full version or the TV size version.
At the very least, it should be made much more obvious which version a request thread is for. I understand that anime openings/endings are a somewhat niche category though and that many of these differences in versions are more relevant for acoustic/stripped down or live versions of songs. However, the official tabs already have tags for live and acoustic versions.
A little while ago, the official tab for Shinzou wo Sasageyo from Attack on Titan was put out, and it ended up being the TV size version which was disappointing. I checked the request thread and there was no mention of which version it was for. The only way you could tell which version it was for was to search for the song, click on a tab of the full version and of the short version and compare the number next to the "Want Official Tab" option. Additionally, none of the user submitted tabs are marked as full or short despite them having two different categories.
I think its fair to assume that most people upvoting a request for a song would want the full version. I think that if a tab is requested enough to the point a thread is automatically created, its safe to assume that people would want the full version of the song. Its especially ironic to me that the short version was made despite the full version having multiple solos on multiple instruments which are presumably a major factor for people wanting to learn the song. Also, the official tab for the previous Attack on Titan opening
was
the full version. I'm still salty about that, lol.

I suppose the issue could be alleviated if it was made more clear to the users what 'Acoustic' tabs mean. When they choose 'Acoustic' in the request form, ideally a popup should talk them out of it if there is no 'regular' tab for the song yet.

author: BaptizedinFire
text:
I had this idea pop into my mind today, after I had a pleasant experience with the customer service of a small Chinese company from whom I'd ordered some pedals.
If you're anything like me, then you're always going to do some Googling before buying new gear from an internet store. The competition in this particular market is absolutely fierce, and there are hundreds of retailers out there who want your attention. Some of them are run by honest, hard-working people who will bend over backwards for their customers. Others are mere scams who will sell you defect products with no warranty, and many are somewhere between those two extremes.
The information you can get from googling a small retailer is mostly very disjointed, coming up sporadically in different forums and whatnot. So my suggestion is this: We make UG the place where everyone goes to get this kind of information! Create some new "Retailers"-section where customers can add any retailer they have bought gear from, and share their experience, positive or negative! What did you think of the prices at Thomann? Did the customer service at WTFaccessories help you out if you had a problem?
Or perhaps this idea could just be merged with the regular "Reviews"-section? Whatever form this idea would take, I will be sure to try and give my five cents about the retailers and companies I have interacted with, and I hope you will do the same. I certainly think that this would be a worthy feature for the largest community for musicians on the net.
So what do you think, fellow UG:ers?

author: Deliriumbassist
text:
My main issue is that most people will only write about bad experiences. Secondly, staff turnover can be massive- bad staff one year could be replaced by awesome staff the next year, but won't be given a chance because of their predecessors.
Maybe a thread to collate actual scamjobs, but I don't think a review section is wholly appropriate, or even fair.
EDIT: And then you have those who don't understand consumer law and bitch about it. An example being unable to return a new item (that you've opened and used) 'because you don't like it anymore'- if it's opened, it cannot be sold as new, and therefore has to be sold at a lower price, and takes up space that should be used for shiny new awesomeness. Imbeciles will see refusal to refund/exchange for another new guitar as the shop being unreasonable, when it's actually the shop doing what it has to in order to, well... stay open.

author: Deliriumbassist
text:
It's well known that bad news travels faster than good news, which is unfortunate. We love to complain, which does suck, and whilst you may do a "counter review", if a retailer is generally a good one, then you need more good reviews than bad reviews to show that, which I personally don't feel would happen.
And yes, companies should be hiring good staff from the off, but they hire off of interviews, and anyone who's been interviewed knows that an interview really is a shit way of hiring- answering inane questions, jumping through the hoops, saying the right things at the right time in the right way- you can learn that, and that's applicable to most jobs. So the right staff at interview may not be the right staff on the job, and the customer may just get the shitty one that's on his 3 month probation. Then there's personal issues where the staff's mind is somewhere else- obviously the customer can't do a thing about that, and the staff member shouldn't be bringing it in to work, but we are only human.
Then there's the influence of expectations. An example from myself is that I had a guy come in to work and expected a demonstration of 3 different home cinema setups there and then ON A SATURDAY. Saturday is extremely busy for us. Even on a weekday, I probably wouldn't be able to set up a demo of that magnitude without taking a booking for it. I asked him to come back in an hour (forsaking my lunch break as well) so I could at least try to get stuff all set up for him, which apparently wasn't good enough, so he went and complained to my head office. HE felt hard done by, because his expectations were beyond what could be fulfilled at that point in time. If he had factored in and allowed me a reasonable amount of time to set up, he would have had a good demo. If he had allowed me to take his details so we could book him in for a demo, he would have had a FANTASTIC demonstration. But if he reviewed, he would've given a bad review based upon his expectations, which would've been unfair.
I'll stop before this becomes a rant against shitty customers

author: BaptizedinFire
text:
I don't really understand why you put so much responsibility on yourself as a customer. If the companies have an ineffective way of finding good people to recruit, then it's not our responsibility to change our behaviour so that they can keep hiring people in the same way and hope things will work out. In fact, our it's our responsibility to show them, through our freedom of choice, if they're doing things right or wrong. And they will have to find the causes of their problems themselves. Over time, this exact mechanism is what will improve any market.
We can apply this "fairness"-principle to other situations as well: If you've had a distusting meal at some restaurant, should you then just walk away silently, concerned about the people who might at some point work at that restaurant? I would say that it's in the best interest of everyone that you express your opinion. Especially the chef will want to know how if there is something he needs to change to not see his income plummet.
I agree with you about the fact that bad news travel faster than good news, though. But if that would turn out to become a real problem, then there is alway the option of shutting down the section.
How do you feel about the countless other sites that do this kind of thing, albeit in a less specialized manner? Are they being unfair and mean as well?

author: KennethSmith
text:
It would be nice to have an edit feature in Tab Pro. I understand that Tab Pro just reads Guitar Pro files that are posted to UG, so perhaps an edit feature within Tab Pro is not possible, so I suggest that Tab Pro users should be able to download GP files for the purpose of making edited versions, which would then appear on UG as Tab Pro versions. Consider the following argument:
The error message that reads "This tab has been removed at the request of the publisher" is confusing since the
exact
same Guitar Pro tab that has been removed at the request of the publisher is usually available on Tab Pro. My best guess is that UG wants people to pay for a Tab Pro subscription, so they are limiting the availability of GP tabs to encourage people to switch to Tab Pro.
If this is true, then once people sign up for Tab Pro, there is no reason to prevent them from accessing Guitar Pro files. Of course, if a Tab Pro subscription allowed you to download GP files, dishonest people would sign up for a Tab Pro subscription, download the GP files they need, and then cancel their Tab Pro subscription. This could be avoided by only allowing Tab Pro users to download a set number of GP files at a time for editing purposes (i.e. the edited version must improve the original in some way, as verified by the tab submission process). For example, suppose UG enables Tab Pro users to download ten GP tabs for editing. If a user downloads ten GP tabs, there should be a feature that prevents them from downloading any more tabs until they submit revised versions of the tabs they downloaded previously.
While it is currently possible to post edited versions of songs as GP files, only the tab author has access to the original GP file, so anyone else who wants to edit the tab has to recreate it from scratch, which is time consuming and discourages UG users from posting edits in this manner . I would guess that very few GP tabs have had edited versions posted
after
being "removed at the request of the publisher" (except for edited versions submitted by the tab author, who has the original GP file).
Allowing users to download GP files for editing purposes in the manner described above would increase the quality of GP tablature on Tab Pro, which would in turn increase the number of Tab Pro subscriptions as people became aware of the quality of tabs on Tab Pro.
UG Staff/Moderators: If you think this idea has merit, please pass it on.

author: sjones
text:
Long time UG'er, First time caller....
(that's how they say it, right?)
Just want to bring up a scenario that I see on the forums that irks me. Think it's something that might be addressed somewhere in the rules section(s).
Now, quite often threads get made in the wrong forums, expecially by new members. It just happens. Normally, members and/or mods correct them, they go on their merry way, UG as we know it goes on without a hitch.
However, I've seen this scenario happening (mainly with people out of that window to claim "noob-dom") and I haven't really seen much deterrent from it in the rules. I'll use a recent example:
A member posts a "Recording" thread in the Pit. I, and other members of course (along with expected spam posts) direct the member in the right direction. Well, I decided to check the Recordings forum, and whaddaya know?!....there's the exact same thread made by the exact same member. If this member was more of a "noob", I'd just overlook it like usual, assuming a "rookie mistake". However, when someone has ~2 years+ of experience on the board (as the member did in this case), I just find it an utter annoyance. I've been seeing this popping up and I know it's nothing new (hell, I've been browsing/posting since '03), but the annoyance of seeing something blatantly posted "out-of-forum" from the members outside of the "noob-window" of sorts just rubs me the wrong way.
Some topics can be covered in multiple forums, of course, but when someone who has been here long enough to know better intentionally double-posts a thread in wrong forums, it's just an annoyance to me, and I'd assume others.
I didn't see anything about this in the rules. Thought it seemed like a decent suggestion to put on the table for something to add. Once again, with newer members doing this and claiming "rookie mistake" is one thing. But I'd suggest people who have been here more than a fair amount of time to know how the forums work who do this, in my humble opinion, probably merit some type of warning (formal/informal) and repeat offenders of course see the effects of the ban system.
(....or maybe I'm just a crusty, old '03'er. Damn whipperschnappers! I need my nap...and a new adult diaper)

author: Carmel
text: Posting intentionally in the wrong forum is considered spam, and depending on you mentioning it in the report or the mod checking on his or her own, the user receives a warning as well.

author: sjones
text:
Ok. I assumed that could've be how it worked.
I'd still suggest that something be mentioned about the topic in the Pit/Site rules to maybe deter it from happening. Possibly just a brief sentence or two under the "No Spam" section would be sufficient perhaps?
Either way, just an observation/opinion of mine that I thought was worth mentioning to the UG brass.

author: Terrapin2190
text:
Hey UG'ers!
I was wondering if there might be a string of code that can signal a page break while editing a personal tab.
I've been finding that chords and lyrics get a little messy when trying to print them off. Sometimes, the lyrics will reach the end of the page (think, 'mid-chorus' as an example) and the rest of the lyrics for the chorus will be placed on a different page. Making it difficult to read while practicing a song.
Is there anything I can do to manually set a place that the lyrics will begin on the next page from within the UG edit/publishing app?
OR
Is there any type of workaround I can use?
Say, saving the webpage as HTML or PDF or XPS, then use an external editor to insert page breaks until it reaches the next page in a print preview pane?
I would like to keep the fancy UG header and chord diagrams at the top of the page intact...

author: Terrapin2190

Thanks!

It could even somehow be tied to the preferred tab format to insert page breaks by default. Have the 'engine' (if it can be called that) look for strings such as [Intro], [Verse], [Chorus]. Have it bunch together the contents below each marker. If the contents extend to the next page, the engine could move the contents (starting at the marker) to the top of the next page? If contents extend beyond a single page, leave it as is.
I'm not very knowledgeable with coding, but I know enough to brainstorm 'if/then' scenarios.
I'm open to suggestions of 3rd party apps that can read HTML or PDF, etc. and modify text in order to achieve the results I'm looking for. Hoping to find a fix...

author: fabiospark
text:
Quote by mandelstamdavid
Hi. We can't add a page break to the tab page because we don't want a tab page to be complicated. I recommend you to use these references:
https://prntscr.com/n2ii0y
In my opinion, NOW it is complicated because it is unpredictable and it makes us waste A LOT o time when trying to get a decent print.
Also:
-  the maximum number of chords diagrams should be ten instead of eight, using the same margin you used for the line above the title
And some little layout change would be highly welcome too, i.e.:
-  all the OPTIONS could be written on a single line instead of four
-  the word CHORDS could be omitted
And, in the end, a long time request from a lot of people:
-  please move the "PRINT" button to the top of the page, beside the edit button
Thanks.

author: fabiospark
text:
I forgot another very important one (to me, at least):
-  in the subsequent printing sessions please remember the chords diagrams chosen in the previous printing sessions
Now, every time I go to print a tab for the second, third, fourth, ect, time (I usually never get the result I want the first time)
I have to re-choose the diagrams because they got reset.
Thanks.

What about 6/8 time? Or 5/4 time? Or 9/8 time? Or 2/4 time? Or 5/8 time? Or mixed time sigs?
Point is, you probably don't want to add the time signature as an attribute to the tab. If you think someone might not know the song or feel the pulse you could add it as a comment at the top. (In tabs I like adding 1 + 2 + 3 + over the staff to show exactly where the beats land.)

author: Renka
text:
There's been a couple of these kind of threads floating around recently in the Guitar Gear & Accessories forum, but personally I'd like to see one for each major brand.

author: hyvyys

I always wondered what is the purpose of the 'Key' property in a tab. And specifically what is supposed to be chosen when the song is tabbed with Capo? If the original key is F#m and I tab the song in Em and put Capo 2, am I supposed to choose Key Em or F#m? (Until now I chose F#m, the original key without considering Capo in such occasions).
I assumed the Key info might be useful for Simplifying the chords. For instance, in a Key of Fm, F5 would be simplified to Fm and not F. However, I just tested and it's just simplified to F major.

author: NSpen1
text:
hyvyys
I would agree with you, key F#m.  We had a little discussion about this (can't find atm) and that was the consensus.
Well, F5 to either F or Fm isn't really a simplification
I think the Key info may be aimed mostly at people wanting to play songs in a specific key.

author: hyvyys
text:
NSpen1
F5 → F is a simplification in the sense that inexperienced players just strum all the strings and a full chord is easier for them to play. When playing solo on an acoustic guitar, full chords also sound exactly what they are called – fuller
But technically, of course you are right, this is more of an augmentation than simplification.
That's why I'm usually against using power chords in tabs (even for heavy metal) because though they are technically more accurate, they convey less information. Using them seems like lack of imagination to me. There are of course isolated cases where neither a major nor minor chords really fits and the fifth is actually the most honest choice, but I think those are extremely rare. Sometimes I will use a "power chord" to express a fifth in a progression of added intervals (say, E6 E5 E6 E7). Idk if that's a good use case, but yeah. One nice power chord to play is D5 played on the bottom 4 strings, I think I used that once in a tab. In UG's chord visualizer it's version 8, I think it should be version 2 at least

author: NSpen1
text:
hyvyys
Hehe, I don't know, I think I started out more with power chords because that was the type of thing I wanted to play, and they should be easier anyway.  Plus aren't people always complaining about playing barre chords, and F is like the hardest barre chord?
Anyway, the rest of what you say makes sense, I have a tab where I put the full major or minor chords but said you can play them as power chords to make it more accurate to the song.
D5 on the bottom 4 strings or top 4?  xx0235 ?

author: Pencom
text:
Hello, regarding the IQ Rewards program and  tab manipulation; upon reading and re reading the "What is UG IQ?" I'm not surprised that there is so much confusion about what is and what is not a "point". The whole information page is really not well written. It is a series of verbal contradictions and should be corrected. English is my native language and I'm having difficulty understanding it. I can just imagine all the people reading and trying to comprehend it where English is not their native tongue. Some tab manipulation is obliviously deliberate. No question about that. When a nice guitar is used as a prize that sort of thing is going to happen. I also suspect that because of the poor wording in "What is UG IQ" some people are not quite clear on what the requirements for points are. I will give you an example: Please read the "IQ points for submitting articles, tabs and chords. Now I, like all of you, get weekly "stats" from UG. You can review my last report below. You will note the figure of 29, 453...the number of times a user added a tab to their favorites. You will also note that that figure netted a total of "8" points
Now, I'm not in the running for anything, nor do I wish to be. I'm fairly certain that what UG "wrote" is not what UG "meant". I'm asking that everyone on this forum "read" very, very carefully the UG IQ info page and let us "all" suggest corrections and enhancements to the verbiage so that tab manipulation and prize cheating is avoided in the future.

Special: Points cannot be gained during this time period

Special: You get points for text tabs, and text tabs only

Special: You get points for text tabs, and text tabs only

author: Pencom
text:
Shura_FYI
Reading Franks comment (thanks Frank) made me realize that we have a simple "wording" issue here on the UG web site , i.e,  incorrect "English" terms are being used.  If I could speak Russian "half" as well as you all speak English I could work for the State Department. (but I'm retired)
When I and others receive the following:
"The more hits you get, the higher your chance to earn Contributor of the Month status. Invite your friends to view your tabs by sharing on facebook."
You will note the word "Contributor".
(Definition)
Contributor: a person or thing that contributes something, in particular.
"UG IQ Top Users"
You will note the word "User"
(Definition)
User: a person or thing that uses something
In this case, the IQ system would want to be talking about the people who are "contributing" to UG...not "using".  The users would be the person (s) who comes to the UG web site and takes advantage of, or uses, the tabs to play music.  There would be other areas where they would "use" the UG web site.
Again, in this case, Frank would be a "contributor" not a "user".  He is adding, not taking.
Another word or words needs to found to replace "UG IQ Top Users".  If you wish to replace "users" with "contributors" UG will need to be "very" specific about what constitutes a "contribution".  One would have to assume, as has Frank, that writing a tab would be a contribution, not a use.  UG defines "hits" as a contribution, so that, as well would need to be specified.  Perhaps the over riding factor here should be:
1. What is helping or adding to the UG web site?  What makes the UG web site better? Should we define or refine what "helping the UG web site means?  If someone writes a tab does that help UG?  I believe so.  Are people who vote for tabs helping the UG web site.  I believe they are.  Are accurate tab corrections helping the UG web site?  Yes, I would agree with that. (as long as they are not my tabs
)
UG defines "hits" as helping or contributing to the UG web site.  There would be others.
My suggestion is this:  I would suggest that UG break up into "several" categories (lists) instead of just one.  The two categories would consist of:
1.  a.  Number of tabs posted by users (UG used to have that list).  b. average of votes tab posters are receiving. c. number of hits (as is now being shown) tabs and tabbers are receiving.
2.  a.  Everything else that is now currently in the UG IQ Top Users (but change the name) list, i.e, comments, corrections...everything on the list.
I believe that a two category system would be much more accurate in defining what is helping UG rather then arguing about whether comments, corrections, tab postings, hits etc., have too much or too little merit.  I believe most people would agree that if you are helping UG you should get some sort of credit for your effort.  By breaking this down into two categories you don't risk pitting one group...say the group that likes to comment etc., with the group that likes to tab or vote etc.  Everyone wins and harmony is restored.
Please, let's discuss.

But, I believe he was making a good point which I agree with about the "weight" or "measure" of what constitutes "helping" or "contributing" to the UG web site.  This is not about who is a good guy or who is a bad guy.  It is, IMHO, about making the UG web site better and giving credit to any and all persons who do so.
My argument, suggestion, is that UG implement a "multi" tier system that shows credit for doing various things that benefit the guitar community, i.e, UG.  As an example to what I'm saying, and I hate to keep dragging Frank into this, but let's say that Frank posts a boat load of tabs on the UG web site. Likewise, there are a number of other areas that should be given recognition.  I say recognition because nobody here (other then UG staff) are getting paid to do this.  It is, at least for me, a labor of love.
The IQ system allows for recognition of a certain "kind".  As far as I can see, it puts a very high emphasis on "commenting".  Nothing wrong with that, however, it is, in my opinion, rather trivial relative to tab posting, voting, hits, number of votes etc.  "Quality tabs" take time and effort to develop and post and that should, in my opinion, be applauded and recognized. In the long run quality tabs are what people come to UG for. Comments have their value but in the long run it is not generally a "lasting" value.  A person who posts a tab does far, far more work and that work has a much more lasting value.  People visiting the UG web site will see that tab (yes, your tabs Frank..) for many, many years to come.  They may learn how to play a song because of what Frank did.  What they will not do months or years from now is read a "comment".
What I propose is UG, with ample discussion, develop a multi list of different "types" of contributions so that those people who favor "comments" are accommodated,  and those people who favor other forms of contributions be accommodated.  I don't want various parties to be at odds with each other about this.  I believe all sides can get something and UG will come out better for it because a "broader" group of it's members will be satisfied.
Lastly, as has been mentioned, the "terminology", i.e, user, contributor etc needs to be revaluated for technical accuracy.

I am a bit unsure of how to correctly express myself here... Well, here it goes:
UG has a very complete blog-software, from writing a blog to publishing it - but as soon as something is published, it disappears among thousands of other posts, of which most is of the "slash h4xx0rs ok cool"-kind. People who write stuff only does that because they know that if it is good enough, it will get attention. On UG, a writer can spend three hours writing about the philosophy of songwriting without having more than two-three readers. I believe that a lot of skilled writers and guitarplayers on UG knows this, and therefore chooses not to write - the odds of getting the post out there to the users are just too small. author: nnf
text:
Two years ago when I started using this site I really liked it but the way the editing system is managed killed it for me eventually. I personally invested quite some work into correcting tabs on this site and also have written one completley by myself.
However I had to witness other users just correcting them to something wrong way too often. All the work being lost. I am not the only one who sees this problem.
For example roar by katy perry:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/katy-perry/roar-chords-1410981
Version 1 is having the most votes because it was just 100% accurate in the past. Someone really did a good job putting in the work. Then someone else - for whatever reason - puts in nonsense and the original work that thousands of people saved as favourite is just gone. If you read the last comment you can see me asking the author what went wrong and him answering he is also fed up and also stopped using UG for this exact reason.
This behaviour is just hijacking top rated versions for I don't know what. Incompetence or blatant trolling maybe.
I corrected some serious timing issues on the Ed Sheeran Lego House chords not too long ago only to find out that all the work was for absolutley nothing because someone else just changed it to something absolutley wrong again. Just compare the chords to the offical video by yourself:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/ed-sheeran/lego-house-chords-1093774
Now, one could say: "Well, why don't people just create new versions so that people who actually liked the old ones can keep their favourites that worked for them in the way they were when being favourited?"
Well, that would make sense as the word "version" would suggest, but no. If you try to hand in a correction as new version the UG moderators get very unfriendly towards you and turn it into a correction themselves. So even if you don't intend to destroy the work of other people, the UG moderators make you do so.
Yeah sorry for the rant but I wanted it off my chest before leaving since I believe its pretty sad it has become like this.

author: fanapathy
text:
I've been observing this for a while. Tab approval can range anywhere from 1 day to 6 weeks in my experience. Depends on if the band/song is well known, new/old and if there are many existing tabs already. Old songs from lesser known artists take the longest, tabs with 8 versions etc do as well.
What I'd like to comment on though is approval votes. They seem to make absolutely no difference. There's been tabs with 7 approval votes stuck in the queue for a month, and newer submitted tabs with no votes being approved within a short time. Tab mod votes is the only one that makes a difference, tabs with +M will get approved quickly. Reject votes with a good reasoning on the other hand is effective.
Because of this, I see no reason to go on and review tabs as a regular user. When votes have next to no value, it's a waste of time. It's not fair to people spending time reviewing in TPA and I'd like to see an improvement in this system, especially as the frequency of submissions is constantly growing.

author: Joshua Garcia
text:
Quote by fanapathy
What I'd like to comment on though is approval votes. They seem to make absolutely no difference. There's been tabs with 7 approval votes stuck in the queue for a month, and newer submitted tabs with no votes being approved within a short time. Tab mod votes is the only one that makes a difference, tabs with +M will get approved quickly. Reject votes with a good reasoning on the other hand is effective.
Because of this, I see no reason to go on and review tabs as a regular user. When votes have next to no value, it's a waste of time. It's not fair to people spending time reviewing in TPA and I'd like to see an improvement in this system, especially as the frequency of submissions is constantly growing.
Usually, the one's that stay there longer are the one's the tab mods REALLY need to look into (mostly misc. tabs). At least I think. So it would probably be a little harder for the tab mods to review it compared to every other tab that gets reviewed and accepted/rejected within a few days.
As for user votes, it's obviously not the deciding factor for pending tabs, but I do believe it helps tab moderators make their decision. It goes in order of:
User's votes -> Tab moderator's votes -> Tab admins -> Approve/reject.
So it's just a matter of how often the tab mods check in the TPA. But I imagine they have a lot to go through everyday, so cut them some slack.

author: matter
text:
We are happy to announce a test launch of the Meebo Community IM service on Ultimate Guitar. This means that now you can chat with your UG friends and buddies from dozens of various IM platforms straight from your favorite guitar website!
The bar, which you can see at the bottom of the page, is currently available only on the Community pages (user and artist profiles, and groups), but in just few weeks you will be able to use it everywhere on UG.
What is Meebo IM?
It's dead simple: this browser-based chat client allows you to communicate in real-time with your friends on Ultimate Guitar, all you need is just to log-in to the site!
If you also want to talk with friends on any chat network Meebo supports (including AIM, MSN, ICQ, Facebook, Gtalk and much more), then sign up for a free Meebo account
here
, add the desired networks to your profile and sign-in to Meebo through the bar on UG.
Share the pages
As another bonus addition, Community IM has a cool sharing feature. Click the "Share" button at the bottom left hand corner of the chat bar, and either send a link of the page you are currently viewing to Facebook, Twitter, or Email, or to any of your buddies in the chat list (just click on the username).
In other words - just try it, it's very simple and intuitive.
PS: Clear your browser's cache if you don't see the bar on the community pages.
PPS: Upset that you can't find Meebo bar on the Forums?
Try blogs
!
-----
Please look through these known issues/bugs:
Upon using the "View Profile" feature you can find yourself logged out, with a user number displayed instead of your actual username. Just refresh the page to bring everything into place (the glitch should be fixed soon).
The notification sounds are a little bit loud, so if this confuses you - just turn off the sound notifications (the speaker icon is in the header of your buddies list).

author: michaud.joel2017
text:
Dear Ultimate Guitar Community and Administrators,
I am a long-time user of Ultimate Guitar and have always appreciated the value this platform offers to musicians of all levels. However, I recently made a
disturbing discovery
that I believe needs urgent attention for the well-being of our community.
Upon using Norton Anti-Track, I was
alarmed
to find that the Ultimate Guitar website is deploying an astonishing
74 trackers
. This level of tracking is
far beyond the norm
and raises
serious privacy concerns
.
Most alarming is the potential use of
fingerprinting
. For those unfamiliar, fingerprinting is a method used to
uniquely identify and track users
by their device and browser characteristics, often without their knowledge.
The implications here are deeply concerning. With such extensive tracking, one can't help but suspect that our data could be
sold to third parties
. This infringes on our privacy and raises ethical questions about user consent.
I urge the Ultimate Guitar team to
address these concerns
. It's vital that this platform, which has earned our trust over the years, does not betray that trust through practices that endanger our privacy.
I hope to see a commitment to transparency and better standards in data collection and usage, ensuring that Ultimate Guitar remains a safe and trusted resource for all musicians.
Thank you for considering this pressing issue.
Sincerely,
J

author: michaud.joel2017

author: phaddrill
text:
I made this python script which exports a song list from any page on Ultimate Guitar site to a CSV spreadsheet. It pulls in other handy attributes as well, e.g. song ID, date added, url, etc. Tested with my favourites list and a regular playlist. See script below or the attached file. If you have python installed you can run the attached, just change the file extension from .txt to .py.
## Python script exports 'song list' from an Ultimate Guitar html page and saves it as CSV file.
## Steps:
## 1. Login at
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com
/ and navigate to
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/user/mytabs
## 2. Sort your list as needed, then right-click anywhere on the page, click Save As and select type "Webpage, HTML Only...".
## 3. Set the input folder (workingDir) and file name (inputHtml) in Variables section below.
## 4. Run the script (You can download and install python from
https://www.python.org/downloads/
)
## Updated on 9 Mar 2024. Tested with Python 3.9.18.
import json, os
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from datetime import datetime as dt
## Variables.
workingDir = r'C:\z_dev\gitRepos\py-tools\ult-guitar-scraping\input'
inputHtml = 'My tabs @ Ultimate-Guitar.Com.html'
todayAppend = '-' + str(dt.today())[:10].replace('-','')
outputCsv = 'ug-song-list' + todayAppend + '.csv'
## Open the html file.
fname = os.path.join(workingDir, inputHtml)
with open(fname, 'r') as file:
beautifulSoupText = BeautifulSoup(file.read(), 'html.parser')
## Find tag containing song list.
tag = beautifulSoupText.find(class_="js-store")
## Get attribute value containing the raw json string.
jsonString = tag['data-content']
## Loads JSON string into python dictionary
data = json.loads(jsonString)
parentObj = data['store']['page']['data']
if "list" in parentObj:
## Get list if favourites.
list = parentObj['list']['list']
else:
## Get list if playlist.
items = []
list = parentObj['songbook']['tabs']
for item in list:
items.append(item['tab']
list = items
print("Songs in list: " + str(len((list))))
## Convert dict to pandas dataframe. Convert unix date. Sort by band then song name.
df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(list)
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'],unit='s')
if "list" in parentObj:
df = df.sort_values(by=["band_name", "song_name"],ascending=[True, True]
df.reset_index(inplace=True)
df.index.name = "row_id"
print(df)
## Export dataframe to csv.
df.to_csv(os.path.join(workingDir,outputCsv))
print('CSV saved at: ' + os.path.join(workingDir,outputCsv))

author: Colohue
text:
Lesson writers need to know how they can improve the lessons. Ratings are important for users who just come in as well. Like/dislike is a popularity contest. Ratings are a display of quality.
Some of the most popular articles on here contain incorrect information. They've been rated a lot of times, but the total score is fairly low compared to other articles. Also, older articles, say from 2005, seem to naturally have considerably more ratings that more recent ones.
I would consider the removal of ratings to be devolution, and the removal of something that is actually helpful, whereas 'like/dislike' is of no actual factual benefit to anyone, for any reason.

For me "bad tabs" can be done away with.
Why? 1) If a beginning tab author submits a tab it is approved ie checked, corrected and after that approved.  OR if you have a more experienced tab author that can directly submit tabs these authors have achieved a certain level of experience and knowledge to produce good level tabs .
So why are bad tabs needed at all?
My experience is that bad tabs are given by raters who do not have any experience either in making tabs or/and even in playing guitar.
Why is it we authors are "checked" for the tabs we submit while the raters can just do anything without being checked?
Examples:
1)  Should a starter  guitar player be allowed to rate a  tab? For me no.
2)  Should a rater be allowed to give a bad tab because there is one spelling mistake? No (but it does happen unfortunately)
3)  Should a rater be allowed to give a bad tab report because they "think it doesn't sound right"? (happens often) Again for me No.
4)  Should a rater be allowed to give a bad tab because the rater lacks the skills to play the song? Needless to say for me also a No.
5)  Why would level 5 authors with over say over 1000 tabs on the site and with a very good rating record be allowed to receive bad tabs or bad ratings  at all?
Unfortunately exactly the same happens with the rating system.  A lot of mis-use and  misunderstanding.
So for me there is something not correct as authors (simply put) are "checked" before a tab is put on the site while for raters it is a free for all ie there is no check whatsoever on their skills.
I refer to earlier discussions & contrubutions (starting #2653) on this concern in this thread :
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1832452&page=67#2655

1)   to do away with the bad tab option either the button or the one linked to the 1 star rating, and
2)   no ratings lower than 3 without a (good & hopefully valid) comment as to why this low rating was given. (this comment should thus increase the quality of the tab).

author: drmcclainphd
text:
Quote by Colohue
If you have taken out a copyright notice on your own work, then UG can not legally host it on their servers, even under your own username. It's a blanket rule, since proving that the person on the other side of the screen is, in reality, the copyright holder, is extremely difficult and time consuming.
So I'm afraid you're wrong on this one. The fact that you wrote a piece of music does not mean that you are the copyright holder.
I understand the blanket rule as it stands and will comply. However, it is flawed for the reasons stated and should be changed.
No, I'm not wrong. If you write a work, you most certainly are the copyright holder, unless you transfer all rights (sell as opposed to license).
A copyright notice is a mark on the work. You can place it as part of the creation process or later, or not at all. The law covers ownership
What you "register" for is copyright protection. It is the most certain way to prove ownership and/or transfers of rights. There are other ways to do so but are the responsibility of the owner to produce in a form beyond reasonable doubt.
Proving one to be the copyright (using UG's definition, which should more properly include the term "published" and/or "commercially available") holder is not difficult, time consuming or the responsibility of UG. Works available for purchase can easily be confirmed if the copyright notice and/or owner's name is affixed.
One can prove that one is that person in the generally accepted way, by providing a verifiable credit card number under that same name. UG trusts this to get peoples' money, they ought to be able to trust it in the less stringent sense of proving identity, using a means already in place. Unless, of course, they don't care if credit card fraud is being perpetrated as long as they get their money, but want to dodge possible liability issues when they don't stand to profit.
Liability is the issue here, and a perfectly valid one. However, UG goes to such extremes that it cuts off its own nose. I should think they'd be utterly delighted to have users posting material from their published CDs in order to show just how many professionals participate here. By simply requiring a link to a publicly available source with the owner's name affixed, plus ID verification just as used to sell things, UG would be more than adequately protected from liability. Without such protection, despite all the disclaimers, if someone uploads copyrighted material they don't own and it gets found out by the owner, UG *IS* liable, as it has not made a reasonable effort at verification.
With this level of protection, acceptable in any country that prescribes to the copyright law in US Code Title 17, UG is covered and protected and need not make any effort to investigate or enforce further. It becomes the responsibility of the copyright holder to notify UG of infringement and provide evidence of ownership. This is typically done via the relevant entry of infringement contacts (mostly attorneys) listed in the US in the Library of Congress's web site.
Publicly available copyrighted works can be verified. What UG can't verify is whether or not someone's MP3 upload was swiped from someone else's long defunct page, a covert recording of a concert, local garage band, etc. These receive the same consideration under the law, and although harder to prove can in fact be proven, and UG remains wide open to liability.
So, no I won't. I wish I could, and if UG thought about it, so would they. In such a case, rather than simply checking a box saying it's not copyrighted, one could simply fill in a box providing a URL to a public source with name affixed, and fill out the self-same credit card form to run an automated verification. Then UG users with things published could share them on UG making it look better, thus attracting more users to sign up, including for UG+.
If one creates and affixes (ie. writes or records) something, one owns it. Ownership confers the right of control over one's possessions regardless of any overt marking naming the owner. Control over affixed material means control over who may use it and in what form, and with what permission from the owner. This is the very essence of the nearly globally accepted copyright law. Unless there is a verifiable (there's that pesky problem again, but worse this time) statement by an owner of donation of a work to the public domain, every single recording posted on UG is either pilfered or copyrighted (despite the checkbox and the sadly flawed UG definition of "copyrighted"), or both, and anyone who ever posted these should be banned and the material removed. I've removed mine and won't be uploading 10 cuts from my three albums to share here, as I was just about to.
Side note: Where "liability" is mentioned, try inserting "scandal". Even if there's no legal action taken there can be a hell of a lot of bad publicity.

I am not a lawyer. But you don't need to be to know your rights. I was in fact an expert witness in a copyright violation case against a major ISP, working for a group of intellectual property lawyers, so I know I know my rights To serve the music community, you should learn this as well. Liability protection, covering your asses should someone violate an owners copy rights, is no excuse for misrepresenting an important law.
I'm not a lawyer, but I do have a law degree. Those instructions are for the common user whose understanding of 'copyrighted work' is usually 'professional recording made by a famous person'. Considering the jurisdiction of the site, the wording you're objecting to creates an impossibility. As soon as a work is fixed it is copyrighted, as such there is no such thing as non-copyrighted music unless you make an explicit statement that you release the work into the public domain (which is not on that page).
Given the context of that page, nobody could argue that you, as a creator of an artistic work, put the work into the public domain by uploading it to UG. There is even an explanation of what is meant by 'copyrighted music'.

I have to agree Mandolin chords would be a great addition. However this little gem of knowledge may help.
Has it occurred to you that many Mandolin chords are actually the same SHAPE as OPEN Guitar chords, Except they are mirror images I.E. Inverted.
Think G and C for example.  bass end of your hand, so not index finger end. do the mirror image of the bass strings on the trebble strings of the mandolin 2nd and 3rd frett. Bingo.
It also works for some Barre chords too. Bb is index finger first 2 strings 1st frett. Ring finger top two strings 3rd frett.
You will get the idea It took me 20 minutes to learn to play mandolin one night at a gig well enough to knock off Dirty old town and 20 something years to realise about the chords.
I hope this helps.

author: SFBay-James4
text:
Hello UG,
I currently work-up a song in Guitar Pro using the best available Guitar Pro or Power Tab from Ultimate Guitar.  I tried to learn straight off of the official tabs but had to switch back to Guitar Pro.  I want to explain how I work-up a song so that you can better implement a system on your website.  That would increase usage of your official tabls.
I hope you take my comments below as I sincerely want to use your website instead of downloading to Guitar Pro but have some honest suggestions to improve your website.
Yes the below is long but hopefully if gives you the context to translate into user stories.  Suggestions are in
bold/italic yellow
Disclaimers:
I get it.  For royalty and copyright reasons, you can never offer your official tabs as Guitar Pro or MIDI files.  Very few people can make money making music and I don't want to infringe and further rip a living wage from creators.
My learning system is a mish-mash of others and I don't quite know how to credit them in a way that balances their contribution and the fact that they are competing sites.  They are "classical guitar shed," "unstoppable guitar," and "joe deloro."
My system is "involved" (some say overkill).  I play in a cover band with a drummer who is classically trained.  I cannot be as sloppy as I could be if I was playing by myself.
Macro-steps:
Chunk up the song into sections (usually verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, etc.)
Work-up each section
If needed, work-up "transitions" between sections (usually by taking 1-2 bars on either side of a section.  For example, the last 2 bars of the verse and the first 2 bars of the chorus)
Work-up the entire song (play the entire song)
Meso-steps:
If needed, strike the rhythm on muted strings.  Work-up to tempo,.
Work out the notes and fingerings. Sometimes I divide picking hand and fretting hand individually before trying them together...if the part is difficult.  This is untimed (no tempo)
Play along with the part (often with the other tracks muted)
Play against the other tracks (with my part muted...usually just drums and bass)
Play along with the studio recording (to learn the "touch" and "feel")
Micro-steps:
Play successfully at 50% tempo (or -50 BPM) 8 times in a row
Play successfully at 60% tempo (or -40 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 70% tempo (or -30 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 80% tempo (or -20 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 90% tempo (or -10 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 100% tempo (or +0 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 110% tempo (or +10 BPM) 4 times in a row
Play successfully at 100% tempo (or +0 BPM) 8 times in a row
If the part is <= 4 bars then I double the number of times in a row to 16x and 8x
If the part is >= 16 bars then I halve the number of times in a row to 4x and 2x
If it's the whole song then I quarter the number of times in a row to 2x and 1x.  I still try to do the entire song at 100% at least 4x
If I stall (start making mistakes) at a tempo then, after a break, I do a "small reset" and do the last successful tempo 8x and then start progressing again.
If I stall again at a tempo then, after a break, I do a "large reset."  I slow down by 10%/10BPM, do that tempo 8x in a row.  Then I do the stalled tempo (+10%/10BPM) 8x in a row.  Then I go back to progressing after 4x in-a-row.
If I am super stuck (like the two lead parts merged together on Foo Fighters "Pretender" ...ugh), I may slow down the tempo jumps to +5%/5BPM or even +2%/2BPM.  A 2% increase is so subtle that I have never had that fail.  It just takes a really really long time.
I know that 8-times-in-a-row and 4-times-in-a-row seems excessive.  However, I also do statistics for a living...
Likelihood of doing something again a 3rd time after doing it 2x in-a-row before = 22%
Likelihood of doing something again a 4th time after doing it 3x in-a-row before = 37%
Likelihood of doing something again a 5th time after doing it 4x in-a-row before = 54%  <-- More than random luck / flipping a coin
Likelihood of doing something again a 9th time after doing it 8x in-a-row before = 70%   <-- Casino-grade odds
Likelihood of doing something again a 17th time after doing it 16x in-a-row before = 80%   <-- Business-grade odds
Likelihood of doing something again a 33rd time after doing it 32x in-a-row before = 90%   <-- Almost pharmaceutical-grade odds
Likelihood of doing something again a 65th time after doing it 64x in-a-row before = 95%   <-- Pharmaceutical-grade odds
Ok, my suggestions are in this color...
Macro-steps:
1. Chunk up the song into sections (usually verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge, etc.)
Suggestion:  Overall, the "lyrics + chords" section of your official tabs are kinda useless other than to screen-scrape for lyrics.  I need to screen-scrape because currently it rarely fits on one page, it doesn't say what lyrics have backing vocals, and the font is too small to read on-the-fly.
It would be super helpful if the lyrics were aligned to measures using 4 bars per line...no exceptions.
What I need is a proper "band chart."  I end up having to do these by hand for my bands and they take hours away from time on my instrument.  A band chart is like a lead sheet but more structure and without the melody.  It fits on 1 page.  Going from top-down and left-right it has...
Name of song and artist
Tempo and groove (swung 8ths, "shuffle" etc.) (optionally you can put the main drum beat [groove] and main guitar strum in TUBS (time box))
Key and original key (we transpose to match our singer's range)
A one-line statement summarizing the song structure:  ("3-pass Verse-Chorus:  Intro + Verse-Chorus + Interlude + Verse-Chorus + Bridge + Verse-Chorus + Chorus + Outro")
The chord charts for each section in the order  you encounter them in the song.
Please please please...4 bars per line no exceptions and nothing silly, old-fashioned, and awkward like codas.
What chord to end on and how to end (choked, let ring, etc.)
Suggestion:  Get very consistent and hyper-militant about section names.  You cannot imagine the time wasted during rehearsal trying to figure out where to start in the middle of a song.  Or when someone is lost and does something in the wrong place (ahem, singer).  Gawd.
Refrain = repeated section of a song.  Not a chorus.  Doesn't mention the title.  May/may not have lyrics.  Often the hook.  The "Nah nahs" of J. Giles "Centerfold" is a refrain
Chorus = a refrain that mentions the song title.  Often has backing vocals
Interlude = a small section that joins two other sections of a song.  Often variable (i.e. keep the bar-counts in the verses and choruses consistent and vary the interlude
Bridge = a very different section from the verse or chorus.  A "B" section.  Different than an interlude in that it is providing musical contrast rather than joining sections.  Often 8 bars or longer
Pre-chorus = optional section between the verse and chorus that either bridges (very different) between the two or has lyrics that repeat less consistently than a chorus but more consistently than a verse.  Can be thought of as a refrain between the verse and the chorus
Verse = section of lyrics that is different each pass through (unless the songwriter is lazy and chooses to repeat lyrics for the last verse).
"as" = When a section does double-duty.  For example, "Refrain as Intro."  Or,  "Chorus as Outro."
"over" = what section the solo is performed over.  For example, "Solo over Verse."  Or, "Solo over Bridge."
Intro = first section of the song.  Usually never repeated (otherwise it would be something like a "Refrain as Intro.")
Outro = last section of the song.  Usually never repeated (Suffragette City has "Bridge as Outro.")
I am okay with 2 strategies here...
The verse-chorus strategy
The A-B strategy (Badfinger's "No Matter What" seems better suited for an A-B strategy)
Please, please, a 12-bar Blues is simply chorus+chorus+chorus. That is the convention.  Why do people (seemingly always formally trained Brits) try to force-fit a verse-chorus structure on the Blues?)
2. Work-up each section
(I can do this on your website already, thank you.
What I need is 4-bars per line, no exceptions
.  With screens in landscape mode this should be easily achievable.  Remove everything on either side of the frame and place them above or below.  I also need to be able to see multiple tracks on the screen.  Or at least 2...the track that I have selected to learn and the track that has the chord names.  Bonus would be to have the 4-bar line I am currently playing and the next 4-bar line coming up.)
3. Work-up "transitions" between sections (usually by taking 1-2 bars on either side of a section.  For example, the last 2 bars of the verse and the first 2 bars of the chorus)
(I can do this on your website already, thank you.)
4. Work-up the entire song (play the entire song)
(I can do this on your website already, thank you.)
Meso-steps:
1. Strike the rhythm on muted strings.  Work-up to tempo,.
(I can do this on your website already, thank you.)
2. Work out the notes and fingerings. Sometimes I divide picking hand and fretting hand individually before trying them together...if the part is difficult.  This is untimed (no tempo)
(I sometimes think your fingering is questionable but this is a minor concern.)
3. Play along with the part (often with the other tracks muted)
(I can do this but it would be nice if somehow the site could both remember past mute/solo/volume selections I have made and quickly "reset" them to default.)
4. Play against the other tracks (with my part muted...usually just drums and bass)
(I can do this but it would be nice if somehow the site could both remember past mute/solo/volume selections I have made and quickly "reset" them to default.)
5. Play along with the studio recording (to mimic the "touch" and "feel")
(Being able to stream and slow-down like Amazing Slow Downer but honoring the royalties of a streaming website...that would be, um, amazing.  If you could replicate Riffstation's attempt at chords on top of this...it would be nirvana.)
Micro-steps:
(This is where I think your website really really comes up short.)
The tempo slider is super difficult to use.  Too sensitive
The tempo slider is not in percentage
The tempo slider doesn't have a +/- BPM option
I don't have the option to have 2 bar countdown
I don't have the option to have a countdown in between loops (very important if you are looping things in-between bars like solo phrases)
I don't have the option to increase tempo or stop after a certain number of times.  In Guitar Pro, I set the tempo increase increment to something ridiculous like +40% to signal that I have gone through 8 times.  Or I set it to increase 10% after 4 times.)
1. Play successfully at 50% tempo (or -50 BPM) 8 times in a row

author: Phil Starr
text:
OK it hasn't happened yet but UG could become a victim of its own success.
I've noticed that the approval queue has gone down by 2000 this week but several hundred new submissions have been added over this time. I suspect that a million tabs aren't that far away.
Some Tabs have many versions (14 tabs for smoke on the water) most of these are wrong in some way.
There is clearly no way that UG staff or even volunteers could work through the 300,000+ tabs and clean them out so we need a fix so we can retain the best tabs (say no more than half a dozen versions of any song) and clear out the rubbish. We need choice but there is no need to waste memory and bandwidth and the time of users on completely dumb tabs. Somewhere there is a balance.
The most useful information are the user ratings but most people are not rating. I've had 500+ hits on my tabs and no ratings at all. If we could get the ratings level up to say 5% thenwe would have much more data to work on. Anything with say, ten ratings which is two points behind the second best version could then be removed automatically. The more ratings we get the easier it is for users to find a good un and the easier it is to manage the site.
Couldn't we do more to encourage ratings. Printing off a copy means you are more than just browsing so putting a reminder to rate on the printed version might help. Pop ups could be used to remind people to rate. An email to newly registered users could contain encouragement to rate. Giving UG points to people who rate might be useful encouragement or even just putting the number of ratings on their profile might help. Some articles and stickies could be added too.
If we really wanted to increase ratings we could record who prints and ask them directly to rate a week later when they have had a chance to play the song.

author: pAmpH

Firstly, if this has been suggested before, I'll get rid of it...
I've seen on a few websites that they have what are known as 'buddies' who's job it is to guide new users of the website around and get them familliar with it's users/sections/forums etc.
I thought that with UG's very large number of users and the rate of new users registering that maybe we could incorporate this somehow...
Some suggestions of how this could work:
* In the 'New Members Q&A Forum' we put a stickied thread in there explaining the buddy system.
* Potential buddies put their name in there and when a new user comes along and wants a buddy, they get assigned one from the list of volunteers.
* To make it fair, only one person per buddy. To see who has a buddy, both buddies would need to indicate some way through their signature that they are taken and who is their buddy.
* This could also be a way of new users to become 'initiated' into the website alot easier and to meet some new people and make some new friends.
I don't know if it would work or how successfull it would be, but we could only try it out I guess. I'd be very willing to try and organize it, but if there's a better person for the job, by all means.
Thanks

author: MazeDaBaze
text:
Hi!
I must say that I don't understand the UG policy in regard to Guitar Pro files. I know, that many other people don't either, and I've read a couple of threads about this in order to try to understand UG's point of view. But anyway I still don't understand it, since what I've read so far is not logical ... maybe there are any other reasons which UG doesn't publicly talk about - but if there aren't, then I'd like to make a concrete suggestion.
First of all, what I understood about UG's point of view is, that the Guitar Pro files shall serve the opportunity for each musician to chose his specific instrument from the file. And I think that we all agree that this is a great opportunity. Plus there are more specific opportunities (listening options, playback options, editing options for personal needs like simplyfiing some riffs and many more), which we all will most probably agree upon.
So I think that the opportunities are not the point of the discussion: the more complete they are, the better it is - we all agree.
My considerations are more about how Guitar Pro files are developped:
1. There are simply not many people existing who are able to tab different instruments.
2. For those, who are able, it would still take a huge amount of time to make the files with all instruments. Mainly professional musicians would be able to do it, but I guess that those are not willing to spend their spare time with tabbing for the UG community - that's just not UG's tabber target group, right?
3. Me at least, I will never be able to tab other instuments than mine. But on the other side, I would hate to tab out my instrument within the currently existing options, which I perceive as very inconvenient (and which also would let me produce different kinds of tabbing mistakes which I could avoid by tabbing in GP).
4. And btw: Having more Guitar Pro Files would also mean having more Tab Pro Files, which would most probably raise the number of UG premium members, wouldn't it?
5.
Conclusion
: Having more GP files on UG would be good for UG as well as for the users - Win-Win - but that will simply NOT significantly happen with the current GP policy.
So how about an approach like this:
You could add the following upload options: GP Lead Guitar, GP Rhythm Guitar, GP Bass, GP Drums, GP Keyboards, GP Trumpet and so on.
So single tracks could - explicitly marked as single tracks - be uploaded to the database.
It's still MUCH better for musicians to have a single track GP file and/or a single track Tab Pro, than having no GP/TP for those songs at all.
Hm ... am I wrong?
And finally: If different GP single tracks would exist, then one day there would also come along a tabber who would be willing to merge those.

author: MazeDaBaze
text:
Hi
evfidripiy
,
h0spid
,
NSpen1
,
anderssoncaro
,
constantinebass
