I'm sorry to re-open this discussion, but I just had an idea, which I'd really like to add.
While the problem was so far, that only people could submit a GP file, which were able to tab several instruments, now the problem is, that only people can submit one, which can tab at least the guitar. Others have to wait now to tab a specific song in GP, until a guitarist likes that song enough to tab it out, and only then they can add their other instrument, Right?
So how about this:
1) As long as there doesn't exist a GP file in the database for that specific song in that specific version (e.g. album version from the album xy), each instrument of the original version can be submitted as a single track.
2) As soon as that specific song in that specific version already exists in the databse (= as soon as the first track of whichever instrument has been submitted), other instruments can only be added to that file.
Note: The adding would have to be an explicitly wanted behaviour, in my opinion, because
a) otherwise a second instrumentalist might hesitate to take the work from someone else as the base of his own work (he might consider that as respectless towards the first tabber).
b) the first instrumentalist knows already when he submits, that his work might be taken from others to be expanded.
3) The explicit goal in regard to GP files would be to finally get accurate (no individual interpretations or such) and complete multi-instrumental transcriptions.
4) Submitted GP files must clearly point out, which version they transcribe (e.g. "Album version from their 1996 album xy"), to be approved (just Youtube links or something like this would not be sufficient, cause Youtube videos might disappear later).
5) Submitted GP files must be absolutely correct in regard to the structure information: the number of bars, the time signatures and whatever else is needed (e.g. swing feel in case) for making sure, that other tabbers can add their instruments properly.
6) Codas, repeats and such would not be allowed, because they are seldomly valuable for all instruments, which might get added later.
7) If a GP file already exists, which is wrong in regard to the aspects metioned in 5) and 6), then any single track can still be submitted (= jump back to step 1).
8) I also have an idea to even spice that up a little more, but I think that would be complicated again. Anyway, just to be mentioned:
Each track of the original song might get IP Points, but Guitar tracks might get the double amount of IP Points. I know, this would be difficult to detect, but maybe the person who approves the song, could manually record that somehow when he/she approves it.
9) In case, that rewarding an added track would be technically too difficult in general, it might be an alternative, that specificly guitar tracks would always be allowed as single track, even when another version already exists.
With or without 8) and 9): To get a complete GP file finally, a starting point is needed. And if a song could be started with any instrument instead of only with the guitar, then
a) much more songs would get on the road and
b) all creative forces could start to work at the songs they prefer, unless having to wait for a guitarist with the same taste of music.
c) And last but not least, complete GPs could be generated in a pretty collaborative process.

author: DarthTyrannus83
text:
Quote by MazeDaBaze
1. There are simply not many people existing who are able to tab different instruments.
2. For those, who are able, it would still take a huge amount of time to make the files with all instruments. Mainly professional musicians would be able to do it, but I guess that those are not willing to spend their spare time with tabbing for the UG community - that's just not UG's tabber target group, right?
Oh please. Theres nothing difficult learning to tab other instruments. If youre a guitarist, you pretty much have the bass down as well (unless its a really technical band with different bass leads). The drums are probably the easiest to recognize sonically as you dont need to have an ear for music, just be able to recognize different cymbals and tell apart snare from kick lol. I know youre a basist, but imo using GP should evoke a desire to learn how to fully use it featues. You can even tab other instruments like piano/synths/wind instruments, etc, if the song parts arent too chord-oriented. All you do is find the notes on your preferred instrument, write it on the tab of the respective instrument in gp (GP7 has added tab editing feature for any instrument, so you can write on in a tab instead of sheet notation) and voila. If the instrument is out of the range of bass/guitar, you can use something like Transcribe! or any DAW to pitch-shift either the song track or your instrument signal to match the needed octave. Unfortunately, yes, writing a quality gp tabs is a lot of work, i wrote an article with some guidlenes as ive seen a lot of poor gp tabs over the years. But my point is, no you dont have to be a pro musician or have perfect pitch to be able to write decent quality gp tabs, all you need is dedication and tools (ie guitar, DAW/software, googling live videos, interviews, etc). Also, writing tabs really trains your ears for better note recognition with time so it becomes easier the more you do it.
Regarding the IQ abuse, the only way i see it is not rewarding IQ for single track gp tabs and forcing them to be collaboration-free so that other users can add missing instruments. And when the tab is complete, ie includes at least the basic band setup of drums+guitar+bass, then each contributor + original submitter get a certain amount of IQ or something.

author: MazeDaBaze
text:
DarthTyrannus83
Hi Darth. I totally agree: The option to submit single tracks free of rewards and explicitly allowed to be copied (and if necessary modified) into other tabs - that would be the best solution (if technically possible), and I'd love this solution, as well as many others might also do, I guess.
Also thanks for letting me know about the new GP 7 options. I'll check out GP7 soon.
Anyway, in regard to how easy or how difficult it is to transcribe for other instruments than your own (and even totally leaving out the tremendous efficiency aspect of specialization here):
You know, I'm quite good in several kinds of sports. It's sooo easy to me to play a topspin in tennis very cross from the very right front of the net to the very left behind the net, for example. Can you do that, too? It's very easy! You just have to pull the racket quickly from the bottom to the top while you hit the ball.
So why do other people have so many problems playing a topspin at all? What the hell do other people find so difficult at this? - Well, I'm sure: They just don't want."
The way you talk about the transcribing subject, sounds to me - if I may say so, just to outline the clue of my argumentation - like some kind of music nerd. Just like mathematic or computer nerds also often are unable to take the perspective of "normal" fellows.
Everything that you have once learned is then easy to you - and before, it often seems to be an unclimbable mountain.
And even worse: Not many people find the power to try it anyway, to climb that mountain.
But if you build in some plateaus, where they can rest, then more people will definately try it. Well ok: at first they are happy enough to make it until the first plateau. But one day, they will also try to climb the second one. And so on ...
In my opinion, even single tracks in GP would be only a second plateau for many people: I experienced very very often, that other instrumentalists - even of much higher level than mine - feel unable to transcribe even their own instrument.
But btw, I think that personal tabs -  terrific idea! - could (expanded by good GP file editing options and some specific collaboration options, which will probably/hopefully also come at some time) serve as a first plateau.
Last but not least: Compare the number of Chord tabs and the number of GP tabs in the contribution list. The numbers speak for themselves, in my eyes.
And simply saying "people should ..." will not make people do ...
So in my eyes, finally we can ignore the facts or we can roll up our sleeves and plant plateaus for the people.
However, after exploring Personal Tabs, I'd like to add: I trust in the UG team meanwhile, that they'll also find a good solution for the single track issue.

text: I have been very frustrated by the fact that tabs don't link to the correct version of the video (particularly for acoustic renditions) because it is very helpful to be able to play along with the version intended by the tab author. One of the mods told me that the video links are auto-populated by YouTube so Ultimate Guitar has no control over what videos appear even if the link appears in the body of the tab or the detail fields we populate when we submit a tab. As a test, I saved a few of my approved tabs that have bad video links as personal versions and changed the song title to match the name of the YouTube video.  Making this change instantly results in the correct video appearing in the app or on the site. Since the tab moderators won't allow alternate titles (even if the alternate title is an official alternate title for an acoustic version that appears on the artist's CD...), I am wondering if there is a way for UG to add a field for "YouTube Video Name" and, if the tab author fills in that field, have that be the value that is fed to YouTube for creation of the video links instead of the "Song" field that contains the title.

I don't know if people here are familiar with it or not but a good percentage of forums out there incorporate some type of 'reputation' system, rep for short.
Basically, when you read someone's posts you can decide whether it's a good post (helpful, on-topic, smart or whatever) or a bad post (spam, useless, stupid).
Whenever someone gets a good review they get points added; points are taken away for bad reviews. A bar is shown under every user's name, location and avatar and it gets longer and shorter with better and worse reputations (if u get negative rep the bar becomes red and gets longer with more negative rep).
The more reputation a particular user has the more he can affect other user's reputations (referred to as 'Rep Power'). A user with negative rep has no rep power.
I don't know if UG has tried it before but, personally, I think this would work really well for us.
Consider it?

author: SFBay-James4
text:
Two ideas here.
First, canons (no, not "cannons").
A “canon” is the collection of works considered representative of a period or genre. The collected works of William Shakespeare, for instance, would be part of the canon of western literature.  We've all seen these "top 20/50/100" songs/solos of all time.  These are the first attempts at establishing a "canon."
If someone is new to guitar and want to learn "blues" or "blues rock," they would have no idea where to start.  A curated "canon" list would help them.  You could even crowdsource this by putting songs into some sort of listing platform for UG users to upvote or downvote a song's "Canonical" status.
However this leads to a problem fixed by the second idea...
That problem is, most likely, "Stairway" or "Hotel California" or "Jimi Hendrix" is way out-of-reach for many guitarists just starting out.  Furthermore, the current "difficulty" rating is highly highly subjective.
So the second idea is some sort of A.I. generated "difficulty" rating.  Basically a numerical score based on tempo, note values, length of solo parts, etc.,  Whatever...let the machine learning figure it out.
Here is an example.  A beginning guitarist wants to learn the Blues.  Certainly BB's "The Thrill is Gone," BB's "Rock Me Baby," and SRV's "Pride and Joy" would likely be in the Blues Canon.  However, starting that new guitarist on SRV (or Hotel California in the Rock Canon) will likely cause that guitarist to get frustrated and quit.  Even starting them on "The Thrill" might be too difficult (48 bar solo at the end anyone)?  But "Rock Me Baby" is a song that likely a beginner could tackle quickly and gain confidence and momentum.
So you have a "Blues Canon" (100 Blues "standards") sortable by difficulty rating.
Title / Artist / Difficulty
Rock Me Baby -- BB King --  3.9
The Thrill is Gone -- BB King -- 4.7

author: durga2112
text: I've been working on ordering a playlist in precisely the order I want to play it in - the perfect opening and closing songs, little themed mini-sets in the middle, etc. I had things looking pretty good, but then I wanted to do a quick check to make sure I didn't have too many songs from any one artist in there, so I sorted the playlist by artist. Now I'm unable to quickly put the playlist back in the order I originally had. It's only a small playlist of about 30 songs so this isn't the end of the world or anything, but I think it would be nice if the custom order of a playlist could be preserved somehow so that I could sort a playlist by song or artist and then go back to the order I had it in. For an example of how this works, just look at a Spotify playlist - if you click to sort it by, say, Artist, then clicking on Artist a second time sorts it in reverse order, and clicking it a third time puts the playlist back into whatever order you may have previously dragged and dropped the songs into.

author: durga2112
text:
Hi Murad,
Thank you for your response. This was done on the website, where there are handy buttons at the top of the playlist view to sort by either Artist or Song. So the steps are simply:

author: brettsanace
text:
I've noticed that a lot of strumming pattern submissions don't specify the song part. It should be made a mandatory field so that if a user tries to submit a pattern without completing the field they get a message saying "You must complete all fields" with the "Song part" field highlighted. It doesn't take much effort for a submitter to type "Intro" or "Verse" or "Chorus" or "Whole song". This would beneficial for users of the tabs and also make life easier for the people reviewing/approving the strumming patterns.
If you could do the above it would be great, but it would be even better if you could get the field to not accept an entry that starts with a numeral. For some reason people like putting  a line number as the song part. The field can't reject numerals completely as it sometimes necessary to enter say, "Verse 2" as the song part. The field just shouldn't start with a numeral.

author: brettsanace
text: Further to this, if making the field mandatory is a problem for all the existing patterns that don't have the field populated you can just auto-populate those fields with "Whole song" as that is what most people intended, and if it is wrong then eventually some user may post a correction (after all, power of the people is what UG relies upon).

author: NSpen1
text:
brettsanace
Not sure I agree with this, particularly about filling in existing patterns with "Whole Song", because often they're not intended to be that.  It's also easier sometimes to just leave the field blank and it should be obvious when you play the pattern, rather than trying to think of a description when it's the intro, part of the verse, a 4 bar interlude here, another 8 bars there, it's impossible to fit it all in the heading sometimes.
Would be nice to eliminate the people putting a line number as the song part though.  When I say "eliminate" I mean that practice ... I think.

author: brettsanace
text:
NSpen1
I only said to auto-populate if it was required to implement this change otherwise I'm fine with leaving the existing ones blank. If a pattern was used in the intro, part of the verse, a 4 bar interlude here, another 8 bars there, surely a description like "Main Pattern" or "Pattern 1" and "Pattern 2" if there are a couple, could be used. However these are exceptions, generally the patterns are for "Intro", "Verse", "Chorus", "Interlude", "Outro". If it applies to more than one then you can easily fit "Verse/Chorus" etc and if it starts incorporating more song parts than that, then that is when you are getting into "Whole song" or "Main pattern" descriptions. I know you always manage to put  a description into your fields and sometimes it is hard especially when you need to include instructions such as "X = Rest", but you always manage to do it, as do I, so I don't see why other people can't.

author: NSpen1
text:
brettsanace
I think I have done the odd one or two where there's been no description
, and something like I described might be a case where it's not played in enough of the song to qualify as the "Main Pattern".  But you're right that those would be a minority of cases so perhaps it is worth making it mandatory from now on - hopefully not affecting existing patterns.

author: Lardin
text: I guess it`s a good idea to include the function that makes mandatory to write at least "something" in that space. I don`t like the idea of giving limited options because it`s impossible to cover all the possible options in a single list, but forcing the submitters to write at least ("Main Pattern", "Whole Song", etc or whatever the submitter think serves as a guidance) would help the learners to understand a little bit better the intention of the submitted pattern. In general I think any written guidance may work best than just leaving the blank space, which only causes the listener to go through the song trying to figure out where did the submitter was based to suggest such pattern.

author: NSpen1
text:
Lardin
There's not really that much of a problem with it if people are submitting good patterns, I'd say 95% of the time when people leave it blank it's supposed to be either a general pattern for the whole song or it would be the pattern played right at the beginning of the song. author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by soulflyV
I understand if it's too much, too hard or too time consuming to add to the forums, but I've been thinking about this for a while now.
Thoughts?
i'm guessing the way it works:  the timestamp of the last post in the thread is what's used to sort the priority of the threads in the index.  so to defeat this for an individual post, it would require the timestamp to be a null, or a hidden flag to be set, either of which the application would see as a signal to use the timestamp from the previous post in the thread to determine thread's position in the index.  obviously, this would require a major-league vB hack to implement.
since hacks are reserved for critically important features (vB hacks can lead to lots of problems and lengthy debugging), it will be necessary to make a strong case for the need.  i can imagine a few cases where this feature might be useful, but i'd guess it's not all that important.

Is it just a good idea in theory, or will it float?

author: pian0_player
text: When I use the apps transposition feature it will use the chord A# when it should always be Bb.  A# only occurs in the key of C# major and should definitely not be the default.  C# major should be spelled as Db as well, as the key of C# major is obscure and rarely used.  Essentially 99% of the time the correct chord is Bb.  Please fix this, it is very annoying.  It should be applied to every chart on the app.  Thanks!

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
B major? F# major? Harmonic context dictates proper naming.
Ignorance is equally annoying.

author: pian0_player
text: So the vii half-diminished chord in B is A#, fine.  The III chord in F# major, fine.  The VI chord in D minor, not fine.  Be careful before you start labeling people as ignorant.  Both examples you cited are rare and do not negate the point.  The vast majority of the time the correct chord is Bb, so whoop dee do for you, you found two exceptions.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
cf.
It's not just A#, it's D#. Would you change all D#'s to Eb's?
It may be true that Bb would occur more often in flat keys, but it almost never appears as such in any key with sharps, even if it functions as a non-chord tone.
Solving "most" of a problem is nonproductive. The problem is so much deeper than you make it out to be, and a blanket statement will not help.

author: pian0_player
text:
I enjoy a good Dude quote as much as the next guy, so nice.  That being said, clearly I spoke hastily.  It is true that there are examples in complex keys where A# is used, the fact is those are somewhat rare and really beside the point.  Yes, Bb does not occur in # keys, of course not.  Diatonic keys do not have mixed accidentals with the exception of some altered minor keys.  In the # keys of G, D, A, E the pitch is A natural so it is not an issue.  In the key of B, it is far more likely to see a dominant F# major chord and not a diminished vii chord rooted in A#, especially considering that both the V and vii chords function interchangeably. This leaves the III chord in the fairly uncommon key of F# major which is the least commonly used chord in any key and the VI chord in C# major which 99% of the time is spelled as Db.  You would see an A# half diminished ii chord in G#m, A# fully diminished vii in Bm or the A# V chord in extremely rare key of D#m.  The key of A#m does not exist because it would require double accidentals in the key signature.  All of these are uncommon, especially in guitar charts.
In all fairness, I guess my original post should have instead said that the transposition function should use diatonic chords that exist in the key and not strange enharmonic spellings.  When I wrote the post I was reading a chart in F spelling the IV chord as A#, honestly that is just inexcusable.  I would think we would be on the same team here and not nitpicking the point with obscure examples.  I am hoping they will improve the app as I use it sometimes for gigs and often for teaching.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
For your first paragraph, the corollary is that keys with sharps will use sharp notes with marginal exception (augmented 6th chords, chromatic passages, etc.). You insist on discussing chords; however, the building blocks of chords are ultimately notes, of which your complaint is rightly about root notes of chords not being correctly named following transposition to keys with flats.
The root of the problem lies in the fact that chord charts do not encode metadata such as key into the system. Some of the tabmakers struggle with the concept of key as well and will thus mix sharps and flats.
This is what would have to happen:
1. The original tabmaker would need to identify the key.
2. For each instance of sharp/flat notes, the system would have to determine the function of the corresponding chord with respect to the governing tonal area (global tonic or local tonic, ie if there's a secondary dominant or other temporary tonicization).
3. Based on the determined function in 2, the system will output the name of the relevant chord.
(As you may have noticed, I have disregarded talk of transposition, because this is a task beyond just transposition discussion. However, in the case of transposition, you may want to add an extra step:
1a. When transposing to a new key X, the system should determine if X is more commonly named with sharps or flats. Output the more common name.
Example: transpose from D major up one half-step. The system determines that 3 (0 = C, 1 = C#/Db, ... t = A#/Bb, e = B) is more commonly known as Eb and outputs such.)
This is far more complex than you make it out to be. There are more pressing issues as well on the programmer side. Thus, I suggest that you let this go and either manually change this or treat this as a teachable moment or more for your students.
Incidentally, on many occasions, Frédéric Chopin would modulate between parallel keys, but change to the complementary accidental for ease of both notation and reading.

author: pian0_player
text:
So, basically you are saying that people who make charts for the site don't understand what the hell they are doing (no argument there), and that it would be impossible for the programmers to write a program that analyzes simple diatonic chord progressions in the correct key?  Wow, what a wondrous technological age we live in.
The reason I mention transpositions is because that is often where the problem happens.  When the chart is in G and uses C as the IV chord, it is not the fault of the transcriber when the program notates the IV chord as A# in F.  Its bad programming.
Also, I am well aware that Chopin, and other composers who were writing highly chromatic music, used enharmonic spellings and parallel keys for ease of notation.  Once again, that is completely beside the point.  I have tried to be civil, but you insist on being condescending, but Im done debating.  Feel free to have the last word, it seems quite important to you.

author: khalil1220
text: Well seeing as it is more or less a free site, with no cost to use the app, how much quality are you expecting? You can simply just adapt to it, because it's not like if you get used to reading A# in place of Bb it will diminish your reading skills, it just makes you have to think a little bit harder which can be beneficial. If you do any work as a studio musician it's not entirely uncommon to get music with mistakes in it. You don't just refuse to read it until it's changed instead you have to learn to read through the mistakes. If it's for a student or something you can either make a note at the top of the chart that A#=Bb or go through the chart and cross out all A#s and write Bb in its place. Anyway most of that is beside the point. Also just to note from my experience using Sibelius when ever you use the transpose feature it does not encounter this problem. But again for your sake that probably isn't to helpful because you'd have to make the chart first before being able to use the transpose feature and the time spent making the chart would take longer than going through a printed copy on this site and making changes. But point is the technology for smart transpositions is out there, just not for free.

author: NSpen1
text:
Well, for all guitar stuff tuned down a half step I've always seen it referred to as Eb, not D#.  e.g. Hendrix, early Van Halen, Yngwie Malmsteen, Guns n' Roses ...  You're tuning
down
from E so E > Eb, A > Ab, etc.  Also it's much easier to relate it to standard tuning when the letters for the strings are the same just with a flat added, rather than having it be a different letter + a sharp.
In what context would you rather call it D# than Eb?  When the guitar isn't the main instrument and you'd prefer to think of the song as being based off a D# for some reason?
I have to think that that would be a minority of cases compared to when it would make more sense to call it Eb.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
Quote by NSpen1
Well, for all guitar stuff tuned down a half step I've always seen it referred to as Eb, not D#.  e.g. Hendrix, early Van Halen, Yngwie Malmsteen, Guns n' Roses ...  You're tuning
down
from E so E > Eb, A > Ab, etc.  Also it's much easier to relate it to standard tuning when the letters for the strings are the same just with a flat added, rather than having it be a different letter + a sharp.
Difference in experience
In what context would you rather call it D# than Eb?  When the guitar isn't the main instrument and you'd prefer to think of the song as being based off a D# for some reason?
I have to think that that would be a minority of cases compared to when it would make more sense to call it Eb.
D#m F# B A# or Ebm Gb Cb Bb?
F# B C# D#m or Gb Cb Db Ebm?
C#m A F# G# or Dbm Bbb Gb Ab? (particularly relevant for drop C#)
G#m B E D# or Abm Cb Fb Eb?
I usually prefer flats too; however, context is everything. Flats will work better in the cases of Eb major, Bb major, Ab major, and Db major (and relative minors); however, that's just one side of the coin, unfortunately.

author: NSpen1
text:
NeoMvsEu
Possibly my experience might be more relevant to a guitar website?  I mean I've never seen a guitar mag or tab book write a song that's tuned a half-step down in D# rather than Eb.  Another point is that most guitar players if they're tuned down a half step, are not thinking of all notes / chords being Eb, D#, Ab or G#, you think "I'm playing in E or A or D, just tuned down a half step".  That's why professionally published guitar tab is written as if it's in E standard tuning even though the actual pitch is Eb.
ok, some keys work better with sharps and some with flats.
(D#m - 6 sharps, Ebm - 6 flats, basically that one's a draw, I'd still prefer Ebm in that case though.
F# major , Gb major - equal, 6 accidentals in both
C#m over Dbm, sure
and G#m over Abm)
Having said that, it seems you're coming at it more from a theoretical / chord tab point of view, whereas I'm more thinking about text tabs and applying the tuning to each line of tab.  In that case it really doesn't matter about what keys work best with the tuning.
The point above about naming of notes / chords versus actual pitch is like the chord naming in terms of shapes versus concert tuning as in this thread
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1715954
If half-step down tuning could be treated as a 'negative capo' then the need for determining between Eb and D# would be eliminated.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
From writing chord charts, diatonic chords:
D#m E#dim F# G#m A#m/A# B  C#
Ebm Fdim  Gb Abm Bbm/Bb Cb Db
It doesn't look that different, but considering that B (IV in F#, VI in D#m) is far more common than Fdim (iio in Ebm, viio in Gb), it's a lot more practical to write in sharps for that set of accidentals (but that doesn't stop me from hating F# major with a passion)
There are definitely chord submissions that are in other tunings, which is why it's unwise to disregard all of the cases in favor of tab completely. However, I definitely agree with C tuning, drop Bb, and, in the case of
this article
, it's really misleading to write an augmented third (F-A#) where any natural listener would hear a perfect fourth (F-Bb).
I think a compromise could be to rename the tunings we agree on and to agree to disagree on the others; otherwise, the negative capo sounds like an interesting idea, even though it might look non-intuitive to end users... which is another consideration

author: NSpen1
text:
Quote by NeoMvsEu
However, I definitely agree with C tuning, drop Bb, and, in the case of
this article
, it's really misleading to write an augmented third (F-A#) where any natural listener would hear a perfect fourth (F-Bb).
And absolutely agree with your reasoning re fourths.  They really should have called the 8th string E# to be consistent
There are definitely chord submissions that are in other tunings, which is why it's unwise to disregard all of the cases in favor of tab completely (....) I think a compromise could be to rename the tunings we agree on and to agree to disagree on the others; otherwise, the negative capo sounds like an interesting idea, even though it might look non-intuitive to end users... which is another consideration
I think looking at just chord charts it could go either way, no huge difference between sharps and flats.  But for guitar text tabs and from the point of view of how (most?) guitar players think I would strongly favour Eb (and even drop Db still, it relates to drop D the same way Eb does to E).
But that's JMO of course, and I guess it's not up to either you or I to decide so perhaps we could get some other people's thoughts on it or maybe discuss in another forum.
Eb tuning is the preferred nomenclature

the song uses a capo on the 3rd fret. The fret numbers are never relative to the capo, why is that? Since the capo is on the 3rd fret , song should start on the 10th fret, but the tabs say start on the 7th fret. Yes of course because of the capo, I get that. So I have to add 3 because of the capo, 7th fret, add 3=10th fret.Why do you have to do math with songs that have a capo? Why not just show the real fret number that should be played when using a capo as well as the open strings? I Fall Apart with capo should be, frets 10/8, then 8/7, then 6/5....Official I fall Apart TABS shows, 7/5, then 5/4, then 3/2....Add 3 to those because of capo and you get the real notes.Why not just show the real fret number on songs with a capo? Is it a music theory thing?
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/rory-gallagher/i-fall-apart-tabs-999295

author: NSpen1
text:
Quote by brianpond1
The fret numbers are never relative to the capo, why is that? Since the capo is on the 3rd fret , song should start on the 10th fret, but the tabs say start on the 7th fret.
No, the fret numbers are relative to the capo, that's exactly the point.  The fret numbers are 5, 7, 4, etc _relative_ to the capo.  The _absolute_ numbers would be 8, 10, 7.
Showing the absolute numbers along with open strings would not be right.  You would get chord shapes like x-10-8000, x87000, x65000 which don't make sense, compared to more easily identifiable Em, D and C chord type shapes, x75000, x54000, x32000.
I'm afraid this is just how tabs using a capo are written, relative to the capo, and I'd suggest getting used to it.  Addition isn't hard
and you'll soon be doing it without even really thinking about it.

author: mrmatt8111
text:
a.faretdinov
Aydar,
When I look at the transcriptions of songs on this site the rhythms are frequently notated in the most confusing manner so as to not be readable.  It appears as though the transcriptionist was only thinking about the playback of the part and not the readability.  Rhythms are frequently notated without any consideration of the rhythmic accents in the notation or any thought to the natural rhythmic grouping of the time signature.  Also sections are frequently labelled incorrectly, the terms verse, chorus, bridge, pre-chorus, pre verse (??), transition, "heavy riff" and whatever else  are thrown around on the page without any logic, without following any standard notational practices.  Or the sections arent labelled at all, making it difficult to determine where the verse, chorus or bridge are unless you take the time to listen to the song and label them yourself.  Also chords are frequently not lableled at all, right hand notation (pick strokes or finger picking notation) is completely wrong or ignored.  Chords are usually mislabled regarding their harmonic function within the context of the chord progression.  Those are the types of things I see all the time and it makes the product, the tablature, difficult to read without serious revision.  It's all very frustrating.

author: andrewtc4
text:
The notation style guide at
https://blogs.iu.edu/jsomcomposition/music-notation-style-guide/
gives a pretty good rundown of how to write proper rhythmic notation; see the sections on beaming and rhythm in particular. I found it in high school as someone dabbling in composition and arrangement, and I've used it since.
Looking at the UG tab guide, they seem to have some amount of code that does checks on submitted Pro tabs (guide section 4.2), so it seems reasonable to suppose that they could add code that would implement the rules in the notational guide linked above.

author: andrewtc4
text:
Also, the complete disregard for proper accidental usage, while understandable if were to happen occasionally—formal music theory is not something
everyone
studies, after all—makes me wonder who's selected for the transcription team. Key signatures are often wrong, and weird—often superfluous enharmonic—accidentals are everywhere. It's awful. There ought to be at least a few classically-trained people on the team to help make things follow notational conventions.

because we all know that theres nothing more frustrating than trying to play one of your favorite song but you cant get the tone just right
There are a ton of problems with this.  Different guitars will sound very different with the same pedals and amp.  So you basically have 3 variables that all have to match up for this to make any sense.  The same guitar/pickups, the same pedals, the same amp/cab.  That's not likely to happen.
Use a different guitar or a different pedal, and you might be able to get an acceptable tone for the song, but the settings to achieve that might be radically different.  Use the same guitar and pedals, but a different amp, and again the settings are likely to be radically different.
The chance of any of this info being useful to anyone is small, because of the difference in the equipment each of us uses.  It will just make a lot of clutter.

author: GuilliamXD
text:
Hey guys of UG, Tonebridge and users,
I just recently came up with a third-world problem: I can't seem to find a place where I can get good tones for my amp/effects processor and I am not able to figure out how to do it myself since I am unexperienced in this world. I currently own a BOSS GT-1000  amp/effects processor and I have been searching days and days for settings for certain songs but cant find anything. Then I thought about Tonebridge since this app provides real good patches for loads of songs. So with my 0 knowledge about these things I went searching if tonebridge was compatible with e.g. my effects processor. But I couldn't find anything so I went here and started to write this message.
The thing I want to say with this long and boring story is:
Is there a way you are able to get the power and simplicity of tonebridge and combine it with your amp/effects processor. What I mean by this is there a way you could connect the app with you processor and with one push of a button get these settings transported to your amp/effects processor. And if not possible could the developpers maybe try to get this feature. I think loads and loads of people would be helped with this and it would enrich this appa lot. I would love to hear your guys ideas and if the developpers of tonebridge read this their opinion about this little idea. Thanks!
UG Team
tigermetal

author: tigermetal
text:
GuilliamXD
hi, thanks for the question. Tonebridge uses its own preset technology under the hood, so it's not possible to use Tonebridge presets in other apps or amps. Why would you want it to work that way though? Why not just use Tonebridge app itself?

author: GuilliamXD
text:
tigermetal
Thanks for the answer. I basically wanted to work it this way since I love to play songs like  Sweet Child O'Mine with the most accurate sound. In my setup I use a Boss GT-1000 and I can't seem to find settings that sound accurate. So I hoped I would be able to get tonebridge sound function combined with my setup so I can click the button in tonebridge and get the sound blasting trough my amp. It might be able that I just don't know how to use the app properly so if that's the case would you be so kind to explain me how I could get this to work?

Hello,
You have 15 or so forums of fairly narrow scope, and then you have THE PIT, which seems to be the only place where anyone is invited to post questions which are too general for any of these other forums. Thank you for considering the above.

author: Paul Lambeth
text:
EDIT. Nuts, the title should probably be "Searching"; excuse that, I'm sure if you read it you'll know this has nothing to do with browsers
-------
I checked through the previously submitted suggestions and couldn't see this, so sorry if it's been suggested and I missed it.
Often, for bands such as Radiohead, Pink Floyd etc who have several hundred tabs, searching through these multiple pages is time-consuming. Equally irritating is searching for a song name which contains some or all of a very popular title, e.g. "Just" - especially if it's by a band with many tabs, "Just" by "Radiohead" gives you the choice of 6 or 13 pages to search through.
My suggestion is combining those search functions, "Band" and "Song", probably as two seperate drop-down boxes next to two relevant search bars.
https://img143.imageshack.us/my.php?image=songsearcheger0.png
(EDITED: image did not show)
^ That is an example. I don't know what program you run your database with, but with basic ones such as MS Access, it is possible to search in multiple criteria at once.
There are issues involved, such as confusion with new members should they wish to search Reviews but have Song search also open with criteria filled in.
To combat this, my other suggestion would be to have the options for one (visible) search drop-down menu as:
Song+Artist
---
News
Reviews
Columns
Lessons
Band Promos
---
Users
with a second search bar appearing if "Song and Artist" is selected, making the top box "Band" and the bottom "Artist". I hope you understand my explanation - multiple criteria function would only be available when required, e.g. specific song and artist.
Thanks for reading my suggestion.
Paul

author: Chaos Nil
text:
Giving personal rights to create the stickers would be a good idea really. I mean seriously, the only thing you really need is the User Agreement stating you will make no profit in the transfer of the stickers. That means that you can "Sell" them but without profit. In other words, you will have the person pay for the cost of the sticker (paper, ink, electricity, wear on printer, etc). In the end, everyone wins. UG gets free advertising, users get stickers at their own cost. UG would be the one making profit off the additional advertising from new users.
Edit: It should probably also state that the usage of the images for stickers can be taken away at any time and further distribution and production of such images cease. This would most likely be in the event that UG actually makes a store to sell stuff.

author: 199X
text:
I have been uploading bass tabs on this website for something like 7 years. My first tabs were pretty crummy but I over time I improved and I think I have a high accuracy rating for the stuff I do nowadays. I have contributed over 100 tabs to this site.
Recently, however, I keep getting comments telling me I need to change the way I write my tabs - which were fine for 7 years - and conform to a new set of standards that no-one told me previously existed. At the moment my tab for "No Plans For Tomorrow" by the Emotions, which took a good amount of time to write and is highly accurate, is stuck in the approval queue because it doesn't meet your standards.
Worse still, the standards are incomprehensible to me. I'm being told I have to put the tuning (E A D G) in front of *every* line of my tab. Not withstanding the fact that my tab editor does not provide this feature, meaning I would have to put every letter by hand, the fact is that I cannot imagine someone stupid enough to forget halfway through a song which way his bass should be tuned. On the precious few occasions when an alternative tuning
has
been required, I have made this known in the notes before the main body of the song.
Other standards, like putting headings in square brackets, seem arbitrary. The rule that all notes should be seperated by at least one "-" makes sense in theory, but for people like me who are used to interpreting the note duration by the distance between each note, it is a lot easier to speed read tabs that keep 16th notes right next to each other (as an example). I have always done this, but this too is now unacceptable apparently, to the point where people are clumsily editing my tabs themselves before they get approved.
I am really surprised and saddened by this desire for conformity from you Ultimate Guitar, your logo seems to suggest rebelliousness and music is such a creative endeavour that I think you would understand that (a)
tab writers each have their distinct way of presenting their work and that providing it is
understandable
, they should be allowed to express themselves
, and that (b)
WE ARE NOT YOUR FREAKING EMPLOYEES
. We give our tabs to you free of charge so that you can make $$$ off ad revenue. Many of us are talented enough that we could charge for our efforts, but we want to share the cool riffs and licks we hear in songs for everyone to enjoy. So please, don't patronise veteran tab writers but forcing them to conform to finicky and unnecessary rules!

author: LewtElune
text:
The rating system
The rating system for Tabs is not helpful at all. First of all the 3 star should be "Accurate" and the 4 "Worth learning", because if it's not accurate it's not worth learning...
My biggest issue with the rating system is there is a lot of 4/5 stars Tabs that are wrong.
Some of theme are very very wrong.
My suggestion to remedy (or at least improve) this would be to have rating from two different categories of members.
First category would be the "common" members who's musical knowledge or hear is not competent enough to judge the accuracy of a transcription.
Second category would be the "expert" members who by their training or passion or simply musical hear are able to rate the accuracy of transcriptions.
The ratings used by the first category would display as hollowed out stars and the second category as full stars.
This way people would know that the score obtained by the tab was based on appreciation or on accuracy.
I teach guitar and a lot of my students while looking for tabs have this issue and are learning inaccurate pieces because they thought that 33 5 stars rating meant it was good.
It's really a problem concerning beginers who's hears are not trained enough to be able to detect errors. Thus making learning guitar harder.
As for the expert status this could be granted either automatically after a certain numbers of contributions, or by putting together a test for them to complete.
The test could consists of a few randomly generated chord progressions. A few musical phrase to transcribe. And a few wrong melodies to correct. (Any of those should obviously not be from popular source that could be found elsewhere)
Clean up
As already discussed above UG is plagued by inaccurate 4/5 stars tabs as well as totally inaccurate rated lower or not. To those with good musical training or hears it's not difficult to see if a tab is wrong or not. However to the less trained it's difficult.
Sometimes there's song or music with 8 different versions and only 2 are accurate.
So adding a Recycle Bin button close to the rating "report for deletion" or something like that would be nice. Because so far all I is a small report icon and it doesn't really help because it's mostly here to correct errors.
The report for deletion tabs also could still remain accessible in the band/composer trash folder.
And only be moved there after a # (to be determined) report has been issued.
Or find another way to mark or get rid of those inaccurate Tabs.

author: kuschelschock
text:
Hi there! Not for the first time, I encountered the situation where a user submits more than one correction for the same song. The first one was approved - I approved the second one (not knowing about the first one) undoing the first correction. Thinking about, how to  prevent this in the future, I thought it might be a nice feature to see if there are other pending corrections to this very same song - maybe even a list of the past ones (approved or not).
Greetings
Andy

author: NSpen1
text:
kuschelschock
Yep, in that case the first one had just been approved so you wouldn't have seen it in the queue, so a list / link to past corrections could help.

author: thequadrat
text:
NSpen1
kuschelschock
what if there are two corrections for the same song but different authors and different changes?

author: NSpen1
text:
thequadrat
If one is obviously wrong, reject that one and leave the better looking correction to be judged.  If they both look like they could be valid, reject the later submitted one and tell the submitter of that one to wait their turn.  This is only a general guide and you'd have to take it on a case by case basis; maybe there's a small lyrics correction for instance and you could approve that and then incorporate that change into the other correction.  Of course that's only for mods who can edit.
(This could also apply to some extent when there are two corrections from the same author but with different changes.)

author: thequadrat
text:
NSpen1
seems a bit overcomplicated since you need to check different parts and click many times (it's in terms of UI). But it sounds nice to have an ability to track TPA similarities in one place on the tab page.
By the way, how do you think how many cases like these could appear daily/weekly?

author: kuschelschock
text:
thequadrat
NSpen1
Why allow multiple corrections to one song at all? If there is a correction pending, ckicking the "Suggest correction" button could show a popup like "Sorry - another correction to this song is currently pending. Do you want to get a message / notification when this is approved / rejected. Yes/No".
Nevertheless, a history of past corrections (approved or not) would be benificial anyways.

author: NSpen1
text:
thequadrat
Yeah, it doesn't bother me too much though, if I see there are two corrections for the same song in the queue I just open them both and assess, hopefully quickly, which is the more valuable correction.
It's a bit hard to say how many of this type of correction there are because there are different subtypes -
Two corrections for the same song but different authors - fairly rare except when you get a case with a user like calebstrovas recently who sees corrections in the queue and decides to submit his own for the same tabs
(He was looking at the tabs with strumming pattern submissions and then submitting corrections to those tabs for minor formatting things mostly.)
Two corrections for the same song by the same author - this is quite common so that we frequently have to tell people "only submit one correction at a time", "please edit your first correction", or edit some changes in to another correction for them.
There are also still some spam strumming pattern submissions, where the same bad pattern, or ones with small changes but still all bad are submitted multiple times. 2, 4, up to 7 at a time recently.
So it could well be a good idea as
kuschelschock
says, to not allow any multiple corrections to be submitted.

author: NSpen1
text:
Just had 4 corrections from an unregistered user for the same tab, all changing different things, not gonna sort through that mess.  So yeah, don't let multiple corrections be submitted!  Also how about a notice when you submit a correction saying please make sure to put all your proposed changes in one correction, and edit if you need to add any more?
Oh, and just adding this thing again which has been mentioned before, change the wording from "suggest correction" because still a lot of people think that's all you have to do, suggest it, not actually make the changes to the tab yourself.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
Three things:
- There are crappy old tabs. We don't deny that.
- New tab versions should be both better and friendly to all users, not just experienced musicians. Some beginners have to have chords above all lyrics, even if repeated.
- The Auto-Scroll feature basically necessitates the writing of all chords. Off-site is fair game, but this is UG's system, not yours.
We've tightened the reins on formatting because we want to be user-friendly, not ego-friendly. If your tabs were only rejected for that reason, surely you both can suck it up, appeal, and make the proper changes. It's nothing personal.

author: Roc8995
text:
I don't see any major utility in making this change. Most news articles don't get enough comments for this to be an issue, and if there's really that much to be discussed on a news article, maybe it should be done on the forums instead, where there's a better infrastructure for dialogue. The whole point of news article comments is to get quick reactions to the news as it's released, so there's not really a lot of value in putting someone's comment at the top just because they typed it out three days after everyone else stopped commenting or reading.
If anything it would make some sense to sort by the thumbs up/down score. But sorting newest at the top doesn't seem like a beneficial change.

The reason why it includes "gunshot" but not mandolin is because General MIDI includes specific sounds.  So these are the "instruments" in General MIDI and therefore you're searching by the voice that is selected:
There is no mandolin in GM because so steel string acoustic guitar sound is typically used for playback since it sounds closest to mandolin.

From what I have been able to find in January 2020,
-There is no API for ultimate-guitar, nor are there any plans to implement one
-There are a couple of scrapers for the site on Github that essentially acted like an API, but they have all been shut down by ultimate-guitar
-Ultimate-guitar pays for the rights to the chords/tabs on its site using advertising and subscription revenue
-They say the record companies would come after somebody for creating a program that would distribute the tabs for free
https://github.com/masterT/ultimate-guitar-scraper
This link has a copy of the email from ultimate-guitar explaining the problem. So it seems like, because of the music industry, there is no legal way to connect an application to ultimate-guitar

Ximich
I think perhaps you are not understanding what I would like and I suspect what other users would like. Your users playlist data stored on your servers is surely the property of UG if not it would be a good idea to disclose that to your users.
The API in question, I don't want it for FREE... I am a paid member so if you pay the idea is you would get an API key to get access to the API to only manipulate your data (aka playlists). The token would allow you to audit, throttle and potentially limit the number of requests sent to your servers.
Simply put I had hoped for a way to allow me to more easily manage my ultimate guitar playlists via a restful API as I have some programming skills. I just thought you would have already had a restful API in place and be using it for the website and mobile application and been so kind as to expose some of it to your customers.
You wouldn't need to give us copyright content to do that just allow us to search your catalog via some filters just like we do via a website search. Using the identifier for the tab item we could then add it to the playlist.
The MovieDB has a nice API that demonstrates how this could work -
https://www.themoviedb.org/documentation/api
In regards to legality Spotify has a developer API and would have much the same legal restriction yet still manage to give developers access to a restful API to build experiences on top of their platform.
Hopefully something you can provide moving forward. I am sure there are ways to provide this without infringing on publishers copyright.

author: mikeryan776
text:
As darktemplaau1 said, there's no legal or technical reason an authenticated API can't be implemented that only provides users access to content they're entitled to. And the initial response that "ultimate-guitar.com is written in PHP" isn't at all a barrier - I'm a PHP developer and have implemented APIs myself, there are plenty of open-source frameworks and libraries to do most of the heavy lifting.
Here's my use case - like I'm sure many musicians, I've got Spotify playlists of songs I'm working on, UG playlists corresponding to them, MuseScore files for originals and my own arrangements of covers, GarageBand files of my recordings, etc. I'm starting to try to put together a POC of an app that would help organize all this - for whatever song in my repertoire (or songs I aspire to add), in one place link to all my associated resources regardless of what type or platform they are. Probably a bit ambitious for a solo developer, but that's what the POC is for - to gauge the scope.
Anyway, I understand that you need to prioritize your efforts, and that you're not going to invest the time and effort into developing an API without a good sense of the benefits. If you do comes around to that conclusion - I'd be happy to contract to help with the development!
Thanks.

Interesting idea, man.  Dunno if it'll fly, but it would fix a few problems.
I think this is a good idea.
What I believe would have to be done:
- The subforum would have all the ONLY Threads contained within them.
- Regular users would not be allowed to make new threads, but still retain the ability to post IN the threads. (as you stated)
- Mods could move threads/make new threads and other modly business that needs to be done (as you also stated)
- All threads would have to be on the one page (otherwise you get lazy people saying, "I checked the ONLY forum and it wasn't there" where checking = scrolling down the first page, as it is with "checking" the searchbar)
- When posting a thread in the Pit, there would be a box to tick that confirmed that "I have checked the ONLY Forum before posting", which has been falsely ticked (which would be picked up by users and then reported, or even mods themselves trawling the Pit every now and then) would result in the thread being closed and a warning given to the TS.
I think this would definitely make people think twice about starting a thread. (I believe this would be the only forum that the ONLY forum would apply to, as the other forums work well with a few stickies)
- AeroRocker's idea is good, but would be redundant if the hypothetical "ONLY" Forum became a sub-forum of the Pit, as it would be displayed as a link box as the Songwriting Competitions and such threads are displayed in their parent forums.
If the "ONLY" Forum were to be a separate entity, then a button such as the one AeroRocker posted before would need to be placed at the top of the Pit, in place of the new thread button, but move the new thread button to over to the right. This would help with the visibility of the link as people look to the top left hand corner of a page more than anywhere else when looking at a page [studies have proven this, cbf looking them up right now though, but read any book for evidence
].
Extras:
- Maybe an off-topic thread: "The ONLY Off-Topic Chat Thread"?, just to give the forum a community feel, which might reduce the amount of off-topic discussion going on in other threads which would drag attention from actual inquiries and questions that so often "go unanswered".
I realise that some/many of these ideas are not viable as they would require hacks or extensive amounts of work (which I gather the Russians are not fond of
), but this is what I believe would have to be done or at the very least considered before a this hypothetical sub-forum came into being.

And like I've pointed out in this thread already, the guy that's been making the majority of the offensive posts has been doing this for months, just making new accounts under different IP addresses. author: McGryphon
text:
You're asking for the impossible: running a forum on two versions of the forum version itself at the same time. To do that, you'd have to run them both separately, which doubles to triples the load on your servers. Also, you'd have to come up with a solution to make any replies visible in both versions; this is essentially the same as posting it on two seperate forums, as that's what they'll be. There's no feasible way to realize what you're suggesting, the closest one might come is add the features you describe to the forum later on. Even then, you'd need a few highly skilled developers to integrate everything, and it would most likely have an impact on the speed, one of the biggest reasons to stay with an older version of vBulletin.
I don't know what sort of hardware is used to host the site, but if it's up to dat maybe switching to React instead of vBulletin might yield the mixture of features and speed you're asking for. I'm routinely seen on another forum, somewhat bigger than this one, which runs on React. It's at least as fast as this one, and it's a lot easier to customize in my opinion.

author: Roc8995
text:
Hi all,
Here's an update on the situation.
Given Tom Hess' previous abuse of our system, and because he made several shill accounts to do so, he's been banned forever from the forums and comments.
However, since articles may be submitted by email, it is possible that you may see other articles from him in the future. They will not be the same promotional articles, though.
We've talked with the articles and content editors, and they've agreed to be much more discerning in the kind of content that is allowed on the articles. Articles that serve primarily as self-promotion, or that link too heavily to the author's site, will be declined or the links pared down. Something really important that came up when we were talking with content admins is that we don't have enough good content to work with; to this end,
please consider writing and submitting articles.
The more good content we have, the easier it will become to decline lesser articles.
Thanks for your patience on this issue. I think the new article policies are going to be much better. If you're interested, here are the specific actions that the editorial staff have committed to:
- Double-check the content which we receive for Lessons and Columns
- Throw out obvious infomercials
- If an article is more or less informerical, but still contains valuable info, reduce the advertising aspect only to a small sentence with single link to author's resource
- Contact talented UG writers (if their articles are being really enjoyed by audience) for closer collaboration

author: James Scott
text:
As one of the more regular article writers here at UG, can I make a couple of requests in light of this?
Firstly, can UG publish a precise set of article guidelines for contributors? I know there are already some guidelines, but what we need are some very specific instructions on:
-what can be linked to
-precisely how many links per article are permitted to:
a) the author's own site
b) other UG articles the author has written in the past
c) links to third party sites
d) where images etc should be hosted and how to link to them
-what constitutes too much self-promotion/sales
-what is/isn't ok in an "about the author" section
That way I, and other contributors, will be able to get articles right first time out, reducing the workload on the moderators and getting better quality articles out there.
Secondly, if a submitted article doesn't match up with the policy, please could it be rejected and sent back to the contributor rather than put up in edited form. Once or twice I've had articles put up in an edited form that stopped the article from making sense or being as useful as it could be. I would much rather take an article back and submit a new version that complied with the rules than have a broken article end up on the front page, and I'm sure that UG's readers would too.

author: Hydra150
text:
warning, sort-of-unrelated wall of text incoming;
Quote by Cavalcade
This. There's little to no oversight on user-submitted content, other than basic formatting, which the submitter should be able to handle themselves.
Not entirely related to the topic at hand, but I've said this in the comments section of a few lessons which had taught dubious music theory - music theory articles should be read over by someone who knows what they're talking about
before
they're posted onto the front page.
Now don't get me wrong, I appreciate that regular users on this site are contributing original content rather than just complaining about it (guilty as charged), I'm grateful for their efforts, although sometimes lessons read like a sounding board for half baked ideas, or do more harm than good - with users coming to the Musicians Talk forum confused by what they read in these lessons (normally in the case of articles with 'modes' in the title).
Several times I and other users have, in the comments sections, ended up educating the author of the lesson on the very subject that they tried to teach about  (and sometimes they are even grateful). The quality control for these types of lessons isn't great, and I guess that's understandable if it's a technical subject that whoever checks the articles isn't knowledgeable of.
But there seems to be a simple solution to this - there are regulars on the forums who
are
very knowledgeable about all things music theory, and I'm sure some of em would be happy to help. The Musicians Talk mods themselves are both knowledgeable and eloquent on the subject, and they will know which regulars are smart and can be trusted to read over and advise/amend submitted articles. Outsource the quality control to the know-it-alls.
The same idea would work for lessons discussing the purview of the Guitar Techniques forum and maybe others - then you'll have regulars helping with lessons rather than poking flaws in them.
Obviously that idea is not relevant to articles posted by the likes of Tom Hess and other professionals, some of whom reek of arrogance, but more for the regular UGer who wants to contribute.

author: brettsanace
text:
alatiel321
As UG seem to be intent on continuing to experiment with this new feature, here is my constructive feedback.
Issues
Default View - The default view should always be Versions. It seems this is half fixed now and I'm sure UG will be easily able to remedy this.
Irrelevant Content - People don't look at a tab and want to see suggestions for random songs that they are not interested in even if they are the most popular songs on the site.We already have the "Recommended For You" section on the home page which fulfills this role.
What Might Users Want
Without having conducted any detailed research it seems to me that if a user is looking at a particular tab then they probably like:
The Song - If that is the case then they will likely be interested in more tab versions of the song.
The Artist - Then they may interested in tabs for other songs by the same artist
The Author - They might like the tab author because they always do accurate tabs, or easy tabs for beginners, or tabs songs that the user likes, or they are a friend.
Suggestion
Rather than have More Tabs populated by tabs that are irrelevant to the user make the section something like:
MORE TABS
Versions Artist Author
Versions should always be the default but the user should be able to select Artist or Author if they want.
"Versions" would operate as it does now. If the user selects "Artist" then provide them a list of random or most popular (viewed/rated) tabs by that artist. If they select "Author" provide them a list of random or most popular (viewed/rated) tabs by that author.
Of course users can do all this (find songs for artists and authors by other means), but if UG is going to continue with this feature then it may as well be relevant to what the user is actually interested in.

Hey,
This isn't really a bug, more an annoying flaw in PM functionality. When you send a PM to a user whose PM inbox is full, you'll get a notification saying that the user couldn't receive the PM. Now, the problem is that at this point, the PM you typed up is completely lost. The message isn't saved in the Sent Items folder (since it's not sent), and there's no way to go "back" to the PM editor and retrieve the message. Kind of annoying, especially if you typed up a wall of text and then lose it all because the receiver has a full inbox. (I had this problem some time ago. Damn you CoreysMonster!)
Can this be fixed somehow? Maybe make a "draft" folder for messages, and let messages that are unsuccesfully sent automatically be saved to that folder? Or provide a "go back" button when you get the "failed to deliver" notification?
Cheers!
PS: I know I could've saved my PM to Notepad before sending, or something. I would have, if I knew the problem existed. I still think it's a problem worth fixing.

author: djerzinski
text:
Why is it not a thing, either as a feature, or as an understanding among UG users.
Let me explain:
On this site, it is a fact that Guitar Pro tabs are rated not for the guitar transcription accuracy but for its likeness to the original song, which includes all instruments, the structures correctly reproduced, etc. If someone post a GP tab with just the guitar part, it will trashed by visitors even if the guitar transcription is perfectly OK.
The silly solution against this is bouncing your guitar pro file to text and post it as a text tab, so it is understood it's just a guitar transcription, which is a little lame, you lose convenience and information for bad reasons.
My point is that it would be good if UG implemented an intermediate system for people who got interesting stuff but don't want to spend two hours transcribing instruments they don't play, just for internet points. Like, make tabs with just elements of a song (main riff, verse) a thing (you figure out the rest yourself).
Personally, I got tons of rare, accurate and interesting (I believe) tabs on my hard drive. You can check my profile, I used to upload stuff here ten years ago, but stopped for these reason, incomplete GP tabs and utterly entitled visitors (bro, it doesn't make a difference for me if I share it or not, so I won't).
Sometimes, I find wildly inaccurate tabs (happened not later than this morning), fix everything in 20 minutes, but just keep it because it's such a pain to shape it to the standard.

author: djerzinski
text:
a.faretdinov
It's not exactly a problem, it's more about convenience for people who transcribe tablatures and how things work in the transciption world.
Transcribing the main riffs of a song: 20 minutes max if you have a good ear (and it will get you a one star, no matter how good you did).
Transcribing every guitar parts and giving the structure to the tab: from 30 to 2+ hours depending on the complexity of the song (same)
Transcribing the whole thing (the only thing that will get you a good rating, supposing we care about this): same 30min/2h each time for the bass, drums, keys, etc.
20 min vs. 6+ hours is a big gap for someone who wanna share info for free to complete strangers without any compensation (more likely to get negative feedback actually).
On a related issue, letting people pick up where other people left, in a more formal manner, would be cool too.

author: h0spid
text:
Welcome to all Personal tabs beta testing participants
This page contains more information about beta testing itself and about Personal tabs feature as well as F.A.Q. about it.
Please note:
Personal tabs feature is available only for Ultimate-Guitar.com website at the moment, but for both desktop and mobile versions -- so you could create your tab from desktop and access it from mobile version of the website as well. Later this year feature will be implemented to current UG apps on iOS and Android as well.
The goal of this beta testing is to provide you an early access to the Personal tabs feature that will be available later for all Ultimate Guitar users and get as much feedback from you as you could provide:
- whether you like it general
- whether it's easy and obvious how it works
- whether you faced with any bugs or issues
- whether there is something unclear for you
- whether it's comfortable to view Personal tabs from mobile devices
- etc
So feel free to use green "Feedback" button located on the right side of any page and write all your ideas and thoughts -- you can use it as many times as you want. The more feedback we receive, the more helpful will be for us.
You could also ask your questions and provide any feedback you want at this page using the post reply below.
At the end of the beta testing we'll also send you a small survey to get more general feedback from you, but for now please use instant feedback form: green button at the right side of any page or this page (you have link to it in Facebook).
P.S. If you don't have an access to Personal tabs beta testing, but want to -- just post a comment below and we'll provide you access!
About Personal tabs
Personal tabs are a great way to create and store your tab collection in the cloud, where only you can see it. You can view and edit your collection from any device, view chord diagrams, edit text tabs, create strumming patterns and use various tools such as transposing, auto-scroll, and playback (for Guitar Pro and Power tabs).
We know that a lot of Ultimate Guitar users store their tab collections in text files or through cloud storage services such as Google Drive or Dropbox. However, none of these services were made specially for tabs, so the possibilities there are quite restricted.
By creating and saving tabs on Ultimate Guitar you get all the advantages of cloud storage-like access to your tabs from any device and also special tools for tabs and chords such as the ability to view chord diagrams, auto-scroll, transposing, annotations, and playback (for Guitar Pro and Power Tabs).
Key Personal tabs features include:
- Special tab submission form that will help you create tabs faster in the most convenient way.
- Drafts: No matter how long you’ve been creating your tab, it will always be preserved.
- Cloud: After creating a personal tab you can access it from any device connected to the Internet. Later, Personal tabs will be available in existing Ultimate Guitar apps for iOS and Android (even offline).
- Tools that help you with tabs: chord diagrams, auto-scroll, strumming patterns, transposing, revisions, printing, etc.
So to create your first personal tab, press the
Submit tab
link located on every Ultimate Guitar page, make a tab and then press the ‘Save as personal tab’ button. It will be available only for you as a part of your personal collection.
F.A.Q.
What is a personal tab?
A personal tab is a tab that was created on Ultimate Guitar and is available only to you and those who you shared it with. All the features that are available for public tabs, such as editing, drafts, auto-scroll, transposing, etc. are available for personal tabs as well.
How to create a personal tab?
To create a personal tab, just click the
Submit tab
link on any
Ultimate-Guitar.com
page. The link is located to the right of the search field. After creating a tab, press the ‘Save as personal tab’ button.
How to create a personal tab from a tab published on UG?
Click ‘Save as a personal tab’ button and save any tab on Ultimate Guitar as your personal. You can make any changes to your personal tabs that will be available only for you.
What tab formats are supported?
You can save tabs in any format you want: chords, tabs, guitar pro, power, bass, video, ukulele. You can also play Guitar Pro and Power tabs online via our player, so you don’t have to download them in order to play in any other software, unless if you want to edit them.
Where can I see the list of all my personal tabs?
Press the ‘My tabs’ button that is located next to your profile picture, to see the list of all your tabs. Personal tabs are marked with a lock icon and placed next to your published and favorite tabs. To see only your personal tabs use the filter located before the list of tabs.
How to edit personal tabs?
Every personal tab has an ‘Edit’ button – by pressing it, you will open the editing mode where you can edit it. After you finish editing, press the ‘Save’ button – the corrections will be saved, and a new version of the tab will be created. You can write a brief description of the new version of the tab in the ‘About’ field if you want to.
How to save a new version of my personal tab?
After creating a personal tab, you will create its first version. Then you can save successive versions, gradually improving your tab. You can see all the previous versions in the ‘Tab history’ section. To compare two versions, click the ‘Compare’ button.
How to publish my personal tab on Ultimate Guitar?
You can make your personal tab public by pressing the “Publish” button in the editing mode. The tab will be reviewed by our community and moderators following all the standard procedures before it will be added to Ultimate Guitar. You can learn more about tab moderation here:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/help/approvalQueueFAQ
If your tab is rejected by our community or moderators it still will be available as a personal tab.
Can I make a published tab personal again?
No, after you have sent your personal tab to review, it will become public and available for millions of users, and that means they can save it in favorites or share with friends. If we make this possible, users won’t be able to learn a song from your tab, so we decided not to include such a feature.
Every time you change the status of your tab you’re notified that the changes can’t be reversed.

author: chris2424
text: Is there any way that UG could make it more clear when a chord is played for a half measure.  I can sometimes tell when chords are listed close together, but is is usually not at all clear and I have to play the song and sing along to try to figure it out.  Usually, I only figure it out by watching a non UG tutorial that explains which chords are shared between a measure so that the strumming pattern is split.   Other tabs use a bracket or lines around chords that share a measure or where the strumming pattern is split.    Would it be too difficult to institute this as a SOP?   I just had my renewal for my second year and I seriously thought of pausing my subscription and finding another service because of my frustration over the number of songs where the measure/ strumming pattern is split and it takes many hours of playing to figure it out.  This really slows down the learning process.

author: brettsanace
text:
chris2424
I have suggested in the past that for strumming patterns they use two different colours for the arrows and each time a chord changes the colour changes (so not a different colour for each chord just two colours that can be alternated each time a chord change occurs in the strumming pattern). I know they can use different colours as currently the strumming patterns have black arrows but when you listen to the pattern they highlight as blue and I have also seen red arrows (but can't remember the situation). The person creating the strumming pattern would need a mechanism to indicate that the arrow colour should change.
As with the vast majority of my dozens of suggestions UG chose to ignore it.

author: brettsanace
text:
It is also not just chord changes half way through the measure, as often the changes occur on the 4& strum and are tied over the start of the next bar. Whilst this may be obvious to most it would also be good to have a way to indicate that the chord change occurs (on what would typically be an upstrum) at the end of the bar rather than the start of the next bar.
And then there are more complicated ones where there are multiple chord changes within a bar, for example the following uses chord changes on each strum of a triplet just on the 4th beat. Again it would be helpful to have an easy way to indicate this without having to write out tab.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/george-thorogood-the-destroyers/bad-to-the-bone-chords-3856613
