author: hellbound_jonny
text:
Hi! Recently, I realised that one basic yet fundamental thing is missing from UG.
I'm talking about a Like/Dislike button, not far of ones currently used on Facebook and YouTube. Such a button is in massive use on both sites and repeatedly marks the sophistication of both sites as well as developing community interaction at the same time. Of course, it also has more practical uses.
It would allow users to 'recommend' a certain post or alternatively, dislike a post. In doing so, certain posts would be marked out for relevance to the thread or disliked as spam and therefore an unnecessary read. As a result, regular users can easily pinpoint the best posts in a thread.
Practically, the button it would also save pointless posts that simply quote a phrase and subsequently state "+1".
To expand on this, one could also implement a Mod Like button that allows a mod to highlight a useful post, for example, in the Electric Guitar forum, an outstanding post that helps the original question posed. Ultimately, it saves effort for the Mod and allows them to focus their efforts elsewhere.
In certain forums, such as the aforementioned Electric Guitar forum, a tally could gained from all the relevant posts and thus collected in a thread allowing ease of access to common and outlandish questions.
I think a Like/Dislike button would benefit the UG community immensely and should be implemented. Of course, I'm not an expert on bandwidth issues of internet sites so I'm not sure how such a button would affect the site's performance.
I hope you enjoyed reading this and I would appreciate feedback
Jon

By implementing the button, the option for those that do want to read every post is still there, however, for people who want to be guided by 'likes' they have that option as well.
In this way, a community is developed; by catering for the needs of all people, UG can invite everyone to the forums.

author: .george.
text:
Hey
UG Team
!
I recently had an idea for an additional points system akin to the Guitar IQ system. It would be called something like Popularity Points, and users would get one point for every rating they got on a tab, regardless of what the rating was.
Right now, there are a lot of users that have tens of thousands of IQ points because they sit in their house all day and submit tabs for obscure bands nobody's ever heard of (no offense to these fine people, of course; I respect the side hustle). If the Popularity Points idea was implemented, other users would have a chance to climb up their own leaderboard (which could, like the Guitar IQ leaderboard, refresh every week depending on how many ratings got in one week).
I am not suggesting replacing the Guitar IQ system; I am simply advocating for a new, additional system that would be a fun extension to the site.
Thanks for reading! If you're interested, I hope you take this into consideration!
- George

author: UG Support
text:
.george.
hi!
Thanks so much for sharing your thoughtful idea — we really appreciate when users take the time to think about how Ultimate Guitar can evolve in fun and meaningful ways.
You’ll be glad to know that our PR and Marketing team has recently started exploring the concept of an expanded points system, and your suggestion around a “Popularity Points” feature aligns closely with some of the early brainstorming that’s happening. While nothing is confirmed yet, ideas like yours help shape the direction of what we build next.
We’ve passed your message along to the team for consideration, and we’ll be keeping the community posted as things develop. Thanks again for being an engaged and creative part of the UG family!

author: killergege
text:
I don't know about this 15 words limit (maybe it depends on how it counts, I don't think I've ever seen it), But I feel that "This tab is inaccurate" is not really a good comment.
It might depend on the tabs, but maybe the tabs you've commented has been crafted by people that thinks this is good and accurate. This kind of comment doesn't help them.
When you want to rate 2-stars, you should have a few reasons, it shouldn't be that hard to describe. If you don't want to spend too much time commenting, you don't have to enter a very detailed response, but at least a few information (for the author AND for the other people that will open the tab).
A few words like : the rhythm in the chorus is wrong. The chords of the verse should be X, Y, Z. The lead riff in bar X should be A, B, C... Etc.
With a low note like that you should have a few things to say, no ?
Is 15 words too much to ask. Maybe, but there should be a limit to force the commenter to think about what is the problem with the tab, and not just clicking the stars. A bad rating is useless if you don't say why (your reason might not be a good reason for someone else - eg: someone might give a bad rating even on a really good tab because the tuning is wrong, while others might not care).
And +1 for removing "I just don't like it", it's a useless comment.

Constructive feedback that shows an active author how to improve would help the author the most. It's not safe to assume that someone will know how to change their tab without being informed of flagrant errors.
A word as it pertains to English is defined as a unit of letters and/or punctuation with meaningful spaces on both sides. At the end of sentences, ending punctuation will precede a space. Silence or tab stops will precede the first word in a sentence, with the beginning word capitalized for effect. There might be a counting error, but the above Megadeth example is rightly counted as two words.

author: Dyuha
p3tari
text:
I could make a lengthy list of things that have been added to the website over the last 5 years or so. Instead of doing that, I will try to squeeze everything into one broad category of flaws. these flaws are related by the way in which they affect how the user interacts with the website. This is essentially about the changes to the UI, since many changes have made this website less efficient and basically a huge headache to use. However, the root of this problem can be reduced to the great deal of effort that has been put into making this website more lucrative. And I understand that with increased web traffic, there comes increased costs to operate the website. So in order to keep things running, there is a need for increased revenue. I totally understand that. But maybe there is a way for you guys to make money without pissing off users who have been coming here since the very beginning. Man, things were so much simpler and better back then...
The main issue is all of the advertisements. It didn't used to be this bad. Right now, I am looking at a banner that runs along the left side of the browser. Sounds like there is a great sales event that includes major savings on Taylor guitars. Ok, cool. I like Taylor guitars. The banner takes up quite a bit of space though. A rough estimate is that this thing takes up about 15% of my monitor. So it's not TOO bad. However....
There is another banner on the right side of the browser. It shows an advertisement for... a sales event? savings on Taylor guitars? Oh cool. Sounds familiar? That's because it is the same ad that is shown on the other banner. Now we're talking 30% of my screen being used for advertising. Why double up on this ad? Do you get paid by Taylor everytime a user loads one of these banner ads? And so why not just make us load 2 ads... that doubles the profits without needing to reel more consumers in. This is just shameful. And I mean, this would be really annoying with two different ads. But the fact that it is the same ad, shown twice, it just makes me want to sign out and never return again. It's disgusting, to be frank.
on a related note, it seems like ever since I stopped paying for a pro subscription, this site hardly works. Every couple of minutes, I am blocked from what I am doing and redirected to some stupid page. And the purpose is always to try to make me get a subscription. I'm not even trying to look at premium content most of the time that this happens. This is clearly a terrible marketing strategy. You are literally annoying users with aversive popups and redirections, and then telling them to pay up so that it will all go away.
This does not motivate me to renew my subscription. You are nagging like an annoying and overbearing mother. Now I've learned to associate this website with obnoxious nagging and the frustration of having little to no control as I try to navigate from page to page. How about, instead of using negative reinforcement by nagging at me until you get me to comply, try using positive reinforcement. Show me how truly rewarding it is to get a pro membership again. You can start by allowing us to download official tabs, so we can get the heck off of this ridiculous website as soon as we find what we are looking for.
It seems like every couple of months, there is less and less space being dedicated to guitar tab content. There are more pop ups. More redirects. More nagging at us to pay up.
I think ultimate guitar would be awesome if there was some sort of desktop app available. I would even prefer to pay for this instead of a subscription fee that is way overpriced. it would be like a UG tab player, and you can download files form the website and load them in the app. Kind of like guitar pro. But strictly for viewing/playing tabs from this site. The mobile app sort of attempts to do this, but it misses the mark. It is just not very practical for me to have to use a small screen. My eyesight is not great so if I am looking at tabs, it needs to be on a large monitor. Besides, I can't hold my freaking phone up if my hands are occupied with playing a guitar.
So in summary... stop being so obnoxious. You are filling my browser with too much crap I don't want to see. II can live with ads. But not when almost half of my screen is dedicated to a single advertisement.Stop blocking me. Stop redirecting me. Stop interrupting me. I don't want a pro membership. I had one for years, and you guys ruined it by hiking the price up tremendously. You're asking for way too much money. And the way you do it feels intrusive. As a result,  I feel resentment towards the people who ruined the best website on the internet.

Dear Ultimate Guitar Team,
First of all, thank you for your incredible app—it has been an invaluable tool for musicians like me. I am reaching out with a suggestion for a feature that I believe would greatly enhance the user experience: the ability to adjust the metronome volume during playback.
Currently, it seems that the metronome's volume is fixed and often way too loud, even if adjusting the single volumes of the instruments. Having a dedicated control for the metronome's volume would provide more flexibility and make the app even more user-friendly.
I hope this suggestion aligns with your development goals, and I’m excited to see how the app continues to evolve.
Thank you for considering this request!
Best regards,
Florian

author: a.faretdinov
text:
NSpen1
first: the issue
cwrye83
describing is not a simple UI preference or a one-line fix. It’s a backend/search-engine behaviour that affects how results are aggregated, ranked and presented across several categories (including Misc). Changing it requires work in multiple layers: query parsing, index weighting, faceting logic for categories, caching rules and the sync between the website and our backend services. Those are not cosmetic tweaks; they’re architectural changes that must be designed, tested and deployed carefully so we don’t break other users’ search results.
Second: yes — it
is possible
to change how search handles “Misc” and other categories. The search can be tuned to prioritise song title vs. artist, to prefer exact matches, to collapse duplicates, or to present results grouped by contributor or tab type. The point I’ve been making to the team is exactly that: the current behaviour can be surprising and inconsistent, and it’s reasonable to consider different ranking rules for user-saved lists and for the public search index.
Third: I don’t pretend to know every single detail of every subsystem. I’m the Community Manager, not the search engineer — but I am aware of this problem, I’ve raised it, and I’m actively communicating with the engineers and product owners who own search and categorisation. They’re investigating where the mismatch is happening (index vs. frontend vs. caching), what the safest fixes are, and how we can roll out improvements without creating regressions for millions of users.
A few concrete things the DevTeam is looking into right now:
If you have specific examples (song titles, URLs, screenshots showing the exact mismatch in Misc vs other categories), that would be extremely useful — concrete cases help the engineers reproduce and fix the bug faster. Please send them to me and I’ll attach them to the bug.
Finally: I understand the passion behind your comment, but please remember — public accusations and insults don’t speed up engineering work. If you want this fixed, the fastest path is: provide reproducible examples, let us triage them, and I’ll push for prioritisation. I’m doing exactly that already.

I don't believe you can move songs within a playlist. The "Move" function that is offered only allows you to move the song to a different playlist. The songs in a playlist will be ordered in the order that they are added to the playlist. If you subsequently click on the Artist or Song headings the tabs will be re-ordered alphabetically (or reverse alphabetically) based on which heading you click and then you will never be able to get back to the order that the songs were originally added. This is what many people have complained about in the forums - that they can't move/re-order songs in their playlists when they want to change their set list, so they need to create a new one each time.

author: thepublicaccessshowcase
text:
As I'm sure all of you are aware, the old player has been removed entirely from the website, with the most common reasoning provided by staff being that bugs in the old player could potentially impact user experience in a negative manner. Therefore, I understand why the new player would be prioritized, despite it lacking certain features that the old player once had.
However, I am unsure why such a nuclear option had to be considered; there was truly nothing wrong or extremely broken with the old player justifying its complete removal. Many pro users including myself greatly preferred the old player, and seeing as the new player is still a bit buggy and lacking in certain areas, it doesn't seem like a fair trade to pay for a service and have aspects of it removed without equal additions to it.
Therefore, I would like to know why the old player cannot be turned into a toggleable option that one can enable in settings. If a major concern is related to the player having potential bugs, a simple disclaimer before activation could properly inform the user that they are willingly choosing to use the outdated player and that they may face bugs that they would not encounter with the new player. There is a reason why software developers allow users to downgrade to previous versions per their own choice, and especially when the option was never impeding on the new player to begin with and only serving as a positive addition to the user experience, it doesn't make much sense to me why this cannot be implemented as a way to please both sides.

author: sjones
text:
I've bit my tongue on this for a while now, but being an almost daily user of UG and regular browser/poster/user in the Promote Your Band forum, I've been so annoyed by what I'm seeing in PYB that I'm making this post.
In regards to the PYB rules, the forum has been infested lately with:
a) Threads that belong in the Original Recordings or Cover Recordings forum as they're not for the promotion or discussion of any band. Rather, they are just individual posts of songs recorded by a member that are wrongfully being posted in the PYB forum without deletion.
b) Voting (or "Vote for Me") threads, which are strictly against the PYB forum rules
c) Threads promoting other sites and services which do not appear to have mod-approval
d) Multiple threads for one band. Prohibited by rules.
Normally, these threads would be delivered and offenders appropriately warned and/or punished. However, at a glance just before writing this thread, neither mod of the forum has been on UG for over a week.
Personally, I enjoy the PYB thread and think it needs to be paid more attention to. I know it's by no means the most popular sub-forum on UG, but in my opinion it warrants more attention from the mods than it's being given, as the listed recurring offensive are a major annoyance and deterrence of what the sub-forum is to be used for.
Thanks for the taking the time to read my post. If there's any way I can help out to make the PYB forum better, I'd be very interested in lending a hand.
sjones

It's very annoying and completely pointless, all they are doing is copying and pasting the tab and relabelling it a uke tab. I couldn't agree more! It does not make any sense to automatically copy existing guitar tabs and re-label them "ukulele". When I submit a tab, I take care to include tips/voicings that are useful for players of for 6-stringed instruments (like ... yes, the guitar for example). Now this very same tab is headed under "ukulele". Uke-players do not need that. They - just like guitarists - need tabs that are written with their specific instrument in mind, so they can actually profit from it.
All in all, I think it's a great idea to implement the possibility to submit ukulele tabs. But adding existing guitar tabs as ukulele tabs is misleading and does not help uke players.
BTW: What if ukulele players looking for a good uke-tab come across my perfectly good re-labeled guitar tab (that is now supposedly a ukulele tab) which isn't any good as a ukulele tab? Do I have to take the bad ratings for something that I never intended to be a ukulele tab?

text: I was playing a complicated chord where you have to stretch your fingers. It was very awkward for me to play the d shape chord but playing it as a Gmajor chord. Meaning you have to use all four fingers and stretch to play the chord. I played the chord for too long and playing other complicated chords where you have to stretch. And I felt some pain in the wrist but I didn't stop, thinking it was ok. The irratitaion wasn't too bad but after 30 mins of playing I stopped and noticed the pain. For a week now my left wrist for fretting has been numb. My question is, did I strain my muscles or sprain it? After a week, the numbness calmed down. I'm not in as much pain as a week ago. My wrist feels better but I can't play and it feels weak which is a sign it needs to heal more. Has anybody had this problem where they overstretched their muscles or tendons and didn't stop right away and over played? How long was the healing process, what is it that I'm dealing with? Is this a serious injury, is it minor? Let me know!

text:
The reason I use and subscribe to UG Pro is because I jam with a buddy that uses it and we share playlists. That whole shared play list feature is bizarre. Whomever designed that must have been doing shrooms or something. However, I digress. That is a rant for another day.

The issues with the playback are;
1. There is zero indication of measures on the chords screen.

- This feature is included on the mobile version. Why not the PC version?
- I've seen this feature request many times in different forums here. Always the same reply. "We are working on it." Somehow I doubt that. Are you actually working on it?

- It is beyond tedious that we have to do this every time a song is opened or refreshed.
Best,
Rick

Okay, these are the ones for which there are recognised names on UG :
C7sus(b9) > C7sus4b9
Cm6(9) > Cm6add9 or Cm6/9
Cmaj7(#11) > Cmaj7#11
Cmaj9(13) > Cmaj9add13
C9(13) > C9add13
C6(9) > C6add9 or C6/9
Cm7(b5) > Cm7b5
Cm7(b5)/Gb > Cm7b5/Gb
These ones, not so :
C13sus
Not possible, could use C13 (no3)
Cm7b13
Not possible, but equivalent to Abmaj9/C
C7(b9,b13)
Not possible, but could it be a #5 instead of b13?  You wouldn't want a regular 5th as well?
Then C7#5b9 works.  Otherwise define as C7b9* (b13)
Cm11(b5)
Not possible, would have to define as Cm7b5* (add11) or Cm11* (b5)
Or rename, = Ebmadd9/C
Cdim(b13)
Not possible.  Do you mean C Eb Gb + Ab?  That's Ab7/C.

author: Roc8995
text:
Please stop rambling on about how nobody else is as smart as you. If you really think a post is that stupid, just ignore it. You're not adding anything by posting a long, grammatically poor diatribe about how petty and unintellectual everyone else is. I hope you can find some irony in that.
To actually answer your question, Ultimate-Guitar has begun to expand its scope beyond just guitars. We have a bass and a drum forum now, and a lot of other music-related news and forum discussions. Just as the YMCA isn't just for young christian men any more, and Radio Shack doesn't just sell radios, so too has this site moved on from its narrow original purpose. We're happy to have such a large audience, and we're trying lots of different things to bring a more diverse group of people into our community. If people keep reading, commenting on, and sharing articles about music, they'll continue to show up on the site. Guitar was and remains the primary purpose of the site (tabs, forums especially), but UG is branching out into the music community in general.
As far as seeing more of what you like, UG is a content-driven model. If you're not happy with the quality or the type of articles being published, comment on the ones you like. Submit articles yourself. Engage the types of things that you want to see on the site, and get others to join you. Complaining that other people's interests are favored over your own doesn't solve anything on a site where the content is determined by results.
To be perfectly honest the last third of that long post was nearly unintelligible. We'd be a lot more likely to seriously engage your thoughts if they were expressed more clearly.
Last thing - sorry for the long post - please stop being so unpleasant. You're only making things worse by insulting people. Your attitude in this thread is contributing to a lot of the negative responses you're getting.

author: johnnycanuck
text:
I'd love to resurrect the thread at:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1693310
Having done some importing/exporting of 'chords' songs (and I'm talking .txt files with non-proportional font), it seems that the ChordPro format is a great standard for interoperability.
Response #2 by NeoMvsEu to that thread doesn't make any sense (from an experienced programmer's perspective), because you can parse ChordPro files to CIL (chord in line) or COL (chord over line). It's an OPEN and well defined markup language. 3rd party programs do it (and I've seen a few on GitHub), and so could UG if they wanted. After all, they do have this 'Automagic' feature when editing songs.
Furthermore, response #4 doesn't respond to interoperability and/or sharing.
As for UG's exports:
PDF - sucks because you are stuck in that key, along with fixed layout page formatting . . with page breaks, often separating chords from the accompanying lyrics.
UG's text export (private songs from the edit screen) - is not good because it puts the title and artist on the same line. Not easily sortable (but I fixed it with Notepad++ Macros).
UG's (apparent) recommended cut and paste method - just plain sucks because it's manual. Try doing that with a setlist or greater. Who comes up with this stuff?
Furthermore, this thread is misleading:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=2334170
It's doable, just not at all straightforward.
In the case of the recent pedal *FIASCO* brought on by UG themselves, if UG had a mass export function using an interoperable format, then people could have migrated their songs over to another platform for their gigs. They'd still use UG, because of the HUGE amount of content available, along with Pro, etc, but at least they could play without having to paw at their iPads on stage to keep up with the scrolling.
Then there's this whole sync business which UG apparently doesn't support. UG has great content, but, from what I can see, sharing edited songs/playlists with band members leaves a LOT to be desired. Sharing songs/playlists via emailed web browser bookmarks is the response I got from
support@ultimate-guitar.com
. The mind boggles at this 25+ year old solution.
I'd give UG a 4/10 for interoperability and 2/10 for sync.  The only reason interoperability gets that high is because of the previously mentioned edit screen. And I had to mass edit/parse those files to make them Title/Artist sortable.
Please point me in the right direction if I'm missing something, because I've missed things in the past here.
/rant

author: johnnycanuck
text:
And to the folks that say that ChordPro is hard to read. That's because, like HTML, it's a markup language. It's not meant to be read directly by people, but rather parsed and used by the application and THEN displayed / sorted / filtered with all the metadata that ChordPro can provide.
In the meantime, there are sure a lot closed threads on exporting people's songs here. In my case, I don't want to leave, but I DO want metadata based backups in case UG goes under.  Much larger organizations with products like WordPerfect, Visicalc, Lotus 1-2-3, Novell, Solaris and more come to mind here.

author: johnnycanuck
text:
I've eventually been able to import my 476 UG song collection into Songbook Pro. . . for 'gig' display purpose. Sorry, not ditching UG. I had to write several Notepad++ macros in order to massage the .txt songs I'd exported so that I could sort by title/artist.
The bigger problem was the key the song was in. UG's inability to print a personal edited/transposed song required me to reset EVERY song back to the orignal key and then export the lot of them on the download personal edits page. Of course, they're no longer printable in the key I want, but I've already done that and I really don't want to go back to PDF anyways.
In the meantime, SongbookPro and a Donner Bluetooth scroller give me a reliable and offline viewing/scrolling experience on Android. Oh, and I can quickly sync/share my songs with my buddies without having to resort to web browser links.

text:

"Search Titles Only"
GG&A

+SG pickups
"SG pickups"

Another example: I wanted to know which preamp tubes were the V1, V2, etc in my amp, so I typed this into search:
preamp v1 v2
"Search Titles Only"
GG&A
But all the results were of the word "preamp". I then tried the term
V1
Entire posts
All forums
And the search came up with no matches, which leads me to believe the search isn't too comprehensive.
Just some little things I've found with the searchbar, and I thought I'd bring them up.

author: paddyirishman
text:
These suggestions are for the main website
1.
No email notification for comments made by the tab author:
I have chosen to receive an email when someone posts a comment on one of my tabs, but I also get an email when I post a comment on my
own
tabs, which is somewhat irritating and completely pointless.
2.
Editing tabs:
in order to edit an already-accepted tab you have to go through
My Profile > Contributions > Tabs
and then click the little blue U.  This is fine, but I think it would also be handy to have an option on each tab page itself letting a logged-in author edit it.  When tabs reside in the validation queue there's a box with two options in it on the top-right: "Put on hold" and "Update tab!".  The "Update tab!" option should persist after the tab is accepted.
3.
Option to disable the friendship system
4.
The ability to opt-out of appearing on top tabber/contributor lists, or opting out of the score system completely
5.
More tunings available during the tab submission process:
there are many tunings which are quite common but aren't offered as an option when submitting a tab.  For instance, doom metal is almost always tuned down 1 and 1/2 steps to C# but this option isn't included.
6.
Multi-tiered tab rating:
I often feel that a simple star rating for a tab doesn't really tell us how good or bad it is, especially if someone rates it down for one shortcoming while ignoring any good aspects of it.  I think an aggregate rating based on several sub-ratings would be better.  For instance:
Overall Accuracy [1 - 5]
Readability/Coherency/Presentation [1 - 5]
Completeness/Attention to Detail [1 - 5]
These ratings would then be tallied together to form the total rating, and each of the sub-ratings would be visible to other users who want to gauge the tab's worth.  The tab's star rating could have a small section below it like this:
Based on 33 ratings
Overall Accuracy -
77%
Readability/Coherency/Presentation  -
50%
Completeness/Attention to Detail -
68%
7.
Optional MIDI accompaniment for ASCII tabs:
I think this idea has already been kicked around in the past, but I think if a tab author has a complete MIDI version of an ASCII tab (complete in that it contains all or most of the instruments used in the song) it would help guitarists immensely if they could hear it when they're trying to learn from ASCII tabs, many of which are transcribed in such a way that makes sight-reading impossible.  If a built-in MIDI player is out of the question a simple MIDI file upload/download system would be a fine alternative.
The website HamieNet.com has a built-in MIDI player which has a set of realistic instruments allowing the MIDIs to be heard as high quality backing tracks (high quality compared to vanilla MIDI, anyway).  If UG had similar functionality it'd be the most user-friendly tab site in existence.
I understand that this would create more work for mods/validators, not to mention the folks who maintain the website and upgrade its code, but the benefits it would bring are worth considering.
I think that covers it
Cheers!

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Suggestions 1 and 2 are very sensible, so I support them completely. Suggestion 5 seems easy enough to implement as well.
Suggestions 3 and 4 don't seem to be worth the trouble of implementing. I don't see why anyone would want to opt out of friendships (just don't accept friend requests). Opting out of the scoring system is even stranger to me; not being scored or ranked doesn't really hold any advantage for the contributor at all, and it would only be disadvantageous to the people who would want to know what the overall quality of your contributions is.
Suggestion 6 is kind of iffy. First off, you'd need to define the scoring categories more clearly than just "accuracy", "readability" and "completeness". Second, although I like the idea of more concise ratings, I think it'd actually be more trouble to implement than it'd be worth.
And regarding suggestion 7, I don't think it's going to work on UG because of its affiliation with Arobas Music, the company that created the Guitar Pro software. Basically, instead of a general MIDI format, tabs are provided in GP format instead, so you'd need the Guitar Pro player to view the tabs. That's part of the deal with Arobas, and I'd imagine them not being very happy if UG started to provide free MIDI tabs of their own all of a sudden.
Then again, there are free PowerTab files available as well, which can be opened with free-to-download software (PT or TuxGuitar). So maybe having MIDI tabs as well isn't such a problem after all, in which case I'd be all for it.
You'll have to wait for some UG staff insight to see what they think about these suggestions, though. But bear in mind:
- They're on holiday right now, so be patient;
- They're working on some major website updates at the moment, so it's possible that none of this will be priority (or will already be part of their update scheme).
Cheers!

author: paddyirishman
text:
Cheers for the reply!
1, 2 and 3 were what prompted me to post the thread, the others were really just afterthoughts for which I didn't hold out much hope.  If just 1, 2 and 5 can be implemented I'll be very happy
The reason I wanted to disable the friendship system (or at least just block all friendship requests) is because I don't use UG for social networking purposes and find it to be quite awkward/arrogant to refuse or simply ignore requests.  If I could just disable the feature it would remove any ikciness about wanting to keep my involvement on the site devoted solely to submitting tabs.
This is partly why I also wanted to opt out of the top tabber lists; I tend to get reams of requests for tabs or friendships from people because they simply scan these lists and pick a name at random and contact them for whatever reason.  The PMs generally begin with "I see you're on the top tabber list, can you tab x, y and z?" I don't see what purpose these lists serve except to encourage those who like being on them to contribute regularly.  I don't need that particular motivation.  If I was removed from the lists or if I had my score frozen at zero the individual tab ratings would still exist to show how good or bad my tabs are, so I don't see the scoring system as being especially important.  I think it also encourages elitism and clannishness, and if you look at the top few contributors you can see that it also encourages abuse (i.e. posting other people's tabs to get your score up).
With regards to the multi-tiered tab ratings, those sub-categories I listed were just examples, I'm sure better ones could be devised.  Having said that I'm also sure that the current rating system is probably fine as it is haha.
Thanks man!

author: paddyirishman
text:
I have another small suggestion.  When submitting a tab there's a difficulty option, through which you can convey to other users how difficult the tab is.  When you read the explanation of this option in the site's Help page, however, there's something of a contradiction in how the option is put to use.  It states that the difficulty is gauged by accounting for how "complete" the tab is.  For instance, a tab which just gives you the gist of the song is to be slated as "Novice" whereas a tab which contains all of the guitar parts tabbed in full should be labelled "Advanced".  This is fine so far, if a little vague.  The Help page then states that if the song itself is easy - such as a song by Blink 182 - then the tab should be labelled as "Novice" anyway even if the tab is 100% complete.
This seems like we're running around in circles.  If the difficulty rating can have two incompatible meanings - i.e. that it refers to the difficulty of the tab AND the difficulty of the song
despite
the tab's difficulty, with the Help page telling us that each meaning is simultaneously separate and intrinsically linked - then of what use is the rating?  How are we to know which meaning of the rating to take on board for each tab?  When we see a tab labelled as "Novice" do we assume that it's an incomplete tab, an easy to play song which is either complete or incomplete, or what?
My suggestion is that we boil this option down to one meaning - how difficult the song is to play.  In that sense, a "Novice" rating would let novice guitarists find tabs which they'd feel more comfortable playing from, rather than stumbling across a difficult-to-play song which has a mediocre/incomplete tab (which is what the "Novice" rating currently signifies in most cases).
If a tab's completeness is to be denoted by someone we can either leave that for the current star rating system to imply (rarely does half a tab get a 5-star rating), or we can have a separate drop-down menu for tab authors to use to indicate how complete their tab is as well as one to indicate what level of skill you'll need to play it.
Sorry for the long-winded post; it's kinda hard to explain this in one paragraph!

author: van01010100
text:
Maybe it was a bad idea to put 3 suggestions in one thread. Here is a detailed breakdown of the reasoning behind my first suggestion. If you feel inclined to argue the points made below please make sure you use objective logic and respectfully explain your reasoning.
Reasons why a NGD subsection would be good:
- Organization, self explanatory I hope.
- No more threads that just say "ngd!!!". The rules could require that the thread title must follow the format of "[Brand] - [Model] - " or something like that. This means if you're looking for threads about a specific guitar you'll be able to find them quickly and easily instead of searching through a bunch of unrelated randomly titled threads where the guitar you're searching for is mentioned once.
- No more NGD threads w/o clips or a review, or at least a lot less because the 'rules' sticky wouldn't have to be hidden under several other stickies.
- Has the potential to encourage people to make really high quality NGD threads because they no longer have to worry about their thread getting lost among the dozens of repetitive "Why are my strings buzzing?" and "What guitar should I get for metal?" threads posted in the EG forum every day.
Reasons why a NGD subsection would be bad:
- Would require adding one extra subforum, which is frowned upon unless strictly necessary. My argument: The Bands & Artists section has 10 subforums while the EG section has 0. This is illogical for two reasons: a) there are always more people viewing the EG forum than all 10 band subforums combined, and b) this is ultimate-GUITAR.com, not ultimate-BAND.com.
- Has the potential to wither and die if everyone who frequents the EG forum simultaneously decides they have no more interest in looking at people's new electric guitars solely because it would require one extra mouse click. My argument: Based on the view counts of existing NGD threads compared to other threads in the EG forum, and based on simple logic, this is borderline impossible.
- Could potentially involve moving recent NGD threads (optional).
Reasons why the review section of UG is good:
- It's very well organized.
- The reviews are broken down in to specific topics. This is something that should be encouraged for NGD threads IMO.
Reasons why the review section of UG isn't good enough for this purpose:
- You can't post pictures or clips.
- People can't comment on your review specifically.
- It's geared more towards people doing research (ala Harmony Central reviews), and not towards sharing your new baby, which is what NGD threads are all about. Nothing wrong with being excited about a new guitar in a guitar forum. Forums are supposed to be about sharing and discussing.
Reasons why a single thread would be good:
- Easy to find.
- Everything would be in one thread, saving people a few mouse clicks.
Reasons why a single thread would be bad:
- Everything would be in one thread, making it extremely hard to follow unless there were strict rules about not posting comments. Not allowing comments would be even worse than leaving the NGD threads randomly dispersed throughout the EG section, as the whole point of a NGD thread is (or at least should be) to share and discuss.
- There's already a "Post Pics Of Your Gear" thread.
If I'm an idealist for dreaming of a forum where everything is in the right place, thread titles are descriptive and accurate, and people respond to threads with intelligence and respect, then I guess I'm an idealist.
TL;DR - I still think a NGD subsection is a good idea.

Ban all posts in NGD threads, that consist of simply HNGD or something of that variation, and see how much the NGD threads get in the way. So in reality, in my opinion at least, its not the system that is flawed, its the users using the system.
Also, you ask why the Bands & Artists forum has more subforums than Electric Guitar, despite having less activity. Firstly, if you were to abolish the subforum divisions, and lump all the threads together, it would probably end up being worse than the Pit. The place would be a complete mess, and threads would be a nightmare to find. Also, i think you will find that each subforum within bands and artists has its own community of regular users, many of which are on first name terms. Getting rid of those subforums, means getting rid of those communities, which would a backwards move for the site. Also, i think you will find, you wont see much of a community form in a NGD forum, unless you can find a group of users that have enough money to be buying a couple of guitars a week.
As for where the mods discussion about the EG forum, mods have their own hidden forum so they can dscuss important things about the site, without the mindless and annoying input of pit monkeys etc.

Someone asked me about authors voting to approve their own tabs or corrections and after a minute I realised what they meant: it's the people who appear anonymously in the queue just as "Author" with a random avatar. author: steven seagull
text:
You haven't got a clue what you're talking about - the website and the forums are two very different things.
The forums have an age requirement, providing your date of birth is part of the sign up process. Forum content is user generated, so there has to be a certain amount of responsibility to ensure that users create content that is appropriate for all ages 13 and up, because that's the minimum age limit for signup. You have to agree to terms and conditions to be a member of the forums, you don't have to agree to anything to simply view the website.
Technically there's no obligation at all to regulate what gets posted, as far as the main site goes all content there is generated by UG itself, even user submitted contributions are approved first - it's up to the site management to decide what's appropriate and what isn't, and even then if people are unhappy with an article they can feed that back.

author: lastoria.bretton
text:
The issue: Often when using standard notation the translator will misrepresent a note. For example, a song might be in Db but the player will display it as C#. In really bad scenarios, the entire song is translated wrong and comes across as jibberish. This happens pretty often and is a source of confusion. A good example is the tab for Riptide -
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/vance-joy/riptide-official-2104813
.
Take the bassline, which is notated as Bb G# C#. The harmonic quality of these notes is now entirely misleading as their real values are actually Bb Ab Db, not to mention the horrible practice of mixing sharps and flats like that. The entire song suffers this issue, with the vocal utilizing a lot of sharps and flats when a proper key system would eliminate a lot of confusion. I hope this explains the issue properly.
The solution: There are a couple ways this could be done. One would be a button that would change every instance of a specific note to its enharmonic equivalent, so you could turn C#s into Dbs across the song. Or, some extension of the transpose button could do a broad sweep on every note.

Hi everyone,
I posted a while ago this thread on the pit without knowing it wasnt suposed to be there so it got closed. Thanks to the instructions from the dude who closed it ill post it here to keep the conversation rolling.
-----
UG (Ultimete-Guitar) has been steadily releasing their pet program "Tab Pro" over the course of the past couple of months or so. This program is similar to Guitar Pro or Tux Guitar but the difference is that there is a monthly subscription to use the software.
This software comes with a special format of tablature that is not compatible with other programs and if you are looking for a song on UG it is most likely that you will find such version. The problem here is that all "tab pro" files are mere copies of work submited by other users as gp (guitar pro) files or power tab and UG just copies the highest rated tab for each song and transforms it into their "tab pro" format which they then sell to people.
Now, the problems i have with this are:
1- There is no credit to the original uploader or in fact any credit at all, meaning that UG is taking full credit for said tab.
2- As a paying service "Tab Pro" is not sharing any monetary retribution to the original uploader.
3- There is no intention to ask for permision from the original uploader to transform it into "tab pro" format
Because of this ive been very critical about their way of making content available, specially when our work is involved. So far out of the 49 tabs i have under my user name ive counted a couple of tabs have been translated to "tab pro" format and are fully visible if you look for tabs under Buckethead name while there are more not so visible that can be looked when vieweing the "Tab Pro" format, among those some of the album tabs ive done. This has pissed me off for a while.
I in collaboration with other friends, make tabs that everyone can enjoy for free. We do not ask for money, we do not ask for fame or whatever, we do it to help bots (or at least thats my reasoning behind my tab making) and the way UG is been doing buisness is not very tasteful in my opinion.
I contacted UG a couple of times regarding the situation and they reply very quickly saying that by the end of the month they would be adressing the issue.
Now, i try to be polite here and everything but whatever the end result is on UG i still want to make tabs and i still want to help other bots learn songs.  Because of that, one of the scenarios i was contemplating was that UG tells us to go to hell (in which they do not give credit nor compensation) in which case i would stop posting on UG. I can understand your concern over the fact that you aren't given credit for your work, and that's the only thing that I can't figure out why it is what it is.
As for the other concerns, there's a subscription because it's a web based solution. Every time you access it, you're using resources on UG's servers. This isn't exactly the same as guitar pro or tuxguitar. It's something that you don't have to have admin permissions in order to install and run. Think of it like a cloud based guitar pro.
The money issue is the way it is for 2 reasons. 1) the license you give to UG when you submit content is royalty free and 2) the money received from subscribers isn't for the tab itself at this point, it's for the service/program that you're using to read the tab (similar to guitar pro).
UG has always received money from your tab (via ad revenue), if it didn't the site wouldn't last long. Why has the expectation changed because the revenue stream has changed?
As for the "This limited license does not grant Ultimate Guitar the right to sell or otherwise distribute your User Generated Content outside of the Service" sentence. Although it's not in the ToS now, I'm pretty sure it was at one point. But regardless of that, the important part is 'outside of the service'.
The service is defined as "OUR INTERNET-BASED SERVICE TOGETHER WITH ALL INFORMATION, CONTENT, PRODUCTS, MATERIALS AND SERVICES MADE AVAILABLE TO YOU THROUGH THE SAME BY US AND/OR THIRD PARTIES" as such the content is being distributed within the service and that particular sentence wouldn't apply anyway.
I should point out that my views don't necessarily reflect the opinion of the office, I'm just giving you a response because I've read into these things in the past.

author: Wolfsbora
text:
Hi all,
'Tis the time of year to let bygones be bygones. But more importantly for someone in the wrong to make it right.
When I first joined the forum I thought that providing fresh feedback would be a helpful way to introduce myself and express my experience in a way that I thought would help the site grow. Instead, I allowed my ego to get in the way and I ended up feeling not rightly threatened and angry. In the process I insulted many people and the site itself both internally and publicly.
With that said, I was wrong. I've known for a long time I was wrong but I had to wait to express my feeling about it until the right time came. That time is now. Not only have I been welcomed back into the forum after expressing immature behavior, I've grown to like the staff and I've learned so much in my time here. My initial banishment was well deserved and I recognize the kindness of the mods to allow me to rejoin the ranks of this wonderful community.
I need to apologize to
Roc8995
most of all. Not only did he take the brunt of my anger and frustration, I publicly shamed him even though he was just doing his job, and it was a job well done. I'm sorry,
Roc8995
. I truly am. And I'm sorry to everyone else that got pushed into the oath of my belligerent steamroller of an ego.
You all have become a group that I look forward with whom to interact and discuss our favorite hobby: guitar and the music it makes. You have a friend in me. I will be sure to step into the line of fire any time someone becomes as belligerent as I did.
And finally thank you all for your hard work here. You do this with passion, experience, and a need to share your incredible knowledge to those of us that are new or old at the craft of playing guitar.
I will forever be a grateful member of Ultimate Guitar, not because it has the best tab selection on the web, not because of the great guitar porn only this site has, but because of the members, and in particular the staff that keeps the site running with little help from the folks upstairs.
So thank you, thank you so much for letting me back in and for giving me a chance to find out that you are truly good people with a shared passion of guitar and music.
Your grateful friend,
Wolfy

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
Quote by Alex Vik
Isn't that what your ban reason was? Al mine said was "sdf", because that's what I got in my email.
So, it's not broken anymore apparently.
Not necessarily.  Those are
insta-bans
.
Common ban procedure:
First warning:
Message with reason for warning #1 sent via email.
CS widget shows reason.
Second warning:
Message with reason for warning #2 sent via email.
CS widget is updated.  Reason for warning #1 is removed.
CS widget now shows reason #2 .
A few moments later...
Ban is issued:
Message stating reason "2 active warnings = ban" is issued via email.
CS widget is updated.  Reason for warning #2 is removed.
CS widget now shows reason "2 active warnings = ban"
The user won't have a chance to see the reason for the second warning on the CS widget.
The reason YOU guys were able to see the reason was because the process was different, because of the instaban.  Insta-bans are not the norm.
Perhaps it has been fixed.  But I suspect not.

author: maguri
text:
Not sure whether this has been suggested before:
Some chord voicings that are suggested when hovering over the highlighted chords are ridiculously difficult and not helpful for beginners or even remotely intermediate players.
Example:
LIKE A DIAMOND CHORDS (ver 2) by Tom Petty and The Heartbreakers @ Ultimate-Guitar.Com
There is a G#m7-5 chord in this song. The chord name sounds intimidating, but the voicing is not difficult, you do not even need a barre. It's just an A minor shape, played on the third fret with G# as the root: 4-x-4-4-3-x .
When hovering over the chord, however, this easiest of options is not shown as the first suggestion. The first voicing shown there is a barre chord: 4-5-4-4-7-4, really hard to play. But it does not stop at that. Versions 2 and 3 make it even harder by adding a pinky small barre: 4-5-4-4-7-7 and 4-5-4-7-7-7. And it goes on and on and on until suggestion 19 of 19,  when finally the voicing 4-x-4-4-3-x appears which sounds good, is easy to play and which should have been number 1 for any regular player.
Suggestion: Weed through the suggested options of voicings and choose which ones should appear before others because they can be played by more players than others. I'd help doing that, too!
What do other users and UG think?

author: Gutch220
text:
My idea would take a lot of work and a lot of start-up money but I think the concept would be cool even though it is probably dead in the water. Having a Ultimate-Guitar Magazine might catch on to people outside the realm of the web-site. The content of the magazine would be mostly tablature (sort of like
Guitar Edge Magazine
) so the ammount of original content would be less then, say, a Guitar World. The magazine could consist of
- ~10 songs transcribed
- reviews and analysis of new
AND
older/vintage gear (nobody does this)
- short interviews of guitarists/musicians/and established users of the web-site
- concert/album reviews
- articles on achieving certain tones
- a fold-out picture of a musician(s) with a pin-up girl type picture on the other side
- web-site news
- articles from forum members
- feature small sections of UG members' bands
- etc.
The web-site and magazine can be interactive with eachother, to my knowledge this really hasn't been done before. Of course you need to buy one-time printing rights to the songs, find a publisher, distrubutor, sell advertising, sell subscriptions, and so on but it would have to start out small and grow. As long as the subscription price was reasonable (let's say $20US +/- per year) and the magazine was distributed to newstands, shops, etc, I don't see why it wouldn't be very popular. I know I would buy it considering Guitar1 recently went out of business. %75 of the magazine would be transcriptions so putting something together each month shouldn't be hard as long as you have the effort of the people behind it. It would also be fun to have a forum for people to discuss and participate in the creation of each issue online
I know this will probably never happen but the at least the idea is out there.

author: Simonwalker
text:
as for the Junior reviews. It's a pretty nice guitar in the price range but it does leave a lot to wish for.
If you are the kinda person Who tends to travel around quite a bit and don't exactly own a personal jet to carry around your equipment for ya, and still u don't wanna compromise on the way you want your guitar to sound, look no further! This baby has got all the features and tonal versatility that you'd have wanted to be in that practice amp you've always dreamt of! The two channels (clean/overdrive) with seperate volume controls (no foot-pedals, but better stop dreaming about them in a 10W amp, kiddo) along with the controls for gain and 'tone' (which basically determines whether u want a 'flat' or a 'v-shaped' midrange varies the tone of ur guitar from slisha mushy to bright and twingy) supplies me with all the bright, squeaky-clean tone or the mildly distorted crunch that I need for my blues play. Turn the gain knob way up to unleash Monsterous Metallic Mayhem, with the tone still maintaining an amazing 'Marshall' signature (read clarity) in it! It has never been a necessity to turn up the volume beyond 6 even when practising with a drummer, and my neighbours started banging on my door when once (just for the fun of it) I turned up the volume all the way to 10... but the tone was still surprisingly clear (although it does get a li'l bit 'buzzy' if you are using high-gain at high-volumes)! It has a line-in (which I've never used) and a handy head-phone socket for those silent practice sessions, particularly useful when your parents/room-mates are not in a good mood
This must've been a marshall employee who was making those amps. (sorry about the length of the quote about MG10)

So some time ago you guys fixed the display of chord diagrams for half-step down tuning (or I managed to finally persuade you to

author: thequadrat
text:
NSpen1
Thanks for the research, it definitely needs to be fixed.
By the way, I noticed also that transposing half-step down tabs on -1 gives you new chord names but the diagrams remain the same.
Actually, this is quite an interesting topic for research - how to show chords and diagrams on non-standard tuning tabs. Let's take the first tab from your post. I can imagine this could be a few options to show:
1. Chords by pitch and diagrams by pitch. xx0232 in half-step down is Db by pitch and this is the actual fingering to get this pitch. So, this chord and fingering will be displayed.
2. Chords by shapes, diagrams by pitch. xx0232 shows as D despite the real sound is Db. So the authors should use chords by shapes of standard tuning.
3. Chords by pitch, diagrams by shapes. Db chord name shows like that but the fingering shows you position for the standard tuning - x43212 (this is how tabs look on the site now and for me it's a bit weird)
I think most guitarists are used to use options 1 and 2. Option 3  is the most confusing in my opinion.
It's interesting to know the distribution of choices between these options among the users.

author: thequadrat
text:
Also, I think we have the only option to show chords and diagrams for open tunings - only by pitch because there will be custom diagrams.
And one more thing - dropped tunings. I prefer to see the drop D by pitch (000232 - D). But lower - by shapes of drop D (drop A:  000232 shows as D)

author: NSpen1
text:
thequadrat
Not that surprised because the tuning I was most concerned about was Eb, and I queried at the time which should be changed.  Even D tuning, I know that people do write it in both ways.  But then you guys decided to change how it worked for all down and drop tunings.
Well, this is for sure, a lot of these are people not knowing how to set the tuning.  I sometimes come across tabs set in random tunings when there seems no reason for it to be anything but standard, and in random keys that relate to nothing in the tab.  How many of the A tuning examples are really supposed to be in a low A tuning?  New York Dolls, Dean Martin, Johnny Hates Jazz with the first two of those also with key A set?  I'm sure they're not.  Bob Dylan in a "strange open A tuning.", that doesn't count, that's someone putting it to an A tuning because that's all there is (we need that custom tuning option!), A D G C E A not E A C# E A C#.
I find more open A and key A examples.  Maybe relatively few are correctly set for A tuning.  These "Tigapagi" ones seem to be the main exception, that are really for a low A tuning. "Notes: if using standards tuning transpose +5"
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/tigapagi/batu-tua-chords-2460938
So Dm for the first chord, transpose +5 = Gm for standard, that's the actual pitch.  If you play a Dm shape in A D G C E A tuning, that sounds as Gm.  That means those ones are written BY SHAPE, not BY PITCH.  I'm not convinced that any of the A tuning examples are actually for real A tuning written by pitch
Edit: yeah, so far for the A tuning examples I have seen zero evidence for people writing chord charts in a low A tuning by pitch.
Also, what if you have a song played on a 7-string?  There is no 7-string tuning option so it's easy to imagine that people will select B tuning as being the closest (and sometimes drop A).  In that case it's natural to think of the chord names as by pitch because you have all the same strings as a 6-string instrument, just with an added lower one.
So how do we do it?  With it working differently depending on the tuning??  I still feel strongly that it should work according to chord shapes for Eb tuning everywhere, and on balance for D tuning as well.
Here is Jeff Loomis describing something as being in the key of A minor (plays Am shape chord), but the tuning is C standard, so it's really F minor by pitch
Show

author: maguri

That's interesting history, I hadn't seen that.  So did they actually introduce the Ukulele category at the same time as they made all the bad ukulele copies from existing guitar charts?
Yup!, that came very close to each other
And sadly, tab authors weren't asked what they thought about the consequences of this change. We were really surprised to wake up one morning to find that we suddenly had lots of tabs added to our profile (and the IQ too ...). And then to realise that what had been added would not be good for our reputation as tabbers. After some time we had the uke-clones removed from our lists of contributions (and the IQ too) because we didn't want to receive the bad ratings that these Frankenstein-uke-tabs deserved ...
And now, seven years later, UG still works to clear that mess ...

author: Koenigtiamat
text:
Hi, folks!
We know that almost 10% of our community plays the piano. The ability to switch to piano chords was one of the most
suggested feature
for a long time. We heard you loud and clear. Therefore we're happy to introduce Piano chords mode for chords tabs!
From now on you can easily switch between guitar, ukulele, and piano chords in tabs to your favorite songs.
We'll be very happy to hear your feedback on the feature in the comment section below. If you find any problems, please leave a comment with the link to the tab and information about the issue.
FAQ:
How does it work?
-
Open any
Chord
tab (example:
Frank Sinatra - Fly me to the moon
), switch between piano, guitar, or ukulele in the CHORDS section of the tab (chord diagrams area). You can also use the "More settings" menu in the bottom right corner of the tab.
Is Piano mode available in Official tabs?
-
The
Piano mode is available in Chord tabs only.
We will add this mode for other tab types later this month.
Is Piano mode available in UG Tabs app?
-
I
t's not at the moment. But we plan to add it to the app later this month.
I found errors in your implementation of piano chords.
- Please, describe the problem in this thread and specify the browser you were using. Please, attach a screenshot, if possible. This will allow us to identify the problem.
I know how to make Piano mode even better!
- Leave your suggestion in this forum thread! We will definitely look into it. Perhaps your idea will be the next one we implement.
=)
Sincerely
Dmitry,
Tab Content Team

author: brimill68
text:
I made the transition to UG about a month or so ago after years of using old school paper. Published a few songs to UG, corrected others, etc. since. That said, a few observations / site suggestions.
1) Add a Mandolin Tabs / Chords song option.
2) A little more flexibility on the "no symbols / other text" in the chord line rule.
I saw in the tab guidelines that this is only "recommended" as opposed to "required," but I've been pretty clearly told to remove such characters. UG could add some limited symbols in the chord line and clearly state which ones are recommended in the tab guideline. Things like:
h/s ...to denote a single-strum, immediately-muted hard stop (I call this a chop)
s/s ...to denote a single-strum or soft stop (letting it ring)
| ...to denote bar breaks, esp. in solos and musical interludes. There seems there is disagreement among UG moderators on this. I had such pipes rejected as per the above "no symbols / other text" rule, but its very handy when breaking up solos where sometimes the number of chords in each bar differs. See example below from Heart of Gold.
[Harmonica Solo]
|
Em
C
|
D
G
|
|
Em
C
|
D
G
|
|
Em
C
|
D
G
|
|
Em7
|
D
Em
|
3) A "Song Overview" as an optional section at the top of a song. I might add these anyway unless it's prohibited, but I'm thinking a section that just reviews the broad song structure which in most cases is all I need to play it since it's mostly (but not entirely) memorized. I usually just need the first 3-4 words of the section. This would be easily viewable on one screen (no scrolling) on a smartphone when our and about. Something like:
Song Overview
- INTRO - Em F# x4
- VERSE 1 - This is what...
- CHORUS - Falling...
- VERSE 2 - Now that...
- OUTRO - Em F# x3

author: brimill68
text:
BTW
NSpen1
, I noticed you were the one who posted the edit to the Heart of Gold solo using the pipes as bar separators. I gather that UG is fine with using pipes in solo or instrumental sections? ...but not in chord lines above lyrics?
Would still love some kind of standardized notation for hard and soft stops in the chord lines above the lyrics. This would be especially nice when playing in groups as having everyone hit that stop at the same time is essential.

author: NSpen1
text:
brimill68
Ah, that was a combination of

and me on Heart of Gold actually
Yes, that would be my view, use | as bar divisions in instrumental sections, but not in chord lines above lyrics (generally, there may be the odd exception where it's useful to do so).  If anyone is telling you to remove | from instrumental sections then they really shouldn't be.
You pretty much can do those kind of stops you are talking about already.  Use N.C., e.g Em N.C. for a hard stop.  And some people use * = single strum (just put that at the top of the tab), e.g. Em*.
I don't mind your idea of a song overview, not sure what others might think.  And sometimes moderators can be too strict about removing notes at the top of tabs, when  often there can be helpful information there.
We probably need to add Ukulele Tabs (as opposed to Chords) before Mandolin.

author: leahyse
text:
I have one simple and easy (yet important) suggestion as it pertains to new tab submittals. Currently, when a user populates the form with Song Name, Artist Name, etc one of the most important fields is Tuning. Presently, users must choose from a predefined list of tunings, but some artists utilize some rather obscure tunings which are NOT on the predefined list. Moreover, among the choices listed, there is no option for "Other tuning". As a result, authors must note in the body of the their submittal (and in the optional description field) what the intended turning is. This isn't a big deal except that the website also assumes and displays "EADGBE" when a user is unable to choose from the predefined list of turnings (this results in inconsistent turnings displayed on the Tab).
This issue can be corrected by either I) adding another entry in the list called "Other tuning", ii) OR eliminate the predefined list of choices altogether and let users enter the 6 letter tuning (as they do with most other information). Data integrity can be controlled by ensuring 6 letters are entered in the field (and you could still make the "default" entry be EADGBE (so long as it can be edited by the user).  Personally I like the second option better as more users know (with certainty) their intended turning (but not necessarily) the common name equivalent of their tuning (and your list is currently based mostly on common name references). A more subtle detail might pertain to the "show chords" option for users viewing and printing the tab. For songs in "Other Tunings" I would further suggest that the "show chords" option be disabled (tab authors should detail their intended chord voicings for songs in "Other tunings".
Thanks in advance for considering this change. Hopefully its an easy fix.

author: NSpen1

There would be room in the drop down list to spell out most of the tunings in addition to the name actually.

1. People use the Edit button to create personal tabs.
2. If someone wants to make his changes public, he/she could use the Publish to UG button.
3. We warn them about creating duplicates and suggest to create a corrections if changes are minor.
4. We ask people t create a version description. Then a tab will be submitted and appears in the queue.

- approve tab as a new tab version if there are a lot of changes
- convert it to a correction to the existing if changes are minor
- reject it

author: whistlingcow
text:
Well deleting my account (so I could change my username) deleted all my forum posts....so, here I am posting my opinion again.
I guess I'll just note that it's a bit ironic to solicit site suggestions and then ignore them.
---
The way the tab pages are laid out makes it tempting to use the "edit" button rather than the "correction" button.  This means a large number of new users are creating edits which are actually corrections and this is very apparent in the approval queue.  It'd be a simple fix to change the "edit" button to read "edit copy" and place a "correction" button right next to it (rather than only at the bottom).  I think this would largely fix the issue of new users creating edits which are really corrections, alleviate some frustration with the approval process, and encourage community participation in general.
Actually, on further thought, why is there a difference between the correction workflow and the edit workflow.  These two workflows should ideally be combined.  With a public correction, publish as new tab (with a second page which confirms and maybe encourages editing metadata), and a save as personal tab.  Anyway, that seems like a larger change, fixing the buttons would largely fix the problem immediately.
Thanks,
Manfred
P.S. I created my own thread, but this probably fits better here.  Anyway, take this as one more vote to fix the "edit" button.
---
Encouraging participation is good.  But, you also want the interactions to be good.  If you go look at the approval queue you'll find that the first interaction of a bunch of people in the approval queue is confusing and demotivating.  Several people have basically said "forget about it, I'm taking my ball and going home." In response to the edit mess, which could have been easily avoided by just relabeling the buttons.  You don't want to optimize your participation metric without regard to the long term effects.  And in this case, maintaining the current situation is increasing "participation" in the short term but driving people away in the long term.
---
mandelstamdavid
I did read the entire thread, but thanks for dismissing me so easily.
I may be a new user, but that's exactly the perspective you're asking for.  It's very confusing to a new user as is apparent from the personal anecdotes expressed here and by the content of the approval queue.  Also, I may be new to the guitar, but I'm not new to website design.  The tabs page has confusing buttons.  The best thing to do would be to combine the workflow for making edits, saving personal tabs, and publishing corrections so that you can use the same button everywhere.  From a user's perspective those shouldn't really be different things.  The next best thing to do is to make it absolutely crystal clear what the very similar buttons you're making available do and how they're different.  You made the statement "1. People use the Edit button to create personal tabs."  That is not clear from a button labeled "edit", particularly when another button in a different place on the page is labeled "correction" and doesn't do the same thing.  If your intention is to convey that one of those buttons should be used to create personal tabs, then you've failed.
So in answer to your question "Do you really think that this process is confusing?"  The answer is yes, I do think it's confusing.  I think it's confusing enough that I, a completely new user, got annoyed enough that I figured out how to post in the forums to complain about it as one of my first community interactions.
From an open source community building perspective (another area I have some experience with) I also think the way this thread is being handled is pretty bad.  The development team is saying "no" with basically no data backing them up when the most prolific community volunteers are annoyed about an issue that would be very simple to address.  In that sense, it doesn't even matter if you're right or wrong, it's bad community outreach and makes your most valued volunteers feel ignored.  Just make the change, it's not worth your time.
Mic drop...(I don't intend to reply further on this thread, you have my perspective.  I'm going to go practice guitar and hope this gets fixed.)

author: pmalavi
text:
I've noticed some confusion around strumming notation and what the muting symbols mean ("X" vs. "x+arrow" vs "Rests"). To help address this, I think the UG Tablature Guide could make a more clear distinction between these strums:
1.
Fully muted / percussive strums
: chord hand lightly touches strings to fully mute, open strum (i.e. not palm muted)
- UG strumming notation: X
2.
Partially muted / palm muted strums
: chord hand creates full pressure chord, palm muted strum
- UG strumming notation: x+arrow
3.
Staccato strums
: chord hand creates full pressure chord, open strum, then chord hand immediately lifts to lightly touch and mute strings
- UG strumming notation: " (R = rest)
To reflect this, here are a few minor suggested changes to the Tab Guide:
- Section 1.9.B.5, 3rd bullet: change to "to add palm muted (partially muted) strums, press Ctrl + up or down buttons"
- Section 1.9.B.5, 4th bullet: change to "to add percussive (fully muted) strums, press X"
- Section 1.9.B.5: add a new 5th bullet that says "to specify a staccato strum, add a rest immediately following the strum by pressing R"
- Section 1.9.B.6, 2nd bullet, 4th sub-bullet: change to "... fill in the pause on the 3rd beat with a *partially* muted strum."
*** Background: this all stemmed from a recent chat about strumming notation for one of my tabs. Here's the thread FYI:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/maroon-5/memories-chords-2831476

author: brettsanace
text:
pmalavi
I like what you are proposing but the one change I would suggest is for Number 2. Apart from partially muted and palm muted strums (which I think are basically the same thing) we also use the X+arrow symbol to represent a partial strum when only ony or two strings are strum (but not necessarily muted) as is often the case when it is a transition strum. Also when doing patterns for songs that use fingerpicking we will sometimes use the X+arrow to represent a bass string pluck which is often followed by a strum (or pluck) of several treble strings. Ideally it would be great to have different symbols for every scenario but we don't, so we have to be a bit flexible with the ones we have. I know this post is the result of the discussion we had on the pattern for "Memories" so, whilst it is generally good to do so, I also don't think you should always base patterns on how they sound in the playback/listen feature because the partially muted and fully muted sound identical (though UG claim that they don't). With the "Memories" pattern I used the x+arrow as a partial strum as only one or two strings were played (I can't remember now) but you interpreted it as being a partially muted strum which in the playback sounds like a fully muted strum so you didn't like it. I am not criticising you as you were just following the guidlines, but I was just trying to provide the best interpretation given the limited options available in the strumming interface. Cheers

author: pmalavi
text:
Regarding the on-going "EDIT" button debate, here's an idea for your consideration:
- Remove the small "Edit" button that allows Level 4 users to edit a published tab
- Remove the "SUGGEST CORRECTION" button at the bottom of every tab
Instead, have a single "EDIT" button located where the current button is. Just as you've done with chords, usernames and contributors, a floating pop-up window could appear with a set of choices when a user hovers over the "EDIT" button. The choices could be labeled as:
1. Submit correction for review
2. Submit brand new version for review
3. Modify and save as personal tab
4. Edit existing tab
A few notes:
- Option 1 would take users to a "Submit Correction to TPA" page (replaces the previous "SUGGEST CORRECTION" button)
- Option 2 would take users to a "Submit New Tab to TPA" page (replaces the previous "PUBLISH TO UG" button in the Save As Personal Tab page)
- Option 3 would take users to the "Save as personal tab" page (no change except the "PUBLISH TO UG" button must be removed)
- Option 4 would allow direct edits and only appear in the pop-up list for Level 4 users (replaces the previous small "Edit" button)
Benefits of this approach:
1. A single Edit button that covers all forms of editing
2. Precise descriptors telling users exactly what their editing is doing within the system
3. A clean user interface that avoids multiple buttons or long button names

author: h0spid
text:
Guys, today we want to introduce you one cool (we hope it's cool) feature to try -- rich-text editor for post reply. So with it, you will be able to see how your post looks like before submitting it, people call it WYSIWYG or a rich-text editor.
Actually, we started this project from the idea that we don't want to use long and clumsy bb-code for mentions. We decided to use Facebook's plugin called draft.js in post reply to implement rich-text editor instead of old-fashioned bb-codes. This project was not very easy to implement and it's still in beta cause draft.js is an absolutely new technology for us and it's the first big project of our junior front-end developer .
Here is how it looks like:
To enable it just click "Try new reply form", the page will reload you'll get the new form:
Here is the list of known issues:
- 'mention' option may not work in some rare cases (investigating this issue)
- 'spoiler' option is not working for images, only for text (working on it at the moment)
- some issues may occur from mobile devices
- insert link and image forms are not sexy looking
So if you have the free time and want to help us, please try it and leave your feedback and suggestions here. You can also mention Nikcrysis anytime with any questions and bug reports -- he will in touch with you all the time.
Important:
you can return back to old form any time you want, but please note that if you have any text in reply field you will lose it. So it's better to switch between new/old fields with no text in it.

author: ckindle56
text: I found a workaround to this problem.  A chart can be edited, transposed, & saved  in  the Android app.  Then it can be printed correctly in the transposed key via Windows (or the Android app).  However, the chart will have to be saved in the transposed key in the editor until you transpose it back again to the original key & saving it in the Android app. This transpose issue appears to only be present in the  Windows Ultimate Guitar web site.

author: thesandrock
text:
001charl
The easiest way to do a personal tab of a transposed song is to transpose the tab, select/highlight the entire song, copy it (Ctrl C), then click edit, delete the original chords and text (Ctrl A, delete), then paste the transposed version (Ctrl V) and save to your personal tabs (oh, and change the capo before saving). That seems a long winded explanation but on a laptop/computer it's a 2 second job, maybe 10 seconds if you don't use the keyboard shortcuts. I know it's a work around rather than a solution but hope it helps

text:
The toolbar at the bottom of the tab/chords (FONT, SHOW CHORDS, TRANSPOSE etc.) obscures part of the text, rather than sitting fully below the text box. Hitting the PageDown key will scroll the page to start below the last 2 lines of the tab that were hidden by the toolbar, so you'll have to scroll back one line to see these lines at all. Should be a simple change to scroll a bit less to make PageUp/PageDown keys more useful on UG.

Sebastian.

author: Benster28
text:

I agree about the live video links, you add all the info on the edit page but users can't see the link on the tab page. Should be fixed.
As for acoustic versions, we always confirm the nature of the tab with the author before approving.
