author: That_Guitar_Man
text:
To Ultimate Guitar,
Recently I've notice many tabs have been taken down. I find so many have been taken down that sometimes you search for a song and all the tabs for that song are now gone.
THE PROBLEM:
Currently how your system works is all tabs that have ever been uploaded seem to populate the list when you search for one. This is a pain for the users of this site because if the tab has been taken down then the only way to find out is to click on it and see this message:
The material that was posted to this page was removed from the site. Ultimate Guitar received a takedown notice from the copyright owner claiming that the user submission was an infringement of their rights. In compliance with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act we have removed the submission as requested by the owners.
The Digital Millennium Copyright Act gives the person who posted the material the right to file a counter notice to dispute the removal of the material. If you posted the material and you believe the identification of the material as infringing was incorrect and that your submitted material should be reinstated then you must submit a formal counter notification with the information set forth here
And furthermore, the first time I encountered this message I just saw a big blob of text and spent a couple minutes looking for the download link. Then I switched tabs thinking it was on a timer or something. Only later I finally read it and saw the takedown message.
POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS:
There seems to be a couple ways to deal with this issue. I thought the easiest thing for the site owners for now would be to load some kind of image or large text saying "THIS TAB HAS BEEN TAKEN DOWN" then have the long message below it after you click on a tab link. This would at least help people who haven't encountered the message yet.
In addition to that I thought maybe the taken down tabs should no longer populate search lists. I posted about this subject in the tab talk forum and a user responded with this suggestion as well:
Quote by linkno1
I agree with this though I think they should still appear in the search, they should be noticeably altered so that I know they have been taken down before I click on them. This way if I ever search for something that has been taken down I know it has and know not to bother tabbing it myself and trying to upload it. I don't write tabs but yano, I'm sure it would save others the same effort.
I don't mean anything special when I say "noticeably altered", they could just put it in the column that says what type of format the tabs are (I.E Tab, Bass, Drums, Guitar pro, Power tab)
Doing this would also be an acceptable solution. The bottom line is I just think it would be more convenient to users to warn people beforehand of the tab being taken down or at least make the message already in place more noticeable.
Great site otherwise though! I've been using this since ive picked up a guitar about 8 years ago.

author: January85
text:
I think the way the site handles different versions of tabs could be improved because often the best versions get buried.
I'm not sure how this could be best achieved, so I'm opening a discussion.
I was checking out if Out Of the Silent Planet by Iron Maiden had an accurate Guitar Pro tab and there are two versions with 4.5 stars that have the very first riff completely wrong, which makes it incredibly difficult to play. So, I went through all the five versions and every single one of them is wrong. Then I noticed that OH! there's a hidden section that you have to click to even see all the tabs.
Why does this "View 2 versions more" exist?
Does it somehow save on queries from the DB? I can't believe that. Or is it there because 20 years ago we had smaller screens and not everything could fit on the screen? Perhaps, but I don't know why everything should fit on the screen. Why can't they just be listed there and if you have to scroll, then you scroll. Why are the best tabs hidden behind this link?
Which brings me to the final point. The latest tabs are often,
not always,
but often the best versions of the tab. This was the case with the example song here. The final version actually had the correct intro riff. The first versions are from days gone by when anyone could upload anything and there are cases when three different people just uploaded the same tab with different instrument names or something (check out Infinite Dreams by Iron Maiden). The ratings barely work for obvious reasons. Anyone can rate the tabs and if most of the people posting the tabs don't know what's wrong with them, then why would most of the people viewing them know? It's like if I was asked to rate professional diving.
And one more thing. I noticed many times that there's a tab for a song with hundreds of ratings giving it 5 stars. Yet, there are seven more versions for that song, cluttering the search results and, apparently, even the "More Versions" section on song pages. Moderation is always difficult, but for conversation's sake, is there something that could be done? If we had infinite resources, would there be a way to make the site better in this regard?
Now, I do realize that this isn't an easy issue with a simple solution, but I think we can do better than this, yea?

author: theogonia777
text:
I feel like it isn't really a necessary thing because you can look at the guitar chord charts and then just use a mandolin chord finder to find tge four chords that the song uses.  Especially if they are common chords that you really should have memorized or are movable chord shapes.  It's necessary to have the chord voicings for guitar because the song might voice the chord in a particular way.  But with the mandolin, you're not playing the same voicings alon mandolin as you would on guitar due to the wider intervals between strings and so if you already don't have the same voicing, that it kind of doesn't matter which one you use.  Especially when any "mandolin" chords are just going to be automatically copied from guitar chords and thus they won't have any specific voice chosen.
An important part of learning to play the mandolin is learning to play a number of entirely stopped chords (no open strings) in as small a range on the fretboard as you can.  You really need to learn these voicings in order to chop because chopping doesn't work with open strings.  This is something you're not going to learn if some arbitrary voicing full if open notes is given to you rather than you figuring out the chord from a dedicated mandolin chord finder that will allow you to select from a number of closed position voicings up the next.  For example, 7523 or 4523 for G.  I guarantee you that if UG automatically generates mandolin chords it will give you 0023.  Not the voicing you want because it has open strings.

"EXTRA EXTRA! Kids play video game, and they really enjoy it!"

author: drmichael
text:
Okay, so I was trying to think of THE best way to find new songs to learn.  Here's what I came up with:
Add some sort of search option where you can either input your last.fm artists or where you can input all of your favorite bands (separated by commas).  And then make it so that this search is sorted automatically by most popular tabs from that artist (most popular could be comprised of a rank of most views or ranking as well as highest ranking).  And THEN also make it so that you can add filters to this list (for example: only show tabs of 4 stars or better, only show guitar tabs, only show chords, combinations of those, etc...).
Basically this would be the best way to find new songs to learn.  This would just show all of your favorite bands and their best songs/tabs.  I realize that you can currently type in each band one by one and look through all tabs, but when you have 20+ bands that you love and each of those bands have 30+ songs, that can be quite time consuming.
Please vote on how useful this idea sounds to you.

author: Shady Guy Jose
text:
Hello. I apologize if this is the wrong section, but I thought it would be more appropriate than the general tab section. I found a tab for a song I wanted to learn in Guitar Pro format. However, as I was playing the song, I noticed a few mistakes and made the appropriate changes in the tab. In the solo, I actually made a lot of changes, and big ones at that. Since the final version ended up being quite different, and I also added the voice track, I thought it could very well be uploaded as a different version. However, since it was based on a previous one, and I wouldn't want the original tabber to go uncredited, I tried to upload it as a correction. Yet that option only allows for ASCII tabs. Is there any way I can post this as a correction, or am I stuck trying to upload it as a different version and crediting the previous tabber in the description, risking even a rejection for being similar?
Thanks in advance.

author: ruker
text: You could try contacting the tab's creator, to have them update their tab. If they're unregistered or unresponsive, I'd say just submit it as a new version. When I come across unresponsive users, I'll just give them some credit in the score info.

author: fanapathy
text:
^Seconding that. This is OK but only if you
1)Ask the original tabber
2)Give him/her credit for relevant tracks in the tab
3)Actually have significant changes (a couple of notes in a solo or a chord isn't enough and that makes the "16 versions" problem, just saying - but I understand you got big corrections in this case)
Sometimes tabs will be from old mysongbook or otherwise have no contact info on creator, would be fine to submit it then.
I've done this a couple of times but ended up re-transcribing the whole thing eventually, for example if the main riff is wrong, in general everything else will be sloppy too.
I'm all for having the most accurate version on the site and think is quite alright with permission.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
chemicalvip
, what exactly is this contributing, though?
You can't compare tabs and chord charts. Chord charts have more tools to help people find what they want, and the tool set includes transposition.
For example, Am F C G throughout one chart is
identical
to Em C G D with capo 5. If the latter were the existing version on site, a +5 on the transposition tool will get you to the former chords. Saying that the two are different is simply untrue.
The queue approval guidelines specifically say to reject duplicates with minor corrections. Such chord chart transposition, along with general line breaks and one chord - which is wrong - constitutes "minor corrections" at best, regardless of the amount of time spent reaching the same conclusion. Ignorance regarding the transposition function on the sidebar doesn't erase its existence or excuse the fact that you wrote it down as your tab description.
This sort of thing has happened before, and with far fewer guidelines explicitly stating what is accepted and rejected. That's what happened to calculus in the case of Newton and Leibniz, though unfortunately it was Newton who had a larger sphere of influence, regardless of who published first (the latter). In the case of tabs, though, since everyone is drawing from the same source of material (a third party, the same track cut for artist Lana Del Rey), reaching the same conclusion only esteems publication date.
Incidentally, you can always use your variant as a
personal tab
. However, harassing other people or resorting to personal remarks - even edited - just because they don't share a deeply entrenched opinion, is unacceptable no matter where you are.

author: Andrewbiles
text:
This isn't for the admins to worry about but rather the users who are submitting tab requests.  Please check your spelling and search before submitting a request.
Going through them I'm finding a lot of basic errors in spelling and deleting the requests.  If you're not sure about the spelling of a song title search for the artist and have a look through the pages.  Some requests have been for 'Hotel California' (missing the 'r'), 'Suffragette City' (using double 'g'), 'Whisky in the Jar' (missing the 'e'), 'What Iv Done' (missing the 'e') and 'Knockin on Heaven S Door'.  These are all popular songs and have lots of tabs already.
There are plenty of dictionary websites, and if you just search the word in google it will give you spelling corrections.  Also keep in mind the differences in British and American spellings (e.g. 'favourite' and 'favorite').
If you're requesting songs that do already have versions up please provide an explanation.  Yeah some tabs are bad but a lot of people don't check tunings - easy to skip over - and really just don't read what the tabber has said.
Thanks.

author: rkl3
text:
I had submitted this previously as a Music News article, knowing full well it would never be published on the UG site.  This is my opinion and surely that of 10's of millions of UG members.
WE NEED TO MAKE OUR VOICES HEARD!!!
Since its inception in 1998 Ultimate Guitar [UG] has framed itself as a "Guitarist Community Website".  As described on the UG YouTube channel; "Ultimate Guitar is the best way to play songs you love. Home to millions of quality tabs and the world's largest musician community."  Currently with some 60+ million members [as stated on the UG website], a vast majority being free subscribers,  with paid [Pro] subscribers as well.
The vast majority of these "millions of quality tabs" have been submitted by members, who are not compensated for their submissions, to make this site what it has become today.
Over the past 27 years members, both free and paid, have been able to view, play along with, download and print these tabs, other than those marked as "official" or "Pro", at any time FREE of charge.  The "official" and "Pro" tabs are I assumed compiled by UG staff at a cost to UG.  Myself, being a former Pro member and currently a free member, rarely use these "official" or "Pro" tabs as I personally have found them in most instances to be inferior to those provided by volunteers at no cost.
Recently, it was discovered that if you wished to download or print, for whatever reason, one of these volunteer submissions or even a "Personal" tab, that you yourself had created, are now hidden behind a "pay wall" forcing you to purchase a Pro Membership at a cost of $124.99 CDN annually or $30.99 CDN monthly.  That being said, the Pro membership does provide some "bells and whistle" features that are not available to a free member, however the vast majority of members, including myself, do not require or would never use these features.  Printing and downloading are ESSENTIAL and have always been FREE.  The vast majority of free members would not even notice or be aware of this change until such time as they require a downloaded or printed version of a volunteer submitted tab or their own Personal tab, for that matter.  No prior warning or heads-up had/has been given to the membership of this or other changes; as a major update to the tab format appears to coincide with this change. [The pros and cons of the format changes are being discussed in the Community Forums on UG]
When the inability to download/print was first reported as a "Bug Report" on the Community Forum at the end of March 2025, the report was moved to the "Site Suggestions" forum on the website with a response from UG Support; "Printing is part of the Pro service.   Due to recent requirements, we had to disable access to the Print feature on the website.   To use the Printing feature, a UG Pro subscription is required."
This change has left literally 10s of millions of UG members unable to download or print these "millions of quality tabs"!  Why the change? No answers or reasoning has been provided to the members.  This has left many members with a very soured opinion of UG, which has been expressed in several threads on the UG Community forums.  UG Support has stated they are taking feedback and will report it to the "Development Team", which is commendable, however it has been over a month with no response from UG decision makers.
How can it be fair for UG to compile "millions of quality tabs" from uncompensated volunteer "authors" and to now, after 27 years, turn around and demand to make an increased profit from material that essentially does not belong to them, but belongs to the members who built this website!
This decision needs to be reconsidered.
Submitted by an 8 year UG member and former uncompensated tab author.

author: UG Support
text:
rkl3
hi!
Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed and passionate message. We truly hear you — and you’re not alone in these concerns. We completely understand how frustrating this change has been for long-time users like yourself who have contributed so much to Ultimate Guitar over the years.
First and foremost, please know that your feedback — and the feedback we've been receiving from other members of the community —
will be shared directly with our Development Team
. We’ve been actively compiling all user input on this topic and continuing to pass it along internally. You’re raising important points, and it’s absolutely essential for the people making decisions behind the scenes to understand the impact these changes are having on the real users who helped build UG into what it is today.
You're right: since UG's beginnings, the strength of this platform has been its community — the people who submit, refine, and engage with tabs day after day, often without any compensation. That foundation has always been at the core of what makes UG valuable. Your passion, your contributions, and your time matter. So when changes like this come along, we completely get why it feels like a betrayal of that spirit.
Regarding the Print and Download feature — yes, it’s now part of the Pro subscription. This was not an easy decision, and we understand that it feels like a sudden shift, especially without advance notice or a broader community conversation around it. To clarify: the change was made in response to updated platform requirements and internal restructuring around how features are offered — but that doesn’t mean your concerns aren’t valid. They are. In fact, they’re vital to helping us re-evaluate how we balance monetization with community respect and transparency.
We also understand that for many users, the Pro features may not be needed or even relevant — and we’ve heard clearly that printing and downloading tabs, especially community-submitted ones or your own personal tabs, are not luxury features but essentials.
Again, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this has caused. We’re not ignoring the feedback. It’s being collected, reviewed, and passed up. That said, we understand the frustration grows when changes feel one-sided or go unacknowledged for too long. We’ll continue advocating internally for better communication, transparency, and hopefully more balanced solutions that reflect the needs of our diverse user base — especially the loyal contributors who helped build UG into the platform it is today.
Thank you again — not only for this message but for being part of the UG community for eight years, and for your volunteer contributions as a tab author. You have every right to speak up, and your voice matters.
With respect,
Aydar
UG Support Team

User-generated content (UGC) is protected by copyright law, meaning the creator retains the rights to their work.
This means that they have the right to control how their content is used, including selling it.
Additionally, the rights to publish/sell the lyrics and the chords are by the author of the song.
You probably claim to only sell the printing feature, but that's certainly up for debate. Without any songs this feature would be worthless, you could use it to make your own compositions (if you write them in plain text with a monospaced font, yeah why not) look a little nicer, that's it. You could only print pro tabs with it and to view pro tabs you need a subscription anyway.

author: jthm_guitarist
text:
I think the largest problem plaguing the forums today is the constant creation of spam accounts and threads. Most of the time, the entire list of threads on the front page consists of the same advertisement repeated five times. There obviously aren't enough mods/they aren't fast enough, but I don't think this problem should be solved by manpower.
These are my suggestions:
-Captcha required to create a new thread (this cut down spam on imageboards, not sure how willing the spammers will be to enter repeated captchas. Creating a new thread isn't a daily thing for most people so this shouldn't deter actual users.)
-1 new thread per day (the spammers will only get one thread made before their account is deleted)
-1 new thread per day for new users (say for the first x amount of days or posts you are a new user; I've seen this done on other forums)
I'm sure there are even better ideas.

author: nyr4chrwgc
text:
This has probably been suggested before, but given the age of UG and the lack of it being addressed, I'm going to attempt to describe the problem perhaps yet another time with the hopes that it gets some attention, as I think this would be a great addition (and honestly, the lack of it seems like a glaring oversight IMHO).
Sometimes authors of tabs/chords will notate the chords as though a guitar was in standard tuning even though it is actually tuned differently.  This allows the player to sight read a piece with familiar chord names without having to transpose them in their head, and while the chords specified are technically the incorrect notes with respect to what is actually being sounded because of the guitar's altered tuning, it is much easier for the player, especially beginners.
Conversely, other times the alternate tuning is specified by the author and the chord chart reflects the actual note names, not those of standard tuning.  While this is more correct in terms of reflecting the actual notes, one has to perform that transposition while reading chords over the lyrics while playing, which again is a bit more difficult.
For example, Elliott Smith's Alameda is played with the guitar tuned down a whole step to D (D G C F A D).  This means that the first chord played is Bb, but to a guitarist it is played like a C chord using the open C shape.  Because of this, I prefer to see the standard tuning chord names.  No problem!  I can simply use the transpose feature to shift things two half steps up and now I have those chord names above the lyrics.
Things are going swimmingly until I encounter a chord I don't know and look at the diagram...uh oh!  The chord diagrams have all been altered to reflect the transposition applied to the alternate tuning.  Using our Bb example, I am now displaying it as a C as desired to reflect which standard tuning fingering to apply, but the chord diagram is now showing what guitarists think of as a D major chord.  So, yes, if my guitar is tuned to D and I am trying to play a C major chord it would be the D shape, but that's not my objective in this case.  I want to play a Bb; I've only transposed the piece to help my sight reading.
Other times I have encountered tabs where an alternate tuning is shown, but the author has already transposed the chords to standard tuning.  In this case, the chord diagrams that the app is generating based on the alternate tuning are wrong.  E.g., for the Alameda example (this isn't actually the case for this song, mind you), the author would have already noted a C chord, but the diagram would display the D shape.  Once again, the user needs to transpose the song to see what should actually be played in the diagrams, but doing so results in the notes over the lyrics no longer displaying the standard tuning chords.
This creates a very inconsistent experience for the player that reflects the inconsistency of the user generated content, but I think some simple tweaks could help deal with it.
Some possible solutions:
1. Add a flag (checkbox/boolean) to the Transpose feature named "adjust chord diagrams" that is checked by default.  Then I could transpose the piece as desired, uncheck this and have the chord diagrams be unaffected by the transposition done for conceptual reasons.  The note names for the diagrams would need to be changed for this to be consistent with the chords over the lyrics, but the diagram, if left untransposed would be correct.
2. Allow one to change the tuning.  In the app ATM, if one clicks "tuning" in the "adjust" modal, it brings up the tuner and it doesn't appear that one can change the tuning provided by the author.  Since the app is diagramming the chords with respect to the noted tuning, changing the tuning to standard would correct the chord diagrams.  Note that for this to be useful, you might have to also include a similar flag as suggested in #1 to take into account whether or not the author charted the chords transposed to standard tuning already.  If it transposes all the chords over the lyrics in this case, we're back to square one.
3. Given the point in #2 about chord chart transposition varying by author, provide separate transposition settings for the chords over the lyrics and the diagrams.  This allows the user to address both independently to adjust for the way in which a given song was notated.  I.E., add a 2nd transpose input over the lyrics/chords.  Perhaps a check box somewhere  would suffice.
4. (Perhaps this could be combined with one of the solutions above) Allow a way to specify the tuning used for the notation in the tab/chord chart itself, so the app can take this into account when it generates chords/diagrams.
Thank you for considering this input and apologies if I am reiterating something you are well aware of and I recognize it as a nuanced problem, but am hoping perhaps one of my suggestions might lead to a simple solution that would work for most people, without being that difficult to implement.  Or perhaps there is an existing solution I am ignorant of, if so please let me know.
Thanks,
Kyle
(long time pro subscriber)

author: brettsanace
text:
nyr4chrwgc
Either I am missing the point or what you are saying is simply incorrect.
Your first point (2nd paragraph) you say the author notates the chords as if the song was played in standard tuning (when it is actually played a full step down) which would mean that for a Bb sound the author would actually write a Bb chord and the chord diagram would show the fingering for a Bb chord, but as you go on to say this will give the player more familiar chords but it will not sound correct I assume you mean they write the tab in standard tuning but using the chord shapes for full step down tuning so the Bb would be written as a C. Again this is no problem as the chord diagram will show the fingering for a C chord, but as you said playing this will not sound like the recording as it will sound like C rather than Bb.
However, what you have said in your next point (3rd paragraph) is not correct. You say "other times the alternate tuning is specified by the author and the chord chart reflects the actual note names". If by this you mean, the author has specified full step down and then written the first chord in the tab as Bb then that is simply a mistake by the author (unless they believe the first chord is actually an Ab) and it is not a problem with the UG functionality. If the author, has specified full step down tuning, then to represent a Bb they should be writing a C chord above the lyrics in the chord chart and the chord diagram will show the fingering for a C chord and will be called C so there is no need to transpose anything, (though if you do transpose, the chords in the chord chart and the chord diagrams will transpose correctly). When someone then plays the C chord using standard fingering it will sound like a Bb. This is how it works for chord tabs published on the site and is correct. Note however, there is a bug with with unpublished and personal tabs when non-standard tuning is used, whereby the chord diagrams incorrectly display the fingering for the pitch rather than the chord shape. I reported this over 2 years ago and received a reply from UG saying they were fixing it but of course it hasn't been fixed yet. Refer to:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=2338769
Edit: All my above comments were for the website, but it just occurred to me that you might be talking about the app where it also doesn't work (which is also noted in the linked forum thread above).

It would have a visible advantage over text tabs in terms of formatting issues (some browsers might not display text tabs properly) and the fact that they may include the actual staff, which gives users rhythmic information that may not be present in the text tabs, and may be more convenient to classically trained musicians who prefer musical staff to tab. It would also allow people to download the tabs without having to take the time to copy/paste the text and with no fear of formatting loss. For convenience, they could be divided into PDF-tab, PDF-staff, and PDF-combo, so people have a greater choice. Guidelines may also be implemented as to how they should be exported (what information they should include) in each case.
EDIT: something I posted below, which I think might be convenient here:
Quote by Shady Guy Jose
Just so that anyone with actual power to implement this (or anyone curious) can see what I mean, this is an example of what I described as a PDF-combo of the song I Am... All of Me by Crush 40. This was generated by Guitar Pro 6, using only the guitar track of my own tab for this song (I will be uploading it in gpx format through the standard means when I finish all the tracks, which may take a while, since I have no experience ear-transcribing drums and I find the bass hard to distinguish in the mix, but I digress):
I Am... All of Me.pdf (587 KB)
https://mega.co.nz/#!MQVQRQSb!V8zDy1h-N5uZ7j2Cis4jIyOY9e4hWKAF1yQc19Q2IAM

I love how the responses here all seem to relate to "you have no choice", "you should have thought about that before", with no actual reason given. Heaps of users wanting to change there names? Well, if so many would want to do it- I don't see why you wouldn't have that service.

Reasons?
If you can have people change their names, it becomes harder to keep track of who is who (bans/warnings etc).
If people have been reported for suspected bad trading, then changes their name, how are future traders meant to check if that user is trustworthy.
If people have the option to change their names, you'd have a ton of people imitating threadstarters or admin.
If only admins have the power to change names, it's a lot of work to go through the potentially thousands of requests for name changes.
If you make this time an exception, you set a precedent which allows other users to at least appeal against the rule.
If you want the option to delete profiles, it'd enable people to get rid of their warning record, effectively nullifying the sites rules.
one last thing...
they don't need to give reasons, it's a private site and the owners can set out any terms and conditions they like, and basically those terms and conditions give mods and admins power to do what they like with or without reason (at least, zappp doesn't need to justify himself to anyone)

text:
So this is something which I asked for right at the start when strumming patterns came in, it's well past time I raised it again.
There are many strumming patterns which would work better with a rest symbol that could be used to cut the sound off.  Some patterns are just not going to sound right with all the strums ringing out, and could even be misleading.   At the moment I and
brettsanace
and
Lardin
and a few others are improvising by using the X to indicate a rest.  But this is not ideal obviously, the X still makes a sound even if it's not that loud and we want a complete absence of sound.  Also it makes things difficult if you have a pattern where you want rests, percussive strums and/or muted strums, there aren't really enough symbols to do that properly.
And I'm getting tired of telling people we don't have a proper rest symbol :
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=72561
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=36761
How to implement it?  Obviously it's not practical to use the standard musical notation for rests and have a different one for each note length - quarters, eighths, 16ths, we need one symbol that can be used everywhere.  My suggestion, some kind of a solid black block, I was thinking of a square initially but maybe that's not the best shape to fit.  I'm open to other ideas!  Though maybe I'm wrong, there would actually only be 3 different symbols needed for the note lengths, less than I was thinking, as triplets won't affect it, you can tell me if it's possible.
To enter it into a pattern, simply press r.

may be the guy who would be involved with this on the technical/programming side.

https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/dragon/april_sun_in_cuba_chords_138103
I think only a single rest symbol would be required as the rest length would be indicated via a combination of the strumming template being used eg Eighths or Sixteenths and the number of blank (strums) spaces following the rest symbol within the pattern.
It would be good if this function was added as quickly as possible, as the list of tabs using the improvised solution grows longer each day which is not ideal as using the same symbol "X" to represent two different things (Percussive strum and Rest) is confusing for users, especially when the ones intended as a rest don't sound like a rest when the pattern is listened to, and it will take more and more effort to go back and amend the affected patterns after the Rest symbol is introduced.

author: brettsanace
text:
evfidripiy
There shouldn't be any new sounds involved. You already have the sound of silence (ha that's a good one) as you can start a strumming pattern on beat 2 so the start of the pattern is silent so the issue is when to terminate the sound of a strum which you are already doing as well. If a pattern has a downstrum followed by an upstrum the downstrum sound stops when the up strum is played. If you have a pattern with a downstrum on beat one and the next strum is a downstrum on beat 3 then the first strum will ring until beat 3 at which time it stops because of the new strum. So we don't really need any new sounds, we just need a new rest symbol and a strum will continue to ring until it encounters the rest symbol at which point it stops, just the same as if it encountered another strum.

author: evfidripiy
text:
NSpen1
, the user way usually "search tabs in google - ultimate guitar is the first link - oh thanks guys let me play this song to my girlfriend". They don't want to learn something, they just want to play the song in the fastest way
So they will see strumming with pause - "oh ok, i'll pause the strum right here"
They will see the musical notation rest symbol - "wtf is this?" - he is searching for another tab.
Also there is no place to put an explanation, so symbol should explain himself.
Personally I want people to understand the musical notation, but in the real life people on UG don't want to learn something, they want to start playing immediately. And strumming pattern is the thing for absolutely beginners, so I don't want to force newbies to do something. Let them just enjoy the guitar

author: Steve7878
text: There was a previous post (that I cannot find), Where countless folks complained because they didn't like the way this was done or that was labeled. I even commented on it myself but wasn't entirely right. We, (all of us), need to understand that UG is global. Therefore there HAS to be a standard for making tabs. Standards are important. We have standards in place for all kinds of things. Imagine if we had no standard for American made bolts and nuts. Or metric even. No standard for building cars? Nothing would fit together. Now I can take a car and put my own standards on it if I wanted. I can cut off nuts and bolts, weld on them, make my own standards. But there HAD to be a standard made in the first place. If you do not like the standards set in place then do what I do. I learned to use the personal tab section. In there I can make the tab anyway that I like to. Don't like Brackets? Great! don't use them. Want to triple indent something? Great ! Do it! Want to leave a line Blank? Nothing wrong with that! But whatever you do leave the standard alone. It's there for a reason

author: fanapathy
text:
If you go to your contributions:
https://my.ultimate-guitar.com/main.php?mode=contributions
- you'll see its status there, assuming you submitted the tab while logged in to your account. W means Waiting (still in queue), D means Denied and A means Approved. You can click "Tabs" to see a list of your approved tabs.
There should also be an option to turn on email notifications so that you get an email when tabs are approved/denied - but I can't seem to find it right now.
How long tabs stay on the list varies greatly, right now the queue is still large after the holidays. It can take anywhere from 1 day to 2 months before a decision is made, but usually within 2 weeks.

author: samoo
text:
For quite some time, the Blues and Jazz forum has been pretty dead, while the Other forum has perhaps 2 to 4 active threads.
My suggestion would be to merge the two, and name the single forum "Blues, Jazz, Soul, Hip-Hop" or something along those lines.
This would encourage more new threads, busier and more lively debates, and also give the people who want to discuss a certain artist an actual chance of getting replies.

author: Amuro Jay
text:
My take on this is that by doing that you'll be excluding all of the electronic music, which is a bulk of what makes up the Other forum.
And I mean, if you really just mean merging the two, well, it's counter-intuitive to the organization of the forums. We do it based on music genres. Usually. Putting dubstep into the same forum as blues, as the same forum as kpop, makes no sense.

author: Colohue
text:
As with all of the 'only' threads, they are fast moving. However, the regulars typically answer all the questions they can, often repeating themselves several times in order to do so. Without the thread there would simply be a ton of others that would be constantly pushing other threads down. This is pretty much exactly what happens to the posts in the 'only' threads.
Put simply, new threads are just pushing the 'only' thread further and further down when posting there would simply add a post to the end of it. Often a new thread for a gaming question is rather pointless as it's answered within one post anyway. Or, knowing the Pit, it's answered within the first twenty or so, once you scroll through the memes and the abuse.

author: divid3d
text:
we understand that it can be difficult to be noticed in fast moving threads like the gaming thread, but it's exactly the same thing in the forum itself, on an even bigger scale. threads are made and forgotten about within hours, or sometimes even minutes if there is enough activity at that time to make them slip off the first page. our solution to the greater forum issue was to compile certain topics into the ONLY threads, so that current and fresh discussions on other topics would have a fair chance of being viewed and partaken in on the first page of the pit, instead of it being clogged up with relationship/religion/gaming/politics/sports/etc threads. currently, adding subforums to the pit is not an option, so this is the only thing we can really do to lower the thread count.
perhaps having just one gaming thread is not working though, i don't know as i don't spend enough time in there to properly judge how many posts are ignored, etc.
do you think having a "console gaming thread" and a "pc gaming thread" would help lighten the load and help people get better responses faster? this is just a suggestion btw, i'm not promising anything as it would need to be discussed with the other pit mods first, and i'd like some input from gaming thread regulars on this matter as they know how the current thread works better than anyone else.

author: GLP_Arclite
text:
We do our best to answer questions, but people have to realise that we just aren't able to answer every question put forward. We haven't played every game on earth, and quite often we just don't have an answer. I don't think a post in the thread is ever ignored, but if we responded to every question there would just be hundreds of "I'm sorry, I don't know" posts.
Also, quite often a quick google would sort people's problems out anyway. If I'm stuck in a game, the Gaming Thread isn't even close to the top of the list of places I'd go to for a solution. What we usually do is more with discussion of gaming, not answering questions.
IF there was going to be a splitting of the thread, a "Discussion" thread and a "Q&A" thread would make sense. That way most of the idle talk would be separated from the actual questions, but it doesn't guaruntee that people will actually get questions answered. Chances are us regulars would still be the only ones frequenting both, but it could stop people getting ignored when a thread is going fast. A better thing would be for people to just google things first, since far to often people have come in to the thread looking for answers, I've gone to google and it's been in the very first result.
EDIT: hehe, last few posts look like a gaming thread invasion.

author: Gaz_m2k5
text:
It's really annoying when people get pissy and complain that their questions go unanswered in the gaming thread.
It's a fast moving thread so I don't always see the questions. If people quote their own questions and say "any help?" then I usually see it the second time and give an answer.
I've had to start spamming the thread with posts like "I don't know" just so people don't feel ignored. Which usually follows me googling their problem and finding the answer, and then posting a link.
If we don't know the answer, then people can't expect a response. We're not google.
Infact most of the questions people ask should have just been taken straight to google. The amount of people that have said "so and so is wrong with my xbox, what do I do" or "how do I send my xbox for repair"
These questions could be much better dealt with by google.
Generally problems with consoles occur all over, so chances are the solution will be found by google. For PC games it's a lot more varied, but the computer help thread is good for that too.

do you think having a "console gaming thread" and a "pc gaming thread" would help lighten the load and help people get better responses faster?
No that's needless separation.
What we want if anything is a "gaming discussion thread" and a "gaming technical problem thread" thread, or they could just go and use the only computer thread, but I think that may be moving too fast already.

I'm new so maybe I haven't figured it out yet, but the chat system seems a bit old and awkward to use.  There are two free cross platform applications
Skype - audio and video conferencing

UG is working to fix this and trying to make sure the best articles are readily available.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Quote by daytripper75
If someone posts a shoop thread and the majority of the responses seem negative then I close it.
If it seems to be working well then I let it go.
This is how the majority of Pit mods handle shoop threads. If someone goes "lulz I wants to maek awsome sh00pin thred lolol" and posts some lame picture in a desperate effort to earn himself some e-cred, the thread will crash and burn fast. It usually doesn't even take a full page of negative replies before a mod closes it.
Occasionally, though, someone posts a really good picture resulting in some really funny shoopwork... and the mods won't touch these threads, they know the difference between a good and a bad shoop thread. So, let's not overcomplicate things for the mods. They do a very good job at sifting out the good threads from the crap ones. Also, I wouldn't want those threads to be forbidden in the future, because an "ONLY" thread exists, nor do I want the whole "one shoop thread at a time" rule - it spoils the fun, what's the problem if there are 2 good shoop threads running at the same time?
Furthermore, having an "ONLY" thread won't stop separate shoop threads from appearing regularly, since it overcomplicates things for the users too. New users who aren't aware of the vast amount of "ONLY" threads in the Pit will still post threads on subjects covered by those "ONLY" threads; for example, despite the "ONLY computer thread", people still post dozens of computer-related threads in the Pit. The same thing will happen if we make an "ONLY shoop thread".
So, tl;dr:
- The advantage of an "ONLY shoop thread" isn't so much an advantage, since you'll still see shoop threads popping up everywhere;
- The disadvantages are bigger than the advantages: an "ONLY" shoop thread spoils the fun of separate threads, and it also creates a lot of unnecessary work for the mods, like Matt said.
So, IMO... naw, dude.
ZEDIT: Sorry about the wall of text, just read the tl;dr at the bottom if you're lazy.

In order to fix the issue of unwanted space (which happens to show up between pages, as shown on UG's print preview page):
1.) In Firefox, click the 'hamburger style icon' at the top-right to open the options menu.
2.) Click 'Print..' to open Firefox's print preview page.
3.) Click 'Page Setup...' near the top-left of the window currently displayed.
4.) Where it say 'Scale' in the window that just opened, change 100% to 95% and click 'OK.'
This has fixed the unwanted space and printing formatting issues for me!

author: MazeDaBaze
text:
Hi!
I'd like to suggest two options regarding Links in Blog postings as well as in Group postings.
1) Option to add to links in Blog postings and in Group postings: target="_blank"
This option causes the link to open in a new browser window instead of the same one.
Since it's the nature of Blogs as well as Groups to include a lot of links, this option would be very helpful: On one hand, the author of a posting for sure doesn't want the reader to leave the own Blog or the own group thread without having finished reading - but readers too often don't come back, once they have clicked a link which hasn't the target blank feature (and that counts for blogs even more than for group postings, since in UG Blogs they would currently also have to scroll through the whole Blog again to find the posting that they had just read). And on the other hand, the requested option would for sure also raise the convenience for the readers of the postings.
2) Option to embedd videos in Blog postings and in Group postings
Other than in request postings, it seems not to be possible yet to embedd videos in Blog postings or in Group postings.
I don't know why embedding videos is currently only possible in request posting, but not in any in other forum postings. - But whatever the reason might be in regard to "normal forum postings", I guess that this reason doesn't also count for Blogs and Groups: Since each specific Blog and each specific Group only has a small target group (only a few regular readers), I think that embedding videos wouldn't cause any problems there.

author: UG Support
text:
MazeDaBaze
Thanks for the suggestions, they'll be passed to the developers!
I personally support the idea of target blank, but there are a few unpleasant tricks that can exploit this attribute.
Not that excited about embedded video, to be honest, but we'll think about it as well.

author: UG Support
text:
Hey guys,
Based on the results of our
first poll
we've set up a new one!
So, here's the deal.
Currently when you're using UG forum in mobile browsers you get to see 40 posts per page if the thread is long enough.
In our opinion this is a bit sucky because when 40 posts need to be loaded:
a. the page's loading time is long
and
b. more internet traffic is needed
We think that if we reduce the number of posts per page these two criteria could be substantially improved and you'll only benefit from it.
(Yes, we think even about such details).
So, please take this poll to help us determine the optimal posts/page ratio.
You're welcome to give your reasoning in the comments!
Thanks in advance!
UPDATE:
The poll is closed now.
Guys, thanks for sharing your opinions! Now it''s 20 ppp and according to our data we've substantially cut the page's loading time.
We'll be finetuning stuff for some time and if there are bugs, please do let us know in the comments.

author: divid3d
text:
i remember when half the pit was 'i broke up with my girlfriend'/'i can't get a girlfriend' threads, farking annoying :|
ITT, carmel speaks the truth. if something technically belongs in an ONLY thread but is a big enough topic/discussion to warrant it's own thread and is going well on it's own, then we make an exception and leave it. however, every single little trivial question someone wants to ask simply cannot have it's own thread, and that's why the ONLY thread exist, to clean up the clutter.
people will often name a thread "official" or "ONLY" but that doesn't make it so (and we don't have time to edit peoples' thread titles to remove this sort of thing when it's done). if it's not in the list of ONLY threads in the sticky marked "forbidden threads", then it's not recognised as an ONLY thread, and we won't close threads on those topics or direct people to use a single thread for those topics unless we see an abundance of the same thread being made over and over, in which case the 'fake' ONLY thread may be added to the proper list.
so - if people call a thread "ONLY"/"official", it's not a big deal. if it's crap, it'll die. if it's actually a good idea to have an ONLY thread for that subject, then it will thrive.

Not only is that a bad attitude, it's a bad idea.  I've seen threads that needed to be close even though they don't "break the rules".  Were it necessary to make a rule to cover every possible bit of aberrant behaviour, the list of rules would be unmanageably long.
Quote by reelbigfish2020
if a mod bans or warns someone or closes a thread and they are found not to be in the violation of anything, the mod should get warned or banned, or lose their mod privileges or authority for a few weeks. any support for this idea?
Absolutely not.
Create a situation where Mods have to be concerned about being sanctioned for ANY judgment call they make and they'll simply not make those calls.  This leads to
bad
users finding ways to become a nuisance for the forums in general.  It only takes one or two users who find the grey area to play in, and the overall environment becomes unpleasant for ALL.
To prevent a forum this large from becoming chaos, either the rules have to be extremely restrictive OR the Mods have to use judgment.
Extremely restrictive rules = no fun.
Restricted Mods = chaos.
Happy medium is happy.

author: mjuul1
text:
I suggest that UG removes the thing that prevents you from rating low if the system thinks that you have rated low too many times.
I consider myself as a serious user of this site and rate tabs after having tried them. And then suddenly I was hit by this rule.
I really can't see the point of this rule. According to UG, this rule is made to prevent people from abusing the rating system but that does not make any sense. Unless, of course, if think that all users have a tendency to rate randomly or are rating low of other reasons than the quality of the tab. In that case why have a rating system at all? If you have an open rating system you can never prevent some stupid people from abusing it but the majority will not. And since the majority are not trying to abuse the system, the rating will be fair in average.
But having a rule like this will actually make the ratings higher because some people will be prevented from rating low and other will not rate as low as the otherwise would because there are afraid that they will be prevented from rating low in the future.
So all in all you get a rating system that overrate the tabs and you prevent serious users from rating as they think is most fair - which in some cases means giving only one star to a poor tab.
I hope to start a debate about this subject since I believe this rule is counter-productive to the site.

author: Logz
text:
There is always some kind of quality control in any business or organisation. This is ours.
In regards to if the system works if you vote too high, there is no need. People who want to cause trouble for other members will always want to vote low.
The thing is though, its a big hassle to create new accounts, you need new emails, new usernames, you need to go through the registering process again. After a couple of times, people get tired of doing it then getting banned again.
The fact of the matter is, if this system deters malicious users from down-voting constantly, then its doing what it was designed to do. We wouldn't have implemented it otherwise.

author: Pencom
text:
Neo brings up some very interesting points.  I do, indeed, see merit in displaying strumming patterns, for some songs.  I think it would be silly to say otherwise.  As to whether those strumming patterns are actually correct is quite another matter.  Personally, I prefer to finger pick a song when possible.  I hope this does not give anyone any ideas of putting finger picking patterns on tabs.
I'd leave that question open for discussion at another time.
I am only speaking for myself but this strumming pattern issue brings up some major issues that I believe should be addressed.  The question I'm addressing to Zappp and the UG staff is rather fundamental; "exactly what are the responsibilities / obligations, moral or otherwise (if any) between UG and the people who posts tabs on the UG web site?"  These are questions and not "rhetorical" questions.
UG is in a sense a huge library.  A magnificent library of music tabs.  I believe it is the finest such library in the world.  Yes, there is more to the UG web site then tabs, but it is the music that is transcribed that really attracts its huge audience.  UG spends a significant amount of resources to provide this service and to keep the library open and thriving.  Staying within copyright laws and dealing with musical artists and their representatives is probably not easy, or cheap.  From time to time I've been a critic, but, frankly, it is very, very hard to find any fundamental fault in UG and how it is operated and managed.  If UG was a tab it would have all 5 stars.
When someone posts a tab (of any type) to UG it is reviewed and accepted (or not) for a variety of reasons that are well known and well published by now.  In a sense, the poster is providing UG with a book for its library. The person (s) posting the tab must abide by certain "standards" / regulations / rules / guidelines.   UG also wants to provide the tab viewer with the finest and most complete musical experience.  This is how it is and this is how it "should" be.  Having said all of that, I would like to believe that there is sort of an unwritten contract between UG and the people who provide the tabs.
The question, and this "is" the question: is there any such "unwritten" contract or understanding between UG and the people who posts tabs to the UG web site?  What are the obligations, responsibilities (if any) between the two parties?  If there are none then I believe it should be so stated in a prominent location on the UG web site.  If there are, however, some unwritten or unstated "assumptions" between the two parties then those, too, should be stated.
Here are some questions, I for one, would respectfully like to have answered.  I (and I suspect many others on this forum) would like some candor so we can put this to rest.
When someone posts a tab to UG it is not copyrighted.  It can't be.  The poster does not own the song or any rights whatsoever regarding the song.  This has all been well stated on the UG web site.
1.  Does UG now own the tab (s)?
2.  Does the poster of the tab give UG de facto rights and or to delegate the right to modify, change or reword said tabs?
3.  If UG owns the tab (s) can UG remove the name of the tab author?
4.  If UG does not feel that they own the tab (s) does UG feel the tab author (s) have any protections granted to their own work?  If so, what are those protections?
These questions may appear harsh or a bit too candid.  I sincerely don't want them to come out that way but I believe it is best to be up front on these issues so that there are no misunderstandings down the road.  My personal positions, highlighted by this strumming issue, is that anyone can and should place strumming patterns on their own tab if they so desire.  Also, anyone can and should place strumming patterns on someone else's tab "if" that person agrees to it.  The broader questions that I'm raising deal with the relationship, if any, between UG and the tab author community.

author: h0spid
text:
Hi UGers,
We have a new feature to introduce you today called Drafts. So from now you'll be able to create tabs on UG and be sure you'll never lose any change during tab creating -- every change will be automatically saved to the draft without any action from you, just like on Medium or Google Docs. Moreover, you will be able to work on your tab from different places, for example, start at work, then complete and submit from home or any other desktop device you are logged in with your UG account.
Drafts are private and other users cannot see them unless you submit tab to Ultimate Guitar.
So please try and let us know about your experience using drafts. Btw, here is how it looks like:
We also wanna thank tabs moderators who helped us with beta test of draft feature.

author: Mikaelwallen
text:
So throughout my maybe 7-8 years of occasional visits on this website and your various tabs and chord charts, I have noticed a few things.
First of all, the "limited" deals (Mostly consisting of 80 percent off the PRO subscription), are not limited. I do not think that I have not been exposed to these deals a single instant in all of the time I have been an active user on this website. Additionally, these deals are shown with a countdown, ranging all the way up from, what I can tell, 24 hours. And I did indeed wait one of these countdowns out, and it turns out it just resets after it ends. So the countdown and the seemingly "limited" deal, is not limited at all.
Second of all, the video that is provided besides many of the tabs or chords of a person playing the current song that me as a user is looking at the tabs for, is the same video for all of the songs. This stands true even though the title of the video is the title of the song, making it look like the video actually has to do with the actual song. This is also very misleading.
I tried to reach out to Ultimate Guitar for some answers to why it is like that but I have not gotten any replies, even though I have sent my questions multiple times.
Has anyone else thought about these things and wondered why they are?

author: stanito
text:
Hi, I'm curious about when AI tools for transcribing audio into Guitar Pro format will be implemented. From what I can see, competitors are already actively integrating such tools, allowing users to convert audio from a YouTube link into notation.
As I understand it, besides developing your own LLM models, there are already existing tools capable of doing this. Why not consider integrating these tools via a subscription model, offering this functionality as an optional paid feature? This approach would be beneficial both for users and for the service itself, as the tool would evolve while also generating additional revenue.
Given that manually creating tabs is quite time-consuming, an AI-assisted tool would significantly simplify the process. It seems likely that if this isn't implemented, you might risk losing users to competitors.
Additionally, it would be great to have online tab editing through a WebUI. The current workflow of downloading and uploading files feels inconvenient, and competitors, such as Songsterr, already provide such tools.

I really do think that there are better ways of dealing with this than accusing you of being a troll, but there are actually people here who think you're a troll and they're not afraid to say it. For the record, I don't think you're trying to troll but lots of the replies you make to others could easily be considered trolling.
For example, in a reply to fanapathy on this page you said:
or you're being an overly sensitive defensive crybaby over something that's not that big of deal, with that said then maybe you really are a musician.
Can you see how this is trolling? To be fair, the message you quoted in that post was trolling you but don't you see how trolling him back in retaliation is just going to make it worse? When both sides of an argument start trolling eachother, the chances of getting anything constructive out of it are quite slim. There are simply far more constructive ways to deal with this. You could have just as easily asked them why they are ridiculing you without responding with disrespectful remarks and silly logical fallacies.
Here's links to definitions of two logical fallacies you have used in arguments multiple times so far:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straw_man_argument
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad_hominem
If you want me to point a few occasions where you have used these, I would be happy to point them out to you.
About this multi-posting thing...
Making a double post or two in a thread isn't really a problem. However, if you keep making multi-posts repeatedly you're probably going to get banned from posting on this site. This is because people don't like this- it really spams up the boards, takes up unnecessary amonts of space, and lots of us also find it annoying to read. It would be a lot more difficult to find a certain "pearl of wisdom" on these boards if everyone made multi-posts all the time. Like it or not, you're going to find far less productive responses from people if you keep doing this. author: JimDawson
text:
Lastly, I'd like to comment on critical thinking. There's a certain process any of us can use to figure things out on our own without actually asking questions on this forum. You can actually figure out the answers for some of your own questions quicker than it takes for other people to reply to them.
I'll give you an example with a question you made a thread about:
How many octaves does a 22 fret bass have?
With the most basic knowledge of music theory you could easily answer this yourself. Seriously, it's really easy to figure out.
First off, when you're trying to figure something out it's always better to work from the start rather than jump into something without knowing the background of it first. Do you know that there are 12 notes in an octave? Do you know that the 5th fret on any string of a bass is usually tuned to the same pitch of the open string above it? Do you know that the amount of range an instrument has is an inherent property of how many strings it has as well as its tuning?
If you know the answer to the three questions above, you can easily answer your own question. Also, if you do know the answers of those three questions you'll begin to be able to see just how useless knowing how many octaves a 22 fret bass has really is to someone who doesn't even have the knowledge to figure out how many octaves it has on their own.
If you don't know, (and there is no shame in not knowing, but I think there is shame in not willing to learn) feel free to ask the guys on the Music Theory board where to start learning; I am sure lots of them, as well as myself, would be able to help you. You need to be humble about it too or you'll come across as a dick. If someone calls you stupid or something like that, just be respectful and remind them that you're just asking for some direction.
The point is, you need to think more about what you're saying, how you're saying it and why you're saying it. Do this with the aim of making what you say as constructive as possible. That's all there is to it.
There you go. If something in these two posts I have made isn't clear, or doesn't make sense to you, I would be happy to try and explain it better. Please take this seriously- I am really trying to help you.

author: JimDawson
text:
why should i listen to someone who might have the mentality of gg allin?
That's actually an interesting question. I suppose if you randomly met someone on the street, there is a chance they might have the kind of mentality to throw poo at you for no reason. Why should you listen to anyone at all if there's a chance they'll just throw poo at you?
However, I'm fairly certain that most of us know that the chance of getting pelted with poo by some random guy on the street is quite negligible. I know this from reflecting on my own experiences with others and creating a model of what random people are like without actually knowing this for certain. I know that I can walk around in a crowd of people and not get poo flung at me at all because my past has demonstrated to me that this has never happened to me ever; the probability of myself going out in public and getting sprayed with fecal matter is close to zero- but demonstrably not impossible.
You don't really know what kind of mentality people have without a proper demonstration. So why not give people a chance to show you? You simply can't know for sure unless you try. Going out into the world, experiencing things and studying those experiences is something which makes it possible for us to have nice things.
Short answer to your question: You might just learn something- and better yourself because of it.
and what kinda fan of gg cares about rules? especially if you are a musician to.
I don't see what being a musician has to do with caring about rules. However, the answer to this kind of ties in to what I have already written. I just find it interesting, and entertaining, to witness the extremes of what people are capable of.
I am the sort of GG fan who cares about rules because I like having nice things. Tying in to my answer to your previous question, rules in their various forms give you a certain structure to build upon. That structure enables us to have nice things.
better turn your stereo down before someone complains.
This actually ties into what I have been saying all along quite nicely. What you're doing is drawing a conclusion based on a false premise which you can't even prove in any demonstrable way. I'll forget the "stereo" part, because that's just splitting hairs.
You have just made an assumption that I listen to music loud enough that someone might complain. It's entirely false, but that isn't the point. The point is, it isn't good to reach conclusions without adequate evidence simply because your chance of being wrong goes up a lot. It's better to make inquiries about things first, and your format of doing so is quite important. You simply don't know enough to make a reasonable conclusion without adequate evidence.
My conclusion: You should probably respect the rules of the forum and those who use it if you actually care about getting nice things out of your inquiries. I sincerely hope you consider my response one of those "nice things" regardless of what decisions you make.

The threads started by user is simply a link to the advanced search, with certain parameters already filled in. From what i can see anyway. May as well wait for the Russians
Actually, I'm pretty sure you're right on this one.
Due to the current state of the forums, the search function is immeasurably taxed. Since it is a search function, I don't believe that there is a database for each user that lists the threads they created. If there was, this would be much easier overall, as you could simply be alerted whenever a new entry appeared.
As it stands, linking in to the search feature would mean that every time your profile runs a query to determine whether or not a new thread has been made (each time you go to a page where a notification is potentially available) it would indulge in a new search. It would have to do this for each and every person you have subscribed to, for each and every person who has ever made such a subscription. It would mean that the sixty second wait would also be bypassed. This would kill the search feature altogether, and swallow resources that are already stretched thin,
If threads could be duplicated, when created, onto the profile database (in much the same way that the contributions are) then the search feature would not have to be involved, which would make it not only feasable but efficient. Seeing as each duplicate would simply be the link to the OP rather than the thread itself, it also wouldn't take up that much room.
This is how I understand it. I honestly don't know too much about it, but for other forums that I've run in the past. The only non-Russian I'm aware of that knows more about this particular field is Sicky, so it might be worth swinging him a PM if nobody from the Office replies before the weekend starts.
Concerning post counts, I believe that's just a display of a number straight from the forum database. Since post count was visible on the original vB profiles, which still exist to draw data from in the forum database, the field has just been pulled from that onto the current UG profiles.

author: SomeoneYouKnew
text:
(copy/paste from a similar thread)
Let me start out with a disclaimer:  I'm not a major tab contributor, so I don't know everything about the process.  I've never had a tab rejected, so I don't have first-hand experience on that end.  But I do know few things about how the process is supposed to work and how it can break down.  I'll share with you, what i do know.
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
These go into the TPA (tabs pending approval)
UGers who successfully have uploaded enough tabs, have access to this area.
They vote and comment on the submitted tabs.
The Tab Moderators and Tab Master use these votes/comments to decide which tabs will be accepted.
An approved tab simply gets added to the archive.
A denied tab is not added to the archive.
An e-mail is generated that goes to the user who submitted the denied tab
This e-mail contains the reasons for denial from the comments submitted by users in the TPA
Where the system breaks down:
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
Not all tabs in the TPA get voted on / commented.
A tab without votes / comments must still be processed.
Decisions must be made quickly, because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
Tab Moderators / Tab Master often don't have time to write out the reason for denial because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
If a Tab is submitted where there are multiple versions already in existence, it is generally passed over, because...
UG gets TONS of tab submissions every week.
While this might seem unfair, the fact is: most of these submissions for tabs with multiple versions are just copy/paste from other sites or some kid writing a poorly crafted tab.
Even if the tab has votes/comments, the information for denial can only be relayed to the author IF he has "receive e-mail from administrators" selected in his profile.
The Tab system on UG isn't perfect, but it does function.  Considering the heavy load on the system, it works well.  If you want to make a difference, once you have access to the TPA, become active in voting/commenting on the tab submissions.  This will greatly help with the heavy load.
Thanks in advance, for your cooperation.

Suggestion
: Transpose should be remembered at the account level and not device level.
I use the application on my desktop computer, on the iPad and the iPhone. Whenever I like a song, I transpose it to my comfortable voice pitch and add it to my favorites. What happens is that the chord transposition is remembered at the device level.
For example, if a song is originally on C and I transpose it to D on the iPad, next time I open the song on the iPad, it remains on D which is good. But if I open the song on my desktop computer or my iPhone, it is still on the original key of C. I need to manually change it to D on each device.
It seems the chord transposition is stored at the device and not at the account level. It will be more convenient if it is stored at the account level on your record in the application cloud database. That way, whichever device you play the song, it gives you the transposed key you stored or updated the last time.
Is there a way to store the last chord transposition at the account level?
This is a great site and app!
Thanks!

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Hey all,
I have a suggestion that would help home-recording users like myself and lots of other users out very much.
It would be handy if it were possible to replace an uploaded mp3 with a new one, without having to delete the old one, because that way you'd lose all the ratings and comments you received. That way, if someone posts a critique on a certain recording, the uploader could improve their recording and "update" their song.
An example: people have told me the piano in my 9 Crimes cover is too loud. I could quickly fix this in my recording program and make a new mp3, but I don't want to delete the mp3 from my profile to replace it; I'd lose all the ratings just for this quick fix.
I hope this can be implemented!
Cheers!

author: pwrmax
text: I think people would abuse it too much.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
^ How? It makes no difference if you upload a copyrighted mp3 from the bat, or later on if replacing mp3s were possible... the profiles get moderated too, so you'd still get warned/banned for it.
It's like saying we shouldn't allow posting in the Pit because people would abuse it too much.

author: guitarsftw
text: I would definitely be in favor of a way of stringing different versions of the same piece together in a way that the progress would be apparent and that the ratings/comments for each stage remain available.  But if you're suggesting that we should merely be able to swap out mp3's and keep the ratings/comments, the whole bait-and-switch thing becomes an issue that may be too difficult to deal with on a case-by-case process.  Just my 2 cents.

now if there was an "update version" option or something, that makes more sense to me. the old track would be kept on hand and the ratings wouldnt transfer over. however, the tracks would be linked, and keep the same title and stuff. then when you click the song, it shows there are multiple versions and lets you pick which to listen to. or at least have some way of doing that. then you can see each version with their own ratings/comments, but still have the ability to update your track and keep things together in a way that makes sense.

author: madbasslover
text:
The music you listen to won't get any kind of validation just because someone might call it metal. It wouldn't work because nu-metal and metal are two very different types of music. They start at the same point, yes, but they go in opposite directions.
Nu-metal has many elements that water it down and often takes extremely immature lyrical approaches to various subjects, i.e. "F
ucking Determined" and "People = Sh
it."
Metal, on the other hand, is extremely varied. Unlike Nu-Metal, which is really a bit of a one-trick pony, metal has so many various subgenres that more often than not one metal band will sound nothing like another. People in the metal forum don't want to discuss nu-metal bands because to the majority of them nu-metal bands simply aren't interesting. Likewise, if they were merged no one from the Nu-metal forum would post outside the Nu-metal threads. This would create excess traffic in the forum without really changing anything or increasing the productivity of the discussion.
It makes more sense to keep them separate, otherwise the nu-metal threads will be buried under the metal threads and then the nu-metal posters will simply complain about how they're basically sitting in the corner while everyone else is discussing metal.

author: ctfod
text:
I understand that there might be issues with the amount of stuff in the tabs section, but I think PDF tabs could help a great deal. It would:
1. Eliminate the potential bugs with tabs warping and becoming hard to read
2. Show proper rhythm of the tab
3. Be a good alternative to Guitar Pro/PowerTab, although PowerTab is free, and it would be exported from GP/PT
4. Be much easier to weed out people who have scanned it in from the tab books, and much more obvious, too.
I don't know what anyone would think of this idea, but hell, drum tabs were added recently so I may as well give it a shot.

First day I got it I tried tuning it but it didn’t work, like the strings were too tight? Like playing it open would work but upon fretting, it doesn’t pick right. Okay, so I took it home and I checked the tuning and the tuning was a little off and it was more at standard tuning. BEADGBe and I always have my tuning a whole step down. ADGCFAd. So I thought I had it all figured out with tuning it and I loosened the nuts on the top and then drop tuned my guitar. Which took awhile for me to get it to right tuings. After, I tightened the nuts, I picked the strings open and they sounded fine. Then when I tried fretting, it sounded like crap...again...can’t fret it, because it sounds too tight and I don’t get real noise. Just annoying buzzes
I also noticed that if I’m holding my guitar normally and I pick it open, it sounds fine but then if I lean it back the strings tightens up and I get that sound again. Any advice? There’s nothing I can find on google and I don’t wanna go back to the guitar stor

author: zimlad
text: Hi........I've  noticed over the last year or so, that all the mods corrections are  directed at making the chord symbols UG-compliant or correcting errors in how the suggested chord is written or to do with lay-out/appearance  issues. That's fine. I appreciate the need for consistency with that  side of things. However no-one ever actually corrects/improves (or make  suggestions) for the actual chords themselves. Some songs can be  complicated chord-wise and they need the chords  correcting/improving....you might get to say  an 80% accuracy level but need help on a few very tricky parts...... .there were a couple of exceptionally good  transcribers I found on UG who I used to ask for their corrections on, but there's a limit to how many times you  can ask someone to correct stuff, without it being an imposition....so  what about this as an idea?....UG creates a section, inviting expert  chord crackers for their input on tricky parts of songs, saying "these chords  needs improving/correcting" it can just apply where the original tabber has specifically asked for that input]....I think this would benefit  everyone....what do you think? cheers

author: UG Support
text:
zimlad

author: zimlad
text:
UG Support
the point is this....the substance of the chords themselves are never corrected or improved (you'll get corrections on how the chord symbol is written but never on the accuracy of the chord itself). ..I've uploaded over a 100 tabs so I know what I'm saying is accurate.....majority of tabs dont need correcting, but there can be a few difficult ones or ones with tricky sections where it would be very useful to have the sort of facility I've suggested (ie for expert chord crackers with great ears  to check those ones)...cheers
