author: krachmak3r
text:
I don't use UG much but even in a short time there are quite a few things that bother me:
I was not able to edit my comment of a tab multiple times
After the first edit (which went wrong) I was only able to "reply". I consider this really bad usability. At least one should be notified about this limit.
Comments have a character limit, which is not visible to the user
Which is why my first edit went wrong. To be clear: The problem is not that there is a limit for the size of comments, but that I, as a user, can not see how much space is left.
Actually I was not able to see it, until my comment was saved and cut off after a certain size.
The site is slow. Scripts are buggy?
At least if you are doing more than just watching tabs, the site is pretty slow. Further in about half an hour my Firefox hung multiple times because of some script on UG, that seems to be stuck.
The song editor preview is useless
If I hit preview, I can not see the final result of the tab on UG. The only difference is that the text box not editable anymore, making the scrollbar go away.
A preview IMO should show the final result of the tab on UG. A good example for a preview, is the preview of posts on the forum. These show the final result.
The scrollbar in the tab editor is hiding text of the tab
The last two columns of the tab which is edited, is not visible because of the scrollbar.
This issue occurs for me, if I re-edit a tab. Then even the red line is outside the text editor. However, when I create a new tab, the text box uses the full width of the browser window and no scrollbar is hiding any text.
I can not see the comments I make in the tab editor
Maybe I missunderstand this feature. When I "Post a comment" in the tab editor, I can not see the comment I made. There is just a message "** Tab has been corrected".
However, I would interpret a comment in the tab editor as the same, if I add a comment on the resulting page on UG. This is useful when I want to add information, which is not part of the tab itselt, e.g. a hint for a version, where you can clearly hear the guitar part, or whatever.
But maybe this comment is for internal use only and only visible in the approval que?
Anyhow, if the comment feature of the tab editor is eqivalent to comments on the resulting UG page, the preview of a tab should of course show the comments as well.
The "Leave Feedback" button on the backend is linking to a forum-thread, which is not made for general feedback
If I hit
Info
>
Leave Feedback
I am linked to
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?p=33529187#post33529187

https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/forumdisplay.php?f=14

Regards

author: copperwreck
text:
Hi,
I see a risk that for every popular song in existance we'll get yet another, almost identical, submission but this time classified as "live".
In the submission queue it looks like this is first tab for that song and you can't compare it to the album version easily. And there are no guidelines for how much different a live version must be to an album version to warrant a new submission. The cynic in me sees a million easy points for the next win-a-strat competition, similar to how the uke-chords often don't add any value but are only copies.
Any ideas on how to tackle this? Or am I being overly distrusting in our submittors?

author: NSpen1
text:
copperwreck
I don't think that's so much of a problem because you always could add acoustic and live versions.  You have to now fill in extra information for live versions, and acoustic versions should have a link to a performance also.  We are trying to make sure versions are categorised correctly, but we do have to be quite vigilant at times.  (btw people have been disqualified from competitions for submitting duplicate or near duplicate normal and acoustic versions.)
The thing I don't like is that at the moment normal, acoustic and live versions are all mixed up together in the tab listings ... I think that must be a bug, not anything deliberate ...

author: NeoMvsEu

, besides the provided link, are you talking about:
A
1. user U makes tab T
2. U provides link L to an acoustic live performance
3. U submits T as both an acoustic and a live tab (total 2 contributions)
or
B
1. user U makes tab T
2. U provides link L to a live/an acoustic performance
3. U submits T as both a regular and acoustic/live performance
?

NSpen1

author: maguri
text:
NeoMvsEu
As far as I understood, copperwreck  talks about C
C
1. There are already N versions of a song S.
2. User U wants to submit his or her own version but does not want this new version to become version N+1 because late versions do not get much traffic.
3. U discovers there are no acoustic or live versions of S. U therefore declares his/her version to be acoustic or live so it becomes version 1 at least in this category.
a ) In the olden days, before it became mandatory to provide a link to a special live or acoustic recording of S, U submits his/her tab for the fake live/acoustic version and gets a version 1.
b) Now, U searches and finds a live or acoustic version on the net that is as close as possible to the studio version and uses this as reason for his/her version to be published.

text:
So as some of you may have heard, The Last of Us Part II Reveal Trailer came out pretty recently, and I decided to do a tab for the song Ellie sung in the trailer.
I went and searched for “Last of Us” to see the format they’re in, and its completely random. Its so hard to actually know how to submit the “correct” way.
Examples (Artist : Title):
Gustavo Santaolalla : The Last Of Us
Gustavo Santaolalla : The Last Of Us - Main Theme
Gustavo Santaolalla : The Last Of Us You And Me
Misc Computer Games : The Last Of Us - Main Theme
Misc Computer Games : The Last Of Us Theme
Misc Soundtrack : The Last Of Us Main Theme Intro
Misc Soundtrack : The Last Of Us Part Il - Shawn James - Through The Valley
As you can see, there is a lot of inconsistencies. (I didn’t even search for a super popular game either)
There needs to be some type of format to make more sense of all of this.
My recommendations:
- If its from a computer game soundtrack, it cannot be in “Misc Soundtrack” as there already seems to be a “Misc Computer Games” artist.
- If its from a movie soundtrack, it cannot be in “Misc Computer Games”.
But theres the first issue. What happens if its in a computer game and a movie soundtrack? Well, The Last of Us has not got a movie, so why would it be in “Misc Soundtrack” if there already is a “Misc Computer Games” artist section?
My proposal of how this should all be formatted (using the tab I done as an example):
Misc category : Movie/Game - Track name
Therefore,
Misc Computer Games : The Last Of Us Part II - Through The Valley
Please let me know what you think. I know there’s a lot more to go into about this subject and a lot of things I missed out on, but I’d like to hear feedback/plans before I continue.
Thanks.

text:
Quote by pwrmax
Is there a way to report flaming/spam in groups/blogs/etc? If not then I think it would be nice if there was a "report" button for comments, just like how there's one for forum posts.
Group behaviour is largely the responsibility of the Group Owner and Group Moderators.
They can edit or delete whatever they need to within the group.
They can block problem users from the group
The report button for group posts should NOT be used for minor issues like flaming/spam.  Instead, the Owner and Moderators of the group should handle that.
Please DO report any porn, etc, by clicking the report button.  Else just PM the owner or a moderator of the group for the small stuff.
Porn can't be hotlinked as a comment, so it's unlikely links will be placed there.  In the rare case where there is a link to porn or malicious site like a CAPTIVE rick-roll in a comment, please contact a member of the UG Staff.
Adding links to make it overly easy to report are really unnecessary and could lead to too much intervention being required by the UG Staff.  Reserve reporting for only the most serious matters.

author: maguri
text:
I'm the last one to defend lazy guitarists, but ...
"D" = a D-major chord, no need to add maj; everybody reconises "D" as a major chord.
Adding "maj" to D indicates that a major 7 has to be added, otherwise the "maj" would just be redundant. So people who indicate a "Dmaj" chord (hopefully) use some sort of abbreviation but actually mean "Dmaj7". "Dmaj" should never mean a plain major triad. If it still does, it should of course be corrected, but I really hope, these are the minority.

author: NSpen1
text:
maguri
Not sure about that
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_chord
"An example of a major chord is the C major chord, which consists of the notes C, E and G. In harmonic analysis or on a lead sheet, a C major chord is usually notated C, Cmaj or CM."
And I would guess that there are more times when maj is written to mean a major chord than a major seventh ... it's like the people who write Emin for Em.

author: maguri
text:
NSpen1
Thanks, I wouldn't have thought so ...
But then, the same Wiki article says this in the third paragraph:  "Major triads with additional notes, such as major seventh chord, are also called major chords. Major seventh chords are used in jazz and occasionally in rock music. In jazz, major chords may also have other chord tones added, such as the ninth and the thirteenth scale degrees." So here, right at the beginning of the article, we have "major chords" which are chords featuring more than just the basic triad. The quote you brought forth in your post (#7) says a  C major chord is "usually" called C, Cmaj, or CM (we could probably add CΔ7 and CΔ ). "Usually" implies that the usage varies.
I think it's a question of mutual understanding on the use of a certain terminology. To me, economy is key, so using more than just the plain "C"  would indicate that there is more to the chord than " c - e - g ". For many players of "jazz and occasionally rock" "Cmaj" indicates just that, there's more to that chord than the basic triad.
Coming across un-economical use of chord names, UG should simplify them in order to make chord names as generally recognisable and as unambiguous as possible. From the posts above, I read that we all agree on that and will work towards that goal.

You sometimes see C7M or C7+ and one of those is translated by the system to some weird chord shape other than the major seventh which is intended.  We can try to fix this un-economical use if we see it in tabs in the queue (or on the site for that matter) I guess

author: trevormdm

Hey all,
I've noticed for a long time that for the tab titles, none of it is as it should be (in title casing), meaning that articles, conjunctions, and prepositions should
not
be capitalized unless it is the first word in the title.
For example: "Through The Fire And Flames" by DragonForce title is
incorrect
, it should really read "Through the Fire and Flames" ("the," & "and" shouldn't be capitalized).
This grammar rule not only applies to music titles, but also movies, scripts, and anything that is considered a public work.
I'm not sure if I am explaining this perfectly, so here are some sources for further information:
GrammarCheck - Capitalization in Titles
CapitalizeMyTitle - Title Capitalization
GetProofed - Understanding Title Case/Sentence Case

author: WugtheBug
text:
I am an avid listener of progressive rock, a musical genre that often has very long songs (upwards of 20 minutes).
When searching for these tabs on UG, I am usually slightly disappointed at the quality of some of the longer tabs of this type; often, they appear to be simple shoddily done midi imports, or just badly formatted in general. However, unlike many users, I am more than willing and I actually enjoy correction these tabs, so that I (and others) are able to access well-made tabs of these songs.
Keep in mind that I am referring generally to GP tabs.
Many of these tabs that I think about correcting were made over 10 years ago, and theres little chance that the original author is even still active on UG, much less that they would be willing to make these changes themselves. However, I am very discouraged from making these corrections when I remember that all I will get in turn is a dismal 2 IQ and a credit mention that is only viewable when other users hover over the 'contributors' text. I doubt that many people looking at tabs will take the time to check who else made the tab, so this way of crediting seems pointless when users such as myself make major corrections.
This system has caused me to almost primarily make major corrections only of unregistered tabs, where theres a chance that I can gain authorship.
Also, keep in mind that I am not speaking of minor edits, such as just adding section titles or making a single chord change. I am thinking of
major
edits, that usually involve me spending 30 minutes a day for up to a week (the longest being two months for my correction of the King Crimson Lizard tab) making tedious edits, such as correcting auto-midi spacing mistakes throughout the entire 25 minute tab over 15 different instruments.
I would say that, for major corrections of this type, in which the corrector is often putting as much or even more work into the tab than the original author, it would be extremely appreciated and encouraging if  A) I received more credit  in some way, maybe having a joint mention with the original author, or even creating some kind of a joint-authorship system, and B) if there was a possibility to gain more than a measly 2 IQ for each time-consuming correction.
Obviously, I don't want to disregard the contributions of the original authors of these types of tabs, but I would enjoy having more appreciation for corrections. There are many tabs that I can think of that I would make major corrections to if I could gain more recognition.
Naturally, a system like this would have to work on a case-by-case system.
Maybe a forum thread could exist (similar to the thread for ownership of unregistered tabs) where users could request to have tab mods to review a correction they made to see if they could somehow gain more recognition or possibly more bonus IQ.
This would be very helpful for me, and I am sure that there are others as well who are in a similar position to myself.

author: strawforest007
text:
If you already know there are problems with UG member-run competitions in the sub-forums then skip to the possible solutions!
I've been involved in and am currently involved in several projects here in the UG forums and there are flaws with many of them, examples:
1. Organiser sets out a thread in the Blues & Jazz sub-forum
2. Anyone can join sign up policy, some rules laid out
3. No time-scale!
4. Threads drawn out for months and months with new people continuing to sign up but the organiser had long gone due to commitments, leaving the project on hold, or the organisers had changed hands several times so rules etc are altered.
5. Frustration for those who've worked on a piece for the project and are waiting for voting or something to happen are sometimes venting in the thread (evident in the current 'UG Album').
6. The thread and competition becomes less attractive to new and current competitors because of the timescale (evident in guitar duels - example: current Blues Duels)
Unfinished projects: UG Acoustic Album, UG Blues & Jazz Album II, Blues Duels (and many more I'm probably not aware of).
Possible solutions?
Maybe a page designed for UG members where anyone can set up a competition, filling an online form of project title, numbers of entrants, competition type (private invite-only, or open), voting system (knockout competition or some sort of league or ladder), time-scale (between voting if multiple voting dates required: for duels?), date setting (would fit nicely with the UG Calendar suggestion which could also serve as a nudge to UG members to get a song or piece submitted).
This UG projects page would have pre-fixed structures for certain competitions and would allow all UG'ers to follow projects as well, as most are hidden in the depths of sub-forums but many are worthy of being show-pieced.
Entrants would have to sign up to projects to enter, probably on a first-come first-served basis, or being accepted by the organiser or project mods. Mods can also adjust certain aspects of the competition and remove/add competitors etc.
Any other ideas or additions then please add some here, but I'd personally like to see something like this on the UG site.
Peace.

author: strawforest007
text: Also a possibility of a set maximum and minimum time-scale for the projects (would be set by the organiser and cannot be changed)? Many people don't like these projects going on for months and months but I don't see it being a problem if the UG Members were made aware of the time-scale upon sign-up of the project.

author: Emptywordsbass
text:
It is a common refrain in the news comments sections that most articles written by jomatami are just quotations from interviews with maybe 100 words written by the author (typically just " During a/an conversation/interview/appearance/etc. with [fill in the blank], [Artist] spoke about/talked about/discussed [topics]," with maybe another sentence or two added in between long quotations). These quotations are also often split into multiple articles over a period of time, with jomatomi being called out for milking content. Additionally, the specific topic the title of the article describes is sometimes buried, requiring a laborious process of reading or skimming to get to the information the title promises (although this is not always the case). Finally, the current form of reporting is not quite honest as over 90% of each article is not the author's original work. While press releases and paid newswire services are often meant to be taken from verbatim, I am not quite sure if this level of copy-paste is legal in many countries and could leave UG liable to potential suits.
I think the news section would be more reader-friendly if articles paraphrased their source material, got more to the point, added a few key phrases as quotations, and then linked to the source material. Such a format would be a slightly slower process when the material comes from a written source, but it would be much faster to compose if coming from an audio/visual source. Regardless, the difference in writing time should be negligible, but the difference for the readers' experience would be drastic. Shorter, more efficient articles, cutting right to the heart of the matter, with less fluff and digging. Links available for all the additional content that would typically be copy-pasted.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Hey all!
I'm a little tired of the current forum skins, and I'm sure I'm not the only one. They look a bit bland, sterile, and most of all they look very old. IMO, they look "as if they were displayed on an old 10Mhz IBM with DOS 6.0", like SYK so eloquently stated...
What's more, they don't match the rest of the UG pages. The home page, profile pages and community pages all seem to be similar in style, with a sleek modern look that the forums can only be jealous of...
A few examples. Here's what the UG header looks like on the community pages:
(Click the thumbnail to see full-size pic)
It's handy,
and
it looks nice, as you can see. It sports links to your profile, as well as an easy to reach "sign off" button so you can easily log out while browsing the forums. But where are all those handy features on the forum pages? All I see is this:
(Click the thumbnail to see full-size pic)
As you can see, it's not consistent with the rest of the website. A different logo graphic, no update bar, and no links to your profile. Also, for some reason, the links in the navigation bar at the top are lowercase, as well as on the homepage and profile pages, while on the community page they're uppercase. Weird inconsistency that can be fixed easily I think...
As for the rest of the forums, they don't lack any features that the rest of the website does have, but the layout isn't consistent with the profiles and community pages. UG Black matches the rest of the website more than UG Classic does, but they're still both bland and boring, like I said. Look at this:
(Click the thumbnail to see full-size pic)
The grey colors are boring, almost depressing. Don't get me started on the UG Classic colors, they're even worse IMO. The sterile grey modules could be spiced up a little, as well as the black-and-grey-dotted background (that is all over the website, incidentally).
So! I tried visualising what the forums could look like if they matched the modern, sober but stylish look of the UG profile pages... here's my amateurish effort of a "ZeG Black" forum skin, made with Photoshop:
(Click the thumbnail to see full-size pic)
And here is a "ZeG Classic" variant for UG Classic fanboys!
(Click the thumbnail to see full-size pic)
IMHO, this looks a lot more modern, while still being clear, well-organised and easy on the eye. As you can see, the "stripped down" UG header is now the full-fledged and fully functional header, complete with all the profile links and updates bar. The skin also uses the blue striped backgrounds in the forum modules, as well as the grey striped backgrounds for the main background. Someone might have a better idea for a better looking background... but even like this, it looks sexy, am I right?
Now, this thread serves two purposes:
- For users: so you can look at my designs, and tell me what you think of them, what you'd like to see improved, etc.
- For the UG team: so the programmers can tell us if this can be implemented, how long it will take, and if they actually have that time...
So... fire away with your feedback!
Cheers!
ZeG
ZEDIT: Updated with "ZeG Classic" example design.

author: brettsanace
text:
Now that you have the arrangement with Youtube and Spotify that displays a link to direct users to UG tabs for the selected song (as long as they are using Chrome web browser)
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=2402758
it may be better to not call UG tabs "Official" but rather "UG" or "UG Team". The reason I say this is because I foresee potential complaints from artists.
Using Youtube as an example, many of the videos will be on the "Official Artist Channel" and will be described as "Official Music Video" or "Official Lyric Video" as the videos have been provided by or approved by the artist. Now there is a link on these "Official" videos that take people to the list of available tabs on UG for the selected song (see the first screenshot below). However, often the first tab listed when people follow this link is described as "Official",  which includes chords with lyrics and strrumming patterns, and interactive tab synchronized with backing tracks, but it has not been provided by or approved by the artist (see the second screenshot below).
This was not such an issue in the past as artists were unlikely to come to UG to check how to play their song so would never know about these "Official" tabs, but now that there is a link on their official video or with their official song on Spotify I can see that some artists may actually click on these links and take issue with the tabs being described as "Official".
Anyway, it is just a suggestion.

author: UG Support
text:
brettsanace
Hello!
Thank you for taking the time to share your thoughtful suggestion regarding the recent integration with YouTube and Spotify, which provides users with a link to UG tabs for selected songs. We truly value user feedback, and your insights are invaluable in helping us enhance the Ultimate Guitar experience.
Your concern about the term "Official" being potentially misleading, especially in the context of artists' official channels on platforms like YouTube, is well-founded. We understand the importance of accurately representing the source and approval status of the tabs.
After careful consideration of your suggestion, we agree that using terms like "UG" or "UG Team" might be more appropriate to avoid any potential confusion or concerns from artists. This adjustment aligns with our commitment to transparency and clarity for both users and artists.
We greatly appreciate your vigilance in bringing this matter to our attention. Your feedback contributes significantly to the ongoing improvements we make to better serve the Ultimate Guitar community.
If you have any further suggestions or thoughts, please feel free to share them. We're here to listen and continuously improve our platform.
Thank you once again for being an integral part of the Ultimate Guitar community.

author: stevierich
text:
This is my first post but I have been a user and a fan of UG for years now. I am a singer songwriter with a small studio and an ambitious goal to produce my own records. Doing it alone can be daunting so the more tools available in one place, the quicker I can get my work done.
Since I consider myself more of a studio musician, basically because I have arthritis in most of my body and playing out these days would be too much of an effort. I have done it though and back when, we didn't have the tools available today.
So, here are what I consider major improvements to UG and it's offerings to my type and just about any musician I suppose.
1.) The ability to build set-lists (taken from already created favorite's list)
2.) To be able to use a search tool to search your own lists as well as all lists by genre and add to play lists.
3.) To be able to add notes to each song in a fly out box for things such as tunings, amp settings, midi notes and the like for stage or studio work.
4.) To be able to set both scroll speed and key changes inside of set list.
5.) Finally (for now anyway) to be able to start your play list with total play time counter, ability to build in break times between each song and even for a set break.
OK then
Peace out

author: thewrongsondi
text:
I have been making my own "hybrid" tabs in GP for awhile now and think it would be a great addition around here. Basically instead of playing along to tab pro in rhythm and then having to race to get the solo tabs pulled up, or worse having to stop and then switch track only to have to switch back to rhythm again after the solo you integrate them.
Take something like Man In The Box for example. The rhythm has two tracks that are very similar and then 2 solo tracks. So not only do you have to switch for the first solo but then race from solo to solo. I can't be the only person who's cut up tabs to  have all these parts in one playthrough. Even from rhythm to rhythm there's small flourishes individual to each track that you might want to play. This way you're playing the most complete version of the song possible as a single guitarist. You're basically guessing at what the live version is I suppose.
You would still have the tabs that reflect the proper parts for the proper instruments if you wanted them but for those afternoons when you just want to come on and jam along to some songs it's so much more satisfying to have it all in one track (you'd still have drums, bass and a backing guitar if applicable). Nothing kills the mood like stopping a song a few times throughout.
Or am I wasting my breathe here and I should just slap a "Live version" label on them and hope they get approved?

author: Skullivan
text:
It has come to my attention recently that quite a noticeable amount of album reviews by the UG Team (mostly by a particular author, Lou Vickers) have gone through a rather large drop in quality, mainly due to their inclusion of a mini-biography of the artist.
For example (Intermezzo- Michael Angelo Batio):
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/michael_angelo_batio/intermezzo/index.html
The "Sound" category consists of four paragraphs, three of which are back story on MAB. The fourth only talks about his style in a very bland way, being universally applicable to any of his albums. Now I do know this is MAB, notorious for his cookie cutter shred albums, but still an album review requires at least a little insight on the album itself.
Another (Proof of Life- Scott Stapp):
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/scott_stapp/proof_of_life/index.html
Now I'm not familiar with this artist so I can't vouch for his diversity in albums (though I'm sure he can't be worse than MAB when it comes to repetitiveness), but the writing format is still the same, worse even. Four paragraphs of bio and two sentences of vague "Sound" description.
Some more guilty reviews:
Fun on Earth- Roger Taylor
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/roger_taylor/fun_on_earth/index.html
Tres Cabrones- The Melvins (not too bad but still a bit too much of bio)
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/melvins/tres_cabrones/index.html
Now Lou can write a good album review, as demonstrated by some of his earlier work, but recently it's just become unreadable-y bad. I'd rather we nip this in the bud before it starts becoming a regular thing.
Thanks,
Skullivan

author: brettsanace
text:
Why is is that the Song (Title) field only displays in lowercase when creating a tab? This causes confusion for people when creating their tabs as they keep trying to edit the title to get the correct capitalisation. When the song is published it capitalises the first letter of each word. Why can't the Song(Title) field just accept the text case as written as it does in the Artist field? Similarly, why is it that the only symbol you can use in the Song(Title) field is a dash when you can use lots of symbols in the Artist field? The system allows search by Artist and by Title so why are the different?
Even though the first letter of each word in the title is actually capitalised when the song is published this is also dumb as then you end up with songs like "La Woman" instead of "LA Woman" or "Born in the Usa".
Another example of the problem this causes is I did a tab for a song called "R.I.P. (Rock In Peace)" and as the Song(Title) field does not accept periods or parentheses I thought "Rip Rock In Peace" would look stupid so I replaced the periods with spaces so it is now "R I P Rock In Peace" but now no one can find it it as they don't think of searching for RIP with spaces between the letters.
I don't have a problem with any other search engines on the internet when using capitals or symbols, and the fact that the Artist searches seems to work when these characters are entered makes me wonder why the Song (Title) field can't be the same. Is it because you have 1m+ tabs and don't want to bite the bullet because so many of the titles would be wrong e.g. all the songs that have a sub-title in parentheses?  Or is it the search engine wouldn't match "Born In The USA" with "Born In The Usa" or "Escape (The Pina Colada Song)" with "Escape The Pina Colada Song"? I doubt it that would be ridiculous. Whatever the reason it makes UG look very amateurish.
So my suggestion is:
- The Song (Title) field should display whatever the author enters when creating a tab, including case and symbols.
- The title that appears on the published tab should be identical to what was entered in the Song(Title) field when the tab was approved.

author: NSpen1
text:
Quote by brettsanace
- The Song (Title) field should display whatever the author enters when creating a tab, including case and symbols.
- The title that appears on the published tab should be identical to what was entered in the Song(Title) field when the tab was approved.
No, this is a very bad idea.  Let's leave aside the symbols for a moment.  Allowing the text case to be how an author enters it would result in people submitting tabs with all different/random/weird ways of writing the song title with respect to capitalisation.  Then if the system can deal with different ways of capitalising a title, won't this result in the same song having potentially 5 different titles all listed separately?  Or if they are to be combined under the same title as they must, how do we decide which is the right one?  It's a lot easier if it's set automatically.
It's bad enough as it is, getting people to submit tabs with the right titles (unfortunately they can't be trusted
)
If different symbols could be used in song titles this would be good, e.g. apostrophes and parentheses, but when this has been brought up in the past UG have said it's due to technical reasons and it's not something they would be able to implement any time soon.
What would be good is to have some sort of instructions for new tab authors, to tell them how the capitalisation of song titles works so they don't keep trying to edit it.  And for other things, like to explain what a transposed duplicate is and why there is never any need to submit a tab like that.
Btw we already have to be careful with the Artist field accepting the text case as written, when adding a new artist.  If it isn't written correctly and is approved like that it's not so easy to change.  We wouldn't want to extend that to Song titles.

author: Colohue
text:
There have been quite a few comments in the articles recently stating that news/columns and reviews are all in need of better proof-reading. I should point out though that the good bulk of the information available is completely user-generated, titles included.
Having a dedicated english/american proof-reader or two would be good, but it would take up a large amount of time checking over every piece of work submitted, so it would be more of a job than a volunteer worthy idea. After all, the proof-reader(s) would
have
to be there in order to check everything over. Over in the UGC we've been trying to get people volunteering to edit/proof read, as well as trying to get users to let us make suggestions and brainstorm.
Unfortunately, having proof-readers could also quite easily be considered a slight to people's work. For example, if a user had poor grammar and the proof-reader corrected it, the user who submitted the work could easily complain about it. People with particular ways of speaking/writing/typing could become annoyed if these were changed.
Then there's also the potential to get things wrong. Let's use the article title in question. If a proof reader were to read the article and look at the title then they would likely know that it was somewhat misleading and also know how best to fix it. However, if you consider the interview section. If a proof-reader altered the spelling of something that the artist said when it was actually a direct phonetic quote for something that the artist did say then UG would be misquoting people.

Adding a Fingerstyle Arrangement (or Fingerpicking Arrangement however you might want to call it) would save some trouble and make things a little easier for those interested by it.
Here's my story (which is only really meant to be read by the people who's handling UG)
So I had to struggle (and still struggling since it is as of yet to be resolved) to contribute to UG regarding personal fingerstyle arrangements I worked on from some classical rock songs.
Instead of submitting my tab and be happy about contributing in my little way to the guitar community. I end up wasting a whole lot of time for nothing. Which pretty much pisses me off ever since I go out of my way (as well as many others) to make a contribution to what is a commercial website. I surely don't expect to have to spend many much time than I already did on the work I'm contributing.
Because let's face it what we give for free turns into revenue for UG. This is not really a problem (except for the pesky ads) because it's mostly a win-win situation.
However when said contributors as to struggle to contribute, therein lies a problem.
First there's no comment of why a tab is rejected or not. Which would be the decent thing to do instead of letting contributors spend time searching the basic grounds for rejection.
Second when you got the ground rules and resubmit your work and it's getting rejected you got to take on your time again to ask why it's been rejected.
Third when you got the reasons why your tab has been rejected you got to argue a solution because what's offered doesn't make sense.
So I guess taking a bit more care of your contributors might goes a long way. Because I personally contribute to many different guitar community and UG is the only place where I feel being jerked around (it also happens to be the biggest)
Maybe I'm the only one who feels that way maybe there's a hundred like me.
All in all working a solution for not discouraging people from contributing would be in both our interest.
I'll see how it turns out but in my case I guess I'll not bother trying anymore if nothing change.

1. we have a similar tab in the archives
2. there are too many versions of the tab already

In your case it was the par. 5, because we accept only "[Song title] Acoustic" or "[Song title] Live" tab variations. But, since your tabs represent an arrangement that differs from the ones we already have, they were re-considered and approved.

author: furin121
text:
blue_strat,
You're right. It's a tough situation. Even in 'serious' conversations you're always going to have people interject some humor since it's really human nature to try to ease the tension. Where do you draw the line between someone being an active part of the conversation with a humorous comment and someone who is just tossing in crap to be a smart ass? And the people you want to avoid will always pop in to cause trouble but I think if you had a consistent group effort to not promote that kind of thing that it would be a minimal issue.
Forums like 'the pit' really kind of feed into that mentality. I think many people on here, even those I would like to avoid in a serious conversation, are generally good people and are just trying to have fun. I think they would tend to stick to the pit where it's appropriate and not come to the more serious area with the intent of just being a jerk (although there will be people who would).
But again, I don't think there is an easy solution and there may not be a viable solution at all. But it's worth discussing at least to see what, if any, options are available.

author: offspring93
text:
In the danger of getting kicked in the ass by forum members, 'cause hey this is the internet... But I can't keep my mouth shut on this, I can't.
I am thankful from my heart for everybody who makes the effort of reading this.
Dear UG team,
I find it hard, very hard to find words for what's currently happening in Ukraine.
If you take a look at this world's history, aside from the civil war in Jugoslavia in the 1990s there was no war between two countries in Europe since the end of WWII in 1945.
The last man who had started an open war against another country on this continent was a man everybody knows. A man who once ruled the country I grew up and live in, whose name I, as well as most of us, condemn and I won't speak out now. A man from whom I hope none of his kind will ever again set up shop in any country, as the scars he and his actions have left on this world are forever painful and visible.
Born in 1993 I grew up in a time of relative peace, of new dialogue between the East and the West, of a belief that humanity had, at least in some regard, finally created a world with a little less borders, a little less hostility, a breath of a little more hope and a brighter future to approach hand in hand instead of fist against fist.
Though tension has apparently and unfortunately grown in the past years, as national egoism is on the rise in many countries, in spite of all threats and saber-rattling, I would have honestly never thought it possible for a European country to throw all efforts of diplomacy and all the efforts for disarmament and peace of the past decades in the garbage and start a war against another, obviously much weaker country over night.
Honestly, I am speechless, shocked and frankly speaking: Kind of hopeless about this situation. These events have the potential of throwing the world back half a man's lifetime, reducing many achievements of the past thirty-five years to nothing.
This is not a statement against Russia as a country or even worse against Russian people - which should be obvious I want to make clear - as the actions of a regime are not controlled by the people of a country. But I think this is important to mention as I am not here to insult or accuse anybody who's reading this.
As we know, Ultimate Guitar was founded in Kaliningrad, Russia in the 1990s and has evolved into a magnificent, worldwide community of music, joy, love and collaboration, one of the biggest websites in the realms of guitars and rock music.
I believe that this would not have been possible if we'd still have an Iron Curtain isolating the east and the west today. I am glad and thankful about the networking possibilities of the time I grew up in and it frightens me that many of these aspects could be shattered now withint weeks due to a new era of isolation which might rise in front of our eyes right in this moment.
For the reasons stated in these past 500 words you have (or haven't) just read I want to express that I would honestly and heartily appreciate a statement from the UG team in the article section about the current events. This website, which is my start page ever since picking up a guitar in 2007, this community which I grew to love deeply in the past 15 years is a place where resentment, war and disunion should have no place.
Thank you, from my heart, for reading this.
Love, Peace and Punk Rock from Germany,
Valentin

author: offspring93
text:
zappp
With relief I have read your statement on this in a pit thread which confirms what I have said to multiple upset UG users in the past few days: UG is an international company today, operated mostly from the US and Cyprus (part of Muse Group). Though many users think UG is still solely a Russian company. I know the UG team has very recently mentioned in a news article that politics are "A big no-no" on UG. However I'm not sure if an exception might be justified here. The current situation is much more than some rockstar's opinion. It's a humanitarian and economic disaster and may be the worst event in Europe since 80 years.
Many UG users don't know that UG is an international company today and many UG users might not realize that many, many Russians are against the war (though it's getting harder and harder for them to express that in public...)
So maybe, just maybe a statement in the news section does in fact make sense. To make clear 1. UG is not really a "Russian thing" and 2. you do not support the war (I guess this goes for most of the team...or at least I hope...). It's not about shouting around political opinions (there are other places on the web for this, hence I understand that "big no-no"), it's more about ending some misunderstandings amoungs many UG users.
However I understand that you don't want to risk seeing anyone from the team in Russia or the project itself on some "lists". I know oppression is a serious topic. So it's up to you. I don't want to demand anything, it's just a suggestion.
Thank you.

Quote by james4
I have no idea how hard it'd be to implement
, but it'd be pretty handy, I think
A little tricky but not terribly hard, James.  But priority on something like this is gonna be fairly low.
One of the problems with this would be managing what to do when multiple friend requests are accepted at the same time.  There would need to be
a new page
(or a new section in the friends management area), where requests you have recently accepted are listed and
special links
* to those profiles are available.
Each link would open a new browser window when clicked, that would put you at the user's profile.  Close the new window after you've made a comment and proceed to any others if you wish.
The only other way to manage it, might be to make multiple acceptances at the same time impossible.  I don't think that would be a good way.
The special links* I mentioned would be similar to the "view group profile" that appear in your group management area on "my profile".  The one with the red outline around it.

author: society86
text:
The UG link on my browser goes directly to my 'favorites' page so I can pull up tabs I've saved.  I imagine this for most people is the single most important page in ones profile, so I'm fairly certain I am not the first to be bothered by these annoyances but anyway here we go...a few suggestions:
1.) More tabs on one page option -  Scrolling page to page to find an artist with no indication of where that letter is becomes time consuming.  This could be solved either by allowing the option to view more tabs per page or/and perhaps an alphabetical drop down list at the top.  If not a drop down menu that lists the bands, just an a-z links that will take you to that section.
2.) The ability to sort 'bass' tabs from 'guitar' tabs (or any other instrument)
3.) When I do finally reach my destination, pages away, I always have to open up the tab in a new window.  This is frustrating since I am a multitasker and already have 10 pages opened almost all of the time.  If I do not open in a new window, and instead just click, then when I push the back button, I am redirected back to the start (alphabetically) of my list.  I then have to scroll back looking for where I left off.
4.) Search Bar - Since my main page is my 'favorites' it would be nice for there to be a search bar rather than opening the first tab on my list to type in what I'm looking for.  I don't typically venture too far out of the main sections but I'm sure if I did there would be other pages without the search function.  This bar should be available on every page of this site.
Hope everybody enjoyed my bright ideas, everybody feel free to let me know what they think, good or bad.  Hopefully I didn't break too many rules, I haven't spent much time scrolling through other posts.

author: rodnolan
text:
re: suggestion 3) I totally agree. I actually came here to the forum to offer the same suggestion but you've done the typing work already. So I vote also vote for that one.
OR... another option would be to make the favorites section a drill down page where you get only the list of artists on the first page. A click on the artist would provide a list of your favorite songs by that artist. Kind of kills two problems at once. Lets you drill down quickly without having to hit too many "Next" links and hopefully, with another page in the mix, the need to start over at the beginning when you click the back button would be less of an issue.
OR... (too many options?) ditch the next buttons all together, load all the favs on one page and give users two filter boxes, one for the artist and one for the song name. That way, all the data gets loaded in the first page and never has to get reloaded again during that session because the filter feature would negate the need to re-load and re-navigate from the start.
I have hundreds of favorites in my list and either of these options would be a huge improvement.

author: dolphinsrule01
text:
I've a whole lot of incomplete tabs and chord charts in my drafts, usually because I've lost motivation to complete them, gotten sick of the song in the midst of tabbing, or can't figure out enough of the song to post as a complete tab onto the site. I assume that this is probably the case for a lot of users, and though UG has an email push-notification system to remind users about their forgotten tabs, I'm not sure how effective it'd be to encourage those who can't figure out a tab to complete the rest of it.
I'm just getting out an idea here (inspired by the new "Supremacy" tool
), but I feel that it'd be useful to have a queue where contributors could view and add to incomplete tabs. If a user felt that they need help with completing a tab or believed that they couldn't finish it, they could submit the incomplete tab directly from their drafts to the queue and other contributors could help complete it. (The tab would then be sent to the tpa like any other tab, and all contributors would be notified of its comments/progress in the queue). This could also help solve the issue of incomplete tabs in the tpa submitted by unregistered users (sometimes it pains me to reject nearly complete tabs that must be rejected as the unregistered submitter can't edit the tab). If these tabs are simply sent to another queue, others could finish tabbing them and they could still have a chance of making it on the site.
Of course, this would raise issues like how the IQ points are distributed among the participating contributors once the tab is published, how much of an edit is worthy of a user being listed as an author on the published tab's page, bad-natured editing or unnecessary deleting/spam, etc. (Now that I'm actually thinking this through it might not be a good idea to give the entirety of the UG community access to editing tabs- but for the sake of this suggestion I guess we must assume that all UG contributors are considerate people who wouldn't sabotage tabs in this hypothetical queue)
All in all, I think that there's a lot of wasted potential with incomplete unregistered tabs and unfinished drafts (maybe that one's just a me-problem) and that a solution like this could help get them on the site.

author: Rick540
text:
I was browsing the site today and thought of something that I think would be very helpful to users. I think it would be great if there was some way to show how long a member has been playing guitar under their avatar.
I don't know about coding websites or forums, but if something like this were possible I think it would be great. Depending on what the code would allow or how difficult it would be to code, a user could go into their control panel and either put the years and months they've been playing or even better, put the year they started playing guitar and then the amount of time would be automatically calculated and automatically increment as time goes by.
I think this would be great for two reasons. One, when someone asks questions about what kind of gear they should get or questions about theory, technique, and things of that nature, the user answering their question/giving them advice would easily be able to see how long the asker has been playing and be able to factor that into their response. Secondly, let's say a someone new to the guitar asks a question and another user answers it. The user who asked the question could look at the other user's time playing and that would let them know if an inexperienced player or a more experienced one is giving them advice.
Now with that said, I know that the time playing can be kind of vague. You might have a guy that has been playing a year but practices 10 hours a day and then a guy that's been playing 10 years but only plays a couple times a month. Still I think this would be a great feature to have.
Thanks.

another option, I noticed that the android app had my favorite flagged tabs even when off line. I assume the android app might cache these to memory. So I loaded Bluestack on my Surface pro, signed in with my same google phone credentials and loaded UG app. It worked. Tabs flagged as favorite were accessible with all network connectivity turned off.
A couple of notes, Bluestack can be downloaded free. Its a Android emulator for Windows. Works very well.
https://www.bluestacks.com/
No idea on Apple. I'm not in the cult...  :-)
I dont know if there is a limitation here, or if the UG guys intended for it to work this way on a windows machine. For instance I'm unclear if there is a limit to how many tabs it caches. Hopefully this will help the UG dev team. could be an option without having to write a windows app and all its hassles.
Note the Andriod app is not as robust as the windows via browser app. But worth a try if your going to use this to play somewhere with no internet.
Brett

From the 'Upload New' terms:
Quote by Terms of Uploading
Use the form below to upload your mp3 files.

Quote by Colohue
UG does not encourage breaking the law. I would suggest you stop mentioning anything of that sort. It is against the rules if you do it enough to be considering 'encouraging illegal activities.' UG offers the ability to listen to any uploaded material. However, the uploaded material is copyright to the user who's profile it is uploaded to.
If the user them self has copyright on their song, then they could choose not to have their song available for download. In the uploading options, a new box could be added with 'I approve for my content to be downloadable', so every user has a choice whether they want to make their song downloadable or not. It seems as though you think 'making songs available for download' equates to 'make EVERY song available for download regardless of the user's choice'.
Quote by Colohue
UG offers the ability to listen to any uploaded material. However, the uploaded material is copyright to the user who's profile it is uploaded to. If you like the music, then either ask the user for a copy or just listen to it using the mp3 player that the UG office worked damned hard to create.
The only downside to asking someone is that no one is easily available. Say someone lost their net connection for a month or so, meanwhile you wanted to have a copy of their music for a presentation, a video, movie, or just for your own personal enjoyment whenever you wanted, and you contact the person who is away. You would have to wait for 30 or so days (a whole 1st ban in UG terms), before you get any sort of contact back. Even then, the answer could be 'no'.
With the option to download the song, you know then and there whether the user is going to let you have a copy.
Now, as someone who doesn't know much about web-hosting and servers, and bandwidth, but has your average amount of logic - Wouldn't making songs available for download have little to no effect on how things work as they are? When you listen to a streaming song, you are downloading the song from wherever it is hosted. The only difference with the 'downloadable content' option is that the file is then saved to your hard drive, and instead of having to be downloaded again from the hosting server, it uses up less of UG's bandwidth and the listener's bandwidth.
Now, onto your point of using the player they created:
Everyone would still be using the player. I don't know anyone who, given the option, wouldn't listen to something before they downloaded it, hence the listening stations at music/CD stores.
The download option would just have to be added as another button in the player, similar to how the Myspace 'download song' option works in their player.
Quote by Lemoninfluence
I think making covers downloadable would still involve paying out extra license fees, even though there's no profit involved. But I'm no expert so I couldn't tell you for sure.
that, combined with the potential for using UG as a means of distributing copyrighted material means I think it wouldn't be a great idea.
OverClocked ReMix is pretty much a site based primarily on downloading covers, and I don't believe they pay anything except for hosting and the site itself.
https://www.ocremix.org/info/Content_Policy
I admit that there is potential for distributing copyright material, and to combat this, there would have to be a team of users who would be able to remove material that breaches the rules from profiles, that would scour all recently uploaded mp3s as well as profiles for copyright material.
I realise how much work has gone into the player as it stands, and I'm not suggesting that the download option should or must be implemented straight away, but it would be a great feature for UG to have.

author: drmcclainphd
text:
This may a bit too techie for some and too hard to do easily. And it may need to get moved elsewhere if it warrants attention.
I'd like to see a smart search function that could take some small input of chords, tabs, etc. and do a search for things in the database that match it exactly, or a smarter search that can run through transpositions and find same.
For instance, I recalled a Hendrix riff, played it, and then went on into what seemed the natural follow up. But it was wrong. I was doing (*sorry if the spacing is a little off)
---------------0--00-----------------------------------------------------------
---------------8--88-----------------------------------------------------------
---------------7--77-----------------------0-2-3-2-0------------------------
-----------2--6--66----------------2---2--------------------------------------
---------------7--77----------------------------------------------------------
-0--0h3------0--00-----0--0h3----------------------------------------------
One look at the chords and you can see why I confused it with Hendrix. Well I didn't think I'd made it up but could imagine where it came from. It took weeks before I recalled Raging River Of Fear from the first Captain Beyond album. Like wise I'd been playing around with something I thought I'd made up
[A(B) = beating out some boogie underneath an A chord]
A(B)  A(B)  A(B)  A(B)   G GGG   D DDD  A (repeat)
but that's got to be almost common. I don't want to rip someone off inadvertently.
There's also the easier case where I remember the chords
D A C G F# G A A

author: jonathanonfire
text:
As a long time member (4+ years) and user of the powertabs.net tabbing community network, I was part of a site that focused on creating and maintaining quality tabs. Now that the site has been shutdown by the MPA, I haven't been able to find another community as dedicated and disciplined to creating great tabs. Although I have found tabs on this site that I couldn't find anywhere else, these tabs(powertabs), like most on the internet, are littered with errors, such as missing guitar in symbols, incorrect time signatures, missing time signatures, no separation of sections, bad layouts, etc. I just thought I'd put in my two cents on how we used to do things in powertabs.net so maybe in the future, better quality tabs will be submitted onto the site. There are way too many **** tabs on this site, in all formats... there needs to be a better approval system. Here we go.
Score Checking
The single most important thing to use when you want to submit a good quality tab is the Power Tab Editor's Score Checker. If you look on the 'Tools' section along the top toolbar, you will find something called the 'Score Checker', which can also be accessed by pressing F11. This will show you all of the errors found in the tab. You can go directly to the source of the error by double-clicking the item.
How To Fix Score Checker Errors
Missing Gtr. In Symbols
Sometimes people forget to put in the correct guitar into the tab. I've even seen some tabs that have two guitars but only one is heard during playback! Make sure you add each guitar into the tab by accessing the guitar setup (the button looks like a red guitar) then add as many guitars as the song needs (max. of 7). Here you can change the tuning on the right side. Load a tuning from the 'Tuning Dictionary' (tuning fork and book) so you don't have to manually tune. After all your guitars have been added you must place Guitar In symbols into the actual tab so they can be heard during playback. Click on the 'Guitar In' button by the 'Guitar Setup' button to access the guitars added, then click the 'Staff In' check box to add the guitars to the staff.
Showing and Correcting Time Signatures
Using the Score Checker you can see which measures have the wrong time signature. It will usually say "Staff # - Measure total over/under by #/#." If it says that the measure is over by a certain amount you must raise the number of the time signature and if it says it's under by a certain number you must lower it. Easy enough, right? Let's give an example. Say I have one whole note and one eighth note in a 4/4 measure. The Score Checker might say "Staff 1 - Measure total over by 1/8." Adding one whole note (4/4 or 8/8) and one eight note (1/8), we get 9/8. The time signature should be 9/8. To change the time signature, either click the time signature by the clef or the 'Time Signature' button (looks like a 3 over 4) and change it accordingly. Make sure the 'Show Meter' check box is checked or else the time signature will not be shown on the tab and it will come up as a score checker error.
Showing The Dominant Key
This helps with the chord naming in the next section. Using the 'Tonality Tool' in the 'Tools' section, you can find the dominant key in a certain section, measure or the entire score. In this case, click on the 'Entire Score' button in the 'Data to Analyze', then click the 'Analyze' button (the magnifying glass) to show the keys in the tab. The key with the highest number in the total column is the dominant key in the tab. Knowing that, go to the beginning of the score and click the 'Key Signature' icon (looks like 3 flats) find the dominant key that you found with the Tonality Tool and click on it. After that, make sure the 'Show Key' box is checked or else it may show up as a score checker error.
Missing Repeating End Symbols
If there is a riff that repeats, you can use a repeating bar line instead of writing the riff multiple times on the tab. To add a bar line, click the beginning and/or end of the measure or click the "Music Bar" icon that looks like a |. Make sure that you put the repeating lines (looks like a double bar line with two dots next to it) at the beginning and end of the measure to avoid score checker errors and ensure correct playback. And also, at the end of the score, put a end bar line. The end bar line is the last bar line, that looks like a thick bar line and a thin one.
Empty Measures
This should be self-explanatory. If there is an extra measure, delete it with the 'Remove Section/Staff' button (icon looks like a staff with a minus). 'Remove Current Staff' removes only the staff/guitar track where the blue cursor is located and 'Remove Entire Section' deletes all staffs/guitar tracks in one section.
Other Tips For Submitting Quality Tabs
Showing Alternate Tunings
On the powertabs.net site, we had a few more rules for submitting good quality tabs. First off, we entered a line of text on the very top of the tab showing the guitar tuning. This helps so you don't have to go to the tuning part of the forums to find out the tuning of a certain band and which recording. That's just silly! Why not put it all there on the actual tab in an easy-to-read place to save time, space and effort? Press the 'T' key on your keyboard to open a new textbox. Look at the tuning in the guitar setup in case you forgot and enter it into the textbox. Afterwards, just drag it to the top of the powertab.
Separating Sections With Rehearsal Signs and Bar Lines
It's a good idea to separate each section (verses, choruses, solos, etc.) with a rehearsal sign. To add one, click where you want name the section and then hit the 'Rehearsal Sign' icon ([R]). Make sure to go through each section in order, alphabetically, for example, the first section is A, the next B, and so forth. At the end of a section, if there isn't a repeating bar line, use the double bar line. It just looks better.
Identifying Chords
This really isn't necessary but I think it's good to teach yourself and others what chords you are playing. For every 2 or more note chord, hit the 'Chord Identifiction Tool' (or press F12) in the Tools section. The starred(*) chord is the one you should use most of the time because that makes the most sense with the current active key signature. In any sections without chords, it's good to use 'N.C.'s' (No chords) to identify such. To show an N.C., click the 'Chord Name Text' button (the Cm icon), select N.C. then OK.
Showing File Information
Inputing the right file information such as the name of the artist, the song and the album it's from is good because it shows up when you try to print a powertab and also for reference purposes. The 'File Information' tab can be accessed by in the 'View' part of the top toolbar or by pressing Shift+I. Try to enter as much information as possible, even lyrics!
Score Polishing
When everything else has been done, use the 'Score Polisher' in the 'Tools' section up top so everything is aligned and spaced correctly. Easy, right?
I hope this helps. It may seem like a lot but if you use these guidelines enough, your tabs will look better and be easier to read. Make it section nature! For an example of a good tab (IMO) that follows these guidelines look at my tabs. I don't expect the mods and gods of this site to really take any of this **** in but it would be very nice if other members would take this advice in and use it for submitting/approving better tabs. Please. For all I know, this is the largest tabbing site around. People! Take pride in your work! Make this site better! For any questions, feel free to message me and such. Happy tabbing!

author: Roc8995
text:
The terms of service specifically prohibit advertising or promotion:
(e) Communications of any kind which include any unsolicited or unauthorised advertising, promotional materials, junk mail, spam, chain letters, pyramid schemes, requests for money, petitions for signature, or any other form of solicitation;
Clearly this was the case with your thread; the only purpose of your thread was to get people to vote for you, which is solicitation. The purpose of the competition itself is of course to get free promotion for that company too, so you were advertising for them at the same time.
In case that was not clear, the rules hub of the forum you posted in say this:
Advertising or Promotion Threads: Do not advertise. You will be banned. Since there has been some confusion about what advertising entails, here are a few examples of advertising:
-Starting a thread about your own business, your friend's business, etc. (We do occasionally make exceptions if you have useful input/content, so PM a mod if you think you have something of value to contribute).
-Threads whose primary content is a link to a blog, youtube video, press release, kickstarter, etc.
-Threads whose primary purpose is to link or promote a contest, Facebook page, or third party group.
UG policy against promotion is very clear and your thread was deleted for that reason. Promotion and advertising continue to exist even when you're a nice guy who isn't asking for any money. If you recognize that what you are doing is promotion, then it becomes obvious that the TOS sections on advertising mean that you cannot post what you did. We've seen the same misinterpretation a few times which is why the above rules are posted in the forum to be more clear.
Sorry, but it's definitely not allowed on UG. It doesn't matter at all if you think you're a nice guy or that the competition is important to you. It's still promotion.

author: Amuro Jay
text:
I want to talk about the way reviews are structured for a minute.
Having the reviews split up into sections with individual scores for each section is great for gear reviews, concerts, DVDs, etc, but it is extremely limiting for album reviews.
On one hand, it provides a good skeleton for inexperienced writers to organize their thoughts in a coherent way.
On the other hand, every time I write a review for UG I feel like I'm back in high school where the professors make you write your essays according to a formula. Some kids couldn't write papers at all, so the teacher would require everyone to write with a "topic 1 - point 1 - supporting reason 1, supporting reason 2 - point 2, etc" structure. It required little thought to put together, as it was more of a fill-in-the-blank exercise than writing an essay.
Any time I would try to break from this simplistic structure, I would lose credit. And yet, when I got to college, everyone who was using that minimal structure would make minimal grades.
Having that "sound - lyrics - overall" setup for album reviews is incredibly restrictive and I think a lot of UG writers are held back because of it. I mean, albums aren't written like that, why should reviews be? Most other major music sites on the internet (absolutepunk, allmusic, pitchfork, sputnik, NME, rolling stone, rocksound) don't write reviews like that either.
I'm not proposing to get rid of it, because I think some writers do need it.
What I propose is that UG gives reviewers the option to review albums in freeform. One of the reasons why I haven't written in so long is because I can't fit the square peg of what I want to say into the round hole that UG gives me.
Also, I think the numerical rating system has to be changed somehow as well. You can say a lot more with words than with numbers, and I feel like numbers are abused. Fanboys will rate everything with 9s and 10s and not say anything at all with their reviews, and too many people vote on albums without actually having heard them. It's silly. An unpopular artist will get tons of 1 votes from people who won't even bother to listen to the album just because of the fact that they aren't liked.
So, UG should have two ways to write the reviews.
The old way:
Predetermined structure
Individual scores for each category
Benefits include helping people write and helping users get a quick glimpse of how the album stacks up. The cons are that the individual scores for each category are always abused and based on that, many people choose to ignore the review in general.
The new way:
Free writing, not bound by boxes or categories
One aggregate score for the entire album
The cons are that the users will actually have to read the reviews to get a clearer idea of what the album is really good for, but then again, that really isn't a bad thing. It's actually a good thing. It will also require the writers to be more in depth to justify their overall score of the album. But they'll have the room for that since they won't be bound by those little boxes.

author: maguri
text:
The title of the reocrding may change. On a similar note even though it's not American vs. British:
Sometimes re-releases of the same recording have the title in a different way. For example:
John Lennon's song has been called "Give Me Some Truth" on the record (album and single) since it was released in 1971. in the 2000s album and song have been re-released/remixed several times and now the song is called "Gimme Some Truth" on these releases. Result: Wikipedia articles covering the song, title "Gimme Some Truth" but showing the record with the original title "Give Me Some Truth" -
Gimme Some Truth - Wikipedia
UG too has tabs under both titles. Difficult to say which should be updated. Sometimes things get complicated ...

The  re-mix on top of that is of a quality that most people wouldn't even notice as being a re-mix at all, beause it just sounds a little "fresher" but is otherwise true to the old mix  ...

author: johhnyshugg
text:
Hey guys, great site. I've got a suggestion to make searching for songs by a particular artist easier.
TLDR:
Would it be possible to group all the same song or album submissions for an artist into a single clickable link? If you want to see that song, you click the link and it takes you to another page where the 27 different variants of that song are then displayed.
LONG VERSION..
For example, I've just searched for Red Hot Chili Peppers, I actually clicked on their name from one of their songs, but I ended up at their list of songs.
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/artist/red_hot_chili_peppers_554
I'm now shown a page of their songs, with Albums at the top, then songs alphabetically below, going up to Apache Rose Peacock (ver 3), and a row of page numbers up to  10 and Next>.  A quick look, shows about  110 song links on the page, but  15 are for 21st Century,  17 for Aeroplane,  12 for Animal Bar,  15 for Annie Wants A Baby,  3 for Apache Rose Peacock.  So those  110 links have only shown  10 albums and  9 songs.
If I go to page 2, another 6 for Apache Rose Peacock there, so I can't even show all those versions on the same pages. Then Page 2 only goes up to Brandy. So 2 pages and we are only up to the B's, implying that I would have to wade through 26 pages to see their entire song list.
I realise that these lists include 9 different instrument versions, and that I can click the button at the top to show only the versions I am looking for, but even then, I click Chords, and there are still 3 pages, and some songs are listed 6 or 7 times. And I can't show combinations, like Chords and Power, or Tabs and Pro, together.
An easier way would be to have the main Artist page display with a list of Albums and Songs and just one link line for each, which you can then click to show the different versions of that song. You could then filter that list by type, All, Chords, Power, Bass, whatever, and then click the Artist name at the top to go back to the entire song list again if you want to see more.
You could maybe display the list for however long it goes down one page, although there probably should be some limit in case one artist ends up with a thousand different songs or albums, but that would be a rarity. It would make it easier for Admins to go through song titles looking for spelling mistakes, if a new song shows up in an artist page, it should be easier to see if it should be renamed to go on the proper song page. Or even leave the title as it is, but manually put it on the correct page, that would probably require an extra field in there somewhere to allocate the proper song page.
Anyway, thanks for reading far enough to see this message (if you did haha)
I just think it would make it a lot easier to search through an artist's list of works. Like, I've heard a Beatles song on the radio, so I came here to learn it, while I'm here, I wonder if I know any of their other songs, oh crap, there's more than 10 pages of them, don't got no time fo dat.
Thanks guys.

author: jakewillis92
text:
So, I am trying to get a bug resolved related to this, but it made me think... why is it that when you transpose a song into a traditional "flat key" (F, Bb, Eb, Ab at least), the transposer always reverts it to sharps? Would it be difficult that when you transpose a song into one of the above keys (or when you have a Bb in the key of C as a flat seven for example) that it knows that the "correct" and non-confusing way for people familiar with key signatures to read this would be in flats? Or somehow lock it into the number system so it knows a C in G = Bb in F?
I just tried this to be sure with three songs in the key of G, transposed down to F, and each times it turns the four chord Bb into A#, which by any traditional metric is an incorrect way to transcribe it, not simply a matter of preference.
Obviously "use flats" generally works as a work-around (except when it doesn't at least in personal edit pdfs, which is the bug I'm trying to get fixed), but in my opinion it would look much more professional to not be throwing gross A#'s at me all the time.
I'm a music teacher who uses the transposing function to get things into appropriate keys for my student's voices on a weekly basis.

author: jakewillis92
text:
UGMKZ
Yeah that makes sense, it would take a lot of consistently accurate metadata, and must account for capo positions. Makes me wonder if a place to start could be in the "official" versions, which presumably would have accurate metadata and could be an easier place to at least try it. I really do think in the long-term it could be a major improvement to the site. I know there are other programs like Planning Center that do a good job of working around sharps and flats when transposing when it knows what key something is in, so there are algorithms out there for it.

author: tasting123
text:
UG Support
Not an exaggeration. I've always known the asterisk was intended to mean
something
, but I couldn't figure out what, and there's no legend anywhere to explain it. It's always felt like I was missing something important.
First assumption was that the songs with an asterisk might be UG's preferred version of a song. But the asterisk never quite lined up with star ratings or any other obvious quality metric.
Then I thought maybe the asterisk denoted songs that are fresh and new. But there are some pretty old songs with asterisks and new songs without, so that theory didn't hold.
Then I thought maybe the asterisk meant a song needed attention, like something was wrong with it. But I couldn't figure out what was wrong with any of the songs with asterisks.
Now that i know it just means you can hover over and get a little popup, I think, "ok, that's fine, but I can't think of a situation where the asterisk would be helpful." IMO it's not worth giving new users the impression that there's a secret code that no one's explaining to them. But maybe other folks use the site differently than I do, so perhaps there are some users out there who benefit from the asterisk. Would be curious to hear from anyone who thinks it's a good feature.

I think it would be cool to have a similar type of forum to the Tab Requests forum but where people can easily upvote feature requests/changes they support (and be able to sort by date and upvotes).
Many of the suggestions I've had for the site have been addressed in the past, but never implemented (and the threads are closed and the ideas are sometimes added to the "backlog"). A lot of times the responses to requests are "we don't hear about  that issue a lot" but right now the only ways that I see to support requests is to post the same suggestion/request over and over or to necrobump or get old threads reopened, and none of those options seem that great.

text:
We will note this idea in our backlog ))
In fact, forum users are not the only ones whose opinion we take into account in order to prioritize the implementation of features.
