author: Amuro Jay
text:
I know that the idea of spoiler tags has been rejected repeatedly over the years for two reasons. One is that some people think it isn't necessary. The other is that it would be too hard to implement.
Some people do think it's necessary. It may not be the overwhelming majority required for UG to take the suggestion seriously, but there are those out there in certain threads (gaming, film, literature, etc) threads that think it would be good to have.
I'm going to run a poll in The Pit at the same time and report back later with the results to see how many people think it would be a good idea.
Now, the second reason. I get that it's hard on the current VB software to have the type of spoiler tags that require a hover to see or a button that opens a box to let you see.
But what if I proposed an easier solution, one that utilizes already existing features? Namely, font colors.
Spoiler
Quote by jetfuel495
Spoiler
Spoiler
Quote by jetfuel495
Spoiler
You'll notice that "Spoiler" only appears twice, but there are four lines of text, two of them are quoted. Which ones show up depend on what skin you're using.
My proposal is that we write a code that changes the font color of the text in the tags accordingly. The code will change the color of the text based on two things. Whether the text is quoted or not, and what skin the person viewing it is using.
The hex values for the spoiler font colors are as follows:
UG Classic: #e8e8e8
Classic quoted: #dfdfdf
UG Black: #181818
Black Quoted: #232323
Since UG has two skins, I'm assuming that the coding in the skin changes the default font color in the forums as well. So you write the code in a way that determines what skin the user viewing the post is using, like I assume UG does for the default font colors on each skin.
So the code would work like this: when text is written between spoiler tags, the font color is #e8e8e8 on classic and #181818 for black. If the  tag happens to be inside  tags, then the font color is changed to #dfdfdf on classic and #232323 on black.
I'm pretty sure this is possible because of the fact that default text colors change with the skin, and text is italicized automatically inside of quote tags.
That way, the only way to see spoilered text is to highlight it.
There. A way to implement spoiler tags without having to add any new features into UG's software.

author: GordWood
text:
There are far too many versions of a tab allowed for a single song. I have attached a picture of an example. The version with over 700 5 star ratings is not even close to the most accurate and even has sections of chords missing! Once a version has all those 4 and 5 star ratings, they remain on the page even if they are very wrong. Many beginners are giving ratings to these tabs that they absolutely do not deserve.
Have you thought about having a cap on how many versions to allow? You are not allowed to submit duplicate tabs if they are too similar, but for some reason we can have any number of the same song. This decreases the incentive for experienced individuals to create precise tabs for the community when there is no way to ensure that the more accurate tab is either the highest rated or the most used. Check out Hotel California if you want an extreme example! There are so many almost identical versions.
Many community members aren't experienced enough to accurately rate a tab and are very likely to rate poor tabs very high. However, these people are exactly what this community is all about! They need to be able to find the most accurate tab all of the time!
I suggest that community members that have received a certain level of notoriety have the ability to rate a tab with a separate rating from the 5 star system. Each song with many versions should have a version that is shown to be the highest rated by members of a certain level or higher. This would ensure that songs aren't receiving unwarranted and exaggerated ratings and help the beginner to know which version really is the most accurate.
There's no way I'm the only one who feels this way.. What ideas do you have about reinventing the star rating system?
"You can't spend all of your time sitting there grinding your axe.. You need to get out and swing it!"

When tablature is uploaded, it drives me mad when people compose guitar lines like the following example:
THE RIGHT WAY TO DO IT
E||-----------------12-17h-20h-24p-20p-17-12-
B||--------------13--------------------------

author: Ximich
text:
We're planning to introduce several major features designed to make the process of contributing and editing tabs a whole lot better.
After discussing it within UG Team, we came to a conclusion that it'd be better to ask how you guys think it should work, instead of offering a ready-made solution of ours.
What are your thoughts on how we can make the whole tablature thing simpler, more convenient and more effective? In other words, what can we do to make contributors' lives better? Don't hesitate to post your ideas, even crazy ones - we'll love them all

author: fanapathy
text:
It's a bit hard to read what this is actually about, but here are some thoughts I've had regarding tab improvement
-Instant update feature (for users who submitted >X tabs). It seems tab updates go into their own manual approval queue, perhaps to prevent contributors from turning their tab into spam or another song. Seems unnecessary and takes up time for whoever is clicking the accept button daily for a probably huge amount of submitted updates.
-Elimination of bad/obsolete tabs when new/better ones are posted (max # of tabs for a song, yet allow new submissions). Automatic flag/removal of tabs that get X 1-2 star votes as average.
-Instant approval regarding new tabs for trusted tabbers with a high average rating, their tabs are gonna be high quality and don't even need to be in the queue
-Allow title corrections
-Allow deletion of own comments and possibly comment moderation for the contributor
-Mandatory explanation of low ratings, similar to the "Reject" requirement in TPA
-Sort tabs by date in reverse order of what's current. More often than not, Ver8 is going to be better than Ver1 yet will only get a fraction of the views

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
Nope, never going to happen. Not just because of the amount of programming that would entail to change just the two notes:
Anglo
C C#=Db D D#=Eb E=Fb E#=F F#=Gb G G#=Ab A A#=Bb B C
Other Germanic
C C#=Db D D#=Eb E=Fb E#=F F#=Gb G G#=Ab A A#= B  H C
but because the wide majority of people using this site are from Anglophone countries, which use B and Bb. Also, the German system isn't the only one that exists; there's solfège/solfeggio, but we strictly stick with the Anglophone system. This is part of the "Tab Layout" section of the
Tab Guide
.
I'm not against using them at all - I've expressed support for letting both systems coexist - but this is policy, and many less well-versed people have been confused by "H" notes (and solfège) before.
Also:
it's infinitely clearer if the site sticks to ONE convention instead of multiple conventions.
it's bad practice to mix Bb and B in one song unless you have good reason
(e.g. in Anouk's "Birds", tritones; Céline Dion's "My Heart Will Go On", modulation). Check
this guide to tab/chord transcription
out!
Hope this helps a bit.

author: killergege
text:
Hi !
While browsing on the UG tabs I often noticed that the first versions of some tabs are really poor or incomplete. And more recent tabs are pretty good.
So I would suggest that UG implements a "Vote for deletion" functionnality.
I see it working like that :
- Somewhere on the tab's page, there is a link or a button " Vote for deletion".
- A windows would open asking the user to justify the vote.
- A moderator would have a page listing the votes. They may appear only if there is several votes for a tab (to prevent isolated votes to pollute the screen).
- He would review the tab and its comments to check if that it is worth the deletion.
- If ok, the tab is removed from the versions list. If you don't want "holes" in version number you may display the links grayed or "disabled".
- if the tab is correct and don't havereal issues, the moderator removes the votes and disables all other deletion votes on that tab (as he has extensively reviewed it, he knows it is not a deletable tab).
To prevent abuse and user conflict there may be some limitations :
- user may be registered for more that a defined time, maybe limit it to only users that have access to the TPA page, etc...
- the deletion may only occur if the tab has been submitted as "unregistered" or by a user that did not visited the site for a long time (say 1 year).
- the "vote for deletion" feature may only be accessible if there is at least 2 other tabs with 3+ rating.
- maybe it could be available only on low rated tabs.
The main objective here is to limit the number of version for some tab and remove uninteresting tabs as in most cases when there are lots of versions, the first versions are often incomplete or poor.
But this only works if the moderator checks the tab, the comments, and the other tabs to be sure that the deletion is worthy. Which may take some consequent time.

author: carriep63
text:
Quote by loloyd
UG is forcing me to write Chris Daughtry as the artist on one of the chords I am submitting.  The chord set I was submitting should be attributed to Daughtry, the band, not Chris Daughtry, the lead vocalist of the band named Daughtry.  Incidentally, the band named themselves Daughtry to take advantage of Chris Daughtry's name recognition after he got to the end of that popular reality show.
Kindly fix this and thanks.
You don't have to choose Chris Daughtry when writing a new tab. It will tell you that the artists name wasn't found in the database, but all you have to do is choose a genre and it will still let you keep the artists name you've typed in.  This is how we get new artists in the database all the time.  Just make sure that the song you are tabbing isn't already tabbed under the artist of "Chris Daughtry" because it could be rejected for being a duplicate.

author: carriep63
text: Also, once you do that and submit your chords, it may ask for a confirmation of the artists name. It's not actually asking YOU to confirm it. You can push the "confirm" button over and over and it won't go away. It's actually asking for a moderator to confirm it.

author: loloyd
text:
Yes, that is correct, carriep63.  The submission facility
would not
allow me to save my submission edits unless I relent to choosing a different artist name from among the jQuery-provisioned list.  Unfortunately, there was no way for me at that point in asking any moderator to consider the artist entry I was proposing for my submission as the system wouldn't allow me to simply save my submission for further moderator action.
I can see that the only "sound" resolution (no pun intended) for this particular problem is to add Daughtry to the list of acceptable artists and subsequently attribute all the existing songs submitted and ascribed to the actual band.
I am not sure if this problem also persists for other artists with similar problematic constraints.

author: johnchandler200
text:
I love the features offered on the Android devices for the playlists....First of all actually having them and being able to switch between songs quickly is superb.  But...In my field of music (Church/Worship) the scrolling options are not feasible.  The following options for either the browser version would be great!
1)  Make a "full screen" mode for playlists.  This would make it more usable in a live setting.
2)  Give an option for "dual column" mode for playlists too.  It keeps more print on the screen and has less possibility for losing your spot when you have to scroll.  I would make this the standard for the "full screen mode" mentioned in item #1.
3)  Provide single button "hot keys" for quick changes.  For example....The down arrow key be used for a "page down" functionality, and moves the text down the page but shows just enough of the previous view so it seems "seamless" and you don't lose your place in the motion.  Up arrow would do the opposite,, while left arrow would go to the "previous song," and right arrow would be "next song."  Space bar could be used to start or stop scrolling if needed.....etc....you get the idea.
4)  Give some color options to the parts of the song.  Make it where i can change the colors of the text "Verse 1" to a specific color so it stands out, then the actual lyrics be a lighter/darker shade for further differentiation.  Have the chord notations also have this function to where they also stand out from the lyrics.  The App "Chordale" has some of these features.  It requires downloading the library of music and importing it.  Having access to it on UG is much better option.
5)  Create a downloadable app for WIN-10 devices with this functionality.

2) Illegal selling of personal interpretations of copyright material in order to make a quick buck
3) Selling out, pure and simple
I suppose all textbook publishers are non-profit organisations too.
The idea is that you can have guitar pro/powertab type functionality on the go. You don't have to have guitar pro or tuxguitar installed on the computer you're using, you just need to log in to your account. Which is useful if you're around at a friend's or at a computer where you don't have admin rights to install programs.
UG has already 'caved' to industry pressure in that it obtains licenses that allow it to distribute derivative works i.e. tabs. It's either that, or be taken offline.
As to your other point. Firstly, they aren't selling any tabs. They're selling access to a software. Exactly the same as what happens with guitar pro. And secondly, By submitting works to the site you're giving UG a license to modify and distribute the work through the service (the site in general). So it's hardly illegal.
In 10 years, the internet has changed. Laws are now catching up, business models have changed and ad revenue is becoming less valuable due to changing browsing habits. You can't expect a business (which is what UG is) to stay with an outdated model and survive.
In what way are you harmed by it existing? It's an optional extra that's still in its early stages.

author: CrispedRice
text:
I have a brand new account, i.e. I have the default notification settings, and I find it strange that some of the notifications are turned off by default:
New private message - mobile app push notification
Discounts, special deals and offers - email notification
Why? Shouldn't everything be turned on by default and then I can choose which ones I want to turn off?
And the one called "
Most Wanted Tabs digest
" doesn't have any options at all? Why is it on the list if I can't get those emails?
I have used UG before so I know how the tab submission workflow works around here and I would like to know why the contribution-related things don't have email notifications as an option?
Contribution was approved
Contribution was rejected
Contribution got a vote
Contribution got a new comment
Tab was rated
Tab got a new bad tab report
Tab was edited
Tab got a new correction
Tab in the Approval Queue got a comment
The way I see it, I think someone makes a tab, decides to send it in to you guys and then they're quite likely to log off again. If you don't send them emails about the status of their tabs, how are they supposed to know that something has changed? They're probably not logging on every day to check for new notifications on the website. Don't you want users to be notified so they can come back and check things out if someone says their tab needs to be edited? At least send out emails for "
Contribution got a new comment
" and "
Tab got a new bad tab report
" and "
Tab got a new correction
" and "
Tab in the Approval Queue got a comment
"

author: UG Support
text:
CrispedRice
hi, thank you so much for taking the time to share such detailed and thoughtful feedback—it really means a lot to us. You’ve brought up some excellent points, and I want you to know that your insights are being heard.
You're right—it
does
seem a bit odd that certain notifications, like new private messages via push or discount offers via email, are off by default for new accounts. Our team is actively reviewing notification settings and preferences, and feedback like yours is exactly what helps us understand where the experience can be improved.
Regarding the “Most Wanted Tabs digest,” we agree—it’s confusing to see it listed without a toggle. That’s something we’re aware of, and we’re looking into how we present these options so everything feels more consistent and transparent.
And your thoughts about contribution-related notifications are especially valuable. You've made a great point about users submitting a tab and then logging off, not realizing there’s been activity—whether it’s a vote, a comment, or a correction. We absolutely want contributors to stay engaged and informed about what’s happening with their work. Email notifications for events like "Tab got a new correction" or "Contribution got a new comment" would help with that, and I’ve passed your suggestions directly to the product team.
Thanks again for such constructive feedback. It’s clear you really understand how things work around here, and we truly appreciate your help in making Ultimate Guitar better for everyone.
If there’s anything else on your mind, don’t hesitate to reach out!

author: antonburton36
text:
Upon the issue of the ability to change usernames, user theguitarists states the following:
This isn't up for debate. If you have a legitimate reason for a name change, you can message an Admin (red name) regarding it. Only acceptable reason for a change from my point of view is for serious privacy concerns where your account can be connected to your identity and you've made some extremely compromising posts here. Considering this is supposed to be a "family friendly" site, this is very rarely an issue.
This response and attitude is NOT OKAY regarding online safety and personal information control. Before I start I would like to say I am a qualified software engineer / computer scientist, I know what I'm talking about.
1. Email leak
- Currently spam artists can take usernames from this website, append common email service names to the end (e.g. "@gmail.com", "@yahoo.com" etc) and determine with 100% accuracy if the email is valid. THIS IS NOT OKAY! They can monitor our threads on this website to create phishing emails especially designed based on what information we have posted here. This is a HUGE security risk and a utter failing of UG to provide their users with a safe platform.
2. Personal Information Leak
- A lot of email addresses contain sensitive information (e.g. full names, dates of birth, etc). This can be used for identity theft online. This is yet another massive security risk UG has overlooked.
3. User Friendliness
- We do not live in the year 2005 anymore, it is 2016 - to be allowed to choose your own username is a BASIC standard that is upheld on good websites on the internet today. The fact that UG hasn't supplied this feature speaks millions on how outdated this website is. I do not trust UG with any of my information and will be requesting my account to be deleted shortly.
4. No Delete Option
- So UG has our personal information and they are publishing it online without our consent. On top of this they do not allow us to delete our accounts - so our only other alternative is to delete our email addresses and change ALL other  sensitive online services (e.g. online banking) that are associated with said email to prevent security risks.
5. Facebook Identifiable
- Using a combination of username and avatar (or either) anyone can identify your Facebook account. The information there, coupled with posts here will further building on the ability to perform identity theft and individualized phishing attacks.
Just to point out, if I did something like this at the company I work for, I would be fired instantly. This is not acceptable and should not be treated lightly.
SOLUTIONS
- If a user signs up via FB, allow them to choose their own username upon redirect from FB. UG can store our personal information on their database(s), but this information should never be publicly published. This is VERY easy to do from a software point of view. If the developers at UG say otherwise, they should be fired and some more competent developers should be hired.
All users who have signed up via Facebook should be given a link via email to allow them to change usernames, this can be an easy automatic process with the EXACT same checks done as a user who is signing up for the very first time. If UG have designed their database structure correctly, all FB accounts should be identifiable, to create a bulk email list and secure edit username page should take no longer than two hours.
Those of you who expressed concerns were 100% right to be concerned. This is a problem that cannot be ignored, if it is ignored again I would advise all who have created FB accounts to delete your account immediately and create a separate account via email.
Do not Lock this thread
, this is
NOT
how you deal with problems of UG, especially those detailing valid security concerns - not to mention it is pathetic response, to be honest.
View the original thread here:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1285209

Your comment shows a worrying amount of ignorance for a developer.
You also haven't addressed all of the other huge security flaws that antonburton36 mentioned.
The fact that you don't allow accounts to be deleted is a huge violation and you already have people forming class action lawsuits against you.
I'm genuinely confused as to why you think sticking your fingers in your ears and telling people that "If you do not want to identify you - don't use social networks" is an appropriate response when people are geniunely trying to inform you of an issue it's clear that you're not too educated on.
I've also worked in the data industry and your stance is incredibly troubling. I really on't see things going well for you if you continue with this attitude.
All that people are asking for is the respect and decency that they used to on other websites. Let's not forget that they are entitled to this under EU law. Your current username policy does not comply.
Here is an appropriate excerpt from the data protection act.
"Appropriate technical and organisational measures shall be taken against unauthorised or unlawful processing of personal data and against accidental loss or destruction of, or damage to, personal data."
This is the seventh data protection principle. In practice, it means you must have appropriate security to prevent the personal data you hold being accidentally or deliberately compromised. In particular, you will need to:
Design and organise your security to fit the nature of the personal data you hold and the harm that may result from a security breach;
Be clear about who in your organisation is responsible for ensuring information security;
Make sure you have the right physical and technical security, backed up by robust policies and procedures and reliable, well-trained staff;
Be ready to respond to any breach of security swiftly and effectively.
The fact that you have a username policy which means personal information is made publicly available and the user has no control over this is a violation of our rights under EU law as you fail the first point. You have not designed your security to fit the nature of the personal data you hold.

author: Dexex
text:
My name is "Dexex." I'm a rhythm guitarist. Over the last 30+ years I've made hundreds of guitar chord charts for the various bands I've been in.
I joined UG in 2009 after the On-Line Guitar Archive (OLGA) was shut down for copyright infringement. I believe that the Music Publishers Association (MPA) of the USA shouldn't have the ability to prevent anyone from sharing their interpretation of an artist's song. So, I decided to post some of my charts outside of MPA jurisdiction, to the Russia-based UG.
As of today, I have 117 charts posted at UG, most of which have four or five-star ratings. My rank (today) is #372. Pretty good, if you consider estimates are that 10,000,000 people use the archive.
However, I believe that UG's efforts to force chord charts to work with their mobile platform is making UG a poorer resource. And I believe that the moderators who are enforcing the standardization of chart format are approaching submissions negatively with a determination to find a reason to reject, rather than positively looking for a reason to approve. That's about power and profit, not community.
As evidence, please read the comments below for my latest, and last submission. The song is  "Thank God For The Summertime" by Ben Rector from his 2013 CD "The Walking In Between." If you search for it, you won't find it (today) at UG or anywhere else. If you search for lyrics, you won't find correct lyrics anywhere on the net. In the chart I used an industry-standard method to distinguish single notes from chords — lower case letters in parentheses — to indicate a walkup that is essential to playing the song. Go listen to it and you'll see what I mean.
Despite the fact that this chart would be the only chart for the song available anywhere — despite the fact that it has all the correct chords and lyrics — and despite the fact that it is immediately playable (see comments below), it was decisively rejected. Why? Because UG moderators are leading the effort to force chord charts to work with the UG mobile platform.
Why? Because the UG owners only want products they can sell. If they can't capitalize on my chart, they don't want it. And that approach will ultimately cost UG the community they've built since the demise of OLGA.
Let me know if you find a resource that is about the music, instead of the money.

author: brettsanace
text:
Firstly, let me say I applaud the effort to clean up the site by limiting the versions of each tab and forcing users to make corrections to existing tabs rather than submitting new versions. However, in addition to only allowing, recorded, acoustic and live versions I believe a beginner version is also required, particularly for Chords.
Whilst I understand the desire to have accurate tabs, the vast majority of people who play the guitar do not aspire to become professional and perform live gigs (except in their fantasies) and are happy to be able to strum out a song and sing along in their living room, or at a party with friends or around a camp fire. They don’t need it to be perfect, they just need it to be playable for their skill level and to sound reasonable.
Beginners do not want to be limited to beginner level songs (there’s only so many times you can play Mull of Kintyre) but also want to play the classics and current top 40 songs. I believe UG is letting these people down.
I have seen people try to submit beginner versions of tabs (chords) only to be rejected because there were more accurate tabs already on the site, where it was obvious they were not trying to provide the “official” chords but simply to provide an easy version for beginners.
I have seen people try to submit a version of a tab that only uses open chords only to be rejected because it can be generated by using UG’s Transpose function on an existing tab. Whilst that is true, when a beginner checks out the tab and sees it is full of bar chords generally they won’t sit there and keep clicking the transpose button in the hope that they might find a version with mainly open chords, but rather they will be disheartened and go look for another song. Would it really be so bad to have one beginner version of a song even if it is simply a transposition of the “official” tab.
It might be argued that beginners could use UG’s “Simplify Chords” function, but simply taking the root chord of the various dim, aug, sus and add chords does not necessary result in the best chord for a beginner version of the song.
I have seen a recent forum post complaining that the star rating system is stuffed because there are so many incorrect tabs with high star ratings because most users aren’t skilled enough to know if a tab is correct or not. I would suggest that these “incorrect” tabs are receiving high ratings, not because people believe they are perfect, but rather because they are easier for them to play as compared to the “correct” tab.
Unfortunately, these tabs that have received high ratings because they are easy for people to play, are now getting overwritten as people attempt to submit the correct tab and get rejected and are told to submit a correction to the existing version, thus complicating the easy to play version.
All these factors are contributing to beginner players not being serviced by UG’s product. All I’m asking is that “Beginner” be added as an option for Version along with Recorded, Acoustic, Live (as distinct from the Difficulty Level of Novice, Intermediate, Advanced) and as with the other versions aim to only allow one Beginner version for each song.

author: UG Support
text:
brettsanace
Thank you for a very detailed explanation, and for all the care about UG and our users. We really appreciate the effort, and we do try to serve our users as well as possible, but sometimes we just can't accept some tabs, because they are too far from the original, or too close to some other, already submitted version. Star rating has its own troubles, and it's a subject of another discussion.
Simplify function, Novice difficulty level, chord transposing option - they are all meant to ease the process of learning for beginner guitarists, as well as lessons, lists of best songs for beginners and occasional  breakdowns of famous songs. I don't think we'll add a Beginner type of version, but we'll think about a way to give novices another way to learn songs. Anyway, thank you for the initiative, we appreciate it.

author: pizzapat12
text:
Full screen scrolling doesn't work as it should. Possibly not full screen, but I haven't tested that. The scroll should be after the SECOND to last line vs the last one. When it scrolls after the last line on screen, you have absolutely no way to see what the next line will be. This is sometimes what happens and it seems to work 75% of the time, but if even a tiny little portion of a line is peeking out of the bottom of the screen in full mode, it counts that as the final line and won't scroll until it is finished playing the last line that we can actually see.
The tempo and transpose functions are brutal now too. After also working perfectly fine before, they now get bafflingly screwed up when you simply change instruments. It'll sometimes put the tempo back to full speed, sometimes not, sometimes show it at 100% despite still being slow, sometimes the opposite. Same with transpose, it seems like the tab uses a random number generator to decide whether it changes both the displayed transposition and the actual playback one when you switch instruments. So, for example, when I try to play Back in the USSR by the Beatles at the recorded tempo and key vs the sped up version we here on record, it's a mind numbing process every time I want to simply switch to a different guitar part. I'll set it to -2 transposition and 89% speed, then switch to lead guitar 2 and it'll show 89% speed, play at 100% speed, show the tabs not transposed at all, and play them at -2. It's horrendous.
Or, to edit what just happened after I posted this, I'll change the speed to 89%, then transpose down 2, and it'll reset the tempo back to 100% for no discernable reason despite still showing 89%. There is no rhyme or reason to any of it. If you set the tempo and transposition, it should stay on those values no matter what you do unless you leave the page or change them back.
The new player is seriously making me reconsider paying for the pro membership. It's just inexcusably bad at stuff that the old player did completely fine.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
The rules themselves are good guidelines. If you read through them thorougly, you'll have a good idea of what the general code of behaviour on UG is, and what is and isn't acceptable for the UG mods.
Not every specific situation is described in the rules, to avoid making it a rulebook the size of a football stadium. But from the general descriptions and with some common sense, you should be able to deduce the specifics. For example, the "no spam" and "no vulgar content" rules are very general, but it's kind of obvious that UG, being a 13+ website, isn't the place to discuss shock porn websites, for example.
We don't really operate on the basis of specific guidelines other than the rules, but if you really want something to hang on to, remember these three things:
1) The rules generally contain all the info you need on how to behave on UG;
2) If something specific in the rules isn't clear to you, feel free to ask a moderator;
3) One moderator's decision is almost always backed by the rest of the moderator team, so there aren't really any "one mod's hate post is another mod's joke" issues. Should you feel you've been treated improperly, again, feel free to ask another moderator.
Hope that helps.

author: SFBay-James4
text:
These have been problems ever since I became a member. Doesn't seem to matter what browser but I am on Safari.
Search:
1. You start typing in a keyword search ("Tom Pet" and you get an autofill.  However mouse-clicking on the drop-down with "Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers" doesn't seem to auto populate into the search box.  Highlighting "Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers" and pressing return doesn't either.  And neither (mouse-click nor highlight+return) actually triggers the search to begin.
2. There seems to be no rhyme or reason to the results.
Search "Oasis" and then filter by "Guitar Pro." The results include and prioritize "Don't Look Back in Anger (Live)."  Many pages later you get "Don't Look Back in Anger (Acoustic)"
Search for "Don't Look Back in Anger Oasis" and then filter by "Guitar Pro."  The results take you straight to the recorded version (and official tab) of "Don't Look Back in Anger."
Also, if you search "Oasis," filter by "Guitar Pro," you get "Official," "Guitar Pro," and "Pro" tabs.  I actually like that...but maybe create a filter of "Downloadable" or something.
However, if you then filter by "Official" then you get official tabs but they are no longer hinted with the same color scheme that denotes official tabs everywhere else.  Then if you re-click "Guitar Pro" to go back and filter by Guitar Pro compatible tabs, not only do the official tabs get hidden, the Guitar Pro table get hidden and you only see "Pro" tabs.
Also the sorting seems way out of whack.  Clicking on sorting by "ABC" (alphabetical) seems to destroy any relevancy.  After searching "Oasis" and clicking "ABC," the first page gave me "Iris" by the "Goo Goo Dolls" before going back to Oasis.
Probably needs a legit UX designer to review because it's kinda a mess right now.

author: SFBay-James4
text:
Searching for Tom Petty makes it appear that you have no Official nor Guitar Pro tabs for "American Girl," "Breakdown," or "Learning to Fly."  Searching for the Song Title + Artist got me eventually to the tabs but I had to navigate through a Bob Dylan + Tom Petty collab of "Knocking on Heaven's Door."  Except for Learning to Fly which placed Frank Sinatra's "Fly Me to the Moon" as its top choice.
I could not even get to Tom Petty's "Don't Do Me Like That" until I removed "Tom Petty" from the search criteria.
You also have some huge data quality issues which is common for community/crowd-sourced data.  You might want to...
1. global find and replace "&" with "and," "dont" with "don't" (heh, your forum autocorrect even does this) and similar clean-ups
2. for all of the "The" bands (e.g., "The Cars") put the "The" into brackets (e.g., [The]) code the results engine to ignore the brackets.  So "Cars" and "The Cars" appear together.
3. You should download a table with Artist, Song, and Views/Downloads.  Then group+sort by artist then  views/downloads (or count of songs).  Then you can manually clean up "Joan Jett" versus "Joan Jett & the Blackhearts" versus "Joan Jett and the Blackhearts."
It's clear that your relevancy engine plus data quality causes tabs (even official ones) to get lost.

author: JustLikeMe
text: In order for us to hold a contest on Ultimate Guitar, we must comply with the legal requirements in every territory in which the contest is available (on the Internet, this means virtually the entire planet). Thus, our posted rules satisfy the requirements for participants in specified territories. Also, sometimes the contest sponsor wants to limit the participants to certain countries for one or more reasons.

author: plaindaye
text: I think this forum is special in that it’s a concentration of guitar players. They can come here to share information, music and all of that good jazz. Another issue I’ve noticed with this forum is how archaic it is. I’m well aware that usually comes included with forums but: there are some ideas I think could be cool to implement. Make it possible for users to create their own individual categories. Make it possible for users to change the color scheme of their for their taste. I really think part of the reason this forum has been alive for so long is that it has a lot of guitar players here (bassist too). And no matter what, people are always going to need guitar tabs. author: brettsanace
text: The current Approval Guide has a section for Working with Tabs and another section for Working with Corrections. Both of these sections include reasons for approving and rejecting, however none of these really apply to approving/rejecting strumming patterns. In the TPA - Pending Approval queue Stummings are listed separately from Tabs and Corrections, however in the Approved and Rejected queues Strummings are lumped in with Corrections so people may simply regard Strummings as a type of correction. However, as stated the approval and rejection reasons for Corrections don't really apply to Strummings. Also, whilst I understand why the 3 day rule is not required for Corrections I believe it should apply to Strummings as often many of the comments relate to suggested corrections to the submitted Strumming. The Working with Tabs section also includes rules about comments some of which should also be applied to Strummings eg Don't repeat other peoples comments,  Don't leave comments that won't help the author to improve the strumming

author: NSpen1
text:
brettsanace
Yep, agreed, except I'd like to add that the 3 day rule shouldn't apply to all strummings ... some may not be so far out and you can leave comments as to what needs to be improved, but other patterns are totally wrong and could only be fixed by completely rewriting the pattern, so I believe those should be rejected straight away.  I would regard them as the strumming pattern equivalent of a tab which is in the "Total mismatch with a classical formatting." category, or a "(completely) Inaccurate correction."

Quote by captaincrunk
I've been moderating a couple groups, and I think the ability to send mass PM's would be really useful.   Or a nudge, or something to get the attention of the members.  It's been a fight at best to keep things moving with them, and it would be a big help.
There may be a way to do this already, but I don't know of it!
There is currently a way, but it's rather clumsy.
1  -  Post a blog in the group.  Group admins (and group moderators, if the admin enables extended privileges) can post a blog.
2  -  Have all the members of the group subscribe to the blog.
3  -  Any new blogs posted in the group will generate a notice on the group members "my profile" section.  If they have email notifications set, they will also get a notification that way.
4  -  This turns group blogs into bulletins.  The problem is, you have to get all the group members to subscribe.
imho, it would be very useful to have all group members get a notification on new posts in group threads, by default.  They could opt out of it, but the norm would be to get notices.
You couldn't have picked a worse time to bring up this subject.  It's Christmas break for UG Office.  The chance of this being discussed by the Russians during the next week is almost nil.

author: travislausch
text:
I'm really not sure where to post this. I thought the "Tab Pro Suggestions" section would be appropriate but every thread there seems to have to do with subscriptions rather than the tabs themselves. And I'm not even sure if there
is
an appropriate place to post this or what can be done about it but I feel I should bring it to someone's attention or see if anyone else has this issue or if it's just me somehow...
Anyway, I've seen some visual changes in the Tab Pro tab layout that I really like with regards to things like note spacing, but there's still an issue I'm finding makes the Tab Pro tabs hard to read, and it has to do with beamed notes (eighths, sixteenths, thirtyseconds, etc.) that are surrounded by rests. The notes have stems but no beams. This is just an excerpt of what I mean by this:
Every single one of those unbeamed notes is supposed to be read as an eighth note, but they're not. This isn't just a problem with this one tab, it's every tab I read on Tab Pro. While it's not the most pressing issue in the world, it makes reading tabs a little bit harder if I'm trying to follow along with the rhythmic notation in my head (especially for those pesky djent tabs!), and I thought I'd bring it to someone's attention anyway.
Either way, I'm really digging the subtle changes being made to the browser version of Tab Pro. It's constantly improving and I really appreciate that, and there's a reason I absolutely swear by it, even despite some issues that haven't been cleared up. Thanks for providing the service!

author: ghostmasterjay
text:
First, I would like to thank you for the service you provide.
Many people in America and around the world have monthly download limits with their internet service. When I click a tab, at least 3 moving ads come up. Sometimes I can pause them, others I cannot and they eat up data. Even when all the ads have been stopped, the page loads continuously, even when I hit "x" to stop it from loading. It often causes my computer to crash. I use the site for my job and it can be problematic.
I feel like this is a problem as old as the internet. I would like you to consider limiting video ads to one per page, and turn the others into still ads. The site would run much much better and look much more professional. I understand the need for ad revenue, but there are some alternatives. (A store perhaps, I haven't been able to find one on the site, so if there is one already, nevermind)
I hope you'll consider this or something like it to solve this problem. I love that sites like this exist, but there comes a point where the balance tips from "tab page with ads" to "ad page with tabs".

The way I remember this alternate tuning feature is like this.  If a song on this site were tabbed based on the guitar being tuned to an alternate tuning this was explained and if I didn't want to learn to play it in an alternate tuning I could click on a button and all the tabs were changed to be accurate with a standard tuning. author: schasm
text:
Hi all,
This is my first post on here and hoping you guys can help me.
I have recently brought out my hughes and Kettner 18w twelve tubemeister, I’m getting back into my pedal boards and although the lead channel is not to my liking for various reasons the clean channel serves a nice purpose for my pedal boards (within the budget I currently have for a new amp lol).
I have been researching replacements valves -
The amp currently has the shite Chinese stock valves in and I plan on switching them out and generally giving the amp a service before taking it for a spin (a service to my limited capability of course lol)
I’m looking at sets of JJ’s and The ELL84’s are a given for me at the moment (am open to change of course) but some additional feedback with regards to the 803 or 83 for the V1 and V2 slots would be appreciated.
My aim is to smooth out the high end of the amp (I know EQ adjustment is key lol) but this amp has killer high end and I want to smooth it out for my pedals with the new tubes. My pedals will push all of the variation of tone required, I just want to take some of the ‘fizz’ out of the little thing.
Current planned valves -
ECC83/5751 JJ Tesla - pre amp V1
ECC83/5751 JJ Tesla (balanced triodes) - V2
2x EL84 matched pair tubes
Although the above slightly sounds like I know what I’m talking about I can ASSURE you I do not and just some light research has led me to these choices.
Thank you in advance.

author: metalmingee
text:
schasm
if you are in the USA, checkout eurotubes.com.   They have a few options listed for your amp and you want to get a few extra tubes to try.
5751 will lower the gain and the gold pin version is supposed to be “smoother”.
I still have a pile of different tubes from when I was tube swapping an old 5150.  Single tubes are an inexpensive experiment!

author: schasm
text:
Hey!
I’m based in the uk, have some great tube suppliers local to me. To be honest I am starting think buying a few variations is a good idea but for a couple of sets worth it’s going to be mildly costly, it’s always the same - do I start to invest or do I swap out lol.
The older I get the more I like to swap things out and try and find my own flavour to be honest. Only thing is I’m a little reluctant to spend a lot on an amp designed in Germany and built in china lol, makes me sound like a gear snob which I’m not……….. or at least I don’t think I am!

author: haynesr
text:
I spent awhile swapping various pre-amp tubes in and out of my Jet City (as well as running an MXR 10 band EQ in the fx loop) trying to tame the fizz. A better speaker cab ended up being the thing that made the difference I was looking for.
Also, managing my expectations, high gain amps are fizzy; and a lot of that fizz doesn't really stand out in a mix.

author: schasm
text:
Hi!
I appreciate your comments and agree.
Thing is I loved this amp when I wasn’t using pedals,
I have never been a fan of the lead boost just because the volume change is ridiculous and there is no way of changing that but I would just use the gain and lead boost both ‘on’ for when I wanted the high gain and adjust the volume on that which was fine.
Now I am using pedals with it the amp just makes it a nightmare because the pedals just don’t seem to like the fizz (gain pedals).
I will sit on it a little longer but think I may just sell the amp and look for a different amp that is more suitable for pedals.
Thank you again

author: maguri

cjheinz
The pitch of the Ink Spot's reecording is not 440Hz for the A, so it might sound a little off, if you tune your guitar to 440. But it is just a little higher than the B and way closer to B than to C.
Seems you guys sorted it out by yourselves, even though it took some effort.
Things like that happen from time to time; as a tab author you better get used to that, try to not take it too seriously and always stay calm and neutral in your replies, no matter what the other party says ...
Keep up the good work!

But the Edit-button does work?
Changing keys: I usually transpose the existing chord sheet, then copy the transposed chord sheet, go to the edit page and copy it over the existing tab. Sometimes in this process a lot of new line breaks are added, though, and it would be tedious to remove them manually. In this case I copy the transposed tab into my word processor and remove the unwanted double line breaks with the find and replace function.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
I started contributing things regularly from 2014 until the beginning of 2018, during which time I saw a lot of changes to the site (and still do). During that time, I managed to make some long-term friendships and contribute to running conversation about updates on the site, particularly on the contributor side. Come 2016, the site was ready to migrate its Contributor group to the forum platform, and I accepted a nomination to be a moderator, expecting to allow conversation to flow civilly, to organize topics of discussion, as well as oversee the general tab approval process as I had done in 2015 to the tune of even being acknowledged by the site for being the most active contributor that year.
When the Author Community (meant for contributors to the site) opened, I opened a few threads meant to facilitate contributor conversation - if their contributions were lying in wait or were poorly duplicated, for example. As a then-active member of the Musicians Talk community and an avid tester of nomenclature, I created a running list of chord nomenclatures that would work with the UG system as it was before. All this work was done with the intention of making UG a more hospitable place for all users - including non-contributors. Not all of these additions were met positively.
There have been many changes since then, and the site stressed me out, if I'm honest. More senior contributors had been using their artificial status to demand changes of bad ratings and even attack other users based on their non-contributor status, among other uncivil actions. Friend voting - quick perfect ratings for friends - as well as rating with multiple accounts often went unchecked for long periods of time, sometimes at the expense of other contributors with competing contributions. The combination resulted in these people's contributions looking far rosier than they would under a stricter standard. The attitude among most contributors was actually quite friendly, but the cumulative effects of years of bullying other users - of which at least some would be likely to be real people - was disheartening, to say the least. People on the other side of the screen are still humans with feelings, no matter where they come from, after all.
The most stressful part of moderation came in the summer after I started moderating: IQ contests. Giving away monetary prizes was guaranteed to attract the most attention. During that time, the UG employees did minimal proofreading of submissions: it was up to the unpaid contributors of the site to navigate the large influx of submissions. It resulted in many public incidents broadcast in the news section and even before. The last time someone won a guitar (mid 2017), uncivil behavior resulted in their "permanent" expulsion from the site (although he has somehow managed to write something about winning that guitar three months ago, and moderators can't do anything about it because a part of the moderation system is broken. Figures.).
In the interest of other, less well-versed users of the site, I defended the implementation of, for example, the strumming pattern interface, as well as corrections. Blowback from senior contributors added to the stresses.
I used to have decent conversations with the staff of the site as well until they stopped actively responding to me about things that were important and/or urgent. I understand that there is a lot to do on the site, but a community with issues left unchecked was bound to generate further issues of the same sort. Furthermore, actions taken without consideration of all sides would not yield the fruit desired. Revenue is an important aspect of the success of a company, but it should not come at the cost of integrity.
I write this because I have recently seen the rebirth of IQ contests. Before I left, I had begun to think that monetary prizes without supervision and rigor befitting the value of the contests were a really bad idea, even though I would still like to own an electric guitar.
Now that a few things that UG has undone have come back to bite you since I left, including:
- uncivil behavior aimed towards your employees and other users alike;
- friend voting; and
- your own ignorance, feigned or not, on the effect of prolific contributors' behavior, to the point of demodding me for banning a (now permanently banned) contributor whose toxicity lashed out at everyone who disagreed with his opinions and transcriptions/formatting, as well as even holding a vote on unbanning another contributor who changed his profile to say "Your A Horses Ass" repeatedly after he was banned for similar abusive behavior patterns, and one of them who posted this lovely message after being banned;
I have this to say. Despite flaws and occasional high feelings (and misunderstood intentions on many sides), this site has generally decent contributors and users. However, a contest with valuable winnings needs to be held to a higher standard than has thus been demonstrated by staff. Should the staff be unable to hold a contest's results to a rigorous standard, you should simply not hold the contests.
I shall not return (for) responses;
I have better things to do with my time
. Best wishes.

author: SgurrnaCiche
text:
I'd like some clarity on what's a duplicate and how appeal works.
I went to see the film "Three Billboards...". It starts with Townes van Zandt's "Buckskin Stallion Bluues." I got enthused and checked the chords here - they were wrong.
Some detail was wrong but in the last two verses, Townes ceases to use the whole verse chords and just keeps repeating the chords for the last two lines. This gives a different tune which you can't sing to the earlier chords.
So you get
UG version     Actual
ADA               DA
AEA               ADA
ADA               DA
AEA               ADA
DGD               DA
AEA               AEA
Someone's already commented that the earlier version doesn't work.
So first question. Is that still a correction or is it a new version?
I appealed the decision with a description of the difference.  About five minutes later the user who'd rejected it first time, rejected it again with one word "Duplicate". I think an appeal system which doesn't involve a second opinion is flawed.
My second question, what is the appeal system?
I'm not a sore loser. I had a String Band song rejected as duplicate last year. I put in an appeal and another user, a String Band fan, gently told me I was an idiot and it was a duplicate. I looked again and went away red-faced. I'd been changing the key in my head and got it totally wrong.

author: WugtheBug
text:
I'm sure this has been brought up many times in this thread, but the process for notifications in user profile comments is ineffective.
Basically how it currently it works is that users only get notifications for comments or replies
in their own profile
, but not for replies to their comments on others profiles. This makes any forms of communication in profiles absurdly impossible, especially since many newer users are not aware of this issue and end up creating replys that are never seen.
I know a fair amount about software engineering, so I know that this honestly shouldn't be a very complicated fix, and I'm surprised it hasn't been corrected before, but I just wanted to point it out as a reminder of a very annoying issue,

author: WugtheBug
text:
Another issue I just noticed:
When editing my profile "info," I just realized that I can add bands, guitarists, bassists, etc. I assume that this means my favorites in the categories.
I filled in the "band" category, but once I saved it, they were all just listed with a single space in-between the bands. This makes it very hard to read or distinguish between bands, especially when the band-names themselves are multiple words.
It would be much better to list them all in a column, for example:
Boston
Camel
Caravan
David Bowie
The Doors
Dream Theater
ELP
Focus
OR if this is not practice, which it may not be since it takes up so much space, it might be better to put a dash (-) or something inbetween the band names to distinguish.
I assume that this problem also extends to the other categories, such as "guitarists" and "bassists," etc.
EDIT: I've added my own dashes in the guitarist and bassist categories, as I assume this problem will not be fixed, but I left the artists category unchanged so that you can view it and understand what I'm saying.

author: WugtheBug
text:
Also, seeing that official tabs, GP tabs, and the option of showing piano chords all appeal to other instruments, this is really a music-in-general site, not just guitar and bass.
Therefore, it would be nice to add more categories to the info section I discussed in my last post, such as "vocalists"  "drummers" and "keyboardist."
Since the point is just to describe the tastes of the user (as proved by the already existing "books" and "movies" categories) it makes complete sense to add these.

author: LMBozovich
text:

the system does indeed automatically check to see if an official tab or a request of said tab has been made or not, and it prevents a second request from being made.  That being said, it does not automatically upvote said tab(s) when you search for them.  I see nothing wrong with how things are done nowadays with the official tabs requests though, as the position we’re in lets us show how much we want said tabs to be approved.

author: Nothinglessness
text:
Yo.
I have some criticism to offer for the UG Guitar Team if that's okay.
I understand the workload the UG team is under (the amount (and variety!
) of tabs you people crank out every week is pretty astounding and I really do commend that!), but I have to point out that the quality of the official tabs is a bit questionable at times,
especially considering that they are automatically tagged "high quality"
and are advertised as such.
What I mean is that I was under the impression that the official tabs are supposed to offer comprehensive tabs that are
clearly distinguishable
from the basic stuff submitted by users here. Of course no tab is perfect and everyone makes mistakes (and some songs
do
have way too many tracks to fit in a tab, so completely comprehensive tabs are not always possible), but if I'm being 100 % honest, some of the official tabs just seem plain lazy to me.
Here's two examples to illustrate what I'm getting at:
1. The recent official tab for Simple and Clean by Utada Hikaru.
The original song is
full
of all kinds of small flourishes often present in modern pop production and most of those are ignored entirely in the official tab (even the backing vocals are almost completely missing!?). There are very basic mistakes with the rhythm of the vocal melody etc. There are only 3 tracks in the official tab that are not vocals or percussion (8 tracks in the tab overall, whereas just the synth tracks of the actual song should make up at least 7 tracks by themselves. And that's just with a quick listen).
I'm sorry but I don't see how that counts as "high quality"
.
2. The official tab for Harvest by Opeth.
The time signature is very obviously wrong in multiple sections (this is evident if one tries to relate the tab player's metronome to the song's main pulse) and the hi-hats on the drum track are not at all what they are supposed to be. These are mistakes that wouldn't be that unusual in user-submitted tabs, but in
official
tabs? C'mon. I remember reading that some of you have degrees in music so it shouldn't be a matter of skill.
Of course there's the fact that I view tabs (and especially official tabs) as more than just specifically GUITAR tabs and would like the official tabs to be fairly consistent with all elements of the song, minor flourishes included. They are often useful with picking up on other stuff going on in the song, if, for example, trying to learn the song with a full band setup. Obviously if one is of the opinion that the accuracy of the guitar part is the only thing that matters, then I suppose it's just a difference of opinion. But as long as the intention is to create as full of a representation of the song as reasonably possible,
it takes more than that
.
I know there are a shit ton of requests to cover and that making properly comprehensive tabs takes a lot of time. But still, I personally would be completely okay with some tabs taking significantly longer to create than they currently do if that meant that they would be comprehensive and more consistently accurate. The tab will be useful forever once it's created, after all!
Thanks for reading
I love the site and I really appreciate the work you all do – this piece is by no means intended to provoke or anything. Just that at least for me, the quality should be top priority if I've understood the concept of official tabs properly.
P.S. There are countless great official tabs and this criticism does not apply to most, obviously. Some of them just have really weird omissions or blatant errors that seem very out of place in official tabs.

Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.

FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team

author: mendace
text:

The UG guitar team (i.e. the guys who create UG's official tabs) choose which requests to work on based on a number of criteria. There are 32,000 requests and they have to prioritize them somehow. They usually pick the most popular requests but sometimes they create tabs for newly released songs or songs from the top list that they are familiar with and can transcribe quickly. Here is the top list:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/tab-request-top
At the top of that page, you can find this message:
Everyday UG Guitar Team fulfills the top-1 request and 4 random top-100 requests from the top requests list.
Other tab types, such as guitar pro and bass tabs, are fulfilled by UG's community members. They can choose any song they want to work on and most tab authors choose requests based on their own personal preferences. We currently do not have a lot of authors who fulfill GP or bass requests.
You can find all of your tab requests here:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/user/threads?user_id=55153307
Please note that tab requests which only have one upvote are deleted after 12 months.

author: rlasher1999
text:
Regarding the official tabs, the backing tracks are separate thing that you should not make downloadable. However, I agree with making the tabs themselves downloadable. In Guitar Pro 7, you can lock the editing of the tab with the password, so that people can just print, play back, and export to other file formats. If someone wants to make a change, they can just export it to MusicXML or MIDI and change it in another program. But who would want to edit the official tabs anyway considering they are of very high quality! If there is a mistake noticed, it's better for the benefit of the whole community that you let the UG team know about it so they change it themselves and let everybody have the revised version!
If you were to download an official tab or any tab for that matter, it will play back either in MIDI or with the Guitar Pro RSEs, not with the UG team's backing tracks. If someone were to steal the tabs and reupload them to another site, there still would be no good web player, no backing track, no Tonebridge preset, no support from the UG community, etc. There are still a lot of features of the official tab experience that are very very hard to steal no matter what!
In summary: please make the official tabs downloadable, but don't make the backing tracks downloadable! Instead, people should learn how to make their own backing tracks using the downloaded tab in Guitar Pro and exporting to a DAW like Logic Pro X! Or better yet, go out there and record some real instruments! It's way more fun and rewarding that way in my opinion!

For duplication issues, would it be difficult to implement a system where you compare let's say an MD5 hash of the original file (your official tab) with the MD5 hash of the user's upload. Another thing I noticed is that all the official tabs have a hidden strumming and chords track named a particular way. If a user's uploaded file contains those two tracks it could be suspect. In the end, a good thief will find a way to cover his tracks, but fortunately for the rest of us many thieves can be careless and stupid.

author: thequadrat
text:
eastwestrocker
Hi. There is a bug with requests that have more than 1000 votes we faced previously - notifications do not send for such requests. So when we fix this issue we will make Official version.
Speaking of choosing songs for Official tabs production and priority.
Official tab team have been established 7 years ago to make the most accurate versions of popular songs. With time we were able to cover most popular songs on UG and then requests were announced to realise what our users would like to see as Official versions. Some time after we've added an ability to vote for any song in UG catalog which have no Official version. Last year this option has been added in our apps.
At the moment we have over 58000 requests and most of them are requests of songs which already exist on UG as other types.
It is impossible to fulfil all these requests so we need to prioritise them.
Priority rules also been changed several times depending on amount of requests and voting activity.
Official tab team consists dozens of musicians and we work hard to deliver tabs non-stop every day. Our main goal is to make tabs that most users will appreciate and want to see. The amount of tab views is our blood which lets our team exists and brings tabs for you. We've researched many aspects of created tabs and figured out that not only votes but also voting speed, popularity of artists and songs on UG are also very valuable criteria for us. There is no any profit for our team in fulfilling requests and make tabs which would be seen few times a day so we are focusing on requests that potentially will bring us more views. Non-requests such as new releases from popular artists and songs with many views without Official version are fulfilling constantly and bring us solid portion of views.
We are now in the process of reviewing our whole request system to make the song choice transparent for users and focusing on the most desirable requests. We are experimenting with different approaches of which requests we take to work. We will also try to find a solution for those requests which have no any version on UG and created by users because now such requests have almost zero chances to be made.
Hope to give you some updates in 2024, stay tuned and thank you all for supporting, commenting on Official tabs and being active all this time!

Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.
Our office team (left to right): Nick (
nick_zubarev
), Eugeny (
indieee

mandelstamdavid

bratanchuvak

FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team

hey guys, just wanted to say that I love the official tab feature. It's probably one of the best features you guys have ever added as it fixes nearly every problem I had with the site previously. however I do have a few questions/suggestions. sorry that it's lengthy
1. Is there any official rules or even a general guide for how many tab requests are too many or how long it usually is for a request to get filled? I realize that requesting for a ton of tabs means won't help someone's case for getting them filled more quickly, and that different songs have different levels of complexity and therefore can take longer/not as long to fill but it is somewhat confusing. a general rule I think would be helpful as people would have a better understanding of what they're paying for (for example something like: "roughly one tab request per month for a intermediate complexity song is guaranteed any more depends on how many upvotes they get")

hi could you explain the difference between official and pro tabs please?

author: LMBozovich
text:
segersoversea1
mandelstamdavid isn’t here anymore, but I can answer that question.  Pro tabs are the tabs made using the softwares guitar pro and/or PowerTab Editor, and are typically posted by regular tab authors.  They can be seen by anyone with the software, or anyone with a pro membership on the website.  Official tabs are made by the UG Team, and have not only every instrument and vocals, but also an instrumental backing track for the song also made by the team.  These tabs can only be seen by those with Pro Membership.

author: thequadrat
text:
Hi all.
A small update to give you an understanding of how we work with Official requests now.
As being said here (
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/redirect/post?p=38457094),
we are not rely only on amount of votes now.
At the moment we have 85000+ requests for Official tabs. Most of the top requested songs with many votes are complicated prog rock songs which take 2 and more days (4 and 5 are quite common thing). These upvotes have been collected for years and as a result, when we check metrics for such tabs - more than half of them are quite low in terms of views and activity.
At the same time we see that we have other songs where people vote more actively and views on other UGC versions of these songs are way bigger (which means more people visiting these songs and would see Official tab version redirect). This also works with freshly released songs - we can see how they got 15 votes on the day the first tab appeared on UG and many users visiting them and vote for Official. We got way more views and responses from such tabs and they usually take 1-2 day to produce tabs. Comparing to complicated most upvoted songs it just more efficient for us to work with most demanded content.
But we built a system to take all parameters into account with corresponding weights for each. This results in new parameter we call 'Score' which shows real demand for our community. We used this parameter for the whole 2024 and metrics for Official tabs boosted very good. It also let us to increase percentage of songs covered with Official versions.
Anyway, top requests by votes are still valuable and we work with them also on a regular basis (it is quite common for requests to speed up with votes collecting when they get to the first page on the forum).
It is hard now to set this new 'Score' parameter on the site to give you real list of what we see and choose but we have plan to implement it somehow and let everybody see the whole list, use search, vote for as many songs you want quickly etc. We also need to improve flow for working with requests in the app, it could help to increase value of votes parameter.
And for understanding, this is the top list we have now, where we take one or two from the top everyday. Notice how different votes and score parameters, this is the reason of complaints, we understand it, but this approach shows way better results. The three requests per day rule has been in force and abided to by most regular tab authors for a while now.
