author: Eric_Stenlund
text:
Quote by mandelstamdavid
Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.
Our office team (left to right): Nick (
nick_zubarev
), Eugeny (
indieee
), David (
mandelstamdavid
), Alex (
savenkoalex0
), Ivan (
bratanchuvak
) and Dmitry (
Koenigtiamat
)
FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team
Hi Team, I´m a new user and I have a question about the tabs where the tuning is half-step down. Why are the chords in the tabs written as the true tuning? I mean, if the chord is clearly played as a G the chord above the tab is saying F#. This is only creating confusion when playing.
Thanks/Eric

author: LMBozovich
text:
Eric_Stenlund
I can’t say for sure, but if I had to guess, it’s probably so the newer users can recall the original shape(s) of that chord.

author: NSpen1
text:
Eric_Stenlund
It's because of a fundamental flaw in the system UG uses, and one of the things about the site that most badly needs fixing.  You're absolutely right, the chord is played as a G shape and that's the way that anyone sensible is going to be thinking of it.  You play a G and because of the half-step tuning it sounds as F#, but you don't want to have to mentally transpose every chord by a half step.  The official tabs are slightly different as they're written with the pitches that actually sound whereas the vast majority of tabs written by users in half-step down tuning are written according to the chord shapes you play, which is how it should be done.  But because of the system all the chord diagrams are messed up, so if you put G it'll tell you you have to play a G# barre chord.
Sweet Child O' Mine for instance is played as if it was in D, the tuning means it sounds as Db
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/sweet_child_o_mine_official_1910965
This is how it should be written
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/guns_n_roses/sweet_child_o_mine_chords_176076
More Than Words, you think of it being in G, sounds as F# due to the tuning.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/extreme/more_than_words_official_1982595
This is how it should be written
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/extreme/more_than_words_chords_14087
btw Highway To Hell is not supposed to be in half-step down tuning, it's just that the tuning on that album is all over the place, 30 cents down here, 65 cents down there.  It's supposed to be played in A in standard.  (And I don't know who on earth thought that was a good strumming pattern to use.)
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/acdc/highway_to_hell_official_1916729
How it should be
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/acdc/highway_to_hell_chords_139966
It's A, D/F#, G, not Ab, Db/F, Gb
Users have resorted to writing tabs for half-step down tuning with the tuning set as standard to avoid the wrong chord shapes, and then writing a note on the tab to say it should be half step down.  Previously you were able to at least put the tuning to "not selected" so that it wouldn't wrongly say "standard" but that possibility has been removed.  It was also useful for when you had a song in a non-standard tuning that wasn't among UG's list of tunings.
I've posted about it many times, and I still hope that they'll eventually fix it.
Last thread on it
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1814902
And I don't believe any research is needed, I must have given enough examples by now, and I have more if needed of course

author: NSpen1
text:
Btw in the Sweet Child O' Mine official tab B is theoretically incorrect, that should be Cb in the key of Db.
Similarly in More Than Words, Db/F is wrong for the key of F#, that should be C#/E#.  You would have avoided that if you'd written them the correct way, just sayin'.

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
Quote by NSpen1
Btw in the Sweet Child O' Mine official tab B is theoretically incorrect, that should be Cb in the key of Db.
Similarly in More Than Words, Db/F is wrong for the key of F#, that should be C#/E#.  You would have avoided that if you'd written them the correct way, just sayin'.
We specifically decided not to use E#, Cb and etc.

author: LMBozovich
text:
mandelstamdavid
why? Wouldn’t it make a world of sense more to use the pitch names based off the key you’re in, instead of using different names for said pitch class?

author: NSpen1
text:
mandelstamdavid
Yes, but they do exist and I think it would be better to allow the possibility of their use, instead of writing things incorrectly and giving people the idea that you can write e.g. flats in a sharp key when the notes you're using are staying within the key.
And best to write the official tabs in half-step down the way I say, so you have C in the key of D, and D/F# in the key of G.

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
LMBozovich
NSpen1
We just don't ant to make these tabs more complicated for beginners. They are afraid when they see E# or Cb.

Perhaps it is handy to know that here in Ultimate Guitar we have two different lists to find songs to make a tab for. One is the Request queue, where anybody can ask a certain song in CHORD - TAB - PRO etcetera. When you want to work on a request, it is wise to claim. Just write underneath "I do this one"
On the other hand we have a computer generated queue, that we call the MWT (Most Wanted Tabs). When the Untimate computer see a TAB song from The BEATTLES called I WANNA HOLD YOU HAND, but computer sees no CHORD type of this song, the computer adds this song in the MWT.
Because the MWT contains a lot of OLD songs like THE WHO and THE CURE, seldom anyone does such a song. It happened to me once that while I did a song from the MWT gueue, someone else finished the same song I was working on. You cannot claim a song in the MWT queue. Clever is not to work on the top 10 in the list.
You can find the MWT on your homepage (Right top block called Tab Requests) and under the MY CONTRIBUTION - PENDING APPROVAL - ect, the 5th item from the top.

author: alexandrevida
text:
Quote by mandelstamdavid
Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.
Our office team (left to right): Nick (
nick_zubarev
), Eugeny (
indieee
), David (
mandelstamdavid
), Alex (
savenkoalex0
), Ivan (
bratanchuvak
) and Dmitry (
Koenigtiamat
)
FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team

author: rlasher1999
text:
If it was only a MIDI file, that would not be completely OK due to the way GP exports to MIDI. It doesn't have the capability to write volume or pan data to the proper MIDI expression values. It also doesn't apply pitch bend, dead notes, or any of the other numerous guitar/bass effects that GP's engine plays back so excellently! The way I work around this is to solo the guitar track I want to export and then export it as a WAV audio file after turning off all the effects. Then I have a clean audio file where I can apply all the effects in the DAW and still get an authentic sounding guitar. I'm sorry, but that's where MIDI just doesn't cut it! Not you guys fault but rather the GP developers.
There's no way working around it, I believe to satisfy all your pro users that want official tab downloads you're gonna have to enable it! However, enabling MIDI download would be a great option IN ADDITION TO enabling tab downloads for those users who don't feel like paying for Guitar Pro software.
And I personally don't think tab piracy will even be much of an issue. Access to UG Pro monthly is so affordable for 99% of users that people won't need to engage in piracy to get access to the premium tabs when they can just sign up for the pro subscription and get it legitimately along with backing tracks and other features. People engage in piracy mainly for economic reasons, not just to be jerks and rip off your work. Since your product is affordable, the chance of people pirating your premium tabs to work around the issue of paying is very very low.
And YES, a new audio and visual engine would be greatly appreciated!

author: rlasher1999
text:
mandelstamdavid
I would suggest if anyone on your team has the opportunity, that they export a guitar track to a DAW or MIDI sequencer and hear how it comes out, especially recommended with songs with multiple complex guitar parts, and then compare that to Guitar Pro's playback engine. Then hopefully you will understand my point of view on why MIDI downloads only is not a good compromise.

author: LMBozovich
text:
fanapathy
I disagree regarding ear-transcriptions.  If one is actually patient enough, and one has had substantial ear training, then it is indeed possible to have a 100% accurate tab.  The positioning might not be correct, but as long as it’s playable, then it doesn’t matter what position it’s played in.

author: fanapathy
text:
LMBozovich
There are probably cases where it could theoretically be possible but depends what one means by 100% accurate, how it's originally played in regards to strings and fretting or simply getting all notes right. Strings will produce different sounds obviously even if playing the same note, making it incorrect depending on how you'd define perfect. You can listen for those sounds, string changes I mean, even still it might not match your instrument. I haven't transcribed for years but what I liked to do for instance, and you get this by experience as you probably know, you realize the artists are making subtle mistakes/missing strokes or even hitting unintended notes. Now, should you tab those accidentals or leave it be as probably intended written, looking more perfect...Or tab in those tiny mistakes, because that's authentic. Then there's the case of bad mixing, excessive amount of guitar tracks, especially if distorted, where you can't really be positive which track played what - then what if the FX used on the tracks are identical and are panned the same way. Sometimes you just can't tell, but make a good guess. Sometimes orchestrals can blend in with the guitars, if you can't hear every single stroke of every string in a chord. Was it really just a 3 string power chord on that track? These things can drive a perfectionist transcriber insane and might never get done, at least not in a few days. And not with confidence. But hey if you find a 100% accurately tabbed advanced song, let me know and I'll be eager to find the mistakes

author: tom627
text:
Quote by mandelstamdavid
Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.
Our office team (left to right): Nick (
nick_zubarev
), Eugeny (
indieee
), David (
mandelstamdavid
), Alex (
savenkoalex0
), Ivan (
bratanchuvak
) and Dmitry (
Koenigtiamat
)
FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team

author: mandelstamdavid
text:
Hi, I'm David, head of the UG Guitar Team. I would like to introduce the team and tell a little bit about what we do here.
Official tabs
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. Our main goal was to provide our users with a complete experience, when everything you need is already in the tab. All official tabs are created by the UG Guitar Team.
So, every official tab includes:
a high-quality interactive tab;
a backing track that is synchronized with the tab;
a chord tab;
a Tonebridge preset.
Also, each official tab was double-checked to insure the best quality. There are already more than 11,000 official tabs in our database, so there's a lot to choose from.
Access to UG's official tabs is a part of our
Pro service
. Pro users can request Official tabs from our team completely for free.
Browse official tabs
UG Guitar Team
UG Guitar Team was formed in 2016 to create Tonebridge presets and, later, UG's official tabs. There are more that 30 people in the team, including remote workers. Every guy in the team has 10+ years of guitar experience, and half of us have music school diplomas.
Our office team (left to right): Nick (
nick_zubarev
), Eugeny (
indieee
), David (
mandelstamdavid
), Alex (
savenkoalex0
), Ivan (
bratanchuvak
) and Dmitry (
Koenigtiamat
)
FAQ
What is an official tab?
Official tab is a completely new tab format invented here at UG. It includes chords with lyrics, an interactive tab with playback, a backing track that is synchronised with the tab, and a Tonebridge preset. Watch our
quick guide to UG Official Tabs
to learn more.
Where can I find the official tabs?
You can browse them on the
official tabs page
.
Who creates official tabs?
All official tabs are created in-house by UG Guitar Team.
Why can't I open official tabs?
Since official tabs are part of our Pro subscription, only Pro users have access to official tabs.
Become a Pro
What if I didn't find a tab for the song I want to learn?
If you are our Pro user, you can request an Official tab from our team completely for free. Every day we fulfill most popular requests: 1 request from the 1st place of the Official Tab Requests top and 4 random requests from the top-100 by upvotes.
What songs can I request an official tab for?
You can request a tab for any song that doesn’t have an Official tab on UG. One more thing, we fulfill only the most popular requests.
How can I get more upvotes on me request?
People will upvote your request if they need a tab for this song. Asking other users for upvotes in attempt to promote your request is prohibited.
Where can I find the most popular requests?
You can find the list of top Official tab requests by votes
here
. You can also find top 5 requests by votes on the main page of the site. Upvote the songs that you want to learn and play. When we start working on a request, it disappears from the list.
What does the “Want Official Tab” button on the tab tab page do?
The button appears on tabs for the songs that don’t have an official tab yet. Click the button if you want to get an official tab for the song. If a song gets at least 15 votes within one month, a new official tab request will be created. The request will appear in the
Official Tab requests top
, and other users will be able to vote for this request.
I saw a request from the UG Robot with a lot of upvotes. What is it?
This request was created automatically according to the increasing number of votes that came from the "Want Official Tab" button for this song.
How long does it take to create an official tab?
It usually takes 3-5 days depending on complexity of the song to make a tab. You will usually get a message that UG Guitar Team has started to make the tab. Expect to wait more than usual if you request a complicated song like
“Bohemian Rhapsody”
by Queen or
“Shine On You Crazy Diamond”
by Pink Floyd.
How many requests can I create?
The best way is to create a single request and then wait until we fulfill it before creating another one. We don’t limit a quantity of requests that you can create, but remember that there are other people who requested tabs.
How do I know when the tab I requested is ready?
You will get an email notification and a forum notification when we’ll start and when we’ll finish fulfilling your request.
How can I create a request?
Use our request form:
Request an official tab
(Pro users only)
Don’t forget to add additional details to your request that can help us make the tab better for you.
I have a question!
Feel free to ask our team any questions here, we will be happy to answer.
Cheers,
David @ UG Guitar Team

On other forums I use, I think the OP can delete the thread within 30mins or having to PM an admin to make the judgment (and get an infraction by default). That prevents some bad threads and ensures OP thinks through what he writes somewhat more.
It's not just that, for example in Tab Talk someone asks for help on a song, then you decide to tab it and spend some 30mins or so, but meanwhile OP had second thoughts and deleted the thread.
Threads that turn "bad" in the subjective eyes of OP could also be deleted or otherwise when threads don't turn out the way they expected it to (which is very often).
Of course, if someone posts themselves playing a cover hoping for positive/constructive feedback, then gets slaughtered by awfully negative comments - a mod would (probably) agree to delete it on request anyway.
Not super frequent here on the forums, but the delete option is indeed surprising - especially if you can delete a big thread you made at any time (which I think is the case, lock would be a more fair option to posters yet again - why should OP get to decide when it's over).

author: Roc8995
text:
I think that's the point, though - the delete option is very rarely used. I don't think it's a big enough problem to put the effort of the posters above the autonomy of the person who started the thread. I think the threadstarter ought to be given the option to delete the thread, having started the topic. They don't "own" the thread, but I think starting a thread gives a certain small authority to that person, and they should be allowed to remove it if they want. Sure, people should be careful about what kind of threads they start, but what about the users that are trying to get a job five years later and don't want that thread in the pit that they started showing up on a background check? It would be unreasonable to expect people to anticipate any reason they might have in the future to delete a thread. Sure, a mod can do it, but I haven't seen it abused to the point where I wouldn't trust the users with the ability.
If anything, the ability to close the thread seems like it would lead to more petty use than the deletion. Getting the last word and then locking a thread would be a much more annoying use than just deleting a thread that didn't go the way you planned.
Ideally, it could work Reddit-style, where deleting the first post just removes the identity of the poster and the content of the post, and the rest of the content stays. But I don't think that vBulletin has that kind of capability, or at least it would not be worth the work to add it. So to me the fairest option is to let the threadstarter keep that small amount of control over their topic.

It's too bad that the current system pits that against keeping content from other users, but unless that changes I think it's more important that people be able to remove their own content from the forums.

author: NeoMvsEu
text:
Licensing isn't the problem. The issue is that standard notation introduces a lot of detail not found in tab. It's like asking for a map with detailed directions when all you have are the directions left, right, straight, and back and road names. Tablature to notation, particularly ASCII tablature, is not going to give the amount of detail required to create notation. Notation, on the other hand, is sufficient to create tablature (as long as finger positions are known); however, notation is not the focus of the mainly guitar and bass guitar audience of this site.
With the Tab Pro interface, I'm pretty sure the majority of the site users are more comfortable with tab than with notation. Even if they were to use notation, both Guitar Pro/Power Tab and the Tab Pro interface have limitations not found in more robust notation programs. (they're not automatically theory smart in cases where theory would necessitate changes:
https://www.sputnikmusic.com/forums/showthread.php?t=538098)

I don't see anything in there about granting copyright privileges of our posts to the site owner.  My understanding is that copyright-able material (pictures and literary works, etc) are inherently copyrighted unless you explicitly grant that right to another party.  if you check the image attachments on wikipedia, they do have an explicit grant to the public domain by the author.  I don't see such an agreement on this site.
However, there is the question of whether its actually useful to register your copyright.  If you're not making money from the copyrighted work, what damages would you claim if someone steals it or reposts it without your permission?  If I read correctly, you need to register your copyright if you want to obtain damages in excess of the amount you would have made had the material not been stolen.  Since you weren't selling the material to begin with, the registration is pointless.
In all countries where the Berne Convention standards apply, copyright is automatic, and need not be obtained through official registration with any government office. Once an idea has been reduced to tangible form, for example by securing it in a fixed medium (such as a drawing, sheet music, photograph, a videotape, or a computer file), the copyright holder is entitled to enforce his or her exclusive rights. However, while registration isn't needed to exercise copyright, in jurisdictions where the laws provide for registration, it serves as prima facie evidence of a valid copyright and enables the copyright holder to seek statutory damages and attorney's fees. (In the USA, registering after an infringement only enables one to receive actual damages and lost profits.)
source:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright#Obtaining_and_enforcing_copyright

author: Hyacinth3
text: I assume it would help other editors if, when one clicks, "Suggest correction", a warning that your suggestion may be rejected because it improves upon the tab rather than making it perfect, while others may reject your suggestions because more than one is suggested at a time. It should definitely be made clear in the Approval Guide whether simultaneous corrections are preferred or not. Contributors should be able to approximate the response to their suggestions. Will your single suggestion for improvement get rejected because it didn't make the tab perfect or will your suggested improvement get rejected, even though it would make the tab perfect, because it contains simultaneous suggestions. Contributors are less likely to make suggestions for improvement if they get tossed back and forth between contributors who believe in perfection or nothing, and users who believe in improvements.

author: evfidripiy
text:
Hyacinth3
, the rule of corrections approving, according to common sense is simple - if your correction makes the tab better formatted or more precise - it should be approved. If the correction reflects the opinion (like "I think that this tab better sounds with Csus4 instead of C") - it should be rejected. Also, if it completely changes an author's idea (like "this tab definitely was not played on 7-string bass, so I'll make it standard 4-string") - it should be rejected too.
But corrections absolutely should not be rejected if they didn't make the perfect tab. We made this feature mostly for little changes, like lyric errors or tab formatting improvements.
Do you have an example of rejected corrections? I'll try to solve it, if there is a problem

author: Garci
text:
jof nailed it on the head: captchas would pretty much annoy the existing userbase more than they would stop the spammers. Personally looking after every single account is simply out of the question, maybe if it were a smaller forum, but as it stands, monitoring at such a scale would involve a massive number of moderators being online 24/7.
One thing which could be implemented, closing threads with websites on their titles. That won't stop all of the spam, but it's a way to stop at least a portion of them. They mostly advertise through the thread title, which is an obvious giveaway to the contents. Of course, it's not all of it, but it's a measure which won't hurt the users.
Another one might be limiting the number of threads that you can create every half an hour (for example). A regular user would just go "meh" and post the same thread later. But spam bots are known to post several times in the course of a couple of minutes, so it would stop them. If a notification gets sent to the mods when this is broken, it just might deal with the spam account altogether when found.
And then there's the good old report function. It's not perfect, but it's a tool we've got.

author: kidrick
text: Since UG forces tabs to be of a certain format, it means that the scroll is inconsistent due to different spacing requirements for the lyrics and labels etc. Ideally I could have each bar of the sang be X number of lines long, but that violates the format standards and doesn't work when the spacing automatically moves down to the next line because of a large font size. A solution is a scroll speed marker that's embedded in the tab but not visible. So i put markers at each song section and tell the app the scroll speed or how long I want it to take to get to the next section. If the verse takes 52 seconds to sing, then I could put 52 beside the verse 1 label and it will take 52 seconds to scroll to the next label at the chorus. An elegant way to once and for all set the scroll speed once per song that works even when changing font sizes.

author: Roc8995
text:
Tabs are listed by artist and not author because in many, many cases there are different versions based on who performed it (e.g., Bob Dylan's All Along the Watchtower vs. Jimi Hendrix') , and it's the easiest way to capture which specific performance is being tabbed. It's not "miscrediting" or "attributing" at all, in the way you imply, because it's not actually crediting or attributing authorship in the first place. Nowhere does UG actually claim that the song was written by Bette Midler. It's just a transcription of her performance of that song. Plus, it's a whole lot easier for someone to find the song if they remember that Bette Midler sang it but can't remember the name. It would be nearly impossible to find if it were listed by author in that case.
For the exact same reasons, you'll see a dozen different artists listed for popularly covered songs like "Knocking on Heaven's Door" because users are interested in playing each unique version of that song (and there are often many different versions even of the same song by the same artist). UG is not implying that Eric Clapton, Bob Dylan, Guns and Roses, and Avril Lavigne all collectively wrote that song. It's just a catalog of their performances.

text:
There are already not one but two ways of doing this. The TPA approval system would work if enough people used it. Most tabs get to the end of their nominal two days waiting without any votes to approve or reject because we UG users don't have the time,energy or expertise to help out. I plead as guilty of anyone here.
The tiny UG team are then faced with roughly 100 tabs a day of songs spanning every genre and over 60 years of music. Most of the tabs will be for songs they barely know or have never heard. Checks are mainly for proper formatting.
Once the songs are up we get a second chance with the rating system. If we all rated unplayable messes 1 or 2 and playable songs 4or 5 we would soon know which are the bad tabs but people can't be bothered by and large. Some of my tabs have had thousands of views but no ratings at all. I have had something like 15,000 hits and only two ratings.
Then there is the problem of flaming. There are people out there who deliberately rubbish peoples contributions, we all know about the internet giving power without responsibility. I wouldn't be happy about having tabs removed on the say so of one or two random people.
The trouble is that I agree with you. There are too many poor tabs slipping through and to say that you should just be able to work everything out by ear is to miss the whole point of UG which is about sharing our efforts.

author: JD Close
text: It's because all the songs were submitted separately, sometimes by different authors years apart. As to why we can't just combine all of the songs into one album tab - there are serious logistical issues that would be involved in that, such as choosing the best variation of each song from each album, giving the author credit, copying everything over into full album tabs (which is pointless), and that all of that would have to be painstakingly done individually by the UG staff. All of the hassles involved in that trump your desire to not have to click on a new tab each time, and that's why we don't do that. There are a lot of issues on this site already, that would create a lot more.

I apologize in advance if this has been covered before, but I wasn't able to find it.
In short, some of the weirder chords aren't recognized/highlighted by the system, and so can't be transposed.
Because so many of the sheets suggest a capo, and I really just want to transpose them back to the original key, I get frustrated that some chords don't get transposed along with the rest.
An example I found last night is Ben Folds Five 'Kate'
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/b/ben_folds_five/kate_crd.htm
All chords are correctly highlighted and transposable except for Em7b5.  I've seen this with other variations as well, and I assume it's a problem with the regular expression used to match chords.
Oh heck, now I'm not so sure if you're using a regex at all, because Fmaj7b5 is correctly matched here:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/d/david_bowie/space_oddity_ver9_crd.htm
Maybe it's just certain combinations (*m7b5, *2, etc)
Hey, this one has several problems as well:
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/d/david_bowie/life_on_mars_ver2_crd.htm
Ab/Gb, Gm/F, F/Eb and others are all matched as 2 separate chords, not slash chords.
Gb+ is matched only as Gb, without the augmented.
Gm2 isn't matched at all.
I think the problem also sometimes occurs when chords are enclosed by or next to certain characters, but I can't find an example right now.
A while back, I came up with a regular expression that matches an enormous amount of weird chords.  Maybe it could be useful here?
Anyway, the transpose feature is one of the best things about this site, and all too often, I find songs that it won't work for because the system doesn't recognize some of the chords.

author: pazil

Hello! You can appeal and the tab will be added to the approval queue again. The point is that the moderator could have made a mistake and after the appeal, another moderator can consider it (not necessarily).
If the moderator's arguments were valid (for example, your tab is a duplicate, or has gross errors), then it does not make much sense to appeal. Your tab will be saved as a personal one

author: oconor531
text:
NSpen1
pazil
"the tab in question" is completely irrelevant.  If the I had appealed and a different moderator had used their veto on it, I wouldn't be here complaining.  I would've accepted it and moved on.
The issue, which has absolutely nothing to do with the tab in question, is that a moderator shouldn't be allowed to veto a tab, and then decide that the author doesn't deserve an appeal.
The same moderator that vetoed that tab originally also vetoed my appeal, less than an hour after I clicked "appeal."  That shouldn't be allowed.  From what I read, normal users cannot vote on the same tab twice.  That should be the case for moderators too, unless the tab is a gross TOS violation.  That is the issue.  Not the tab itself.

author: NSpen1
text:
oconor531
I can't agree with that; in cases where a tab is very obviously a duplicate or very similar to another tab, or should be a correction for an existing tab rather than a new version, I don't see any problem with the same moderator dealing with it.
Tab Moderators can't vote to reject the same tab twice but we can convert it to a correction if an appeal is made, which is what happened here and makes total sense.
UG Moderators can reject a tab twice, and do so when necessary.
If you (or anyone) feel that a tab has been rejected unfairly then you can post in the forum and ask for another opinion.  There is a thread for that -
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1701389

author: cobwebscavern1
text:
oconor531
We are all adults here and there's absolutely no need to anonymise the Tab Mod name and I am more than happy to admit that I am the person who made this decision.
Yes, I rejected your initial submission. Any of the other TMs or UGs can check this and see the decisions made in the TPA queue (and they already have). I did so as it was a copy (by your own admission in the song decsription) of the existing version which you had made some minor changes to.
After you appealed & complained (and then apologised for rudeness in your initial posts), during the course of that discussion I decided that I had perhaps been a little harsh with my first judgement in rejecting and that while it still was in no way valid as it's own version it perhaps had some merit as a correction so I chose to convert it to that.
Technically speaking, there would be nothing against the same TM carrying out those actions and then going and even voting on the correction but given you had already expressed your displeasure, I decided not to add any further actions, comments or thoughts onto the correction after that point and to let a fresh set of eyes make a decision on it.
I am more than happy for any other TM or UG user to review both the initial submission and the conversion to a correction and let me know if they think that I did anything wrong or made a decision that they disagree with - the initial submission being either a rejection or a correction was an edge case which, as I have explained, upon reflection and the almost instant appeal I decided to convert to a correction. I very, very much doubt that any user would disagree with it being one of those two things and would think that this had merit in being its own new version.
While I understand that you are saying that you aren't talking about this specific instance but the generality of a TM rejecting a submission and then converting the appeal to a correction there is nothing untoward, underhand or wrong about those actions.
I'd also point you to the TPA FAQs here -
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/help/approvalQueueFAQ
- and refer you to sections 2 and 6 namely the parts that say:
"Before you submit your tab, please use the search bar for the song and/or the band name to understand whether it's already exists or not, as we may already have several tabs on some songs."    &    "We immediately reject tabs if:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So the TL;DR - your new chord sheet submission was never going to be approved by any TM or UG as it was far too similar to the existing version - it was either going to be rejected and/or made into a correction.  You seem to be unhappy that both those things happened by the same TM. As another independent TM,
NSpen1
, has also pointed out, that is a perfectly acceptable line of action to happen.
In closing, I am sorry that you feel so aggrieved with what happened that you took time out of your day to make a thread here to discuss and seek clarification on what happened - I cannot change that and all I can do at this stage is to confirm again that nothing bad or wrong happened and that if another user did something similar with a submission into the TPA just now then the same course of actions could well apply.

author: oconor531
text:
cobwebscavern1
NSpen1

author: cobwebscavern1
text:
oconor531
It does both - I admit that can be somewhat confusing but you do get the "converted to a correction" message -
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/queue/decision/view?id=3941000
- (third message from the bottom).
What happens is that the correction becomes a new submission in the TPA queue and it says rejected to try to discourage folks from appealing when this happens as if they do  then they will have both the correction and the new submission being live in the TPA queue (which still does happen).
Just FYI your (now) correction is still in the TPA queue and is still to be decided upon -
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/contribution/correct/view?id=547670
- one other thing to note is that when a convertion to a correction happens it mucks up the timeline of comments (dunno why, technical reasons that are beyond my pay grade here) so they will look jumbled and out of place.

I guess it's a similar argument to the amount of lessons etc on the site, but you still get people creating threads asking generic theory questions which could have been answered if the poster had bothered to look.
At the end of the day, the reviews in a studio equipment section (if it were to happen) may not have been written by professionals, but then neither were the reviews in any of the other sections.  They'd be written by the average user, for the average user.
Yes, that may be a different perspective than a professional would have, but surely that's the point of reading user reviews - to get the opinion of someone in a similar position to yourself.

author: gergrylowe
text:
The biggest things i find with the new player all relate to the readability of the music.
I like to use the arrow keys to move the red line tracker to line up with what part of the song im playing along to. In most of the tabs the tempo is off either due to not wanting to crowd the sheet music with tempos or the studio tracks slightly changing. While its minimal in most cases sometimes its good to have a quick way of fixing it by hitting the arrow keys, especially when theres a brief rest which to do so. With the new player the responsiveness of the arrow keys is not there, not even with the mouse cursor, which I have tested on multiple computers to check its not just from one source.
Tying into the red line is the auto scroll. In the old player the auto scroll would jump every few bars. More specifically it would jump to the top when there is a full line below the current line the tracker is on, jumping to include the previous line above where the tracker currently is. this allows the red line to be faster or slower and still be able to read the music if the tempo is slightly off. With the new player, the autoscroll waits until the red line reaches the very bottom corner of the screen to jump up to the top corner. this acts similar to a page shift and causes spots while playing along that if the music is too fast or slow relative to the program the music isnt visible.
The last issue i have with the new player is the formatting, a lot of the time the note lengths are compressed together and illegible and certain markings are overlapping. I find the time signatures to be very large while every other icon and symbol too small (relatively, i know there is a zoom button).
I also find bugs with different instruments overlapping in the tab. For example, the page will open with bass selected first and when switched to guitar, the bass parts will fill the empty measures on the guitar tabs with bass tablature and vice versa, along all instruments selected while the page is open. Refreshing the page resets but does not fix the issue and usually sends the selected instrument back to the original one, which makes it impossible to read if the inital instrument selected is not the one that i am wanting to play
While i understand the old player may have too many bugs and causes a lot more work to keep running, id rather see the good things about it be implemented into the new player

author: blacklight86
text:
metelev.vladislav.ug
I make music with many people in several projects. The first question you're asked when you want to play covers with anyone is "what type of music do you play?".
You don't want to create a playlist every time you're asked this question. First, you'll need to create a playlist with all of your fav tracks and that takes time - you've got to select each single track in your library and add it to a playlist, I haven't seen anything like a bulk insert option around. Second, it takes time to keep it up-to-date - if I add some new song to my favourites then I need to keep in mind that I should also add it to the relevant playlists.
The most obvious solution is to share the full list of favourites, and let people pick whatever they like (and those songs, yes, you can add to a playlist). I've been doing this lots of times already with many musicians, they all appreciated me sharing my full list of favourites with them, and lots of times they've selected songs that I wouldn't have thought of. I've achieved this with scripts like the one I've posted above, and converting the resulting JSON object to CSV or Google Docs. The use case sounds so obvious to me that I can't see what's preventing the UG staff from seeing it.
The next question would be how to implement it. I've seen a few ideas from the other posts.
I personally like the idea of a shareable link like you would do with a Google Doc or Dropbox item - generate link with a click, copy it, and anyone with the link can access your list of favourites, unless you refresh/revoke the link. I like it because it's very easy to implement, very straightforward for users to understand, it integrates well with messaging apps and it works both on mobile and desktop.
For more advanced users it could also be a good idea to have an export to CSV/JSON format option.
Someone has also proposed some in-app mechanisms, but while those will make life much easier for users with the app installed, they risk cutting off all the musicians without the app (but hey, then I can work to convince all of my bandmates to install the UG app).

That involves investors, contracts... the whole nine yards, in order to get bands off the ground financially, staff, resources etc. It's a lot of work, and something that may not be profitable in the end, with UG being a Russian website catering to the international stage. It's better to have any costs covered by sales rather that a fee for the people providing the music.
Quote by Chaosinborn
I think that this is a good idea but starting off small would be a good idea. Enstead of being an actual label it could just start off as the Ultimate-Guitar demo disk or something of the sort.
You're starting down a difficult path right here.
A disk is a
physical
product.  It requires distribution through physical means, like mail, UPS, Fed Ex, w/e.  This adds cost.
An electronic product requires no physical shipment.  Just download via the net.
Quote by Chaosinborn
This could be fashioned in a way that every month or so there is a UG sponsored demo disk. This can contain a random assortment of music or it could be organized to contain a little bit of everything.
Early products could  be "samplers".  Compilations bridging many genres.  I'm not certain that's the best approach, though.  Most customers would likely prefer a compilation within a specific genre.  Having several products, each in a different genre would sell better.
Quote by Chaosinborn
Now if a band wants to put in a song there is an X ammount entry fee. To cover costs. Depending on how the business model is (profit or not) then it could be just enough to cover the projected cost of getting the cd's made.
The CDs can be free
(except for shipping since that can vary)
This is a
horrible
business model.  Since you're dealing with a physical product, you have TWO kinds of costs.  Manufacturing set-up (fixed) and production (varies.  determined by number of units created).
The better an album sells, the more copies must be made.  You can't just wish them into existence.  Who pays for the these extra copies?  The bands?  Ridiculous.  You've created a situation where the liability of cost to the bands increases the better the product is.
Quote by Chaosinborn
It can also be done in different editions (metal edition, rock, punk etc) and have different types of CDs for those that dont want listen to the other genres.
Of course.  But remember, with each different edition, there are new set-up costs.  You really need to break away from the mindset of a physical CD.  This is more appropriate for a mature distribution network.  Electronic-only distribution has extreme cost advantages.  That is where to start.

author: Naturist
text:
I often used to avoid unrated tabs, probably still do. On the search page there is no indication of their age (you can sort by date, but if you're looking for a certain song you won't) they look like forgotten entries that no one liked enough to rate.
I think if people see an older version that has a rating, even if it's not 5 out of 5, just some sort of validation, they will view that tab and MAYBE then give the mystery one a shot.
Therefore I think a "New!" flag in place of the star rating (which is where people are looking) for unrated tabs of less than a month old would draw the user's eye and help give new versions a small window of opportunity to get attention and, hopefully, a rating to help compete against the relics.
Cheers
Nat

author: RockInPeaceDime
text:
I truthfully do not desire to be an asshole. I understand monetizing a website -- you all provide a great service that absolutely has costs involved, and those costs have to be covered.  That's a given and I would never fault an organization of this sort for monetizing their website through advertising.  It's a necessity and fully expected.
But as someone who works in the digital marketing field, the advice you've received is coming from a poor source and you need to consult a genuine professional that understands digital marketing.  It's really gotten to the point where your monetizing strategy significantly takes away from the functionality of the website and makes the site almost chore-like to use in some respects.  That's not good, obviously.
I would encourage you to rethink your overall strategy and implementation.  I say that as someone who really does like this site, visits fairly frequently, has recommended it to friends, and so on.  I genuinely do believe if you continue down the path you're on, a substitute is sure to arise in the long run.

But really the main reason (and certainly why I use GP) is because these programs audibly play the tab, so we can make judgments straight away as to whether or not the tab is correct. 2nd then comes a way in which we can edit these tabs as well as create our own, but that's not the point (because you can also do that with ascii tabs). The MAIN thing that separates ascii tabs and GP is that in GP you can HEAR what is written in the tab.
So my point being, by advertising in such a way to GP users, who have already really have a program that have the function they want, which is a tab reader they can hear, you're kinda targeting the wrong audience. Now, of course you need to keep making money to keep this site running, so I agree you need to advertise (in a tactful way) But instead of advertising to the GP user to use your Tab Pro product, instead advertise to the much BIGGER audience of ascii tab users.
Now that makes logical sense because those users don't have a tab reader with play back and I'm sure the main criticism ascii tab users will have with the ascii format is that they have to physically go through and play a tab to see whether it's correct or not. So by you going straight to those type of users and saying 'look, we understand the problem you have and we have a product which is cheap and is a good solution to your problem.' And I'd imagine the amount of users who would jump at that chance would be enough to cover the overheads of many things on the site. I mean say you have 50,000 visitors to your site a day who use ascii tabs, and your marketing campaign persuades 5000 of those users to try Tab Pro and they sign up to the $2.99 option for one month. Well then you've made almost $15000 for that month. That is just an example of course as I don't know the actual statistics of this site.
But my point being is that I'm not saying 'throw out all adverts and go to hell', but to actually make you consider that you're targeting the wrong people on the site and are doing so a tad too aggressively. (And just a side note, I'd imagine from having talked to a few people, that GP users who have switched to Tab Pro have done so just to see what its like, rather then thinking that they've found an all better solution to GP)
Hopefully you see that I'm trying to work with you rather then criticize you and maybe this might get the ball rolling in another direction.

author: ZeGuitarist
text:
Hi,
I was just browsing the Pit and I noticed how many threads were made about topics that are covered in the "dedicated threads", such as the Computer thread, Gaming thread, Sex thread, etc... Those new threads are of course always quickly closed by the mods, but they just keep spawning because most users just don't know that these dedicated threads exist. Something funny I noticed: at a certain point, Slut (the Pit mod) was replying in a computer-related thread which got closed by Carmel, and then Slut apologized to Carmel saying "I didn't know we had a computer thread"...
I'm not blaming her, or anybody else, for not knowing there are threads like these, because the Pit is so crowded. My suggestion is to make a subforum in the Pit, to move these dedicated threads to. Something like the Advanced Techniques subforum in Musician Talk; AT has less activity, but still enough.
A Pit subforum will make it easier for users to find the dedicated threads, which also makes it more "attractive" for them to post in there. I think the number of "wrong" threads/posts in the Pit will drop... In short, I think a Pit subforum for the dedicated threads may be advantageous.
Of course, I realise there are some issues. First of all, there IS a sticky with all the dedicated threads listed. I know, but I think a subforum AND that sticky will be much more effective. A bigger issue, however, is that users shouldn't be allowed to make new threads in that subforum; it's supposed to be ONLY for the dedicated threads, and the mods decide which threads belong in there (kinda like Archived threads, but not read-only!) I don't know if this is possible...
Anyway, just a suggestion... What do you think?
Cheers!
ZeG

author: UG Support
text:
jgordstevens1
Hello!
Workarounds to Try
Use Browser Tabs
Right-click (or long-press on mobile) the tab or song title you want to explore and choose “Open link in new tab” (or "background tab"). This way, your main list stays where you’re browsing, and you won't lose your spot when jumping into an individual tab.
Open in a New Window
Similar to using tabs, you can open the selected song in a new browser window. The benefit is that your original list stays intact in its own window, so you can easily return without resetting.
Use Search Filters Instead
If you're repeatedly navigating through the same subset of artists or songs, try narrowing down the list using the search or filter tools (like filtering by artist name or song title). This will help you quickly return to the items you're interested in without flipping through pages.
Bookmark or Copy the URL
If your browser's back button jumps to the first page, consider bookmarking the URL of the exact page you’re on—or even the specific filtered list. That lets you return right where you left off with just a click.
Why This Happens
Many users have observed that the site doesn’t retain the scroll or pagination state when using the browser's back button. It’s a limitation of the current site design and not something that can be changed via user settings. In fact, numerous forum users across similar topics have seen this behavior—when clicking back, the page resets to the top, meaning your browsing position gets lost.

author: Lemoninfluence
text:
The forums and the front page articles are moderated differently because they cater to different audiences. While there's a lot of crossover, a large number of people who read the articles do not read the forums and vice versa. The articles and front page are held to a different standard because they're the first thing people see on the site, and it's important that those are suitable for all audiences (although I know from personal experience that there have been times where the articles themselves are a bit nsfw).
The forums on the other hand are a relatively close and closed community. Apart from the popular threads list on the front page, you have to seek out the content on the forums and so there's more leeway given, especially in the 'off topic' section. And although they're given more leeway to suggest that they're given free reign is a massive exaggeration. The forums (mainly the pit) is given leeway because of its off topic nature, it's for any topic that isn't covered in other forums, whereas the comment sections are there for commenting on the article, lesson or interview that you've just read. And posts like "X sucks" aren't really related to the article, nor do they serve to encourage constructive discussions. What they usually do is start arguments which actively stifle more reasonable conversations. And so we warn people in order to try and prevent those things from happening.
With the comment system being restructured, it's difficult to keep track of which comments have been checked or not. That's why you used to see a lot of posts which were just the word "checked" (or variations on that). It allowed us to carry on from there under the expectation that comments previous to that had been checked and were suitable. Now there's more chance of a comment slipping through the net. But that shouldn't be taken as approval of those comments, it's merely a flaw in the system that allows those people to get away with infringing the rules.
Also, a writer didn't get banned for saying a band sucks. A user got warned for saying "X sucks, deal with it". The user (who happened to be a writer, which had no bearing on the decision) was banned for a misunderstanding and was unbanned as soon as the mistake was brought to light.

The other user's ban was related to two infringements of the rules, one was for band bashing, the other for homophobic spam. I'm not going to go into detail because it's not really anyone else's business, but this does outline that there's almost always a wider context to a ban. author: bstetar
text:
Finding a song within "My tabs" is a tedious venture. Gotta open My tabs->find the artist->scroll some more to find the song.
Why not have single cross-referenced index of songs that the user can set as the default view in "My tabs"? Think about it. It's the songs that people ultimately want to find and play! I am so tired of scrolling the list of "Artists" to get to the song I want to practice. There's no search either in My Tabs. You have the user search the entire UG catalog when I only want to search My tabs or my Playlists. Again, having a list of songs that the user could sort, search, and find would make for a more user-friendly program.
I began subscribing to UG over 5 years ago, but I'm not seeing any effort to streamline the program to make using it more efficient and easier. I am starting to look at alternatives to UG. Look, little things get overlooked. There are two infrequently accessed links between "My tabs" and "Playlists." Courses and books can go to the bottom of the list. I'll bet the number of hits on My course and My books are miniscule compared to My tabs and Playlists. Users can get carpal tunnel scrolling over those two links to get to Playlists or My tabs. It's almost seems to say: "UG doesn't care because UG doesn't have to."

author: brettsanace
text:
On UG many songs have multiple versions (not including Acoustic and Live versions). I am going to call these the "Recorded versions". When a strumming pattern is approved to be added to one of these recorded versions it should automatically be added to all of the "Recorded versions" of the song on UG. "Acoustic" and "Live" versions should have their own strumming patterns.
This will prevent people collecting IQ points for adding the same pattern to half a dozen versions, or other people simply copying an already submitted pattern and adding it to another version, also save time for moderators and others having to review and approve these copies, and also ensure that whichever version of the song the user happens to prefer that the strumming pattern is available to them.

author: NSpen1
text:
brettsanace
It's a good idea in theory, but I think there could be a few problems in practice.
Some songs may not have one clearly defined strumming pattern and people may want to add slightly different patterns.  If someone adds only one pattern for a song and that's then applied to all tabs, it's not so easy to then add further patterns which the song may need - hmm, actually you can, you have to go to "edit" next to strumming pattern but I've only just worked that out, not sure how many people will be aware you can do that.
Not all tabs are correctly labelled as to whether they are Acoustic or Live, so patterns could be added to those which don't necessarily apply.  And lastly, as you know, some authors don't want strumming patterns added to their tabs.

author: brettsanace
text:
NSpen1
As you said people can edit a strumming pattern if the tab is incorrectly labelled as Recorded, Acoustic or Live, or they may also add an alternative strumming pattern which if approved will also show, However if a strumming pattern is deemed to be correct for a recorded version of a song I don't see why it shouldn't apply for all versions of the song (apart from Acoustic and Live). I understand the problem of authors who don't want strumming patterns added to their tabs but I'm happy for them to go to the effort of deleting it considering other people have gone to the effort of adding it. I am going to add a separate thread about authors who don't want changes to their tabs or strumming patterns added to their tabs  when I get around to it. Love your new profile pic!!!!

author: theogonia777
text:
I know that there has been plenty of discussion about this over the years and all, but this is not so much of a "suggestion" thread so much as a "relaying data on the subject" sort of thread.
After a recent discussion yesterday, I was curious to see what kind of interest there would be in that sort of thing, so I made a thread in the Pit with a poll to get an idea of the level of interest, and any ideas people had, so I figure I might as well report the results to you guys over here.
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1501933
There doesn't seem to be an overwhelmingly large amount support for it, but it does seem that there is at least some, though the data naturally must be taken with a grain or two of salt, since I'm sure (as common sense would dictate) that a number of the people that say they would be interested would probably not actually buy anything if UG products did go on sale, but perhaps the data could still be of some use for the higher-ups to consider the whenever they next discuss that sort of thing.
There are some decent suggestions in there (and some pretty bad ones, though it's hard to tell which ones are and aren't serious of course), so those could be other things to consider.
I'm sure that more data would have to be collected to get more accurate figures in terms of the level of interest, since there are numerous variables that need to be considered here, but I figured that this is at least a start, and could give at least a rough idea, and at the least it does indicate that there isn't an overwhelmingly low level of support.

text:
On Guitar Pro tabs, it would be nice if autoscroll had an option that lets you preview/read-ahead. For example, the current autoscroll will only scroll once it hits the bottom of the visible tab. This means that I cannot read ahead in the tab to see what's coming up and I tend to mess up wherever there are these "page turns". So I either need to memorize the next measure, pause to preemptively scroll (rendering autoscroll useless), or rewind the tab after hitting the next measure.
What I would like to see is an option for the tab to scroll one line or measure ahead of where it currently does (and subsequently scroll one line/measure less). This means that the next measure would always be visible, so you would always be prepared for it.
I realize that on smaller screens or when not in fullscreen, it's common to only be able to see two lines at once. So this option might not work as well in those situations, since there would be a lot of scrolling, but I think it would be very helpful for people with larger screens or who use fullscreen.

Right, it got messed up in my head. Actually apostrophes only show up in personal tabs. Anyway, some unicode, like Eastern European characters, show up correctly in regular tabs, too, e.g.
https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/2262701
and the URL is just digits. So I thought it wouldn't be much hassle to allow apostrophes as well?
Btw the capitalization feature goes cranky sometimes, and besides it is not desired in all languages. For instance, in Polish only the first word should be capitalized by default. And even in English, I think it is reasonable to leave conjunctions lowercase, like "of" and "and" and "to" instead of "Of", "And", "To". This feature fails especially in unusual combinations, like "Hi-Lo" — it ends up as "Hi-lo" which doesn't really look too well. I think it would be best to leave the casing choices to the tab authors. If someone is lazy, we can always correct them afterwards. After all, lettercase is also a piece of information that shouldn't be just thrown away like that.

author: NSpen1
text:
hyvyys
Yeah, you're right, those can be in song titles and others like umlauts, other accents, hyphens.  But characters like brackets, apostrophes, slashes, etc. can't.  I'm sure there's some technical reason for it, and it should happen eventually but probably won't be too soon, I think.
All individual 'words' get capitalised by default, so there's not too much that can be done about the Polish case.  May be some other examples like when numbers are involved - 2nd will be 2Nd - or a hyphenated word may have another capital when you don't want it to.

author: NSpen1
text:
Ah, you added some more to your post - so I might have had the hyphenated case the wrong way round.
I agree with you that song titles look better with those little words in lower case, but I think it would be chaos if we allowed tab authors to write titles however they wanted.  You don't want one song with 3 or 4 different versions of the title appearing in tab listings.  Despite the drawbacks, I think the system as it is with regards to capitalisation is probably the most sensible.
P.S. I do enough correcting of wrong song titles as it is, don't give me more work

author: collinkc
text:
I submitted a tab recently and had it rejected because I had not put the chords above every (musically identical) verse. This bothers me, but not so much because I have to go back and redo it.
Not everyone who receives this message is going to take the time and effort to resubmit. Sometimes I don't have time to figure out a song and just want to find a tab for it quickly. Even if it doesn't have chords above every single verse. Even if it's not completely accurate. Even if it contains mis-heard lyrics. And I can't help but feel like anything that discourages someone from submitting is going to limit the information I have to draw from. I think that's what the rating system is for. If I see two tabs for a song and only one took the extra effort, that one is going to get a good rating. If someone put the chords above every verse, and someone else didn't but the chords are more accurate, that's the one that's going on my favorites list.
I also would prefer some tabs don't have chords over every verse since it makes the tab much longer than it needs to be. I have a big phone, but it's usually not big enough to show the whole song as it is. Chords over every line doubles it. The extra clutter also makes it easier to lose your place when you look away for a moment.
I appreciate the attempt to improve the quality of the work on the site, but I feel like it's a little heavy handed. If I submit a lazy tab and someone else copy/pastes it with the chords repeated for every verse and gets a better rating than me, that's on me.
Now I'm off to resubmit.

author: mendace
text:
The biggest problem I have with these pages is that there isn't a mobile version. Apart from that, much of the information and some features that are available on the current profile page are either outdated or unnecessary. These features can be removed, I think:
- mp3's & playing skills
- UG Score
- Blogs
- MSN contacts
- Friendship requirements
- Status field
- Lifestyle & Your School information
- Favorite & forward user profile
- Bands
- Groups
- Last online date (private profile only)
Quite a few of the existing features are broken and/or can be improved:
Block users
- As mentioned above, the block feature is broken and only restricts some actions
- The list of blocked users is just a wall of text and usernames get cut off
- Usernames disappear when you add/remove a user from the list
Private messages
- Notifications about new messages, both emails and site notifications
- The feature that allows you to use automatic hints to add more than one recipient is broken
My updates
- New tabs is the only one that works
- Comments and ratings are already covered by the My Status section on the homepage
Settings
- The settings are all over the place, one page with universal settings should be enough
Moderator actions
- The current format is especially frustrating for moderators. Users can post a lot of information on their profile that we are unable to remove, e.g. spammers often post links to scam sites as their status and we can't clear that field. We shouldn't have to contact admins when we want to remove offensive content.
- It would be a lot easier to delete spam and insults if we could delete comments in the comment section of profiles directly instead of having to go to the user's comments page (profile comments should show in BB, imo). Too many clicks for a simple action.

author: MatrixClaw
text:
I swear I replied to this post a long time ago, but I don't see anything in my recent posts. Weird.
I'm sure you're perfectly capable, but if you need any help with design / development, I'd love to help. Professionally, I'm the senior developer on a team of front end engineers and before that I was a graphic designer for 5 years. The biggest issue I have with these pages are their mobile responsiveness. The forum works well enough for browsing and posting, but the profile section of UG is nearly unusable on a mobile phone (which I assume is where over half the traffic to the website comes from). Until more recently, I couldn't even reply to messages on a phone because the text area wouldn't open the mobile keyboard, which was very frustrating and, honestly, one of the reasons I've been less active on the forum as a whole.
