I feel like the whole website needs a overhaul on its social aspects, otherwise it's more useful to just have a simple profile built into the forum section, like most other forum-based sites, and move the messaging system back into it, so you don't have to leave the forum at all to reply to messages.

author: a.faretdinov
text:
rkl3
when they make a decision. I don’t want to create unrealistic expectations regarding the changes being discussed here. Decision-making at Ultimate Guitar is a complex process and is never based on a single source of feedback. It involves research, experiments, testing, user surveys, broader data analysis etc.
The Forum is an important and long-standing part of the Ultimate Guitar community, and we genuinely value the discussions and feedback shared here. At the same time, it’s important to keep in mind that forum users represent only a small portion of our overall user base. A much larger number of UG'icians are not active on the forum and often have different priorities or opinions on the same topics. This can sometimes lead to a false consensus effect, where opinions shared within a relatively small but vocal group feel more universal than they actually are. In reality, feedback from the forum does not always reflect the preferences or needs of the broader Ultimate Guitar community, which we must take into account when making product and strategic decisions. It may be frustrating, but it's a fact. It doesn't mean that your thoughts and feedback are not useful, we still hear you!

author: Pbuzzguitar
text:
a.faretdinov
Thank you for your response. Your explanation of the interplay of factors that go into decision-making at UG is welcome, well reasoned and even-tempered, in the face of user comments that are sometimes irritable, sarcastic or provocative.
However, I'm sure you can also appreciate why user frustration arises, when it seems that users' repeatedly-raised concerns often seem to meet a wall of silence, or official responses that are glacially slow, or are anodyne reassurances that really don't address the details of the issues raised.
For example (to return to my own personal hobby-horse!) the lack of an easy-to-find logout button has been repeatedly raised by several different users since the previously-existing one disappeared in the site redesign around eight years (!) ago, and as far as I can see, in all that time there has been no official explanation, or even response beyond "we hear you and we're thinking about it".
This seems not only frustrating but also bizarre, since it's diificult to see what the objection would be - the technical implementation would surely be trivial, and virtually every other website with logins makes a logout option easy to find from every page of the site.
So is there some mysterious official objection, and a policy of stone-walling any comments on the topic? No-one knows. This is honestly kind of infuriating, and surely helps contribute to the kind of bad-tempered comments that I'm sure you'd prefer not to have to deal with.
So - how about some action on this, or at least some update on the official position and current state-of-play regarding this issue?

author: a.faretdinov
text:
Pbuzzguitar
hi again, I would like to clarify, however, that not every change on the website or in the app is tied to a formal “official position.” Much of Ultimate Guitar’s development is iterative and driven by technical, architectural, or long-term product considerations. As with any evolving service, every decision- even positive ones will inevitably generate criticism from some users. That is an unavoidable part of development at this scale. Regarding examples like the missing logout button, I fully understand why this feels especially frustrating. While such issues may appear trivial from the outside, they are often connected to broader UX or platform-level decisions. The absence of a visible change does not mean the feedback is ignored or intentionally stonewalled, but I agree that clearer communication would be helpful.
My role as Community Manager is to ensure that recurring, well-reasoned feedback like yours is collected and shared with the responsible teams. While I cannot promise specific outcomes or timelines, I can assure you that this input is being heard and documented.
Thank you again for engaging in a respectful and constructive way. Feedback like this genuinely helps improve both the product and the dialogue around it.

author: Lemoninfluence
text:
Quote by Anything Goes
What's stopping people from copying copyrighted tablature books currently?
tab moderation.
the site is legally ok as long as they're making an attempt to remove the copyrighted works. Tabs are a legal grey area. They're not exactly note for note transcriptions and they don't wholly originate from the writer (i.e. they're based on other works) so it's questionable as to whether or not they receive copyright protection.
Standard notation is covered by most copyright regimes and producing a standard notation manuscript of a copyrighted song is an infringing act in some countries. It's ok to do if it's for personal study, but UG is hosting the works for gain/profit (or at least that's how the courts will likely see it).
Tabs are a grey area, standard notation isn't.

author: jlawrence0723
text:
Idea: Prohibit Authors Voting on Corrections to Their Own Tabs
Rationale:
Tabs should be allowed to be improved.
Many authors are currently basically locking their tabs from being manipulated. This prevents improvements. How do they do this? They vote to reject improvements. Usually these authors have votes that count for 5 points, and some of them have full control over the tabs so they have the power to reject anything without discussion. While the speedy resolution of disputes has its merits, democratic, crowdsourcing tactics allows many minds to come to a more central resolution.
2.  Community should get a voice.
The voices, ideas and contributions of the many are being silenced in order to protect those of the few.  Valuing the individual is very important, but doing so at the cost of the community is detrimental.

author: Hydra150
text:
Hey dudes
I have taken to bookmarking tabs/chord charts on this website so that I can quickly get back to them, but it's a bit annoying that I have to work out the correct key and then use the 'transpose' feature each time I open them (especially so since I want to play along with a whole album without stopping between tracks, so that's 12 pages I have to correct).
The site would be easier to use if it remembered what transposition settings I have on each tab - I'd think this would be easy enough to implement.
Another thing - when transposing chord charts up or down there will often be more sharps or flats, and this can cause problems because it seems that the software automatically uses sharps instead of flats - often this is incorrect and I will find a D followed by a D# chord, where there should be an Eb. Using the wrong sign can make it much harder to read.
I would suggest the implementation of a feature which lets the user toggle whether the chords are displayed as sharps or flats, a button next to the transpose feature perhaps.

author: N04Hz_Ark
text:
Hey all,
So many tunings that are not ‘supported’ on this website. Even when a song has alternative tunings and clicking “Tuning” to show the tuner function, it appears if the tuning is not in the database, it just refuses to show the notes on the tuner.
For example, if you open the tuning feature on a ‘supported’ tuning, such as Metallica’s “
One
” it will show the notes on the tuning pegs as well as “Tuning: E A D G B E” down the bottom. If you open the tuning feature on an unsupported tuning, such as Tiny Moving Parts’ “
Birdhouse
”, no notes are shown on the pegs, and the label is “Tuning: “ with no notes listed. These tunings are also nowhere to be found on the search page. These things should not be predefined.
Another request, bit of a long shot:
Alternatively, it would also be cool to have a tuning system where you can filter by tunings with the same relative tuning intervals rather absolute pitch of the strings.
For example, E Standard (E A D G B E) has an internal pattern of "+5, +5, +5, +4, +5”, which is the same as D Standard (D G C F A D).
This would be helpful for these weird-alternative tunings such as the one found in Birdhouse (C# G# D# G# C D#). It’s Open Aadd9 (D A E A C# E) tuning, but half step down. This tuning is super popular in midwest emo songs.
I hope the first one can be done where tunings do not need to be predefined, and if this change isn’t implemented, then at least being faster at adding them to the database...
Thanks.
